attorneys.name: Patrick C. Bernal
attorneys.firm_name: Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Trial Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Patrick C. Bernal, a partner with Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C. is a litigator in the areas of municipal and governmental law. Mr. Bernal served as an Assistant City Attorney for the City of San Antonio from 1983 to 1988, advising various City departments as general counsel and representing the City in litigation. Mr. Bernal continued litigating as a tax attorney for the law firm of Heard, Goggan, Blair and Williams from 1988 to 1991, dealing primarily with property tax suits on behalf of governmental entities.

Mr. Bernal has practiced civil trial law in the area of local government defense since joining the firm in 1991. He directs federal and state court litigation involving employment law, annexation, civil rights, torts, contracts, and personal and property damage relating to flood events, in both federal and state courts. Mr. Bernal also pursues appeals on behalf of governmental entities arguing before state and federal appellate courts.

Mr. Bernal received his J.D. from The University of Texas School of Law, his Master's Degree in Public Administration from the Lyndon B. Johnson School of Public Affairs, and his Bachelor of Arts from Texas A & M University, College Station.

In her position as the firm's Managing Attorney, Ms. Bernstein also manages and all of the attorneys at the firm.

attorneys.name: Kevin H. Berry
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Kevin H. Berry, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kevin H. Berry was born and raised in San Antonio. The Berry family has been in the cattle & ranching business for over 145 years. He has approximately 5,000 acres of his family's cattle and commercial hunting ranches in Bandera, Frio, and Milam counties.

After he started his professional business career as a business management consultant with an international accounting firm, Kevin left consulting to go to law school to pursue a legal career practicing real estate law. In 1989, after a few years as an associate attorney with one of the largest law firms in San Antonio, he opened his own private law practice specializing in real estate and probate law.

Private Practice / Real Estate and general business practice.

Kevin H. Berry has extensive experience in real estate and financial institutions law, and mortgage lending. He has represented Banks, Savings and Loans, and Credit Unions and has served as counsel for numerous financial institutions throughout his practice; documented multi-million dollar commercial real estate and non-real estate loans; negotiated and documented loan workouts and restructuring; and handled hundreds of real estate foreclosure matters under conventional and Tex. Const. art. XVI, § 50a(6) home equity loans.

Mr. Berry has:

negotiated, documented, and closed residential and commercial real estate sales of all complexities;

represented developers in subdividing, platting and restricting residential and commercial subdivisions and developing shopping centers, and office buildings;

represented commercial and residential building contractors, property owners, in negotiating, preparing and reviewing construction contracts and related documentation;

examined title to millions of dollars worth of commercial, residential, and farm & ranch real estate on behalf of investors of those properties;

represented surface and mineral owners in oil and gas disputes with discovery companies;

acted as adviser for numerous investors in farm and ranch properties;

represented both tenants and landlords (including apartment management companies) in a wide variety of residential and commercial leasing transactions; and

handled hundreds of foreclosures in numerous counties throughout Texas.

Insured Real Estate Closing.

Mr. Berry is a licensed Escrow Officer by the Texas Department of Insurance and Fee Attorney for Old Republic Title, authorized to close insured title closings on behalf of the company. A representative example of closings include Purchase and Sale transactions, refinance of existing debt, new loans origination, FHA, VA, and Conventional lending; for residential, commercial, and farm & ranch transactions.

Business Organizations.

Mr. Berry is experienced in the areas of business entity planning, and the formation and operation of corporations, limited l companies, partnerships, and joint ventures. He acts as general counsel for several small and mid-sized entities. These entities have both real estate and non-real estate related businesses such as real estate brokerage, development, construction, and property management; personal property leasing; retail sales; restaurant ownership and operations; insurance; roofing; and light and heavy manufacturing.

Former Municipal Judge City of Castle Hills

attorneys.name: William E. Berry Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Mediation Lawyers in Midland, TX
attorneys.bio:
Bill is a shareholder in the law firm's Litigation Section. He is licensed to practice before all Texas state courts, the United States Supreme Court, the United States Courts of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, and the United States District Courts for the Northern and Western Districts of Texas. Bill has argued appeals before the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, one of which was before the en banc court and resulted in the court reversing its prior decision as well as a District Court's judgment. Bill is a member of the Texas Association of Defense Counsel and the Defense Research Institute. He served as President of the Ector County Bar Association and as President of the Downtown Rotary Club. Bill received the Young Lawyers' Pro Bono Award from West Texas Legal Services. He was named a "Rising Star" in Texas Monthly Super Lawyers - Rising Stars Edition." He is a member of the Pro Bono College of the State of Texas. Bill served as the Section Head for the litigation section of the law firm and serves on the law firm's Board of Directors.

Bill has participated in over 300 mediations. His clients appreciate his knowledge, experience, skill, care, judgment, and common sense approach to solving difficult legal issues. Bill will be prepared and he will work hard to settle your case. If the matter does not settle at mediation, he will remain engaged as long as the parties desire for him to help facilitate a settlement. He has nearly thirty years of experience representing plaintiffs and defendants in oil and gas litigation, commercial litigation, and insurance defense litigation in both state and federal courts in Texas and New Mexico.

Bill is active in his church, coached youth soccer, is a past president of the Downtown Rotary Club, and is a past president of the Ector County Bar Association. Bill has completed the Big D. Texas Marathon, Rock ‘n' Roll San Diego Marathon, White Rock Dallas Marathon, Bath Beat Marathon in Bath, England, White Rock Half Marathon and Sprint Triathlons. He has summited Mount Kilimanjaro and Mount Kenya in Africa.

In law school, Bill was a lead advocate on Baylor's National Mock Trial Team, which won the Regional Finals in Dallas and represented the region and Baylor University at the National Mock Trial Team Finals in Washington, D.C. He was also a member of Baylor's Order of Barristers and recipient of Baylor's Pakis, Giotes, Beard & Page Advocacy Award.

In his undergraduate studies, Bill was named the Outstanding Graduate in Mass Communications, served as Editor-In-Chief of the school newspaper and graduated with honors.

PRACTICE AREAS

Mediation

Bill Berry has participated in over 300 mediations. Bill grew up in West Texas. He has tried lawsuits, mediated cases, and handled cases on appeal for nearly thirty years in Texas and New Mexico. He has represented plaintiffs and defendants, individuals and businesses, charitable institutions, and governmental entities. He has broad experience in oil and gas litigation, commercial litigation, and insurance defense litigation in both state and federal courts. He has served as lead counsel on hundreds of cases that were resolved through bench trial, jury trial, arbitration, mediation, or other means of voluntary settlement. His clients appreciate his knowledge, experience, skill, care, judgment, and common sense approach to solving difficult legal issues. Bill will be prepared and he will work hard to settle your case. If the matter does not settle at mediation, he will remain engaged as long as the parties desire for him to help facilitate a settlement.

Oil and Gas Litigation

Bill spends much of his time representing clients involved in oil and gas related disputes. On behalf of corporate and individual clients, he prosecutes and defends suits involving operating agreements, master service agreements, drilling contracts, well service contracts, indemnity provisions, surface use issues and royalty payment disputes.

Commercial Litigation

Bill has extensive experience litigating commercial disputes. He has an active and successful trial practice and has successfully resolved lawsuits through trial, summary judgment and voluntary settlement for individuals, corporations and governmental entities in cases involving contract disputes, partnership and corporate/shareholder disputes, breach of fiduciary duty, collection matters, products liability, commercial tort/DTPA lawsuits, fraud and misrepresentation.

Personal Injury and Insurance Defense

Bill devotes a significant portion of his practice to defending clients who have been sued in cases involving claims for personal injury and wrongful death, including oilfield injuries, on-the-job accidents, automobile accidents and trucking accidents. attorneys.name: Karri Bertrand
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Legal Matters Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Karri was born the first of ten children and raised in Dallas, Texas. Her large family afforded her an early opportunity to learn and understand complex family dynamics. Growing up, Karri excelled as a leader, earning recognition not only academically but also earning awards in extracurricular activities from archery to women’s chorale. She also personally experienced challenges, including her own divorce and custody matters; these events later inspired Karri to become the compassionate, ardent advocate she is today.

Karri did not pursue higher education right out of high school, unlike many attorneys. Instead, she raised her son while working as a certified paralegal for sixteen years. Not only did Karri balance the challenges of motherhood during this time, she gained invaluable practical legal experience from the ground-up. As a paralegal, Karri performed a broad range of legal work in complex litigation and appellate cases: drafting pleadings, reviewing evidence, preparing for trials and mediations, and of course, working directly with clients.

It was no wonder, then, that Karri was a high-achieving student as well. Karri graduated with major honors with a thesis, summa cum laude, from the University of Texas at Dallas. Later, she attended the University of North Texas at Dallas College of Law—all while continuing to work at one of the premier family law firms in Texas, O’Neil Wysocki. Karri graduated cum laude, after receiving multiple awards for academic performance, writing for the Accessible Law review, and serving as an inaugural appointee to the Board of Advocates.

Licensure allowed Karri to transition from paralegal at O’Neil Wysocki to attorney, where she quickly flourished. Karri’s brilliant legal mind, commitment to leadership, and tenacious representation garnered additional honors and awards. She has published numerous articles and received invitations to speak at conferences, from Advanced Family Law (“the” family law conference for Texas lawyers) to Lavender Law, a nationally renowned conference focusing on issues affecting the LGBTQIA community. Texas Super Lawyers named Karri a Rising Star in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024; Best Lawyers named Karri among the “Ones to Watch” in 2021, 2022, and 2023.

After only four years, Karri branched out to found her own firm, KB Family Law. Karri’s litigation and appellate practice flourished rapidly, allowing Karri to assemble a growing team equally committed to respect and collaboration. Each of her staff offers unique experiences and broad perspectives, and each shares Karri’s passion for serving the unique legal needs of diverse Texas families.

attorneys.name: Craig Bettis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
I am a native of Texas and grew up on the Southside of San Antonio. I graduated from East Central High School and attended Texas A&M University where I graduated with a Bachelor of Science Degree. I attended the South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas and have been licensed to practice law since 2003.

I am licensed to practice in all state, district and county courts in the State of Texas as well as in the Federal District Court for the Western District of Texas. I was recently voted a Rising Star 2009 of Top Young Layers in San Antonio’s Scene in SA Magazine. I am a member of the State Bar of Texas, San Antonio Trial Lawyers Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and the San Antonio Bar Association.

I represent individuals who have been wronged by the negligence of others. My goal is to settle your claim in the most efficient and economical manner possible. If I am not able to settle your case, I will vigorously litigate your case in court. I feel that too many people are not given their fair and constitutional right of access to the legal system. It is important to me that people who are wronged have their day in court and that the attorney of their choosing provide them the best advice and legal representation possible. I strongly feel that an attorney should care about their client’s needs and keep them informed of what is going on with their case. Providing as much information as possible to the client allows the client to make the right decision for themselves and their families when it comes to settling a case. These are the rules that I try to live by when I represent my clients.

My practice focuses on all personal injury and wrongful death claims, including but not limited to, on the job injuries, automobile collisions, trucking collisions, products and premises liability. If you have been injured as the result of someone else’s negligence, I can help you and I will work hard on your case.

I have personally tried cases in Bexar County District and County Courts at law, Wilson County, and Ulvalde County. I have personally filed or settled cases in Atascosa, Bexar, Brazos, Denton, Gonzales, Frio, Karnes, Kenedy,Ker, La Salle, Nueces, Medina, Uvalde, and Wilson Counties.

attorneys.name: Rachel Bethel
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rachel Bethel represents employees before federal and state courts, as well as in administrative proceedings before the EEOC, TWC, and OSHA. She has experience in a wide range of civil rights and employment issues, and she truly enjoys working on them all. Prior to joining Rob Wiley, P.C., Ms. Bethel practiced at a Washington, DC civil rights law firm and at an American Lawyer 50 international law firm.

The best part of being a lawyer for Ms. Bethel is connecting with her clients and supporting them on their legal journey. She hopes that each client knows and feels that someone cares about them, their story, and the wrongs that they have endured in the workplace. For Ms. Bethel, fighting on behalf of everyday people while going up against corporate giants or governmental agencies is deeply rewarding.

Ms. Bethel graduated from the George Washington University Law School in Washington, DC. During her time in law school, Ms. Bethel developed a strong background in civil rights and employment law. She clerked for a Washington EEOC Administrative Judge, served employees as a student attorney with GW’s Public Justice Advocacy Clinic, and clerked for three plaintiffs’ firms, one of which was another DC civil rights firm. She also had the opportunity to intern for the Office of the General Counsel at the Department of Health & Human Services.

While at GW, Ms. Bethel was also a member of GW’s Federal Circuit Bar Journal, as well as a member of the Metropolitan Washington Employment Lawyers Association and the South Asian Law Students Association. Finally, she was a Workers’ Rights Clinic volunteer for the Washington Lawyers’ Committee.

Prior to law school, Ms. Bethel obtained her bachelor’s in international relations from American University in Washington, DC. She spent a year of college abroad in India on a Boren Scholarship from the National Security Education Program. She had the opportunity to conduct field research on sex trafficking with an HIV/AIDS prevention NGO. She also took master’s level courses with Manipal University’s geopolitics department.

Ms. Bethel originally hails from Garland, Texas. She graduated with an International Baccalaureate diploma from Garland High School and is a very proud Garland Owl.

Ms. Bethel is licensed to practice in Texas and Washington, DC. She is also admitted to practice in the federal district courts in the Northern and Eastern Districts of Texas and in Washington, DC.

attorneys.name: Curtis Bickers
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Curtis Bickers is a Board Certified Trial Lawyer in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization since 2010 and a proud member of The Alfred Firm’s trial team.

For over 18 years, Curtis has dedicated his career to advocating for individuals and families who have suffered life-altering injuries or the devastating loss of a loved one. His mission is rooted in compassion, integrity, and an unwavering commitment to securing justice for those in need.

A native Texan, Curtis was raised in Houston, Texas. He earned his undergraduate degree from Texas A&M University, where he was actively involved in the Corps of Cadets, holding several leadership positions. While in high school, Curtis achieved the prestigious rank of Eagle Scout in the Boy Scouts of America. He went on to earn his Juris Doctor degree from South Texas College of Law – Houston, where he was active in the school’s highly respected mock trial program.

Curtis began his legal career representing various Fortune 500 companies in product liability, employment, and mass tort litigation. Though successful, he soon realized that his true calling was standing up for individuals—not corporations. In 2007, Curtis shifted his focus exclusively to personal injury and wrongful death litigation, fighting for those harmed by the negligence of others.

Throughout his career, Curtis has obtained significant verdicts and settlements on behalf of clients in cases involving offshore injuries, 18-wheeler and commercial trucking collisions, dangerous and defective products, and other catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death matters. His courtroom presence is marked by skillful advocacy and a deep understanding of the physical, emotional, and financial toll his clients suffer from when faced life-altering injuries or the loss of a loved one.

For Curtis, the greatest honor isn’t just winning a case—it’s the relationships built along the way. Many of his former clients have stayed in touch over the years, calling to check in or simply express gratitude for how he helped change their lives for the better. Besides obtaining the certification of a Texas Board Certified Personal Injury trial lawyer, Curtis has been recognized by his peers as a Texas Rising Star from 2013 to 2015 and a Texas Super Lawyer from 2015 to 2025.

When he’s not advocating for his clients and their families, Curtis enjoys spending time with his family, supporting the Houston community, and continuing his lifelong commitment to service and leadership.

attorneys.name: Geoffrey S. Binney
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Practice Lawyers in Spring, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Binney is the Managing Partner of Gauntt, Koen, Binney & Kidd, L.L.P. He represents both plaintiffs and defendants and covers a wide variety of commercial and personal injury litigation matters, including contract disputes, Qui Tam lawsuits, automobile accidents, products liability, catastrophic construction-related accidents, premises liability, wrongful death, and litigation stemming from the purchase/sale of residential properties. A large percentage of Mr. Binney’s docket is comprised of home inspector errors and omissions defense cases. Mr. Binney, who represents home inspectors all over the country, does public speaking focusing on topics relating to home inspectors, specifically how they can best protect themselves from claims and litigation.

After graduation from West Point, Mr. Binney served as a lieutenant in the U.S. Army, after which he served in the FBI for eight years. As an FBI Special Agent, Mr. Binney initiated and led Operation Candyman, one of law enforcement’s largest investigations into online child pornography, resulting in over 100 convictions and the identification of dozens of victims. In that regard, he appeared on several local news stations, Wired Magazine and on Fox News, The O'Reilly Factor. As a Supervisory Special Agent, Mr. Binney created and staffed the Houston Area Cyber-Crime Task Force, supervised the computer forensic examination efforts of all Houston-FBI investigations including the Enron and Arthur Anderson investigations. He also oversaw all cyber-crime related investigations, including computer intrusions, online crimes against children, fraud, cyber-terrorism, and theft of intellectual property.

Mr. Binney is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, American Bar Association (Litigation Section), The Houston Bar Association, the Montgomery County Bar Association, The Woodlands Bar Association, and the West Point Society of Greater Houston. He is licensed to practice law in Texas as well as federal court in the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts of Texas. He is a member of St. Anthony’s Catholic Church. He and his wife Amy raised three sons in The Woodlands.

attorneys.name: George Scott Bishop
attorneys.practice_type: Energy Law Lawyers in Sweetwater, TX
attorneys.bio:
Scott joined the firm in 2020, after practicing energy law in Abilene, Texas from 1974 until he moved to San Antonio to be closer to family. Scott is now retired but prior to such retirement was Board Certified in Oil, Gas and Mineral Law (1997) and represented energy firms, mineral owners and landowners in a variety of matters, including, without limitation, negotiating and documenting purchases and sales of producing properties and mineral interests; drilling and division order title opinions; and obtaining court appointed Receivers to deliver oil and gas leases and leasehold interests.

He graduated from the University of Texas (B.B.A., 1968) and was commissioned a Second Lieutenant in the Marine Corps. Upon graduation from the University of Texas School of Law (J.D., 1970), he served in the Marines, last as a Special Court Martial Judge at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, until 1974 when he moved to Abilene to practice law.

In many instances, this allows clients to keep their legal costs in check.

attorneys.practice_type: Labor and Employment Lawyers in El Paso, TX
attorneys.bio:
Steven J. Blanco was born and raised in El Paso, Texas. He attended El Paso public schools and graduated from Eastwood High School in 1987. Mr. Blanco attended the University of Texas at El Paso where he received a Bachelor's Degree in Business Administration. Following his graduation from UTEP, Mr. Blanco attended law school at Baylor University where he graduated cum laude in 1996. At Baylor, he was a member of the Baylor Order of Barristers and served as Notes and Comments Editor and Assistant Executive Editor of the Baylor Law Review.

Mr. Blanco is licensed to practice law in both Texas and New Mexico. He was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 1996 and the State Bar of New Mexico in 1997.

Mr. Blanco is a shareholder and Chair of the Labor and Employment Practice Group at the Firm. He is Board Certified in Labor & Employment Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. His practice is focused on representing employers and local government entities in labor and employment law matters, including defense of wrongful discharge and discrimination claims, managing employee relations, representing employers before state and federal agencies and related employment law matters. Mr. Blanco is a member of the State Bar of Texas Labor and Employment Law Section, the El Paso and American Bar Associations and the El Paso Society for Human Resource Management. Mr. Blanco currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Workforce Solutions Borderplex Workforce Development Board and is a former member of the Board of Directors of the American Lung Association of Texas. He is the past president for the American Lung Association of Texas Western Region Advisory Board, and past chairman of the Legislative Committee for the El Paso Society for Human Resource Management.

Mr. Blanco is a frequent author and speaker on labor and employment law topics for both regional and national human resource management training companies. He has authored articles for the State Bar of Texas Advanced Employment Law Course and the Texas Labor Letter. Mr. Blanco has served as a faculty member for the Human Resources Management: PHR/SPHR Review Course presented by the University of Texas at El Paso Division of Professional and Continuing Education.

In 2007 and 2008, Mr. Blanco was named a Texas "Rising Star" by the publishers of Texas Monthly and Law & Politics magazines. "Rising Stars" are considered among the best in their profession. Those receiving the honor represent the top 2.5% of up and coming Texas lawyers who are 40 years of age and younger or have practiced law less than 10 years. The Texas "Rising Stars" were selected from the results of an extensive nomination and polling process conducted by Law & Politics and published in the Texas Monthly and the Rising Stars edition of Texas Super Lawyers magazine. Since 2009 and through 2016, he has been selected for inclusion in the Texas Super Lawyers list published in Texas Monthly Magazine.

He is a member of the Texas Council of School Attorneys, the National School Boards Association Council of School Attorneys and is a Graduate of Leadership El Paso, Silver Anniversary Class of 2003.

Mr. Blanco practices in the Firm's Labor & Employment, Litigation and Local Government & School Law Practice Groups.

attorneys.name: John C. Blazier
attorneys.practice_type: Business Formation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
John C. Blazier founded Blazier, Rutland & Lerner, P.C. in 1976, and has remained the president of the Firm, now Blazier, Christensen, Browder & Virr, P.C. Blessed with an active business practice, Mr. Blazier is keenly aware of the tax implications of various business transactions. He serves as corporate counsel for a number of mid-sized companies, handling numerous complex corporate matters, from acquisitions and restructuring, to employment law issues. He acknowledges he is a teacher, striving to help clients understand the tax implications in their planning process, whether in personal estate planning or the corporate setting.

Mr. Blazier earned his B.A. degrees at the University of Texas at El Paso in 1966, then attended the University of Texas School of Law, where he was editor-in-chief of the Law Forum and was published in the Texas Law Review. He received his J.D. and was admitted to the Texas Bar in 1969. He is also licensed to practice before the U.S. district Courts of the western, Eastern, and Southern Districts of Texas, as well as the U.S. Tax Court.

Following law school, Mr. Blazier entered the U.S. military, serving in Vietnam. He was awarded the Bronze Star on two occasions, as well as a Military Service Medal. Upon return from active duty, he served in the Texas National Guard, attaining the rank of Lt. Colonel, and was employed by the IRS Estate and Gift Tax Division, Austin, District. Here he gained significant insight into complex tax matters and business valuation. Using his GI Bill, he then attended New York University School of Law, where he completed his L.L.M. in taxation.

Mr. Blazier is an active member of the American Bar Association and the Travis County Bar Association. He is a passionate leader in the Austin community for systemic change in public education. He is the founder of the Seedling Foundation, which provides mentors for children of incarcerated parents and works with the Austin Independent School District for campus beautification. He has served as Chair of Austin Partners in Education (2002-2003), and helped implement a number of initiatives, such as seeking logistical technology support from governmental entities and private businesses for high schools and middle schools in AISD. More recently John, along with Fleur Christensen, has worked to help build school to career pathways and facilities, such as the Institute of Hospitality and Culinary Arts at Travis High School, Auto Collision and Repair at Crockett High School, and the Kocurek Health Science Institute at Lanier High School.

Mr. Blazier has been recognized for his commitment to children with the award of Five Who Care, Partner of the Year with the Travis Education Foundation in 2001, and an elementary school named after him.

Alison Bloom is an experienced attorney whose practice focuses on business transactions, estate planning & probate, and optimization of business structures for tax and business law. attorneys.name: Emily Klair Bloom
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Criminal Defense Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Emily Klair Bloom is a litigation associate who mainly focuses on white collar criminal defense, government & regulatory investigations, and commercial & securities litigation.

Emily Klair worked at the North Hill Country Public Defender’s Office before she joined Ford O’Brien Landy in 2024. She began at the Public Defender’s Office a student attorney during her last semester of law school; during that time, Emily Klair represented juvenile clients in detention hearings, pre-trial hearings and negotiations, and in pleadings. Emily Klair also managed a full caseload of adult criminal defendants charged with misdemeanor offenses and state jail felonies. In May 2023, Emily Klair was the second-chair attorney for a second-degree felony jury trial where she cross-examined witnesses and prepared for the sentencing trial. In November 2022, Emily Klair was the first-chair attorney for post-adjudication hearing in a juvenile case in state district court. During that hearing, she gave an opening statement, proffered legal arguments to the judge, cross examined 6 witnesses, and gave a compelling closing argument for her client. And two months prior to that hearing, in September 2022, Emily Klair was the second-chair attorney for a jury trial on a four-count indictment of first- and second-degree felony charges. During that trial, Emily Klair cross-examined witnesses, prepared the full case-in-chief for sentencing, and worked closely with the client and his family to educate them about the criminal judicial system and its processes.

While in law school, Emily Klair was a student attorney for the Criminal Defense Clinic where she represented individuals in Travis County charged with misdemeanor offenses. She was a student attorney for the Capital Punishment Clinic and interned at the Office of Capital and Forensic Writs, supporting capital defense attorneys in their fight against the death penalty. Emily Klair volunteered her spare time in law school to the Mithoff Pro Bono program at the William Wayne Justice Center, contributing more than 1,000 hours to pro bono projects while a student at the school. One project in particular led to a woman’s release on parole after 14 years of injustice in the state prison.

Before law school, Emily Klair worked as a legislative intern for Texas Senate District 1 during the 86th Legislative Session. She is a graduate of the University of Texas at Tyler.

Outside of work, Emily Klair enjoys reading mysteries, practicing yoga, and spending time with her husband and their 4 dogs.

attorneys.name: Caj Boatright
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
When everything is on the line, you need a lawyer who never backs down from a challenge. Caj will not, and he has proved it time and again. Caj’s relentless work has resulted in hundreds of millions of dollars of jury verdicts and settlements for people suffering from the worst times of their lives.

Just a small sample of the recent results Caj has obtained as lead trial counsel is staggering:

$78,000,000 settlement for injured west Texas oil field worker

$18,750,000 settlement for Louisiana man burned in a pipeline explosion

$18,000,000 jury verdict for a south Texas family injured in a shopping center

$12,500,000 settlement for a Mississippi man injured on an offshore oil rig

$12,000,000 settlement for a Louisiana boat captain injured on the job

$11,000,000 judgment for a businessman wronged when a company breached its contract with him

$10,000,000 settlement for an injured child

$10,000,000 settlement for a family who lost its husband, dad, and sole income provider in a truck accident

$9,100,000 jury verdict for an injured oilfield worker

$9,000,000 settlement for an injured oil field worker in Texas

Caj’s success for his clients stems from the case preparation at Arnold & Itkin:

Unmatched preparation – we will not be outworked

Dedication – we will do everything we can to get each client the maximum recovery

Unrivaled resources – we will put everything into winning our cases

Refusal to back down – We will go toe-to-toe with the biggest companies in the world, and we will win

Endurance – we will treat and prepare every case as if it is going to trial

That formula rests on Caj’s strong sense of justice and his belief that the American jury system is the best way to help people get what they deserve when it matters the most. He does his best to make sure his clients receive maximum compensation when companies refuse to take responsibility for their wrongful conduct.

One of Caj’s greatest strengths is his vast and diverse experience. He spent four years practicing complex commercial litigation and appellate law at one of Texas’s largest and most well-respected firms. He also had the honor of serving as a law clerk for the Honorable Reynaldo Garza on the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. Additionally, Caj spent five years handling high stakes litigation for ExxonMobil, overseeing the company’s largest cases in various states with tens of billions of dollars in exposure. And on top of that, most of his career has unfolded in the courtroom, representing injured clients who have no option but to win. It is unlikely that there is a lawyer in the country with a more well-rounded and accomplished resume.

Caj grew up in the small west Texas town of Sweetwater. He attended Southwestern University in Georgetown, Texas where he graduated cum laude with honors. Caj then got his law degree from the University of Texas with Kurt Arnold and Jason Itkin. Caj was the first lawyer to join Arnold & Itkin after the firm was founded in 2004.

When he is not in the courtroom, Caj is with his wife Jodi and his three kids at a sporting event, or outdoors at their west Texas ranch or at their home in Park City, Utah. Caj and Jodi are members at Kingwood United Methodist Church and volunteer for Young Life.

attorneys.name: JB Bobbitt
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
I have built a strong interest and background working with families dealing with non-traditional custody issues for over a decade in the city of Houston. I have extensive experience with adoptions and suits affecting the parent-child relationship where child safety is at risk. I have seen, too often, children needing an extended family member or loved one to take legal action when the parents are unable to provide a safe and stable environment. I am trained in TBRI or Trust Based Relational Intervention from the Karen Purvis Institute.

As a father of two daughters, I understand the constant challenges we have as parents. I have experienced a separation and a divorce and understand the hardship that lies beneath the legal process. As your attorney, you can expect empathy, understanding and I will work to give you a clear and realistic path toward resolving your case. attorneys.name: Robert J. Bogdanowicz III
attorneys.practice_type: Business Disputes Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rob is the "go to" lawyer for his clients when a dispute arises, no matter the issue. He is a trial lawyer who routinely appears on both sides of the docket, whether his client is a giant, multi-billion-dollar company or an individual seeking justice.

Rob's peers have recognized his commitment to excellence; he has been recognized by Super Lawyers®, a Thomson Reuters publication, every single year since 2012. For ten consecutive years, he was honored as a “Texas Rising Star” (2012 – 2022). Selection to this list is a distinction limited to no more than 2.5% of all lawyers in Texas. From 2017 – 2022, Rob was distinguished further as one of the "Up-and-Coming Top 100 Rising Stars", a select list of only 100 attorneys in the state. Since 2022, Rob has been named a Texas Super Lawyer. Rob also has been honored as one of the "Best Lawyers in Dallas" by D Magazine five times, as one of their “Best Lawyers in Dallas Under 40” twice, and has been rated as "AV Preeminent" by Martindale-Hubbell since 2022, which reflects that he has reached the highest levels of professional excellence, skill, and integrity.

Rob has tried lawsuits in state courts, federal courts, before regulatory tribunals, and before arbitration panels for both plaintiffs and defendants. He has gone toe-to-toe against some of the most accomplished and revered trial attorneys in the country, emerging victorious. That said, his successes are not limited to courtroom victories alone; in 2013, Rob obtained one of the top ten reported settlements in Texas according to VerdictSearch in a complex construction defect lawsuit. Over the past 15+ years of practice, he has obtained multi-million dollar settlements for plaintiffs and, on the other hand, also has secured take-nothing or complete defense verdicts for defense clients.

Rob's longstanding clients span across a number of industries, including international manufacturing companies, retailers, financial institutions, contractors, healthcare providers and organizations, software developers, consulting firms, and more. He is often called on to assess risk and negotiate matters in an effort to avoid litigation. When that is not feasible, he fiercely advocates for his clients in his "second home"--the courtroom.

A New York native, Rob made his way to Texas after graduating from Rutgers University in New Jersey to attend Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law, where he earned Dean's List honors and was one of only ten graduates named to the Order of Barristers, a prestigious honor society recognizing outstanding advocacy skills.

attorneys.name: E. Michelle Bohreer
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law – Employer Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
There isn’t much of anything I’d rather be doing than picking a jury or delivering an opening statement. I have represented clients in numerous jury and non-jury trials, which have involved a wide variety of legal issues, including self-insured workplace injury defense, discrimination, whistleblower, retaliatory discharge, securities fraud, usury, non-compete agreements, mineral lease enforcement, contract disputes, business fraud, and tortious interference, just to name a few.

Responsive, Zealous Advocacy, & Resourceful

As a trial lawyer, I routinely see what can go wrong with a client’s business, and for this reason I am uniquely positioned to help clients prevent business and employment disputes by anticipating them and by being proactive. As a certified public accountant who at one time practiced public accounting for a Big Eight accounting firm, I also understand the practical and financial aspects of disputes. In my practice, I assist clients with hiring and termination matters, developing and implementing appropriate employment policies and procedures, and responding to EEOC charges and Department of Labor or Texas Workforce Commission wage audits. I also offer training programs designed to assist my clients in meeting the ongoing challenges associated with federal and state employment laws, which continue to present a moving target. I frequently provide advice to client entities who are in the process of restructuring their business, and I have conducted due diligence investigations in connection with a nationwide roll-up of staffing companies, as well as strategic mergers and initial public offerings of staff leasing and PEO companies.

Each year since 2004, Michelle has been recognized by her peers as a “Texas Super Lawyer” in Law and Politics Magazine and Texas Monthly. She has also received the top rating from the preeminent attorney rating service of Martindale-Hubbell, identifying her with the highest ethical standards and professional ability.

Philanthropy

For many years, I have been actively involved with Rotary, serving as President of the largest Rotary club in our area (2008-2010) and serving as an Assistant District Governor for 2 years (2010-2012). I was named Rotarian of the year in 2013. In 2006, I was the chairman, in fact, the first woman chairman, of the 37th Annual Rotary Lombardi Award, which honors the outstanding college lineman of the year, while raising significant monies for cancer research. I am excited to be a member of the Rotary Club of Houston Skyline, with a commitment to bringing Rotary’s presence and preeminence back into downtown Houston. In 2021-2022, I will have the privilege of serving as District Governor for Rotary International District 5890.

I also serve as Chair of the Board of Directors of National Senior Campuses, Inc., which has Continuing Care Retirement Communities across the country and leads the industry by providing an exceptional lifestyle for more than 25,000 active seniors.

attorneys.bio:
Caitlin, a native of Manhattan, New York, brings the distinctive style and commanding presence of her hometown to her legal practice at Coldwell Bowes.

After receiving her Bachelor’s Degree with honors in Psychology and Sociology from the University of Michigan, Caitlin began her career as a paralegal in Manhattan. Caitlin then moved to Austin, Texas, to attend the University of Texas School of Law. During her time at UT Law, Caitlin dedicated her efforts to the Domestic Violence Clinic, where she served as first chair in family law trials and gained a solid foundation in the intricacies of family law issues.

Prior to joining Coldwell Bowes, Caitlin worked as a Law Clerk at another prominent family law firm while completing her juris doctorate. During this time, she became familiar with the exceptional trial skills and courtroom prowess of the attorneys at Coldwell Bowes and aspired to join their firm. Caitlin joined Coldwell Bowes in August of 2023.

Caitlin is able to continually achieve favorable results for her clients in part due to her clear and consistent communication with clients and un-yielding tenacity.

Outside the office, Caitlin is an avid animal lover, often accompanied by her loyal dog, Bandit.

attorneys.bio:
Troy D. Bolen is an associate attorney at Bollier Ciccone Stinson LLP. He focuses his practice on construction litigation and real estate law.

With a strategic legal mind and extensive experience, Troy brings a proven track record of crafting and executing successful legal approaches to achieve favorable client outcomes.

Troy earned his J.D. from South Texas College of Law Houston and his Bachelor of Arts in Economics with a minor in History from the University of Texas at Austin. He is licensed to practice law in Texas and Colorado.

Prior to joining Bollier Ciccone Stinson LLP, Troy honed his skills at several prestigious law firms, where he was intensively involved in cases involving construction defects, real estate transactions, and commercial litigation.

Troy also founded and managed his own practice, The Law Offices of Troy D. Bolen, P.L.L.C., specializing in construction defect litigation, real estate law, and commercial litigation. His experience extends to his time at The Fowler Law Firm, P.C., where he led a team of attorneys in developing and executing complex legal initiatives.

Troy is committed to giving back to his community. He currently serves on the Advisory Council for Hill Country Pop Warner and is an Approved Foster Parent for Gold Ribbon Rescue, Inc.

She is known for establishing a close rapport with her clients by guiding them through the family law process and delivering the best outcome achievable for them and their children. Leslie understands the unique challenges clients face in family law matters and is dedicated to delivering the highest level of legal representation.

attorneys.name: Ruby Bolton Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ruby Bolton is the founding attorney of The Bolton Law Firm and a trusted advocate for families navigating life’s most challenging transitions. With over 25 years of experience in family law, Ruby has built a reputation for excellence by blending deep expertise with genuine compassion.

Expertise and Credentials

Ruby’s credentials reflect her dedication to excellence in family law. Her extensive expertise is highlighted by:

Board Certification: Board certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization.

Top-Tier Recognition: Recognized as a Super Lawyer, placing her among the top 5% of family law attorneys.

Professional Leadership:

Member of the Legislative Review Committee for the Texas Bar Association.

Member of the Professionalism Committee of the State Bar of Texas.

Specialized Practice Areas: Handling complex cases including high-asset, military, and same-sex divorces, as well as child custody, property division, adoption, and probate matters.

Community Involvement: Active board member of the Woodlands Bar Association and an engaged local community volunteer.

A Personal Commitment to Family Law

Ruby’s journey into family law began following her own divorce, an experience that gave her a deep understanding of the complexities families face during transitional periods. This personal insight drives her empathetic approach, ensuring that every client receives personalized guidance and support through challenging times.

A Life Rooted in Community and Family

Beyond her legal accomplishments, Ruby is a devoted mother of five. With four of her children currently in graduate school and one successfully running a wedding photography business, she understands the importance of strong family bonds. Her passion for children and community extends to her active participation in local organizations, reinforcing her commitment to making a positive impact both professionally and personally.

Educational Foundation and Professional Involvement

Ruby’s academic achievements and professional involvement lay the foundation for her distinguished career:

Education:

J.D. from the University of Texas at Austin.

B.A. in English from Brigham Young University.

Professional Associations: Active member of multiple legal organizations, reinforcing her role as a thought leader in family law.

At The Bolton Law Firm, Ruby Bolton combines her extensive legal experience with a heartfelt commitment to guiding families towards a better future. Her blend of authority, empathy, and community spirit makes her a formidable advocate for families throughout The Woodlands, Tomball, and across Texas.

attorneys.name: Douglas A. Booth
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Douglas A. Booth, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate (Residential, Commercial) Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Since 1997, Douglas A. Booth has been providing clients with the personal service and attention to detail that can be hard to find at larger firms. Prior to joining Sneed, Vine & Perry, P.C., Mr. Booth was shareholder and president of the Law Offices of Douglas A. Booth, P.C. where he practiced for 20 years.

Mr. Booth is board-certified in both residential and commercial real estate law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, and handles all types of real estate transactions -- both large and small -- including purchase and sale, and development and financing.

Mr. Booth also handles the purchase and sale of closely-held companies and has a wealth of experience in the areas of estate planning, probate of estates, business formation and business law.

Mr. Booth received a B.A. in Philosophy (High Honors; Phi Beta Kappa) from The University of Texas at Austin in 1989, and a J.D. from The University of Texas School of Law in 1992, where his is a regular guest lecturer.

He lives in central Austin with his wife and college sweetheart, Cybele, a public relations professional, and their two sons, Harry and Teague. A Texan since before he could walk, Mr. Booth runs, cycles, lifts weights and enjoys live music, barbecue, cold beer, hunting, fishing, paddling, hiking, long motorcycle trips and just about everything else outdoors.

attorneys.name: Jacob Boswell
attorneys.practice_type: • Catastrophic Personal Injury Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jacob Boswell is an experienced personal injury litigator. He has broad experience in handling cases involving commercial and personal vehicle accidents, wrongful deaths and property damage. After spending years defending truck drivers and motorists for numerous insurance companies, Jacob brings his knowledge of the intricacies of insurance litigation to Cherry Johnson Siegmund and James to help the injured seek compensation from those insurance companies. With experience on both sides of these cases, Jacob is able to assess the strengths and weaknesses of his cases in order to secure favorable settlements and verdicts for his clients.

Biography

Jacob Boswell has handled a variety of litigation ranging from consumer protection cases and family law matters including divorce and child custody battles, to business litigation, business receiverships and building contractor disputes. However, Jacob now specializes in personal injury claims involving 18-wheeler accidents, catastrophic injuries and wrongful deaths. He has spent years working for the insurance companies so he could learn how they evaluate claims and make settlement determinations. This insider knowledge gives Jacob an edge in handling these cases that many attorneys do not have. Jacob now uses this knowledge to zealously represent his clients in seeking rightful compensation from these companies.

Jacob has been recognized by his colleagues as a Texas Super Lawyer and Texas Rising Star and by numerous other organizations as a top attorney in his field. He has interned for a district court judge, served as a guardian ad litem representing minors in injury cases, argued cases in all four federal district courts in Texas and has written briefs for the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals and federal bankruptcy court as well as to the Texas Supreme Court.

Jacob played NCAA Division II basketball at Harding University before graduating summa cum laude from the University of Texas at Dallas. He attended the Dedman School of Law at Southern Methodist University where he participated in numerous mock trial competitions across the country. Jacob is an Eagle Scout. He is a native of Dallas and lives there with his wife. Jacob enjoys international travel, listening to books on Audible while walking his dogs and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Sarah Botros
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Botros is an partner at Key Law Office. Her primary practice area is family law.

Sarah grew up in Houston, Texas, and lived in Norway and Dubai during her childhood. She attended the University of Texas at Austin where she majored in French as an undergraduate and obtained a certificate in Business Foundations. After graduating, Sarah worked at an immigration law firm in Houston, Texas, and later attended the University of Texas at Austin School of Law. After law school, Sarah worked as an Assistant Attorney General in the child support division of the Office of the Attorney General for many years where she gained extensive experience establishing, modifying, and enforcing child support obligations. Her time spent prosecuting child support cases gives Sarah unique insight into litigating child support issues. Sarah has practiced family law in and around central Texas, including in Travis County, Hays County, Williamson County, Bastrop County, and Caldwell County, and has a deep knowledge of the practices and procedures of the various court systems.

Sarah is fluent in Arabic and French and in her free time, she enjoys reading, running, and baking overly complicated desserts.

attorneys.name: David Bouschor II
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of David S. Bouschor, II, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denton, TX
attorneys.bio:
David S. Bouschor, II is a 1991 graduate of the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law. Mr. Bouschor was a sole practitioner and a shareholder in a previous law firm until January 2000 when he opened The Law Office of David S. Bouschor, II, P.C. in Denton, Texas. For over twenty-eight years, Mr. Bouschor’s legal practice has consisted of Family Law, Guardianship and Probate.

Since 1995 Mr. Bouschor has been Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization - a certification awarded to lawyers who have proven specialized knowledge of state laws, codes and who have tested experience in the trials and appeals of Family Law cases. He is also a member of the College of the State Bar of Texas and MENSA.

Prior to becoming an attorney, David S. Bouschor, II received his Bachelor of Science in Geology from the University of Wisconsin-Superior in 1980. This led him to work in the oil industry for several years. He has also owned a rescue and salvage diving business.

Mr. Bouschor prides himself on the highly individualized, quality service he can offer his clients as a firm structured to provide small firm client attention with large firm resources. Mr. Bouschor and his legal team work one-on-one with his clients to get to know their full legal and personal situation, assess the client’s legal issues, and help them craft the best approach to dealing with the legal matter at hand. He is a firm believer in dispute resolution through negotiation. However, when negotiation fails, he has proven himself to be a skilled litigator.

Notable Achievements

Mr. Bouschor has spent significant time training other professionals on Guardianships and the Collaborative Divorce process. He has shared his expertise with statewide, national, and international audiences. Other significant accomplishments include:

Founder and current President and the Denton County Alternative Dispute Resolution Program (DCAP), the non-profit organization that supports the community by offering low-cost mediations to resolve disputes, saving money, and lessening the caseload at the courthouse. In addition, Mr. Bouschor annually serves dozens of hours as a mediator for DCAP Pro Bono.

Founder of the Denton County Bar Family Lawyers Section in 2001

Selected to Super Lawyers (awarded by Thomson Reuters) from 2011- Present

Accepted to and attended Harvard “Project on Negotiation: Deal Design and Implementation” by the Harvard Business School and Law School in 2010

As a fourth generation attendee, he received his Juris Doctorate from Washburn University in May 2002. While at Washburn University Brent was a member and competed as an oralist in the Moot Court Competition held at Fordham Law school.

Brent is a well rounded and experienced attorney beginning his career practicing as a third year bar card attorney for Shawnee County District Attorney's Office handling bench and jury trials. Brent has held past positions in the Johnson County Attorney's Office as an Assistant County Attorney, Denton County District Attorney's Office as an Assistant District Attorney, Jackson & Hagen as an associate attorney, Bowen & Lloyd, PLLC, as partner. In 2008, Brent joined his wife in practice and formed Bowen Law Group in which he is the managing partner.

Brent has been involved with numerous cases that received media attention. He has appeared on Channel 11 in the controversial Sanger ISD SEXTING case which was featured on Good Morning America. Brent has been quoted in the Texas Lawyer Magazine regarding discovery policies and has received media attention for a Pilot Point DWI case involving an assistant coach.

attorneys.name: Allison Bowers
attorneys.practice_type: Fintech Consumer Disputes Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
In the words of her peers, Allison Bowers "represents the very best of the legal profession - smart, honest, caring, and extremely capable." Born and raised in a small Texas town, Allison's approach to law reflects her grounded, practical roots. Allison is a frequent speaker and has been named to the Best Lawyers and Texas Super Lawyer lists.

Allison practiced as a commercial litigator with Baker Botts LLP for over ten years before co-founding Hutcheson Bowers LLLP in 2011. Currently, her practice focuses on consumer disputes for financial technology companies and advising employers on various aspects of employment law.

Allison oversees the management of a national arbitration and litigation docket of consumer disputes for one of the country's largest digital banks. Since 2015, together with her partner Shannon Hutcheson, Allison has been at the forefront of defending fintechs and banks in consumer litigation over violations of the Electronic Funds Transfer Act. Allison and her firm represent some of the leaders in the fintech industry including a pioneer in the prepaid debit industry, several of the top leading digital banks in the country, and the inventor of the credit builder account as well as the issuing banks that partner with our fintech clients.

Allison also maintains her employment law practice, which she's had since 2000. Allison's sensible and sympathetic perspective make her especially sought after as a workplace investigator and counselor on difficult employee management issues. Allison has several clients she's represented for decades.

After busy days at work, Allison enjoys peacefully tending to her orchids, some of which she's had for over 10 years. Her oldest plant, a philodendron, is over 30 years old and has survived being dug up and hauled all over Austin. Her husband and teenage daughter often try to interrupt her, but she's learned to tune them out. Allison was born a Longhorn and has been to many momentous sporting events in her lifetime, including the 2005 Rose Bowl when Texas won the national championship, also known as the greatest college football game of all time.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
In the words of her peers, Allison Bowers "represents the very best of the legal profession - smart, honest, caring, and extremely capable." Born and raised in a small Texas town, Allison's approach to law reflects her grounded, practical roots. Allison is a frequent speaker and has been named to the Best Lawyers and Texas Super Lawyer lists.

Allison practiced as a commercial litigator with Baker Botts LLP for over ten years before co-founding Hutcheson Bowers LLLP in 2011. Currently, her practice focuses on consumer disputes for financial technology companies and advising employers on various aspects of employment law.

Allison oversees the management of a national arbitration and litigation docket of consumer disputes for one of the country's largest digital banks. Since 2015, together with her partner Shannon Hutcheson, Allison has been at the forefront of defending fintechs and banks in consumer litigation over violations of the Electronic Funds Transfer Act. Allison and her firm represent some of the leaders in the fintech industry including a pioneer in the prepaid debit industry, several of the top leading digital banks in the country, and the inventor of the credit builder account as well as the issuing banks that partner with our fintech clients.

Allison also maintains her employment law practice, which she's had since 2000. Allison's sensible and sympathetic perspective make her especially sought after as a workplace investigator and counselor on difficult employee management issues. Allison has several clients she's represented for decades.

After busy days at work, Allison enjoys peacefully tending to her orchids, some of which she's had for over 10 years. Her oldest plant, a philodendron, is over 30 years old and has survived being dug up and hauled all over Austin. Her husband and teenage daughter often try to interrupt her, but she's learned to tune them out. Allison was born a Longhorn and has been to many momentous sporting events in her lifetime, including the 2005 Rose Bowl when Texas won the national championship, also known as the greatest college football game of all time.

Andrew Bowman was born in Humble, Texas. Growing up in a military family, Andrew and his siblings knew they would serve at one point. After High School, Andrew joined the U.S. Navy as a Hospital Corpsman. For the next five years, he served in places such as Guam, Connecticut, and Maryland.

Once his service was over, Andrew attended Texas A&M University. After graduating in 2018, Andrew began to work at Arnold & Itkin, where he quickly became enamored by the legal profession and the potential to help people who need it most. While not at work, Andrew enjoys spending time and traveling with his wife and two sons. As an Aggie, Andrew avidly supports Texas A&M athletics and attends as many sporting events as possible.

attorneys.name: Leslie J. Boykin
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Leslie J. Boykin, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Leslie J. Boykin started her law firm in the Summer of 2005, less than nine months after being licensed by the State of Texas to practice law. She has always intended on being a Criminal Defense attorney, since she was a teenager, growing up in East Texas. Born and raised in a family who treasured the right to vote, and used it, gave her a close look at Government and the way it worked.

She pursued Government studies at the University of Texas at Austin and moved here two days after graduating high school. But she soon realized her calling would be better fulfilled with a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice, and she obtained that in 1999 from Sam Houston State University, in Huntsville, Texas. Then she went on to obtain her Juris Doctorate from South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas.

For over fifteen years now, Leslie Boykin has served clients in the Austin/Travis County community, as well as in surrounding counties. She believes in the 6th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, that, among other things, all accused Defendants in criminal cases have the right to representation, and therefore still accepts some court-appointed cases in which she assists indigent clients (Travis County only). It was by taking these appointments, as a young, solo defense attorney, that she gained trial experience in several different areas of criminal defense. She also became one of the defense attorneys in the first-ever Travis County Mental Health Special Reduction Docket (Mental Health Court), and after ten years of taking those appointments, she’s gained more knowledge than the average defense attorney, on how to represent, treat and assist clients who have one or more mental health diagnoses.

After all this time, with thousands of clients represented and both jury and bench trials won, clients continue to be pleased with her representation, and she enjoys guiding them in the right direction so that they may better their own lives.

Leslie spent over eight years, during her college years, working in the service industry (Restaurants and bars), so she understands the heart of what customer service is – making the client feel comfortable, and listening to what they want and expect. She strives hard to give them the care and attention they deserve, and to keep them informed at every stage of the case’s progression. Her Paralegal keeps the lines of communication flowing while she is in court each day.

Standing between the Accused and the Government, while defending the Constitution, is a dream come true for Leslie. Our law office guarantees representation by an attorney with the highest ethical standards, who charges reasonable fees for services provided, and who is available to clients as needed. Leslie Boykin works with the intention of obtaining the fairest, most just and reasonable disposition for her clients. She is licensed to practice in all State courts, as well as in the Western District of the United States Federal District Court. She has also completed the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA)/International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) Standardized Field Sobriety Testing Program (SFST) Instructor Course (2015 curriculum).

Then she went on to obtain her Juris Doctorate from South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas.

For over fifteen years now, Leslie Boykin has served clients in the Austin/Travis County community, as well as in surrounding counties. She believes in the 6th Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, that, among other things, all accused Defendants in criminal cases have the right to representation, and therefore still accepts some court-appointed cases in which she assists indigent clients (Travis County only). It was by taking these appointments, as a young, solo defense attorney, that she gained trial experience in several different areas of criminal defense. She also became one of the defense attorneys in the first-ever Travis County Mental Health Special Reduction Docket (Mental Health Court), and after ten years of taking those appointments, she’s gained more knowledge than the average defense attorney, on how to represent, treat and assist clients who have one or more mental health diagnoses.

After all this time, with thousands of clients represented and both jury and bench trials won, clients continue to be pleased with her representation, and she enjoys guiding them in the right direction so that they may better their own lives.

Leslie spent over eight years, during her college years, working in the service industry (Restaurants and bars), so she understands the heart of what customer service is – making the client feel comfortable, and listening to what they want and expect. She strives hard to give them the care and attention they deserve, and to keep them informed at every stage of the case’s progression. Her Paralegal keeps the lines of communication flowing while she is in court each day.

Standing between the Accused and the Government, while defending the Constitution, is a dream come true for Leslie. Our law office guarantees representation by an attorney with the highest ethical standards, who charges reasonable fees for services provided, and who is available to clients as needed. Leslie Boykin works with the intention of obtaining the fairest, most just and reasonable disposition for her clients. She is licensed to practice in all State courts, as well as in the Western District of the United States Federal District Court. She has also completed the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA)/International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) Standardized Field Sobriety Testing Program (SFST) Instructor Course (2015 curriculum).

Evan has been a practicing trial attorney since 2015, bringing nearly a decade of legal experience to our firm. His career began with an invaluable foundation as an Assistant District Attorney with the Harris County District Attorney’s Office, where he gained extensive courtroom experience and honed his litigation skills. This role provided Evan with a strong understanding of the complexities of legal proceedings, which now serves his clients well in family law cases.

Before joining Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers, Evan served as AVDA’s dedicated Sexual Assault attorney, a role where he demonstrated his commitment to justice and advocacy. In this capacity, he prosecuted protective orders and provided legal representation to survivors of sexual assault in family law matters across Harris, Brazoria, and Fort Bend Counties. This experience has given Evan a deep empathy for clients navigating sensitive and emotionally charged situations, such as divorce and custody disputes.

As a native Houstonian, Evan’s ties to the community are strong and personal. After completing his undergraduate degree in biology at Indiana University – Bloomington, Evan worked in pediatric cancer research at the renowned MD Anderson Cancer Center. His drive to make a difference led him to pursue a legal career, and he earned his law degree from South Texas College of Law Houston. While in law school, Evan excelled in the moot court and mock trial advocacy programs, showcasing his passion for trial work and his ability to represent clients effectively in court.

Evan now focuses his practice on family law, providing compassionate and results-driven representation for individuals navigating divorce, child custody, property division, and other family-related legal matters. His diverse professional background equips him with a unique perspective and the ability to approach each case with precision, dedication, and care. Outside of work, Evan enjoys spending time with his wife and two children in Houston, Texas, where he continues to serve the community he calls home.

attorneys.name: Lara Bracamonte Davila
attorneys.practice_type: Juvenile Lawyers in Rockwall, TX
attorneys.bio:
There are many people who don’t have the courage, strength, or knowledge of how to stand up for themselves. I strive to be the voice for the voiceless, whether that’s a teen in trouble, a woman in an abusive situation, a father struggling to gain parental rights, or any individual charged with a crime.

Over the last 10 years, I have earned a reputation among my legal peers (defense lawyers, trial lawyers, prosecutors, and judges), for being compassionate but tough. They know I am a determined proponent who communicates effectively with jurors and clients.

I have a thorough background in all aspects of family, criminal, civil, and juvenile law. I am a fierce debater, which makes me a resourceful advocate for my clients. I love the Law, the challenge of tough cases, and the immense satisfaction I gain in being the champion for my clients. I particularly enjoy partnering with my juvenile clients, as their guardians often don’t know how best to help them navigate the legal process.

I represent clients in all North Texas counties. My daily goal is to provide attentive, dependable, and trustworthy counsel and representation. At the end of the day, I want justice served.

If my client is not guilty, he or she deserves to be set free. If he or she is found guilty, it’s my job to ensure the punishment doesn’t exceed the crime. Just as my clients are held accountable, so we must hold police officers and the State accountable for staying within the Law.

attorneys.name: Jesse Branick
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Nederland, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jesse was a beloved and dedicated member of the community. He passed away on November 20, 2023. He was born on September 1, 1951, in Port Arthur, Texas. Jesse was known for his dedication to the law and his contributions as an attorney and public servant.

After completing his B.B.A. in marketing at Lamar University in 1973, Jesse went on to earn his Juris Doctorate Law Degree from South Texas College of Law. Upon graduating from law school, he joined Provost Sheldon and then Provost Umphrey in Beaumont, Texas. He opened his own law practice in Nederland in 1999 where he represented families in the areas of Wills/Probate, Real Estate, Personal Injury, Adoptions, and Business Law. Jesse's commitment to justice led him to serve as a city attorney for Nederland from 2009 until just before he passed. Additionally, he served as a prosecutor for the cities of Port Neches, Nederland, Groves, and Port Arthur. In recognition of his knowledge and capabilities within the legal field, Jesse also served as a magistrate judge in Jefferson County starting in 2007.

Jesse leaves behind a legacy that extends beyond his professional accomplishments. He deeply cherished his family and friends and will be dearly missed by all who had the privilege of knowing him.

Throughout his life, Jesse demonstrated unwavering dedication both personally and professionally. Throughout his career, Jesse was known for and looked forward to helping families through his true passion for adoption. His strong sense of morality and passion for justice were evident to all who crossed paths with him. While he will be profoundly missed by those who knew him best, Jesse Branick's memory will endure as a source of inspiration for generations to come.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Jesse was a beloved and dedicated member of the community. He passed away on November 20, 2023. He was born on September 1, 1951, in Port Arthur, Texas. Jesse was known for his dedication to the law and his contributions as an attorney and public servant.

After completing his B.B.A. in marketing at Lamar University in 1973, Jesse went on to earn his Juris Doctorate Law Degree from South Texas College of Law. Upon graduating from law school, he joined Provost Sheldon and then Provost Umphrey in Beaumont, Texas. He opened his own law practice in Nederland in 1999 where he represented families in the areas of Wills/Probate, Real Estate, Personal Injury, Adoptions, and Business Law. Jesse's commitment to justice led him to serve as a city attorney for Nederland from 2009 until just before he passed. Additionally, he served as a prosecutor for the cities of Port Neches, Nederland, Groves, and Port Arthur. In recognition of his knowledge and capabilities within the legal field, Jesse also served as a magistrate judge in Jefferson County starting in 2007.

Jesse leaves behind a legacy that extends beyond his professional accomplishments. He deeply cherished his family and friends and will be dearly missed by all who had the privilege of knowing him.

Throughout his life, Jesse demonstrated unwavering dedication both personally and professionally. Throughout his career, Jesse was known for and looked forward to helping families through his true passion for adoption. His strong sense of morality and passion for justice were evident to all who crossed paths with him. While he will be profoundly missed by those who knew him best, Jesse Branick's memory will endure as a source of inspiration for generations to come.

attorneys.name: Liz Branning
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
With over 25 years of experience, Liz is a highly skilled litigator known for delivering strategic and results-driven legal representation. She has represented a wide range of clients, from Fortune 500 companies to individuals facing life-altering personal injuries or navigating challenging divorces. Having worked on both sides of the docket, Liz understands that litigation is rarely the preferred option, but when it becomes necessary, clients need more than paperwork—they need a fierce advocate. Liz meets that need, combining creativity, determination, and hard work to guide clients through the complexities of litigation, both inside and outside the courtroom.

Throughout her career, Liz has built a reputation for achieving client-centered outcomes:

She has secured multiple divorce clients a disproportionate share of their marital estates (80% to 90%) in cases involving family violence, adultery, and substance abuse.

In partnership with JB, Liz protected a client’s immigration status by defeating a fraudulent annulment claim and helped a mother retain full custody of her child in a heated modification case.

Liz successfully obtained protective orders for victims of domestic violence, including a two-year order against a father for violence against his children.

She achieved a record-setting $577,206 discovery sanction in a federal case where a party failed to produce key documents in the case.

Liz secured multimillion-dollar settlements for families affected by defective baby products—spearheading a nationwide recall campaign with the CPSC and appearing on 20/20 for her advocacy work.

Liz played a pivotal role in overturning a $37 million verdict by exposing another party’s malfeasance in hiding critical evidence in the case.

Together, Liz and JB obtained a six-figure settlement for their client—a victim of childhood sexual abuse—against the psychiatrist who failed to report that abuse to the police in violation of Texas law.

Liz’s expertise also extends to non-compete litigation, products liability, and high-stakes business disputes, where she has consistently secured favorable outcomes, including full dismissals, injunctions, and substantial settlements. Liz’s commitment to her clients and her ability to deliver meaningful results make her a trusted advocate, ready to handle the most challenging cases with focus and determination.
