attorneys.name: Matt Breeland
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Matt Breeland was selected to the 2023 Super Lawyers list after being selected as a Super Lawyers® Rising Star in 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021. Only 2.5% of lawyers age 40 or under receive the prestigious Rising Star recognition, which is based on a multi-phase selection process that includes independent research, peer nominations and peer evaluations.

As lead trial counsel, Matt obtained one of the top 100 jury verdicts in the state of Texas in 2019. That verdict was also in the top 50 in Texas for cases involving motor vehicles.

After spending the first part of his career defending personal injury cases, Matt knows how the other side works. In that role, Matt gained a unique and highly valuable perspective on the litigation tactics employed by insurance companies against those who fall victim to another person's carelessness. In 2016, Matt had a calling to switch sides and begin Representing Texas Injury Victims. Since then he has worked exclusively as counsel to accident victims.

Matt is married to Austin Realtor Leslie Breeland, who is also an attorney. Matt and Leslie met in law school and now have two young children, a boy and a girl, and a pug named Jerome (who spends most of the day at Matt's feet or on his lap). The Breeland family helps keep Austin weird and fun. When he isn't zealously representing injured clients against giant insurance companies, Matt is usually goofing around with his family and friends, cooking or eating great food, watching live music and sports, binging a crime documentary series, or playing bad golf. Matt has completed a marathon without walking or stopping (just don't ask him how long it took him). Matt has also served as a film screener for the South By Southwest Film Festival.

attorneys.name: William A. Brewer III
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
William A. Brewer III is a founding partner of Brewer, Attorneys & Counselors. Since co-founding the firm in 1984, Mr. Brewer has earned a reputation as one of the most creative and successful lawyers in the United States practicing extensively in the field of complex commercial litigation.

Under Mr. Brewer's direction, Brewer Attorneys & Counselors specializes in assisting clients faced with matters that involve substantial financial or business exposure, cutting edge legal issues, or significant public policy questions. The practice is not confined to particular areas of law, but to the art of advocacy on behalf of its clients. As a result, Mr. Brewer and the firm have gained national attention for their handling of matters in a variety of fields, including commercial litigation, insurance, environmental law, antitrust, intellectual property, hospitality, securities and more. The firm is organized around a singular goal - to achieve consistently higher than expected outcomes for clients while managing their advocacy needs in all forums, including courts and arbitration centers, before regulatory bodies, and in legislative arenas.

In order to support the firm's global practice, Mr. Brewer pioneered the utilization of offshore professionals and paraprofessionals to reduce the costs associated with high-stakes litigation services. He has earned national acclaim for the firm's in-house Consulting Group, Investigation Unit, and Issues & Crisis Management practice group - all innovations that work in concert handling high-stakes advocacy.

Born and raised on Long Island, New York, Mr. Brewer received his bachelor of arts degree, cum laude, from St. John’s University in 1974, followed in 1977 by his juris doctorate, cum laude, from the Albany Law School of Union University. Thereafter, Mr. Brewer attended New York University School of Law where he received a master of laws in trade regulation in 1978. Mr. Brewer is admitted to practice in Texas and New York, as well as a number of federal district courts and the Courts of Appeal for the Second, Third, Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, Tenth, and Federal Circuits.

Mr. Brewer is annually recognized in Dallas and New York, and throughout the United States, as one of the top lawyers practicing in complex commercial litigation arena. In June 2024, Mr. Brewer was named "Litigator of the Week" by The American Lawyer after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled unanimously for his client in a case against a former New York state financial regulator.

Mr. Brewer is chairman of the Brewer Foundation and the Brewer Storefront, the firm's public interest law firm. Mr. Brewer is a founder of the Brewer Foundation Future Leaders Program (FLP), an academic and leadership development program that benefits students from Dallas Independent School District and FLP alumni in college. He is also founder and chairman of the Brewer Foundation/NYU International Public Policy Forum (IPPF), the first and only competition that gives high school students around the globe the opportunity to engage in written and oral debates on issues of public policy.

In recognition of his philanthropic efforts, he has received the President's Award from the Puerto Rican Bar Association, the "Communicator of the Year" award from the National Speech & Debate Association, and the "Hero for Children" award from the Texas State Board of Education, among many other awards. He serves on boards of Albany Law School and Paul Quinn College, and is a past board member of New York University. He is on the Board of Advisors of the Institute of Judicial Administration at the NYU School of Law.

attorneys.name: S. A. Hayden Briggle
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hayden Briggle, co-founder of Briggle & Polan, PLLC, is a trial lawyer with extensive experience protecting his clients’ rights before judges and juries all over Texas. Hayden is dedicated to obtaining the best possible results for his clients in the areas of personal injury, business litigation and criminal defense law. Hayden's passion lies in obtaining justice for those going through difficult times and who need help putting their lives back together.

Hayden was born and raised in Texas. After graduating from high school in Austin, Hayden attended The University of Texas where he earned his Bachelor’s degree in Plan II Honors and Spanish. Hayden then went on to earn his Masters in Professional Accounting and Law Degree from The University of Texas. During law school, Hayden was a member of the Texas Law Review. Upon graduating from law school, Hayden joined the esteemed law firm of Fulbright & Jaworski, L.L.P.

Hayden spent the first four years of his practice at Fulbright & Jaworski, L.L.P. At Fulbright & Jaworski, L.L.P, Hayden worked with the firm's litigation, health law and corporate departments on a wide variety of matters, including representing clients in complex disputes in state and federal court. Hayden further honed his trial skills at Fulbright & Jaworski, L.L.P. by serving in the dual role as a prosecutor for the City of Austin during his last year of practice with the firm. In this capacity, Hayden first chaired over 25 jury trials.

attorneys.bio:
Dean is a native of Southeast Texas who graduated from Lamar University with distinction. Dean left a successful corporate career to attend law school at the University of Tulsa where he graduated with honors. Dean returned to Jefferson County to establish his law practice, and since 1994 he has met the legal needs of individuals and businesses throughout Southeast Texas.

Dean has extensive civil trial experience as well as extensive experience with business, estate planning and real estate transactions. Dean has helped form hundreds of area businesses and represents several local businesses in their transactions and disputes.

On an individual level, Dean’s skills and experience make him an excellent choice for those with family, probate and real property issues. On a national level, Dean has been called to serve as Special Master in Chancery overseeing the allocation of over one billion dollars in aggregate settlements to thousands of claimants living throughout the United States. Dean’s clients are well served by his trial experience and his wide body of knowledge in a number of legal areas.

attorneys.name: Rhonda H. Brink
attorneys.practice_type: Trusts and Estates Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rhonda Brink specialized in estate and trust law and her practice addressed all aspects of family wealth management and disposition. Before Brink Bennett Pargaman Atkins & Sanchez PLLC, for many years, Rhonda was the supervising shareholder of the wealth transfer section of a major Austin law firm. She was admitted to the Texas Bar in 1974. Rhonda's education includes a Bachelor of Science degree in economics from Trinity University in 1971 and her J.D. from the University of Texas School of Law in 1974.

Rhonda is Board Certified in Estate Planning and Probate Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and was admitted as the first female Fellow in Texas of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel ("ACTEC"). Rhonda served as Past Chair and board member of the Estate Planning and Probate Section of the Austin Bar Association, Past President of the Central Texas Estate Planning Council, and Past President of Austin Lawyers Care (the initial Travis County pro bono legal services referral organization). Rhonda is a frequent speaker at State Bar of Texas Professional Development programs and spoke regularly in the past at ALI-ABA Estate Planning and Administration Programs around the nation. Rhonda has twice served on the faculty of the University of Miami, Heckerling Institute on Estate Planning, and served as Director of the 1999 State Bar of Texas Professional Development Program--Advanced Estate Planning Strategies Course in San Francisco. She has also presented at national ACTEC meetings on topics ranging from Non-Marital Status Issues in Estate Planning for Committed Couples (2012 Annual Meeting with co-speakers, Joshua S. Rubenstein, New York, NY, and Anne Wynne, Ikard Wynne, LLP, Austin, TX) and "Until Divorce Do Us Part" - the impact of divorce in estate planning (2014 Summer Meeting with co-speaker, Dennis Belcher, McGuire Woods, Richmond, Virginia).

attorneys.name: Cambry Bristow
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Georgetown, TX
attorneys.bio:
Cambry Bristow is an experienced trial lawyer who finds deep joy in connecting with others. She loves spending time with her clients, learning their stories and creating a plan to fight for their case. Cambry received her undergraduate degree from DePaul University and a law degree from Loyola University Chicago.

She began her career as a criminal defense attorney and gained extensive experience handling nearly every type of criminal case in courtrooms across the Chicagoland area. Throughout the first ten years of her career, Cambry earned her reputation as a respected and compassionate attorney who fought fiercely for her clients against the vast resources of the government. During her practice in Chicago, Cambry was named a Super Lawyers Magazine “Rising Star” five times from 2017 to 2021 and was also repeatedly recognized on Chicago Magazine’s “Outstanding Young Lawyers” list.

​In 2018, Cambry was selected as one of 55 attorneys to attend the Trial Lawyer’s College, in DuBois, Wyoming. TLC is a non-profit organization that is “committed to training a new breed of lawyer—a warrior who has the courage to become a real person first, and who then has the heart to fight for justice in their own passionate voice.” The experience changed Cambry’s life both personally and professionally. She has since been invited to join TLC’s faculty where she trains other trial lawyers to fight against the government and insurance companies. She has been a member of the TLC alumni board since 2020.

In 2023, Cambry shifted her practice from criminal law to civil. She now focuses on representing injured clients across the state of Texas. Cambry understands that her clients are real people with real lives that matter. She takes great pride in giving every client the individual attention they deserve. Justice is not one-size-fits-all and Cambry enjoys cultivating unique and creative solutions to complicated problems.

She is happiest in trial, where she can share stories with a jury and fight bullies, head on. Cambry grew up in Lawrence, Kansas and now lives with her husband, two children and a couple of derpy dogs just north of Austin, TX. Outside the courtroom, Cambry loves reading, writing, puzzles and enjoying the Texas outdoors with her family.

Over the following years, her practice evolved into a transactional practice with an emphasis on ensuring deals were successful and enhancing client understanding of their legal transactions.

While Ruth has conducted both non-jury and jury trials and has argued before the Texas Supreme Court, she discovered that her true interests and abilities lie in the transactional field. She enjoys focusing on language refinement to create clear and concise documents and educating her clients on their responsibilities under the documents she prepares.

Ruth places a strong emphasis on collaboration and enhancing client understanding of the law and its processes. She is highly skilled in drafting clear, concise legal documents and has experience in both jury and non-jury trials, including arguments before the Texas Supreme Court. She is passionate about transactional law and client education.

attorneys.name: Victoria Broussard
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Victoria Broussard
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Lago Vista, TX
attorneys.bio:
My mission is to build an abounding law practice where clients will always receive courteous, competent, and compassionate service from me. My clients will have the benefit of receiving excellent legal representation from people who have a genuine passion for justice, humanity, and the law. I provide compassionate and vigorous criminal defense services to people throughout Harris and surrounding counties. You can count on me to fight for you every step of the way!

I am committed to making my clients feel comfortable, and my clients know they are cared for as a person first and as a client second. I focus on the human aspect of legal representation, and I am devoted to helping clients solve problems.

Prior to opening my firm, I received my Juris Doctorate from Texas Southern University. I received the Distinguished Intern Award from the Honorable Judge Calvin Botley for my tenure as a Law Clerk in Houston, Texas; worked for a large Texas Based law firm, Jackson Walker LLP; and I clerked for Reliant Energy in the corporate legal department.

My ambition and commitment to excellence earned me a coveted position as an associate for one of the largest firms in the nation, Kirkpatrick & Lockhart Nicholson Graham LLP, where I worked on an array of litigation cases ranging from massive toxic tort litigation to simple contract disputes.

Victoria Broussard is a resident of Harris County, is a member of the American Bar Association, and is licensed to practice law in all courts in the State of Texas. She was born in Port Arthur, Texas and has lived abroad and throughout the United States.

She possesses highly developed personal skills with a talent for gaining and building the confidence of others that is readily recognized. She graduated from The University of Texas, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in Sociology. She received her Juris Doctorate from Texas Southern University, with honors, and was a member of Law Review where she served as the Executive Editor.

She received the Distinguished Intern Award from the Honorable Judge Calvin Botley for her tenure as a Law Clerk in Houston, Texas; she worked for a large Texas Based law firm, Jackson Walker LLP; and she clerked for Reliant Energy in the corporate legal department. She is the author of "Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition: Legislators Push for Policy Direction to Protect the Age of Innocence While the Court Turns a Deaf Ear" and received numerous scholarships and awards during her law school tenure.

In addition to operating a successful solo practice and raising a son who is a freshman at a private college in the Northeast. Ms. Broussard is also an advocate for the rights of survivors of childhood sexual abuse. She has lent her voice to this terrifying issue to bring awareness to a topic that has lurked in the shadows of society and caused immeasurable damage to countless people. Ms. Broussard joins her efforts with other survivors to dispel the myths surrounding childhood sexual abuse, encourage legislation that provides counseling and therapeutic services for victims, educates parents and caregivers to recognize the signs of sexual abuse, and that adequately punishes convicted offenders.

Ms. Broussard has authored her first novel titled, i-Comfortable Victim. The story is based on real events in her life, but told through a fictional lens. The book chronicles the life of Saxxine De La Croix, a young woman destined for greatness who struggles with the soul stains caused by childhood sexual abuse. Tate Publishing Company will publish Ms. Broussard's first novel, which will be available in stores and online in the summer of 2014. Please visit www.facebook.com/icomfortablevictim for more information.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Distinguished Intern Award, Hon. Judge Calvin Botley, 2002

A Godsend Foundation Humanitarian Award, 2015

attorneys.name: John M. Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Banking & Finance Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
John Brown is one of the firm's three founding partners. He practices in the areas of accountant's liability, director and officer liability, fidelity bond litigation, fiduciary and trusts and estates litigation, and estate planning, trust and probate law. Mr. Brown has taken a lead role in every significant accountant malpractice investigation the firm has undertaken, and has litigated cases against all of the national accounting firms. Mr. Brown has handled major cases in federal district and bankruptcy courts, and state courts in Texas, California, New York, Florida, Oregon, Michigan, Missouri, Delaware, Kansas, Arizona, Illinois, West Virginia, and Mississippi which have resulted in recoveries in excess of $200 million. In 2004 Mr. Brown and David Mullin successfully tried a major accounting malpractice case on behalf of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation against Grant Thornton in federal court in West Virginia. The judgment against Grant Thornton was affirmed by the Fourth Circuit in July 2011. Mr. Brown also served as lead counsel with Steve Hoard in the firm's successful representation of Enron Creditors Recovery Corp. (formerly Enron Corp.) to recover theft losses caused by Enron's former Chief Financial Officer and those acting in concert with him from Enron's insurers, resulting in the largest settlement of a crime policy coverage case in U.S. history.

Mr. Brown specializes in representing creditors' committees, trustees of litigation trusts established in bankruptcy proceedings, and receivers of federally insured financial institutions seeking to recover on various professional liability and fidelity bond claims on behalf of creditors. Most recently, Mr. Brown successfully represented the FDIC, as receiver, in its claims against certain former officers and directors of First National Bank of Arizona and First National Bank of Nevada.

For over twenty-five years, Mr. Brown has also successfully represented trustees, executors, guardians and beneficiaries, on both sides of the docket, in a wide variety of contested trust and estate issues. He also advises clients in connection with their private tax and estate planning, structuring their business interests, and carrying out their duties as trustees and executors.

Mr. Brown has been Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Estate Planning and Probate Law since 1986. Mary Kate Brown is a dedicated attorney committed to providing exceptional legal representation and advocating for her clients’ best interests. She earned her undergraduate degree from Concordia University in Austin, Texas. Beyond her professional endeavors, Mary Kate is happily married and a proud mother to two almost grown children. Family is her greatest joy, and she cherishes the moments they spend together, whether enjoying outdoor adventures or cozy movie nights at home. They also have a couple of lovable dogs who bring endless joy and companionship to their family life.

Mary Kate places a strong emphasis on balancing a successful career with a fulfilling family life. She seeks to serve as an advocate for her clients while simultaneously supporting her loved ones. Mary Kate is committed to cultivating strong relationships characterized by trust and understanding, both within her professional endeavors and her personal interactions.

attorneys.name: Patricia L. Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Round Rock, TX
attorneys.bio:
Patricia Brown founded her law firm in 1997 and focuses exclusively on people and families, and on family law. Having gone through a divorce, and raising 2 children as a single mother, Ms. Brown founded the firm based on her personal experience and philosophy: genuine empathy for men and women seeking help, and treating people as she would wish to be treated.

She understands how family law issues are stressful. often causing clients to experience anxiety, and feel a loss of control. Patricia focuses on listening and understanding each client's individual needs,

She has the unique ability to distill complex emotional and legal family issues into their essence, and communicating in a way that her clients feel a sense of comfort and relief, and a bit more back in control of their lives.

Patricia received her law degree from Albany Law School in 1996, after completing her final year at the University of Texas Law School in Austin. She grew up in New Hampshire and proudly served a four-year tour of duty in the United States Navy, simultaneously putting herself through the University of Mississippi. After graduating from college and completing her Navy service, she taught junior high school English. She then relocated to Albany, NY, and after undergoing a difficult divorce, raised her two children, working 3 jobs, and decided to go to law school, going heavily in debt to fund it. She moved to Texas in 1995.

Patricia was a state-recognized oboe player in high school and continues to love music. She is also a talented artist and enjoys painting and sketching, and cross-stitching. She has 7 grandchildren, five in Central Texas, and two in Colorado and spends as much times as he can with them. She also loves to travel, particularly to New Hampshire, where she grew up, and to Hawaii, where she loves to whale watch.

In 2015, Patricia took great personal pride in being recognized and honored by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization (TBLS) as Board Certified in Family Law. To achieve Board Certified by the TBLS, an attorney must meet a set of rigorous requirements and evaluations by peers and judges, before even being permitted to take the TBLS 6 hour examination.

According to the TBLS, "Board Certification is a mark of excellence and a distinguishing accomplishment. Within the Texas legal community, Board Certification means an attorney has substantial, relevant experience in a select field of law as well as demonstrated, and tested, special competence in that area of law." "An attorney has to do something extra to get certified and then they have to continue to work and acquire knowledge in their specialty area to remain certified. You could say it is a life-long commitment," said Hal Moorman, Chairman of the TBLS Board of Directors. Less than 1% of all the lawyers in Texas are Board Certified in Family Law.

See and hear Patricia Brown answer common questions in our video center.

attorneys.name: Scott M. Brown
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Angleton, TX
attorneys.bio:
As founder and senior partner at Scott M. Brown & Associates, Mr. Brown is board certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of legal Specialization. Out of the attorneys in the State Of Texas, Less than 1% are board certified in Family Law, which distinguishes Mr. Brow as an expert in the field of Family Law. His firm has offices in Angleton, Pearland, and League City. Texas and represents clients throughout Brazoria, Harris, Galveston, and Fort Bend counties. His firm specializes in complex and adversarial child custody cases, high-net worth property divorces, and cases involving Children's Protective Services (CPS). His firm also focuses on criminal defense, handling cases that involve the following matters: domestic violence, assault, drug charges, major felonies, white collar crimes, juvenile crime, DUI/DWI, sex crimes, violent crimes and theft.

Scott M. Brown is an experienced and passionate trial attorney who produces results. He is Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization (less than 1% of all Attorneys in the state of Texas are Board Certified in Family Law). Scott was named to the 2016 Texas Super Lawyers (only 5% of the attorneys in the State of Texas are named to this prestigious list). He was also recognized as a Texas Super Lawyers Rising Star in 2012-2014 (only 2.5 percent of attorneys under the age of 40 in the state of Texas are named to this list). In 2015 and 2016, Scott was named as one of Houston's Top Lawyers in H-Town magazine. He also possesses a 10.00 Avvo rating, which is the highest possible rating awarded by one of the nation's premiere legal ranking services.

Scott's focus on family law issues include the toughest of divorces, modifications, complex child custody cases, enforcement actions, high net value divorce (including multimillion dollar estates), as well as representing business owners, medical doctors, white collar professionals, those in the entertainment industry, and other high asset valued clients, in addition to cases involving CPS (Children's Protective Services), terminations and adoptions, and suits involving the parent-child relationship. Scott is a powerhouse and is devoted to his firm's vision of giving his client's the best possible legal representation.

Scott is also a published author having contributed to the book Strategies for Family Law in Texas, 2013 ed.: Leading Lawyers on Handling Negotiations, Managing Client Expectations, and Navigating Recent Trends (Inside the Minds). He has handled numerous jury trials and bench trials in family law and criminal defense cases. He has extensive experience handling all types of family law and criminal defense matters, including but not limited to misdemeanors, felonies, DWI, assault, sexual assault, family violence, intoxication manslaughter, drug charges, etc. The legal team he leads is committed to achieving the best possible result for every client.

attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
As a member at Cobb Martinez Woodward PLLC, Stacy Bruce represents clients on a wide range of legal matters including appeals, employment, professional liability, personal injury, construction, premises liability, and commercial litigation. For numerous years, Stacy has been named a Texas "Rising Star" by the publishers of Texas Monthly and Law & Politics. Stacy has also named an "Outstanding Lawyer Under 40" by the Cardozo Society of the Jewish Federation of Greater Dallas.

Representative matters:

Stacy has obtained summary judgment or dismissal on the merits numerous times in a variety of areas in which she practices, including lawsuits involving employers, health care professionals, title companies, officers and directors, mortgage brokers, and apartment complexes and their management companies. Below are a few of the more significant summary judgments that Stacy has obtained:

An employment discrimination and retaliation lawsuit in which the plaintiff sued under the ADA, FMLA, and ERISA seeking over a million dollars in damages. The final dismissal was affirmed by the Fifth Circuit and the United States Supreme Court denied certiorari

Defending Officer and director defendants in a foster care placement agency lawsuit

Defending a mortgage broker against a plaintiff alleging fraud and seeking over $100,000 in damages

Defended an employer from a defamation claim

Obtained numerous dismissals on premises liability claims against a retailer

Stacy has also successfully defended a home inspector in a trial before a judge obtaining a take-nothing judgment. In addition, Stacy has successfully defended several dismissals as appellate counsel.

In addition to representing clients in employment cases in state and federal court, Stacy regularly handles claims at the TWC, EEOC, & DOJ. She also advises employees in their workplace investigations, policies and procedures, employee discipline, and termination, and has helped conduct several investigations of claims for discrimination and retaliation.

attorneys.name: Steven W. Bruneman
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Texas Family Law Attorney

Steven Bruneman is an experienced, AV Preeminent® rated attorney with both the knowledge and skills to serve clients in all types of Family Law cases. For large and more complex cases, Bruneman assembles a team of experts to perform various functions including forensic accounting, business valuations and investigations. Whether the case is large, small or anywhere in-between, Bruneman works on a dedicated course focused on achieving each of his client's objectives.

The mission of Bruneman Law P.C. is to provide clients with quality legal services to achieve the results they desire.

Steven Bruneman has been a trial lawyer since 1982 when he served for three years as an Assistant District Attorney in Midland County, Texas. In 1985, he entered private practice handling family law cases and eventually joined the law firm of Koons Fuller in 1999. In the mid 2000's, he and two of his Koons Fuller partners formed the law firm of Bruneman, Lake & Griffin specializing in family law. Steve's practice became BrunemanLaw, PC in 2010.

Family Law requires more from an attorney than just strong legal skills. Bruneman deeply understands the psychological dynamics involved in family law cases and he utilizes this knowledge in every case he handles. Bruneman's goal is to help move his clients through the emotional aspect of the case in order to focus on the bigger picture, that being resolving difficult issues and moving on with their lives.

Family law attorneys should work to minimize conflict. Divorce law was not intended to create a battleground to resolve issues yet many attorneys intentionally engage in those tactics. Regardless of how cases are handled, they all eventually come to an end; and ending them with the least amount of destruction is what Bruneman always seeks to accomplish. While he is always prepared to do battle and excels at it, Bruneman's vast experience has taught him that battling in this arena should be avoided if at all possible.

Bruneman's experience and reputation rank him among the top family law attorneys in Texas.

attorneys.name: Judith Bryant
attorneys.firm_name: Bryant, Colletti, Kaplan, Kinsler, & De La Reza, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
“Let us never underestimate the power of a well-written letter.” Jane Austen, Persuasion

Judith often eliminates controversies in a case with this one skill—and that saves her clients time, stress, and money. That’s important to Judith, because she wants her clients to come out of their marriage with as much as possible—and not spend it all paying lawyers to fight over things that don’t really matter in the end. As a happily married mother and grandmother, Judith knows what really matters in the end.

Judith’s goal for her clients is to help them become stronger and better able to cope with the consequences of a failed marriage. She never forgets that the people she represents are real people who have to one day leave her office able to manage a life very different from the one they envisioned when they got married. She focuses not only on their financial well-being, but on their ability to move forward as a co-parent or single person, many of whom are getting back into the workplace for the first time in many years.

Judith graduated from the University of Texas School of Law with honors in 1987, after obtaining her English degree from UT. She worked as a commercial litigator with a large Austin firm for several years, where she learned not only the practice of litigation, but business as well. Like many of her contemporaries, she and her husband made the decision that she would stay home for several years with their young children. With their two oldest in college, she decided to go back to work, becoming a family law attorney. Judith has quickly gained the respect of her peers, being honored as a Texas Monthly “Super Lawyer” every year since 2015, and recognized by Best Lawyers every year since 2019.

When she’s not working, Judith enjoys spending time with her family (especially her grandchildren), travelling with her husband, Bill (a partner at the commercial law firm DuBois Bryant & Campbell), reading and writing.

attorneys.name: Roy Buckmaster
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
It’s rare to find an attorney who lives for the fight, who isn’t afraid of the long hours and all-nighters that come with trial preparation. Roy Buckmaster is one of those rare attorneys. Roy finds real joy in advocating for people who have been victimized by things outside of their control. No matter how difficult the case or tough the battle, Roy puts everything he has into helping his clients get the best result.

At the University of Arizona, his favorite coursework was with the Child of Family Law Clinic—representing the interests of children in child protection proceedings. Consistently on the Dean’s List, Roy excelled in law school, participating in the Veteran’s Clinic, the Arizona Journal of International and Comparative Law, the Volunteer Lawyers Program, the American Inn of Court, and clerking for a prestigious Tucson litigation firm.

After graduating in 2014, Roy chose a career in the courtroom and was a criminal prosecutor for various Arizona agencies, including Yavapai County and the City of Prescott. Roy excelled in this role as the voice for victims. He managed hundreds of complex cases from charging through trial and was often a guide and a counselor for those who suffered from the effects of devastating events like domestic violence and sexual abuse.

For the last two years, Roy has transitioned his focus to civil litigation. His passion for fighting for victims has only sharpened. Roy’s trial skills and understanding of pre-litigation strategy have made him a valuable part of Arnold & Itkin and has helped those injured by the negligent, reckless, or intentional acts of others.

Roy lives with his wife Elliot and three children in the beautiful Heber Valley, Utah, where he snowboards in the winter and wakeboards in the summer.

attorneys.name: Russell W. Budd
attorneys.practice_type: Mass Torts Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Russell W. Budd is a major force in the world of plaintiff’s attorneys, having devoted his three-decade career to championing the rights of people and communities injured by corporate malfeasance. Currently Mr. Budd presides over one of the nation’s largest plaintiff’s firms, Baron & Budd, PC, headquartered in Dallas, Texas with offices in Austin, Texas; Los Angeles, California and Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

Mr. Budd, a shareholder of Baron & Budd since 1985 and president and managing shareholder since 2002, has expanded the firm from its cornerstone asbestos practice to a national firm capable of tackling the biggest defendants in areas as diverse as pharmaceutical and medical device injury, water contamination, BP Gulf oil spill, financial fraud and various other areas of practice.

Over the last decade, Mr. Budd has played significant roles in asbestos litigation on a national level. As chair and member of several asbestos creditors’ bankruptcy committees, Mr. Budd successfully resolved over 100,000 victims’ claims with some of Wall Street’s biggest companies. Mr. Budd was the chief negotiator of a $4 billion national settlement with Halliburton that established a trust fund to protect present and future asbestos victims throughout the United States – the largest asbestos trust fund of its kind anywhere in the world. He was on the committee that negotiated a $3.9 billion settlement with United States Gypsum to benefit asbestos claimants. And, he participated in negotiations that led W.R. Grace to agree to fund a bankruptcy trust on behalf of asbestos claimants with nearly $3 billion in cash and stock equity.

Under Mr. Budd’s direction, Baron & Budd provided the initial funding for the launch of the International Pleural Mesothelioma Program at Brigham and Women’s Hospital to research curative therapy for Mesothelioma, a cancer caused by exposure to asbestos. The firm has also given generously to the Asbestos Disease Awareness Organization, Lung Cancer Alliance and to other asbestos awareness advocacy organizations.

Mr. Budd serves on the Board of Governors of the American Association for Justice (AAJ) and previously served on the Board of Directors and Executive Committee of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA).

On July 13, 2010, Mr. Budd was awarded the prestigious Harry M. Philo Award Trial Lawyer of the Year Award from the American Association for Justice (AAJ) at the organization’s annual conference in Vancouver, BC. The award was presented in recognition of his dedicated and consistent leadership in protecting the rights of individuals through the civil-justice system. In 2007, he earned the prestigious Wiedemann Wysocki National Finance Council Award from the American Association for Justice, an award honoring attorneys for their commitment to the legal profession and their efforts to improve the civil justice system.

Under Mr. Budd’s leadership, Baron & Budd has won numerous awards. The firm was recently named by National Law Journal’s to its "Hot List" of exemplary plaintiffs’ firms in the United States and has been included in the Hot List eight times.

Mr. Budd and his wife are very involved in the community and one of the causes closest to his heart is Habitat for Humanity, which gives hardworking Dallas families a chance at first-time home ownership. He has personally contributed generously to the "Building on Faith" project, a collaborative initiative between the Dallas Faith Communities Coalition (DFCC), the City of Dallas and Habitat for Humanity to build 100 affordable single-family homes in West Dallas. In addition, Mr. Budd has donated land to the City of Dallas that enabled the completion of a massive bike and hike trail. In 2010, Mr. Budd was the only attorney selected to serve on the Foundation Board of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN).

attorneys.name: Andrew Bullard
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Andrew grew up in Kerens, Texas, where his small-town upbringing had a big influence on his path to becoming a trial lawyer. As the son of a mortician, Andrew saw firsthand how his father worked with people through the most difficult times in their lives following the loss of a loved one. That perspective has had a tremendous influence on the way Andrew approaches his clients as he helps them navigate the legal world during what is often the most difficult time in their lives.

Since joining the firm in 2018, Andrew has gained extensive state and federal court experience litigating a variety of personal injury matters including auto defects, product liability, medical malpractice, premise liability, motor vehicle accidents, commercial motor vehicle accidents, assaults, and sexual assaults.

Andrew is a member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association where he serves on the Board of Directors as well as the Advocates Board of Directors. He is a member of Dallas Trial Lawyers Association where he also serves on the Board of Directors. As a former tennis coach and teacher, Andrew enjoys mentoring and serves as Alumni Mentor for Oklahoma City University law students.

Away from work, Andrew enjoys cooking, the outdoors, golf, tennis, and spending time with his wife, daughter, and twin sons.

attorneys.name: Ralph K. Burgess
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Counsel Lawyers in Texarkana, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ralph K. Burgess has an extremely diverse resume' during his 32 years of practice that uniquely qualifies him to serve as appellate counsel in state and federal civil and criminal cases, trial counsel in complex civil litigation matters, and as a mediator in civil and family law cases.

Mr. Burgess returned to the practice of law in February 2022 after having served nineteen years as a Judge for the State of Texas. Mr. Burgess was Justice of Texas' 6th District Court of Appeals for seven years, and prior to that, was Judge of Texas' 5th District Court for twelve years. As Appellate Justice and District Judge, Mr. Burgess handled complex civil cases of all types, felony criminal cases, and family law cases. Prior to his tenure as a judge, Mr. Burgess spent thirteen years practicing law in Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas. He is board certified in civil trial law (1998) and personal injury trial law (1997) by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He has completed the A.A. White Mediation Training Course at the University of Houston twice, in 1997 and 2021. During his career as an appellate attorney, he presented and argued cases before the Fifth and Eighth Circuit Courts of Appeals, the Texas Supreme Court, the Texas Court of Appeals, and the Arkansas Court of Appeals. During his career as a Justice on the Court of Appeals, he authored more than 300 published opinions. During his career, both as trial attorney and judge, Mr. Burgess tried more than 200 jury trials to verdict in state and federal court including three state and federal death penalty cases.

Mr. Burgess is licensed to practice law in all trial and appellate courts in Texas and Arkansas, in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas and the Eastern/Western District of Arkansas, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth and Eighth Circuits, and the United States Supreme Court. Mr. Burgess received his Bachelor of Arts Degree from Texas Christian University, magna cum laude, in 1987 and his Juris Doctor Degree from the Bowen School of Law at the University of Arkansas at Little Rock in 1990, where he served as an Assistant Editor on the UALR Law Journal. He will practice primarily as appellate counsel in state in federal civil and criminal cases, trial counsel in state and federal court litigation, and serve as a mediator in civil and family law cases.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Jurist of the Year for the Texas Chapter of American Board of Trial Attorneys, 2007

attorneys.name: Carla M. Burke
attorneys.practice_type: Water Contamination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Carla Burke, an attorney and shareholder with Baron & Budd's water contamination litigation group, began her legal career with the firm's appellate section. She has a gift for writing and oral advocacy that has been very persuasive in the MTBE Multi-District Litigation cases. Carla has also authored and presented numerous papers and presentations on the topics of toxic tort and water contamination litigation and premises liability law.

Carla is a natural teacher, which is perfect for her role as a legal issues attorney in complex water contamination cases. She has also been an adjunct clinical instructor of law at the Southern Methodist University School of Law Legal Clinic and, before law school, an English professor at a local college.

Not long after law school, she successfully briefed and argued, pro bono, the case of Lawson v. Dallas County, 112 F.3d 257 (5th Cir. 2002) before the United States Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit, where she represented a disabled man whose lack of medical treatment while in the custody of the Dallas county jail amounted to cruel and unusual punishment.

Carla's work for her clients is driven by her conviction that "law is a powerful force for social change. What starts with one person can affect an entire nation." Carla found the opportunity to be a part of that force for change at Baron & Budd. "Baron & Budd is, literally, changing lives for the better," she says.

A graduate of Baylor Law School, Mr. Burke has successfully represented clients involved in high-stakes litigation across Texas and the U.S. He guest lectures at Baylor Law School and serves as a consultant and monitoring counsel for manufacturing companies, automotive and other product dealerships, oil and gas companies involved in pre-suit matters and litigation. He has represented a wide range of domestic and international companies, such as automobile manufacturers, automotive and RV dealerships, heavy equipment manufacturers and dealerships, firearm manufacturers, oil and gas operators, drilling companies, tubing companies, and other energy entities. attorneys.name: James J. Burnett
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
James Burnett is an experienced trial attorney licensed to practice in all Texas courts and in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas and before the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. Appeared as counsel of record in cases in the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Eastern Districts of Texas, the District of Arizona, and the Central District of California. He has many years of experience representing clients before municipal, county, state, and federal regulatory and governmental entities.

Commercial Litigation and Appeals: Active representation of businesses and key personnel in a variety of professions and industries, ranging from small, closely held enterprises to large companies with national and international corporate endeavors. Numerous mediations, arbitrations, trials, and appeals in state and federal court in a number of diverse situations, on behalf of both plaintiffs and defendants, including the following:

• Construction Litigation: Suing for and defending builders, developers, general contractors and subcontractors, and the customers acquiring and using services in residential and commercial construction, and in trials and appeals regarding claims of structural or construction defects. Represented condominium regime sued for mismanagement of the reconstruction of fire-damaged units whose owners alleged fraud and fiduciary breaches as well as negligence, obtaining a dismissal with prejudice of all claims against the clients.

• Consumer Protection: Representation of individuals in a wide range of cases involving the Deceptive Trade Practices Act, the Residential Construction Liability Act, and fraud in real estate litigation.

• Oil and Gas Exploration Litigation: Specialized experience representing oil and gas exploration contractors including three seismic dimensional survey projects in the continuing exploration for petroleum resources throughout Texas. Represented one client sued in 46 simultaneous lawsuits in different venues in Texas, which cases involved over 600 plaintiffs alleging both extreme property damage and mass tort personal injuries; obtained decisive findings solidly in favor of the client in all cases, including summary judgments and both directed verdicts and jury verdicts at trial. Appellate courts uniformly upheld all verdicts appealed by plaintiffs. All cases obtained findings of no liability on behalf of the contractor.

• Litigation Against Governmental Entities: Successfully represented a non-profit cultural and performing arts entity in a suit by, and a countersuit against, a municipal economic development corporation. Successfully defended repeated attempts to assert governmental immunity, resulting in a unanimous decision by the Texas Supreme Court ruling that such entities have no immunity from suit, which resulted in a near-immediate settlement of the suit with no liability against the client and an agreed-upon settlement from the ECD. Extensive experience in disciplinary, employment discrimination, Title VI and VII, and related claims against school districts and universities.

• Chemical Litigation: Over 15 years' experience representing distributors, re-packagers, and sellers of water treatment, industrial, and petroleum industry chemicals. Active and successful defense of negligence, intentional tort, environmental discharge, remediation, and CERCLA claims. Represented clients in all manners of commercial disputes concerning the chemical industry and commercial matters including unfair competition, Lanham Act, violation of non-competition agreements, and related matters. Numerous appearances for clients before state and federal agricultural, environmental, and other regulatory agencies.

• ERISA Litigation: Solely responsible for the preparation, presentation, and negotiation of Level 1 and Level 2 administrative appeals and then the judicial actions for damages and equitable relief on behalf of health care providers under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act. Prepared and filed complaints, undertook discovery, prepared cases for mediation, and where mediation was unsuccessful conducted the cases to trial before federal judges.

• Computer Hardware and Software Technology Litigation: Appeared as counsel in state and federal litigation relating to the development, marketing, licensing, or infringement of licenses, copyrights, or other proprietary rights, on a variety of computer software and other technologies. Other litigation has involved issues of defective design, manufacture, or implementation of systems. Extensive knowledge of and litigation experience involving Cloud Computing, including IAAS, PAAS, and SAAS.

• White Collar Crime: Active and decisive civil prosecution of employees and former employees who embezzled company funds and misappropriated company property for profit. Obtained and collected from $350,000 to over $7,200,000.

• Industrial Equipment Litigation: Suits on behalf of multinational turbo-machinery and other heavy industrial equipment enterprises in state and federal litigation involving diesel, electric, and gas turbine generators, and related turbine equipment, including litigation with international implications.

• Regulatory Disputes: Protected clients before a wide variety of state and federal regulatory agencies, including the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, OSHA, the U.S. Department of Transportation, the Texas Board of Professional Engineers, and the Texas Workforce Commission. Represented client in case where the Federal Aviation Administration alleged that client had violated hazardous materials shipping regulations and sought maximum penalties for over 20 specific regulatory violations, if sustained, would have exceeded $1,000,000 in liability; resolved the dispute for $40,000 with a non-liability finding on behalf of the client.

• Employment-Related Litigation: Representation of businesses in litigation arising from employment agreements and employment relationships. Claims included lawsuits filed by former employees, suits to enforce non-competition or trade secret agreements, and disputes arising from unfair competition and business defamation actions by former employees or individuals acting with their information or under their direction.

• Professional Practitioner Litigation: Served broad group of professionals including aerospace engineers, chemical engineers, mechanical engineers, and a variety of physicians, physical therapists, and others, in cases involving professional activities and conduct.

• General Commercial Litigation: Represented clients in general commercial matters ranging from contract disputes and negligence claims to intentional torts including complaints of civil fraud, conspiracy, RICO violations, and similar claims.

• Insurance Defense Litigation and Appeals: Trial and appellate experience in above- described categories involved representing both plaintiffs and defendants; in defense litigation, especially in regard to the oil and gas exploration, chemical, industrial equipment, professional practitioner, and general commercial matters, involved representing clients through their insurance carriers, including American General, Travelers, and Union America. Additionally, extensive experience in both commercial and individual (principally automobile collision) insurance defense matters as both assigned counsel and counsel under reservation of rights.

Commercial Transactional Matters: Representation of clients in a variety of corporate transactions ranging from contracts for goods and/or services to commercial real estate leases and sales, franchise agreements, intellectual property agreements, non-disclosure and non- competition agreements, and other related matters. These have ranged from local endeavors to enterprises with interstate, national, and international involvement. Representative transactions have included:

• Technology: Represented clients in a variety of technology-related transactions including Cloud Computing, licensing, marketing, and e-commerce, computer hardware and software and network licensing and marketing agreements and operations, intellectual property copyrights, trademark, patent and service mark issues, technology development and transfer agreements and transactions, reverse-engineering and re-engineering agreements, and international software development transactions involving individuals and companies in the United States, Canada, and Japan simultaneously.

• Industrial: Extensive experience in negotiating, drafting, modifying, finalizing, and enforcing all manners of commercial transactions in all aforementioned fields. Agreements in multinational turbo-machinery equipment transactions and complex contractual agreements between clients and various American and foreign owned business entities, including the negotiation of the acquisition contract of turbine equipment from four power companies in Japan, the establishment of new Texas and Arizona corporations for the receipt and refurbishment of the equipment, negotiations with Hong Kong corporation purchasing the refurbished machinery, and with the Manila municipal authorities purchasing them from Hong Kong in turn for installation in the Philippine Islands, and with the Dutch shipping company responsible for transporting the equipment by sea from the United States. Represented clients in transactions involving the purchase, operation, sale, and warranty issues of various types of equipment and machinery ranging from small office equipment to large networked computer systems and major industrial and factory equipment.

• Energy: Represented three-dimensional seismic survey monitoring and risk-management companies with transactions involving all aspects of petrochemical exploration and development, onshore and offshore, with exploration, production, and transmission entities. Transactions have included contract negotiation, drafting, and revision in matters from single subdivisions to multistate pipeline contracts and international natural gas purchase and sale agreements.

• Chemical: Served all aspects of the sale, distribution, packaging, and repackaging of chemicals from master sales agreements for a broad range of products to specialized contracts for unique niche compounds. Transaction work includes constant due diligence and structuring to ensure compliance with state and federal laws and regulations regarding environmental, import/export, strategic materials, and other chemical restrictions.

• Employment and Labor: Initiated actions by and handled the defense of businesses from small, family-owned entities, to multinational combines, in a variety of employment-related transactions including, drafting, review, and updating of personnel policies, employment manuals, and guidelines; the oversight of human resources personnel to ensure compliance with state and federal employment regulatory requirements, review and amendment of safety protocols, drafting, review, and amendment of document retention and preservation procedures, employment agreements with employees and independent contractors, corporate records review and modification regarding stock purchase, sale agreements, and "key man" processes, retirement and severance agreements, and negotiation of employment disputes not requiring litigation.

• Corporate Counsel and General Business Transactions: Comprehensively handled all facets of business formation, organization, operation, and winding down. These ranged from formation of business entities through restructuring and changes of ownership to end- strategy transactions. Handled sale, purchase, lease, and operating agreements on a variety of corporate entities, types, and operational variations.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: Cause No. B-164,082; Conex International Corporation vs. Fluor Enterprises, Inc. and Leslie Antalffy; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Burmeister served as local counsel for the Plaintiff which was alleging business disparagement. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff in the amount of 95 million dollars. Case is on appeal

Cause No. E-162,269; Michael Gordon as next friend of Ryan Gordon and Sarah Gordon vs. Little Rock Assembly of God, et al; 172nd Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Sexual molestation case against local church and its regional headquarters and national headquarters for youth minister molesting Plaintiffs where Mr. Burmeister served as co-counsel. Judgment for the Plaintiffs in the amount of 80 million dollars. Case settlement thereafter at mediation for confidential amount

Cause No. B-126,144; Texas Metal Works vs. O. L. Gear Co.; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Burmeister served as lead counsel in a case whereby the Defendant sold a faulty steam hammer to the Plaintiff. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff in the amount of 5 million dollars

Cause No. B-134,751; Herbert Straughter, Jr. vs. Gaumer Co., Inc.; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Burmeister represented the injured Plaintiff due to a malfunction of the electric eye manufactured by the Defendant, which allowed bags of resin to continue moving on a conveyor belt at Goodyear, causing a bag to strike the Plaintiff, resulting in a lower back fusion. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff in the amount of 4 million dollars

Cause No. B-176,143; E. I. DuPont DeNemours v. Travelers Casualty & Surety Company, et al; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Burmeister served as co-counsel for the Plaintiff, which was seeking to recover asbestosis payouts it had made to various claimants. Confidential settlement

Cause No. B-173008; Hooks v. Sampson Oil. Mr. Burmeister was local counsel in an oil and gas case. Burmeister did jury selection and gave the closing arguments. The jury awarded 20 million dollars. Case is on appeal

attorneys.name: Jason K. Burress
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in McKinney, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jason Burress is a 7th generation Texan who earned his law degree from SMU School of Law. After law school, Jason worked for a prominent Texas based law firm, managing hundreds of high-stakes cases involving personal injury and wrongful death with millions of dollars at risk.

Since founding Burress Injury Law in 2008, Jason’s practice has shifted from defending insurance companies and product manufacturers to representing people who are injured or have lost loved ones due to someone else’s negligence. Jason dedicates his practice to helping serious personal injury victims of catastrophic 18 wheeler crashes, motorcycle wrecks and car crashes, as well as victims of drunk drivers and dangerous or defective products.

We have been fortunate to have earned many honors and accolades. We take pride in these awards, as they reflect our unyielding commitment and dedication to the people we serve.

attorneys.bio:
I understand that divorce both ends a legal and personal relationship and begins a complex and distinct relationship. The client’s immediate future requires practical legal guidance and knowledgeable negotiations concerning substantive rights, obligations and entitlements.

Resolving these very personal needs and issues, whether by agreement or litigation, requires the experienced, balancing and careful consideration of spousal and child support obligations and property division, including business interests, pension and profit-sharing entitlements, trusts and investments.

attorneys.name: Clay A. Butler
attorneys.practice_type: Clean Energy | Solar | Wind | Other Renewables and Clean Tech Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Clay A. Butler is founding partner of The Butler Firm, PLLC. A legal and consulting firm located in Austin, Texas, providing comprehensive legal and consulting services to clients in the renewable energy and clean energy sector.

Clay is one of the leading attorneys in the US on renewable energy law and represents clients from all spectrums from utility-scale project development to distributed generation. He has served as lead project counsel on over 500 megawatts of utility-scale solar projects. On the distributed generation side, Clay developed a utility-sponsored solar lease model for a Client, the first of its kind in the Nation.

In addition to providing legal counsel on the development side, Clay is heavily involved on regulatory and policy matters for his clients as well as assisting in the arrangement of project financing and structuring. Clay additionally has expansive knowledge and experience in general energy law and the wholesale electricity markets.

Clay is very involved in renewable energy and clean tech outside the law firm at the locally and nationally. He serves as the President of the Board for Solar Austin and is the current Policy Chair for the Texas Renewable Energy Industry Association. Clay was also selected to participate in the National Renewable Energy Laboratories “Energy Executives” program.

A native of Austin, Clay joined the United States Marine Corps at the age of 17. During his four years as an infantryman, Clay earned the unique privilege of being stationed in Washington D.C. in the honor guard with duties at the Pentagon and White House. The underlying principles he learned in the Corps carry on in the foundation of The Butler Firm.

As managing partner of The Butler Firm, Clay manages the attorneys and energy consultants at the firm who provide a multitude of services ranging from project development to due diligence for investment and engineering firms. Clay and the rest of the team at The Butler Firm have provided legal and consulting services for developers, manufacturers, municipalities, integrators and corporations in various clean energy matters giving them unparalleled experience in their field.

attorneys.name: Kimberly Butler
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Roanoke, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly has been serving the needs of North Texas families since 1997. She began working with troubled youth and their families as a juvenile probation officer in Denton County. Her love for and belief in the inherent goodness of children fueled her work to reach the youth of Denton County showing them there is another way through life. Kimberly believes that in most children's lives, it takes just one person to show their genuine care to have a positive impact on their outcome in life. Kimberly still hopes today that she may have been that one person for even just one child.

It was only natural that upon being licensed as a Texas attorney in 2004, Kimberly began her journey as a Family Law practitioner for the families here in Denton and surrounding North Texas counties. Kimberly has represented families in all areas of family law, including CPS defense and juvenile law cases. Whatever your family structure, whatever your family's needs, Kimberly is here to help you get through the "business" of the legal system so you can get back to the "living" of life! Kimberly has focused on making sure that ALL families, no matter the makeup, are secure and whole in their familial relationships, whether a single-parent family, two-parent family, grandparents/aunties/uncles raising your grandchildren/nieces/nephews, same-sex parents/families, and foster parents wishing to adopt. All families are welcome, all families matter.

Kimberly has provided competent, financially conscientious representation in all of the following areas:

Family Law

Child Custody and Support

Divorce

Modification And Enforcement of Court Orders

Cohabitation Agreements

Name Changes for Both Adults and Children

Second-Parent Adoptions

Termination And Adoption

Cps Defenses/Juvenile Matters

Matters Pertaining to Same-Sex Couples Testamentary Planning

Estate/Testamentary Planning

Guardianship

Probate

Business Entity Formation

Kimberly grew up in Lewisville, graduating high school as a proud Fighting Farmer way back in 1988. Her family still lives in Denton County so spending time with her parents is a welcome activity anytime! When she is not being a busy family law attorney, Kimberly and her cat, Sunny, reside in Roanoke, where Kimberly likes to participate in the town events on historic Oak Street. She also is an avid genealogy enthusiast and loves to spend time with her three nephews when they come to town! Kimberly also loves volunteering, further serving the needs of all the residents of North Texas in whatever capacity possible.

attorneys.name: Christine Butts
attorneys.practice_type: Probate and Estate Administration Lawyers in Spring, TX
attorneys.bio:
Christine Butts is a 1993 graduate of the University of Texas at Austin where she obtained her BBA in International Business. In 1996, she graduated from the University of Houston Law School. Christine is Board Certified in Probate and Estate Planning by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. As a law student, Christine was publishing editor of the Houston Journal of International Law. Christine limits her practice of law to the following areas: probate, estate planning, guardianship, business entities, and charitable organizations. Christine served Harris County as Judge of Probate Court 4 from 2011 to 2018 and, now back in practice, remains dedicated to the mission of serving families in times of crisis when that crisis involves the loss or incapacity of a loved one. From 2019-2020, Christine served as the president of the National College of Probate Judges. In addition, she is a member of the Texas Probate Law American Inns or Court. Christine serves as on the Pearl Fincher Museum of Fine Arts and is a sustaining member of the Junior League of Houston. Christine and her husband, Donald Butts, have four children, live in Tomball, and attend Christ the Good Shepherd Catholic Church.

attorneys.name: Lynette S. Byrd
attorneys.practice_type: Government Investigations Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Former federal prosecutor Lynette Byrd focuses her practice on governmental investigations, corporate litigation, and employment law matters.

During her tenure as an Assistant United States Attorney (AUSA) for the Northern District of Texas, Ms. Byrd regularly defended the United States Government in a variety of civil matters. She later transitioned within the U.S. Attorney's Office to the government's affirmative civil enforcement practice, where she supervised investigations in the area of Medicare fraud, healthcare fraud, and anti-kickback allegations under the Federal False Claims Act and the Civil Monetary Penalties Law. Ms. Byrd prosecuted these matters with support of the Office of Inspector General, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and other federal law enforcement agencies.

Prior to becoming a federal prosecutor, Ms. Byrd served as counsel to one of the leading international law firms. There, Ms. Byrd focused on business and employment litigation, including defense of fraud, defamation, as well as statutory claims arising under federal statutes such as Title VII, FLSA, FMLA, ADA, and the ADEA. Ms. Byrd has substantial experience pursuing enforcement of non-competition and non-solicitation agreements.

Ms. Byrd's extensive trial experience includes handling health care litigation, employment, and complex business litigation matters across a variety of jurisdictions in state and federal court. Ms. Byrd has served as a first chair and lead counsel in numerous jury and bench trials, including appellate matters. As a litigator, Ms. Byrd has briefed and argued virtually all aspects of litigation in state and federal courts- from complex motion practice to heated discovery and jurisdictional disputes.

attorneys.name: Allison D. Byman
attorneys.practice_type: Business Bankruptcy Lawyers in Pearland, TX
attorneys.bio:
Allison D. Byman is experienced in business and consumer bankruptcy matters representing, debtors, creditors, trustees, committees and equity interest holders. Allison was appointed as a Chapter 7 Bankruptcy Trustee for the Southern District of Texas in April 2012. Since then, she has focused her practice on consumer and small business bankruptcy matters. She also represents other chapter 7 trustee's in the Southern District of Texas. Allison serves as post confirmation trustee and in other bankruptcy fiduciary capacities as well.

Allison was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2003 and is also admitted to practice in the United States Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit, and the U.S. District Courts of Texas for the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts. She was named one of the Texas Rising Stars by Thomson Reuters (Bankruptcy & Creditor/Debtor Rights) in 2010, 2013-2018.

Before starting her own firm, Allison worked as of counsel at Hughes Watters Askanase, LLP and as an associate with Thompson & Knight LLP in Houston where she supported the firms' Bankruptcy and Creditors' Rights Practice Groups. Outside of work, Allison enjoys watching her sons play lacrosse, travelling, reading and working out.

Chad Cacciotti has over 23 years of legal experience serving clients throughout Texas specializing in construction law, regulatory compliance, business formations and general counsel services. Chad has served as legal counsel for numerous small to midsize companies, providing expertise in complex contract negotiation, OSHA compliance, business transactions and civil litigation. He has tried multiple cases to verdict and conducted numerous depositions throughout his litigation career. Chad earned his Juris Doctor from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law (now Texas A&M University School of Law) and a Bachelor of Science in Geography from Texas A&M University. He is licensed to practice law in Texas and admitted to the U.S. District Courts for the Eastern and Northern Districts of Texas. Chad has been continually recognized as a Top Attorney by FTW Magazine since 2018. He has also been recognized as a Top Attorney in 360 West Magazine from 2017 - 2024.

Dedicated to service, Chad has been a Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation since 2019. He previously served on the Board for Hannah House from 2011 – 2015 and in the role of President of the Board from 2011 – 2013. He is a member of Holy Family Catholic Church and is involved with the Holy Family Dad’s Club through which he volunteers for the parochial school.

attorneys.name: Moses Cage
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Moses Cage is more than just a seasoned personal injury lawyer in Dallas; he's a dedicated advocate with a passion for justice, a loving husband, and a devoted father. Hailing from the vibrant city of New Orleans, Louisiana, Moses brings a unique blend of Southern charm and tenacity to his legal practice.

Born and raised in the heart of the Crescent City, Moses's upbringing instilled in him a strong sense of community and a commitment to helping those in need. He completed his undergraduate studies at Bethune-Cookman College, where he majored in Political Science.

In 2006, armed with a Juris Doctor degree from Southern University Law Center, Moses began his journey as an attorney. Since then, he has tirelessly fought for the rights of his clients, advocating for fair compensation and justice in cases ranging from automobile accidents to mass tort actions.

Beyond his professional achievements, Moses’s most cherished roles are those of husband and father. He and his wife Christine have built a beautiful life in the bustling city of Dallas. Their daughter, Celeste, is the light of their lives, and Moses credits his family for providing him with unwavering support and inspiration.

When he's not in the courtroom or spending quality time with his loved ones, Moses can be found playing golf or cheering on his beloved New Orleans Saints during football season.

With over a decade of experience and a track record of success, Moses continues to uphold his reputation as a trusted advocate for the people of Dallas. Whether inside the courtroom or out, he remains dedicated to fighting for justice and making a difference in the lives of those he serves.

attorneys.firm_name: Griffin & Cain Attorneys at Law, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Conroe, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brian Cain is an experienced attorney specializing in family law and criminal defense. With a strong commitment to advocating for clients in challenging and emotionally charged situations, Brian Cain brings a compassionate yet strategic approach to every case.

In criminal defense, Brian defends clients against a wide range of charges, including misdemeanors, felonies, and DUI offenses. With a deep understanding of the criminal justice system, Brian works tirelessly to ensure that every client receives fair treatment, conducts thorough investigations, and explores every possible defense strategy to achieve the most favorable result.

Known for a high level of professionalism, integrity, and personal attention, Brian builds strong relationships with clients, taking the time to listen to their concerns and provide clear, informed legal advice. Whether navigating family dynamics or facing criminal charges, Brian is committed to providing dedicated representation that clients can trust.

Brian was licensed to practice law in Texas in 2009, after graduating from Seton Hall University – School of Law. Prior to that Brian earned a B.A. in History and Religious Studies from The University of Texas at Austin and an M.A. in History from Texas State University. He is a past Treasurer of the Montgomery County Bar Association and currently sits on the Board of 2 local charitable organizations.

attorneys.name: Catherine Wagner Calderaro
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Catherine joined the firm as an associate attorney in 2020 and is licensed to practice in Texas and California. Before coming to Hutcheson Bowers LLLP, she practiced law in Los Angeles for several years as a civil litigator with a focus on employment law. She has managed cases at all stages and knows that effective representation means understanding every client's unique perspective and needs.

Catherine advises the firm's clients on California employment law issues and manages employee handbook creation and updates for the firm's clients. Catherine has extensive experience managing the firm's AAA docket of consumer disputes for the firm's financial services clients and routinely advises them on risk reduction. Recently, Catherine was lead counsel in a non-competition dispute in Williamson County, which resulted in a multi-day evidentiary hearing and argument.

Catherine graduated from the University of Texas School of Law, where she was a Human Rights Scholar, and began her legal career as a University of Texas Public Service Fellow with the ACLU of Southern California. Prior to and during law school, she also worked with several civil and human rights organizations including the Texas Civil Rights Project, the UN Khmer Rouge Tribunal in Cambodia, the Save Darfur Coalition, and Oxfam International. She also holds a bachelor's degree in International Relations from Boston University. Catherine and her husband enjoy traveling, barbecuing, camping, and trying to keep up with their young daughter.

attorneys.name: Robert G. Callahan II
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Robert Callahan’s aggressive style of advocacy is a product of Baylor Law School’s trial-centered education and his experience as a prosecutor. His oratory skills are well known throughout the courtrooms of central Texas.

Robert earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Gonzaga University in Spokane, Washington. After he earned his Juris Doctorate in 2006, Robert joined the McLennan County District Attorney’s Office where he excelled. He was quickly promoted to a misdemeanor Court Chief position, then promoted again to prosecute felony crimes.

In 2011, Robert entered private practice with a vision to serve the people of central Texas. In 2012, he was nominated Outstanding Young Lawyer of the Year by the McLennan County Young Lawyer’s Association. In 2016, he was named one of the National Black Lawyers’ Top 100 Lawyers, and in 2020 he was named the Top Criminal Defense Attorney in the State of Texas, receiving the Percy Foreman Award.

Robert believes that every person has value, and everyone accused of breaking the law deserves affordable legal representation. With that in mind, Callahan & King aspires to meet the needs of every client as a whole person. Robert’s goal is not simply to represent his clients, but to work with them to address the spiritual and emotional needs behind the legal issues. Robert, his wife, and three children live and work in McLennan County.
