attorneys.name: Carla M. F. Camarero
attorneys.practice_type: DWI Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Carla is a seasoned attorney who brings a unique perspective to the courtroom, having served previously as a prosecutor before transitioning to a dedicated criminal defense attorney. Carla has honed an exceptional understanding of both sides of the legal system, providing invaluable insights that benefit clients facing a spectrum of legal challenges.

Carla started her legal career at the Travis County Attorney’s Office, where she tried dozens of jury trials and specialized in DWIs and assault family violence cases. After almost five years with the County Attorney, she moved to the Travis County District Attorney’s Office. At the DA’s office, she handled a caseload of various felony charges and was part of a team that focused on vehicular homicides. Carla later joined the Bastrop County District Attorney’s Office, where she was the sole prosecutor handling all of the crimes against children and sexual assault offenses for the county. Her experience as a prosecutor equipped her with a deep understanding of prosecutorial strategies and tactics, which she now adeptly employs in defense of her clients’ rights and liberties.

Now specializing in DWIs and assaultive offenses as a defense attorney, Carla has successfully defended numerous individuals against a wide range of criminal charges. Her track record of achieving favorable outcomes for clients is a testament to her strategic acumen, courtroom prowess, and relentless advocacy. Beyond her professional achievements, Carla is known for her compassionate approach to client representation and understanding of the profound impact legal proceedings can have on individuals and families. She prioritizes clear communication, transparency, and personalized attention, ensuring that each client receives the highest level of legal representation tailored to their unique circumstances. Her relentless advocacy instills confidence in her clients, assuring them that she will fight for their rights with unwavering determination.

attorneys.name: Danielle M. Campbell
attorneys.firm_name: Danielle M. Campbell, Attorney at Law, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
With almost 20 years of legal experience, Danielle M. Campbell is dedicated to providing compassionate, knowledgeable, and effective legal representation in family law, estate planning, and probate. Inspired by her grandfather, who practiced law in Houston for three decades, Ms. Campbell has built a career grounded in integrity, service, and a commitment to educating clients while keeping the law simple and accessible.

Prior to attending law school, Ms. Campbell graduated from the University of Hawai`i and was a teacher in Spring. A proud graduate of South Texas College of Law, Ms. Campbell was a Dean’s List honoree and received the Merit Scholarship all three years. During her time there, she also served as an Assistant Editor on the South Texas Law Review, was a Director of the Board of Advocates, was named to Who's Who Among American Law Students, and was a member of the Phi Delta Phi Honor Fraternity. She participated in the prestigious Advocacy Program under the direction of T. Gerald Treece, honing her skills as a trial advocate. As an Assistant Editor on the Law Review, she refined her writing and research abilities, which have been invaluable in her legal practice. She also mentored fellow law students in the Mentor/Mentee Program.

Specializing in family law, estate planning, and probate, Ms. Campbell believes that her clients should always be informed participants in the legal system. Her goal is not only to provide expert legal counsel but to ensure that clients fully understand the process and feel confident about their decisions at every stage. She and her team are committed to answering all questions thoroughly, being honest and transparent about the facts and realities of each case—whether the news is good or challenging.

Above all, Ms. Campbell strives to achieve the best possible results tailored to each client’s unique situation, helping them navigate complex legal matters with clarity and confidence. Her clients can trust that they will be guided through the legal process with care and that their individual needs are at the forefront of every strategy and decision.

In addition to her law practice, Ms. Campbell is an active member of several esteemed legal organizations. She is a member of the Texas Bar Association, the American Bar Association, and has served on the Montgomery County Bar Association Board of Directors from 2019 to 2025. Since 2020, she has been a valued member of the State Bar of Texas Grievance Committee, contributing to the maintenance of legal ethics and professionalism across the state.

Outside of her legal career, Ms. Campbell is deeply involved in her community. She has volunteered at her children’s schools for many years and has served on the board of directors for their booster programs. She is also a proud sponsor of programs at College Park High School. Since 2020, she has been a member of the Houston Rodeo Souvenir Program Committee, helping to support one of Houston’s most iconic annual events. Ms. Campbell enjoys spending time with her two children – one in college and one in high school – and their cats.

attorneys.name: Paul H. Cannon
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Paul H. Cannon - Creative. Energetic. Compassionate.

"I think that a lot of what drives me to do this kind of work is compassion," Paul says. "I've always been good at listening to people, listening to their complaints, and developing a plan to address their problems. I have a knack for listening to people and not just acknowledging what they have to say but really hearing them and understanding the problems that lie beneath the surface."

Paul believes that his involvement with his past and present churches has helped him develop a compassionate spirit. As a missions leader for his Sunday school class at Second Baptist Church, he volunteered with the Angels of Light project, providing meals and Bibles to less fortunate families. He organized a project that prepared and delivered over 300 sack lunches to the homeless in downtown Houston, coordinated a project to take the children of the Star of Hope Single Mom's Shelter to a hockey game, and organized a team to strip and repaint an elderly wheelchair-bound Houstonian's home. At his present church, Metropolitan Baptist Church, he coordinated a project that involved having the entire Metropolitan Baptist Church's nursery create Mother's Day Cards (about 300) that he and his family then delivered and distributed to Houston nursing home residents.

Paul believes that there is a missions aspect to his work as an attorney, as well.

"There are people who need help, and part of what we do here is to help those people. People who have been injured don't know where to turn, where to go. My job is to step in and help them put their lives back together."

Unlike some lawyers who are primarily concerned about the financial aspect of the case, Paul takes the time to talk with clients and develop a relationship so that he can understand all the ways a case has impacted their lives.

"This enables me to turn around and present their case to the jury in a way that they can fully understand," he explains. "It's not all about money. Part of my client's life has been stripped away. It's about putting their life back together."

Board-certified in personal Injury trial law by the Texas State Board of Legal Specialization, Paul genuinely enjoys the process of litigating cases before a jury.

"The only thing I ever wanted to do was trial law. I actually turned down an opportunity to do appellate work because my desire was to do the trial work. Contract law has no heart or soul. This is riskier, but the reward is a lot higher, too. When you win a case for someone whose life has been turned upside down--it's a good feeling."

Paul Cannon received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Philosophy from the University of Texas and attended South Texas College of Law, where he received his degree in 1995. While in school, he was an active member of the Phi Delta Phi Honorary Legal Fraternity, the Student Bar Association Student Concerns Committee, and the Houston Young Lawyer's Association Environmental Committee.

Paul and his wife were married in 2001 and are the proud parents of two children. They are members of Metropolitan Baptist Church, where they volunteer in the nursery admissions office on Sunday mornings.

attorneys.name: Anthony B. Cantrell
attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Anthony B. Cantrell
attorneys.practice_type: Drug Crime Defense Lawyers in New Braunfels, TX
attorneys.bio:
Anthony Cantrell - "I have always wanted to be in a profession where I could help people. While in college I was wrongfully accused of a minor criminal act. I did not violate the law and fought to clear my name. I was successful and have never forgotten how it feels to be wrongfully accused."

Anthony concentrates his practice in the areas of Criminal Defense. He primarily handles felonies such as Drug Offenses, Homicides, Sexual Assault, White Collar Crime, Parole and Probation matters. Anthony also handles Misdemeanor Offenses such as, Driving While Intoxicated, Theft, and Traffic Violations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Getting to know Anthony Cantrell...

I became a lawyer because...I genuinely wanted to help people.

What I like most about the law is...That it really is common sense the vast majority of the time.

When you need an attorney...Find a lawyer who understands what you are seeking and is then able to get it for you. Communication is essential.

My most rewarding case was...There is no single case. When I get a "not guilty" from the jury it's always great. However, I feel just as exhilarated when we achieve a favorable compromise for a client and he leaves very satisfied.

My most disappointing case was...A capital murder client who was guilty and did not accept a plea bargain that would have spared his life.

I founded the Law Offices of Anthony B. Cantrell because...I want to help people who need a good lawyer to help them solve their problem.

What makes the Law Offices of Anthony B. Cantrell different from other lawyers?...We do our best to help our client by understanding their needs and then getting the job done.

I was very pleased to be described as..."You are someone who cared about me" spoken by a young juvenile in detention.

My friends describe me as...dedicated and smart

My opponents describe me as...relentless on my client's behalf

Someone I really admire is...a friend, Karl Bradick, 84 years old, living on Canyon Lake; Texas truly enjoying and appreciating life that God has given him

My favorite quote is..."Far better it is to dare mighty things, to win glorious triumphs, even though checkered by failure, than to take rank with those poor spirits who neither enjoy much nor suffer much, because they live in the gray twilight that knows not victory or defeat."

When not at work, I enjoy...being with my son.

attorneys.name: Abundio Rene Cantú
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Laredo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Abundio Rene Cantú, a criminal defense lawyer, combines practical experience with extensive legal knowledge to effectively advocate for the accused. During his time in law school, he acquired a deep understanding of federal criminal matters while serving as a law student clerk in the U.S. Attorney’s Office.

Widely Recognized Career In Criminal Justice

After graduating from law school, Abundio started his legal career as an Assistant District Attorney. He dealt with various criminal cases, including drug crimes. From handling minor marijuana offenses to major trafficking crimes, he gained valuable experience. As a result, he became a prosecutor for the 49th Judicial District of Texas.

Defending Those Accused Of Crimes

For over five years, he has been a sole practitioner, utilizing his knowledge and experience to assist clients facing criminal charges. He possesses a comprehensive understanding of the immigration implications for legal permanent residents and noncitizens in the U.S. on visas, including work visas. Being fluent in both Spanish and English, he is frequently sought after to represent individuals, regardless of their ethnicity, who are accused of offenses such as drunk driving, drug crimes and violent crimes.

Discover The Services The Cantu Law Firm Can Provide

Every case and every client is unique and requires individualized review and investigation to determine the most promising way forward. Schedule a consultation by calling or sending an email through this website. Mr. Cantú can meet you at the jail, at his Laredo law office or wherever is most convenient for you.

attorneys.name: Ruben Cardenas
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Matters Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ruben Cardenas is a civil litigation associate practicing eminent domain matters. His practice focuses on representing property owners facing condemnation and ensuring their property rights are protected.

A proud native of the small border town of Del Rio, Texas, Ruben learned early on the value of hard work and helping your community. He graduated from the University of Texas at Austin in 2017 with a Bachelor of Science degree in Communication Studies and a Bachelor of Arts degree in Government, receiving both degrees with high honors. During his time at UT, he was elected by his peers as the Moody College of Communication representative in Student Government and inducted into Phi Beta Kappa. He interned for then-state Senator Sylvia Garcia, U.S. Congressman Lloyd Doggett, and Judge Robert Cadena of the 83rd District Court of Texas. During the Spring 2017 semester, he was selected for the Bill Archer Fellowship Program, where he had the great opportunity to intern at the Supreme Court of the United States in the Office of the Counselor to the Chief Justice in Washington, D.C.

Ruben received his J.D. from the University of Texas School of Law in 2020. During law school, he served as Vice President of the Chicano/Hispanic Law Students Association (CHLSA) and Managing Editor of Notes & Articles for the Texas Hispanic Journal of Law & Policy. After law school, he served as a law clerk to Chief Judge Alia Moses of the United States District Court for the Western District of Texas from 2020 to 2022, where he assisted with handling one of the busiest dockets of any federal court in the country. He joined the Austin office of Marrs Ellis & Hodge LLP in January 2023. Ruben is licensed to practice in Texas and the United States District Court for the Western District of Texas.

attorneys.bio:
When she joined Coker, Robb & Cannon, Family Lawyers, Attorney Lauren A. Cardamone brought her drive to succeed, problem-solving abilities, and love of the law to our entire family law team. A graduate of Texas A&M University, Lauren earned her Bachelor of Arts degree in Philosophy in 2011, where she also made the Dean’s List and became a Gold Member of the Pre-Law Society.

Following her B.A., Attorney Cardamone was then admitted to the Texas A&M University School of Law where she focused on family law early on in her legal career, interning and assisting at multiple family law firms and the Family Law Clinic in the Fort Worth area while obtaining her Juris Doctorate. Lauren earned her J.D. in May 2015.

Before starting here at Coker, Robb & Cannon, Family Lawyers, Attorney Cardamone gained a deeper understanding of the trial process while working assisting with legal orders and motions. She solidified the depth of her knowledge of the law working as a Barbri exam tutor for the states of Texas and New York. She is passionate about helping families navigate the court system and finding positive solutions to delicate family matters.​

Attorney Cardamone enjoys spending her free time with her husband, daughter, and their golden retriever. She particularly enjoys cooking, reading the newest book series, and going to the movies.

Before joining Coker, Robb & Cannon, Family Lawyers, Attorney Cardamone practiced law at another local law firm as a junior associate. While there, Attorney Lauren Cardamone gained valuable expertise in family law matters and a deeper understanding of the trial process while assisting with legal orders and motions.

attorneys.name: Craig Carlson
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in San Marcos, TX
attorneys.bio:
A former JAG Officer with the U.S. Army, Carlson Law Firm Managing Partner, Craig W. Carlson had a vision of legal services deeply rooted in customer service from the very inception of his firm. His dream for a different kind of law firm that put clients first soon became reality, expanding from a single location in Killeen, Texas to 14 statewide office locations, one in Los Angeles, and more to come.

Experience on your side

A graduate from the University of Nebraska College of Law, Lincoln, Carlson left his position of Senior Trial Defense Counsel in the U.S. Army in 1994. The experience he gained in the Army helped him jumpstart his practice in the civilian world, where he focuses on personal injury, mass tort, medical malpractice, and military law.

As a member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, American Association for Justice, American Bar Association and a long list of industry groups, Carlson's continued efforts to learn, teach and improve the legal climate is combined with his desire to offer a voice to injured clients.

Background

When Craig Carlson was young, his family was unable to afford an attorney to represent them against a Nebraska city trying to take a portion of his family's farmland for water rights. Rather than allow this injustice, 12-year-old Craig stood up on behalf of his family. The outcome? His family was able to keep their land and the future Managing Partner of The Carlson Law Firm claimed his first legal victory.

Fast forward to 2021, Craig recovered millions of dollars in damages for injured clients. The achievements of The Carlson Law Firm stem from more than 40 years of hard work to be the voice for clients throughout Texas and the United States. A well-respected attorney in his field, Carlson has been influential in the careers of many up and coming, as well as already established, personal injury attorneys.

For more than four decades, he has represented clients in auto accident, 18-wheeler, product liability, mass tort, and countless other claims.

In the early years of The Carlson Law Firm, clients began turning to Craig for representation because of his budding reputation as a tireless and diligent attorney working to provide his clients with a voice against big industry players. His early successes led to continued growth within the firm-expanding from its Killeen office and a handful of attorneys and staff to now boasting 14 locations across Texas, one in Los Angeles and expanding into Louisiana, more than 40 attorneys, and over 100 legal support staff. Despite the wide reach of The Carlson Law Firm and its Managing Partner, the firm continues to serve clients with the same patron-focused service that has been its standard since opening its doors.

Under Craig's direction, The Carlson Law Firm provides every client with its signature customer service. This top-notch customer service allows the firm to maintain the Managing Partner's long-time promise to everyone who walks into a Carlson Law Firm location, "We care. We can help."

Charity & Involvement

In addition, Craig has long believed that he owes his success to his personal drive to serve his community. As a result, he has always made it a point to hire employees for their heart. Noticing his attorney's off-the-clock charitable work, Craig decided to launch Carlson Cares. Carlson Cares is the charitable initiative of The Carlson Law Firm dedicated to strengthening the communities we serve through building strong relationships with neighbors, friends, and family.

During his decades-long career, Craig has earned several awards and honors. He is recognized as a Super Lawyer and is a member of the Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum.As a member of the Texas Trial Lawyer's Association, American Association for Justice, American Bar Association, Bell County Bar Association, Fort Hood Bar Association, Association of Plaintiff's Interstate Trucking Lawyers and the Christian Legal Society, Carlson stays active within the legal community and continues to regard the experience and knowledge of his peers.

He is also an active member in his local community through membership in the Rotary Club of Killeen Heights where he served as President from 2001-2002, membership in the Association of the United States Army and as a past President of the Greater Fort Hood Area United Way. Additionally, Craig held a position on the Texas A&M University-Central Texas Foundation Board of Directors.

Craig's plans for the successful law firm shows no sign of slowing. Each day, he continues to work diligently to provide clients across the nation the same advocacy that draws clients to his business.

Craig and his wife Vicki are raising four beautiful daughters.

attorneys.name: India Caroll
attorneys.practice_type: Assault Family Violence Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
India Carroll is a Texas criminal defense attorney serving clients throughout Tarrant County and Dallas County and North Texas. She earned her Juris Doctor from the University of North Texas at Dallas College of Law, graduating summa cum laude. During law school, India gained hands-on experience in Dallas criminal courts through internships with the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office and Judge Nancy Mulder of Dallas County Criminal District Court No. 6.

India developed strong advocacy skills through extensive courtroom and appellate training. She competed in four moot court competitions at both the national and international levels, sharpening her abilities in legal research, appellate advocacy, and oral argument—skills that directly translate to effective criminal defense representation in Dallas and surrounding counties.

India was recently admitted to the State Bar of Texas after earning a 99th-percentile score on the Uniform Bar Exam, demonstrating exceptional proficiency in Texas criminal law, constitutional law, and criminal procedure.

Her commitment to criminal defense and civil rights began during her undergraduate studies in Sociology at The University of Texas, where she developed a deep interest in how the criminal justice system impacts individuals and communities across North Texas. India is particularly interested in criminal appeals, post-conviction relief, and protecting the constitutional rights of clients charged with crimes in Tarrant County, Wise County, Johnson County, Denton County, Collin County, and Dallas County courts.

India is proud to begin her legal career at Pantheon Legal Group, a Dallas-Fort Worth-based criminal defense law firm representing clients in Dallas County, Collin County, Denton County, and surrounding North Texas jurisdictions. She works alongside a team of experienced Texas criminal defense attorneys committed to strategic advocacy and personalized client representation.

Outside of work, India enjoys reading, cooking, and spending time with her friends and family in the Dallas–Fort Worth area, along with her two cats.

India is particularly interested in criminal appeals, post-conviction relief, and protecting the constitutional rights of clients charged with crimes in Tarrant County, Wise County, Johnson County, Denton County, Collin County, and Dallas County courts.

India is proud to begin her legal career at Pantheon Legal Group, a Dallas-Fort Worth-based criminal defense law firm representing clients in Dallas County, Collin County, Denton County, and surrounding North Texas jurisdictions. She works alongside a team of experienced Texas criminal defense attorneys committed to strategic advocacy and personalized client representation.

Outside of work, India enjoys reading, cooking, and spending time with her friends and family in the Dallas–Fort Worth area, along with her two cats.

attorneys.name: Christopher W. Carr
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris Carr, an award winning and nationally recognized lawyer, represents injured plaintiffs in catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death cases. He also represents businesses and individuals in high dollar and complex business disputes. He has practiced law in Texas for more than thirty years.

Mr. Carr’s mission is to seek justice for people catastrophically injured or killed by the acts of negligent corporations and businesses.

Since 1994, Mr. Carr has tried approximately 30 cases to Judges, juries and arbitrators. He briefly interrupted his trial practice for a three-year term as General Counsel at USMD Holdings, Inc. and ultimately managed the legal aspects of the sale of that publicly traded company.

His recent trial experience includes:

As a member of the trial team, Mr. Carr directed four of the Plaintiffs’ experts, cross-examined a Defense expert and cross-examined critical defense witnesses in a home explosion trial for the firm’s burned and injured clients in San Antonio, Texas in January and February 2025. The firm obtained a $109.5 million plaintiff’s verdict which is thought to be the largest jury verdict for a personal injury Plaintiff obtained in Bexar County, Texas. Robert Rymers and Viriginia Rymers v. CPS Energy, Cause No. 2021 CI18484 in the 224th Judicial District Court of Bexar County, Texas.

As co-lead trial lawyer, Mr. Carr delivered opening and closing statements to the jury and questioned the majority of the witnesses in a medical malpractice trial for our firm’s paralyzed client in Dallas County, Texas in November and December 2022. The firm obtained a $10.1 million plaintiff’s verdict which was one of the top fifty largest verdicts in Texas (#28 overall) in 2022. Judy “Jessie” and Richard Adams v. Flower Mound Hospital Partners, LLC d/b/a Texas Health Presbyterian Hospital Flower Mound, Cause No. DC-20-17490 in the 68th Judicial District Court of Dallas County, Texas.

As co-lead trial lawyer, Mr. Carr delivered the opening statement to the jury, cross-examined the CEO of the target defendant, and questioned critical witnesses in a quadruple fatality jury trial in Midland County, Texas in May 2021. The firm obtained a $5.9 million plaintiff’s verdict which is believed to be the largest personal injury verdict in the county’s history. Neva Rogers, in all her capacities v. Luis Rangel, Jr. and Dancar Energy Construction, LLC, Cause No. CV54482 in the 385th District Court of Midland County, Texas.

Lead trial lawyer in business arbitration tried in January and February 2021 in which the opposing party sought millions of dollars in damages from the firm’s clients, but recovered only slightly more than $30,000. Jumbo Bag Corp. v. Mark Oliphant and Pangea Packaging, Inc., American Arbitration Association Case No. 01-19-0001-2610.

Mr. Carr has appeared in courts located in approximately twenty different states. He has represented parties through the trial or resolution of hundreds of cases involving, in the aggregate, hundreds of millions of dollars in alleged damages.

Mr. Carr has been honored as a Texas Monthly Super Lawyer more than fifteen times. He has been recognized as one of the Best Lawyers in America in 2024 and 2025. He was part of the trial team recognized for obtaining one of the Top 50 Jury Verdicts in Texas in 2022. He has been recognized as a Lawdragon Top 500 Leading Plaintiff Consumer Lawyer in 2023 – 2025. He was a co-recipient of the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association John Howie Award for the “courageous pursuit of justice in the face of adversity” in 2021.

Mr. Carr is licensed to appear in all state and federal courts in Texas and in the US Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit.

Mr. Carr is committed to ensuring that his clients receive full access to the legal justice system.

attorneys.bio:
Rebecca grew up in Corpus Christi, Texas and graduated from Richard King High School. Rebecca attended Texas A&M University for her undergraduate degree and is proud to be a Fightin' Texas Aggie! She is married to Andrew Carrillo, who is originally from Mesquite, Texas and is also a graduate of Texas A&M University. Rebecca is consistently recognized by her peers for her legal expertise. Rebecca is a strong litigator and is not afraid to go to court and her peers know this about her. She has handled hundreds of cases ranging from the negotiation of a high asset prenuptial agreements to the handling of contentious custody cases. What is unique about Rebecca is that she personally oversees all aspects of your case. You are not just "another file" to Rebecca. She truly cares about protecting what is most important, your children and your financial security. Rebecca's clients respect and appreciate her communication skills and her client centered approach to representation. As one of the best San Antonio divorce attorneys around, Rebecca is not afraid to go trial if your case needs that but she also understands that often the best outcomes are achieved in negotiations or by utilizing other methods outside the courtroom to resolve your case. This is why Rebecca is particularly passionate about Collaborative Divorces because it protects families from the brutality of court. When Rebecca is not in court or working on cases, she enjoys traveling with her husband, snorkeling, and taking her dog Farley to the park. Farley also comes to the office on a daily basis with Rebecca. We consider him the mascot of the office. So, be prepared to be greeted by a happy and lively Boston Terrier when you come to the office.

attorneys.name: J. Michael Carrillo
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Law Lawyers in Decatur, TX
attorneys.bio:
J. Michael (Mike) Carrillo was born in Ennis, Texas and spent his first 15 years there. When he was a sophomore in high school, his dad was transferred to Decatur, Texas. Since that time, Decatur has been considered Mike’s home.

After graduating from Decatur High School in 1987, Mike joined the United States Air Force where he was trained as a dental technician. Shortly after joining the Air Force, Mike married Martha Patterson in 1988, and soon after they shipped off for Spangdahlem, Germany.

While stationed in Germany, the Carrillos welcomed their beautiful daughter Courtney in 1990.

Mike finished his last year of Air Force duty at Laughlin AFB in Del Rio, Texas, where he enjoyed fishing on Lake Amistad. Mike also spent some off time playing baseball in Acuna, Mexico.

After an honorable discharge, Mike and his family moved back to Wise County, where he would attend Weatherford College and the University of North Texas graduating from both with honors. While at the University of North Texas, Mike was a member of the Golden Key National Honor Society, and the business honors society Beta Gamma Sigma. His next stop would be Baylor Law School in Waco, Texas. After Baylor, Mike and his family moved back to Decatur where he has been practicing law for over 20 years. Since being back in Wise County, Mike has been on the Decatur Chamber of Commerce Board, Child Welfare Board, taught CASA volunteer courses, sat on his church’s administrative board, picked up motorcycle riding and earned his private pilot certificate.

Mike is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and a Top 100 member of the American Academy of Attorneys. He also has memberships in the Family Law Section, Criminal Law Section, and Business Law Section of the State Bar of Texas. Mike has been a member of the American Trial Lawyers Association, Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the College of the State Bar of Texas, and the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, and has also completed mediation courses through Dispute Resolution Services. Mike primarily practices Criminal Law, Civil Litigation, Family Law, Business collections, Business Litigation, and mediates Family Law and Civil cases.

*Not Certified By The Texas Board of Legal Specialization

attorneys.name: Nicole Carroll
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Carroll is a highly experienced Southlake family law attorney who serves as senior counsel for Varghese Summersett Family Law Group. She has been practicing law for more than two decades and has vast experience handling multifaceted family law cases, including complex divorce, contentious child custody, and high-asset property division.

Known for her compassionate approach and strong advocacy skills, Nicole has successfully guided hundreds of Southlake individuals and families through challenging legal situations. In some cases, that meant a collaborative approach that kept the case out of court, while in others, it meant a fierce fight before a judge. Her commitment to helping families find the best solution for their unique situation has made her one of the most sought-after family law attorneys in Southlake.

A former law firm owner who herself has been through sensitive family law matters, Nicole understands these cases are not just about legal issues. They have a profound emotional impact on individuals and families. That’s why she handles them with the utmost discretion and care, taking time to listen to clients’ concerns and goals before developing a tailored legal strategy.

Background

In addition to being a highly skilled family law attorney and certified mediator, Nicole is deeply committed to the Southlake community. She has lived in Southlake since 1994, is raising her two children there, and is actively involved in White’s Chapel Methodist Church and loves Dragon football games. Her commitment to her community and her clients makes her an exceptional family law attorney who truly cares about the well-being of those she serves.

Fun Fact: Nicole loves to travel and play tennis.

attorneys.name: Patricia Nellenbach Carter
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Patricia Nellenbach Carter, has over 14 years of dedicated Family Law litigation experience and is board certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, and in 2012 she was granted fellowship in the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers. Texas Monthly magazine has named her as a Super Lawyer for four years and a "Rising Star" among Texas attorneys four years in a row.

Patricia was born in Heidelberg, Germany, to a German mother and career-serviceman father. After spending much of her childhood moving between Europe and the United States, her family settled in Texarkana, Texas, where she graduated from East Texas State University with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration. She obtained her law degree from Texas Tech University School of Law in 1997.

While at Texas Tech, Patricia was a member of the 1996 and 1997 TYLA National Mock Trial and 1996 AAJ Tournament of Champions Mock Trial teams. In 1997, she was an advocate on the first team from Tech to win the TYLA State Moot Court Competition. Patricia also received the Jurisprudence Award for Trial Advocacy and was inducted as a member of the Texas Tech Board of Barristers and the National Order of the Barristers.

After graduation, Patricia served a Judicial Clerkship with Justice Ben Z. Grant of the Sixth District Court of Appeals. In 1998, Patricia married, moved to Houston, and joined a local law firm, becoming a partner in 2001. She joined Short Jenkins Kamin in 2004 and formed Short Carter Morris in 2008. Patricia has authored and presented numerous continuing legal education articles. She is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Houston Bar Association - Family Law Section (member and board member), the State Bar College, Burta Rhodes Raborn Family Law Inns of Court, the Texas Association of Family Law Specialists and the Gulf Coast Family Law Specialists of which she was President from 2011-2012. Patricia is also trained in Collaborative Law, a member of the Collaborative Law Institute of Texas, and is a past chair of the Collaborative Law Section of the Houston Bar Association.

In addition to practicing law, Patricia enjoys spending time with her husband and three children, and reading just about any book she can find.

While at Texas Tech, Patricia was a member of the 1996 and 1997 TYLA National Mock Trial and 1996 AAJ Tournament of Champions Mock Trial teams. In 1997, she was an advocate on the first team from Tech to win the TYLA State Moot Court Competition. Patricia also received the Jurisprudence Award for Trial Advocacy and was inducted as a member of the Texas Tech Board of Barristers and the National Order of the Barristers.

After graduation, Patricia served a Judicial Clerkship with Justice Ben Z. Grant of the Sixth District Court of Appeals. In 1998, Patricia married, moved to Houston, and joined a local law firm, becoming a partner in 2001. She joined Short Jenkins Kamin in 2004 and formed Short Carter Morris in 2008. Patricia has authored and presented numerous continuing legal education articles. She is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Houston Bar Association - Family Law Section (member and board member), the State Bar College, Burta Rhodes Raborn Family Law Inns of Court, the Texas Association of Family Law Specialists and the Gulf Coast Family Law Specialists of which she was President from 2011-2012. Patricia is also trained in Collaborative Law, a member of the Collaborative Law Institute of Texas, and is a past chair of the Collaborative Law Section of the Houston Bar Association.

In addition to practicing law, Patricia enjoys spending time with her husband and three children, and reading just about any book she can find.

attorneys.name: Shawn Carter
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Addison, TX
attorneys.bio:
Shawn Carter is Partner of the BDF Law Group and is based in the Addison location.

Shawn originally joined the firm in 2001 as an associate in the Bankruptcy Department. In December 2014, he left the firm to join the legal department at Nationstar Mortgage LLP known more widely as Mr. Cooper. While at Mr. Cooper, Shawn was instrumental in a complete overhaul of the Bankruptcy Department working closely with management to design both processes and testing for each aspect of bankruptcy file handling from petition date to case closing. He also managed a large portfolio of bankruptcy litigation across all 50 states during the rebuild giving him keen insight into the impact loan servicing has on litigation volumes, outcomes and cost. Shawn worked closely with management in both drafting and implementing the Settlement Agreement and Consent Order Mr. Cooper entered in December 2020. This work led to Shawn becoming the main attorney for the performing servicing business at Mr. Cooper supporting multiple business units such as Escrow, Tax, Insurance, HOA, Cash Application, Payoff, Servicing Transfer and Claims. In February 2026, Shawn rejoined the firm as a partner with his practice focused on multiple areas of the firm’s products and services.

Shawn received his B.A. from Texas A&M University and his J.D. from the University of Houston School of Law. He is licensed to practice law in Texas.

In his free time, Shawn spends his time trying to keep up with his wife Diane and their two daughters Nola and Addie. He enjoys cooking, travel and attending his daughters’ dance recitals and plays at the North Texas Performing Arts theaters. Shawn and Diane have also become regular participants in their daughters’ dance studio production of The Nutcracker every December – the most nerve-racking experience of his life.

attorneys.name: Riley Carter
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Riley Carter is licensed to practice law in the State of Texas. She is a trial attorney in the Dallas office of Rob Wiley, P.C.

Ms. Carter graduated from the Texas Tech University School of Law with Magna Cum Laude honors. During her time in law school, Ms. Carter was a member of the Criminal Defense Clinic where she had the opportunity to represent and serve many clients in the Lubbock area. She honed her advocacy skills by traveling the U.S. competing in National Moot Court Competitions. She also won the intraschool Advanced Mock Trial and Advanced Moot Court competitions in her second year. She served on the Board of Barristers as the Vice Chair of Appellate Advocacy in her third year. Her outstanding advocacy skills won her many awards throughout her law school career: Most Improved Advocate of the First Year Class, “Top Gun” Award: Top Ranked Mock Trial and Moot Court Advocate of the Second Year Class, and Overall Top Oralist Award for Mock Trial and Moot Court. Ms. Carter also excelled academically, being awarded Top Grade and Distinction Awards in multiple classes. Ms. Carter also served as a Texas Tech School of Law Tutor to first year students for two classes. Ms. Carter was chosen to represent the Law School in an official capacity as a Dean’s Ambassador. Outside of the Law School, Ms. Carter felt compelled to serve her community further and was recognized and graduated with the Pro Bono Honor Roll and the Pro Bono Honors Award.

Ms. Carter received her undergraduate degree from Texas Christian University. At Texas Christian University, Ms. Carter was a University Scholar and made the Dean’s Honor List four semesters in a row. Since undergraduate college, Ms. Carter knew she wanted to be an attorney, which prompted her to be a member of the Pre-Law society.

Ms. Carter is a zealous advocate, eager to meet clients and understand their needs. She has an unmatched drive to give her best efforts arguing the law to get results. Ms. Carter deeply understands the hardships that come with having to contact an employment attorney and she is ready to be your voice.

attorneys.name: Brian Casey
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Casey has an AV® Preeminent Rating - the highest rating available from Martindale-Hubbell, the leading independent attorney rating entity.

Before moving to Austin in 2006, Mr. Casey practiced law in Houston and Dallas for eleven years, including six years with a highly respected international law firm. He has tried cases to jury verdict and has prosecuted appeals before appellate courts. His trials have involved contract disputes, fraud and securities claims, real estate and construction matters, and theft of trade secrets allegations. Mr. Casey gained valuable experience while serving on litigation teams for DuPont, Pfizer, Phillip Morris, Koch Industries, and other large companies.

Mr. Casey has written several continuing legal education articles and spoken at state-wide legal seminars. He co-authored "Taking Cover: Preserving Error When Hit With a Claim for Punitive Damages," 47 Baylor Law Review 923 (1995). Mr. Casey graduated summa cum laude from South Texas College of Law in 1995, where he served on the South Texas Law Review, and obtained his B.A. from the University of Texas in 1992.

Mr. Casey is admitted to practice before all state and federal courts in Texas and before the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. He has extensive experience in all areas of litigation, including discovery, motion practice, mediation, arbitration, trial and appeal. He also has significant experience advising clients regarding business law matters, including the drafting and negotiation of agreements.

In addition to intellectual property disputes, he has defended clients accused of industrial espionage in the nuclear medical industry, and even represented plaintiffs whose civil rights were violated by city and county SWAT teams. Mr. Casper also advises clients on other intellectual property matters such as copyrights and trademarks and serves as a liaison between technology clients and their patent attorneys.

In addition to attending Vanderbilt University Law School, Mr. Casper attended the Intellectual Property Summer Institute and Franklin Pierce Law Center, where he had the privilege of learning from the Honorable Gerald J. Mossinghoff, former Assistant Secretary of Commerce, Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks; and from John M. Whealan, former Deputy General Counsel for IP Law and Solicitor at USPTO.

attorneys.name: Miguel Castillo
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mustang Ridge, TX
attorneys.bio:
Miguel Castillo is an experienced family law attorney providing passionate representation for clients going through divorce, child custody, modification, or enforcement cases.

Miguel understands that any legal process that involves one’s family can be emotionally and physically daunting experiences. Accordingly, Miguel’s goal is to provide clarity and compassion to his clients. He believes that each client and their legal issues are unique. For that reason, he focuses his efforts on finding solutions tailored to the challenges presented by each case he handles. Resolving conflicts through negotiation can be an effective method to achieve the most beneficial results for his clients, but when necessary, he also has the skills and resolve necessary to advocate for clients in the courtroom.

Miguel is also a U.S. Marine Corps veteran, and he credits his military experience with forming the foundation of his work ethic as he continues to apply the Corps values of honor, courage, and commitment to his practice of law. It was also during his military service he learned the vital importance of operating as a team. By brainstorming client issues with the team at Weinman & Associates, Miguel is better able to develop a more comprehensive approach to your case. As a result, the quality of service his clients receive is greatly enhanced.

In his free time, Miguel loves spending time with his wife and son, traveling, and nerds out on sci-fi and comics.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Military Service Awards: Combat Action Ribbon, Iraq Campaign Medal, Global War on Terrorism Service Medal, National Defense Service Medal, Sea Service Deployment Ribbon, Navy Unit Commendation, Navy Meritorious Unit Commendation

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Boerne, TX
attorneys.bio:
Christopher D. Cavazos represents individuals facing criminal charges across San Antonio and the surrounding counties. With more than 15 years of experience and thousands of cases handled, he defends clients in matters involving DWI, assaults, drug offenses, juvenile cases, and protective orders. His approach is practical, trial-focused, and grounded in a clear understanding of what is at stake for his clients.

Before entering private practice, Christopher served as a state prosecutor in Atascosa County and was appointed as a special prosecutor in Wilson and Frio Counties. That experience gives him valuable insight into how criminal cases are charged and prosecuted. After completing his service with the county attorney’s office, he co-founded Barrera, Cavazos & Powers with Stephen C. Barrera and Brian T. Powers, combining 40 years of experience to defend those accused of crimes.

Christopher earned his Juris Doctor from St. Mary’s School of Law in San Antonio and holds a Bachelor of Arts in Government from The University of Texas at Austin. He has been recognized by San Antonio Scene as a Top Criminal Defense Lawyer. As a partner at BRCK Criminal Defense Attorneys, he works as part of a team-based defense model to ensure cases are thoroughly prepared and trial-ready.

attorneys.name: J. Shannon Cavers
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Cavers was admitted to the Texas Bar in November 2004. She graduated from South Texas College of Law Houston in the top 1/3rd of her class. Ms. Cavers is a certified family law mediator and member of the Texas Mediator Credentialing Association, parenting facilitator and parenting coordinator.

Ms. Cavers’ professional associations include the American Bar Association, State Bar of Texas Family Law Section, Houston Bar Association Family Law Section, and Fort Bend County Family Law Section. She served the Houston Bar Association as Co-Chair of the Continuing Legal Education Committee and is the Chair-Elect of the Alternative Dispute Resolution Section. Ms. Cavers is an associate in the Burta Rhoads Raborn Family Law Inn of Court, an organization dedicated to professionalism and excellence in family law practice.

Over her career, Ms. Cavers practiced in the areas of civil litigation and health care liability claims. In civil litigation practice, she represented clients such a Sears and Western Auto. Ms. Cavers’ clients also include physicians, hospitals, dentists and chiropractors in health care liability claims and complaints to the professional licensing boards. Nevertheless, her passion is family law. Each case brings unique challenges, and Ms. Cavers partners with her clients to establish his or her goals of representation and the path to achieving those goals.

Ms. Cavers is a long-time member of the Texas Bar College, an organization for judges, lawyers, and paralegals to enhance professional skills.

attorneys.name: Ivan Celis
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ivan Celis is a bilingual, first-generation Mexican American attorney dedicated to helping clients navigate legal challenges with clarity, confidence, and compassion. As an associate at Song Whiddon, PLLC, Ivan focuses on commercial litigation, business disputes, real estate matters, and corporate transactions. He is committed to delivering practical, effective solutions tailored to each client’s goals—whether that means advocating in the courtroom or structuring a sound business agreement.

Ivan’s litigation experience spans pleadings, motion practice, and court appearances. He has represented individuals and businesses in high-stakes disputes, drawing on a strong foundation built during his time as an intern at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, where he assisted in complex enforcement investigations involving insider trading, Ponzi schemes, and market manipulation. His background also includes employment law experience from the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and early exposure to plaintiff-side litigation through his work on catastrophic injury cases at the Law Office of Domingo Garcia.

In addition to litigation, Ivan regularly assists clients with a wide range of corporate and transactional matters, including drafting and negotiating leases, contracts, employment agreements, bylaws, and articles of incorporation. His goal is always to protect clients’ interests while helping them build toward long-term success.

Ivan earned his J.D. from the University of North Texas Dallas College of Law in May 2024 and was licensed to practice in Texas in October 2024. He is admitted to practice in Texas state and federal courts. Ivan is passionate about using his skills to serve and uplift his community, especially through the areas of law he is most dedicated to: business, litigation, and access to justice.

attorneys.name: Stu Chaney
attorneys.practice_type: Condemnation & Eminent Domain Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
J. Stuart Chaney represents landowners in real estate, condemnation, and eminent domain lawsuits. He focuses his practice on representing and protecting Texas property owners facing contract disputes, condemnation, and eminent domain lawsuits. Stu has handled cases involving the taking of ranches, homes, commercial and residential developments, retailers, restaurants, vineyards, hotels, apartment complexes, quarries, gas stations, and convenience stores.

Stu defends Texas landowners against takings by the State of Texas, counties, municipalities, oil and gas companies, pipeline companies, and electric transmission line companies. He has represented property owners facing eminent domain takings at all stages up to and including trial, regularly handling special commissioners’ hearings, contested hearings, and other court proceedings.

Originally from Brownsville, Texas, Stu graduated from the University of Kansas in 2008. He then spent time working for the Texas House of Representatives as a legislative assistant and assistant committee clerk and taught business English to corporate executives in Barcelona, Spain. Stu started with the firm as an intern in 2012, before attending The University of Kansas School of Law, where he graduated in 2016.

He is admitted to practice in Texas, is a member of the Austin Bar Association and the Austin Young Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Dean Chapman
attorneys.practice_type: Oil & Gas Title Opinions Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dean Chapman has practiced law for almost 50 years. He is currently Of Counsel to the firm, in the areas of Real Estate and Oil and Gas Law. Mr. Chapman was formerly a title attorney for Mobil Oil Corporation, Midland, Texas and Houston, Texas (1964-1973). Thereafter, Mr. Chapman was in the private practice of general oil and gas law in Tyler, Texas (1973-1997), including title examination from abstracts and county records; preparing farm-out agreements, assignments and all other documents of conveyance; before becoming "Of Counsel" to the Firm in June, 1997.

While with Mobil Oil Corporation, Mr. Chapman served as Property Acquisition Specialist, responsible for contacting companies for farm-in of their exploration acreage and for purchasing their producing properties. He toured the eastern seaboard of the United States from Maine to Georgia to learn the laws of each state for obtaining off-shore oil and gas lease purchases.

While in Midland, Mr. Chapman served as a lobbyist for Mobil in the State of New Mexico. His close contact with the governor and oil and gas regulatory bodies, along with his attendance at sessions of the legislature kept him abreast of any proposed bills adverse to the oil and gas industry.

Before completing his undergraduate studies, Mr. Chapman served as a Battalion Sergeant Major of the Army Ground Forces during World War II. He obtained his Juris Doctor degree while working full time as a landman for Mobil Oil Company.

attorneys.name: Kimberly Charter
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kimberly Charter was born in Virginia but spent most of her childhood years in Dallas, and currently resides in Wylie, Texas. As an adolescent she was drawn to speech, persuasive writing, and helping others through volunteer work. After high school, Kimberly attended the University of Texas and obtained degrees in government and history. Kimberly’s undergraduate coursework piqued her interest in legal studies, and she enrolled at St. Mary’s University School of Law.

Desiring to make a difference, Kimberly joined St. Mary’s Center for Legal and Social Justice as a research assistant and student attorney for income qualified individuals. While acting as a student attorney, Kimberly gained real life experience in all aspects of case-handling, including interviewing clients, drafting legal documents, and attending court hearings. In addition, Kimberly acted as supervising attorney over the Social Security division of the Civil Justice Clinic. She also served as Vice President of the Family Law Association and received the Pro Bono Leadership Award.

With her degree in hand, Kimberly took a job as an insurance defense attorney, handling personal injury lawsuits. Kimberly gained significant litigation and trial experience while working as a defense attorney. After years of defense work, Kimberly came to realize that she wanted to help give injury victims a voice against powerful insurance companies. She took a job at a personal injury firm representing plaintiffs in personal injury, wrongful death, and medical malpractice lawsuits. Kimberly quickly learned that fighting for the underdogs was her true passion.

Since joining Thompson Law, Kimberly has focused on representing clients involved in personal injury, auto accidents, general negligence, work injury, pedestrian accidents, premises liability, wrongful death, slip & falls, and dog bite cases. Kimberly passionately represents clients and has a proven track record of favorable results. She is motivated to pursue justice for her clients and is a zealous advocate on their behalf.

attorneys.name: Nicolas Chavez
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nicolas Chavez is a co-founding partner of Chavez & Valko, LLP. Nick is Board Certified in Immigration and Nationality Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He is a recognized expert in the immigration and naturalization field, specializing in helping individuals obtain legal status or citizenship in the U.S. With over 20 years of immigration law experience, he has represented a spectrum of clients in securing their immigration status including a Grammy-nominated artist.

A native of El Paso, Nick grew up surrounded by immigration. Both of his parents immigrated to the U.S. from Chihuahua, Mexico. He earned his J.D. from the University of Houston Law Center in 2001, where he also served in the university's immigration clinic under the tutelage of the late Professor Joseph Vail.

Nick has successfully litigated immigration cases before the U.S. immigration courts as well as the federal appellate courts and the Board of Immigration Appeals. He proudly served on the Amicus Curiae Committee for the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) for seven years, advocating in court for legal interpretations that support immigrant rights.

He is regularly invited to speak at lawyer conferences and community events on various immigration topics. He has written numerous publications on immigration law and has been featured in radio and television shows to discuss immigration-related developments relevant to the community.

Nick served as member of the Texas Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee for 14 years. In this role, he investigated and helped bring civil actions against individuals who falsely claim to be licensed attorneys to provide unauthorized services to vulnerable consumers.

In 2023, Nicolas Chavez was selected by his peers for inclusion in the 2024 edition of The Best Lawyers in America® for Immigration Law. Only the top 5% of practicing attorneys nationwide achieved recognition in the 2024 edition of The Best Lawyers in America®.

In 2011, he was appointed as a legal advisor to the Consulate General of Mexico in Dallas, TX, responsible for advising the Consulate of important legal or policy changes affecting the immigrant community.

In 2022, Nick was selected as a Super Lawyer by Thomson Reuters, a distinction given to only 5% of nominated attorneys.

In 2020, Nick was nominated for and became a Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation, one of the highest honors bestowed upon Texas lawyers for their excellent professionalism and dedication to justice in their communities.

Nick is also a published cartoonist. While in law school, he published his first legal cartoon in The National Jurist. "Chavez World" cartoons have been featured in Immigration Law Today (now VOICE), a national publication by AILA. As a legal practitioner, his experiences and insight into immigration naturally inform his subject matter. However, it's the ironical and nonsensical nature of immigration law and policy that lead to the satire of his cartoons.

In 2018, Nick and his law partner Martin Valko founded Lawpilot, a cutting-edge case management software system for immigration law practitioners to assist them in managing their caseload effectively.

attorneys.name: Kerrisa Chelkowski
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
At the Law Office of Kerrisa Chelkowski, smart, knowledgeable, and experienced criminal defense is what you will find. Whether you are charged with a state or federal crime, criminal defense attorney Kerrisa Chelkowski will always strive to ensure your best interests are protected, from the beginning of an investigation to the end of post-conviction.

Being a former prosecutor for the Bexar County District Attorney’s Office and as a Special Prosecutor for the Medina County District Attorney’s Office, Kerrisa Chelkowski has an in-depth understanding of the various strategies the prosecution may use to build a case against you. Kerrisa Chelkowski has been able to prepare criminal defense cases with intelligence, creativity, and special attention to detail.

With hundreds of criminal cases tried before juries and judges in state and federal courts, including appeals involving the death penalty, Kerrisa has been able to prevail among her legal peers on widely publicized cases across Texas, including a dismissal of indictments against her clients involved in the Southwest Airlines case, and representing clients in the Bexar County multi-million dollar class action lawsuit settlement, involving illegal strip searches.

Individuals and businesses seeking exceptional legal representation consistently turn to The Law Office of Kerrisa Chelkowski for a comprehensive and client-centered approach to legal solutions. Renowned for her unwavering commitment to excellence, Kerrisa Chelkowski proudly serves San Antonio, Texas. What sets the firm apart is her emphasis on personalized attention, actively listening to clients’ concerns, and tailoring strategies that align with unique objectives. The client-lawyer relationship is cultivated on a foundation of trust and open communication, fostering an environment where clients feel empowered and informed throughout the legal process. Choosing The Law Office of Kerrisa Chelkowski means opting for a dedicated ally, a commitment to achieving results, and a partnership that places the client’s interests at the forefront.

attorneys.name: Craig D. Cherry
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiff's Personal Injury Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Craig D. Cherry is a shareholder of Haley & Olson, P.C. Craig has obtained significant settlements and verdicts for his clients during his legal career, including verdicts recognized by legal journals as a “Top Texas Verdict” and “Top 100” verdict in the United States.

As a trial lawyer, Craig is triple board certified and focuses his practice on complex civil litigation in multiple areas including business litigation, catastrophic personal injury litigation, wrongful death litigation, product liability litigation, commercial trucking accident litigation, and construction litigation. Craig has successfully represented both individuals and businesses throughout the United States and in Europe.

Craig is Board Certified in Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. He is also Board Certified in both Civil Trial Law and Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Craig’s board certifications are so rare that less than 1% of all lawyers licensed in the State of Texas are triple board certified. Craig has also been appointed by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization to serve as a Member of the Personal Injury Trial Law Exam Commission and the Civil Trial Law Advisory Commission.

Craig has also earned an AV Preeminent Rating (5.0/5.0) from Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review Ratings, which is the highest possible rating a lawyer can earn for both ethical standards and legal ability. This rating was earned only after Craig was reviewed and recommended by judges Craig has appeared before and fellow lawyers Craig has worked with and against in cases.

During his career, Mr. Cherry has earned the respect of his fellow professionals. As evidence of both his advocacy skills and the superior results achieved for his clients, Craig has been recognized by his peers as a Texas “Super Lawyer” for the years 2013 – 2017 and, prior to 2013, as a "Rising Star". He was also invited to become a Fellow in the Litigation Counsel of America, a trial lawyer honorary society composed of less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers and was named a “Top 100” civil trial lawyer by The National Trial Lawyers Association.

In 2005, Mr. Cherry was given the Outstanding Young Lawyer Award by the Waco-McLennan County Young Lawyers Association, an affiliate of the Waco-McLennan County Bar Association. He is a member of the American Association for Justice and The Judge Abner V. McCall American Inn of Court. Active in his community, Mr. Cherry serves as director of the Midway ISD Education Foundation and has previously served as President of the Waco Rotary Club.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: James T. Chiles
attorneys.practice_type: Assault Family Violence Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
James T. Chiles has dedicated his career exclusively to criminal defense here in the Lone Star State. He has several years of experience defending felonies including murder, family violence and domestic assaults, aggravated assault with deadly weapon, sexual assaults and crimes against children, drug crimes, gun charges, and all variety of misdemeanors.

Mr. Chiles has handled hundreds of cases in at least 20 counties throughout the State of Texas, primarily the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex and surrounding counties. He takes particular pride in a high rate of dismissals and not shying away from trial.

Mr. Chiles graduated with a Juris Doctorate from Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law. Mr. Chiles was the Chief of the SMU Criminal Justice Clinic and was a post-bar intern at the Capital Habeas Unit of the Federal Public Defender’s Office, Northern District of Texas. Mr. Chiles has since been in private practice, and has learned criminal defense primarily for working for prominent criminal defense lawyers with decades of experience.

Mr. Chiles was born and raised in Dallas. In college he was the National Debate Tournament Quarter-Finalist. Prior to becoming a lawyer, he coached teams to multiple Texas State and National Championships. Mr. Chiles believes that his experience as champion debater and coach since 2009 excellently contributes to his written and oral advocacy in an aggressive and outside-the-box approach to criminal defense.

Mr. Chiles’ primary area of knowledge is in criminal procedure, the Texas rules of evidence, and the 6th Amendment’s right to confront accusers through the crucible of cross-examination.

attorneys.name: Brett M. Chisum
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brett M. Chisum joined McCathern in 2012 after graduating with honors from Southern Methodist University's Dedman School of Law and was named a partner in 2019. Brett handles a wide variety of both transactional and litigation matters, including drafting company agreements, providing regulatory compliance, pursuing and defending claims based on breach of contract, fraud and misrepresentation, commercial real estate litigation, business disputes concerning shareholders, negligence, violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act, RICO actions, and first-party bad faith litigation.

In particular, Brett represents property owners that suffer damage arising from wind and hail storms, and has successfully obtained millions of dollars for his clients to assist in the repair efforts. In a notable example, Brett's work on behalf of his client Dunhill Partners contributed to the successful defeat of two motions for summary judgement which eventually resulted in a confidential settlement. In a separate 2018 case, Brett successfully represented a commercial property owner that suffered severe hail damage to a multifamily property that also reached a confidential settlement.

In addition to his work on transactional and litigation matters, Brett is part of McCathern's Banking & Mortgage Section, where he focuses on regulatory compliance in the consumer financial services industry. He has provided guidance to his clients regarding the sweeping regulatory changes that occurred with the implementation of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. This included providing legal opinions and drafting various mortgage instruments and disclosures to ensure compliance with the new and updated federal regulations. Brett has also provided counsel in regards to judicial and non-judicial foreclosures, Regulations X and Z, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, and more. In addition to residential real estate work, Brett's work in this section includes representing land developers and financial institutions in litigation involving commercial real estate and commercial leases.

Brett practices in both Federal (all four judicial districts) and State court, and has obtained favorable outcomes representing clients including professional sports franchises, hospitality companies, C-Level executives, commercial property management companies, transportation companies, small businesses, and individuals.

Brett was named to the Texas Super Lawyers Rising Stars list in 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. This list includes the top 2.5% of attorneys under the age of 40 in Texas. In 2019, Brett was also named to the Texas Super Lawyers Rising Stars Up and Coming 100 attorneys in Texas, which recognizes the state's top Rising Stars. He is a member of the Dallas Bar Association (DBA), Dallas Association of Young Lawyers (DAYL) and has served on the advisory board of the Carr Cares Foundation charity founded by Dallas Cowboys cornerback Brandon Carr.

In a notable example, Brett's work on behalf of his client Dunhill Partners contributed to the successful defeat of two motions for summary judgement which eventually resulted in a confidential settlement. In a separate 2018 case, Brett successfully represented a commercial property owner that suffered severe hail damage to a multifamily property that also reached a confidential settlement.

In addition to his work on transactional and litigation matters, Brett is part of McCathern's Banking & Mortgage Section, where he focuses on regulatory compliance in the consumer financial services industry. He has provided guidance to his clients regarding the sweeping regulatory changes that occurred with the implementation of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. This included providing legal opinions and drafting various mortgage instruments and disclosures to ensure compliance with the new and updated federal regulations. Brett has also provided counsel in regards to judicial and non-judicial foreclosures, Regulations X and Z, the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, the Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, and more. In addition to residential real estate work, Brett's work in this section includes representing land developers and financial institutions in litigation involving commercial real estate and commercial leases.

Brett practices in both Federal (all four judicial districts) and State court, and has obtained favorable outcomes representing clients including professional sports franchises, hospitality companies, C-Level executives, commercial property management companies, transportation companies, small businesses, and individuals.

Brett was named to the Texas Super Lawyers Rising Stars list in 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2020. This list includes the top 2.5% of attorneys under the age of 40 in Texas. In 2019, Brett was also named to the Texas Super Lawyers Rising Stars Up and Coming 100 attorneys in Texas, which recognizes the state's top Rising Stars. He is a member of the Dallas Bar Association (DBA), Dallas Association of Young Lawyers (DAYL) and has served on the advisory board of the Carr Cares Foundation charity founded by Dallas Cowboys cornerback Brandon Carr.

attorneys.name: Hengsun (Andy) Cho
attorneys.practice_type: Business Organizations & Corporate Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Andy is a highly experienced attorney with a track record of delivering outstanding legal services to his clients for over 20 years. After obtaining his Bachelor of Science degree from the University of Texas at Austin in 1990, he worked in the field of international business for seven years. This experience gave him a unique perspective on legal issues that affect businesses, which has been invaluable in his legal practice. Andy went on to earn his Juris Doctor from Santa Clara University School of Law in California in 2001.

Andy is a licensed attorney in both Texas and California, as well as a CPA. He has extensive experience in handling a wide range of legal matters, including business organization, immigration law, real estate law, estate planning, and probate. Andy has helped numerous businesses and individuals achieve their legal objectives and navigate complex legal systems with ease. He has been a proud member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association since 2002 and has assisted clients from all over the world in realizing their goals of living and working in the United States.

Andy is fluent in Korean, and he has helped numerous Korean companies set up their businesses in California and Texas. His comprehensive support includes assisting with all legal aspects required for a successful business launch in these states. These services cover guidance on setting up business entities, navigating the intricate legal frameworks in Texas and California, and ensuring compliance with local regulations. Moreover, Andy provides expert advice on acquiring temporary work visas for employees, which is a crucial step for companies that want to bring in their workforce from abroad. With his vast experience working with various Korean companies, Andy offers customized solutions that address the unique challenges each company faces in their expansion journey. This end-to-end legal support ensures a seamless transition for overseas businesses into the U.S. market.

Christensen was a valued attorney at Blazier, Christensen, Browder & Virr, P.C., bringing more than twenty-five years of experience in probate, heirship, and real estate matters, as well as providing essential leadership in the Firm’s day-to-day administration. Known for her exceptional attention to detail and ability to manage complex matters, she played a key role in the Firm’s multi-district antitrust litigation in the 1980s and in the continued success of its client representation.

She is remembered for her professionalism, generosity, and lasting impact on the Firm and the community it serves.

attorneys.name: Brian Christensen
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Throughout his career, Brian has obtained key victories for clients across the country. He began his career as a judicial clerk in state and federal trial courts, including for Chief Judge Roger L. Hunt in the Federal District Court of Nevada. As a law clerk, Brian honed his writing expertise, assisted with numerous civil and criminal trials, and observed the nuances of judicial decision-making firsthand.

In pursuit of litigation at the highest levels, Brian took his career to a corporate law firm in Washington D.C., where he practiced complex commercial litigation, including in suits against multinational banks for their role in the subprime mortgage crisis. He was also a member of the trial team that obtained the largest jury verdict in the United States that year and the largest price-fixing verdict in the country’s history.

Inspired by helping others, Brian then applied himself in service to the public as an Assistant Attorney General for the Utah Office of the Attorney General. Beginning in 2016, he prosecuted anticompetitive and negligent corporate conduct in coordination with federal agencies and states across the country, facilitating the recovery of hundreds of thousands of dollars for injured consumers. Brian also testified numerous times before the Utah legislature, participated as a presenter and panelist in continuing legal education, and counseled harmed individuals and businesses.

Throughout his career, Brian has zealously applied and argued the law on behalf of his clients. When presented in 2021 with the opportunity to help ensure that any client of Arnold & Itkin receives the highest level of appellate support, he embraced it as a natural fit. He brings to Arnold & Itkin’s clients an indefatigable work ethic, extensive appellate experience—including at oral argument—and determination to reach the best possible outcome.

Brian earned a bachelor’s degree from the top-three-ranked accounting program at Brigham Young University. He received his law degree from the J. Reuben Clark Law School at Brigham Young University, where he graduated cum laude and was Lead Note and Comment Editor for the BYU Law Review. His written works appear in that journal as well as the American Antitrust Institute.

A native of Colorado, Brian resides in Salt Lake City, Utah, where he hikes, runs, snowshoes, and skis in its nearby canyons.
