attorneys.name: Derek S. Dees
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Derek S. Dees is an attorney at Deyerle Silva Smith, PLLC. His areas of focus include complex divorce, child custody disputes, marital property division, and other family law issues.

As a child of divorce, Derek knows firsthand the impact family law has on all parties involved. He brings the utmost care to each case as he works diligently to reach an amicable solution for his clients.

Born and raised in Houston, Texas, Derek graduated from Texas A&M University in College Station with a degree in Business Management. Derek received his Doctor of Jurisprudence from Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law in 2014, where he earned the Dean’s Scholarship. While in law school, Derek clerked at a Dallas family law firm which furthered his desire and commitment to practice family law. Derek has extensive litigation experience advocating for clients in complex divorce and child custody matters. His ability to empathize on a personal level about the difficulties of the divorce process enables Derek to positively impact his clients while helping them navigate through stressful situations.

Outside of work, you can find Derek running the trail at Lady Bird Lake, walking his dog, Maverick, and watching all things sports on television.

Derek provides concierge-level legal services to clients across Texas and most often the following areas: Travis County, Williamson County, Hays County, Bastrop County, Bell County, Austin, Westlake, Lakeway, Round Rock, Georgetown, Leander, Cedar Park, Pflugerville, Lago Vista, Bee Cave, Buda, Kyle, and San Marcos.

attorneys.name: Andrew Del Cueto
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Former Prosecutor with Decades of Trial Experience in DWIs and Vehicular Crimes

A fixture on S.A. Scene’s annual Best Lawyers List, Andrew del Cueto, a former felony prosecutor, has been selected by doctors, journalists, and, most notably, other lawyers and judges, to defend their rights in criminal cases. Andrew’s industry-leading expertise in legal research and writing, drafting of motions, and trial strategies have distinguished him over his 12-year career in the practice of criminal law.

After five years working as an Assistant District Attorney in the Bexar County District Attorney’s office, Andrew entered private practice where he defended clients facing charges ranging from shoplifting to murder. Though skilled in all types of federal and state laws, Andrew’s previous tenure as legal counsel for the Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission makes him uniquely qualified when representing clients in alcohol-related cases.

The lifelong San Antonian is a graduate of St. Mary’s University School of Law and is fluent in both written and oral Spanish.

attorneys.name: Sachika “Sachi” Denham
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Sachika “Sachi” Denham-Hand is an eighth-generation Mississippian and the daughter of an immigrant. This dual heritage has fueled Sachi’s passion for immigration advocacy and justice for underserved communities in the United States.

Sachi received her Bachelor of Arts in History with a minor in Spanish from the University of Mississippi in 2018. She continued her legal education, following in her father’s footsteps by attending the University of Mississippi School of Law, where she obtained her Juris Doctor in 2021. To pursue further studies in international law during law school, Sachi studied abroad at Downing College, University of Cambridge, in Cambridge, England, and was involved with several organizations while in law school.

Sachi was also the Executive Editor for the Mississippi Sports Law Review, which deepened her interest in legal writing. During her final year of law school, she externed with the Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services (RAICES) in Dallas, TX, for nearly a year. During that time, she worked with unaccompanied children and adults in removal proceedings and pursued humanitarian relief. Immediately after law school, she joined RAICES as a Staff Attorney. Later, she became a Staff Attorney with the Children’s Immigration Law Academy (CILA), a project of the American Bar Association, before joining Chavez & Valko, LLP.

Sachi lives with her husband, toddler, and dog. She is passionate about animals and enjoys spending quality time with her family, gardening, being outdoors, reading, traveling, and creating art. Sachi has illustrated a children’s book and continues to paint and draw in her spare time.

attorneys.name: Brian M. Dennis
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Litigation and Arbitration Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brian was born in 1978 in Dallas, Texas and was raised in rural Williamson County through high school; graduating from Taylor High School in 1997. Brian attended the University of Texas at Austin and Texas State University (formerly known as Southwest Texas State University). He graduated Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Science degree from SWT in 2002. Brian then attended St. Mary's University School of Law on scholarship and graduated in 2006, near the top of his class. Brian was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2006. He is licensed to practice law in the State Courts in Texas, as well as the United States District Courts in the Southern and Western Districts of Texas.

Brian's practice is entirely devoted to litigation and/trial work. Brian started his career defending doctors and hospitals in medical malpractice claims and lawsuits for one of the largest insurance defense firms in San Antonio at the time. He then shifted to defending drivers on behalf of their insurance companies. Brian now handles claims on behalf of injured Texans, as opposed to those who cause harm and their insurance carriers. Over the past fifteen years, Brian has handled over 1,000 personal injury cases; including claims involving catastrophic injuries and death in the medical malpractice, premises liability, and automobile accident arenas. While Brian has successful first chair trial experience, he also routinely resolves short of the trial through careful case analysis and stategic case development. Given his background, he is a seasoned litigator who fully understands how to navigate the insurance minefield.

Brian also has a significant amount of experience with residential and commercial construction disputes. Brian began working in his grandfather's interior finish-out business during junior high, and he has been involved in constructing his own homes and those of friends since 2005. With this background and his work experience, Brian brings to the table a unique understanding of modern residential construction issues and its many nuances. Today, Brian uses his extensive experience to protect and assert the rights of owners in claims against their contractors, design professionals, builders and component manufacturers related to construction defects, design defects, and manufacturing defects. Representation often begins at the earliest stages and includes advice and guidance during the contracting stage, RCLA process , and arbitration/litigation as necessary.

While construction and personal injury matters fill most of Brian's available time, he also advises clients in other areas of the law, including real estate, products liability, general negligence, nuisance, defamation, slander, libel, contract disputes, insurance disputes (including bad faith), and employment matters. Past clients range from individuals, families, and homeowners, to very large companies and corporations.

attorneys.name: Lowell F. Denton
attorneys.firm_name: Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Municipal Defense Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lowell F. Denton, a partner with Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C., specializes as a litigator in defense of municipalities, counties and other local governments, and as a lead negotiator in labor contracts.

Mr. Denton is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and has close to twenty years of experience in municipal law.He served as the City Attorney for the City of College Station and the City of San Antonio.Prior to establishing the firm of Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C., he served as the chief attorney for Heard, Goggan, Blair & Williams - Government section.Mr. Denton has dedicated his career to the representation and legal defense of local governments and is an experienced litigator, who has developed an expertise in helping city councils avoid litigation.His expertise in the area of municipal defense and litigation is widely known, and he served as the lead attorney for the City of Boerne in the landmark case City of Boerne v. P.F. Flores, Archbishop of San Antonio, and United States, 117 S.Ct. 2157 (1997) regarding the Religious Freedom Restoration Act (RFRA).

Mr. Denton specializes in the representation of local governments as a negotiator in collective bargaining and meet and confer negotiations in fire and police contract negotiations.He has served as the Lead Chief Negotiator for the Cities of San Antonio, Houston, Austin, Galveston, Waco and Corpus Christi, and Bexar County.

In addition to his expertise in the area of municipal defense and collective bargaining, Lowell and his wife Cindy and four children are active partners in the operation of the Four Aces Ranch located near Seguin, Texas where they do general farming and raise quarter horses, cattle, and hogs.

Mr. Denton attended Baylor University where he received his BA and law degree in 1978.He is an active member of Trinity Baptist Church and their missions committee, and is an active board member of the San Antonio Live Stock Exposition.

attorneys.name: Chris Denuna
attorneys.practice_type: DWI Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris is a criminal trial lawyer born and raised in New Orleans, Louisiana. He received a Bachelor’s degree from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro while on a soccer scholarship as a Division I student-athlete. He then attended Charlotte School of Law in Charlotte, North Carolina, and was awarded his Juris Doctorate in 2014.

While attending Charlotte School of Law, he was named to the Dean’s List in 2013 and 2014, participated on the Charlotte School of Law Moot Court and Mock Trial teams, received the CALI Award for Academic Excellence in Trial Practice, graduated with honors from the selective Charlotte School of Law Advanced Criminal Advocacy Program, and accumulated over 340 hours of pro bono service.

He is a member of the National College of DUI Defense, DUI Defense Lawyers Association, American Bar Association, Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, Harris County Criminal Lawyers Association, Houston Bar Association, and the Texas Young Lawyers Association.

Since 2018, Chris has been recognized as a rising star in the Texas legal community for his excellence in the courtroom, including but not limited to being named a Super Lawyers Texas Rising Star by Thomson Reuters and one of the Top 40 Under 40 by The National Trials Lawyers Association.

Chris has earned the American Chemical Society (ACS) Forensic Lawyer-Scientist Designation, as recognized by the Chemistry and the Law Division of the ACS, which is the highest form of scientific recognition available for lawyers. Chris has completed training in Forensic Chromatography: Theory & Practice, Forensic Analysis of Solid Drugs, and Forensic Principles of DUID by Axion Labs and the American Chemical Society.

attorneys.name: Bobby Devadoss
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law -- Employee Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Bobby Devadoss is an experienced and hardworking attorney with a significant background in handling a wide variety of labor and employment cases within the federal sector. After graduating from law school with Cum laude (Honors), Bobby Devadoss, knowing that he wanted to be a labor & employment attorney, accepted a position with the Federal Labor Relations Authority (FLRA) as a federal labor attorney. During his tenure with the FLRA, Attorney Devadoss handled numerous complex cases in just about every area of federal sector labor-employment law. Based on his job performance and his reputation, Attorney Devadoss was approached by Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to join their agency. Attorney Devadoss accepted the position with FAA where he diligently served FAA's management for several years before starting this law firm where he now exclusively represents federal employees.

In an effort to better inform our clients (and potential clients) of Attorney Devadoss' background and qualifications, we have listed below some of the accomplishments, roles, duties and responsibilities that Attorney Devadoss has experienced in his career.

Represented clients in cases involving several aspects of Title VII Discriminations.

Represented clients specifically before federal sector EEOC

Represented clients before the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB).

Represented clients specifically before the federal sector EEOC.

Litigated, Mediated, Negotiated and settled numerous employment discrimination cases.

Served as lead counsel for federal agency in several Unfair Labor Practice proceedings, Negotiability Issues, Grievances, Arbitrations, Mediations and Unemployment hearings.

Conducted Contract Negotiations and provided Interest Based Bargaining training.

Provide guidance and advice to all levels of management on matters including, but not limited to, employee performance, conduct and discipline and claims of reprisal.

Advice management officials on employment decisions that could be subsequently reviewed by the EEOC or MSPB.

Administer and provide guidance to managers on various Union Contracts.

Conducted several highly sensitive investigations concerning alleged Title VII violations.

Personally investigated over 200 Unfair Labor Practice (ULP) charges.

As Counsel for the General Counsel of FLRA, prosecuted several Unfair Labor Practice complaints before Federal Administrative Law Judges.

Administered highly complicated election proceedings and wrote several Decision Orders involving various union representation issues.

Conducted training for several Agencies and Unions on the Federal Labor-Management Statute and Alternative Dispute Resolution & Litigation

Meet Jasmit Dhaliwal, a seasoned attorney specializing in divorce and custody matters in Dallas, Texas. With 14 years of experience, Jasmit has been a steadfast advocate for her clients, navigating the intricate legal terrain of family disputes. Her approach blends strategic legal expertise with a compassionate understanding of the emotional challenges that accompany divorce and custody battles. Known for her commitment to achieving fair resolutions, Jasmit has successfully guided numerous clients through complex divorce proceedings and custody negotiations. Her dedication to protecting the best interests of families sets her apart, making her a trusted ally for those facing the challenges of family law.

Known for her unwavering commitment to justice, Jasmit has navigated complex legal landscapes with a passion for reuniting families and advocating for the rights of immigrants. Her expertise extends to various immigration matters, from asylum cases to deportation defense, and she has earned a reputation for providing compassionate legal guidance. With a deep understanding of family dynamics, Jasmit strives to make a lasting impact on her clients' lives, combining legal prowess with empathy in her pursuit of justice.

Jasmit, an accomplished attorney, is known not only her legal acumen but also for her involvement in various leadership programs in the community. With over a decade of legal experience, she has demonstrated a commitment to civic engagement by participating in leadership initiatives aimed at fostering positive change. She is a proud advocate for community development and has contributed significantly to programs addressing social issues. Jasmit's passion for both the law and community reflects her belief in making a meaningful impact beyond the courtroom, solidifying her reputation as a dedicated and influential figure in Dallas.

attorneys.name: Chris M. “Matt” Dillon
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Bastrop, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris M. "Matt" Dillon is a seventh generation Texan who can trace his Texas roots back to his great-great-great-great-great grandfather, Gordon C. Jennings, who perished defending the Alamo. Chris was raised in Bastrop, Texas, and graduated from Bastrop High in 1990. Unable to resist the urge to continue being a Bear, Chris attended Baylor University where he received his B.B.A. in accounting in 1994. Chris was then accepted into Southwest Texas State University (now Texas State University) where he graduated with an M.B.A in 1996. While working towards his MBA, Chris worked full-time, first as a substitute teacher in Bastrop ISD, then as an analyst with the Texas Workers' Compensation Insurance Fund, and then as a tax examiner with the IRS.

Realizing a dream first echoed at the ripe old age of 12, Chris was accepted into law school and began his course of study in 1997 at St. Mary's University School of Law. Chris earned his doctor of jurisprudence (J.D.) a full semester early and graduated in 1999. While at St. Mary's, he received a Certificate of Completion for The Program Studies on Global Legal Issues at The University of Innsbruck, Austria in 1998, under the direction of his St. Mary's professors and the Chief Justice of the United States Supreme Court, Honorable William H. Rehnquist.

Chris was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in may 2000. In his first year as a lawyer, Chris served as an appellate briefing attorney for the Seventh Court of Appeals of Texas located in Amarillo, Texas, under the direction of Honorable Justice Don H. Reavis. Chris had also previously served as a legal intern for the Honorable John T. Boyd, Chief Justice of the Seventh Court of Appeals of Texas in 1998.

Upon completion of his one year commitment with the court, and in true country lawyer fashion, Chris returned to Bastrop and opened a private law practice where he continues to work to protect the civil liberties of individuals from all around the state of Texas.

Chris has also served as the general counsel for the Lost Pines Golf Club in the historic Bastrop State Park.

attorneys.name: K. Annette Disch
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Bellaire, TX
attorneys.bio:
Partner

Ms. Disch has tried cases to juries and to the bench in Texas state district courts and federal district courts in Texas for over 23 years. She has also arbitrated cases before the American Arbitration Association and local Boards of Realtors, Texas Association of Realtors, and the NASD. In addition, Ms. Disch has successfully handled appeals of summary judgments in the court of appeals. Ms. Disch handles litigation matters throughout the State of Texas.

Industries Served

Ms. Disch has extensive experience representing professionals in litigation matters. Typical clients include commercial and residential real estate agents, brokers, brokerage companies when in litigation in State or Federal Court, Complaints before the Texas Real Estate Commission, Texas Association of Realtors, and various Boards of Realtors. In addition, Ms. Disch represents individuals and/or corporate clients involved in disputes related to real estate whether commercial or residential. Other professional clients include insurance agents/brokers, securities brokers, financial planners, appraisers, mortgage brokers, builders, directors, and other professionals, as well as commercial development, and hotel development and management. Her practice frequently involves representing these professionals in negligence, fraud claims, deceptive trade practices claims, contractual and commission dispute, as well as other industry-specific claims. Recently, Ms. Disch represented real estate companies involved in the NAR litigation. Ms. Disch also handles business disputes, including between businesses and former employees. Ms. Disch is approved panel counsel for numerous insurance carriers. Ms. Disch also frequently advised real estate brokerages on topics ranging from best practices, reducing risk and agent- related issues.

Mediation

Ms. Disch also maintains a mediation practice. She completed mediator training at the AA White Dispute Resolution Center at the University of Houston over a decade ago and enjoys assisting parties find creative resolutions to their legal disputes.

Professional Clerkship

Ms. Disch held a professional clerkship with the 125th Civil District court in Harris County, Texas for 3 ½ years.

Teaching & Writing

Ms. Disch has written courses for the State Bar of Texas including most recently When Good Homes Go Bad: Residential Services Contracts, for the Advanced Consumer Law Course (August 2011). She has also written courses approved by the Texas Real Estate Commission for continuing education.

Professional Representation

attorneys.name: Shara McDonald Dixon
attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Graduating magna cum laude from South Texas College of Law Houston in 2020, Shara is licensed to practice across Texas. She has dedicated her career to serving the communities of Travis and surrounding counties.

Prior to her licensure, Shara had already cultivated a robust foundation in family law through her roles outside the courtroom. During her undergraduate studies at Texas A&M University, she worked as a paralegal at a family law firm. This early exposure not only honed her legal skills but also ignited her passion for assisting individuals during challenging periods of their lives. Further enhancing her legal acumen, she clerked at a distinguished Houston firm known for handling intricate custody and high-value property division cases during her law school tenure.

In her practice, Shara is committed to delivering tailored solutions that meet the specific needs of her clients—whether that be inside the courtroom or at the settlement table. Recognizing the emotional and often stressful circumstances her clients find themselves in, she approaches each case with a blend of legal proficiency and genuine empathy.

Shara’s primary goal is to steer her clients through their legal challenges with a clear understanding of the process and strategic foresight. By integrating her comprehensive knowledge of family law with a compassionate approach, she strives to achieve outcomes that only resolve the legal issue at hand but also promote the well-being of her clients as they embark on their next chapter in their lives.

attorneys.name: T. Ray Dixon
attorneys.firm_name: McCarn, Weir, & Sherwood Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Oil and Gas Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ray Dixon’s practice is focused on oil and gas office practice and oil and gas litigation; in addition, he represents non-profit entities in a wide range of transactions. He is board certified in Oil, Gas and Mineral Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Ray is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Oklahoma Bar Association and the Amarillo Area Bar Association.

Ray has represented oil and gas companies in a wide range of transactional matters including the acquisition of producing and non-producing properties, the sale of producing and non-producing properties, title examination, drafting of agreements among mineral interest owners including joint operating agreements, purchase, and sale agreements, and farmout agreements. In addition, he has represented both producers and financial institutions in the secured financing of oil and gas properties and has represented creditors in foreclosing liens on oil and gas production. He has drafted numerous title opinions over the course of nearly 40 years primarily covering properties in Texas and Oklahoma.

He has spoken at seminars sponsored by the Amarillo Area Young Lawyers Association on several occasions and co-authored a paper entitled Pickering Your Poison which appeared in the State Bar of Texas Oil, Gas and Mineral Law Section Report. Pickering considers the issue of the rules of “electronic contract formation” as applied to oil and gas agreements.

Ray’s litigation experience in the oil and gas area is extensive and wide-ranging including litigation regarding the construction of oil and gas conveyances, assignments, operating agreements, pooling agreements, and deduction of post-production costs from gas royalties. He represented the prevailing party in Judice v. Mewbourne Oil Company in the Supreme Court of Texas—a case widely regarded as one of the ten most significant oil and gas cases decided by the Texas appellate courts.

He represented the prevailing party in Cambridge v. Geodyne Nominee Corporation which was the first Texas appellate case to apply the doctrine of quasi-estoppel to the receipt of royalties from a pooled gas unit. Ray also has extensive experience in litigating issues under the Uniform Commercial Code and represented Amarillo National Bank in the successful appeal of Amarillo National Bank v. Komatsu Zenoah America, Inc. in the United States Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit. Ray is admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, the United States District Court for the District of Colorado, and the United States Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit.

Ray grew up in Blackwell, Oklahoma. After graduating from high school, he attended the University of Oklahoma where he received several academic honors. Then, he graduated with honors from the University of Texas School of Law and was awarded the Order of the Coif. In addition, Ray has an MBA from West Texas A&M University. His community involvement includes numerous years on the Board of Directors of Kids, Incorporated as well as participation in the Big Brothers Big Sisters program.

attorneys.name: David R. Doehring
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
In the often-impersonal landscape of estate law, David Doehring has cultivated a reputation for a rare caliber of stewardship. He meticulously harmonizes high-level intellectual rigor with a protective, vigilant interest in his clients’ outcomes. David doesn’t simply navigate the law; he orchestrates the logistics of legacy with an unerring attention to detail.

What truly sets David apart is his philosophy of total oversight. He understands that his clients are often navigating life’s most sensitive transactions, and he leads his firm to shoulder the cognitive load of the legal process. By proactively identifying and resolving potential exigencies before they ever reach the client’s desk, he insulates his clients from the fatigue of superfluous decision-making. For David and his team, the legal journey is curated and refined, ensuring that every contingency is fortified. It is this synthesis of sophisticated strategy and genuine, proactive care that defines his practice, providing a sanctuary of expertise where a client’s peace of mind is the ultimate priority.

David brings over two decades of experience to his role as Managing Partner of Doehring & Doehring, a family-run firm with nearly 50 years of collective legal expertise. A graduate of Texas Tech University School of Law and certified as both Guardian and Attorney Ad Litem, he is also accredited by the Department of Veterans Affairs. His work encompasses wills, trusts, guardianships, probate administration, and complex estate litigation.

In David's hands, estate planning becomes more than a legal exercise; it is a refined framework that honors a client's legacy while meticulously safeguarding their future. His singular North Star remains constant: the client's best interest, executed with precision, protected with vigilance, and delivered with integrity.

attorneys.name: Richard L. Doehring
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Probate Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Richard Doehring is a founding partner as Doehring & Doehring. He Graduated from The Kinkaid School in Houston, TX in 1961. After graduating from high school he attended Trinity University in San Antonio, TX until graduating in 1966 with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration. Upon graduation from Trinity University he was commissioned a 2nd Lieutenant in the U.S. Army and spent four years on active duty as a helicopter pilot. He is a Vietnam veteran having flown over 700 combat hours in Cobra helicopters. Upon his release from active duty he was employed as a aircraft salesman, flight instructor and officer/pilot in the US Army Reserve while attending law school at South Texas College of Law. He graduated from law school in 1974 and began his law practice in 1975.

Up until November 2000, Richard Doehring practiced law with his brother in the law firm of Doehring & Doehring in Houston, Texas and has continued practice under that name since the death of his brother in November 2000. He continued his practice with his nephew, David R. Doehring. The last twenty-five years of his law practice has been devoted almost exclusively to matters related to probate law with emphasis on dependent administrations. He has had the privilege of being a court appointee as administrator, Receiver, Guardian, and ad litem in many probate matters from all four Harris County probate courts. He has handled probate and related matters in a variety of counties throughout Texas.

attorneys.name: R. Kelly Donaldson
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kelly Donaldson has practiced construction law in Texas since 1986. Prior to 1986 Mr. Donaldson worked in the foundation drilling industry. Today, he represents clients involved in project development, design, engineering, procurement and construction.

Successful projects require thorough planning, proper risk allocation, comprehensive contract documents and efficient resolution of disputes. Construction is complex and experience counts. Mr. Donaldson has experience in both construction and construction law.

Mr. Donaldson represents owners (private and public), engineers, EPC contractors, general contractors, sureties, lenders, subcontractors, suppliers, manufacturers & fabricators. He has experience with projects related to energy (upstream, midstream & downstream); maritime design & construction; heavy civil public works projects, power generation; public works & infrastructure; schools & higher education; industrial; manufacturing; commercial; healthcare; church & religious organizations; and multi-family residential construction.

Representative Work: Project Development, Engineering & Procurement

Detailed Engineering and Design Contracts, including a $2.2 billion offshore platform and related structures in St Johns, Newfoundland

Master Services Agreements for energy-related and industrial projects, including nuclear power plants, oil distribution terminals, refineries and chemical plants.

Engineering, Procurement and Construction Agreements for industrial and energy-related projects.

Design-Build Agreements for commercial projects.

Construction Manager at Risk Agreements for industrial, commercial, and school and higher education, and church projects.

Owner-Contractor Agreements (Stipulated Sum) and General Conditions for the Contract of Construction for industrial, commercial and school and higher education, church, multifamily and custom home projects.

Owner-Contractor Agreements (Cost of the Work Plus a Fee with a Guaranteed Maximum Price) for construction of industrial, commercial, school and higher education, and church projects.

Representative Work: Dispute Resolution Without Litigation

Represented a major chemical company in the resolution of multiple mechanics' and materialmen's liens filed on the project after the termination of the general contractor.

Represented a large school district in Harris County, Texas in extra-work/change order dispute exceeding $800,000.00.

Represented surety after the general contractor/principle defaulted on the construction of a new airport. Issues included scope of work to complete the project, engagement of a replacement contractor to complete the work, reasonable and necessary costs to complete, repair and replacement of defective work, and resolution of payment bond claims asserted by unpaid subcontractors and suppliers.

Represented contractor found in default on the construction of a U.S. Coast Guard facility. Issues included non-compliant HVAC system, questionable start-up and testing procedures, and certified payroll violations.

Represented owner after contractor defaulted on multiple church projects in Harris County and Galveston County, Texas. Issues to resolve included completion of work, unpaid subcontractors and suppliers, false bills-paid affidavits, mechanics and materialmen's liens, and defective work.

Represented construction lender after the design-build contractor defaulted on a church project. Problems included unpaid subcontractors and suppliers, questionable design, mechanics and materialmen's liens, and defective work.

Represented an industrial contractor on a refinery project in Pt. Arthur, Texas, in the termination of a subcontractor found in default of the subcontract. Issues included defective work, unpaid suppliers and engagement of a completion subcontractor.

Represented a county in east Texas in the restoration of a historical courthouse. Issues included non-responsive architect, defective design, failure of contractor to maintain project schedule, and defective work.

Representative Work: Jury Trials

Represented a contractor on industrial project in claim against engineer for delay, disruption, interference, additional and extra work. Jefferson County, Texas.

Represented an industrial sandblasting and coating contractor in claim against coating manufacturer for delay damages and extra work due to defective industrial coatings supplied by the manufacturer and applied to petroleum storage tanks. Jefferson County, Texas.

Represented an owner of a custom home in defective work claim against the contractor. Hardin County, Texas.

Represented industrial contractor accused of violating of violating the Americans With Disabilities Act. Federal Court, Eastern District of Texas, Beaumont Division.

Representative Work: Bench Trials

Represented a general contractor and payment bond surety against claims made by a subcontractor seeking to recover the sums allegedly due the subcontractor . Tarrant County, Texas.

Represented a general contractor in a suit brought by a subcontractor to recover damages for extra work . Dallas County, Texas.

Representative Work: Arbitrations

Represented a steel erection contractor against the general contractor on 13 building prison project in Harris County, Texas. Claims included delay & disruption, extra work and additional work.

Represented the owner against an architect arising out of the design and construction of a new addition to a medical facility. Issues included defective foundation design and structural failure at the intersection of the addition and the existing building.

Represented an owner of a 600,000 sq. ft. concrete tilt-wall warehouse against the design-build contractor. Issues included defective design, unstable sub-grade, foundation failure and structural damage to the concrete wall panels.

Represented owner of custom home against homebuilder asserting claims of defective work, including moisture intrusion, improper site work, defective placement of concrete and numerous other defects.

2 sons and 3 grandsons

Enjoying motocross since 1969

attorneys.name: Debra Donaldson
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Debra is an experienced litigator and appellate attorney whose practice focuses on protecting her client’s interests from trial through appeal in courts throughout Texas and the United States. Over more than two decades of practice, Debra has successfully advocated for clients in commercial litigation, probate litigation, real estate disputes, first-party insurance litigation and coverage matters, and professional malpractice cases. Recognized for her rigorous preparation and sound analysis, District Courts in Harris and other counties routinely appoint Debra as guardian ad litem for minors in civil litigation.

Debra is licensed to practice law in Texas and has been admitted to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York, the Fifth Circuit United States Court of Appeals, and the Second Circuit United States Court of Appeals.

In addition to her experience in private practice, Debra is a former staff attorney for the Texas First District Court of Appeals, where she handled civil and criminal appeals, original proceedings, and motions. She was an adjunct professor of advocacy at South Texas College of Law from 1993 to 1997, and an adjunct professor in the University of Houston Law Center’s legal research and writing program from 1997 to 1998.

Debra graduated from South Texas College of Law in 1993. During law school, Debra served as a Director of the Board of Advocates, was elected to the National Order of Barristers, and earned membership in the Order of Lytae National Honor Society. She was a member of the South Texas Law Review and served as Assistant Research Editor of that prestigious publication. Debra was a member of three first-place national moot court teams, an experience that kindled a love for legal research and written and oral advocacy that has continued to this day.

attorneys.name: Kerri Anderson Donica
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Kerri Anderson Donica
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Family Lawyers in Corsicana, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kerri Anderson Donica has practiced law in Navarro and surrounding counties since 1983. Kerri received her undergraduate degree from Baylor University and her law degree from Baylor Law School. She has focused her practice on family law matters (divorce, child custody, child support, etc.) and the defense of citizens accused of crimes, ranging from DWI to drug offenses to capital murder. Kerri is a frequent speaker throughout the state regarding criminal law issues.

Kerri has served for many years in leadership with the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association (TCDLA), having served as President for the 2019-2020 year and on its board for many years. She is a Super Fellow of TCDLA. Kerri is also a lifetime fellow of the Texas Family Law Bar and is a member of the Texas Bar College, resulting from her continuous dedication to staying up-to-date through additional legal education. She has also been named a Texas “Super Lawyer” for her excellence in the profession.

The Law Office of Kerri Anderson Donica includes three legal assistants - Lauri, who has been with the office since 1997, Tracy and Mylea and a licensed investigator who works on her cases as needed.

Kerri is also very involved in her community, having served as president of the school board for Corsicana I.S.D., is Corsicana's city attorney, and is active in her church, Northside Baptist, for whom she serves as attorney. Kerri has two sons, Hunter (married to Cheyenne) and Heath (who is married to Ashley). Heath and Ashley have blessed her with three perfect precious grandsons – Brooks, Maverick and Jett and Hunter and Cheyenne have added perfect Emma to the boys!

attorneys.name: William B. Doonan
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of William B. Doonan
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Midland, TX
attorneys.bio:
William B. Doonan is the founder of the law firm. Mr. Doonan made a decision early on in his practice of law to focus on family law and further strengthened that decision by becoming Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He saw the need for excellent representation in matters dealing with children, divorces and all the intricacies involved with such matters of the heart. Every situation is different, vital and deserving of detailed attention as the results of family cases have far reaching, life-changing effects on families and children. With offices in both Keller/Ft Worth and Midland, Mr. Doonan is able to provide representation in all areas of family law to select clients throughout Tarrant and Denton Counties and the Permian Basin. Mr. Doonan was admitted to practice law in Texas in 2009, and has also been admitted to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit.

Mr. Doonan's client base is largely comprised of people who are dealing with family law issues. These include divorce, child custody, modification, adoption, enforcement and all other family law related issues. During this process, Mr. Doonan assists his clients with child custody and possession rights, the division of community property, the preservation of separate property, the allocation of marital assets and debts, along with child support, spousal support and alimony. He brings personal attention to every case in advocating zealously for his clients' best interest. With a forceful and knowledgeable courtroom presence, he skillfully guides and represents his clients through courtroom litigation when negotiations have broken down and mediation has not been successful.

In an effort to ensure that his clients are adequately prepared for the future, Mr. Doonan prepares and reviews wills and other estate planning documents. These documents often need to be revised after a divorce or life changing events. He represents his client through the administrative process of probate filings, and also assists with guardianship proceedings when necessary. Highly regarded by his colleagues, Mr. Doonan has received a 10.0 Superb peer review rating through

Avvo along with the honorable SuperLawyers designation. He attended The University of Texas of the Permian Basin and received a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and a Bachelor of Arts in History, both cum laude, and further he earned a Juris Doctorate from the Texas Tech University School of Law.

attorneys.name: Michael Dority
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Throughout his career, Mr. Dority has enjoyed a vast litigation practice that has permitted him to refine his litigation and negotiation skills on a variety of projects. Mr. Dority’s legal experience includes first-chair trial experience, second-chair trial experience, successfully arguing various motions throughout Texas, as well as taking and defending numerous depositions. Prior to joining Mack Injury Attorneys, Mr. Dority spent a decade defending some of the largest companies in the world in lawsuits brought by injured parties and their families. Through this experience, Mr. Dority gained a comprehensive understanding of how corporations and their insurance companies operate and evaluate legal matters.

In 2021, Mr. Dority grew tired of representing large organizations against the “little guy.” In November 2021, Mr. Dority joined Daniel Linebaugh with a desire to tip the scales of justice in favor of injured parties. Using the collective knowledge he gained while working at some of the country’s biggest law firms, Mr. Dority now zealously represents injured parties with unmatched vigor and determination. Michael Dority serves Baytown, La Porte, Mt. Belvieu and many other cities throughout Texas.

Mr. Dority graduated cum laude from the Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law in 2011. While in law school, Mr. Dority competed in both moot court and mock trial competitions and was invited to become a member of the Phi Delta Phi Legal Honors Society. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Dority graduated cum laude with a degree in Business Administration from the University of Texas at San Antonio. Mr. Dority is licensed to practice law in the State of Texas as well as the Southern and Western District Federal Courts. Mr. Dority is a member of the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys, American Association for Justice, Houston Young Lawyers Association, and Houston Bar Association. In his free time, Mr. Dority enjoys spending time with his family, fishing, and playing basketball.

attorneys.name: Cindra Myers Dowd
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
With nearly 30 years of legal experience, attorney Cindra Dowd focuses her professional practice on complex personal injury, product liability and sexual harassment in the workplace. Cindra is also a private pilot certified by the FAA, which gives her practical insight into the firm’s aviation practice. Cindra has also successfully recovered settlements on behalf of employees in cases involving whistleblower protection (qui tam), healthcare fraud, racial discrimination, illegal unpaid overtime practices, and FMLA violations. She has been recognized by Best Lawyers in America for her work in qui tam law, protecting the rights of whistleblowers, and also for her exceptional work in Personal Injury Litigation on behalf of Plaintiffs. Cindra served as a law clerk for the Honorable Hal J. Bonney, Jr. of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Virginia and is a past President of the Tidewater Bankruptcy Bar. Cindra has earned a Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished® rating for High Professional Achievement. Cindra is a committed advocate for the rights of individuals everywhere.

Cindra thrives on helping people during some of the most challenging times of their lives. Whether assisting car accident victims to recoup compensation following a head-on collision or guardrail accident, seniors who have been taken advantage of in nursing homes, or families affected by childhood lead poisoning or a birth injury, she works tirelessly for her clients. Cindra understands the importance of getting into the trenches with clients and fighting for what they deserve.

Cindra has litigated cases throughout the country and joined the Payne Mitchell Ramsey Law Group to continue litigating personal injury cases, product liability cases, whistleblower cases and employment law matters.

attorneys.name: Shannon Drehner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Shannon Drehner was a long-time and experienced chief felony prosecutor at the Harris County DA’s Office. Shannon was assigned as a chief in the Special Crimes Bureau, where she prosecuted Organized Crime. Her responsibilities included the investigation and prosecution of criminals and criminal organizations across Harris County. Shannon was also assigned as a chief felony prosecutor to the trial bureau, where she supervised junior prosecutors. She also managed a docket of 1000 felony cases, from capital murders to simple drug possession.

Before rising to the level of chief felony prosecutor, Shannon was a chief county court prosecutor, where she managed the prosecution of misdemeanor offenses, including DWI, Assault, and drug offenses. During her time at the DA’s Office, Shannon was also assigned to the Family Criminal Law Division, where she prosecuted domestic violence cases.

Prior to her employment at the Harris County District Attorney’s Office, Shannon was a prosecutor in Broward County, Florida. There, she rose to the level of lead felony prosecutor in the Felony Trial Division. While in Florida, she prosecuted DUI, major drug cases, and violent offenders.

Throughout her career, Shannon has tried over 80 jury trials ranging from DWI, drug charges, aggravated assaults, aggravated robberies, sexual assaults, child abuse, murder, and capital murders.

She graduated from Tulane University Law School in 2007. Prior to obtaining her law degree, Shannon obtained a Master's in Asian Studies and Languages at the University of Texas at Austin. Shannon earned her Bachelor of Arts in Japanese at the University of Texas at Austin.

Shannon is currently licensed to practice law in both Texas and Florida. Shannon is also licensed to practice in the United States District Court, Southern District of Texas. She is a member of the Houston Bar Association and the American Bar Association. Shannon also serves as treasurer of the Houston Bar Association Criminal Law and Procedure Section.

In 2024, Shannon was awarded a spot on the coveted Super Lawyers list, a peer review award published by Thomson Reuters. This award validates the outstanding work that Shannon has been doing for years and shows her dedication to her craft and practice.

Stefanie has devoted her career to family law and in addition to her special certifications, she has experience negotiating and litigating divorces, complex property division, pre and post marital agreements, custody, child support, post-divorce modifications, post-divorce enforcements, adoptions and co-habitation agreements.

In her practice, she is frequently called upon to address these issues that pertain to special needs children in divorce an custody. Stefanie understands the unique we bot therapies and special education options available for children with special needs and understands the complex legal issues in divorce for special needs kids.

attorneys.name: Mark Dreyer
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mark received his Bachelors degree in Mathematics and Political Science from Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri. In 1988, Mark graduated with his Juris Doctorate from the University of Tulsa College of Law.

After three years of practice in North Carolina, Mark began working for Lipe & Green, a highly regarded boutique litigation firm that later merged with Conner Winters, one of the largest law firms in Oklahoma. For nearly three decades, Mark honed his skills, became a partner, and earned a reputation for his exceptional litigation acumen. During his tenure, Mark worked on a diverse range of litigation such as propane explosions across the country, products liability, oil & gas industry injury claims, Consumer Product Safety Commission disputes, insurance coverages and catastrophic damages litigation.

Next, Mark became the Lead Counsel - Tort Litigation for Walmart where he managed serious personal injury claims in Florida, Alabama and Georgia.

Over the course of his career, Mark has been admitted pro hac vice in nearly half of the country’s state courts. Mark has also been recognized for many years by Best Lawyers, Super Lawyers, and Benchmark Litigation.

Mark’s influence and interests extend beyond the courtroom; he is an author, contributing articles to reputable legal publications. His written work reflects his commitment to stay at the forefront of legal developments.

Mark is married and has two daughters. In his free time, he relentlessly pursues a quest for perfect barbeque.

attorneys.name: Rodney L. Drinnon
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rodney L. Drinnon is an experienced litigator who handles complex civil litigation in cases in both federal & state courts. He has served as the lead trial lawyer on matters ranging from antitrust actions, contested corporate control disputes, director and officer liability, contract disputes, employment matters (including misappropriation of trade secrets, restrictive covenants, and Department of Labor investigations), insurance coverage questions, and oil and gas litigation. Admitted to practice in Texas, Ohio, and Illinois. Mr. Drinnon has successfully tried cases in over ten jurisdictions throughout the country.

Mr. Drinnon has been instrumental in representing his clients in "bet the company" type litigation. In 2006, Mr. Drinnon obtained a temporary restraining order for the benefit of a Fortune 100 client, preventing its IT provider from effectively shutting down the company's operations due to a dispute over a licensing issue. The matter was subsequently resolved favorably for his client prior to trial.

Mr. Drinnon has regularly represented both employers and former employees in trade secret and non-competition agreement cases. He has taken an active role in defending clients' interests and preventing unfair competition through the improper acquisition of valuable trade information. Most recently, Mr. Drinnon obtained a temporary injunction against a former director of a major marine construction client in Hillsborough County, Florida. The case later resolved via mediation favorably for his client.

Similarly, Mr. Drinnon has obtained summary judgment or dismissals on behalf of employers defending claims of sex, race, age and disability discrimination, as well as harassment, FMLA, and FLSA claims.

In 2004, Mr. Drinnon became one of the youngest attorneys to obtain a favorable judgment from the Ohio Supreme Court on behalf of a major insurance carrier. The case arose when an insured brought suit following a denial of coverage under a policy of professional liability insurance after the insurer discovered material misstatements of fact on the face of the insured's insurance application. Mr. Drinnon obtained summary judgment for the insurer in the trial court and was affirmed by Ohio's First District Court of Appeals. The Ohio Supreme Court certified the narrow issue of whether the insured's material misstatements required malice to void the policy ab initio. Following oral arguments, the Court decided that the insured's material misstatements were so egregious that it could not disturb the lower courts' rulings.

Mr. Drinnon has represented both shareholders and business entities in pursuing and defending claims of minority shareholder oppression, breach of fiduciary duties, and misappropriation of corporate assets. He has assisted clients in extricating them from soured business relationships, recently coined "corporate divorce" actions. Mr. Drinnon has used this experience to assist emerging businesses and entrepreneurs in the formation and growth of their respective business entities to prevent these type of situations.

A former collegiate wrestler, Mr. Drinnon subscribes to the maxim "Proper Preparation Prevents Poor Performance." Whether resolving disputes for Fortune 50 companies or individuals experiencing their first foray into the litigation arena, Mr. Drinnon utilizes an aggressive, reasoned, and practical approach to the practice of law, focused on serving his respective clients' best interests in an economical fashion.

attorneys.name: John K. Drisdale Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Contract Negotiations Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
With more than 40 years of broad-based corporate financing and business law practice behind him, John K. Drisdale brings vast experience to his role as Attorney of Counsel at Blazier, Christensen, Bigelow & Virr, P.C. Specializing in mergers & acquisitions, financing & recapitalizations, corporate & business succession planning, and contract negotiations, Mr. Drisdale is also known for successfully handling legal issues pertaining to private equity, entity restructuring, and commercial real estate acquisitions and sales.

Along with serving as Attorney of Counsel to the Firm, Mr. Drisdale is the principal and solo practitioner at Drisdale Law Firm, PLLC, a boutique corporate law firm in Austin. Prior to going out on his own, he served as general counsel of an international insurance holding company listed on the American Stock Exchange, general counsel and principal in a private equity investment firm with portfolio company revenues exceeding $400,000,000, and partner in the corporate section of a major national law firm.

Measuring success by the outcomes he reaches, Mr. Drisdale has seen many of his clients evolve from small, entrepreneurial businesses to nationally recognized leaders in their industries. He holds the highest peer review Martindale rating for legal skills and ethics.

Mr. Drisdale received his Bachelor of Science degree in Chemical Engineering from Texas A&M University and his law degree from Baylor University, where he graduated Cum Laude in 1979. A native Texan, he and his wife have called Austin home for 25 years and love the city due to its vibrant business community and exceptional quality of life. Active in the local community, he is a volunteer for Lake Travis Crisis Ministries and elsewhere. He and his wife have four grown children.

In his free time, Mr. Drisdale enjoys spending social time with his family, friends and clients.

Kyle is also an Adjunct Professor at Baylor Law and Program Coordinator for the Baylor Law Executive LL.M. in Litigation Management.

Kyle’s prior trial practice included nationwide representation of a major domestic automotive manufacturer and component part manufacturers. He also served as trial counsel for large corporations in the petroleum, agriculture, and consumer beverage industries, among others. In addition to mentoring the team and helping scale the firm’s continued growth and litigation management, Kyle is directly involved in select catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases.

Kyle is a member of the Texas and Oklahoma Bar Associations. He was selected as a Texas Super Lawyer 13 times since 2006 and Best Lawyer in America every year since 2008 (including 2014 “Lawyer of the Year” in personal injury and product liability) until he retired to coordinate the Baylor Law LL.M. in Litigation Management. Kyle was a D Magazine Best Lawyer recipient multiple times, and was also named an original Leon Jaworski Fellow of Baylor Law’s prestigious Practice Court Program.

When he is not practicing law, Kyle enjoys golfing, fly-fishing, and spending time in Park City, Utah. He is married to Wendy May, a lawyer who serves as Chairman of the Board of Directors for iCivics. Together, they have six children, three of whom have graduated from Baylor, one who is at TWU, and another who attends Baylor. Their youngest is a competitive hockey player and baseball player.

attorneys.name: Erica Dryden
attorneys.practice_type: General Counsel Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
“I want to let my clients know all of their options, so that they can make a truly informed decision for their company, their best business decision. My whole family is in business, so I know how to connect with and relate to business owners beyond just being a lawyer. I appreciate how the business and legal worlds can truly blend together.”

Blended Business and Law Litigation

She deals with all aspects of litigation, including pre-litigation, going to trial, and collections afterwards. Her main areas of experience include construction defect cases, property sales, employment issues, such as a breach of a duty or a breach of a non-compete agreement, property disputes, business partner disputes, and breaches of lease agreements.

Many of Erica’s clients are the company or business owners themselves. Her variety of professional experiences and education in business and marketing allow Erica to relate to where her clients’ business and legal needs collide. She is driven to achieve the best possible results for her clients, presenting them with all of their options so that they can make the most informed decisions possible related to their case.

Reliable Team-Player who Cares for the Community

Apart from various professional experiences with international oil and gas corporations, Rice University, and other businesses, Erica also values her volunteer support of local community organizations such as the Entrepreneurship and Community Development Clinic, the Slavic Alliance of Greater Houston, Polish Home Inc., and more. Her experience as a Division I Volleyball athlete continues to influence her driven, can-do work ethic, as she forms a vital part of our team in support of the firm’s clients’ litigation goals.

Clear Communication for Peace of Mind

Erica values keeping her clients updated about the progress of the case with consistent communication, and following up a conversation with an email to confirm that she and her clients are on the same page. She equips her clients with all of the information that they need to know to ensure their sense of satisfaction and peace of mind in the midst of stressful litigation processes.

Demetrio Duarte, Jr. became licensed in the state of Texas in 1984. In 1991 he became board certified in criminal law. His 40 years of legal experience includes over 200 jury trials to verdict in state and federal court, which is why he is proud to call himself a “trial attorney.” Duarte's courtroom experience includes additional trials to the court or non-jury trials and countless pre-trial hearings.

In his 40 years, Duarte has represented clients in the states of Florida, Tennessee, California, Maryland, Illinois, Ohio, Michigan, Mississippi and Virginia. His fluency in Spanish helps Duarte to assist many Spanish-speaking clients who find themselves needing legal representation. Prior to opening his own office, Duarte worked as a prosecutor with the Bexar County District Attorney’s office. It is this very experience, which has helped him see both sides of every case, and earn the respect of his prosecutor peers.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Beaumont, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dan C. Ducote, Jr., is a personal injury attorney and a partner at Law Office of Dan C. Ducote Jr in Beaumont, Texas. He serves clients in and around the Houston region with areas of the law involving:

Product liability

Toxic tort

Medical malpractice

Motor vehicle accidents

Jones Act

Commercial litigation

Antitrust matters

Patent infringement

Obtaining his bachelor’s degree in business administration from Baylor University in 1997, Mr. Ducote pursued his legal studies at South Texas College of Law Houston and earned his Juris Doctor in 2002. He was licensed to practice in Texas the same year. He is also allowed to appear before the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of Texas and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit.

Having tried several cases at trial and appellate courts, Mr. Ducote is well experienced in handling personal injury cases. The expertise he’s gained over the years has earned him a board certification in personal injury law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Rooted in Beaumont, Mr. Ducote is a compassionate attorney who believes in giving back to the community. He cares about the people and businesses in his neighborhood that are affected by legal issues, and he offers them a helping hand in getting the justice they deserve.

Throughout his career, Mr. Ducote has helped his clients recover millions of dollars in personal injury settlements. His clients appreciate the way he explains and guides them through each step of the legal process until the issue is resolved. His legal experience, litigation skills and trial strategies have been recognized by the legal community, for which he has earned an Avvo rating of 10 out of 10.

A licensed practitioner for more than 18 years, Mr. Ducote is a member of many legal associations, including the American Association for Justice, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and the Southeast Texas Trial Lawyers Association. He is also the former director of the Jefferson County Young Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Clifford Duke
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Clifford Winter Duke is a native of the Pacific Northwest, growing up in the Rocky Mountains of Southeast Idaho. He attended Gonzaga University for his undergraduate and law school education, earning his Juris Doctorate in 2004.

He moved to Texas with his wife after graduate school and started practicing law in plaintiff’s work and criminal defense for three years before joining the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office in 2008.

He spent the next seventeen years fighting for the rights of indigent Texans at all levels, from Class C tickets to charges of capital murder.

He is a Past President of the Collin County Young Lawyers Association, the Dallas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, and currently serves as a Director for the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association as well as a Board Member for the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Project (CDLP), training lawyers across the state. Clifford is also a lecturer in Criminal Law for the University of Texas at Dallas. He knows that every case, no matter the level or charge, is the most important to his client and will walk with them as a zealous advocate and counselor every step of the way.

attorneys.name: Steve Dummitt
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Steve Dummitt is a San Antonio personal injury attorney and partner for The Carlson Law Firm who has been aggressively litigating personal injury and commercial disputes on behalf of injured persons and families. Steve has been ensuring your voice is heard against big insurance and other large corporations in San Antonio and throughout Texas since 2012.

Experience on your side

Steve's practice focuses on trucking and commercial vehicle collisions, product liability defect cases with mechanical failure resulting in severe burn injuries, and other traumatic and catastrophic injuries resulting from the negligence of others. Recently, Steve has focused his practice on insurance fraud and e-cigarette explosion cases where the vaping device or battery have failed leading to severe burns and facial injuries.

Steve is a lifetime member of the Million Dollar and Multimillion Dollar Advocates Forum, was recognized for obtaining a top 50 settlement in Texas in 2016, top 50 car wreck verdict in Texas in 2018, was nominated by his peers as The National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40 in 2019, and recently nominated by his peers in Central and South Texas as a San Antonio Monthly Top Attorney for 2020.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Steve was a sales manager for several years in various markets throughout the United States and Puerto Rico. He is fluent in Spanish having served a two-year mission for his church in San Antonio, Austin, and Del Rio from 2002-2004.

In his spare time, Steve enjoys traveling, spending time outdoors with his beautiful wife and son, playing volleyball, and watching Russell Wilson and the Seattle Seahawks as a lifelong member of the 12's.

attorneys.name: Hilary Duncan Supak
attorneys.practice_type: Healthcare Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hilary Supak is an associate attorney with Rivas Goldstein, LLP. Her current practice areas include healthcare, regulatory and administrative law, and administrative appeals. She represents physicians and other healthcare professionals before their respective licensing boards and has experience representing medical service providers and individual practitioners on compliance with health care rules and regulations as well as with various transactional matters.

Ms. Supak graduated from Texas A&M University with a Bachelor of Arts and obtained her Doctor of Jurisprudence from South Texas College of Law. She was admitted to practice in the State of Texas in 2012. Throughout the course of her career, she has represented numerous individuals, businesses, and healthcare professionals in a wide range of litigation matters throughout the State of Texas.

attorneys.name: David E. Dunham
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
David Dunham is board certified in Civil Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and has earned Martindale-Hubbell’s highest possible attorney rating of AV. Mr. Dunham has been recognized seventeen times as a Super Lawyer by Thomson Reuters, including 2023-2016, 2014-2008, 2006, and 2003. He has also been featured in the annual editions of the Super Lawyers Business Edition and in ALM’s Texas’ Top-Rated Lawyers. Mr. Dunham’s work in the area of patent infringement litigation has landed him on ALM’s annual lists as a Top Rated Lawyer in IP Law.

Mr. Dunham is an experienced trial lawyer whose work on behalf of clients at trial has been recognized by the American Lawyer, VerdictSearch.com and topverdict.com in their annual publications. Mr. Dunham has represented business and individuals in the following industries: semiconductor, automotive products, telecommunications, software, medical devices, wireless, real estate transactions, computer peripherals, recreational equipment, securities, gaming and more.

Experience

Clients regularly turn to Mr. Dunham for representation in the following types of cases:

• Shareholder and LLC member and founder disputes

• Breach of contract

• Covenant not to compete matters

• Intellectual property disputes, including patent, trademark and copyright infringement

• Trade secret misappropriation

• Professional liability

• Securities litigation and arbitration

• Partnership disputes

• Unfair competition and false advertising

• Antitrust disputes

Recent Representations by Mr. Dunham Include:

• Fraud and breach of contract case brought by founding investor in company: result at trial resulted in one of the highest verdicts in the state.

• Breach of fiduciary duty and breach of contract case involving founding member of an LLC who had been “squeezed out” by the majority equity owner.

• Breach of contract fraud and defamation case brought by advertising and marketing company; result achieved at trial was one of the largest verdicts in the state.

• Breach of contract and fraud case brought by telecommunications company almost put out of business by one of the largest long-distance carriers in Mexico. Result at trial was one of the largest verdicts in the country.

• Patent Infringement: Represented owners of computer and cell phone patent in five infringement lawsuits brought in the Austin Division of the Western District of Texas. All cases resulted in settlements and licenses.

• Patent Infringement Defense: Represented large, international software company sued on patent infringement claims in the Eastern District of Texas. Case remains pending.

• Trademark Infringement and Defense: Represented Houston-based company in asserting and defending claims of trademark infringement in Houston and Boston. Cases in both Houston and Boston settled.

• Breach of Contract: Represented oil and gas company in lawsuit filed in Houston Division of the Southern District of Texas regarding breach of an acquisition agreement. Case settled early in litigation.

• Professional Liability: Represented United States Bankruptcy Trustee in legal malpractice and breach of fiduciary duty case filed in Austin, Texas. Case settled before trial and was approved by the bankruptcy court.

• Partnership Dispute: Represented partner in federal court in breach of contract and breach of fiduciary duty case.

• Copyright Infringement: Represented company in copyright infringement case filed against music label in Austin Division, Western District of Texas. Case settled early in litigation.

• Shareholder Litigation: Represented shareholder in minority shareholder oppression case filed in Austin, Texas. Case settled before trial.

Community Involvement

• Board Director, Caritas of Austin, a non-profit organization dedicated to fighting poverty, hunger and homelessness.

• Board Director, Concept Services, Inc., an Austin-based restaurant equipment provider serving clients all across the country.

• Advisory Board Director, KLD Energy Technologies, inc., a company headquartered in Austin dedicated to developing clean energy technologies including high-performance electric motor system technology.

attorneys.name: Ron Dupree
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
I began my legal career in the management services division of a large, publicly-traded real estate investment trust. In this role I was responsible for the recruitment, hiring, evaluation, promotion and coaching of all employees reporting to me. As a member of the management team, I was driven to learn everything that I could about employment law to protect the company from liability. During this process I learned that many employment laws are so complex that they often provide no protection for employees at all. I wanted to do something to make sure that employees were treated fairly in our legal system. So, in 2006 I established the Dupree Law Firm with a valuable perspective on how companies approach employment law claims.

I am proud to have represented Texas employees for over a decade in cases before the United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”), in state and federal court and in private arbitrations. I am confident that my unique background has produced favorable results for my clients. The best part of my job is helping employees who have traditionally been shut out of the legal system get the justice that they deserve.

I am a proud graduate of Florida State University where I completed both my undergraduate and law school education. I am licensed to practice law before state courts in Texas and before federal courts including the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, the Western District of Texas, the Northern District of Texas, the Eastern District of Texas and the United States Court of Appeal for the Fifth Circuit.

Outside the office I enjoy spending time with my wife, our two wonderful children and our feisty Miniature Schnauzers.

attorneys.name: Billy Coe Dyer
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Billy Coe Dyer is a board-certified civil trial attorney with more than 30 years of experience representing landowner clients against condemning authorities at the local, county, state, and national levels.

Widely recognized as an authority in the condemnation and eminent domain arenas, Billy’s lengthy list of notable victories includes the largest jury verdict for a property owner in a condemnation case in Texas and representation of the landowner in Interstate Northborough, the Texas Supreme Court case establishing a property owner’s right to recover proximity damages from an interstate highway project, which has been cited more than 300 times since the ruling.

Billy routinely ranks as a top legal expert on industry lists produced by The Best Lawyers in America©, Super Lawyers, and Chambers USA. Most recently, he was recognized by Best Lawyers in America© as the 2024 “Lawyer of the Year” for Eminent Domain and Condemnation Law in Houston. Billy previously achieved this recognition in 2017.

Admitted to practice in all Texas courts, including the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and the U.S. District Courts for the Western and Southern Districts of Texas, Billy earned his J.D. with honors from the University of Texas School of Law and his B.A., summa cum laude, from Trinity University. After graduating law school, Billy completed a judicial clerkship with the Honorable Homer Thornberry, a federal judge on the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Billy is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and achieved this certification by trying condemnation cases.

content: Jury verdict in 2018 for $28.9 million, 2,223% above State’s offer of $1.3 million in a partial takings case for the Grand Parkway; the State took 40 acres out of a 613 acre tract being developed as a residential subdivision in Harris County, Texas, resulting in development changes yielding a lower value; this is believed to be the largest jury verdict for a property owner in a condemnation case ever in the State of Texas (The Texas Lawbook, February 7, 2018); the State appealed, and the Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment for the property owner; subsequently, the Texas Supreme Court denied the State’s petition for review

Jury verdict 265% above the State’s first offer – Jury trial for the owners of a restaurant and a veterinary clinic in whole taking, resulting in a judgment of $9 million, on an offer by the State of $3.4 million; the State appealed, and the Court of Appeals affirmed the judgment for the property owner

attorneys.name: Greg M. Dykeman
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Dan C. Ducote Jr
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Beaumont, TX
attorneys.bio:
Greg Dykeman has practiced civil trial law in Southeast Texas for over 40 years, representing both individuals and businesses in high stakes disputes. He is board certified in Civil Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and has tried more than 100 jury trials in state and federal courts. His practice includes False Claims Act litigation, particularly representing relators in Qui Tam actions, as well as commercial and contract disputes, business torts, probate and fiduciary litigation, and real estate and construction cases.

Mr. Dykeman’s False Claims Act experience includes matters involving defense contracting, inflated pharmaceutical pricing, and logistics fraud, with total recoveries exceeding 65 million dollars. Outside of that work, he regularly handles ownership disputes, breach of contract cases, and litigation between partners, shareholders, and other stakeholders. His experience covers both trial and appellate courts.

He is admitted to practice in all Texas state courts, the United States District Courts for the Eastern, Southern, and Western Districts of Texas, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Dykeman is frequently appointed by judges to serve as a mediator or special master in complex civil matters. He has served the legal profession through roles on the District 3 Grievance Committee for the State Bar of Texas, including as Chairman, and the State Bar Professionalism Committee, where he received the President’s Recognition Award. He is a past President of the Jefferson County Bar Association, the Jefferson County Bar Foundation, and the Jefferson County Young Lawyers Association.

He is also an Eagle Scout. His approach has always been the same: prepare thoroughly, try the case when needed, and stay focused on the result.

attorneys.practice_type: Immigration and Nationality Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
A native of Amarillo, Texas, Mr. Earthman graduated from West Texas A & M University (summa cum laude), with a business degree, and from Texas Tech University School of Law (cum laude). He has been a member of the State Bar of Texas since 2007, and has been admitted to the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas.

Even before joining Reina & Associates, Mr. Earthman practiced immigration and nationality law almost exclusively. He represented clients before the U.S. Citizenship & Immigration Services as well as before U.S. Consulates. He has also appeared on behalf of numerous clients before Immigration Courts nationwide. Mr. Earthman has successfully handled many cancellation of removal cases for permanent and non-permanent residents, withholding of removal claims, VAWA cancellation of removal, adjustment of status application, and NACARA cases. He has also tried numerous TPS de novo claims successfully, and has also represented numerous clients before the Board of Immigration Appeals. He is fluent in Spanish.
