attorneys.bio:
When complex aviation law issues arise, you want a firm on your side that can face these challenges head on. At the office of William G. Harger & Associates, PLLC, we focus our attention on handling cases within the area of aviation law. From our office in Richmond, Texas, we are able to tailor our services to suit clients in Houston, throughout Texas and throughout the United States.

Experienced Representation From A Former Pilot

For even the most skilled attorney, aviation law matters can be incredibly in-depth and complicated. However, these types of issues are made slightly easier due to our founding lawyer’s previous careers. Before becoming a lawyer, attorney Bill Harger was an ATP-rated pilot and aircraft mechanic. This unique, hands-on experience allows him to have insight into the world of aviation law that is unparalleled by most lawyers.

Now with more than 25 years of aviation law experience behind him, Mr. Harger focuses his attention on:

Representing insurance company insured in plane crash and aviation accident cases

Commercial disputes and litigation including breach of contract and aircraft sales

Under his guidance, our firm also handles a wide range of other legal matters, including business litigation and transactions.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Stanton Hargrave
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Compassionate Dallas divorce attorney, Jennifer Stanton Hargrave, has completed the rigorous requirements to become Board Certified in family law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. In addition, she is a member of the Texas Academy of Family Law Specialists, the Dallas Bar Family Law Section and Collaborative Divorce Texas. U.S. News & World Report has included her in their ranking of Best Lawyers since 2012 (2012-2020), and Texas Super Lawyers has included her in their ranking for eight years running, naming her one of the Top 50 Women Attorneys in Texas(2014). She also is AV Preeminent peer-review rated* through Martindale-Hubbell, is a member of the College of the State Bar of Texas and has been a Fellow in the Texas Bar Foundation since 2017. She has been recognized on the D Magazine listing as Best Lawyers in Dallas and, as she began her career in family law, she was repeatedly included as a Texas Rising Star in Texas Monthly Magazine. Jennifer Hargrave is widely respected by her peers, as well as her former clients.

Ms. Hargrave is an experienced Dallas divorce attorney who focuses her practice exclusively on family law, and provides representation to clients throughout the greater Dallas metropolitan area who are either contemplating or going through a divorce. Ms. Hargrave is especially skilled at helping clients construct creative settlement agreements. In a high-conflict, lengthy, antagonistic battle, she knows that the entire family suffers. Based on her background in collaborative divorce, Ms. Hargrave encourages her clients to approach their divorce using non-adversarial techniques to minimize conflict as much as possible, diminishing the destructive effect on the family. She also encourages her clients to hold on to their core values as they go through this stressful process. Ms. Hargrave helps her clients strategize how to work toward the best possible solution, which in turn enables them to better maintain control of the outcomes in their case. Ms. Hargrave helps her clients work towards crafting an outcome that serves her client’s and their family’s interest, specializing in addressing the many different areas involved in a divorce, including:

the division of marital assets and liabilities,

child custody and visitation,

alimony and

child support,

mental health issues, and others,

As a well-seasoned litigator, Ms. Hargrave is also prepared and equipped to provide strong courtroom advocacy when necessary to advocate for her clients. Her priority is protecting her client’s interests.

In addition to her Dallas divorce practice, Ms. Hargrave regularly prepares and reviews prenuptial agreements and cohabitation agreements, and assists clients who are seeking modifications to child support and parenting orders. Highly regarded by her peers for the sensitive and ethical way that she handles these matters, Ms. Hargrave is able to construct creative divorce solutions with opposing attorneys that help our clients reach their goals.

Majoring in political science as an undergraduate, Ms. Hargrave attended the University of California – Davis, and received a Bachelor of Arts in 1992. Her legal education was obtained at SMU Dedman School of Law in Dallas, and she was awarded her Juris Doctor in 1995. After obtaining her law license, Ms. Hargrave worked for a litigation law firm and as an in-house counsel for a financial services company before she felt strongly led to practice family law beginning in 2006. She founded her firm in November 2013. Admitted to the State Bar of Texas, her professional memberships include the Family Law Section of the Dallas Bar Association, the Texas Academy of Family Law Specialists, the Collaborative Law Institute of Texas, and the Dallas Bar Family Law Section, among others.

Jennifer resides in Dallas, Texas, with her husband and three children. She serves in leadership positions in the Episcopal Diocese of Dallas and sits on the Board of Trustees for The Family Place.

Jennifer knows that in family law, there are battles that certainly need to be fought. However, she also knows that the process does not need to be destructive or inevitably end in warfare. “It is important to educate yourself and have an advocate on your side that knows how to use all of the available resources to work towards the very best outcome for your future.”

Hargrave Family Law – Compassionate Dallas Divorce Attorneys

Hargrave Family Law was founded by compassionate Dallas divorce lawyer Jennifer Hargrave with a strong mission in mind. Using non-adversarial techniques, our firm advocates for you during this challenging life transition in a way that helps you protect what matters most. Reach out to our team of compassionate Dallas divorce attorneys at Hargrave Family Law for the support you need to navigate divorce and other family law matters. We offer a complimentary case evaluation to start your journey with us. Together, we will work towards safeguarding the happiness and well-being of your family, allowing you to write your next chapter with hope.

attorneys.name: Marie D. Harlan
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain/Condemnation Cases Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Marie Harlan practices exclusively in the area of eminent domain law, where she helps landowners maximize recoveries and protects their interests when threatened with a governmental acquisition of private property. Her immersion in this area of the law enables her to quickly assess the impacts of both large and small takings and build a case strategy that prioritizes the individual concerns of each client and the unique aspects of each property.

Marie has developed an expertise in inverse condemnation and regulatory takings, confronting governmental entities of many levels when their interference with property rights rises to the level of a violation of protections against takings under the Texas and U.S. Constitutions. Marie has secured millions of dollars in compensation for the firm’s inverse condemnation clients. Marie has also cultivated a high-level appellate practice to defend these clients against the inevitable efforts to dismiss these kinds of claim as a matter of jurisdiction. She has prevailed in multiple appeals, argued before the Fourteenth Court of Appeals, and had a petition for review granted in the Texas Supreme Court.

Marie hails from Austin and is a double alumnus of the University of Texas, earning a bachelor’s degree in Plan II/History and a J.D. in 2014 from the University of Texas School of Law, where she was admitted to the Order of the Coif and served as an Associate Editor on the Texas Law Review. Prior to beginning her eminent domain practice, Marie clerked for U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Jeff Bohm and practiced commercial litigation for two years in the Houston office of Jackson Walker LLP.

Marie has also cultivated a high-level appellate practice to defend these clients against the inevitable efforts to dismiss these kinds of claim as a matter of jurisdiction. She has prevailed in multiple appeals, argued before the Fourteenth Court of Appeals, and had a petition for review granted in the Texas Supreme Court.

Marie hails from Austin and is a double alumnus of the University of Texas, earning a bachelor’s degree in Plan II/History and a J.D. in 2014 from the University of Texas School of Law, where she was admitted to the Order of the Coif and served as an Associate Editor on the Texas Law Review. Prior to beginning her eminent domain practice, Marie clerked for U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Jeff Bohm and practiced commercial litigation for two years in the Houston office of Jackson Walker LLP.

attorneys.bio:
STATEMENT OF PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Amy Harris received her law license from the State Bar of Texas in 2003, and became board certified in family law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in 2011.

Amy is a member of the state bar association, the local bar associations and is frequently appointed by numerous courts to serve as an AMICUS attorney to provide assistance to the Court in determining the best interest of children.

Early in her career, Amy had the most fortunate opportunities to work with and be mentored by some of the most successful and well-respected attorneys in this area of practice. The experiences provided her with the skills, knowledge, and confidence to establish herself in the community and amongst her peers.

In addition to her successes as a lawyer, Amy possesses the compassion and patience necessary to provide the best legal advice and counsel to her clients. She has a knack for accurately assessing a case and determining the most efficient course of action for a client and their case.

Amy has worked with clients having few or uncomplicated issues, to those clients having complex or high conflict issues. She is a zealous advocate for each and every client and devotes the time and personal attention.

While representing clients in litigation before the trial court is an important part of her practice, Ms. Harris also handles appellate matters in the trial court, courts of appeals and Texas Supreme Court. Lawyers frequently consult with Ms. Harris on their litigation cases about specialized legal issues requiring particularized attention both at the trial court and appellate levels. This gives her a unique perspective and depth of perception that benefits both her litigation and appellate clients.

attorneys.name: Anjelica Harris
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bryan, TX
attorneys.bio:
Anjelica Harris is an Associate Attorney at Shane Phelps Law, where she focuses exclusively on criminal defense and Title IX litigation. With a rich background in both prosecution and advocacy, Anjelica brings a balanced and strategic perspective to each case, fiercely protecting the rights of her clients throughout the legal process.

Anjelica earned her law degree from Texas A&M University School of Law in 2020, where she distinguished herself as Associate Managing Editor and Articles Editor of the Texas A&M Law Review.

Her scholarly work on juvenile sentencing reform was published in the Texas A&M Law Review: Anjelica Harris, “We Can’t Just Throw Our Children Away”: A Discussion of the Term-of-Years Sentencing of Juveniles and What Can Be Done in Texas, 7 Tex. A&M L. Rev. 613 (2020).

While in law school, Anjelica gained invaluable experience through internships with the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office, the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas, and as a law clerk for Judge Bob McCoy. She was also a student member of the Innocence Project of Texas, where she worked on wrongful conviction investigations, and completed a post-bar internship with the Travis County Attorney’s Office.

Before joining Shane Phelps Law, Anjelica served as an Assistant District Attorney with the Brazos County District Attorney’s Office from 2020 to 2024, and later with the Grimes County District Attorney’s Office, where she prosecuted a wide range of criminal cases and gained extensive trial experience.

Anjelica graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a double major in English and History. Prior to her legal career, she worked in elementary education and with the United Way of Tarrant County, where she developed her passion for advocacy and public service.

Known for her thorough case preparation, strong courtroom presence, and commitment to justice, Anjelica is a tireless advocate for her clients and a valued member of the Shane Phelps Law team.

Personal Life

When she’s not in the courtroom, Anjelica enjoys unwinding with a great podcast, whether it’s comedy, investigative journalism, or a gripping true crime series. She’s also an avid hiker who loves spending time outdoors and exploring Texas’s scenic trails. A true crime enthusiast at heart, Anjelica also enjoys diving into books and documentaries that explore the complexities of the justice system. And Pickleball, Anjelica loves to play Pickleball.

attorneys.name: Harry "Trey" Harris III
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law​ Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Harry “Trey” Harris, III is a board-certified family law attorney and lifelong Texan with roots in Fort Worth that span three generations. He has practiced law for more than 20 years, representing clients in adoptions, divorce, child custody, child support, CPS cases, complex family litigation, pre-marital agreements, wills, and estate planning. He brings strategic thinking, a strong courtroom presence, and a results-driven approach to cases in Tarrant, Johnson, Parker, and other North Texas counties.

Trey began his career in a large law firm, later co-owning a family law practice before founding The Harris Law Firm in 2012. He blends legal skill with practical insight to give clients honest advice and assertive representation in high-stakes matters.

As a litigator and mediator, Trey works with the courts to resolve disputes through tailored, big-picture solutions. He has taught continuing education courses on enforcement of court orders, co-parenting strategies, and procedural law, sharing his experience with the legal community.

Trey is a divorced father who has earned recognition as a “model co-parent” from colleagues and judges. His personal experience helps him understand the challenges families face during separation. Outside the office, he enjoys aviation, watch collecting, and exploring the connections between law, culture, and the realities of divorce.

attorneys.practice_type: Commercial & Business Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Katie Harrison is an associate in the firm's Dallas office. Her practice consists primarily of civil litigation.

Prior to law school, Katie received her Bachelor of Business Administration degree in Economics and International Business from Baylor University in May 2001. Katie worked as a litigation consultant for Tucker Alan where her work primarily involved compilation of damage models for complex commercial litigation. Katie left Tucker Alan and Texas to attend the University of Montana School of Law in Missoula and in May 2006 received her J.D. After graduation Katie returned home to Texas and began working for Kelly & Nevins, LLP in her hometown of Kerrville where she practiced civil litigation mostly in the areas of real estate, family, commercial and general civil litigation.

attorneys.name: Shelby D. Hart
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denton, TX
attorneys.bio:
Shareholder and Attorney Shelby Hart has long been associated with our firm. He interned with Coker, Robb & Cannon, Family Lawyers while in college and law school, obtaining experience with all facets of the firm as an intern, legal assistant, paralegal, law clerk, attorney, and now shareholder in the firm. While attending the University of Oklahoma College of Law, Shelby attended the University of Oxford, in Oxford, England, over a summer semester to further his legal education. He is also an alum of the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor of Arts in Government.

In 2023, Shelby was named as a Rising Star by the prestigious Super Lawyers magazine. Shelby was also named as Best Lawyers: One To Watch in America for 2022 and 2023. Shelby is incredibly passionate about helping his clients with all types of family law matters and has helped countless families navigate the complexities of family law and reach the best possible outcomes for themselves and their children. Over the years, Shelby has gained a reputation for his ability to handle even the most complex cases with care, skill, and professionalism. Shelby has handled all types of family law matters throughout his career, including but not limited to divorces involving multi-million dollar estates, representing current and past players of the National Football League, child custody, child support, property division, spousal support, marital agreements, enforcements, and adoption. Shelby strives to achieve the best possible outcomes for his clients through careful analysis of their unique circumstances and needs by providing personalized and effective representation to each and every client.

In addition to his work as a family law attorney, Shelby is an active member of the legal community in Collin County with the Collin County Bar Association – Family Law Section and Collin County Young Lawyers Association.

Shelby and his wife are the proud parents of a daughter and two dogs, Rolly and Belle. Mr. Hart is an avid sports fan including watching Texas Longhorns football, his favorite soccer team, Arsenal, Formula 1, and golf. He and his family enjoy traveling and adventuring around the world, visiting all things Disney, and spending time with their pups in the great outdoors.

In the over 12 years Attorney Hart has spent working with Coker, Robb & Cannon, Family Lawyers, he has developed an immense passion for family law matters and cites Attorney Jackie Cannon as one his most inspiring mentors.

attorneys.name: Terry L. Hart
attorneys.firm_name: Terry L. Hart, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Hart came to Houston in 1979 to study law at the University of Houston. After passing the bar exam in 1983, Mr. Hart practiced commercial law in Houston for 13 years. After pursuing an advanced law degree in Europe, Mr. Hart spent 7 years in government service working for the US Government and an international organization, living both in Washington, DC and in Europe. Desiring to return to Houston and to engage in a legal practice that permitted him to become more directly engaged with the lives of his clients, Mr. Hart opened a practice dedicated solely to family law. He currently accept cases in all areas of family law and restricts his practice to the area of family law.

Mr. Hart enjoys getting to know his clients and helping his clients resolve, in a pragmatic way, the sometimes difficult problems, situations and issues that have developed in their lives. While compassionate in his understanding of people's circumstances, he dispassionately considers the most practical and pragmatic options available to his clients and is aggressive in asserting his clients' rights. His goal always is to obtain the most optimal result possible for his client and his client's family under the circumstances and he endeavors to provide the highest quality legal representation possible.

As a lawyer who is fluent in Spanish, Mr. Hart offers significant benefits and an important advantage to Spanish-speaking clients. He brings an international perspective to those clients whose affairs are cross-border in scope.

Mr. Hart and is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the State Bar of Texas Family Law Section, the Houston Bar Association, and the Houston Bar Association Family Law Section. Mr. Hart received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Spanish from the University of California at Berkeley in 1979; a Juris Doctor degree, cum laude, Order of the Coif, from the University of Houston School of Law in 1982; and a Master of Laws degree, cum laude, from the University of Louvain, Belgium in 1997. He is happily married to Nadia Laamarti.

attorneys.name: Allison Hartry
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Allie is a seasoned employment attorney, certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization as a labor and employment law specialist. Allie joined The Morales Firm in 2014, focusing on labor and employment law. Since joining the Firm, she has successfully represented individuals and companies in complex employment law and business litigation matters involving hostile work environment, discrimination, retaliation, unpaid minimum wages and overtime, breach of contract, non-compete agreements, breach of fiduciary duty, and the Family and Medical Leave Act. Allie regularly provides counsel concerning compliance with employment laws and represents companies facing audits by the Department of Labor and Texas Workforce Commission. Allie also has substantial experience reviewing and negotiating severance agreements for employees.

Previously, Allie served as a judicial law clerk to the Honorable Vanessa D. Gilmore of the Southern District of Texas, Houston Division, for the 2012 - 2014 term. Allie graduated from the University of California, Berkeley, School of Law in 2012. In law school, she served as Senior Notes & Comments Editor of the California Law Review and Commentary Editor of the Berkeley Journal of Gender, Law & Justice. She interned for the San Francisco Public Defender's Officer, where she conducted hearings and argued motions as a certified law student. She also participated in several legal clinics, advising people of their rights and assisting in representing them before administrative and state courts.

attorneys.name: Jay Harvey
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
“Our clients come to us because they don't want what has happened to them to happen to another family. They want a system that is accountable to the patient. We work hard to pursue that goal, get fair compensation for our clients and make the medical professional more responsible to the patient. That creates success for us all.”

Jay’s reputation in the personal injury world is unmatched. He has gained the respect of colleagues and adversaries with his tireless efforts to help those who have been injured because of negligence and medical malpractice.

Jay understands that thorough, hard work is the key to helping his clients win against difficult odds. From injuries caused by health care professionals to those catastrophically damaged by the negligence of others, Jay empathizes with his clients and aggressively pursues their rights.

Jay is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Certification as a trial specialist in Personal Injury Trial Law. Board certification is reserved for only the most experienced trial lawyers.

For decades, Jay has fought to improve the laws that impact patients and workers and their rights in Texas. Jay Harvey is past president of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and remains active in the organization. In 2023, Jay received the Champion of Justice award, presented by Texas Watch, a non-partisan citizen advocacy organization dedicated to ensuring that insurance companies and other corporations are accountable to their customers.

In his spare time, he is an avid golfer and biker, loves to travel, work his ranch and spend time with his wife, adult daughter and their two dogs.

attorneys.name: Katherine Hawkins
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Katherine (“Katie”) Hawkins is a dedicated immigration attorney based in North Texas, with a strong commitment to serving diverse communities. She graduated from Texas A&M University School of Law and was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2018. Before pursuing a legal career, Ms. Hawkins worked as an elementary school teacher in South Louisiana, where she taught third and fourth graders.

Ms. Hawkins holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology from Louisiana Tech University, which she utilizes to provide trauma-informed legal care. Her journey into law was inspired by witnessing a grandmother’s determined fight to protect her grandchildren and access the justice system. This experience fueled her passion to bridge the gap between the broader community and the legal world.

During her time at Texas A&M University School of Law, Ms. Hawkins actively participated in the legal clinic, where she served marginalized communities across family law, civil law, and immigration law. Following graduation, she gained experience in various legal fields before dedicating herself exclusively to immigration law in March 2019.

Ms. Hawkins specializes in Family-based Immigration, U-Visas, VAWAs, Naturalization, and Appeals. She approaches each case with the enthusiasm and dedication her clients deserve, working closely with individuals from all backgrounds to navigate the complexities of immigration law. As an active member of the American Immigration Lawyers Association (AILA) and the Immigration Section of the State Bar of Texas, she remains deeply involved in the legal community’s efforts to fight for the rights of immigrants in the United States.

attorneys.name: Hollye H. Hawkins
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hollye is a partner and a member of the firm Leadership Team. She focuses her practice on business, estate planning and probate law, with a particular emphasis on guardianships and contested fiduciary litigation. Known for her practical approach and ability to guide clients through sensitive family and financial matters, she combines sharp legal expertise with genuine compassion.

A cum laude graduate of Texas Tech University and Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law, Hollye has built her career helping individuals and families protect their legacies while resolving complex disputes with clarity and care. Her clients appreciate not only her deep knowledge of the law but also her approachable style and dedication to achieving positive outcomes.

When Hollye steps away from the office, her life continues to be about positive outcomes—but with a lot more cheering involved. She and her husband, Brent, are busy raising their four kids to be motivated, well-grounded Christ followers (with plenty of sports equipment and travel ball weekends thrown in).

The Hawkins crew are full-blown sports junkies. Hollye stays active running, swinging a tennis racket, teeing off on the golf course, and skiing—whether it’s on snow or water depends on the season. Her kids keep the action going with baseball, basketball, and volleyball, while the whole family rallies around them playing on their school and club teams. Saturdays and Sundays in the fall mean football—college or pro—and March brings a family obsession with college hoops. And when it comes to rooting interests, it’s all about the Texas Tech Red Raiders and the SMU Mustangs.

attorneys.bio:
Patrick is the firm's President and Co-Managing Shareholder. His practice is devoted to commercial real estate and corporate/commercial transactions. His real estate practice covers all aspects of commercial real estate, including acquisition, development, financing, leasing and disposition of all product types of commercial real estate. His corporate/commercial practice centers on the formation and restructuring of commercial entities, including corporations, partnerships and limited liability companies, as well as the acquisition, financing and disposition of business enterprises, the preparation of various contracts and agreements, and the representation of clients in their ongoing business activities.

Mrs. Hayward is a 2011 graduate of Ave Maria School of Law and a 2008 graduate of Texas A&M International University where she received a Bachelor of Arts and Sciences Degree. Rebecca practices in state and federal court, representing governmental entities and public officials. Her practice involves defending governmental employers in labor and employment issues including Whistleblower Act, First Amendment, due process, FMLA, and discrimination and harassment claims made pursuant to Title VII, ADEA, ADA and state laws. She represents cities in collective bargaining negotiations with Fire and Police unions, and represents Fire and Police department heads in all aspects of the Texas Civil Service Act, including contested disciplinary proceedings and litigation of civil service issues.

By doing so, he gives himself the perspective to take the case personally and fight for his clients as if they were his own family. Landon knows that each case requires personalized representation specific to each situation. Although clients are simply just another number to the insurance companies, Landon understands that they are loved ones to someone. What happens to his clients matters to him.

One of Landon's notable cases includes him assisting in a carbon-monoxide poisoning case, where it was alleged an apartment complex intentionally bypassed safety cutoffs, causing individuals to succumb to carbon monoxide poisoning. The case settled for a confidential amount on the morning of the trial. In addition, another notable case of Landon's includes the time when he assisted a client in his 50s who was injured in a minor bus accident. The client had a severe TBI from a previous car wreck and found himself in a less than ideal financial position. Through his hard work and compassion, Landon awarded his client over $130,000 in his pocket and assisted him in setting up a savings market account.

Landon remains an outdoor enthusiast when he isn't practicing law, and he enjoys spending his spare time hunting and fishing with his wife and daughter.

attorneys.name: Marilee D. Hazel
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in New Braunfels, TX
attorneys.bio:
As a former assistant district attorney and successful private practice owner, Marilee D. Hazel (formerly Marilee Hazel Brown), provides clients broad expertise in the legal process and a depth of trial experience when cases cannot be resolved outside the courtroom. She makes a difference by looking beyond the ordinary to find creative solutions that work to the best interests of her clients. In private practice, her experience is drawn from having handled hundreds of cases in the tri-county area.

For the past two decades, Ms. Hazel has built a family law and personal injury practice that has helped hundreds of clients successfully resolve high-conflict disputes. The firm's probate and estate practice is also thriving, as Ms. Hazel and her staff work closely with clients to ensure that their rights are zealously protected against all odds. Additionally, Ms. Hazel has successfully represented client's business and tort litigation.

Prior to being in private practice, Ms. Hazel was a highly productive felony prosecutor and chief misdemeanor prosecutor in Lamar County, Texas. Ms. Hazel led all aspects of legal proceedings related to felony and misdemeanor charges. In addition, she was the county's principal juvenile attorney in cases ranging from class B misdemeanors to first degree felonies. She holds a law degree from Texas Tech University School of Law and a Bachelor of Arts in Government and Languages from The University of Texas at Austin.

Marilee Hazel has argued cases in person before the Sixth Court of Appeals, including a nationally debated case in which Marilee Hazel's prosecution was argued and upheld at the Texas Supreme Court. In her appellate practice she has also represented clients before the Third and Thirteenth Courts of Appeal in Texas in criminal matters. Her writings on DWI law and evidence have been published in the Texas District and County Attorneys Association magazine. Her writings on business torts have been published in the Texas State Bar's Business Litigation Journal.

attorneys.name: Kristin M. Hecker
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kristin M. Hecker joined McCathern in 2019 and is rapidly honing her skills in commercial and securities litigation, working with the firm's many experienced litigators in these specific practices. Kristin leverages her extensive study of these fields while a student and law clerk to bolster her work as a dependable counsel for her clients. Additionally, Kristin was a recent participant of the Dallas Association of Young Lawyers (DAYL) 2020 Leadership Class, an annual program that helps young attorneys expand their involvement in the region's business and non-profit landscape.

Kristin started law school at DePaul University before transferring to SMU in Dallas, where she earned her J.D. in 2019. At SMU, she was a member of the International Law Review Association and wrote her law review note on Bitcoin in the European Union. She was also a member of the Phi Delta Phi legal honor society.

While Kristin was earning her J.D., she was a judicial intern for Justice Paul W. Green at the Supreme Court of Texas. There she conducted extensive research into the cases up for Conference, provided detailed recommendations to Justices regarding petitions for review, and wrote case summaries for granted petitions and published opinions.

In addition to her clerkship at the Supreme Court of Texas, Kristin clerked at the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, a national bank regulator along with the FDIC and Federal Reserve, where she analyzed OCC regulations and interpretations and worked with banks, bank counsels and law firms to clarify OCC policies.

Prior to law school Kristin attended DePaul, where she earned a Bachelor Science degree in Finance and a Bachelor of Science degree in Economics and was the only female recipient of the Brian Campbell Finance Endowment at the Driehaus College of Business. She also served on the executive board of Chi Omega sorority, where she began her ongoing philanthropic work with the Make-A-Wish Foundation.

When not practicing law Kristin enjoys Pilates, spending time with her fur babies Rizzo and Hunter, and riding horses at Hillcrest Farm in Argyle, Texas where she is a competitive hunter/jumper equestrian.

attorneys.name: Mark I. Hefter
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Mark Hefter, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
The Law Office of Mark Hefter, P.C. was established in 2007 after Mr. Hefter spent close to twenty years working for two prominent Austin law firms. Mr. Hefter has participated in various trials and settlements on behalf of consumers and their families in multiple venues combined to amount to over $100 million. His experience includes managing a wide-ranging docket of cases including personal injury, wrongful death, products liability, pharmaceutical and commercial litigation. Mr. Hefter has worked as a defense attorney, defending large corporations and working on behalf of large insurance companies. More recently, Mr. Hefter spent close to 15 years working on behalf of victims and their families who had been harmed by wrongful conduct.

Mr. Hefter was born on June 6, 1959, in Houston, Texas where he attended public school. He graduated from Texas A&M University with a degree in Environmental Science and went on to obtain his license in the State of Texas as an architect. He worked as an architect in Houston while attending law school in the evenings. Mr. Hefter was a member of the South Texas Law Review where he was elected Articles Editor. He also received several awards from both the Law Review and the Advocacy programs. Mr. Hefter graduated with honors from South Texas College of Law in 1987, and started his legal career in Austin, Texas with law firm of Clark, Thomas & Winters, where he worked in the appellate, commercial litigation and products liability sections of the firm. In 1993, Mr. Hefter joined the law firm of Shields & Rusk, which later became The Rusk Law Firm, where he worked until the formation of the Law Office of Mark Hefter, P.C.

Mr. Hefter is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in the areas of Personal Injury Law and Consumer and Commercial Law. In addition, he is Board Certified as a Civil Trial Advocate by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. He is a Registered Architect in the State of Texas. He is admitted to practice in all state courts in Texas and the Fifth Circuit, as well as the United States District Courts for the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts. He was awarded an AV rating by Martindale Hubbell for professional excellence in skill and integrity.

attorneys.name: Craig Kyle Hemphill
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Transactions & Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Craig Kyle Hemphill is the founder of Craig Kyle Hemphill Law Offices PLLC. Mr. Hemphill is a fifth generation Texanborn in Dallas on November 4, 1970. He has a decade-plus of academic and applied experience concerning the practice of law, as well as handling business related matters. Mr. Hemphill has served in governmental entities, international law firms, advised small to multinational corporations and represented individuals regarding general corporate matters, regulatory requirements and corporate ethics/compliance concerns within various industries (e.g., energy, construction, manufacturing, etc.)

Mr. Hemphill's overall practice involves handling complex small to large corporate and business transactions concerning, but not limited to, negotiating and structuring large-dollar construction agreements, handling professional service agreements, licensing agreements, finance and purchase agreements, software agreements and securities filings. Specifically, he advises clients in private and public sectors concerning construction industry matters. Such clients include owners, construction industry professionals and construction companies. Mr. Hemphill's expert transactional knowledge also includes structuring, negotiating, drafting and overseeing legal services regarding domestic and international projects involving general corporate matters, regulatory, and ethics compliance concerns.

Mr. Hemphill has commercial litigation and general business litigation experience, including defending and prosecuting construction disputes and tort related matters such as product liability claims.

Mr. Hemphill's public service record includes serving at local and federal levels in the capacity of Assistant City Attorney with the City of Houston's Legal Department/Contracts Division and as a Federal Law Clerk to the Honorable Kenneth M. Hoyt, United States District Court (Southern District of Texas).

Mr. Hemphill is a graduate of Perkins School of Theology, Southern Methodist University, 2009, Cum Laude, where he earned a Masters of Divinity degree in Theology and received the 2009 B'nai B'rith Award in Social Ethics for scholarly competence in the field of social ethics and personal commitment to social causes. Appropriately, his scholarly interests involve researching and writing about social justice issues such as poverty and cultural inclusiveness in relation to ethics, theology, morality, culture and law regarding human rights, civil rights and racial, gender and socio-economic equality concerns.

Mr. Hemphill's academic background also includes earning a Juris Doctor degree, 1999, Magna Cum Laude, finishing third in his graduating class, from Thurgood Marshall School of Law, Texas Southern University, where he served as Editor-in-Chief on the Thurgood Marshall Law Review, 1997-1999. Accordingly, legal analysis and critical thinking largely influence his academic thought in relation to examining intersections of the law, culture, ethics, theology and politics. Mr. Hemphill's legal scholarship leans on a mixture of religious discourse and legal rationales toward examining and explaining social justice issues in relation to poverty and altruistic goals of cultural inclusiveness regarding human rights, civil rights and racial, gender and socio-economic equality concerns. He also holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Economics, 1995, from the College of Business Administration, University of Texas at Arlington. Thus, economic understandings also influence his research and writing.

Mr. Hemphill's teaching experiences to date include serving as an adjunct ethics, business law and management and labor relations professor in the University of Houston Systems. He has also lectured in the areas of Tort and Constitutional Law as a Student Assistant during his legal studies at Thurgood Marshall School of Law, Texas Southern University. Mr. Hemphill has served as a guest lecturer in Christian History and Systematic Theology courses at Houston Graduate School of Theology.

Mr. Hemphill has published. He enjoys the distinction of his work cited as scholarly authority in the area of Tort Reform.Mr. Hemphill has primarily presented lectures on construction law matters throughout the States of Texas and Minnesota. In line with his ecumenical and academic roles, he has presented papers and lectures within the U.S. and internationally on topics in ethics and social justice in forums such as Prague, Czech Republic.

Mr. Hemphill is a licensed and ordained minister in the Missionary Baptist tradition (Southern and National Baptist Conferences). Reverend Hemphill has served as an associate minister at numerous local church congregations in Dallas and Houston. His roles in the church include serving on boards (e.g., board of Christian education), charring various men's ministries, serving as a Sunday school teacher and providing legal representation to church congregations as corporate counsel. Reverend is also the founder of several non-profit entities, Sober Cup Coffee Foundation, Project F.O.R.K. L.I.F.T. Foundation and The Golden Rule Legal Foundation, all of which serve as social justice ministries.

Mr. Hemphill holds licenses to practice law and appear before federal and state courts. His law licenses include the privilege to appear before the United States Supreme Court, the District of Minnesota, the Northern and Southern Districts of Texas, the State Bar of Minnesota and the State Bar of Texas.

attorneys.name: Kevin Henrichson
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kevin Henrichson Represents Victims of Serious Accidents.

Kevin Henrichson is proud to be named among the 10 Best Personal Injury Lawyers in Client Satisfaction in 2019 by the American Institute of Personal Injury Attorneys. He has also been named a "Super Lawyer" in the area of personal injury by Texas Monthly magazine every year from 2017-2019. Candidates for Super Lawyers’ recognition are evaluated on twelve indicators of Professional Achievement and Peer Recognition, and only 5% of attorneys in Texas are selected. He was also recognized as a “Rising Star” in 2005, 2006, 2007, 2008, 2013 and 2014, a distinction which only 2.5% of attorneys in Texas earn. Super Lawyers and Rising Stars are chosen by Thomson Reuters.

Henrichson's success in the courtroom has led to his invitation for acceptance into the prestigious, American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA). Lawyers must be invited for admittance into ABOTA and meet rigorous requirements of trial experience, ability, civility and professionalism.

Kevin Henrichson grew up knowing that he wanted to follow in the family tradition of serving the public as an attorney. His father, Preston Henrichson practices law in the same building that his grandfather, EG Henrichson practiced for more than 40 years.

“I was enamored with my father’s career because it seemed like he was always doing something important,” Henrichson recalls. “I just thought that was inspiring to watch.”

Henrichson learned at a very young age that good lawyers do more for their clients than just provide legal advice.

“I remember when I was a kid, on my dad’s building it said, ‘Attorneys and counselors,’” Henrichson said. “I really didn’t understand that then, but I’ve learned that there really is a counselor element to the practice of law for my clients. Many times, they need to have someone to hold their hand through the process. There is so much anxiety if they are out of work and have financial stress. So there’s a lot of counsel that goes into being a good plaintiff’s lawyer, not just legal counsel.”

In 1997, after obtaining an undergraduate degree in finance from Texas A&M, Henrichson went straight to St. Mary’s University School of Law. He wrote for the St. Mary’s Law Journal and won first place in the school’s mock trial competition. During law school, he interned for the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. Henrichson graduated at the top of his class in 2001.

Trial Experience and Notable Cases

With his strong academic performance, Henrichson had a range of employment options after getting his J.D., and he knew he wanted to get trial experience as soon as possible. He came to Austin and joined a solo practitioner who let him do just that—in his first year practicing law, Henrichson tried five jury trials by himself and won them all.

A year later, he joined Byrd Davis Alden & Henrichson, LLP and has been focusing his practice on serious personal injury litigation ever since. He has handled many noteworthy cases. For example:

He obtained the second largest jury verdict ($8.2 Million) in Texas for a motor vehicle accident in 2011. This reflects the jury’s verdict at trial and not the amount actually recovered by the client. The case was settled after trial for a confidential amount.

He received the first jury verdict in Williamson County for civil damages for aiding in the concealment of an abducted child.

He recently obtained a settlement ($883,942 to client after attorney’s fees and case expenses) on behalf of a bicyclist who seriously injured when struck by a car. Liability was disputed and advanced accident reconstruction was used to prove the case.

Success From Tireless Preparation

To Henrichson, the most important key to success as a trial lawyer is tireless preparation.

“Before you go to trial, there’s nothing fun about it,” he says. “You’re working all day and all night for weeks in order to be prepared. Once you walk into the courtroom, you have pre-planned every step of the trial. And then it’s fun. It’s really, really fun to be able to try a case after you’ve prepared for so long and worked so hard.”

Outdoor Activities and Family Time

Henrichson says that nothing in life is quite like trying a difficult case in court. But he also enjoys outdoors activities—boating, hiking, fishing—and family time, which includes raising a young daughter with his wife, Kate Henrichson.

Henrichson is a Barrister in the Robert W. Calvert Inn of Court and a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the Capital Area Trial Lawyers Association, and the Austin Bar Association.

He is admitted to practice law by the State Bar of Texas, and the United States District Courts for the Western and Southern Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Robert L. Henry
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
I am a Personal Injury/Civil Trial Attorney based in the Dallas/Fort Worth Metroplex area. I handle all matters of civil litigation. The majority of my cases are plaintiff/personal injury but I also handle other types of cases related to general civil litigation. I have worked on a wide variety of cases from catastrophic and traumatic brain injury cases to complex commercial and business disputes. Although my practice is based in DFW, I am also proud to serve the surrounding areas and have been involved in litigation throughout the State of Texas. I was born and raised in Fort Worth and went to college at Texas Tech University where I obtained a JD/MBA. After graduation I returned home to Fort Worth. I treat all of my clients with honesty and respect. Unfortunately, lots of times this means telling them something they do not want to hear. Every case is important to me. The most rewarding part of my job is helping someone work through a problem or challenge that he or she is facing. I believe very strongly that litigation should always be used as a last resort, but unfortunately, often times it is necessary.

attorneys.name: Diana Henry
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio:
Diana primarily practices in the areas of civil insurance defense and personal injury law. Prior to joining Boyd, Boyd, & Giddens, she practiced family law in Tyler, Texas. Diana was licensed by the State Bar of Texas in 2023 and serves on the board for the Smith County Young Lawyer’s Association.

Diana was born in Dallas, Texas, but was raised in the Tyler area. After graduating from Whitehouse High School, she graduated magna cum laude from the University of Texas at Tyler. She later earned her Juris Doctorate from SMU Dedman School of Law in Dallas, Texas.

As the first in her family to go to law school, Diana worked hard and continued to focus her energy on causes she is passionate about. Diana spent her last two years of law school with the Judge Elmo B. Hunter Legal Center for Victims of Crimes Against Women representing survivors of gender-based harms, including domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking. Diana also had the privilege to serve as a Judicial Extern with the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas.

In her leisure time, Diana and her husband, Ryan, enjoy taking walks and playing with their dog and cat. She loves traveling, researching, photography, and spending time with family and friends.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Recipient of the State Bar of Texas International Law Section Human Rights Essay Contest (2022)

Recipient of the East Texas Crisis Center Hope Award (2017)

attorneys.name: Shaunté Henry
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney LaShaunté S. Henry is licensed to practice in both Texas and Louisiana. With over fourteen years of experience in various fields of law, her primary focus is Family Law. Having previously worked in the legislative, judicial and executive branches of government, she brings a wealth of knowledge and experience to the legal field.

LaShaunté S. Henry is a graduate of the Southern University Law Center in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. While there, she was a member of the Dean’s List and facilitated the agreement between the law center and the Baton Rouge City Court to establish mediations for landlord-tenant disputes. She also represented several family law, tax law, and elder law clients under the supervision of the law school practice clinic, and worked as a law clerk for the Louisiana Attorney General’s Office/Department of Justice, Civil Division—Road Hazards Section.

After graduating law school, she was the Deputy Legal Counsel at the Louisiana Governor’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Preparedness (G.O.H.S.E.P.), a federal flow through agency that administered over $150,000,000.00 in federal disaster grant funds. There she defended civil lawsuits, engaged in complex construction litigation, participated in numerous statewide public speaking engagements, and taught Continuing Legal Education (C.L.E.) courses for other attorneys and stakeholders in the legal community. She previously owned and operated a solo practice focusing on the areas of Personal Injury and Family Law, and also worked as an Attorney Advisor for the U.S. Small Business Administration.

Prior to law school, she worked in Washington, D.C., for a distinguished member of the United States Congress, Rep. Eddie Bernice Johnson (D-TX), while chair of two powerful legislative committees. Attorney Henry previously worked in the East Baton Rouge Parish Mayor’s Office, under Mayor Bobby Simpson (R), where she was assigned to citizen’s issues and helped to perform data collection and analysis for “CanDo” (Community Action in Neighborhoods Developing Opportunities), a Blight Elimination Team designed to implement Organize Your Neighborhood Now!, the training program on how to start and run a Neighborhood or Civic Association. Her past work experience also includes working for the Honorable Pamela Taylor-Johnson at the East Baton Rouge Parish Juvenile Court, and as support staff in several corporate law firms that specialize in insurance defense work, the most notable being the global Jones Walker Law Firm.

Attorney Henry is a member of various religious, community and legal organizations, including the American Bar Association, the Texas State Bar Association, the Louisiana State Bar Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the Louisiana Association for Justice, the Houston Bar Association, The Montgomery County Bar Association, The Woodlands Bar Association, the Baton Rouge Bar Association, and the Greater Baton Rouge Chapter of the Louis A. Martinet Legal Society, Inc. where she previously served as Chair of the Technology Committee and Gala Committees.

She is a proud wife and mother of a young daughter who is following her athletic footsteps in gymnastics competitions. Her favorite hobby is cooking delicious Louisiana cuisines such as seafood gumbos, crawfish ettoufées, and baking homemade French breads.

attorneys.name: Aaron A. Herbert
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Aaron A. Herbert P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
For over a decade he has shown an unwavering commitment to clients who were seriously injured by major accidents and industrial catastrophes. During that time he has earned the reputation as one of America's most aggressive trial lawyers by achieving noteworthy recoveries from judges and juries, as well as substantial settlements prior to trial, the majority of which contained negotiated confidentiality agreements at the request of the defense.

When asked about these cases, Mr. Herbert has said that each case not only justified the recovery level, but that no one would trade places with any one of these victims in return for any amount of money, once they know the facts and severity of the injuries and tragedy involved.

According to Mr. Herbert, "there can be no substitute for passion, preparation and persistence in the practice of law". He is known not only for this tenacious preparation, but also for his imagination in the courtroom. He is passionate and persistent in seeking to obtain the maximum case value for each individual client at trial or through settlement, while reducing the stress of litigation on his clients.

Born and raised in Dallas, Texas, Mr. Herbert enlisted in the United States Marine Corps after high school and later received an Honorable Discharge. After the Marines, he obtained a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice from Texas A&M University, then a Juris Doctorate from the University of Oklahoma College of Law. There he graduated in the top of his class and became an eternal Sooners Football fan. Aaron has worked as a zealous advocate for injured clients at several boutique personal injury litigation firms where he amassed numerous jury verdicts.

After spending a year as the top earning litigation attorney at a firm that frequently tops verdict search as one with the highest number of trial wins in Texas, Aaron accepted a position as a the managing pre-litigation attorney at another Dallas personal injury firm. Over the next seven years he transitioned to the managing litigation attorney, and that firm grew to one of the largest personal injury firms in Dallas.

In 2010 he formed the Law Firm of Aaron A. Herbert, to get back to a focus on developing each individual case and maximizing case value for each client. Mr. Herbert practices law with the belief that a well taken care of, highly engaged and motivated team of employees working in a cooperative team environment will result in superior representation and great results for the firm clients. He believes in always setting a goal of achieving the best possible results for each and every client.

attorneys.name: Amanda Inez Hernandez
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Amanda I. Hernandez is a highly regarded criminal defense attorney known for her extensive experience and dedication to her clients. Licensed in 2016, Amanda quickly established herself as a formidable advocate in the courtroom. Her practice encompasses a wide range of criminal defense matters, including federal cases, felonies, and misdemeanors.

Amanda began her legal career at the Flanary Law Firm PLLC, where she honed her skills as an associate attorney. Her exceptional abilities and dedication led to her current role as Of Counsel at the firm. In 2024, Amanda took a significant step forward in her career by founding Amanda Hernandez Law, PLLC, a testament to her commitment to providing top-tier legal representation.

Amanda's legal acumen is demonstrated by her successful jury trial experience, where she has effectively defended clients in high-stakes cases. Her expertise spans federal and state courts, showcasing her versatility and comprehensive understanding of the criminal justice system.

Her peers have recognized Amanda's contributions to the legal field, notably naming her the San Antonio Criminal Defense Lawyers Association's (SACDLA) Young Lawyer of the Year in 2019. This accolade reflects her exceptional skill and dedication early in her career. In 2024, she was honored as a Super Lawyers Rising Star, further solidifying her reputation as a leading attorney in criminal defense.

In addition to her legal practice, Amanda is deeply involved in various professional organizations, reflecting her commitment to criminal justice reform and the legal community. She currently serves as the Vice President of the Texas Coalition to Abolish the Death Penalty (TCADP), where she advocates for the eradication of capital punishment and works towards a more just legal system.

Amanda also holds the position of Vice President of the San Antonio Criminal Defense Lawyers Association (SACDLA), demonstrating her leadership and dedication to supporting fellow defense attorneys. Her involvement extends to the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, where she actively contributes to advancing the practice of criminal defense in Texas and also serves as a speaker for the Criminal Defense Lawyers Project. As such, Amanda shares her knowledge and insights with other legal professionals, fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement within the legal community.

Amanda's expertise is further recognized through her role as an associate editor for "Voice for the Defense," a prominent publication dedicated to criminal defense issues. Her contributions help shape the discourse around criminal defense strategies and advocacy, benefiting her peers and the broader legal community.

Chris aggressively pursues each case he handles with compassion for his clients and unrelenting enthusiasm for the changes he can effect in their lives.

Chris obtained his JD from the University of San Francisco School of Law and is licensed in California and New York, as well as Texas. In serious injury or death trucking and automobile accident cases, Chris’ education and predilection for engineering allows him a technical understanding of Accident Reconstruction and mechanical failures, which he can then explain to a jury.

Upon graduation from St. Mary's School of Law in May 1984, Lee Hernandez established the Law Offices of Lee Hernandez, P.C., for the representation of both individuals and businesses. As a Senior Associate Editor for the Law Journal at his law school, Lee understood the need for quality representation at a reasonable fee. The firm accepts cases on an hourly basis, a fixed-fee basis or, on occasion, a contingency-fee (no fee if no recovery) basis. Currently we serve clients throughout the United States and Mexico.

attorneys.name: Rosa Hernandez
attorneys.practice_type: Personal injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rosa received her B.A. Degree from The University of Illinois at Chicago and earned her J.D. degree from Chicago Kent College of Law. She is licensed to practice law in the State of Illinois and the State of Texas.

Rosa was born in Michoacan, Mexico. She immigrated, at a young age, to the United States and understands first-hand the plight of immigrants. Rosa was raised in Pilsen, a community in the south side of Chicago, Illinois and later relocated to Houston, Texas. Her personal experiences as a minority woman call for a deeper connection with her clients. For Rosa, being an attorney is more than just her profession, it is a devoted commitment to serve and give back to her community. Her zealous legal representation is coupled with compassion, empathy, patience, and understanding. For Rosa, her clients are always her number 1 priority.

Rosa has been part of the personal injury field for many years and has experience in both plaintiff and defense representation. Her all around experience provides her with significant leverage when negotiating settlements for her clients.

Rosa loves spending time with her family, going to sport events, and dancing.

attorneys.name: Michael Herndon
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Herndon has been licensed to practice law in all courts of the State of Texas since 2006. He is a graduate of the University of Houston where he obtained his bachelor’s of science degree in psychology. He earned his law degree at Texas Southern University and graduated cum laude. He is a member of the American Bar Association, Texas State Bar, and the Houston Bar Association.

Mr. Herndon did not begin law school until his early fifties. He brings a wide range of experience into his law practice. His fifteen year airline career cumulated in his position of Vice President at Continental Airlines. He was president of a large international hotel marketing company before starting his own specialized tour and marketing company which he sold before beginning law school. His business experience makes him one of the areas most knowledgeable attorneys in the field of property valuation, small business valuation, and marital property matters.

Mike has also found a niche in Texas grandparent rights, representing grandparents in asserting their rights to protect their grandchildren.

Mike is a trained mediator having completed the required 40 hours of training and additional twenty hours of family mediation training at the University of Houston Law Center.

Mike has been married to Debra Herndon for more than five years and has two grown daughters, both graduates of Texas A&M University. Both are recently married, and Mike is expecting his own grandchildren any day.

attorneys.name: Alfred R. Herrera
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law/Public Utility Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Alfred R. Herrera is the founder of Herrera Law & Associates and focuses his practice on administrative law in the public-utility arena - electric, gas, water/wastewater, landline and wireless communications. He has served as lead counsel in excess of one hundred contested proceedings before the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Railroad Commission of Texas primarily representing municipalities in rate cases and landowners in CCN cases. He has handled numerous appeals to the Texas Courts of Appeals and the Texas Supreme Court. He is Board certified in Administrative Law. Member: State Bar of Texas; Public Utility Law Section; and Austin Bar Association. Serves on the Administrative Law Advisory Commission for the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Member of the Texas Bar College.

Mr. Herrera has extensive experience in the regulatory arena regarding electric utilities, gas utilities, municipally-owned electric and water/wastewater utilities, landline telecommunications companies, wireless communications companies, and cable companies.

Mr. Herrera's practice focuses on representing municipalities, electric and water municipally owned utilities, and other corporate entities in proceedings before the Public Utility Commission of Texas, the Railroad Commission of Texas, and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality, as well as in the legislative process, and appeals of agency orders to the court system. Mr. Herrera also advises cities in matters affecting use of their right of ways and other municipally owned facilities, including negotiating pole-attachment agreements, review of purchase power agreements, and other complex contract negotiations. Additionally, Mr. Herrera represents private and public clients in transmission-line proceedings before the PUC.

Mr. Herrera has represented municipalities in almost every major rate case filed by an electric utility with the PUCT over the past 15 years and in rate proceedings filed by the major gas utilities in Texas before the Railroad Commission of Texas.

Mr. Herrera represented a municipally-owned utility in a seminal case before the PUC regarding the municipally owned utility's rights under the Public Utility Regulatory Act to control access to its facilities, including its utility poles, and represented the City of Austin, the City of Dallas, and the City of Houston in separate complaints brought by small-cell companies seeking to use the cities' right of ways under Chapter 283 of the Local Government Code and advises municipalities across the state in their rights and obligations with regard to use of a city's public rights of way.

Mr. Herrera served as lead counsel for MCI, Inc., for over 15 years, participating in numerous rate proceedings and interconnection-agreement negotiations and arbitrations, and played a key role in the legislative and regulatory arenas to open the telecommunications market to competition, including the telecommunications market in Mexico, serving on MCI's formative team that crafted the regulatory framework for deregulation of the telecommunications market in Mexico.

Mr. Herrera is a frequent speaker on municipal law and electric, water/wastewater, electric, and gas-utility law.

Mr. Herrera is a Member of the State Bar of Texas; Public Utility Law Section of the Bar; and the Austin Bar Association. He serves on the State Bar of Texas's Administrative Advisory Commission for the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and is a Member of the Texas Bar College. Mr. Herrera obtained a B.A. in American History from the George Washington University and his Doctor of Jurisprudence degree from the University of Texas School of Law.

attorneys.name: Aimee Hess
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Aimee Hess P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Oil and Gas Law Lawyers in Streetman, TX
attorneys.bio:
The philosophy that guides and informs my law practice is to deliver the very highest quality of legal services to my clients on a very cost-effective basis. I am not only dedicated to my clients' success, I am accessible and down to earth, and I keep an eye on my clients' bottom line.

My passion is to help my clients be good stewards of their real property and mineral assets. That means helping my clients get the most out of any real estate or oil and gas transaction, as well as protecting their property and mineral assets.

The transactions with which I assist my clients include:

oil and gas leases

pipeline or utility easement survey permits

pipeline easements and rights-of-way

sale or purchase of mineral interests

assignments of mineral interests

division orders

royalty payment or nonpayment issues

curing mineral title defects

utility/transmission line easements

surface use and damage agreements

purchase and sale of real estate

access easements

solar easements

wind turbine easements

cell tower easements

I deliberately choose to represent only landowners and mineral owners. I never represent oil companies or pipeline companies and so I can always be certain that I will never have a conflict of interest in representing my clients. In addition, I constantly monitor my caseload to ensure that I'm always able to give prompt and personal service to each client. I never want to become "too busy" to give each client the attention they need and deserve.

I'm gratified that many of my clients have been with me for almost 46 years, and repeatedly turn to me for assistance with their real estate and mineral issues and transactions.

attorneys.name: Richard E. Hettinger
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Richard E. Hettinger is a Vice President and shareholder of the Firm and a member of the Firm's Pension Committee. He is Board Certified in Business Bankruptcy Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and the American Bankruptcy Board of Certification. Mr. Hettinger has served as the Estate Administrator to the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Texas and as an Assistant Unites States Attorney for the Western District of Texas. He was admitted to the California bar in 1974, the Texas bar in 1980, and is licensed to practice before the United States District Courts for the Northern, Southern, and Western Districts of Texas, the Northern and Eastern Districts of California, and the Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.

Mr. Hettinger was educated at California State University at Chico (BA, 1970), and the University of the Pacific, McGeorge School of Law (JD 1974). He is a member of the San Antonio Bar Association, the State Bar of Texas and the State Bar of California, and the San Antonio Bankruptcy Bar Association.

Mr. Hettinger has represented creditors including businesses of all sizes, individuals and numerous financial institutions, and major national banks in bankruptcy matters throughout Texas. In his practice he has represented creditors in all matters arising under Chapter 7, 11, and 13 of the Bankruptcy Code.

He has been successful in recovering creditors' collateral from many bankruptcy estates, which has allowed our creditor clients to recoup maximum value for their collateral. His expertise also includes assisting debtor and creditor clients with workouts to avoid bankruptcy through pre-bankruptcy workouts. He has represented creditors in bringing all types of adversary proceedings and defended creditors in preference and other actions brought against creditors.

She also worked full time as a paralegal with the support of her 2 children, awesome husband and many valued family members while attending law school at night.

She spent many years active as a member in the State Bar of Texas Paralegal Division and in the Dallas Area Paralegal Association as the Community Service/Pro Bono chairperson and chairperson of the Personal Injury/ Medical Malpractice Section.

Christy enjoys speaking to upcoming Paralegal students, presenting Continuing Legal Education seminars, and mentoring Paralegals. With her extensive track record as a senior litigation/double board certified paralegal, she brings many years of dedication to the legal field, practical trial and litigation experience as well as the personal attention and interaction our clients deserve.

attorneys.name: Lance A. Hevizy
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lance practices in the areas of commercial litigation, corporate, and real estate law. Lance also serves as a risk management advisor to private companies on corporate governance matters.

Lance represents public and private companies and their directors and officers in high-stakes litigation arising out of mergers or acquisitions (particularly, venture capital or private-equity financed investments), shareholder derivative cases, and internal corporate investigations. Lance has represented companies in array of industries, including financial services, energy, institutional investing, technology, health care and manufacturing. Lance also represents businesses in litigation related to their intellectual property assets as well as real estate disputes.

Additionally, Lance is an effective advocate for pharmaceutical-industry clients involved in disputes. He has successfully represented drug development companies in contractual and IP litigation, winning a unanimous jury verdict of $5.5 million (plus attorney’s fees) in a breach of contract dispute, and obtaining a verdict enforcing a client’s IP rights in a $296 million suit.

In addition to his litigation practice, leveraging his litigation expertise, Lance provides risk management counseling to companies to effectively minimize risk by proactively identifying and addressing governance and common legal issues involved when good business goes bad. Common legal issues include breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, intellectual property protection and enforcement, and shareholder derivative actions.

Lance most recently served as an attorney at Michael Best & Friedrich, LLP, in the Austin, Texas, office, where he worked alongside the Honorable George P. Bush. His prior experience includes practicing with the entrepreneurial law firm RWR Legal in Austin. Previously, Lance was an associate in the Dallas office of Baker McKenzie, LLP, focusing on commercial litigation and e-discovery. Earlier in his career, he handled complex civil litigation matters in the areas of business, real estate, and personal injury law at a full-service firm in Maui, Hawaii.

Honors

Lifetime member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum, Lifetime Member Award

Martindale-Hubbell Excellence Award in Legal Ability and Ethical Standards

attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jude is a Texas trial lawyer who represents clients facing significant civil and commercial claims in the Lone Star State and beyond.

Jude’s practice spans multiple industries and subject matters. He has defended a wide range of domestic and international clients, including automotive and component part manufacturers, engineering firms, insurance companies, and commercial real estate clients. Jude regularly represents clients facing product liability and significant tort claims. He also has extensive experience representing clients in class actions and mass torts. Representative experience includes In re: Takata Airbag Products Liability Litigation and lawsuits related to the water crisis in Flint, Michigan.

Jude understands that professionalism and preparation are critical to successfully positioning a case for resolution or verdict. Jude’s ability to understand and communicate complex, often technical, issues has helped clients successfully navigate high-stakes products liability and complex litigation through settlement and trial.

Jude has been recognized as both a Texas Super Lawyers “Rising Star” and as one of the Best Lawyers in America “Ones to Watch.”

attorneys.practice_type: Banking & Finance Lawyers in Lubbock, TX
attorneys.bio:
Michael Hicks is a partner in the firm's Lubbock office. Michael's principal areas of practice are business and commercial law with an emphasis on representation of financial institutions. In addition, his practice includes business entity selection and formation. Michael also has extensive experience working with the firm's litigation attorneys on complex litigation matters involving loan workouts, bankruptcies, real estate and construction disputes, and related litigation matters.

Michael also has a growing practice in the area of renewable energy, with a particular focus on wind energy. His experience includes representing landowners in Texas, Oklahoma and New Mexico in negotiating and drafting wind energy leases.

Michael received his B.A. degree with honors from Angelo State University in May of 1992. He received his J.D. degree with highest honors from Texas Tech University School of Law in May of 1995. Michael is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the American Bar Association, and the Lubbock County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Whitney Lauren Hicks
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
Whitney Hicks has the unique qualities of a fierce civil prosecutor after a near decade of practicing law. Whitney vigorously sought justice for the children of Hays County in the most complex civil mediations, litigation, and jury trials in her capacity as an Assistant District Attorney. Protecting children from abuse, neglect, and family violence as well as offering ongoing training to clients and professionals remains a top priority for Whitney.

As a founding member of the firm, Whitney's calculated and persistent method of moving her cases forward has been refined over the years. She has the rare experience of preparing 17 civil cases for jury trial, sitting of 9 of those to verdict, and first chairing half a dozen. She has hundreds of hours of litigation experience in highly contested bench trials and hearings representing the Department of Family and Protective Services and individuals. She also has experience writing both civil and criminal appeals, representing the state in various forfeiture actions, and providing trainings to law enforcement and child protective services professionals.

Prior to working as an Assistant District Attorney, Whitney worked as an associate at a premier family law firm in Austin, Texas for two years where she gained valuable experience counseling clients, reviewing and preparing discovery, and dealing with complex issues such as business valuations and substance abuse.

Whitney values her career as a civil attorney and balances work with the demands of being a wife and mother. She understands the pressures of being a businesswoman and parent. While Whitney analyzes each unique case independently, she has the life experience to understand each case from the point of view of a parent and a business professional.

Semi-finalist in 2010 National Trial Competition
