attorneys.name: Stephen Higdon
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Stephen’s clients often come to him when they are dealing with the worst moment of their lives. He is inspired by the trust they place in him and is relentless in pursuing justice for them. Never one to back down from a challenge, he tirelessly pursues the path to victory—regardless of whether it is a creative solution or just old-fashioned, nose-to-the-grindstone work.

Stephen started his legal career clerking for the Honorable Michael H. Schneider in the Eastern District of Texas, giving him firsthand insight into what persuades judges and juries. Equally important, he learned that no matter how large the company or the law firm they hire—a trial lawyer can level the playing field for people and get justice.

Using that insight, Stephen stands up to powerful corporations and their insurers to obtain record-setting verdicts and settlements for his clients.

Higdon has obtained exceptional results for clients in just the recent past:

$70 Million – Wrongful Death, Negligent Security/Operations

$25 Million – Wrongful Death, Gas Explosion

$10.5 Million – Electrical Shock, Utility Work

$13 Million – Wrongful Death, Oil-Field Fall

$9 Million – Wrongful Death, Product Defect

$5.9 Million – Wrongful Death, Motor Vehicle Collision

$5.5 Million – Mild Brain Injury, Product Defect

$3.75 Million – Brain Injury, Product Defect

$3 Million – Arm Injuries, Industrial Facility Accident

$2.5 Million – Breach of Contract, College Coach Contract Buyout

$2 Million – Spine Injuries, Trucking Accident

$2 Million – Burn Injuries, Apartment Fire

$1.75 Million – Spine Injuries, Negligent Maintenance

While Stephen is proud of these results and the necessary resources they provide his clients and their families, he is equally proud of the accountability and ensuing change they inspire the companies that harmed his clients to take. To obtain the resources and space clients need to heal, Stephen levels the playing field for his clients by disrupting the script companies and their insurers follow to delay, obstruct, or deflect—forcing companies to reveal documents and witnesses they would rather the jury not see. Combining the depth of his experience and meticulous planning, he puts real pressure on companies and their insurers to honestly appraise their conduct and the devastating effects it had on his clients.

Stephen’s command of the law and facts not only deliver results for his clients, it has also led his peers to recognize him with the prestigious 2021 John Howie Award and as one of the 500 Leading Plaintiff Consumer Lawyers by Lawdragon (2023-2025), Thomson Reuters Super Lawyers – Texas Rising Stars (2019-2025), Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch (2021-2025), and D Magazine’s Best Lawyers Under 40 (2020, 2022-2025). Never one to rest on his laurels, Stephen continues to strategically and aggressively pursue the best possible outcome for his clients.

attorneys.name: Nita Hight
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nita Hight is a Dallas native and the team’s “research guru,” possessing an encyclopedic knowledge of case law and statutes. The team can always count on her to offer nuanced analysis and brilliant insight, and of course, the occasional witty quip.

Nita is not only committed to justice, but also insatiably intellectually curious. She obtained a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Baylor University with a minor in Forensic Science, in addition to participating in moot court. Nita completed a thesis entitled Legislating Marriage: A Constitutional Examination of Same-Sex Marriage, as a student of the Baylor Honors College. Nita then obtained a Masters of Science in English from Texas A&M University Commerce before completing her law degree at Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law. Nita continued her participation in moot court during law school.

Nita enjoyed the great honor of serving as a research assistant for leading LGBTQ+ scholar, Professor Dale Carpenter. She also participated in the VanSickle Family Law Clinic and W.W. Caruth, Jr., Child Advocacy Clinic during law school. Nita focused her interested not only on family law, but more broadly on LGBTQ+ rights, religious freedom, freedom of speech, and freedom of association.

Nita’s ultimate interest in family law centers around appellate law. Nita contributes to the development of each client’s case by ensuring that evidence and legal argument are thoroughly prepared for the possibility of appeal. Nita understands that the legislative process often reacts to social progress, creating novel issues of law upon which the Texas Family Code is silent. Whenever the answers are unclear, Nita formulates clever, creative argument to pursue fairness and justice for her clients.

attorneys.name: Philip H. Hilder
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Criminal Defense Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
PHILIP H. HILDER was formerly the attorney-in-charge of the Houston Field Office of the United States Department of Justice, Organized Crime Strike Force. Prior to his appointment as a trial attorney with the Justice Department, Mr. Hilder was an assistant United States attorney in the Southern District of Texas with the Presidential Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force. Since leaving government service, Mr. Hilder has practiced in the area of white collar criminal defense, internal investigations, and whistleblower representation. Currently, he is the American Bar Association Criminal Justice Section White Collar Crime Committee Executive Director; Immediate past ABA National Chair of the White Collar Crime Committee; Presently co-chair of the ABA National Institute on Securities Fraud; Co-chair of the ABA subcommittee on Securities Fraud; Past President of the Federal Bar Association (So. TX Chapter); Criminal Law Chair (FBA - So. TX Chapter).

MR. HILDER has consistently received the highest rating from the Martindale-Hubbell legal network (AV) and is listed in the Bar Registry of Preeminent Lawyers. He has been involved in high profile cases, such as representing the Enron and Countrywide whistleblowers; defending BP personal in the Deepwater Horizon explosion; co-lead counsel in defending the Texas Attorney General for alleged violations of securities fraud; represented The University of Texas System/Board of Regents in an impeachment proceeding being conducted by the Texas Legislature; involved in a highly publicized Washington, D.C., lobbyist/Congressional scandal; represented a Major League Baseball player in the Congressional investigation into steroid use in Major League Baseball; represented ex-executive in the Imperial Sugar explosion that killed 14 persons; the U.S. Olympic (Salt Lake City Olympics) Committee scandal; and is a frequent legal commentator on criminal cases for television, print, and radio.

attorneys.name: Duke Hildreth
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Duke Hildreth has focused his entire legal career on criminal law and trying cases in court before a judge and jury. Before joining Hildreth & Rueda Law as a defense attorney, Mr. Hildreth was a criminal prosecutor for over eight years. He tried crimes from DWI to felony murder. With all the knowledge he gained from working as a prosecutor, he understands how the prosecution thinks and acts in a criminal case, so he can plan a more effective defense for his clients.

Mr. Hildreth has tried hundreds of cases in his legal career and his been very successful in achieving Not Guilty Verdicts for his clients. His extensive trial experience is very advantageous in defending clients facing criminal misdemeanor and felony charges throughout Central Texas including the Austin metro area as well as Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop, Caldwell, Bell, McClennan, Burnet, Llano, Comal, Bexar, Blanco, Gillespie and Guadalupe Counties.

Mr. Hildreth is passionate about the law, “I believe in my clients, and I believe in exhausting every avenue to achieve justice for my clients.”

When Mr. Hildreth is not working he enjoys spending his time with his wife and children.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Greg has real world working experience both in and out of the legal arena. Greg graduated from Texas A&M University in College Station, Texas in 1993. After graduation, Greg worked in the field of education as a high school Spanish teacher before going to work as a United States Border Patrol Agent in 1996. Subsequent to his time with the U.S. Border Patrol, Greg worked with Autozone, Inc. where he later acted as a Consultant/Director relating to matters of Loss Prevention and Risk Assessment for the company's Mexico Market. Eventually choosing to practice law, Greg began law school in 2002 at South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas.

During law school, Greg became a member of the Varsity Negotiation Team where he won several awards in Client Negotiation with the American Bar Association. Greg also competed on his law school's Varsity Moot Court Team and at Mock Trial Competitions. In his third year of law school, Greg worked at the Harris County District Attorney's Office in their Asset Forfeiture Division. After law school, Greg became an Assistant District Attorney in Galveston County, Texas where he prosecuted a number of misdemeanor and juvenile crimes, and also handled the Children's Protective Services Docket. After having worked as an Assistant District Attorney in Galveston County, Greg became managing partner at Hill, Russo & Associates, PLLC managing the firm's personal injury docket while also defending criminal claims.

Greg is now an owner and managing partner of Daly Hill, PLLC. At Daly Hill, PLLC, we understand that your needs require individualized attention, especially with respect to legal matters involving personal injury. We pride ourselves on being able to do just that.

attorneys.name: Matthew J. Hill
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
During law school, and even before, Matthew Hill gained a broad understanding of the practice of law having interned and clerked for a Texas County District Attorney’s Office (twice), a Texas District Court Judge, a large Civil Defense firm, and for the Civil Division of the United States Attorney's Office in San Antonio. Upon receiving his license from the Texas Supreme Court, Mr. Hill struck out on his own and began his legal career operating his own firm, albeit on a much smaller scale than M. J. Hill & Associates, PLLC.

In June 2007 he began working for what became one of San Marcos' largest litigation firms. After three and one half years, Mr. Hill decided it was time to make a change and in December 2010 he left his former firm, and opened the doors to M. J. Hill & Associates, PLLC in January 2011 as the firm's President and Managing Attorney.

During his career Mr. Hill has been responsible for litigating matters in both state and federal courts on behalf of numerous clients. This includes spending over two and one half years very early in his career defending and litigating an alleged $20 million lawsuit in federal court, which was ultimately resolved in his client's favor. Having survived that “trial by fire,” he applies the experience he gained to the firm's litigation practice, whether a matter involves general or complex disputes, or appealing an adverse decision to the appropriate court. Mr. Hill has a unique ability to think outside the box, asserting novel legal theories and arguments, and his approach has proven itself time and again to benefit his clients.

Mr. Hill is a litigation attorney with a practice focus on family and divorce law. He also maintains a selective criminal defense and general litigation practice. Mr. Hill has experience in all phases of litigation and trial, ranging from the simple drafting of documents to arguing cases before courts and juries. He has experience as a trial attorney, has appeared and argued countless hearings, taken and defended numerous depositions, represented clients in dozens of formal and informal mediations, and his most recent jury trial was in March 2012. Mr. Hill does not like watching from the sidelines, he much prefers being in the game.

On a personal note, Mr. Hill was born in Casper, Wyoming, and lived in seven different cities all over the state since first moving to Texas in 1981. Mr. Hill personally experienced the difficulty of divorce in 2016-2017 and has a new understanding of what his clients go through. He now lives with his two children in the hill country between San Antonio and Austin. In what spare time he has, Mr. Hill enjoys spending time with his kids, participating in community events and contributing to local groups and charities. He also enjoys traveling and fishing with his children and extended family.

attorneys.name: Wesley Hill
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Longview, TX
attorneys.bio:
Wesley Hill balances a successful practice in patent, oil & gas, business, and federal criminal defense litigation. With more than a dozen trials to his credit as lead or co-lead trial counsel, including ten patent cases, Wesley brings broad courtroom experience to every case he handles. Wesley's trial successes include multi-million dollar plaintiff's verdicts and no-liability findings for defense clients. Most recently, Wesley obtained a defense jury verdict for Ralcorp Holdings and Medallion Foods, defeating claims by Frito-Lay for patent infringement, trademark infringement, and theft of trade secrets. To read more, click here. Other recent trial successes include defense jury verdicts for Callaway Golf Company and Target Corporation, as well as a substantial plaintiff's verdict for an oil and gas operator. Having assisted clients with the resolution of hundreds of cases, Wesley understands how to identify clients' priorities and achieve their objectives, whether through litigation, settlement, or trial.

A former briefing attorney for the Honorable T. John Ward, United States District Judge for the Eastern District of Texas, Wesley is chairman of the Eastern District of Texas Local Rules Committee and is intimately familiar with practice in the district. Wesley graduated second in his law school class at Texas Tech University (J.D. 2001) and received the Texas Young Lawyers Association State Moot Court Best Advocate Award. A native East Texan, Wesley is also a graduate of the University of Texas at Tyler (B.A. 1998).

attorneys.name: Larry Hilton
attorneys.practice_type: Intellectual Property Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lawrence ("Larry") Hilton is admitted to practice in Texas and California. He specializes in complex litigation matters, primarily in federal court, including antitrust claims, Lanham Act trademark and false advertising claims, copyright infringement claims and misappropriation of trade secret claims. Larry also has significant bankruptcy and creditors' rights litigation experience. Larry's practice also includes representation of several national franchise brands and national branded retailers. Larry has spent his career practicing commercial litigation in both state and federal court.

Franchise and Branded Retailer Practice

Larry represents the Driven Brands® family of companies, including Meineke Car Care Centers, Maaco America's Bodyshop, Take 5 Oil Change, Carstar, Drive N Style and Econo Lube N' Tune, in franchise matters and franchise and trademark litigation matters. Larry has also represented The Galardi Group (Der Wienerschnitzel) and Hansen's Juice Creations in franchise-related matters.

Recent representations include:

Morton v. Driven Brands, Inc. and Econo Lube N' Tune, LLC: Larry represented Driven Brands, Inc. and Econo Lube N' Tune, LLC in a franchise-related litigation case that went to trial in 2016. Larry obtained a complete defense verdict and an attorneys' fees award in excess of $400,000.

Meineke Car Care Centers, LLC v. Keller & Sons, Inc.: Larry represented Meineke Car Care Centers, Inc. in litigation with a multi-unit franchisee of Meineke centers in the United States District Court for the Central District of California, with claims and counterclaims in excess of $6 million. The matter was resolved with Meineke taking back all twelve of the franchises.

Maaco Franchising, LLC v. 5296, LLC, et al.: Larry currently represents Maaco Franchising, LLC in franchise and trademark litigation with a former Maaco franchisee, which is currently pending in the United States District Court for the Central District of California. Maaco recently obtained a right to attach order and is in the process of seeking the appointment of a receiver to enforce the writ of attachment.

Maaco Franchising, LLC v. Elsayed: Larry represented Maaco Franchising, LLC in franchise litigation with a former franchisee pending in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.

Carstar Franchisor SPV LLC v. Sunnyvale Auto Body: Larry currently represents Carstar Franchisor SPV LLC in franchise litigation with a former franchisee pending in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.

Larry also represents Sprint Solutions, Inc. and Nextel of California, and their master retailer, Vincent Huang & Associates, in disputes with branded pre-paid wireless retailers operating under the "Boost Mobile" brand.

Recent representations include:

Fernandez v. Sprint Solutions, Inc.: Larry represents Sprint Solutions in a dispute brought by a terminated Boost Mobile retailer claiming that his termination as a Boost Mobile retailer was wrongful. The case is pending in Hidalgo County, Texas.

Bankruptcy and Creditors' Rights Practice

Larry represents the State Bank of Texas in matters involving judgment and lien enforcement, including State Bank of Texas v. Parabia, currently pending in the United States District Court for the Southern District of California. Larry has represented several national banks in receivership and judicial foreclosure matters, including Bank of America, Wells Fargo and JP Morgan Chase.

attorneys.firm_name: Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kassie’s own experience with her family’s divorce at a young age has shaped her level-headed and compassionate approach to family law. She draws on her life experience to be a fierce, empathetic, and loyal advocate for her clients, both in and out of the courtroom.

Kassie graduated from the University of Oklahoma with a Bachelor of Arts in International Studies and a minor in Spanish. She then worked as a legal assistant and paralegal for nearly 15 years. In 2017, Kassie began pursuing her lifelong goal of becoming an attorney by enrolling at UNT Dallas College of Law. While working full-time at a civil litigation firm and attending night classes, she consistently made the Dean's List, held leadership roles, and was an active member of the Board of Advocates and Phi Delta Phi Legal Honor Society. She also completed an externship with Lambda Legal, focusing on nationwide impact litigation for LGBTQ+ civil rights. Kassie graduated cum laude from law school.

As an attorney, Kassie is passionate about representing same-sex spouses and parents in LGBTQ+ family law matters, most notably including adoptions. She also focuses her practice on complex marital property issues, including closely held businesses, complex asset division, and real estate. In addition, Kassie assists clients in need of asset protection through premarital and post-marital agreements. She has contributed to briefing appellate issues for various Texas courts of appeal and the Supreme Court of Texas. Kassie has additionally been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star for 2024 and 2025.

Kassie lives in Dallas, Texas, with her wife, and rescue pup. In her free time, she enjoys concerts, traveling, camping, hiking, and cheering on her favorite sports teams.

Kassie graduated from the University of Oklahoma with a Bachelor of Arts in International Studies and a minor in Spanish. She then worked as a legal assistant and paralegal for nearly 15 years. In 2017, Kassie began pursuing her lifelong goal of becoming an attorney by enrolling at UNT Dallas College of Law. While working full-time at a civil litigation firm and attending night classes, she consistently made the Dean's List, held leadership roles, and was an active member of the Board of Advocates and Phi Delta Phi Legal Honor Society. She also completed an externship with Lambda Legal, focusing on nationwide impact litigation for LGBTQ+ civil rights. Kassie graduated cum laude from law school.

As an attorney, Kassie is passionate about representing same-sex spouses and parents in LGBTQ+ family law matters, most notably including adoptions. She also focuses her practice on complex marital property issues, including closely held businesses, complex asset division, and real estate. In addition, Kassie assists clients in need of asset protection through premarital and post-marital agreements. She has contributed to briefing appellate issues for various Texas courts of appeal and the Supreme Court of Texas. Kassie has additionally been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Rising Star for 2024 and 2025.

Kassie lives in Dallas, Texas, with her wife, and rescue pup. In her free time, she enjoys concerts, traveling, camping, hiking, and cheering on her favorite sports teams.

attorneys.name: Kyle Hlavinka
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kyle Hlavinka is a civil litigation associate focusing on eminent domain and probate litigation matters. Kyle grew up on a farm in East Bernard, Texas, a small town west of Houston, where his family still grows rice, corn, and cotton. His interest in eminent domain began when HSC Pipeline Partnership, LLC took his family’s farmland to build a pipeline. During law school, Kyle took a course in eminent domain and private property rights and was able to follow his family’s case all the way up to the Texas Supreme Court, where they secured a favorable ruling for landowners regarding valuation in condemnation cases. See Hlavinka v. HSC Pipeline Partnership, LLC.

Understandably, Kyle is passionate about helping farmers and ranchers in the State of Texas. He has spoken on his family’s case in front of CLE International’s Houston Eminent Domain Conference and the Eminent Domain Section of the Austin Bar Association. Kyle has also spoken at town halls and guest lectured at the University of St. Thomas.

Kyle earned his undergraduate degree from Texas A&M University and his law degree from the University of Houston Law Center. During law school, Kyle served as the Chief Technology Editor for the Houston Business and Tax Law Journal, volunteered as a student mentor, and clerked for several firms representing clients in property disputes.

Kyle met his wife, Lexie, while attending a Texas A&M football game in Auburn, Alabama. Kyle and Lexie enjoy attending Aggie football games, watersports, and volunteering with their local church.

attorneys.name: Steve Hoard
attorneys.practice_type: Banking & Finance Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Steve Hoard is one of the founding partners of the firm. He practices in the area of complex civil litigation, with a focus on professional and director and officer liability and creditors' rights. Mr. Hoard has extensive experience in these areas, having personally handled cases in federal district and bankruptcy courts and state courts throughout Texas, as well as in New York, California, Oregon, Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, Michigan, Kansas, Florida, and Mississippi.

He has represented the trustees of the creditors' trusts established in the bankruptcies of several publicly traded companies in successfully bringing accounting malpractice and director and officer liability claims. These cases have resulted in millions of dollars of value for the creditors of these failed companies.

He has also represented a variety of creditors, trustees, and receivers in prosecuting complex fraudulent transfer claims. Mr. Hoard has successfully attacked offshore trusts that were established to put assets beyond the reach of creditors, and he has obtained numerous asset freeze injunctions to prevent defendants from making further fraudulent transfers while cases against them were pending.

Mr. Hoard is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in both Civil Trial Law and Business Bankruptcy Law. He is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the North Carolina State Bar, the American Bar Association, and the Amarillo Bar Association, for which he served as President in 1995-96.

Mr. Hoard received his B.A. degree in English with Highest Honors from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in December of 1975. He received his J. D. degree with Honors, also from the University of North Carolina, in May of 1979. While in law school, he served as Articles Editor of the North Carolina Law Review.

His primary areas of practice include estate planning, elder law, wills, trusts, probate, guardianship, business succession planning, and other matters involving family wealth planning and management. attorneys.name: Justin A. Hodge
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain and Condemnation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Justin Hodge is a Texas trial lawyer who represents landowners against the government and other condemning authorities in condemnation lawsuits. He teaches a course on eminent domain and land takings at the University of Houston School of Law and has testified before the Texas Legislature to promote eminent-domain reform. Mr. Hodge is recognized as a Super Lawyer in Eminent Domain by Thomson Reuters. He has co-chaired the CLE International’s Houston Eminent Domain Conference (2016-2021) and has served on faculty at the national eminent-domain conferences at ALI-CLE (2015, 2016, and 2020) and the Brigham-Kanner Property Rights Conference (2020).

Mr. Hodge represents landowners in condemnation proceedings, not the governmental authorities or private companies taking property. Mr. Hodge has won cases for landowners at every level: administrative hearings, jury trials, and appeals in state and federal courts. Mr. Hodge’s cases have involved takings of vacant land and ranches as well as highly improved properties with office buildings, shopping centers, restaurants, motels, banks, churches, c-stores, mines, quarries, and residential subdivisions. He has shown his skill both as a negotiator and as a courtroom advocate.

Both Mr. Hodge’s father and grandfather were Texas cattlemen and ranchers. His family has lived in Texas for nearly two centuries and is listed amongst members of the Sons of the Republic of Texas, direct descendants of those that settled the Republic of Texas. Understandably, he is passionate about Texas property rights. He has testified on Texas condemnation and eminent-domain reform on behalf of Texas landowners in front of both the Texas House of Representatives and the Texas Senate. He also writes a weekly blog at TexasCondemnation.com. His blog educates landowners about current Texas condemnation and eminent-domain issues.

Mr. Hodge has handled complex condemnation and eminent-domain cases throughout the State of Texas including the communities of Austin, Baytown, Bastrop, Beaumont, Bellmead, Bruceville-Eddy, Clear Lake, Cleburne, Columbus, Conroe, Corpus Christi, Dallas, Dayton, Denton, Decatur, Belton, Galveston, Georgetown, Dallas, Elm Mott, Fort Worth, League City, Hillsboro, Hewitt, Houston, Lampasas, Leander, Madisonville, Mansfield, McAllen, McKinney, Killeen, Round Rock, Robinson, Rogers, Salado, San Antonio, Seguin, Shenandoah, Texarkana, Troy, Tomball, Waxahachie, Waco, The Woodlands, and Wichita Falls, Texas. Mr. Hodge has appeared in condemnation and eminent-domain lawsuits in Bastrop County, Bell County, Bexar County, Bowie County, Brazoria County, Chambers County, Collin County, Comanche County, Colorado County, Dallas County, Denton County, Ellis County, Erath County, Fayette County, Fort Bend County, Galveston County, Guadalupe County, Grimes County, Harris County, Hidalgo County, Hill County, Jefferson County, Lampasas County, La Salle County, Leon County, Madison County, Montague County, Montgomery County, McLennan County, Tarrant County, Titus County, Travis County, and Williamson County. He has defended landowners against the Texas Attorney General’s office, pipeline companies, electric transmission line companies, school districts, cities, and counties. Mr. Hodge has offices in Austin, Texas (by appointment only) and Houston, Texas.

In 1999, Mr. Hodge received his Bachelor of Science degree in Agriculture and Applied Economics from Texas Tech University. At Texas Tech, Mr. Hodge taught as a teaching assistant in Farm and Ranch Management. In 2002, he graduated from the University of Texas School of Law, where he was a member of the Texas Review of Law and Politics. During law school, he served as a law clerk in the General Counsel’s Office of then-Governor George W. Bush. From 2008 to 2010, 2013, and 2017 Super Lawyers Magazine: Thomas Reuters as publishers in Texas Monthly Magazine recognized Mr. Hodge as a “Rising Star” in eminent domain, an accolade awarded by Thomas Reuters. Mr. Hodge is also recognized by Super Lawyers Magazine: Thomas Reuters as published in Texas Monthly Magazine as a Super Lawyer in Eminent Domain.

Mr. Hodge is involved in several professional organizations, including the Christian Legal Society (where he serves of the Board of Directors), Young Lawyer’s Steering Committee (chairing the U.S. Supreme Court Subcommittee from 2007 to 2008), the Defense Research Institute, the American Bar Association, Texas Young Lawyers Association, the Houston Bar Association, the Houston Young Lawyers Association, the Texas Farm Bureau, and the Texas and Southwestern Cattle Raisers Association. Mr. Hodge has been a licensed salesman and real estate broker since 1999.

Mr. Hodge and his family live in Houston and are actively involved in their church. He and his wife Courtney are celebrating sixteen years of marriage and they have been blessed with four beautiful children.

attorneys.name: Shaun Wesley Hodge
attorneys.practice_type: Maritime / Jones Act Lawyers in Galveston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Shaun Hodge has handled thousands of state and federal cases throughout the State of Texas and the United States. He has also represented clients in administrative hearings, arbitrations and mediations. Shaun has handled many types of cases, including first party insurance claims, personal injury cases, maritime matters, commercial litigation, residential and construction litigation, as well as general litigation matters.

He has successfully resolved thousands of claims for property owners fighting their insurance companies for damages caused by natural disasters including hurricanes, tornadoes, hailstorms, windstorms, floods, fires, winter storms and more. Shaun has litigated thousands of residential and large commercial insurance claims in multiple states across the country. Shaun is regularly sought out as a speaker to teach and lecture on insurance claim related issues across the country.

Shaun has been hired by numerous governmental entities up and down the gulf coast to handle their insurance claims. These entities included cities, school districts, community colleges and counties. Thousands of policyholders and Government entities across the gulf coast have selected Shaun as their lead attorney because of his proven results, as well as his leadership and experience in litigating large complex insurance claims.

Shaun Hodge is a Texan and has been a resident of Galveston County since 1995. He is happily married to Natalie Hodge, and they are the proud parents of two precious children, Nessa and Slade Hodge.

LEADERSHIP IN INSURANCE LITIGATION

Appointed member of Plaintiff Steering Committee (PSC) for In Re Hurricane Ike litigation (Cause No. 09-CV0147). In his role on the Plaintiff Steering Committee (PSC), Shaun lead and coordinated more than one hundred plaintiffs law firms in litigating and prosecuting more than ten thousand first party insurance claims against more than three dozen insurance entities for damages sustained by Hurricane Ike. As a member of the Plaintiff Steering Committee Shaun prosecuted class actions claims related to Hurricane Ike in Khattak v. Texas Windstorm Insurance, Cause No. 09-CV-0147 as well as lead counsel in the class action claim City of Santa Fe v. Texas Windstorm Insurance Association, Cause No. 12-CV-2015. Shaun has also been a lead attorney in filing numerous class action lawsuits against insurance companies that wrongly depreciate labor in their insurance estimates.

GOVERNMENTAL ENTITIES:

1) Lead attorney for City of Dickinson against TWIA

2) Lead attorney for City of La Marque against TWIA

3) Lead attorney for City of Santa Fe against TWIA

4) Lead attorney for College of the Mainland against TWIA

5) Lead attorney Dickinson ISD against TWIA

6) Lead attorney Texas City ISD against TWIA

7) Lead attorney Santa Fe ISD against TWIA

8) Lead attorney Anahuac ISD against TWIA

9) Lead attorney La Marque ISD against TWIA

10) Lead attorney Chambers County against TWIA

11) Co-Counsel Galveston County against TWIA

12) Lead attorney Hitchcock ISD v. Certain Underwriters at Lloyd’s London

Selected as lead counsel by dozens of governmental entities and agencies including cities, counties, community colleges and school districts throughout Texas for their first party insurance claims.

FIRST PARTY INSURANCE CLAIMS:

Personally handled and successfully resolved over ten thousand claims for property owners fighting their insurance companies for damages caused by natural disasters including hurricanes, tornadoes, hailstorms, windstorms, floods, fires, winter storms and more. Shaun has litigated thousands of residential and large commercial insurance claims in dozens of states across the country. Shaun is regularly sought out as a speaker to teach and lecture on insurance claim related issues across the country.

FIGHTING TO PROTECT THE RIGHTS OF POLICYHOLDERS:

Shaun is the co-founder of the Policyholder Preservation Association of America (PPAA). PPA was established to preserve and protect the rights of policyholders and to advocate on their behalf on insurance related matters and issues. PPA also conducts educational conferences and training to educate the public about insurance related issues and to teach and train other insurance industry professionals how to properly adjust a claim and document a loss.

Manny Hoffmann is an associate attorney at Boyd Boyd & Giddens where he primarily practices in the areas of insurance defense and personal injury law. He was licensed by the State Bar of Texas in 2022.

attorneys.name: Robert Hogan
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lubbock, TX
attorneys.bio:
Robert Hogan is an attorney at the Hogan Law Firm located in Lubbock, Texas. He represents clients with personal injury matters, including wrongful death, oil field accidents, defective products, insurance claims, industrial accidents, sexual assault, workers’ comp, immigration and naturalization, and deceptive trade practices. He has spent over 25 years advocating for the rights of West Texas's hardworking families, assisting them in obtaining compensation for injuries sustained due to the carelessness of others.

Mr. Hogan is a personal injury trial lawyer with Board Certification from the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He has defended clients in the Supreme Court of the United States, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit, and the federal courts of Texas, New Mexico and Colorado.

Mr. Hogan is from a military background and moved to Lubbock in 1979 to attend Lubbock High, Texas Tech University, and Texas Tech University School of Law. In Lubbock, he first worked in insurance defense law before making the transition to personal injury law at the Law Offices of Kevin Glasheen and eventually starting his own firm in 2006.

Mr. Hogan holds memberships in the South Plains Trial Lawyers Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the New Mexico Trial Lawyers Association, and the American Association for Justice. He holds an AV Preeminent* peer-review rating through Martindale-Hubbell and is a life member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer-review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Ratings™ fall into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: Adam Holden
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Adam Holden represents individuals and families who have been injured due to someone else’s negligence.

Before becoming a plaintiff’s attorney, Adam worked in insurance defense, representing corporations and insurance carriers in personal injury and premises liability cases. That experience gave him valuable insight into how insurance companies evaluate, defend, and try cases — insight he now uses to advocate strategically and aggressively for his clients.

Adam also previously served as an Assistant District Attorney, where he developed strong courtroom skills and tried cases before juries. His background as both a prosecutor and former defense attorney allows him to approach every case with preparation, confidence, and a deep understanding of how the other side thinks.

Clients choose Adam because he combines trial experience with personal attention. He is committed to clear communication, thorough preparation, and fighting for full and fair compensation.

If you need an attorney who knows how the defense operates and is ready to stand up for you, Adam Holden is prepared to help.

Adam also previously served as an Assistant District Attorney, where he developed strong courtroom skills and tried cases before juries. His background as both a prosecutor and former defense attorney allows him to approach every case with preparation, confidence, and a deep understanding of how the other side thinks.

Clients choose Adam because he combines trial experience with personal attention. He is committed to clear communication, thorough preparation, and fighting for full and fair compensation.

If you need an attorney who knows how the defense operates and is ready to stand up for you, Adam Holden is prepared to help.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Founder & Managing Attorney

R.J. Holladay is the managing attorney and founder of Holladay Law, based in Spring, Texas. With more than 20 years of legal experience, Mr. Holladay concentrates his practice exclusively on personal injury litigation, representing individuals and families who have suffered serious and catastrophic injuries through no fault of their own. He serves clients throughout Houston, Spring, Tomball, and The Woodlands, Texas.

Mr. Holladay was raised in a small town in Oklahoma, where he learned early the value of hard work, accountability, and personal responsibility. Those principles shaped his decision to serve nearly a decade in the United States Navy, where he developed the discipline, structure, and sense of duty that continue to define his professional approach today.

After completing his military service, Mr. Holladay put himself through college and law school, earning his degrees through determination and persistence rather than privilege or shortcuts. He earned his Juris Doctor from the University of Houston Law Center, where he was inducted into the Order of the Barristers, and completed his undergraduate studies at the University of North Texas, graduating magna cum laude.

Mr. Holladay began his legal career representing insurance companies and corporate defendants, gaining firsthand insight into how injury claims are evaluated, defended, and delayed. That experience now informs every case he handles. He understands the strategies insurers use to minimize exposure and structures cases from the outset to counter those tactics through disciplined preparation and trial-ready advocacy.

From 2005 to 2011, Mr. Holladay practiced as an associate attorney with Rathwell DeFord & Nizialek, where he developed a strong foundation in litigation and case strategy. Over the course of his career, he has obtained successful results in a wide range of cases, including wrongful death and other matters involving catastrophic injury. He is known for his thorough preparation, direct client communication, and willingness to pursue litigation when insurance companies refuse to act reasonably.

Mr. Holladay’s work has been recognized nationally. In 2019, Attorney & Practice Magazine named him a Top 10 Personal Injury Attorney. That same year, he was selected as Litigator of the Year by the American Institute of Trial Lawyers. In 2020, he received the Elite Advocate designation from the American Institute of Legal Advocates and has since been recognized for Excellence in Personal Injury Law for four consecutive years.

He is an active member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and the State Bar of Texas. Mr. Holladay is licensed to practice before all Texas state courts, as well as the United States District Courts for the Southern and Northern Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Steven Holden Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: COVID-19 Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Steve Holden received his undergraduate degree from Missouri State University in 1977. He later earned his law degree from the University of Tulsa College of Law in 1981. Upon graduation from law school, Mr. Holden did a two-year "tour" in the public defender's office where the cases were tough, fast paced, and unpredictable. The remainder of his years of practice have been dedicated to general civil litigation. He has been a trial lawyer for over 40 years. Mr. Holden has achieved an "AV-Preeminent" rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest rating awarded in terms of skill, integrity, and ethics. He has tried an estimated 200+ jury trials with in excess of 90% of his civil cases concluding successfully. He focuses on catastrophic injury/loss cases such as in trucking, product liability, bad faith litigation, construction, medical malpractice, employment law, mass tort litigation, insurance litigation, negligence, transportation, business litigation, class action, medical device litigation, general casualty litigation, coverage issues, personal injury, toxic torts, nursing homes, and first party claims.

Mr. Holden has lectured locally, nationally, and internationally on litigation and continues to lecture in areas involving litigation management and litigation avoidance. He has lectured on Wall Street on alternative dispute resolution and was a featured speaker in a nationwide teleconference seminar entitled, "Dorough v. Bell Avenue Nursing Home: How to Evaluate and Try the Tough Nursing Home Cases," which addressed risk management and evaluation. Mr. Holden was also a featured speaker in a nationally broadcast seminar conducted by direct satellite link to all of the carrier's regional offices to teach evaluation of the critical factors to stem the tide of multi-million-dollar plaintiff verdicts that are occurring throughout the country. The "Social Escalation" of plaintiff verdicts is an area of particular interest to Mr. Holden.

Mr. Holden is a member of the Texas, Dallas County, Tulsa County, Oklahoma, and American Bar Associations (member, American Bar sections on Tort and Insurance Practice Law, Litigation), Oklahoma Association of Defense Counsel, Federation of Defense and Corporate Counsel (FDCC), Defense Research Institute (DRI), and Claims and Litigation Management Alliance (CLM). Mr. Holden is licensed to practice before the United States Supreme Court as well as in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Missouri, and Kansas.

AV Rating, Martindale-Hubbell

Fellow of the American Bar Foundation (ABF)

attorneys.name: James Holmes
attorneys.practice_type: Oil & Gas Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
James enjoys a diverse practice of oil and gas cases and related transactional and regulatory work, business cases and transactional work, real-estate and contract disputes, and close-corporation and shareholder-oppression cases. Apart from his business expertise, he has handled many tort cases involving wrongful death and catastrophic injury. He has significant trial, appellate and transactional experience and is a sought-after legal and business educational speaker. Click here for a sampling of his speeches and publications.

James was born, raised and educated in Texas. Before practicing law in Dallas, he earned his Bachelor of Science from Trinity University in San Antonio and his Juris Doctorate from the University of Texas School of Law in Austin, where he served as an Editor on the Texas Law Review and graduated Order of the Coif. Following law school, James worked as a judicial clerk for The Texas Supreme Court, for Associate Justice Nathan Hecht, who became Chief Justice and the longest-serving Justice in the history of the Court.

James is an active member of several professional associations, including the Dallas Bar Association and the Texas Civil Justice League. For the University of Texas System, he is a member of the Chancellor's Council, the 1881 Society, and the Ashbel Smith Circle. He serves on the Dallas Steering Committee for the University of Texas School of Law.

In addition to his law practice, James operates Robur LLC, an oil and gas first purchaser and marketer. He also manages Robur Capital, L.P., a value-investing style investment partnership. James's concurrent focus on his business activities and his commercial law practice gives him a unique, superior viewpoint on his clients' legal needs and solutions therefor.

attorneys.name: Mackenzie Holst
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mackenzie Holst is a zealous and compassionate advocate for her clients navigating family law issues. She handles a variety of family law matters including divorce, child custody, adoptions, child custody modifications, child support, property division, and LGBT divorce and custody cases.

Mackenzie, originally from Orange County, California, has lived in the North Austin community for nearly a decade. She received her undergraduate degree from TCU in 2017, graduating magna cum laude, and her law degree from University of Texas School of Law in 2023, where she was the recipient of the prestigious Roberta Wright Reeves Presidential Scholarship. As an adoptee, she has had the personal goal of becoming a family law attorney since she was a child. She believes that it is her life’s calling to advocate for families and children as they go through challenging and uncertain circumstances.

Mackenzie is also dedicated to giving back to the community, especially Austin’s most vulnerable populations. In law school, she was a student attorney for the University of Texas’ Domestic Violence Clinic, representing victims of physical and emotional violence, and a Staff Editor for the Texas Journal on Civil Liberties & Civil Rights. She has also clerked at SAFE Austin, the city’s largest nonprofit dedicated to assisting victims of abuse, and dedicated dozens of pro bono hours at Volunteer Legal Services of Central Texas, where she remains a frequent volunteer at their pro bono family law clinics. In 2023, Mackenzie was honored with the Dean’s Achievement Award in Mediation from the University of Texas School of Law.

Apart from family law, one of Mackenzie’s greatest passions is LGBT rights. During law school, she was the President of OUTLaw – UT Law’s LGBT student organization – and a Pro Bono Scholar for the Gender Affirmation Project, which assists hundreds of trans Texans annually with obtaining name and gender marker changes. As a member of the community, and staunch advocate for LGBT rights, she is committed to helping LGBT Texans access legal resources and representation.

attorneys.name: Leslie Martin Hope
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Leslie Hope grew up in Dallas, Texas. She received a bachelor's degree in 1987, and a law degree in 1992, from Southern Methodist University. She has been licensed to practice in Texas since 1992. She is also licensed to practice before the U.S. District Court for the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts in Texas, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, and the Supreme Court of the United States.

Ms. Hope has been board certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in family law since 2004, and has been recertified every year since. Ms. Hope is also a member of the Texas Academy of Family Law Specialists. She has handled cases all over Texas involving complex property issues, appeals and adoptions.

She served as a board of director of the Family Law Section of the Dallas Bar Association, and is a member of the Annette Stewart Inn of Court, an organization promoting ethics in the legal profession. She has also volunteered as a visiting associate judge in the family courts of Dallas County. She is a member of the Dallas Bar Association.

Ms. Hope was also a member of Park Cities Rotary Club, a service organization, where she served on various committees, and the Board of Directors. Ms. Hope and her husband have previously fostered a child for the past six years and have fostered hundreds of dogs from local shelters until they are adopted or sent to their out of state rescue.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Addison, TX
attorneys.bio:
David P. Housel, Jr. focuses the majority of his practice in the area of family law including divorces, child custody disputes, property valuation and division, enforcement and collection of child support, enforcement of visitation rights, modification of child support, modification of visitation rights and modification of prior court orders. Additionally he has had a number of cases representing third parties in family law actions including grandparents, aunts and uncles in seeking either primary possession of a child relative or in seeking access to the child relative. attorneys.name: Jason H. Howard
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Keller, TX
attorneys.bio:
Experienced

Before founding Howard Lotspeich Alexander & Williams, PLLC, Mr. Howard devoted more than five years as a prosecutor in the Lubbock County Criminal District Attorney’s Office. Mr. Howard was involved in every facet of Texas criminal law, but his primary role was as a trial attorney. During his time as an Assistant District Attorney, he tried more than fifty contested cases before Texas juries. Aside from trial, he handled countless plea negotiations and suppression hearings, as well as probation revocations and reinstatements. He also managed grand jury dockets and filed thousands of cases ranging from class C misdemeanors to first-degree felonies.

While Mr. Howard was assigned as a prosecutor to the specialty courts division in Lubbock County, he helped begin one of the first “re-entry” courts in the state. Through Freedom Court, he helped recovering addicts “re-enter” society after leaving inpatient drug and alcohol rehabilitation centers.

Accomplished

Mr. Howard proved himself early in his career as one of the finest trial attorneys in Lubbock County, rising quickly through the misdemeanor and felony ranks before earning the position of Felony Chief for the 140th District Court. His conviction rate at trial ranked as one of the highest in his trial division. Mr. Howard also assisted the Lubbock Police Department in cadet training for the Lubbock Police Academy. He was invited to and completed the Texas District and County Attorney’s Association Advanced Trial Skills Course in 2011 at Baylor University. In 2013, Mr. Howard was named as one the Top 100 Trial Lawyers for Criminal Defense by the National Trial Lawyers Association.

Grounded

Born and raised in a small, West Texas town, Mr. Howard was taught to love his neighbor as himself. Helping others is his passion and giving them his whole-hearted effort is all he knows. He loves God and his family. He also enjoys exercising and the outdoors. He and his family are members at Fellowship of the Parks in Keller.

attorneys.name: Aaron Howard
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Aaron Howard was born and raised in Dallas, Texas. He attended Texas Tech University, where he received his undergraduate degree in Political Science. Thereafter, Aaron immediately attended law school at the University of Houston. While in law school, Aaron served as a board member of the Black Law Student Association (BLSA) and worked as a judicial intern to the Honorable Andrew S. Hanen of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

After obtaining his Juris Doctor from the University of Houston, Aaron began his legal career by working for a personal injury firm in Houston, Texas, where gained jury trial experience in the Harris County District courts. While in Houston, Aaron also briefly worked in insurance defense, representing clients in construction defect claims, commercial vehicle accidents, contract disputes, and real estate transaction disputes. However, Aaron quickly realized that his passion is in fighting for those who have been hurt or wronged by the negligence of others, rather than representing corporations and insurance companies, and returned to practicing personal injury.

Thereafter, Aaron returned to his hometown of Dallas, Texas, and joined a mass tort firm, where he fought on the behalf of individuals who were injured by dangerous pharmaceutical drugs and medical devices against large pharmaceutical companies, such as Johnson & Johnson, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, and Gilead Sciences.

Since joining Thompson Law, Aaron has focused on representing clients involved in injury claims related to car accidents, general negligence, trucking collisions, pedestrian accidents, motorcycle accidents, dog bite cases, and wrongful death claims.

Outside of the office, Aaron enjoys spending time with his friends and family, traveling, and watching his favorite sports teams.

attorneys.name: Mackenzie Howard
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mackenzie Howard has a practice focus dedicated to the representation of victims and their families in complex personal injury and wrongful death cases. She is passionate about effecting needed change while obtaining meaningful results for her clients. Mackenzie’s creativity, attention to detail, and confidence makes her a fierce competitor, effective negotiator, and an aggressive trial lawyer. She is not afraid to go toe-to-toe in order to obtain the results her clients are counting on.

Mackenzie has a unique attentiveness and sensitivity to her clients’ needs, which adds to her effectiveness. It is her thoroughness and ability to explain complex legal concepts in a relatable way that makes her clients feel comfortable and confident with the civil justice system after a life-altering injury or tragedy resulting in the loss of a loved one.

A native Texan, Mackenzie grew up in Sugar Land, TX. She earned her undergraduate degree from The University of Texas at Austin. Mackenzie obtained her law degree from Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law. During her time there, she was an active participant in the Board of Advocates, serving as the director of attorney outreach and competing in several negotiation competitions.

attorneys.bio:
John L. Hubble is a graduate of Southern Methodist University and St. Mary’s University School of Law. While a law student at St. Mary’s, Mr. Hubble distinguished himself by earning the following accolades: K.K. Woodley Memorial Scholarship; Who’s Who Among American Students in Law School; American Jurisprudence Award for Excellence in Contracts; Dean’s List; St. Mary’s Law Journal, 1975 – 1976.

Upon graduation for law school Mr. Hubble became an Assistant District Attorney, Dallas County, Felony Trial Division. After leaving the D.A’s offices, Mr. Hubble entered the private practice of law with a large downtown Dallas law firm representing clients through out Texas in a wide variety of legal matters. In 1994 he formed the law firm of Hubble & Pistorius practicing in the areas of insurance claims and property insurance litigation, personal injury, construction defects litigation, real estate litigation and general business contract and tort litigation. See Areas of Practice. Mr. Hubble has also served as General Counsel to American Federal Bank, F.S.B., Dallas, Texas, and General Counsel to Camden Financial Corporation, a Subsidiary of Sandia Federal Savings, Dallas, Texas.

Mr. Hubble is a member of the American Bar Association (ABA), State Bar of Texas, Dallas Bar Association (DBA), the Tort and Insurance Practice section (TIPS) of the DBA where he has served as an officer and director, the National Association of Public Insurance Adjusters (NAPIA) and the Texas Association of Public Insurance Adjusters (TAPIA).

attorneys.name: Steven F. Hudgins
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Steven is a trial lawyer whose practice represents an even blend of personal injury, insurance and commercial disputes. He is board certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Personal Injury Law. Steven earned this recognition after successfully defending and prosecuting numerous personal injury lawsuits, involving commercial auto and premises liability claims.

Steven’s insurance law practice includes the representation of admitted and non-admitted carriers in first-party disputes that often arise following catastrophic weather events in the Gulf Coast region. Steven is head of the firm’s subrogation practice, successfully protecting the interests of the insurers and recovering millions in settlement on their behalf.

Steven also maintains an active commercial practice, counseling and representing a broad range of business clients, ranging from small family-owned companies to companies listed in the Fortune® 500. Such services include the preparation and review of employment agreements, service contracts, dealership agreements, investigation of pre-suit claims, and resolution of claims brought by and against former employees and/or directors. Steven recently tried and won a lawsuit where he represented an insurance agent being sued under a non-compete agreement, receiving a judgment awarding his client his attorneys’ fees.

Steven is a second-generation Houstonian and second-generation graduate of South Texas College of Law. During law school, Steven interned on the Texas Supreme Court for the Honorable Bob Gammage.

attorneys.name: Michael D. Hudgins
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Legal Matters Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Michael is a trial and appellate lawyer. He focuses his practice on complex legal matters, involving professional malpractice (all disciplines), directors and officers, HOA law, school law, sovereign immunity, and coverage disputes.

Michael graduated from South Texas College of Law in 1993. While there, Michael served as President of the Board of Advocates (1992-93), elected to the National Order of Barristers, and earned membership into the Order of the Lytae Honor Society. Michael was a member of three first place national moot court teams, including the Tulane University Sports Law Competition where he was named Best Advocate and the John Marshall Privacy Law Competition where he co-authored the Best Brief, which is published in the Software Law Journal at 6 Software Law Journal 115 (Feb. 1993). Michael served as an adjunct professor/advocacy assistant for South Texas College of Law’s advocacy program until 2005; his teams won five national titles.

Michael’s professional accomplishments include serving as lead appellate counsel for the City of Houston in a consolidated proceeding with other municipalities before the Texas Supreme Court in a case that answered the question of whether sovereign immunity exists in breach of contract cases. Michael and the firm’s work on this matter resulted in the Supreme Court’s landmark decision of City of Mexia v. Tooke, which recognized sovereign immunity in breach of contract cases. Michael successfully led a litigation team of nine attorneys through a two-month trial defending allegations that his client’s stole two billion cubic feet of gas through a casing leak—a case the Hattiesburg American reported as being one of the longest trials ever in Lamar County, Mississippi.

Michael Hudgins is a second-generation Houstonian and second-generation graduate of South Texas College of Law. Following law school and before beginning his practice, Michael served as a Briefing Attorney to the Honorable Murry B. Cohen of the First Court of Appeals in Houston from 1993-94. He is a frequent lecturer at continuing legal education seminars in both Texas and New York.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: Tanglewood v. Feldman, 436 S.W.3d 48 (Tex.App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2014, pet. denied) (judgment for attorneys’ fees reversed on the basis that attorneys’ fees are not available under the Texas Declaratory Judgment Act where attorneys’ fees are not otherwise available in an HOA dispute).
In re Ranchers and Farmers Mut. Ins. Co., 2011 WL 1631820 (Tex.App.—Beaumont, April 28, 2011) (mandamus relief granted following trial court’s denial of motion to compel appraisal).
City of Houston v. Allco, Inc., 206 S.W.3d 113 (Tex. 2006) (case decided by City of Mexia v. Tooke, which held immunity from suit not waived in breach of contract cases).
Sydlik v. REEIII, Inc., 195 S.W.3d 329 (Tex.App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 2006, no pet.) (affirmed summary judgment granted under the doctrine of release).

Gillespie v. Scherr, 987 S.W.2d 129 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 1998, pet. denied) (affirmed summary judgment against attorney who filed an attempted class action suit, holding lawyer’s professional duty does not extend to putative class action Plaintiffs).

Verinakis v. Medical Profiles, Inc., 987 S.W.2d 90 (Tex. App.—Houston [14th Dist.] 1998, pet. denied) (affirmed summary judgment in a fear of AIDS case where medical testing company reported the claimant wrongly notified insurance applicant and claimant that he had tested positive for HIV).
State v. Wollesen, 93 S.W.3d 910 (Tex. App.—Austin 2002, no pet.) (affirmed judgment following a jury trial in a wrongful death suit, involving waiver of sovereign immunity in special defect case).

attorneys.name: Angie Roberts Huckaby
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
Angie Roberts spent the first decade of her legal career with the Hays County District Attorney's Office. She started as a law clerk and once licensed, she became a civil prosecutor handling every aspect of civil justice with distinction and was promoted to the Chief position in July of 2017. As Chief, Angie managed five assistant district attorneys, seven paralegals, and several law clerks during her tenure. Angie's dedication to protecting children and victims of domestic violence is unwavering.

Angie's experience with civil law at the district attorney's office gives her a unique advantage in managing complex litigation, especially involving, child modifications, termination of parental rights, and civil jury trials. Angie has had the privilege of preparing for over 17 civil jury trials and arguing a dozen civil jury trials to verdict. She has experience with Post-Convictions Appeals and has presented oral arguments to the Texas Appellate Courts. Additionally, Angie has filed numerous Writs, Protective Orders, Motions to Quash, Forfeiture cases, Expunctions, Nondisclosures, Mental Health commitments, open records, and assisted in advising law enforcement agencies.

Angie prides herself on blending the responsibilities of practicing law and running a small business with being a wife and the mother of two energetic young children. Through this framework, Angie is able visualize the big picture for each case and execute a strategic plan of action for her clients. While each case is unique some of the most complex issues are best understood by the perspective of a mother and business professional.

Additionally, Angie has filed numerous Writs, Protective Orders, Motions to Quash, Forfeiture cases, Expunctions, Nondisclosures, Mental Health commitments, open records, and assisted in advising law enforcement agencies.

Angie prides herself on blending the responsibilities of practicing law and running a small business with being a wife and the mother of two energetic young children. Through this framework, Angie is able visualize the big picture for each case and execute a strategic plan of action for her clients. While each case is unique some of the most complex issues are best understood by the perspective of a mother and business professional.

attorneys.name: Caleb Hudgens
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
Caleb is an attorney at Key Law Office. His primary practice areas are family law and estate planning.

Caleb is a native of Haskell, Texas. He attended Texas State University as a Terry Scholar, and served as an officer of the Student Foundation and as a member of the Council of Scholars for both colleges of mass communication and liberal arts. After graduating summa cum laude in 2010, Caleb began a 10-year long career in education by moving to Cuernavaca, Morelos, México, and teaching English at Cuauhnáhuac Instituto Inglés. Once back in Texas, Caleb worked as a public educator in various school districts teaching English, English as a Second Language, reading, and debate before working as a Digital Learning Coach in Hays CISD and later as an Instructional Technology Coordinator in Schertz-Cibolo-Universal City ISD. Caleb also served as Area 20 Director of the Texas Computer Educator Association representing educators in and around San Antonio for the State of Texas. In 2020, Caleb enrolled at Texas Tech University School of Law in Lubbock, Texas. There he was a member of the Texas Tech Board of Barristers, president of OUTlaw, and member of the Family Law Association, Environmental Law Association, and Black Law Student Association. Through his work in public education, Caleb discovered a need and his passion for advocacy for children and their families.

Caleb speaks Spanish, prefers Luzianne tea over Lipton, and is an active member of the Texas Native Plant Society. Most weekends you can find Caleb and his cat, Margo, working in his garden cultivating Texas native plants and cacti.

attorneys.name: Serena E. Hudson
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
A native Houstonian, family law attorney Serena E. Hudson assists clients with divorce, child custody, and child support cases among other family law-related matters, including those that are heavily contested. Her practice encompasses Greater Houston counties, including Harris, Montgomery, Fort Bend, Galveston, and Brazoria, as well as other various counties in Texas, including Collin, Tarrant, Dallas, and Bexar.

Serena earned a B.F.A. in Studio Art at The University of Texas at Austin before receiving her J.D. from the South Texas College of Law Houston in December 2017. During her time at South Texas College of Law Houston, Serena was selected to be a part of the school’s prestigious Varsity Moot Court team, where she traveled across the country, participating in national Moot Court Competitions, and worked on advocacy, legal writing, and litigation.

Serena was drawn to law through an interest in expanding her knowledge in the legal aspects of fine art, but quickly found her passion in family law in law school through her family law and marital property classes. Before becoming an associate attorney, she worked as a law clerk at various firms and institutions practicing in legal areas pertaining to family law, mass-tort litigation, and fine arts litigation.

Serena E. Hudson has extensive trial experience, especially at such a young age.

Apart from her professional career, Serena serves her community of Houston as a member of the Houston Young Lawyers Association.

Serena is a life-long competitive swimmer and loves spending time with family and friends outside of the office.

attorneys.name: C.M. Hudspeth
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
C. M. "Hank" Hudspeth (1919-2019). After serving in the Navy in World War II, Hudspeth joined his father-in-law, Albert DeLange, in 1946 to form the firm now known as DeLange Hudspeth McConnell & Tibbets. Mr. Hudspeth was the managing partner of the firm for over forty years and served as Of Counsel to the firm thereafter until his death.

During his career, Mr. Hudspeth was active in numerous professional organizations, including serving as director and vice-president of the State Bar of Texas, and the chair of the Real Estate, Probate, and Trust Section of the State Bar of Texas.

Mr. Hudspeth was Trustee Emeritus of Rice University and served as the Vice-President and Trustee of the Brown Foundation, Inc. He also served on the Board of Directors of Stewart information Services Corp. and related Stewart companies.

He received his B.A. in 1940 from Rice University and his LL.B. (now J.D.) in 1946 from the University of Texas Law School. While in law school, Mr. Hudspeth was a member of the Order of the Coif and the Chancellors, and he was the note editor of the Texas Law Review. Upon graduation, he served for five semesters as assistant professor of law at the University of Texas.

attorneys.name: Russ Hunt Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Russ Hunt, Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Georgetown, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Russ Hunt, Jr. offers a personalized and unique approach to criminal defense. He takes the time to speak and work with each client individually. His goal is to address their concerns and anxieties, while tirelessly working toward positive outcomes for their cases. When you or a loved one reach out for representation, rest assured that you will have the opportunity to directly speak with Russ about your situation. He does not charge for initial consultations and will provide you with information and options to help make your journey smoother.

Trial History

Russ has been defending the criminally accused since 1994. With 30 years of experience, he has tried dozens of jury trials in Central Texas, in both state and federal courts. He has also tried cases in various locations across the state, such as Hillsboro, San Angelo and Del Rio.

He actively participates in criminal defense associations such as the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL), Alabama Criminal Defense Lawyers Association (ACDLA) and Williamson County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association (WCCDLA). From 2006-2007, he held the position of presiding director at ACDLA. Additionally, from 2012-2014, Russ served as a founding vice president of the WCCDLA.

Honors And Awards

Russ is proud to have been selected for inclusion in the prestigious Super Lawyers list. He has been recognized with this honor every year since 2008. In addition, he has been rated the highest possible rating of AV Preeminent* through Martindale-Hubbell since 2009, a distinction given by his fellow attorneys.

Continuing Legal Education

Russ stays up to date with his legal skills by attending training seminars and also shares his knowledge as a seminar speaker. He has achieved membership in the esteemed College of the State Bar of Texas due to his extensive participation in criminal law seminars.

Licensed in Texas since 1994, Russ Hunt, Jr. is also authorized to appear before the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas since 1995. Additionally, in 1996, he obtained certification to practice in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 5th Circuit. Furthermore, in 1998, Russ was honored with the designation to practice in the prestigious U.S. Supreme Court.

Hunt hails from Waco, Texas. His father, Russell Hunt, Sr., is a seasoned criminal defense attorney, serving clients in Waco and nearby regions for over four decades.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ falls into two categories – legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: Matt Hurt
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Matt Hurt, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in Prosper, TX
attorneys.bio:
Matt Hurt started Law Office of Matt Hurt, PLLC in 2023. He focuses exclusively on eminent domain and condemnation litigation. Prior to starting The Law Office of Matt Hurt, PLLC, Matt practiced successfully at Dawson & Sodd, PLLC, and prior to this he practiced almost exclusively in the area of eminent domain, representing both landowners and condemning authorities while working for Locke Lord, LLP in Dallas. Before focusing so closely in this area, Matt represented clients in construction defect litigation, antitrust matters, personal injury and product liability cases, and numerous business litigation matters.

He graduated magna cum laude from Texas A&M University with a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering while also completing the Engineering Scholars Program in 1996. While studying there, he was nominated by the Department of Civil Engineering for Outstanding Student in the College of Engineering and he served in student government. Matt worked in the civil engineering field for nearly two years before attending law school. Some of his work involved research on the Texas A&M campus for the United States Navy. His engineering background and experience help him to envision and critically analyze the impact that a government project will have on a landowner's property. Due to his engineering experience, he has become invaluable to clients, most notably in highway takings and other matters involving engineering analysis of damage to properties from partial takings.

In 2001, Matt graduated magna cum laude from Texas Tech University School of Law. During law school, he earned the highest grade in three classes: Torts, Products Liability, and Legal Writing. Matt was president of the law school's Texas Aggie Bar Association, served on the Board of Barristers, and was Technology Editor of the Texas Tech Law Review. He and his mock trial partner won the Texas Tech School of Law mock trial competition during their third year of law school.

The Thomson Reuters service has recognized Matt as a Super Lawyer in Texas eminent domain law for 2014-2024. Before being named a Super Lawyer, Thomson Reuters also recognized Matt as a Rising Star in construction litigation in 2005, and in the area of eminent domain in 2013 and 2015.

Matt is licensed to practice in Texas and Colorado, state and federal courts in Texas, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.

When not practicing law, Matt enjoys spending time with his kids, on the ranch, or in the John Deere 4440. Matt and his family attend Prestonwood Baptist Church North Campus in Prosper.

attorneys.bio: Jordan was born and raised in Arizona, with family roots in central Texas. She grew up visiting Rockdale and Temple, Texas. After starting their family, Jordan and her husband relocated to Temple, Texas to be closer to family while raising their young children. Jordan received her Bachelor’s degree in Criminology and Criminal Justice from Northern Arizona University in 2017. In 2021, she received her Juris Doctorate from Lincoln Memorial University Duncan School of Law in Knoxville, Tennessee. While in law school, Jordan took an interest in domestic relations and was excited to begin her career at the firm in the family law department in 2022. Jordan is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Bell County Bar Association, and the Bell County Young Lawyer’s Association. She handles family law matters, including divorce, custody issues, adoptions, and prenuptial/postnuptial agreements. Kind, ethical, and friendly representation are of the utmost importance to her. In her free time, Jordan can be found with her husband, Brian, or playing with their two children. She loves to visit local parks and restaurants, take walks with their Newfoundland dog, or curl up with one of her cats.

attorneys.name: Shannon H. Hutcheson
attorneys.practice_type: Labor and Employment Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Whether it be for the firm's financial services clients or employment law clients, Shannon is known for her strategic advice that never loses sight of the business objectives. As one client said, Shannon is "always spot-on, practical, and efficient. She comes up with creative solutions that avoid costly litigation but, if litigation is the endgame, then she is the lawyer you want."

Shannon divides her time between advising the firm's financial services clients, overseeing the firm's AAA consumer dispute docket, and advising the firm's employment law clients on complex compliance issues. Being Board Certified in Labor and Employment Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Shannon is often called on to conduct independent investigations, lead employment-related litigation or tackle the most vexing employment law problems for the firm's clients.

After law school, Shannon practiced as a commercial litigator with the global firm of Baker Botts LLP for over twelve years before launching a solo practice and then co-founding Hutcheson Bowers LLLP in 2011.

Shannon loves fundraising for her favorite causes and political candidates, and serving on nonprofit and professional boards of directors. She and her family bleed burnt orange and you can often find them at University of Texas sporting events cheering on the Horns.
