attorneys.name: Lynne Jurek
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation & Appeals Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lynne M. Jurek (f/k/a Lynne Jurek Shannon) is AV Preeminent® Peer Review Rated and the firm’s Managing Director. She focuses her practice on Civil Litigation and is Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. She has also been selected for inclusion in Texas Super Lawyers in 2012-2016 and 2018-2020. She recently completed the St. Louis University program and received her certification in Corporate Ethics and Compliance Management (CECM).

Lynne has extensive experience representing insurance companies and their insureds, as well as other self-insured corporate and individual clients in cases involving First and Third Party Property Claims, Oil and Gas Litigation, Public Sector, Admiralty and Maritime Litigation, Product Liability Litigation, General Commercial Litigation, Transportation/Trucking, Construction, Probate Litigation, Family Law, Health and Corporate Law. Lynne is an avid litigator who is adept at handling cases in state and federal courts, from inception of the case through trial and appeal.

An accomplished writer, Lynne co-authored “Proposed Wyoming Title Standards, Part I of III” for the Wyoming Law Review (2013) and “The Business of Gas Pipeline Condemnation: A Multistate Analysis” for the Houston Business and Tax Law Journal (2013). She has also spoken locally and nationally on the issues of cost containment and construction claims, handling admiralty and personal injury lawsuits, as well as on good faith claims handling practices and litigation procedures for claims adjusters.

Lynne is currently or has been a member of the Texas Association of Civil Trial and Appellate Specialists, the Bar Association of the Fifth Federal District, the Minnesota State Bar and the Houston Bar Association. Lynne is or also has been a member of the Risk Management Society (RIMS), the Inns of Court, the Greater Houston Partnership, and the Associated Builders and Contractors (ABC Greater Houston). She is a Sustaining Member of Victory, a branch of the American Cancer Society, and is a Founder of Protectors’ Memorial Foundation. She has enjoyed playing recreational soccer with the Houston Women’s Soccer Association and the TORSO Soccer League in Houston.

Lynne received her Bachelor of Arts Degree from Gustavus Adolphus College in St. Peter, Minnesota, in 1987. She also studied at Exeter University in England in 1986. She obtained her Juris Doctor from William Mitchell College of Law in St. Paul, Minnesota, in 1991. Lynne is licensed to practice law in Minnesota and Texas and has been admitted pro hac vice in Louisiana. She is admitted to practice before the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, as well as U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Kathryn Kahle
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn Kahle is the founder and owner of her own law firm, Kathryn Kahle, PLLC. She is one of only a very small percentage of Texas lawyers to become “double board certified,” achieving Board Certification by the Board of Texas Legal Specialization in both Criminal Law and Juvenile Law. She has 20 years of legal and trial experience.

She focuses her practice on vigorously defending both adults and juveniles charged with misdemeanors and felonies in Harris County, Texas. Notable results have included earning felony and misdemeanor dismissals for a variety of family assault cases, including for aggravated assaults of a family member, choking offenses, aggravated robberies, and injury to a child. Additionally, she has secured outstanding results for her clients, including reductions from capital murder and murder charges.

Kathryn has worked in the legal industry since 2005, spending over 15 years of her legal career as a prosecutor with the Harris County District Attorney’s Office. At the DA’s office, she first chaired over 55 jury trials, including capital murder, murder, aggravated sexual assault, sexual assault, aggravated robbery, and burglary of a habitation cases. She also rose in the ranks to achieve Chief positions in the 179th Criminal District Court and the 314th Juvenile District Court, as well as serving as Chief of the Child Exploitation Section. This means she served as the DA’s top lawyer handling cases in those courts and section. In addition, Kathryn served as a trial prosecutor in the child abuse division, the family criminal law division, the narcotics division, the misdemeanor division, and in various courts in the felony trial bureau. Kathryn can skillfully and successfully defend clients because she knows how prosecutors think.

Prior to opening her own firm and her work with the Harris County District Attorney’s Office, she worked for a large and prestigious regional law firm, where she was an associate attorney in the litigation division. In addition, she worked as a news anchor, reporter, and producer in Abilene and San Antonio, Texas, often covering government, crime, and feature stories prior to attending law school.

Kathryn graduated from Trinity University with a Bachelor of Arts in Communication and Political Science in 2000, magna cum laude. She was a member of the Golden Key National Honor Society, television co-host of "Trinity Today," and received the Outstanding Senior Award from the Department of Communication and the Trinity University Scholar Award. Subsequently, she earned her law degree from South Texas College of Law Houston in 2005. During law school, she served as Assistant Note and Comment Editor of the South Texas Law Review and achieved great success as part of the nationally known South Texas Mock Trial Team.

She is a member of the Houston Bar Association, Texas Bar College, Harris County Criminal Lawyers Association, Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, and State Bar of Texas.

Kathryn is the attorney you need fighting for you or your loved one. She personally handles each case and prides herself on great communication with each and every one of her clients. Throughout the process, you will be kept informed and all of your questions and concerns will be addressed in a timely manner. She looks forward to working with you!

attorneys.name: J. Todd Kale
attorneys.practice_type: Asbestos and Mesothelioma Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
J. Todd Kale, a shareholder at Baron & Budd, has dedicated his career to fighting the companies that knowingly exposed people to the deadly carcinogen known as asbestos. Todd enjoys partnering with patients and families and helping them navigate the legal process during the most difficult time in their lives. Todd works on the front lines with the firm’s Asbestos Litigation Team. He meets with mesothelioma patients and their families across the country to gather the information necessary to successfully pursue their cases. More than any other aspect of his job, Todd enjoys meeting with these patients and families. Through these meetings, Todd becomes part of each of these families and becomes involved in the family’s specific struggles, needs and hopes. He is honored to be trusted by so many patients and families as they deal with the diagnosis and prognosis of mesothelioma. His 20 years of experience in this field make him a valuable resource for any information the family may need—both legal and medical.

For more than two decades, Todd has worked on numerous asbestos lawsuits, managing thousands of cases from start to finish. Through his many years as an asbestos lawyer, Todd has developed an in-depth understanding of the legal system and how to best navigate that system on behalf of clients. Since 1993, he has helped clients recover hundreds of millions of dollars in settlements. Todd also has experience pursuing not only asbestos manufacturers, but also equipment manufacturers and employers who are responsible for a client’s exposure to asbestos. Never one to back down from a fight, Todd is proud to have fought on behalf of mesothelioma and asbestos clients for his entire career.

Todd earned his J.D. from the University of Tulsa College of Law in 1990 and his B.B.A. from the University of Texas.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hillery is the first attorney in her family and has been practicing family law for over 20 years.

Hillery has an analytical approach to the way she practices law. She takes time to understand and analyze the case and client’s objectives, and then strategizes, crafts, and customizes her strategy to achieve her client’s goals and yield the best possible result.

Hillery’s own parents divorced when she was in high school and she remembers well what it was like to live through the major changes in her own life caused by the divorce. She understands how important it is to preserve the ability to co-parent post-divorce. That goal is best served when the parties are able to negotiate an agreement on parenting and property issues without the necessity of going to Court.

attorneys.bio: Tim's primary practice consists of representing water and wastewater utilities in navigating the regulatory requirements of the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and the Public Utility Commission. In addition to his practice responsibilities, Tim is also an Adjunct Professor at Stephen F. Austin State University where he teaches Environmental Law in the Department of Business Communications and Legal Studies and Environmental Policy and Regulation in the Arthur Temple School of Forestry.

attorneys.name: Alexis Katz
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Alexis Katz is an experienced advocate who litigates personal injury claims for the severely injured in Texas and Louisiana. For the first 17 years of her legal career, Alexis defended businesses and insureds from the same kind of lawsuits she prosecutes today. As a prior insurance defense attorney, Alexis uses her vast insider knowledge to advance her client's case with a unique understanding of the insurance industry.

A native of Houston, Alexis attended top-ranked state schools, earning her Bachelor of Arts in Government with Honors from the University of Texas at Austin and her Juris Doctor from the University of Houston Law Center, where she received an academic scholarship. Alexis studied internationally, including in the Czech Republic, and regularly visits her family in South Africa.

After law school, Alexis trained at a boutique Dallas business litigation firm before moving to Louisiana, where she obtained her Louisiana law license. After five years of practice in Louisiana, she moved home to Houston and settled into a decade-long career in litigation defense. While defending a myriad of general liability, commercial, insurance, and product liability matters, Alexis gained invaluable knowledge about the insurance claims and defense process. With the ability to anticipate defense strategy and a unique understanding of the insurance industry decision-making process, Alexis uses her advantage to obtain better results for the severely injured.

Not only is Alexis a career litigation attorney, but she is also an active mother of two. When not fighting for her clients, Alexis enjoys traveling, cooking, reading, and being outdoors.

attorneys.name: Gregory S. Kazen
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning, Wills & Trusts Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Gregory S. Kazen is from an extended family of over 30 lawyers, including judges and distinguished public servants. Originally from Laredo, Texas, he obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree from Trinity University in San Antonio in 1993, studied Jurisprudence and Moral and Political Philosophy at Glasgow University in Scotland, and obtained his Juris Doctorate degree from University of Texas School of Law in Austin in 1998, where he served as an editor for The American Journal of Criminal Law.

Gregory subsequently became a partner at Atlas, Hall & Rodriguez, LLP, in McAllen, where he practiced for over twenty years covering a broad range of property law including estate planning and probate, commercial real estate and banking, leasing, special asset projects, local government law, and eminent domain. Gregory has represented the interests of individuals, businesses, national and State banks, as well as Hidalgo County and Hidalgo County Drainage District No. 1. His representation extended to all sides of transactions, including executors, trustees, real estate developers, sellers, buyers, lenders, landlords, and tenants, from negotiation and drafting through signing and closing.

Gregory is a member of the State Bar of Texas (1998), a member of the Real Estate, Probate and Trust Law Section of the State Bar of Texas, is certified in Professional Fiduciary Management for Trustees, and has been granted Guardianship Certification. He is a former member of the Hidalgo County Bar Association and the Hidalgo County Real Estate Law Section and served as Director of the Hidalgo County Young Lawyers Association. Gregory was previously recognized by his peers as a Texas Super Lawyers Rising Star. While living in McAllen, he served as a Director for both the Civic Center Advisory Board and McAllen Development Corporation, Inc. Gregory is licensed to practice in the United States District Court, Western District of Texas and Southern District of Texas. Upon moving back to Austin with his children in 2019, Gregory joined the Austin Bar Association and is a member of the Real Estate and the Estate Planning sections.

Sarah Keathley is a professional advocate for justice, being a trusted Corsicana lawyer for over 20 years. She received her Juris Doctor from St. Mary’s University School of Law in May of 1994 and was licensed by the Supreme Court of Texas to practice law that same year. In 1999, Sarah founded Keathley & Keathley Law Firm after working for the State of Texas, a Dallas family law firm, and a private law firm in Navarro County for 3 years. At the firm, she handles civil and criminal litigation, family law cases, wills, probate, real estate matters and more. Sarah is not only a Texas TMCA Certified Mediator but also serving again as President of the Navarro County Bar Association, demonstrating her commitment to staying sharp and educated on the legal matters affecting her clients. She aims to be the solution to her clients’ problems rather than part of it.

attorneys.name: Steve Keathley
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Corsicana, TX
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Corsicana, attorney Steve Keathley began his education at Texas A&M University before earning his Juris Doctor in 1993 at Hamline-University School of Law, in St. Paul Minnesota. Steve started his legal career as a prosecutor in the 33rd Judicial District then later joined his wife Sarah in opening Keathley & Keathley Law Firm in 1999. His time at the firm was cut short when he was elected as the Criminal District Attorney of Navarro County, where he served in this capacity until 2007. Nonetheless, he returned to Keathley & Keathley Law Firm and focuses his practice of criminal defense in addition to civil and family litigation. Steve stays actively involved in the legal community as a member of the State Bar of Texas, the College of the State Bar of Texas, the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, and the Navarro College Police Academy Advisory Board.

attorneys.name: Robert Keating
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Rob Keating has successfully represented individuals charged with crimes ranging from serious felony offenses to minor municipal citations in counties all across Texas.

Rob has a unique perspective gained by his broad life experiences before becoming an attorney. Shortly after he graduated from high school in Decatur, Texas, he joined the U.S. Navy, where he served for ten years aboard attack submarines. After leaving the Navy, he worked as a corporate trainer, developing his public speaking skills, before attending law school. While in law school at Southern Methodist University, Rob gained valuable experience as an intern with both the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office and the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office.

As a firearms enthusiast, Rob is an NRA-certified Pistol Instructor, Home Firearms Safety Instructor, and Range Safety Officer. He is a former Texas License to Carry a Handgun Instructor and is an affiliated attorney with the Armed Citizens’ Legal Defense Network.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio: Andie is an associate at Boyd Boyd & Giddens and practices in insurance defense law. Andie was raised in Wichita, Kansas. During her off time, Andie enjoys exploring new restaurants, spending time with her family, and fitness.

attorneys.name: Edward P. "Ted" Keenan
attorneys.firm_name: Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in inner-city Houston, Ted is a trial attorney and advocate for justice. The son of a dynamic trial lawyer and a product of area public schools, Ted knew from an early age that he was called to represent those in need. His practice is built on strong values that matter deeply to him and his clients alike.

Ted thrives under pressure and enjoys working hard towards a goal. While attending Lamar High School, Ted was awarded first-team All-State honors in lacrosse. He went on to earn his B.A. in Political Science from Texas Tech University where he graduated with honors. There, he was captain of the men’s lacrosse team that earned a berth into the national championship tournament, a first for the program. Upon graduation, Ted returned home to attend the University of Houston Law Center where he was awarded the Dean’s Scholarship. During his time at UH Law, he clerked year-round for Abraham Watkins firm partner Mo Aziz, learning how to fight for clients in wrongful death and catastrophic personal injury actions.

After passing the Texas bar, Ted gained invaluable experience with a boutique complex commercial litigation firm where he represented individual and corporate clients in a wide variety of civil matters. In 2019, Ted returned to the plaintiffs’ bar, sharpening his skills at well-respected maritime firm where he successfully advocated for clients in both commercial and personal injury actions. Notably, Ted was part of the trial team that successfully secured an eight-figure settlement from the jack-up rig designer and the classification society on behalf of a group of international workers injured and killed during evacuation when the rig collapsed in the Bay of Campeche.

Ted is licensed to practice in Texas and is admitted to practice in the United States District Courts for the Southern, Northern, and Eastern Districts of Texas, and the United States Court of Appeals 5th District.

attorneys.name: Orlando Kell
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Orlando Kell grew up in El Paso, Texas. He attended the University of Texas at Austin from 1996-2001, where he landed on the University Honors list three separate semesters in earning a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Government and Minor in Radio-Television-Film. He then went on to St. Mary’s University School of Law, where he graduated Cum Laude in the top 10% of his entire 2005 graduating class.

During his time at St. Mary’s, Mr. Kell accomplished many things. He helped pioneer the reformation of the Sports and Entertainment Law Society. He also dedicated a full year of pro bono service to the St. Mary’s Center for Legal and Social Justice, where he served as a “Student Attorney” in representing and defending indigent clients accused of committing crimes. The foregoing service also earned Mr. Kell the “Pro Bono Achievement Award” at his graduation ceremony, which was presented to him by the Dean of the law school.

Since earning his law license in November of 2005, Mr. Kell has engaged extensively and exclusively in the representation of individual persons in the Bexar County and contiguous county areas. He takes on each new client with only one goal in mind - “I want to make them so satisfied with my representation that they will always come to me in the future if they ever have any legal problems or questions.”

Although Mr. Kell has represented many clients from all walks of life, he knows the only case that truly matters is yours. He takes the utmost pride in being accessible, responsive, and diligent with his clients and their situations, and he would do the same with you.

attorneys.name: Audrey Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
With more than a decade of experience as a criminal defense attorney and former prosecutor, Audrey offers clients strategic, aggressive, and deeply informed legal representation. A native Texan, Audrey’s legal journey began early—working in a criminal defense office by the age of 18. She earned her law degree from Thomas M. Cooley Law School after completing her undergraduate studies at Southeastern Oklahoma State University in just three years, all while competing as a dual-sport athlete.

Audrey began her legal career as a prosecutor, trying cases ranging from traffic offenses to serious felonies. That courtroom experience gave her a deep understanding of how the system works from the inside out. She later co-founded the Denton-based firm Jarvis & Kelly, where she served as managing partner for over ten years, building a reputation for sharp trial skills and trusted relationships with judges, prosecutors, and court staff.

Now, as a Senior Attorney at Michael & Associates, Audrey leverages that experience to protect the rights and futures of clients facing criminal charges across Texas. Whether handling DWI cases, drug offenses, violent crimes, or white-collar allegations, she brings a fearless, compassionate, and strategic approach to every case.

attorneys.name: L. Todd Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial trucking Lawyers in Georgetown, TX
attorneys.bio:
Todd Kelly is, first, and foremost, a child of God. He is a devoted husband to his wife (and law partner), Robbye, and father of four amazing children, Joshua, Meghan, Matthew, and Selby. He cooks one large batch of crawfish per year and has become adept at smoking a brisket. Because he has tried to do life without Him, Todd will testify that he is an utter failure without his savior, Jesus, and that the rest of the narrative below is possible only by His unending grace… read more about that miracle in Todd’s recent autobiographical book Worth Dying For.

Professionally, Todd is Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and is “AV” rated by Martindale-Hubbell. Todd is licensed in Texas, Oklahoma, Virginia, New Mexico, Colorado and Pennsylvania. He grew up in Arlington, Texas, and received his Bachelor’s Degree from the University of Texas in 1987, while attending on an ROTC Scholarship. He earned his juris doctorate from the Dickinson School of Law in 1995 as a member of the Woolsack Honor Society, while serving as a U.S. Marine, where he returned to practice as a criminal defense attorney in the judge advocate’s corps.

Todd has been featured on 20/20, The Rachel Maddow Show, and has been interviewed on legal topics by numerous national and local news programs, including CBS’ Insider Edition. In 2009, Todd appeared in front of committees of the United States Congress speaking on the Fairness in Arbitration Act, in an effort to eliminate mandatory, binding, pre-dispute arbitration provisions that are found in consumer products and other contracts. Todd was consulted by Senator Al Franken, who sponsored an amendment to the Senate Appropriations bill during that year which led to the abolition of forced arbitration for victims of sexual assault by most military contractors.

In 2013, Todd was inducted into the Texas Lawyer Hall of Fame following a $16,900,000 verdict on behalf of a mentally handicapped woman who was raped by a caregiver at her daycare facility.

Todd has received his 10-year Super Lawyer award as a Texas Super Lawyer, having been named by that publication in 2011, 2012 and every year since 2014.

​Todd left the Marine Corps to enter private practice in 1998, after attaining the rank of Major. He represented asbestos exposure victims and other seriously injured people in Virginia and Pennsylvania before returning to represent victims of birth injury and nursing home abuse in his native Texas in 2002.

In 2006, Todd opened his own law firm in Houston, Texas, where he gained recognition for his representation of sexual assault victims by overseas military contractors.

Todd has dedicated his life to making America safer. He began that service as a Marine Corps combat engineer officer. He now continues that work by protecting those truly injured people who will never get the justice that our system promises to them without holding greedy, powerful corporate entities responsible for the damage they cause. As a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, as a member of the Executive Committee of the Texas Trial Lawyers’ Association, and as a past president of the Capital Area Trial Lawyers’ Association, he remains a staunch defender of our right to trial by a jury of our peers in all cases with a value exceeding $20.00, as guaranteed by the 7th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

Todd urges that if we fail to protect the 7th Amendment to the United States Constitution, we will eventually lose the rights guaranteed by all of the Amendments because it is this right to hold the powerful accountable, protected by the 7th Amendment, that protects the individual freedoms guaranteed by our Constitution.

attorneys.name: Trent Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Austin Attorney Trent Kelly is committed to providing each of his clients with personalized and attentive representation and has devoted his career to championing the rights of Texans. In fact, Trent became a lawyer because of his desire to help people and because of his devout belief in the role of our justice system – particularly jury trials – in safeguarding the rights and liberties of citizens.

Trent’s practice is primarily focused in the areas of personal injury, business and insurance law. Within these areas, he has successfully represented hundreds of clients – both plaintiffs and defendants – in a variety of matters in the state and federal court systems. Trent has also participated in multiple jury trials in which his clients obtained favorable results.

Trent is known in the legal community as an aggressive and tenacious advocate for his clients and has a proven track record of resolving complex legal matters. Trent has represented individuals in lawsuits against some of the largest companies in the world and has also represented corporate clients in a variety of complicated transactions and litigation.

Trent obtained his bachelors degrees in English and philosophy from Hendrix College and his law degree from the University of Arkansas. Trent is licensed to practice law in Texas, Arkansas and Florida.

When he’s not in the office or the courtroom, Trent enjoys playing golf, experimenting with new cuisine and spending time with his wife, Natalie, and son, Jude.

Let Trent put his considerable experience and skills as a personal injury lawyer in Austin, Texas to work for you by contacting him today.

attorneys.name: James Max Kennedy
attorneys.practice_type: Federal and State Criminal Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
I am a fourth generation Texan born in Dallas in 1972. I graduated from St. Thomas' Episcopal School here in Houston and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from the University of St. Thomas. After gaining a couple years of practical experience in a banking management program, I attended Thurgood Marshall School of Law at Texas Southern University. After my first year of law school, I worked as a full-time law clerk at the Fort Bend County District Attorney’s Office assisting in felony trial preparation and appellate brief writing. While I found the experience very educational, I knew that I never wanted to be a prosecutor, marking my convictions on a scorecard. The next year, in my criminal trial advocacy class, taught by none other than former state senator Craig Washington, guest speaker, Kent A. Schaffer, a master of criminal trial litigation, lectured on how to cross exam a government snitch. It was at that moment that I knew that defending citizens accused of crimes was the area of law that I wanted to master. Within a month (7 years ago now), I was offered a position as a full time law clerk for David R. Bires, a brilliant legal mind, working at the criminal law boutique of Schaffer Carter.

I had the honor of clerking for Schaffer Carter throughout my second and third year of law school gaining valuable experience and insight into being a powerful, successful criminal defense lawyer. After becoming licensed to practice law, I was given the privilege of staying with Schaffer Carter as an associate attorney. I have been there ever since. I have spent my law career defending our citizens accused of crimes by the government. I pride myself when I say that I have never prosecuted or sent another fellow man to prison. I feel that ever person accused of a crime deserves zealous representation and I have gladly taken on the challenge of aggressively defending each and every person that I represent. As the famous criminal trial lawyer, Tony Serra, so eloquently stated, “I continue to battle for more freedom for more people through law!”

My practice is dedicated to representation of all areas of federal and state criminal litigation. I am experienced in defending individuals in a vast array of state criminal law prosecutions ranging from driving while intoxicated (DWI), probation violations to capital murder. I am also experienced in representing individuals in all areas of federal criminal law ranging from money laundering and drug conspiracy prosecutions to white collar crimes. My practice includes representing individuals in front of the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) – Parole Division. Additionally, I have extensive experience in representing juveniles charged with engaging in delinquent conduct. I am currently licensed to practice in the following courts:

State Courts in Texas

United States District Court – Southern District

United States District Court – Northern District

Working in one of the most prestigious criminal defense law firms in the Unites States, I am surrounded by the best and brightest minds in the field with over 100 years of combined experience. Due to my diverse, extensive background and experience as well as the ability to associate with my fellow colleagues at Schaffer Carter, I am able to offer a complete, comprehensive service as a criminal defense lawyer. I am based out of Houston, Harris County, but I handle criminal cases both state and federal all over the state and the country. I have personally defended individuals in federal and state courts in Alpine, Lubbock, Laredo, Dallas, Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio, New Braunfels and San Marcos, Texas just to name a few. In any given week, it is not uncommon for me to appear in court in Galveston, Conroe, Richmond and Houston to represent my clients. Out of the state, I have been admitted to practice pro hac vice in California, Florida, Georgia and South Carolina.

I am a member of the State Bar of Texas and I am either currently or formerly a member of the Harris County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, National Association of Criminal defense Lawyers, American Association for Justice, Houston Young Lawyers Association and the American Bar Association.

When I am not in the courtroom or at the office preparing for court, I enjoy spending time at home and away with my best friend and wife, Alexis, and our children.

Houston Criminal Lawyer

attorneys.name: Kristina M. Kennedy
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kris Kennedy is a partner in the Austin, Texas office of Cunningham Swaim LLP, bringing with her a wealth of legal expertise and an unwavering dedication to client advocacy. With a broad legal background spanning aviation law, personal injury, product liability, insurance defense, and business law, Kris is a formidable presence both inside and outside the courtroom. Her broad legal experience enables her to handle complex litigation with confidence and precision, making her an invaluable asset to clients facing high-stakes disputes.

Kris has tried cases throughout the United States in both state and federal courts. She is deeply involved in every stage of litigation, from initial investigation and strategy development through trial and resolution. Her trial experience, combined with her ability to negotiate advantageous settlements, helps her clients achieve positive, business-focused outcomes in even the most challenging cases.

Before joining Cunningham Swaim, Kris served as the Deputy Chief of the Consumer Protection Division and Managing Trial Attorney in the Civil Medicaid Fraud Division of the Texas Attorney General’s office. In those roles, Kris routinely handled complex commercial litigation cases against Fortune 500 companies on behalf of the State of Texas. Prior to her time in public service, Kris was a partner at a trial boutique in Dallas, Texas, where her practice focused on aviation, product liability, and commercial litigation.

Outside of her litigation practice, Kris is committed to mentoring young attorneys and fostering a collaborative, client-focused environment at Cunningham Swaim. Her passion for the law, coupled with her results-driven mindset, continues to enhance the firm’s reputation as a leader in complex litigation.

Mark S. Kennedy is the founder of Kennedy Attorney & Counselors at Law, a health law firm in Dallas, Texas. The firm's practice is focused on health law and health care provider regulatory compliance.

Mark has handled a wide array of cases and has broad-based experience. He formerly was Assistant Regional Counsel to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. He served nine years in the Dallas Region and was the lead litigation attorney for the 5-state region. He represented the Health Care Financing Administration (now Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, "CMS"), the Inspector General, and other Departmental Agencies in the federal trial and appellate courts and various administrative tribunals.

Mark has represented the government in many cases concerning Medicare and Medicaid involving payment and reimbursement disputes, fraud and abuse enforcement, health and safety compliance, and provider bankruptcy. Prior to his work with HHS, Mark was associate counsel for Blue Cross Blue Shield of Oklahoma and Blue Cross Blue Shield of Tennessee.

In private practice, Mark's depth of knowledge in health care regulation has proven to be an invaluable asset in successfully representing clients in a wide array of civil and regulatory matters. His background and experience provide him a unique understanding of government decision-making and procedures.

Mark's broad-based health care regulation background has brought him numerous honors including the HHS General Counsel's Excellence in Legal Services Award (1992). He was selected to serve as a representative to the North Texas Health Care Fraud Working Group and as faculty of the National Health Lawyers Association. Mark is a member of the State Bar of Texas, Oklahoma Bar Association, American Health Lawyers Association, and participates in other State and Local professional associations. He also is a member of the Dallas Bar Association and was elected to its Executive Health Council.

Mark S. Kennedy has been widely recognized for his legal expertise. He was selected to the Super Lawyers list in 2023, 2024, and 2025. In addition to this honor, he was also recognized by Best Lawyers in 2025.

attorneys.name: Nathan Kennedy
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nathan "Nate" Kennedy is a seasoned trial lawyer in The Carlson Law Firm's South Austin location. He works tirelessly to seek justice for injured people seriously hurt or killed by the negligent acts of careless corporations. Nate is a partner with his firm and is licensed to practice in Texas and Colorado.

Experience on Your Side

Nate graduated from the University of Ohio, receiving his Bachelor of Business Administration and Juris Doctor. Shortly after graduation, he entered the U.S. Army, where he proudly served our country.

To date, Nate has litigated 25 jury trials to verdict in state and federal courts.

In the last 10 years alone, Nate has recovered over $50 million in trial verdicts, arbitration awards and settlements for his clients.

When he's not hard at work representing his clients, Nate enjoys barbecue. He's known for giving excellent barbecue restaurant recommendations and once appeared on the Travel Channel's Diva Q.

Combat Veteran

As a U.S. Army combat veteran and Bronze Star recipient, Nate is no stranger to leadership in conflict. In 2009, he tried and won his first jury trial in Baghdad, Iraq as lead prosecutor for the 1st Cavalry Division. Following an engagement with the enemy in Sadr City while assigned to the 82nd Airborne Division, Nate was also awarded the Combat Action Badge.

Recent Results

2022 - $5.6 Million settlement for brain injury caused when a delivery driver struck a pedestrian in a neighborhood.

2022 - $1,150,000 settlement for spine injuries sustained in a collision caused by an 18-wheeler jackknife during a snow storm on Interstate 35.

2022 - $950,000 settlement for spine injuries caused by an 18-wheeler losing control in a construction zone on Interstate 35.

2021 - $3 Million settlement for brain injury arising out of workplace accident.

2020 - $2 Million settlement for neck injury sustained in a collision caused by the driver for a package delivery company.

attorneys.name: Jason Kercheval
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
A product of the Houston suburbs, Jason Kercheval embarked on a distinguished journey that began with his graduation from Klein Forest High School in 1998. Fueled by ambition and dedication, he earned a prestigious full scholarship to the United States Naval Academy, where he completed his studies in 2002 and was commissioned as an ensign in the US Navy.

Jason spent three formative years on active duty as a Surface Warfare Officer, honing his leadership and strategic skills before transitioning to the Naval Reserves. Returning to his roots in Houston, he pursued his passion for justice by enrolling at South Texas College of Law Houston.

During his tenure at South Texas College of Law, Jason’s exceptional advocacy skills set him apart. Selected as one of just twelve students for the elite Advocacy program, he gained national recognition as a traveling Mock Trial Advocate. His dedication and prowess were repeatedly acknowledged with top 10 placements in Mock Trial competitions, culminating in the receipt of the prestigious “John O’Quinn Heart of an Advocate” award.

After law school, Jason reentered the military, this time as a Judge Advocate with the Texas Army National Guard, serving as the Staff Defense Attorney for soldiers facing disciplinary procedures, a position he held until 2015.

While Jason practiced criminal defense, family law, and probate law early in his career, he found his passion in representing parents and others in family law settings, and has focused almost exclusively on Family law for more than a decade.

Jason also is the president of the Veteran’s Treatment Court Support Fund, a 501©(3) non-profit organization focused on supporting justice-involved veterans and their families in the Montgomery County Veteran’s Treatment Court.

Jason’s unique blend of military discipline and legal acumen, aggressiveness and compassion, combine to equip him with a formidable ability to tackle complex legal challenges with integrity and commitment.

Awards and Honors

Honors

John O’ Quinn Heart of an Advocate Award Time, 2011 - Present

attorneys.name: Andrew Kerns
attorneys.firm_name: Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Andrew S. Kerns, Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, is a Partner at Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law. An accomplished litigation and trial attorney, Mr. Kerns has appeared in court hundreds of times across Texas and California and has led over 50 trials as first chair. Since joining the firm in 2020, he has brought substantial courtroom experience and a commitment to achieving favorable outcomes for his clients. Prior to joining Katie L. Lewis, P.C., Mr. Kerns spent seven years as lead trial attorney with the prestigious family law firm Claery & Hammond, LLP, in Los Angeles, representing clients in Divorce, Paternity, Protective Orders, Juvenile Dependency, and Probate matters. His clients have ranged from small business owners and stay-at-home parents to high-profile individuals, including business moguls, celebrities, and musicians.

Mr. Kerns also gained invaluable experience as a federal judicial extern for U.S. Magistrate Judge Jeffrey Manske in the Western District of Texas, Waco Division.

Originally from Southern California, Mr. Kerns graduated with honors from the University of California at Berkeley in 2007, with a Bachelor of Arts in History and Italian Studies. Pursuing his passion for trial advocacy, he relocated to Texas in 2009 to attend Baylor Law School, where he graduated in the top 10% of his class with honors. During law school, Mr. Kerns served as an associate editor of the Baylor Law Review and authored the article, "Fight or Flight: Traversing the Extraterritorial Battlefield of Modern United States Patent Law," published in the Spring 2011 edition of the Baylor Law Review.

After law school, Mr. Kerns practiced in the civil litigation section at Kelly Hart & Hallman, LLP in Fort Worth before moving to Los Angeles in 2012 to join Claery & Hammond, LLP. His dedication and skill have been recognized through his selection as a Super Lawyers Rising Star in Family Law in Southern California in 2020 and in Texas from 2021 to 2024.

Mr. Kerns resides in Dallas, Texas, with his wife, Abbey, who grew up in Keller, Texas, and attended the University of Oklahoma.

attorneys.name: Jamie Kerr
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jamie Kerr graduated from Rice University with a bachelor’s degree in psychology in 2000. He spent nine years in education, working mostly with high school and university students through the process of application for admission to undergraduate, graduate, business, and law schools. In 2009, Jamie returned to school himself and graduated three years later from the University of Texas School of Law with a Juris Doctor.

During his tenure at UT, Jamie focused heavily on clinical education, the study of the dynamics of domestic violence, and criminal law. He spent a year helping victims of domestic violence with their civil cases while in the Domestic Violence Clinic, and represented indigent defendants accused of misdemeanors while working in the Criminal Defense Clinic. Jamie also clerked for the Travis County District Attorney’s office in the Family Justice division, working closely with victims of domestic violence while the felony cases involving their abusers proceeded through the criminal justice system.

Jamie joined the team at Powers Kerr & Rashidi, PLLC in October of 2012, and has since worked on a wide range of cases involving contentious divorces, child custody modifications, complex property division, pre- and post-marital agreements, parental rights terminations, and adoptions. His background in both psychology and education makes him uniquely suited for working with clients through the complicated, sensitive, and emotionally difficult processes often associated with the practice of family law.

Jamie has been Board Certified in Family Law since 2018, and has been recognized as a Texas Super Lawyer every year since 2022. He has served on the Board of the Austin Bar Association Family Law Section since 2025, and is a member of the Texas Academy of Family Law Specialists, Travis County Family Law Advocates, and Austin Bar Association.

Jamie is also an adjunct professor at the University of Texas School of Law, teaching a class called “Mediation for Family Law” to second- and third-year law students.

attorneys.name: Ty’Queese Keyes
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ty’Queese Keyes is a licensed trial attorney at Rob Wiley, P.C., where she focuses her practice on employment law. Ms. Keyes is deeply committed to advocating for employees who have experienced discrimination, harassment, wrongful termination, and wage and hour violations. She approaches each case with strategic insight and unwavering dedication, representing clients in both state and federal courts with a strong focus on results and justice.

Ms. Keyes earned her Juris Doctor, with distinction, from the University of New Mexico School of Law. During law school, she demonstrated a strong commitment to advocacy and leadership, serving as President of the Black Law Students Association during the 2022–2023 academic year. She also participated in the Child and Family Justice Clinic Program, where she provided direct legal services to families and youth. In recognition of her exceptional work and client-centered advocacy, she was awarded the Clinic Honors Award.

Her passion for employment law was sparked during law school while working as a law clerk at a boutique firm that focused on civil rights, employment law, and criminal defense. That experience deepened her understanding of the critical intersection between employment law and civil rights and shaped her desire to address systemic inequities through legal advocacy.

Prior to law school, Ms. Keyes attended Louisiana State University A&M, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communication, with a minor in Psychology. Her interdisciplinary background enhances her ability to understand and navigate complex legal and social dynamics, particularly in cases involving marginalized communities.

Ms. Keyes brings a strong foundation in employment law, family law, civil rights, and social justice to her practice. She is committed to empowering clients, amplifying underrepresented voices, and pursuing meaningful change through the legal system.

She approaches each case with strategic insight and unwavering dedication, representing clients in both state and federal courts with a strong focus on results and justice.

Ms. Keyes earned her Juris Doctor, with distinction, from the University of New Mexico School of Law. During law school, she demonstrated a strong commitment to advocacy and leadership, serving as President of the Black Law Students Association during the 2022–2023 academic year. She also participated in the Child and Family Justice Clinic Program, where she provided direct legal services to families and youth. In recognition of her exceptional work and client-centered advocacy, she was awarded the Clinic Honors Award.

Her passion for employment law was sparked during law school while working as a law clerk at a boutique firm that focused on civil rights, employment law, and criminal defense. That experience deepened her understanding of the critical intersection between employment law and civil rights and shaped her desire to address systemic inequities through legal advocacy.

Prior to law school, Ms. Keyes attended Louisiana State University A&M, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communication, with a minor in Psychology. Her interdisciplinary background enhances her ability to understand and navigate complex legal and social dynamics, particularly in cases involving marginalized communities.

Ms. Keyes brings a strong foundation in employment law, family law, civil rights, and social justice to her practice. She is committed to empowering clients, amplifying underrepresented voices, and pursuing meaningful change through the legal system.

attorneys.name: Tyler Key
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Buda, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tyler Key is a managing attorney at Key Law Office. His primary practice areas are in family law, civil litigation, and small business development and support. Tyler had been designated as a “Super Lawyers- Rising Star”, an award distinguishing Tyler as one of the top young lawyers in the state.

In the family law context, Tyler’s main interests involve property division in divorce cases with family-owned businesses, and high-value or complicated asset holdings or investment structures. These cases often involve separate property claims by one or both parties, prenuptial agreements or trusts that affect the property rights of the parties, or company or partnership agreements that affect the rights of third parties. Tyler enjoys developing an understanding of the business or assets and the goals of his clients, developing creative solutions, negotiating positive outcomes, and vigorously representing his clients at trial.

In child custody cases, he truly holds the best interests of the children as his preeminent concern and enjoys the opportunity to help individuals develop and implement the best parenting plans possible. In addition to representing parents in custody litigation, Tyler is often appointed by the Court to serve as Guardian ad Litem or Amicus Attorney, directly serving those most affected by custody litigation—the children involved.

In civil litigation cases, Tyler serves his clients with energy and enthusiasm during negotiations or litigation. Tyler particularly enjoys helping develop and advise small businesses and offers advice and connections that will help improve the community.

Tyler grew up in Hays County, went to Texas Tech University as an undergraduate, worked for a state agency after college for a few years, and graduated from the University of Houston Law Center in December of 2013. After law school, he worked for a major insurer in their Special Liability Group where he helped manage litigation for mass tort cases throughout the South including asbestos, toxic waste, and multi-plaintiff defective product cases. He then developed great trial skills at a plaintiff’s firm working under a very successful trial attorney. In late 2014 he returned to Hays County and has since focused on developing a family law practice.

In addition to being passionate about his role as a lawyer, Tyler loves being a father, an outdoorsman with a major emphasis on fly fishing and bird hunting, and a soccer coach.

attorneys.name: Anushay Khalid
attorneys.firm_name: Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Anushay Khalid is a compassionate and accomplished family law attorney recognized for her strategic advocacy and unwavering dedication to her clients. She combines meticulous legal expertise with a genuine understanding of the emotional complexities families face during legal disputes. Anushay specializes in handling high-net-worth cases, child custody matters, and support disputes, tailoring her approach to deliver personalized solutions that meet each client’s unique needs.

Anushay earned her Bachelor of Laws with distinction from the University of London and further honed her legal skills by completing a Master of Laws in Comparative and International Law at Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law in Dallas, Texas. During her time at SMU, she gained invaluable experience through the prestigious W.W. Caruth, Jr. Child Advocacy Clinic, where she represented at-risk minors as an Attorney Ad Litem and worked on cases involving child neglect and family reunification.

Her legal journey began as a legal secretary and law clerk, roles that laid a strong foundation for her current position as an associate attorney at Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law Firm. Based in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, Anushay manages a diverse caseload, excelling in crafting creative and practical solutions for complex property and financial matters. Her commitment to achieving favorable outcomes is matched by her ability to foster cooperative resolutions whenever possible.

Fluent in English, Urdu, and Hindi, Anushay connects seamlessly with clients from diverse backgrounds, ensuring they feel heard and supported during difficult times. Beyond her legal practice, she actively contributes to the community through her volunteer work with Legal Aid of Northwest Texas.

Outside the office, Anushay pursues her passions for photography, traveling, and event planning. Residing in Frisco, she approaches her work with professionalism, empathy, and a dedication to guiding clients through life’s most challenging moments with clarity and confidence.

attorneys.name: Monica Khirallah
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Monica R. Khirallah is a seasoned criminal defense trial lawyer based in San Antonio, Texas, with a practice that extends throughout the surrounding counties. Known for her tenacity, courtroom experience, and unwavering dedication to justice, Monica has built a reputation as a formidable advocate for her clients. Fluent in Spanish, Monica is committed to serving a diverse client base and ensuring every voice is heard in the courtroom.

Monica began her legal career in the Denton County District Attorney’s Office, where she quickly rose through the ranks to become a misdemeanor chief prosecutor. This foundational experience on the prosecution side gave her a unique and invaluable perspective when she transitioned to criminal defense—a field that runs deep in her family legacy.

Over the course of more than a decade in practice, Monica has tried nearly 100 jury trials, a rare accomplishment that underscores her confidence and capability in the courtroom. Her skill and professionalism have earned her repeated recognition: she has been named to the Super Lawyers Rising Stars list every year from 2020 through 2025, an honor reserved for the top-rated attorneys selected through a rigorous evaluation process.

Monica is a proud alumna of the University of Dallas, where she completed her undergraduate studies, and she earned her Juris Doctor from Ave Maria School of Law in Naples, Florida, graduating in 2011. That same year, she was admitted to practice law in the State of Texas.

Outside the courtroom, Monica lives in her hometown of Boerne with her husband, David Khirallah, a partner and trial attorney at Thompson, Coe, Cousins & Irons. They were blessed with four boys, Davey, Daniel(+), Gabriel, and Charlie, who share their parents' passion for legal justice. Whether coaching CYO sports at St. Elizabeth Ann Seton or enjoying time on the family ranch, Monica brings the same passion and dedication to her family life that she brings to defending her clients.

attorneys.name: A. Scott Kidd
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Spring, TX
attorneys.bio:
Scott Kidd represents both individuals and businesses in all types of litigation matters including auto/trucking accidents, workplace accidents, oilfield litigation, defective products, premises liability, and construction. He also provides representation in insurance, business, and real estate related matters. Scott takes a personal interest in every client represented and tailors that representation to their particular needs and desired result.

Scott has been a trial lawyer for over 35 years representing clients in a wide variety of cases. Scott has been Board Certified in Personal Injury Law since 2003.

Throughout his career, Scott has also been an advocate for children serving as a guardian ad litem for minors and as corporate counsel for one of the state’s largest Christian foster care/adoption agencies where he received the Servant’s Heart Award in 2008. He was elected in 2012 to the Board of Trustees for the Conroe Independent School District and served until 2020. Scott has also served on numerous boards, including both the Post Oak YMCA and South Montgomery County YMCA, Montgomery County Community Foundation, and Montgomery County Child Advocates Advisory Board. Scott and his wife Shannon taught youth bible study at The Woodlands First for 10 years where they raised their two now adult children. Scott grew up in Conroe and has lived in Montgomery County most of his life.

Scott has an AV rating with Martindale Hubbell, which is the highest rating level based on legal ability and ethical standards. Martindale-Hubbell Peer Review ratings are established by lawyers. Scott has been licensed to practice law in the State of Texas since 1989 and is also licensed to practice in federal court in the Southern, Eastern, Northern and Western Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Richard C. Killough
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation and Trial Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rick is a founding partner of Murrah & Killough and the firm’s lead trial and litigation lawyer. Over the past twenty-five years, he has represented both plaintiffs and defendants in hundreds of lawsuits in federal and state courts as well as in arbitrations, appeals, regulatory enforcement proceedings, and investigations. He has served as lead counsel, including as ‘first chair’ jury and bench trial counsel, in multimillion-dollar lawsuits. Rick has represented clients in a range of cases, from complex, multi-district litigation involving Fortune 500 companies, to cross-border litigation, to cases involving injured individuals, businesses, estates, and other organizations.

Rick’s practice area concentration is intentionally diverse. He has handled lawsuits and cases involving numerous fields of civil litigation critical to the well-being of his clients. These fields include commercial, business, fiduciary, real estate, personal injury and tort, landlord-tenant, employment, probate, antitrust, trade secret, and other types of litigation.

In his first position after graduating from law school, Rick served as Assistant Independent Counsel in the Whitewater and Lewinsky Investigations under Independent Counsel Kenneth W. Starr.

From 2009 to 2013, Rick served as General Counsel of the Velocity Group, a sophisticated financial services firm composed of a CFTC-regulated futures commission merchant, energy trading hedge fund, software development company, and an algorithmic trading company.

Rick and his wife Katie have three sons. When not enjoying time with his family, Rick enjoys history, reading, music, working in the yard, and fiction writing. He is a life-long member of the Episcopal church.

attorneys.name: Christopher L. King
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Christopher King graduated Magna Cum Laude from Abilene Christian University in 2010, married his college sweetheart Samantha, then moved to Waco, Texas to study the law. Chris earned his Juris Doctorate from Baylor University School of Law in 2013.

While at Baylor Law, Mr. King spent time at the McLennan County District Attorney’s Office, the Williamson County Prosecutor’s Office, Abilene Christian University Legal Office, Lone Star Legal Aid, and clerking for a Baylor Law Professor and a Federal Magistrate Judge in Houston, Texas. This multifaceted experience underlies Mr. King’s varied talents in the law. Throughout law school, Mr. King worked and interned for the Law Office of Robert G. Callahan, II. Their work together prepared them to forge their partnership immediately upon Chris’s licensure in 2013.

Their goal is to provide affordable legal counsel for those accused of crimes, facing family legal issues, or injured in an accident. Chris is dedicated to serving his clients, including going the extra mile to ensure his client’s needs are met.

When Chris is not practicing law, he spends time with his wife Samantha, their three daughters and dog, and their next-door neighbors - who also happen to be his parents. He has served on the Board of Directors for the Cen-Tex African American Chamber of Commerce since 2014, currently as the Chairman of the Board. He attends church regularly at Highland Baptist Church and loves serving in the world’s most dangerous mission field - the 6th grade classroom.

attorneys.name: Coleen Kinsler
attorneys.firm_name: Bryant, Colletti, Kaplan, Kinsler, & De La Reza, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Coleen knew in her third year of law school that she wanted to be a family law attorney and help families. She has been a family law attorney ever since. She is Board Certified in Family Law since 2020.

Coleen understands that this is personal and has a long-term impact on families. Coleen’s primary goal is to assist her clients in resolving difficult family matters and to help them move forward with their lives in a dignified and respectful manner. Coleen recognizes that not every situation requires a courtroom, and instead assists her clients through negotiation and mediation when possible. If negotiation fails, Coleen is a zealous advocate and tenacious family law litigator.

Coleen grew up in the Hudson Valley area of New York and is still a devout Yankees fan. She moved to the Austin area in middle school and received her undergraduate degree from Texas A&M University. Coleen attended law school in Chicago, Illinois, and is licensed in Illinois, but she got back to Texas as quickly as possible. She has practiced family law in Chicago, Harris County and surrounding counties, and most counties in central Texas.

When Coleen is not in the office, she tries to keep up with the lawyer stereotype and can be found on the golf course. She also loves to cook, travel and spend time with her family.

attorneys.name: Cheree Tull Kinzie
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Banks Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Cheree Tull Kinzie is a shareholder and President of the Firm. She is also Chair of the Firm's Shareholders Compensation Committee and Chairman of the Firm's Pension Committee. Ms. Kinzie is Board Certified in both Commercial Real Estate Law and Residential Real Estate Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. She is a member of the San Antonio Bar Association; a member of the Section on Real Estate, Probate and Trust Law of the State Bar of Texas; and the San Antonio Real Estate Lawyers Discussion Group. From 1989 - 1996, she chaired the Attorneys' Conference committee for the Texas Savings and Loan League and has been a guest lecturer on real estate and banking topics. Ms. Kinzie is a member of the Firm's Business and Public Law Sections.

Ms. Kinzie has extensive experience in negotiating major contracts with governmental entities. She worked extensively with the U.S. Air Force and Greater Kelly Development Authority to negotiate the sale and transfer of the 1,880 acres of the former Kelly AFB to be conveyed by the government to the community. In that representation, Ms. Kinzie negotiated the Economic Development Conveyance (EDC) and the Lease in Furtherance of Conveyance (LIFC) with the Washington, D.C. staff of the Air Force Base Conversion Agency (AFBCA). She negotiated with AFBCA for the transfer of Air Force water and power utilities to municipal-owned utility companies. Ms. Kinzie has negotiated leases with major aerospace industry tenants, and arranged financing for tenant finish-out and the construction of new improvements at KellyUSA, including a 70,000 sq. ft. Administration Building and a new aircraft hangar for use by The Boeing Company.

Ms. Kinzie also represented the City of San Antonio and later the Brooks Development Authority in connection with the Brooks City-Base Project. The first ever, one-of-a-kind transaction involved federal legislation to allow the transfer of Air Force-owned property to Brooks Development Authority with a long-term lease back to the Air Force. Ms. Kinzie created all of the contracts and conveyance documents to support this historic effort.

Ms. Kinzie also represents major commercial banks in acquisition and construction lending. She has an active practice in the area of commercial real estate sales, leasing and related transactions.

attorneys.name: Nathanial D. Kitz
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Flower Mound, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nathanial D. Kitz is an accomplished and highly versatile attorney with over a decade of experience delivering valuable, compassionate, and client-focused legal representation. Since joining our firm in April 2025, he has quickly become a meaningful addition to our collaborative culture and rapidly expanding legal team. With a strong background in finance, he welcomes every opportunity to leverage those skills to bring clients peace of mind through practical, empathetic advocacy in civil law, family law, probate, guardianship, and estate planning.

Hailing from a small town in Northeastern Wisconsin—roughly 30 minutes south of Green Bay—Nathanial became interested in the law after watching his mother obtain her paralegal degree. He earned his undergraduate degree in finance from the University of Wisconsin—Milwaukee in 2008 and his Juris Doctorate in 2010 from Drake University. He is licensed to practice law in Texas, Louisiana, and Tennessee. Before joining our firm, Nathanial was a regional managing attorney for Rausch Sturm LLP, a nationally recognized account receivables management law firm representing blue chip banks, credit card issuers, auto lenders, credit unions, and debt buyers across the United States.

His wealth of expertise includes standout roles at several other law firms and a notable role as assistant attorney general at the Texas Attorney General’s office from 2018 to 2019.

Away from the legal world, Nathanial and his wife were married in 2023 and welcomed their first daughter in early 2025. In his free time, he loves to feed his deep love for travel and long road trips—whether it’s a day trip, a weekend, or a cross-country adventure. He boasts that on one trip, he was standing in the Atlantic Ocean on a Sunday morning and was in the Pacific Ocean by Friday afternoon. During that same trip, he stopped at seven state capitols and four national parks. One of his bucket list items is to visit all 63 national parks due to his love for unique landscapes, nature, and historical places.

attorneys.name: Robin Klein
attorneys.firm_name: Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Robin W. Klein is Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, an accomplishment that only 1% of the family lawyers in Texas have achieved. She has been practicing family law, exclusively, for over 13 years, and is also trained in mediation.

As a single mom of two grown children, Robin understands the challenges that clients endure when faced with heart wrenching issues regarding children, divorce and financial struggles. Robin’s passion for helping people and insight, works to guide her clients through the legal process by assisting them make decisions that will benefit them and their families now and in the future. Robin is dedicated to helping her clients get through the legal process so they can begin the next chapter of their life. She listens and will give her cases and clients the attention they need. Robin has the experience and knowledge to look at each case individually and can often find creative solutions to conflicts regarding custody, possession and access, child support and property division.

Robin understands that some cases need to go to trial, however that is not always the best scenario when dealing with sensitive, personal issues in family law cases. Robin is very successful in negotiating a final resolution that benefits her clients and their family. She will help you do a risk assessment when developing your goals towards a temporary and/or final resolution.

attorneys.name: Hailey Klingbeil
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hailey Klingbeil is an Associate at Varghese Summersett in the Family Law Group, where she is passionate about helping individuals and families navigate times of change and crisis. She has a deep understanding of the emotional and legal challenges that come with divorce, child custody disputes, property division, and other family matters.

Hailey is committed to providing personalized attention to each client so she can understand their unique situation and tailor a strategy to achieve the best outcome. In some cases, that may mean an aggressive courtroom battle, while in others it might be finding an amicable resolution that avoids the need for contentious and costly litigation.

In addition to being a fierce advocate for her clients, Hailey is also a devoted daughter, sister, and aunt with strong Texas roots. She and her three sisters grew up on a 40-acre farm just outside of Wylie, a quaint suburb of Dallas. After graduating from Wylie East High School, she followed in her family’s footsteps and attended Texas A&M University, becoming a third-generation Aggie (along with her sisters).

Afterward, Hailey returned to North Texas to attend Texas A&M School of Law in downtown Fort Worth. While in law school, she received an externship at a family law firm, which sparked her passion for this field. During this time, her sister also adopted a 6-month-old baby girl in Tarrant County – an experience that solidified her passion for family law.

Hailey is dedicated to immeasurably improving clients’ lives. She is excited to be part of a team that puts its heart and soul into every case it takes on. When she isn’t in the office, Hailey enjoys helping friends and family with interior design projects.

Fun Fact: Hailey grew up on a small miniature horse farm.

attorneys.name: Nelson Knight
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Justice Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nelson has over 25 years of experience in the criminal justice system in Texas. A Dallas native, Nelson started his legal career as a prosecutor in the Dallas County District Attorney’s office where he tried cases ranging from DWI to Capital Murder, with the majority of his time being spent handling high-level felony offenses in District Courts.

Since 2001, Nelson has focused on criminal defense and protecting the rights of citizens accused of crimes. In both his long-time private practice and as a Dallas County Public Defender from 2007 to 2010, Nelson has fought the state at every turn to ensure that people accused of crimes in North Texas and throughout the state receive the best representation they can get.

As a solo practitioner for almost 20 years, Nelson handled cases across the state ranging from DWI to Capital Murder. He has countless jury and bench trials under his belt and has dealt with just about every type of hearing that could come up during a criminal proceeding.

Communication and listening are two of the most important aspects of criminal defense, and Nelson prioritizes both of them. He looks forward to serving his clients here at Michael & Associates.

attorneys.name: Rob Knight
attorneys.practice_type: Oil & Gas Title Opinions Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rob Knight started his legal career by opening a law firm in Houston, Texas, where he practiced in the areas of family, criminal, real estate and probate law. He relocated to Tyler, Texas, to focus his work on oil and gas title opinions. At Flowers Davis, he practices in the areas of oil and gas title opinions and real estate law. Rob typically works for large multi-national oil and gas companies, as well as mid sized and small local oil and gas companies. He also represents banks, municipalities and title companies.

Rob has prepared title opinions in multiple states, from simple title opinions to complex division order, unit-wide opinions and leasehold opinions. He also prepares title opinions in anticipation of both residential and commercial loans, and for condemnation proceedings. He has worked in several areas of law that currently overlap real property law, including probate and family law, and has a thorough understanding of all instruments within a chain of title.

Rob enjoys working in real property law and reviewing land title. Whether he is preparing title opinions or aiding the issuance of loans and title policies, he understands the importance of providing his services in a quick and efficient manner, and in delivering a quality product.

Outside of work Rob enjoys playing guitar, painting, mountain biking, yoga, preparing for and competing in obstacle course races.

attorneys.bio:
Kaytlyn was born and raised in Houston, Texas. She completed her undergraduate education at Texas Christian University, graduating Magna Cum Laude. Kaytlyn returned to Houston to pursue her passion for trial advocacy at South Texas College of Law. There, she competed in a mock trial, finishing as champion of the Garland Walker Mock Trial Competition. She also competed nationally for the school’s alternative dispute resolution team.

Upon graduating and passing the bar exam, Kaytlyn knew she belonged in the courtroom. An internship turned into a 12-year career as a prosecutor. attorneys.name: Kathryn Knotts
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Bryan, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn was 9 years old when she acted in her school production of "Santa Claus on Trial". It was at this point that she knew she wanted to be an attorney. That ambition stayed with her throughout her academic career, she began noticing inequality in her community. Kathryn applied to the Baylor University of School Law with dreams of becoming an attorney who could help injured persons. She knew that she wanted to fight for clients to ensure they were treated fairly and not taken advantage by a system and industry that did not have their best interest at heart.

Experience on your side

Kathryn L. Knotts is a Bryan-based personal injury attorney dedicated to improving the lives of her clients. After she graduated from law school, Kathryn immediately set to work helping those in her community. She started at The Carlson Law Firm the Monday after she passed the Texas State Bar in February 2005. She has spent her career successfully representing clients in car collisions, premises liability and personal injury cases.

Clients who walk into Kathryn's office know immediately that she will fight tirelessly on their behalf. Because she cares so deeply about her clients, she strives to obtain the absolute best recovery for them and help them put the pieces back together after suffering an injury. Additionally, clients appreciate her creativity and thorough investigations to identify what could have prevented client injuries. In premises liability cases, she works to ensure that companies make the necessary corrections to prevent injuries from happening to others.

Kathryn is a graduate of Baylor University School of Law and earned her B.A. at the University of Mary-Hardin Baylor. She is licensed to practice in all Texas courts and the US Southern District.

She belongs to several professional associations including the American Business Women's Association (ABWA), State Bar of Texas, Texas Young Lawyer Association, Texas Trial Lawyer Association, Brazos County Bar Association, and the Leadership Brazos Alumni Association.

Kathryn has won several awards and recognition for her outstanding legal work. Her awards include the 2014 American Business Women's Association Houston Area Council Shining Star, 2018 Leading Woman Express Top Ten Candidate, 2018 American Business Women's Association Top Ten and the 2018 American Businesswoman of the Year. She speaks at ABWA Leagues across the country and enjoys inspiring and motivating other businesswomen. Kathryn also serves as a Director for the American Business Women's Foundation, which seeks to enlighten, empower, and equip women to achieve parity with an emphasis on opportunity and pay equity in the workplace.

Kathryn was also named a Super Lawyers "Rising Star" in 2019 and 2020.

When she isn't in the office, Kathryn is the proud mother of a little boy. Naturally, her hobbies involve playing with hot wheels, trucks, superheroes, and reading children's books. She can recite "Pete the Cat and the Missing Cupcakes" by memory. In addition, in July 2021, Kathryn was sworn in as a member of the North Zulch ISD School Board.

Although she rarely cooks or bakes, she has an extensive collection of cookbooks. She uses her free time with her health and wellness business where she enjoys helping others become healthy from the inside out. She is an active member of Normangee United Methodist Church and serves on the board of trustees.

attorneys.name: Scott K. Koelker
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Experienced in litigation and trial, Scott is ready to zealously protect or prosecute the interests of his clients. The first decade of his career was with an international Am Law 100 firm - so called, "Biglaw" - until joining one of Texas' largest personal injury law firms. Having literally represented both Fortune 500 companies as well as individuals with a total fortune of $500, Scott's diverse practice now helps reinforce the Burke Bogdanowicz PLLC difference - experienced, innovative, and adaptable litigation attorneys.

Scott has practiced in nearly every type of forum, including federal and state trial courts, courts of appeal, before regulatory authorities, and before arbitration tribunals. And Scott's broad-based experience in these forums includes all aspects of the dispute: presuit case analysis; obtaining and opposing preliminary remedies, restraining orders, and injunctions; written discovery and depositions; motion practice and oral advocacy; bench and jury trials; post-trial motions and judgment collection or enforcement; and appellate briefing and oral argument.

On a personal level, Scott is married to his high school sweetheart of 20+ years. They have four children plus a small petting zoo of animals and livestock. Within the community, they are active with local parent-teacher organizations and the district's education foundation; and Scott is the President and Director of a regional 501(c)(3) charity that assists the families of injured first responders and military/veterans.
