attorneys.name: Martin (Marty) J. Lehman
attorneys.practice_type: Lending Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
We all started somewhere, and Marty started on an Iowa farm. While working with his parents and his 8 siblings raising corn, soybeans, hay, hogs and cattle (and while playing high school and college basketball), Marty had instilled in him a strong work ethic, perseverance, ambition and integrity.

In 1982, after graduation from law school at the University Iowa, Marty moved to Dallas with all his worldly possessions (which fit easily into his ‘74 Volkswagen bug), with no job, but with plenty of drive and ambition. After knocking on many, many doors (this was before the internet), Marty got his start at Hunter, Vineyard, Drake & Miller (which years later evolved into Miller & Lehman). Marty is grateful to his early legal mentors (the late Bill Hunter, Tim Vineyard, David Miller, Barbara Staubus Miller, and Harry Martin), and credits them with helping him develop into the lawyer he is today.

Since 2006, Marty has been with his present firm, Palmer Lehman Sandberg (formerly Palmer & Manuel).

Legal problems come in all shapes and sizes, and often overlap into multiple areas of law. Marty has been helping clients address those problems since 1982, and as a result has a very wide breadth of experience.

Throughout his career, Marty has guided individuals and companies in all areas of their business, from formation and expansion, to transactions, and to litigation and other forms of resolving disputes.

Since early in his career, Marty has represented individuals, businesses and lenders in connection with lending, finance, real estate, commercial litigation and all aspects of commercial transactions, including corporate debt restructuring. He has extensive experience in out-of-court workouts and non-judicial foreclosures of liens on real and personal property.

If out-of-court resolutions are not attainable, Marty serves as lead counsel in commercial litigation in state, federal and bankruptcy courts, including appeals, as well as in arbitrations.

Marty has also developed a unique niche - he uses his experience from lending, real estate, business transactions, and litigation, to assist family law attorneys in structuring and documenting property divisions in divorce proceedings, and to enforce property divisions and payment obligations post-divorce.

Recognition

Marty is "AV" rated. Martindale-Hubbell, the largest and most comprehensive source of lawyer ratings in the world, has been providing peer review ratings of lawyers for more than 130 years. Martindale-Hubbell awarded Marty its prestigious "AV" rating. The "A" portion indicates the highest possible rating for legal ability, while the "V" portion indicates adherence to the highest standard of professional conduct.

Here are some of Marty's representative clients

CIT Bank/ CIT Finance

Commercial Credit Group

Continental Bank

General Sports Surfaces/ Texas Sports Builders/ Texas General Sports

Lee Financial Company

Lucky 21 Group of Companies

Power Up for the Cause

Rojo Energy Holdings

States Resources Corp.

Summit Investment Management

Here is a sample of Marty's relevant experience

Represented an entrepreneur in building a chain of automotive service centers, beginning with the acquisition of a handful of business locations, to generating over $60 million in annual revenue from more than 100 locations in multiple states within 5 years. Marty assisted in all areas of the business, from formation of various entities, the purchasing and leasing of real estate, and the acquisition of assets from other chains, to employment issues.

Represented the owner in the sale of an industrial manufacturing and fabrication business.

Represented the sellers in a multi-million dollar sale of a hospital and various clinics.

Represented a buyer in negotiations for the purchase of office towers.

Restructured multi-million dollar business holdings through various corporations, trusts, partnerships and annuities, to allow for the orderly transfer of assets to succeeding generations without any disruption of the businesses, resulting in estate and gift tax savings of several million dollars.

Obtained a substantial judgment against a borrower and the guarantor for a deficiency following foreclosure on a commercial building, successfully enforcing a waiver of the "anti-deficiency" laws, and defeating the borrower's and the guarantor's claims for alleged violations of the foreclosure laws, breach of contract, breach of the common law tort of unreasonable collection efforts, unjust enrichment, negligence, negligent representation, and common law fraud.

Discovered that, while he was suing to collect a debt, the debtor had taken steps to hinder the collection. During the lawsuit, the debtor converted one of his companies from a corporation into a limited liability company, agreed to poison pills terms requiring him to sell his interests in several companies to his co-owners at a steep discount if Marty's client obtained a judgment and charging order or lien, and transferred half of his companies' ownership to his wife. Marty then obtained a judgment setting aside as fraudulent the conversion, the poison pills terms, and the transfers to the debtor's wife, and awarding Marty's client attorneys' fees from the debtor, and from the debtor's business partner, companies, and wife.

Successfully defended a publicly-traded pharmacy from an $11 million fraudulent transfer claim brought by a bankruptcy trustee. After a 5-day trial, the Bankruptcy Judge ordered that the trustee recover nothing from Marty's client.

Assisted non-bankruptcy counsel in defending a bank from a $29 million claim filed by reorganized chapter 11 bankruptcy debtors. After their bankruptcy cases were completed, the reorganized bankruptcy debtors filed suit against the bank, asserting that the former principals of the debtor companies squandered company funds through an alleged Ponzi scheme, and that the bank should be liable for not discovering and stopping the alleged scheme. Marty used bankruptcy law principles to forge a nuisance value settlement.

Represented a REIT (Real Estate Investment Trust) in actions against a flood control district alleging the district's operations, use of funds and tax scheme violated various provisions of the U.S. and Texas Constitutions, as well as other state and federal laws. Marty's actions resulted in the restructuring of the flood control district's bonds, and a cap on the tax rate the district can charge the property owners (including Marty's client) within the district.

Represented a lender in the financing of a marina leased from the U.S. Corp of Engineers.

Defended to successful conclusion a class action suit alleging that Marty's lender client's foreclosure practices violated the Federal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the Texas foreclosure laws.

Prosecuted his equipment manufacturer/vendor client's claims in a Chapter 11 business bankruptcy reorganization in an Alabama bankruptcy court, resulting in the return to Marty's client of $1 million worth of oil and gas field equipment.

Successfully defended in a state court and the bankruptcy court, an injunction sought to prevent Marty's lender client from foreclosing its lien based upon the lender's purported violation of the borrower's confirmed Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization plan.

In U.S. District Court in New Mexico, obtained a summary judgment in favor of his lender client in defense of alleged violations of various consumer protection laws, including the Federal Truth in Lending Act, RESPA/the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act, the Deceptive Trade Practices Act, and fraud.

Enforcement of mechanic's and materialmen's lien claims against commercial properties and payment bonds.

Represented commercial property owners against tenants for breaches of leases.

Defended actions for alleged violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act arising from a developer's attempted post-sale re-plat of real property.

Successfully defended several stock brokerage firms and numerous individual stockbrokers against "raid" actions (alleging among other things, violations of covenants not to compete and improper use of confidential information) filed by other brokerage firms in both state and federal courts. In one particular action, Marty defeated a request for a temporary restraining order in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, even though prior to that time temporary restraining orders in similar actions had uniformly been granted in U.S. District Courts throughout Texas and across most of the United States.

Defended an action for receivership and partition of commercial real estate brought by the previously undisclosed heir of a deceased predecessor in title.

Obtained a $900,000 judgment for a client against ex-spouse for failure to comply with the terms of their divorce property settlement.

Here is a sample of opinions/court rulings from Marty's representations

In Re Pan American General Hospital, LLC, Debtor, 385 B.R. 855; 2008 Bankr. LEXIS 1295 (Bankr. W.D. Tex. 2008). In the Pan American General Hospital Chapter 11 bankruptcy case, Marty obtained for his client U.S. Bank over $1,000,000 from Pan American's sale of assets. In addition, despite Pan American's objection, Marty recovered from Pan American another $109,000 to reimburse his client for the attorneys' fees it incurred, which Bankruptcy Judge Leif M. Clark found to be reasonable. Further, Judge Clark wrote that Marty's firm's invoices:

"reflect that Palmer & Manuel did this work without overstaffing the case and without the excessive billing that one would expect to be present were this case problematic... After the first month of this case, Palmer & Manuel billed 35.1 hours in September, 42.0 hours in October, 26.75 hours in November, and 56.95 hours in December (the month of the auction and sale closing). With the fight U.S. Bank had on its hands, a bigger firm may have billed these hours in a single week."

Alpha Invesco Corp. v. IRM Invs., 2000 Tex. App. LEXIS 3128 (Tex. App. - Dallas 2000). Marty represented an owner of commercial real property in a lawsuit against a successor-in-interest to the FDIC (as receiver for the failed Willowbend National Bank) who was seeking to foreclose on his client's property. At trial, Marty obtained a judgment that the FDIC successor-in-interest did not have a valid lien against his client's property. This judgment was affirmed by the Texas Court of Appeals, resulting in Marty's client owning the real property free and clear.

Gill Savings Assoc. v. International Supply Co., 759 S.W.2d 697 (Tex. App. - Dallas 1988). Marty represented a pipe and fixture supplier to an apartment complex builder. At trial, Marty obtained a judgment that his client's materialman's lien was superior to the interest of a lender who had acquired the apartment complex by foreclosure, and directing a judicial foreclosure of the materialman's lien. When the lender appealed, the judgment Marty had obtained for his client was affirmed. Further, "in a case of first impression, [the Court of Appeals] set out a rule for proving legal assistant's fees so that they are recoverable under a statute authorizing the award of attorney's fees." The result was Marty's client being paid for the materials it supplied, and reimbursed for the attorneys' fees it incurred.

Highway 82/Fannin J.V. v. Capital One Bank, N.A. (In re Highway 82/Fannin J.V.), 2012 Bankr. LEXIS 4225, (Bankr. E.D. Tex. 2012); Affirmed by U.S. District E.D. TX, Case No. 4:12-cv-707, Doc. 9; Affirmed by U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, 2014 U.S. App. LEXIS 17415 (5th Cir. Tex.). When Marty's bank client sought to foreclose its lien on real property, the borrower filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy and sued the bank challenging the enforceability of the cross-collateralization provision in the bank's deed of trust. On Marty's motion, Bankruptcy Judge Brenda T. Rhoades dismissed the suit against the bank. When the borrower appealed, the dismissal in favor of Marty's client was upheld by both the U.S. District Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals. This preserved the lien of Marty's client on valuable real property, leading to Marty's client being paid.

G.H. Bass & Co. v. Dalsan Properties-Abilene, 885 S.W.2d 572 (Tex. App. - Dallas 1994, no writ). After the tenant filed for bankruptcy protection, Marty filed a lawsuit for his landlord client against the surety/guarantor on the commercial lease for unpaid holdover rent and other charges. Marty obtained a judgment against the surety/guarantor in the trial court. When the surety/guarantor appealed, the Court of Appeals held that the surety/guarantor can be held liable for the holdover rent and other charges, but remanded the case to the trial court to consider whether the surety/guarantor could prove a waiver defense.

Family and interests

Marty and his wife Laurie have been married over 25 years. Laurie (formerly a practicing attorney) has dedicated her time to homeschooling their five children. Marty (a former college basketball player) served as the basketball commissioner of Dallas HSAA - Home School Athletic Association (one of the largest home school sports organizations in the United States), and has coached youth basketball and soccer, including coaching his son's team which in 2014 won the U16 D-II Texas State Homeschool Basketball Championship and the U16 D-II National Homeschool Basketball Championship.

Awards and Honors

Honors

“AV” rating from Martindale-Hubbell

Defended actions for alleged violations of the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices Act arising from a developer's attempted post-sale re-plat of real property.

Successfully defended several stock brokerage firms and numerous individual stockbrokers against "raid" actions (alleging among other things, violations of covenants not to compete and improper use of confidential information) filed by other brokerage firms in both state and federal courts. In one particular action, Marty defeated a request for a temporary restraining order in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas, even though prior to that time temporary restraining orders in similar actions had uniformly been granted in U.S. District Courts throughout Texas and across most of the United States.

Defended an action for receivership and partition of commercial real estate brought by the previously undisclosed heir of a deceased predecessor in title.

Obtained a $900,000 judgment for a client against ex-spouse for failure to comply with the terms of their divorce property settlement.

Here is a sample of opinions/court rulings from Marty's representations

In Re Pan American General Hospital, LLC, Debtor, 385 B.R. 855; 2008 Bankr. LEXIS 1295 (Bankr. W.D. Tex. 2008). In the Pan American General Hospital Chapter 11 bankruptcy case, Marty obtained for his client U.S. Bank over $1,000,000 from Pan American's sale of assets. In addition, despite Pan American's objection, Marty recovered from Pan American another $109,000 to reimburse his client for the attorneys' fees it incurred, which Bankruptcy Judge Leif M. Clark found to be reasonable. Further, Judge Clark wrote that Marty's firm's invoices:

"reflect that Palmer & Manuel did this work without overstaffing the case and without the excessive billing that one would expect to be present were this case problematic... After the first month of this case, Palmer & Manuel billed 35.1 hours in September, 42.0 hours in October, 26.75 hours in November, and 56.95 hours in December (the month of the auction and sale closing). With the fight U.S. Bank had on its hands, a bigger firm may have billed these hours in a single week."

Alpha Invesco Corp. v. IRM Invs., 2000 Tex. App. LEXIS 3128 (Tex. App. - Dallas 2000). Marty represented an owner of commercial real property in a lawsuit against a successor-in-interest to the FDIC (as receiver for the failed Willowbend National Bank) who was seeking to foreclose on his client's property. At trial, Marty obtained a judgment that the FDIC successor-in-interest did not have a valid lien against his client's property. This judgment was affirmed by the Texas Court of Appeals, resulting in Marty's client owning the real property free and clear.

Gill Savings Assoc. v. International Supply Co., 759 S.W.2d 697 (Tex. App. - Dallas 1988). Marty represented a pipe and fixture supplier to an apartment complex builder. At trial, Marty obtained a judgment that his client's materialman's lien was superior to the interest of a lender who had acquired the apartment complex by foreclosure, and directing a judicial foreclosure of the materialman's lien. When the lender appealed, the judgment Marty had obtained for his client was affirmed. Further, "in a case of first impression, [the Court of Appeals] set out a rule for proving legal assistant's fees so that they are recoverable under a statute authorizing the award of attorney's fees." The result was Marty's client being paid for the materials it supplied, and reimbursed for the attorneys' fees it incurred.

Highway 82/Fannin J.V. v. Capital One Bank, N.A. (In re Highway 82/Fannin J.V.), 2012 Bankr. LEXIS 4225, (Bankr. E.D. Tex. 2012); Affirmed by U.S. District E.D. TX, Case No. 4:12-cv-707, Doc. 9; Affirmed by U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, 2014 U.S. App. LEXIS 17415 (5th Cir. Tex.). When Marty's bank client sought to foreclose its lien on real property, the borrower filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy and sued the bank challenging the enforceability of the cross-collateralization provision in the bank's deed of trust. On Marty's motion, Bankruptcy Judge Brenda T. Rhoades dismissed the suit against the bank. When the borrower appealed, the dismissal in favor of Marty's client was upheld by both the U.S. District Court and the U.S. Court of Appeals. This preserved the lien of Marty's client on valuable real property, leading to Marty's client being paid.

G.H. Bass & Co. v. Dalsan Properties-Abilene, 885 S.W.2d 572 (Tex. App. - Dallas 1994, no writ). After the tenant filed for bankruptcy protection, Marty filed a lawsuit for his landlord client against the surety/guarantor on the commercial lease for unpaid holdover rent and other charges. Marty obtained a judgment against the surety/guarantor in the trial court. When the surety/guarantor appealed, the Court of Appeals held that the surety/guarantor can be held liable for the holdover rent and other charges, but remanded the case to the trial court to consider whether the surety/guarantor could prove a waiver defense.

Family and interests

Marty and his wife Laurie have been married over 25 years. Laurie (formerly a practicing attorney) has dedicated her time to homeschooling their five children. Marty (a former college basketball player) served as the basketball commissioner of Dallas HSAA - Home School Athletic Association (one of the largest home school sports organizations in the United States), and has coached youth basketball and soccer, including coaching his son's team which in 2014 won the U16 D-II Texas State Homeschool Basketball Championship and the U16 D-II National Homeschool Basketball Championship.

Michelle Lehmkuhl was born and raised in Rockdale, Texas. She attended and graduated from Rockdale High School in 1996. Michelle graduated from Baylor in 1999 with a B.A. in Political Science and from Baylor University School of Law in 2002. After law school, Michelle worked as an associate attorney in a local law office where she handled a variety of cases, including family law, civil law, wills and probate, and real estate law. In 2005, Michelle opened her own law office where she handles a variety of cases. In 2017, Michelle received her Board Certification from the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Family Law.

In addition to her private law practice, Michelle also serves as the city attorney to the City of Rockdale.

Michelle joined the Law Office of Joshua P. Murray in an Of Counsel capacity in 2022.

Michelle believes every client's matter is important and every client deserves respect. Michelle understands that family law matters involve a highly emotional time and it is important to have an attorney on your side who loves what she does.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey Joseph Lehrman
attorneys.practice_type: Civil and Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Corpus Christi, TX
attorneys.bio:
A proud third generation lawyer, Jeffrey Lehrman was born and raised in Corpus Christi and completed his undergraduate work at Texas State University where he graduated with a bachelors in public administration and minor in mass communication in 2006. Upon graduation from Texas State, Jeffrey enrolled at Valparaiso University School of Law where he later graduated with his JD in 2009. After graduating from law school, Jeffrey was admitted to practice law in New York and New Jersey and practiced law in New York City prior to moving back to Texas to join ALBM. Jeffrey was eventually named partner in the firm in 2017 after developing a well-earned reputation as a successful and hardworking trial advocate for his clients. His professional accomplishments have included being named a Texas Super Lawyer for ten straight years, a fellow in the Texas Bar Foundation, member of the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA), named one of Corpus Christi's 40 under 40 business professionals and elected President of the Corpus Christi Bar Association by his peers. Jeffrey has also received numerous other state and national recognitions and awards for his litigation skills, legal professionalism, and pro bono work. Jeffrey's law practice includes representation of both plaintiffs and defendants and is concentrated on civil litigation with an emphasis on personal injury, medical malpractice, construction law, and commercial litigation matters. Since joining ALBM, Jeffrey has obtained multimillion dollar jury verdicts, numerous favorable arbitration awards, as well as significant pretrial settlements on behalf of his clients. Furthermore, Jeffrey's cases have also been featured in Texas Lawyer, Texas Monthly, Law 360, San Antonio Express News and the Corpus Christi Caller Times among other state and local publications.

In addition to his law practice, Jeffrey is very active in his local community where he has proudly served on the Board of Directors of several prominent local nonprofits including Habitat for Humanity of Corpus Christi and Corpus Christi Crimestoppers. Jeffrey and his wife are also active supporters of the American Cancer Society, the American Heart Association, and NAACP among many others. Jeffrey is also very active with the annual Corpus Christi Buc Days event where he volunteers as a member of the scholarship committee and proud member of the Bucaraders.

Jeffrey is happily married to Ana Lehrman and together the couple have two sons, Diego and Julian.

attorneys.name: Louis Leichter
attorneys.practice_type: Administrative Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Louis Leichter practices administrative, health and criminal law with a focus in the area of licensure and license defense. Mr. Leichter advises clients on disciplinary actions and misconduct allegations that range from standard of care issues and boundary violations to chemical dependency. Mr. Leichter also represents clients on associated issues and problems that are tangential to the receipt of a disciplinary order within the scope of a health care practice. Peer review and medical staff privileges, practitioner data bank disputes, network agreements, contract negotiations and license renewal questionnaires are matters of continued concern to medical and other health care professionals who are involved in the disciplinary process.

Prior to starting a private practice Mr. Leichter prosecuted criminal crimes as an Assistant County Attorney for Travis County, Texas. After gaining invaluable litigation, negotiation and trial skills Mr. Leichter opened the Law office of Louis Leichter and focused on the representation of individuals accused of white collar felonies and drug offenses. After representing a criminal client in a disciplinary matter, Mr. Leichter turned his attention to the representation of licensed professionals in disciplinary proceedings before their respective licensing boards and administrative agencies. To better serve his clients, Mr. Leichter represents, counsels and advises his clients on contractual agreements and other areas of civil litigation pertinent to their professional practice.

Mr. Leichter is a frequent writer, researcher and speaker on the subject of chemical dependency and its relationship to professional licensure defense and criminal intent. After his completion of the course requirements to be certified as a Licensed Chemical Dependency Counselor, Mr. Leichter joined the Sustainers Council at Austin Recovery where he devotes time and energy into developing public awareness about chemical dependency and recovery.

Mr. Leichter graduated from Vassar College in 1984 with a BA in philosophy. He went on to receive a Master of Science from FIU in hospitality finance and management. As a third year law student Mr. Leichter held a clerkship with Justice Louis Lavarato of the Iowa Supreme Court until earning his Juris Doctor from Drake University in Des Moines, Iowa. Mr. Leichter currently resides with his wife and child in Austin, Texas.

attorneys.name: Carlos Leon
attorneys.practice_type: Premises Liability Lawyers in Sugar Land, TX
attorneys.bio:
Carlos A. Leon has been practicing law in Texas for over 14 years. Prior to practicing law, Mr. Leon earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Houston in Political Science in 1991. While at the University of Houston, Mr. Leon was a three-year letter winner on the university's nationally ranked football team. In his senior year, Mr. Leon was selected to the GTE All-Southwest Conference Academic All American team. Upon graduating, Mr. Leon attended the University of Houston School of Law where he graduated in 1995.

After spending his first year as a litigation associate for a small civil firm in Dallas, Texas, Mr. Leon returned to Houston to head the personal injury department at a Houston Litigation Firm. During his career serving the Houston community, Mr. Leon accumulated over 20 million dollars in settlements for his clients. In addition, Mr. Leon has successfully tried cases to verdict in several counties in Texas. Currently Mr. Leon practices in the areas of premises liability, products liability, auto collisions, commercial trucking accidents, medical malpractice, workplace injuries, toxic exposure cases and pharmaceutical claims.

For nearly a decade, Mr. Leon has proudly served the diverse Houston community. He is completely fluent in Spanish and has enjoyed servicing the legal needs of the Hispanic community when called upon.

Mr. Leon currently serves on the Board of Directors for the Houston Trial Lawyers Association. In addition, Mr. Leon is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Association of Trial Lawyers of America and the Texas Trial Lawyers Association. Mr. Leon is currently admitted to practice before all state courts in Texas and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

sections.title: Representative Cases
content: El Paso Train Accident Lawyer Secures $13 Million Verdict - A train/auto collision case in El Paso County resulted in a $13 million verdict in favor of the plaintiffs, who suffered a fatality and serious injuries. The trial involved a strong team effort from The León Law Firm, with successful co-counsel duties shared by Jim Hart. The jury found significant responsibility on the part of one defendant, highlighting the importance of thorough legal representation.

Premises Liability Lawyer Wins $9,600,000 for Traumatic Brain Injury - This case resulted from injuries caused by known premises defect/dangerous condition on a property where our client lived. Client sustained life threatening injuries and a permanent traumatic brain injury.

Car Accident Lawyer Wins $7,000,000 After Delivery Driver Crash - Our clients’ vehicle was forcefully hit by a food delivery driver who failed to yield to oncoming traffic when making a turn. The impact caused our clients’ car to flip upside down, and for them both to suffer traumatic, long-term injuries.

Fatal Cement Truck Accident – $4,500,000 Settlement: Our client, assigned to drive a poorly maintained cement truck without proper training or inspection, was unable to brake due to faulty equipment and entered an intersection, colliding with a tractor-trailer. The crash caused the truck to roll over and strike other vehicles, resulting in his death and significant damages to his family.

Defective Airbag Injury Case Settles for $2,650,000 - This case resulted from injuries caused by a defective airbag that deployed expelling materials that caused severe and permanent scarring, neck, and dental injuries to our client.

Severe Injuries in Teen ‘Donuts’ Stunt – $2,052,500 Secured: Our client was ejected from a vehicle during reckless “donuts” at a high school parking lot in Austin, Texas, and was subsequently run over by another vehicle, resulting in severe, potentially permanent injuries.

Trucking Accident – $2,000,000 Settlement: While exiting a cement plant, a truck driver failed to yield, causing a violent collision that resulted in catastrophic injuries. After the trucking company initially denied liability, thorough discovery led to a successful $2,000,000 settlement.

Fatal Highway Accident: $1.75M Secured in Pedestrian Landscaping Case - While performing his duties as a landscaper on an esplanade near a highway, a driver suddenly lost control of his vehicle and swerved onto the esplanade. The driver struck our client at a high rate of speed, causing him to lose his life and his loved ones to suffer intense mental and emotional anguish

Landlord Liability Lawyer Wins $1,700,000 for Staircase Collapse - As our client walked down the stairs of her apartment building, one of the steps suddenly collapsed, causing her to fall forward and sustain serious injuries.

Wrongful Death – $1,541,000: Our client’s husband was fatally struck in a roadside collision when a tanker truck veered off the highway at high speed and hit him and another worker, resulting in devastating injuries and his death.

Fire Damage Lawyer Wins $1,500,000 for Homeowners - Represented dozens of homeowners whose properties were destroyed by fire due to the negligence of the local electricity company and its tree trimming contractor.

Trucking Injury Lawyer Secures $1,500,000 After Highway Collision - While was parked on the shoulder of a highway in his tractor trailer, our client was struck by the driver of an 18-wheeler who swerved into his lane when looking down to grab his drink. The collision caused the tractors to catch on fire and our client to suffer severe, incapacitating injuries.

Houston Pedestrian Hit in Crosswalk—$1.49M Injury Claim - While walking within the designated crosswalk area of an intersection in Houston, our client was struck by an inattentive driver making a left turn who failed to yield right of way to pedestrians. Our client suffered serious painful and incapacitating injuries, as well as lost wages, as a result of the accident.

$1,367,909 Refinery ATV Accident Settlement: Our client, a foreman at a Corpus Christi refinery, was injured when an ATV flipped after hitting uneven pavement, throwing him from the vehicle and causing serious, incapacitating injuries requiring multiple surgeries.
Workplace Injury Lawyer Settles $1,200,000 for Electrician Burns - Professional electrician suffered severe body burns to most of his body and face after flash fire due to faulty equipment.

Workplace Injury – £825,000 Compensation: Plaintiff recovered damages after being injured while performing work, with claims brought against the employer and its employee for negligence and unsafe workplace conditions that exposed Plaintiff to danger.

Toxic Exposure – $1,000,000: While working in a hospital pathology lab, our client was exposed to toxic substances due to poor ventilation, resulting in serious health issues after clogged filters and improperly installed fans were discovered.
Workplace Injury – $1,000,000: Our client fell approximately 22 feet when an unsecured forklift and pallet became unstable while he was repairing a roof, resulting in serious bodily injuries.

Fatal Pedestrian Accident – $996,009 Compensation: Our client’s son was fatally struck when a freightliner truck veered off the road at high speed and hit him while he was working along a highway, resulting in devastating injuries and his death at the scene.

Fall from Lift at Worksite Leads to £652K Compensation severe injuries - While on his way to work one morning, our client was rear-ended on the highway by a large office supply truck. As a result of the collision, our client’s spine was seriously injured, requiring surgical intervention.

Tractor-Trailer Rollover Injury Settlement of $790,000 - At a stop sign intersection on a service road, our client and his minor child were hit by a driver who failed to yield right of way. As a result, their tractor-trailer rolled over and our clients suffered serious bodily injuries.

Injured by Rebar in Parking Lot? $737K Legal Win for Victim - While making her way back to her car in the parking lot of a store, our client tripped and fell on a piece of rebar protruding upward from the concrete in front of her vehicle. As a result of the fall, she suffered injuries to her back, shoulder, and hips.
Hurricane Damage Lawyer Secures $732,500 for Construction Defect - Hurricane Harvey exposed sub standard construction practices that lead to preventable water and wind damage to a dwelling.

Construction Site Injury – $725,000 Compensation: Our client fell at a commercial construction site while covering a trailer with a makeshift tarp, suffering severe injuries due to hazardous conditions and lack of proper supervision.

Construction Injury Lawyer Wins $706K for Steel Girder Impact - Plaintiff was hired as an iron worker assisting in the steel erection phase at the construction of a major big box store. While installing the steel joists, a girder fell on top of him while he worked from a boom lift. The girder violently struck Plaintiff on his head and left side of his body. As a result, Plaintiff suffered several serious incapacitating injuries.

Struck at Supercenter: Lawyer Wins $675K for Severe Injuries - While working at a supercenter store, our client was struck by a delivery man pushing a cart overloaded with product that obstructed his view of what was in front of him. The force of the collision knocked our client to the ground, causing her to suffer severe injuries to her spine and knees.
Trucking Injury Lawyer Secures $675,000 After Highway Collision - Our clients suffered serious and permanent injuries when an 18-wheeler rear-ended them on the highway.

Construction Injury: $652,500 Win for Fall from Lift Basket - In the process of replacing a window on the exterior of a building under construction, our client fell from the unstable lift basket that had raised him up to the second story and landed on the concrete ground. As a result, our client suffered serious, long-term injuries to several areas of his body.

Construction Injury Lawyer Wins $620K for Power Line Accident - Worker injured in road construction site incident due to lack of proper training and negligence in directing dump truck near power lines. General contractor’s failure to provide a competent spotter and adequate warning signs resulted in multiple injuries to the client. Legal action led by our firm aims to seek justice and compensation for the preventable accident.
Workplace Injury Lawyer Wins $600,000 for Rear-End Collision - Our client was forcefully rear-ended while on his way to work, causing him to suffer debilitating injuries.
Elevator Accident – $600,000: Our client was injured when an elevator in a Houston office building suddenly dropped and came to an abrupt stop, causing her to fall and suffer serious injuries.

Commercial Insurance – $582,833.10 Recovery: The León Law Firm represented a Gulf Coast marina that sustained significant hurricane damage. After the insurer delayed and undervalued the claim, the firm secured full payment under the policy, totaling $582,833.10.

$525,000 Construction Site Injury | Broken Leg Lawsuit - As our client performed electrical work during the construction of a hotel in El Paso, some unsecured sheet rock that was propped up against a wall fell on our client’s leg and broke it in several areas.

Construction Site Injury Claim: $525,000 Case - Client was exposed to dangerous working conditions on a multiemployer construction worksite. The negligence of a nonemployer contractor caused his injuries which included multiple fractures to his legs and spine.

Pedestrian Accident – $514,670: Our client was fatally struck by a truck at a cement plant while it was backing up, resulting in injuries that led to his death, with damages recovered for his widow and children.

Slip and Fall Injury Settlement: $500K Awarded in Grocery Store Case - Plaintiff arrived at the grocery store to pick up a cup of coffee. As Plaintiff entered into the store, Plaintiff stepped onto a puddle of clear liquid (presumably water), slipped, and fell awkwardly to the floor. Video cameras in the store uncovered that the overnight cleaner left the cleaning liquid on the floor while mopping creating the hazardous condition.

Fatal Truck Rollover – $500,000 Claim: Our client lost control of an improperly maintained tractor-trailer and was ejected when it veered off the road and flipped, resulting in his death and significant damages to his loved ones.

Trip and Fall Lawyer Secures $495,000 for Store Injury - After opening the entrance door to a store, our client tripped on an unsecured rug and fell onto the floor. As a result, she suffered serious injuries to her knee and ribs.

Personal Injury Lawyer Wins $490,000 for Unsafe Turn Accident - While on his way to work, our client collided with a negligent driver making an unsafe turn. Fortunately, The León Law Firm’s skilled personal injury attorneys have secured a $490,000 settlement that will compensate this client for his injuries and losses!

Bar Assault – $450,000 Settlement: Plaintiff was assaulted by an intoxicated patron who was served alcohol despite prior removal from the bar, resulting in him being pushed down a flight of stairs and suffering severe injuries.

Restaurant Ladder Accident Lawyer Wins $450,000 Settlement - While working at a restaurant, our client was asked to retrieve items from an attic area on the premises which did not have a built-in structure to allow for regular access. Instructed to use a ladder to gain access, our client climbed nearly to the top until it fell. She landed hard on the floor and suffered serious injuries requiring surgical intervention.

Premises Liability – $450,000: Plaintiff was assaulted by an intoxicated patron who was served alcohol despite prior removal from the bar, resulting in him being pushed down a flight of stairs and suffering severe injuries.

Red Light Truck Accident Lawyer Secures $440,000 - While driving through an intersection with her minor child, our client was hit by a dump truck driver who disregarded his red light. The collision caused our client’s vehicle to spin off the road and hit a pole, resulting in serious injuries to both her and her child.

Intersection Collision Injury Claim—$410K for Back, Foot & Shoulder - At an intersection in Houston, our client was hit by a negligent driver who disregarded a traffic light. The force of the collision caused him to suffer serious injuries to his foot, shoulders, and back
Restaurant Injury – $400,000: Plaintiff was injured when an unsecured ice machine cover fell onto his head and nose while he was filling a cup, causing serious injuries requiring medical treatment.

Rear-End Collision Lawyer Secures $400,000 Settlement - As Plaintiffs approached the intersection, they began to slow down due to a yellow light. Defendant who was also traveling in the same direction, directly behind Plaintiffs, failed to control his speed and impacted the rear of Plaintiffs’ vehicle. The force of the collision caused Plaintiffs to suffer bodily injuries.
Fire Pole Fall – $400,000 Claim: Our client fell through an opening while attempting to use a fire pole at a party, suffering serious back injuries after being encouraged by the host to participate.

Truck Accident Lawyer Secures $399K Settlement for Rear-End Crash - Plaintiff was lawfully at a complete stop at the intersection, his light was red. As Plaintiff was waiting for his light to change, Defendant, driving a rig, violently crashed the front of the rig into the back of Plaintiff’s truck. The collision caused Plaintiff to suffer serious injuries.

Truck Accident – $369,000: Our client, a passenger in a tractor-trailer, suffered traumatic injuries including arm amputation when the driver lost control on a curvy road and the vehicle flipped onto its side.
Premises Liability Lawyer Secures $300K for Restroom Injury - Client slipped and fell inside men’s restroom. Area was wet and slippery due to leaking toilet. No signage was present.

Pool Leak Lawsuit Ends in $281,732 Settlement - Clients contracted a local Pool Company to design and install a high end pool. After the construction of pool, clients began to notice major water leakage from the pool. Engineering test concluded that pool was poorly and negligently designed and installed. Pool Company refused to accept responsibility. Suit was filed under the TxDTPA and Breach of Contract.
Wrongful Death Lawyer Secures $275,000 in Plant Worker Fatality - Concrete plant worker was run over and killed by an onsite contractor. The Leon Law Firm represented the family of the victim.

Trip and Fall Lawyer Secures $269,000 for Parking Lot Injury - While walking back to her vehicle in a parking lot, client tripped over a protruding rebar from a concrete stop. Client suffered severe injuries and aggravated the pre-existing conditions which required surgical intervention.
Stairway Collapse – $253,613: Our client’s husband fell head-first onto concrete when a stairway collapsed at a residential construction site, resulting in serious disabling injuries.
Construction Injury – $242,350: Our client fell from an unstable man lift at a commercial construction site, suffering several serious bodily injuries when the lift basket fell to the ground.

Trip and Fall Injury Case Secures $225,000 Settlement - While shopping with her daughter at a large, well-known department store, our client tripped and fell on an unmarked object. She suffered serious injuries requiring surgical intervention; but with the help of The León Law Firm, our client was fully compensated for her medical treatment and suffering.
Ladder Fall Injury Lawyer Secures $220,000 Settlement - Client fell from a ladder while assisting homeowner paint. Serious head injury.
Tractor-Trailer Collision – $203,281: Our client suffered serious injuries when a tractor-trailer made an unsafe lane change and struck his vehicle, causing it to spin and collide again.

Wrongful Death Lawyer Secures $200,000 for Fatal Head-On Crash - Head on accident killed our clients (two people) after vehicle burst into flames. Driver from the other vehicle had many citations for operating a commercial vehicle without a license. Settlement was split between the families and children of the victims.
Personal Injury – $200,000: Plaintiff was shot multiple times during a robbery attempt at an apartment complex and was transported to the hospital for emergency treatment.

Red Light Accident Lawyer Secures $200,000 Settlement - Client was victim was a victim of a driver running a red light. Suffered severe and grotesque injuries and a brutally broken foot and bodily injuries, plus lost wages.

Construction Injury – $191,000: Our client fell from the second story of a construction site after losing balance while carrying a ladder, suffering serious bodily injuries due to the lack of safety measures.

Car Repair Facility Slip and Fall Lawyer Wins $162,000 - Client was at car repair facility. He was asked by the attendant to go into the work area to view his vehicle when suddenly he slipped and fell into the pit. Injuries included herniated discs, requiring surgical intervention.

Car Accident Lawyer Obtains $150,000 for Turn Signal Violation - Plaintiff was making a left turn when Defendant disregarded his left turn only signal and proceeded straight through the intersection. Defendant’s failure to disregard his turn left only instruction resulted in him colliding with the driver’s side of Plaintiff’s vehicle. The force of the collision cause Plaintiff to suffer bodily injuries.

Truck Accident Lawyer Wins $150,000 for Highway Collision - Plaintiff was traveling in the furthest right lane of the highway. Defendant was driving a tractor-trailer while in the course and scope of his employment. Defendant was entering I-45 through the on-ramp when he failed to yield to traffic on the highway and suddenly merged into Plaintiff’s lane causing the vehicles to collide. The force of the collision caused Plaintiff to suffer bodily injuries.
Concrete Finisher Injury Lawyer Secures $150,000 Settlement - Concrete finisher was injured on the job by third party cement truck operator. Client was knocked over with boom from cement truck.

Veteran Injury Lawyer Wins $135,000 for Military Service Member - Client was serving in the military and was not able to serve again after the accident. Victim suffered internal injuries, and fractures in both legs.
Dog Bite Lawyer Secures $125,000 for Child’s Facial Injury - Child was bitten on the face by the dog while a guest at defendant’s home.

Pedestrian Injury Lawyer Wins $110,000 for Carwash Accident - Her claim stems from traumatic injuries she suffered when a manager of a carwash was exiting from the inside of the building, swung open the door, just as Plaintiff was approaching the doorway, on the outside of the building along the sidewalk. As a result of impact from the door slamming on her person, she awkwardly fell to the ground causing debilitating and serious injuries.

Head-On Collision Lawyer Wins $108,000 for Traumatic Injury - Client was a passenger in a vehicle along with 3 other co-workers. As a result of this head on collision two passengers were killed and our client received severe and traumatic injuries including being in a coma for 15 days, convulsions, cranium inflammation, brain edema, elevated intracranial pressure, cerebral edema, brain damage, collapsed and punctured lung, clavicle fracture and cervical fracture.

Company Vehicle Accident Lawyer Wins $106,946 for Client - As client approached the intersection, another driver, driving a company vehicle, failed to yield the right of way and crossed into our client’s path as he was attempting to turn resulting in the vehicles colliding. There was no time for our client to take any evasive maneuvers to avoid the collision. The collision caused our client to suffer serious injuries.

Construction Defect Lawyer Wins $96,000 for Pool Water Leak - Clients contracted Pool Company to install pool. After the construction of pool, clients notice a water leak from the pool. Pool Company refused to accept responsibility.

Accidental Death Lawyer Wins $90,000 After Insurance Claim Denial - Client died while performing self-induced erotic asphyxiation. Insurance company denied claim saying it was a suicide. Leon Law Firm was able to establish cause of death was accidental.
Intersection Collision Injury Lawyer Secures $73,000 Compensation - Intersection collision resulted in severe injuries to our client, including herniated discs and broken bones.
Warehouse Accident – $72,376: Our client suffered a serious foot injury, including toe amputation, after a forklift ran over his foot due to unsafe work practices in a warehouse.

Accidental Shooting Injury – $60,000: Our client was injured when a firearm accidentally discharged at a gathering, causing a bullet to strike her ankle and resulting in serious injuries, including a fracture and arterial damage.
Truck Accident Injury Lawyer Wins $54,000 Compensation - An unsafe lane change by an 18 Wheeler caused that rig to strike our client resulting in severe injuries that sent our client to the hospital

Assault Injury Lawyer Secures $38,000 for Gunshot Victim - Client was walking to his mailbox when he was assaulted. He received a gunshot to his legs. The bullet punctured from his left to right thigh, where it became lodged.

Work Site Accident Lawyer Secures $36,456 for Ladder Fall - The incident occurred at a residential construction site. Client was a laborer hired to work on the installation of the AC units. While the Client was completing his work attempted to get down from the attic. However, the attic access ladder had been negligently installed by another sub-contractor, consequently Client fell to the ground. As a result, Client suffered several serious and incapacitating injuries.
Motor Vehicle Accident Lawyer Secures $26,000 Compensation - Rear ended by an 18 Wheeler. Client resulting in severe injuries which included disc herniations.

attorneys.name: Clarissa Levingston
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Growing up as the daughter of an attorney and a realtor, Clarissa began learning from an early age what it looks like to advocate for her clients and understand the varied factors that impact property values. Now, she draws on that background as she strives to help landowners of various property types ─ commercial, agricultural, residential, and industrial ─ ensure they are compensated fairly for their property when the government exercises its eminent domain authority.

Clarissa represents clients in cases involving a range of issues, including road widening, inverse condemnation, access issues, regulatory impacts, and various types of easements (HVTL, drainage, water/sewer lines, pipelines, and temporary construction).

A dedicated advocate for her clients, Clarissa has successfully argued for and negotiated greater compensation during the administrative phase of condemnation proceedings to achieve significant increases that resolve the case without the need for a trial. When continuing to the judicial phase is necessary, Clarissa works closely with her firm colleagues and industry experts to ensure the best position possible for the best possible result.

Clarissa’s year as a federal judicial clerk afforded her insights and experience that inform her approach when advocating for clients looking to challenge unjust trial court outcomes, whether in the courts of appeal or the Texas Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Christopher W. Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris Lewis is well known in the legal community as a criminal defense lawyer who gets results. He has earned the respect of judges, peers and clients by zealously defending his clients with skill and integrity. Chris has a vast amount of experience in the courtroom, having tried more than 200 jury trials. Due to his track record of obtaining acquittals at a very high rate and frequently securing dismissals and reduced charges for his clients, Chris is considered "top-flight criminal defense lawyer" and is routinely named as one of the best criminal defense lawyers in north Texas.

After graduating Magna Cum Laude from Evangel University with a double major in Government and Psychology, Chris attended Baylor University School of Law, earning a law degree with a Criminal Law Concentration. Upon graduating from law school, Chris began his legal career as an assistant district attorney. He prosecuted criminal cases in Harris, Williamson and Dallas counties before transitioning to a civil litigation practice. From 2000-2004, Chris worked for one of the largest civil trial law firms in Texas representing large corporations in lawsuits across the State of Texas. In addition to litigation matters, Chris defended clients accused of various misdemeanor and felony offenses in Dallas and around the state.

Chris, a four year starter and all-conference football player in college, spent several years working as a sports agent. Certified by the National Football Players’ Association and registered by the Texas Secretary of State, Chris represented NFL, CFL and AFL players in contract negotiations.

Since 2004, Chris’ practice has been devoted exclusively to defending people whose lives have been turned upside down by criminal accusations. His clients would prefer not to require his legal services. However, when life’s circumstances bring people to Chris’ office, they quickly learn that they are in capable and experienced hands. Chris loves fighting for the underdog, and in a criminal case, the accused always starts out as the underdog. Chris’ number one objective in every single case is to utilize his skills and the firm’s resources to level the playing field against the government and to fight for his clients’ freedom in an effort to restore hope and normalcy to their lives.

Chris regularly handles cases in both state and federal court. He represents people charged with crimes ranging from DWI to Capital Murder. Chris is passionate about people and protecting their rights, and he is determined to provide his clients with the best possible representation in defending their freedom.

attorneys.name: Craig Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Craig Lewis was born in Stratford, Ontario, Canada. After receiving a B.A. degree, magna cum laude, from Baylor University in 1969, he entered Baylor Law School, where he received his J.D. degree, cum laude, in 1973. While attending Baylor Law School, Mr. Lewis represented the law school on its national moot court team and served as Editor-in-Chief of the Baylor Law Review.

Mr. Lewis has been a trial lawyer for over 47 years, representing clients in complex cases including catastrophic injuries, products liability, medical malpractice, probate, toxic torts, environmental, oil and gas, breach of contract, and diverse areas of commercial litigation. During Mr. Lewis's legal career, he has obtained judgments and settlements in excess of $1,000,000 for his clients in nearly 100 cases. Refinery explosions, aviation crashes, industrial and recreational product failures, automobile design defects, pharmaceutical disasters, medical negligence, and catastrophic financial losses and/or death - are just a few of the specific areas where Mr. Lewis has tried over 200 lawsuits to a jury, as lead counsel, in representing the victims and survivors of those who have been catastrophically damaged by the negligence and fault of others. In the areas of healthcare and medical malpractice, Mr. Lewis has handled over 1,000 cases where the negligence of physicians, hospitals, nursing homes, and other healthcare providers unfortunately resulted in serious injuries and significant damages to children and adults - including over 100 cases where medical negligence resulted in permanent brain damage to infants and adults.

As a named partner in the former law firm, Fisher, Gallagher & Lewis, Mr. Lewis was involved in many facets of the Howard Hughes Estate litigation, initially successfully representing two unrelated heirs, and later being retained by the Howard Hughes Estate to assist in prosecuting and defending a myriad of probate issues, including heirship, domicile, and over 300 alleged "Last Wills and Testaments" of Howard Hughes.

Since 1987, Mr. Lewis has also represented homeowners, businesses, subdivisions, ranchers, and other victims whose property, water, and health have been contaminated and injured by businesses who have polluted our environment and precious natural resources. Several States have retained Mr. Lewis as counsel to prosecute those who polluted and contaminated the States' natural resources, including public drinking water supplies. He successfully represented an independent school district which was forced to close one of its elementary schools due to its proximity to a Super Fund site. Mr. Lewis has taken the depositions of over 400 corporate executives, petroleum engineers, hydrologists, chemists, toxicologists, geologists, environmental engineers, and the experts retained by those parties responsible for the pollution. As a sub-specialty of environmental litigation, Mr. Lewis has also concentrated on the economic evaluation of our natural resources, with particular emphasis on evaluating the economic loss of surface water and underground aquifers.

Mr. Lewis has been a trial lawyer for over 47 years, representing clients in complex cases including catastrophic injuries, products liability, medical malpractice, probate, toxic torts, environmental, oil and gas, breach of contract, and diverse areas of commercial litigation. During Mr. Lewis's legal career, he has obtained judgments and settlements in excess of $1,000,000 for his clients in nearly 100 cases. Refinery explosions, aviation crashes, industrial and recreational product failures, automobile design defects, pharmaceutical disasters, medical negligence, and catastrophic financial losses and/or death - are just a few of the specific areas where Mr. Lewis has tried over 200 lawsuits to a jury, as lead counsel, in representing the victims and survivors of those who have been catastrophically damaged by the negligence and fault of others. In the areas of healthcare and medical malpractice, Mr. Lewis has handled over 1,000 cases where the negligence of physicians, hospitals, nursing homes, and other healthcare providers unfortunately resulted in serious injuries and significant damages to children and adults - including over 100 cases where medical negligence resulted in permanent brain damage to infants and adults.

As a named partner in the former law firm, Fisher, Gallagher & Lewis, Mr. Lewis was involved in many facets of the Howard Hughes Estate litigation, initially successfully representing two unrelated heirs, and later being retained by the Howard Hughes Estate to assist in prosecuting and defending a myriad of probate issues, including heirship, domicile, and over 300 alleged "Last Wills and Testaments" of Howard Hughes.

Since 1987, Mr. Lewis has also represented homeowners, businesses, subdivisions, ranchers, and other victims whose property, water, and health have been contaminated and injured by businesses who have polluted our environment and precious natural resources. Several States have retained Mr. Lewis as counsel to prosecute those who polluted and contaminated the States' natural resources, including public drinking water supplies. attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Katie L. Lewis, Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, is the founder and Managing Partner of Katie L. Lewis, P.C. Family Law. With a passion rooted in personal experience, Katie chose family law to make a meaningful difference in the lives of her clients. Growing up as the child of divorced parents, she witnessed firsthand how a skilled and compassionate attorney can profoundly impact a family’s future. This perspective drives her commitment to delivering empathetic yet results-focused representation, always mindful of the broader effects on family relationships.

A native of the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex, Katie earned her Bachelor of Science in Political Science, with a Business minor, from Texas A&M University in 2002. During her time at A&M, she embraced leadership roles as a member of Pi Beta Phi Sorority, the Aggie Pre-Law Society, and as a Fish Camp Counselor and Muster volunteer. In 2005, she earned her Juris Doctor from Texas Wesleyan University School of Law (now Texas A&M School of Law), where she distinguished herself as a member of the Mock Trial Team for her litigation skills.

Katie’s legal career is marked by exceptional achievements and accolades. She has been named to the prestigious Texas Super Lawyers list every year since 2013, an honor reserved for the top 5% of attorneys in the state. For three years, 2023-2025, she was recognized as one of the Top 50 Women Attorneys in Texas and one of the Top 100 Attorneys in the Dallas/Fort Worth area.

Katie is also committed to shaping the next generation of legal professionals. She frequently speaks throughout the state of Texas, sharing her expertise and passion for family law.

When she’s not advocating for her clients, Katie enjoys life in Irving, Texas, where she cherishes time with her nieces and pursues her love of travel, exploring at least one new country each year.

Katie L. Lewis is proud to offer compassionate and strategic legal guidance to families throughout Texas, providing unwavering support during life’s most pivotal transitions.

attorneys.name: Kern A. Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kern Lewis joined Bailey & Galyen in 2020, bringing extensive experience in brain injury cases. He understands the devastating impact that a brain injury can have on someone’s life, and he has dedicated his career to fighting against the negligence of others.

“There is hardly any injury more devastating than a traumatic brain injury. An injury to a person’s back, arms or legs is terrible – but a brain injury is an injury to the very core of who a person is,” says Lewis. “A brain injury impacts their memory, their personality, and their ability to think.”

In a recent traumatic brain injury case – Lewis lived with his client for several days to be able to completely understand and experience the impact the injury had on her life. “When I told her story to the jury at trial – I was able to do so as someone who experienced it – not just heard about it. It makes a huge difference.” His client received the largest jury verdict ever awarded in that court. But even after the trial and the money was paid, he continued to work with that client and her family members to make sure she was taken care of.

Lewis’ skills as a trial lawyer have earned him local and national recognition. He is double board certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Civil Trial Law and Consumer and Commercial Law, a distinction only 15 lawyers have obtained. Lewis has also been inducted into the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA) with the rank of Associate and has an AV Preeminent Rating by Martindale-Hubbell, the highest level of professional excellence. He has been repeatedly named to the Texas Super Lawyers list, which is an honor less than 5 percent of lawyers obtain. In 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2018 he was named a “Top 100” Trial Lawyer in Texas by the National Trial Lawyers Association. He was also named to the National Trial Lawyer’s list of Top 25 Brain Injury Lawyers in 2018.

attorneys.name: Tracey Dominique Lewis
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tracey Dominique Lewis is a seasoned Employment Lawyer and the Managing Partner of Leeds Law Firm, PLLC—a nationwide firm dedicated to advocating for employees across the United States. Licensed in New Jersey, New York (since 2012), and Texas (since 2014), Tracey brings over a decade of focused legal experience and a powerful track record of representing plaintiffs in complex employment law matters.

Her practice centers on fighting for individuals facing wrongful termination, negotiating severance agreements, and recovering unpaid overtime wages.

Tracey has extensive trial experience, having served as both first and second chair in high-stakes litigation, and is known for her strategic thinking, persuasive advocacy, and relentless commitment to justice for workers.

At Leeds Law Firm, Tracey leads a team of dedicated attorneys committed to a contingency-based model—ensuring that all employees, regardless of financial background, have access to top-tier legal representation.

Her leadership has helped shape the firm into a trusted voice in employment law nationwide. Whether in the courtroom or at the negotiation table, Tracey Dominique Lewis is a passionate defender of employee rights, bringing integrity strenght, and sharp legal acumen to every case she handles.

attorneys.firm_name: Orsinger, Nelson, Downing and Anderson, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Amber Liddell Alwais is a staunch advocate for clients, committed to providing highly personalized legal services in all Family Law matters, including traditional and non-traditional divorce, custody issues, property division, child support and adoption matters.

In addition to her legal practice, Amber serves as a Family Law, Probate Law and Criminal Law instructor at The University of Texas at San Antonio. She is vice president of the San Antonio Bar Association Family Law section.

Amber was named the 2003 Outstanding Young Lawyer of the Year by the Women’s Bar Association of Bexar County in recognition of her contributions to the San Antonio legal community. She also has been honored on both the Texas Super Lawyers and Texas Rising Stars listings published by Thomson Reuters, Legal Division, and regularly has been selected to San Antonio's Top Attorneys list published by S.A. Scene Magazine

Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization since 2009, Amber is licensed to practice law in Texas state district courts, U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, and the Supreme Court of Texas. She is a former staff attorney for the Civil District Judges of Bexar County. A 1996 graduate of St. Mary’s University School of Law, she earned her Bachelor’s Degree from Sam Houston State University in 1993.

attorneys.name: Richard (“Rick”) C. Lievens
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Richard (“Rick”) C. Lievens, was licensed by the State Bar of Texas in 1979, and is board certified in Property Owners’ Association Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He has served as committee member of the State Bar of Texas Condominium and Cooperative Housing Committee, has served on the Board of Directors of the Greater Houston Chapter of the Community Associations Institute (1985-1990), including chapter President in 1987, and is a former adjunct instructor of Real Estate Law, Contracts, and Community Association Law at the University of Houston Real Estate Institute.

For over 45 years, Rick has practiced law in the areas of real estate, probate, and lending, with an emphasis in community association matters. His community association practice includes developer representation, homeowner/condominium association representation, drafting/interpretation of documentation (Declaration, Bylaws, and the like) collection of maintenance assessments, and deed restriction enforcement.

Prior to his affiliation with Barsalou & Associates P.L.L.C., Rick was a partner in the law firm of Frank, Elmore, Lievens, Slaughter & Turet L.L.P., a distinguished Houston law firm which focused on real estate, lending, and condominium development.

attorneys.name: Brittany L. Lightfoot
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Accidents Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brittany L. Lightfoot was raised in Onalaska, Texas, and currently resides in Dallas, Texas. Brittany, a first-generation college graduate, obtained an academic scholarship to attend Sam Houston State University where she obtained her undergraduate degree in Political Science. After graduation, she attended law school at Texas Tech University School of Law on an academic scholarship. While in law school, Brittany worked at a family law firm under a supervisory bar card and was secretary of the Raider Bar Association. Brittany graduated from the Texas Tech University School of Law in 2022 and was admitted to the Texas bar in 2022.

Upon graduation, Brittany began her legal career in the complex commercial litigation and criminal defense sector where she gained invaluable trial experience litigating numerous multi-million-dollar cases in state court. After numerous years in litigation, Brittany decided to transition to pre-litigation. Since joining Thompson Law, Brittany has represented clients in personal injury accidents, such as, auto accidents, truck wrecks, pedestrian accidents, motorcycle crashes, general negligence, wrongful death, and premises liability cases.

Outside of the office, Brittany is a member of the State Bar of Texas LeadershipSBOT program, Leadership Forward, and the Dallas Association of Young Lawyers 2023-2024 Leadership class. Brittany enjoys playing tennis, spending time with friends and family, and serving the community.

attorneys.name: Donald Francis Lighty
attorneys.firm_name: Wells Peyton Partain Baldo & Lighty, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Beaumont, TX
attorneys.bio:
I have spent my entire legal career defending people and corporate entities in personal injury, civil, contract, employment, real estate and workers' compensation matters. I have tried over 135 jury cases as the primary trial counsel in state and federal courts throughout the state.

In 1985 I was fortunate enough to begin my legal career handling personal injury claims including automobile wrecks and workers' compensation matters throughout southeast Texas. This allowed me to obtain much needed experience before juries, including in counties known for awarding excessive plaintiffs' verdicts. Over the years clients have retained me to represent them in other parts of the state, and am now statewide counsel for many entities including municipalities, political subdivisions and major corporations.

ln 2022 I became a founding partner of Wells Peyton Partain Baldo & Lighty, LLP. The firm was formed to continue our commitment in defending those who have been sued. l have expanded my practice to include the defense of real estate professional liability claims, as well as representation of clients before administrative law entities such as OSHA, Texas Workforce Commission and the Texas Department of Insurance-Division of Workers' Compensation.

I have been married for thirty-five years, raised three sons, two of which have chosen to follow me in the practice of law. I have served in many philanthropic boards including United Way of Beaumont & North Jefferson County and Beaumont Crime Stoppers. have also served on the Board of Directors for the Jefferson County Bar Association and Jefferson County Young Lawyers Association. Currently I am a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Texas Association of Defense Counsel, a Fellow of the College of the State Bar of Texas and a Life Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation. I am the former Chaim1an of the District 3A Subcommittee of the Unauthorized Practice of Law (1993-2014) and a member of the Equestrian Order of the Knights of the Holy Sepulcher of Jerusalem."

attorneys.name: Phillip A. Linder
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Phillip Linder was born and raised in Dallas, Texas and has extensive ties to the legal community. His family has been involved in the legal community and criminal justice system in the North Texas area for over 45 years. Phillip has been a trial lawyer in both criminal law and family law cases for 20 years. These ties and connections have proven to be invaluable in the effective representation of his clients.

Phillip started his trial career in the Dallas County District Attorney's office in 1992. He quickly rose through the ranks of misdemeanor and felony and was eventually moved into the Organized Crime Section, which handles and tries large drug conspiracy cases. During his 3 ½ years in the Dallas County District Attorney's Office, he handled thousands of cases and tried over 100 cases to jury verdict.

Since leaving the District Attorney's Office, he has again handled thousands of cases in both Criminal law and Family Law and tried over 100 of those cases to jury verdict. He is Board Certified as a Criminal Trial Specialist by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He is one of a very small number of lawyers approved in North Texas to handle Capital Murder cases. He has handled several Capital Murder cases, one of his recent capital murder trials was recently filmed for "the First 48" docu-drama TV show and has aired several times.

In addition to being licensed in the State of Texas, he is also admitted to practice in all four of the federal districts in Texas as well as in front of the Federal Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. He has also been admitted to and handled large federal cases in Oklahoma, Kansas, Arkansas, New Mexico and Alabama.

Phillip's finance and accounting degrees and experience in business makes him infinitely qualified to handle both white-collar business fraud cases in both state and federal court as well as complex property distribution issues in family court. In actuality, he has represented executives from several large corporations; in defending them against fraud and corruption allegations. He has also represented other lawyers, doctors and professional athletes in both the criminal defense arena and the family law arena. Many of the criminal defense cases were dismissed before ever reaching the trial phase as a result of Phillip's intelligent and aggressive representation.

Phillip's reputation among his peers is such that he was appointed to the Board of the Dallas County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association in 1997 and was later elected to and served as President in 2004. Phillip was also nominated as a "Fellow" in the Texas Bar Foundation by his peers in the family law Bar Association. Phillip is A.V. rated as "Preeminent" by Martindale-Hubbell, rated as "Superior" by AVVO and appeared in the D Magazine Best Lawyers in Texas edition in 2011. In 2012 he was also rated and listed in the list of Texas Super Lawyers.

In addition to his criminal and family law trial qualifications, Phillip has always been concerned about quality representation of the clients, by other local lawyers. Over the years, he has both investigated and represented lawyers, charged with poor representation of their clients, before the State Bar. He has also lectured at local Bar Association meetings around the state about the effective representation of one's clients and the disciplinary process. In 2007 Phillip was appointed to the Board. In 2009, he was elected as Chairman of the Dallas Area Committee for Lawyer Discipline that investigates and prosecutes attorneys who do not represent their clients effectively.

attorneys.name: Patrick W. Lindner
attorneys.practice_type: Public Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Patrick W. Lindner is a Vice-President of the Board of Directors, a shareholder of the Firm and a member of the Firm's Management Committee. Mr. Lindner is a member of the Firm's Public Law, Utility and Environmental Sections. He is board certified in Administrative Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He was educated at Texas Tech University and the University of Texas (BA, 1976) and St. Mary's University (JD, 1979). He was admitted to the Texas bar in 1979, and is licensed to practice before U.S. District Court for the Eastern and Northern Districts of Texas.

Mr. Lindner has served as lead counsel in several contested matters under Texas Water Code, Chapter 26 (relating to water quality), Chapter 13 (relating to retail public utilities), and Chapter 11 (relating to the diversion and use of water) and has assisted with the preparation of applications for solid waste permits and injection well permits. He is familiar with the rules restricting and regulating certain activities upon the recharge zone of the Edwards Aquifer since 1976.

Before receiving his license to practice law, Mr. Lindner served in the Hearings Division and in the San Antonio Field Office of the Texas Water Quality Board. While employed with the Texas Water Quality Board, a predecessor agency of the Texas Water Commission, Mr. Lindner was responsible for reviewing application for waste discharge permits to determine administrative completeness, reviewing and summarizing evidence submitted in hearings regarding waste discharge permits, reviewing and summarizing evidence received during hearings regarding substantive revisions to the rules for protecting the Edwards Aquifer, field inspections of waste treatment and disposal facilities to report compliance with applicable laws, field inspections of solid waste storage and disposal facilities and sites to report compliance with applicable law, and monitoring water quality in lakes and streams.

Mr. Lindner has spoken at seminars and has presented speeches such as "Aquatic Biota Protection Using Specific Chemicals and Total Effluent Toxicity", written for the Environmental Seminar in Beaumont, Texas, held in September of 1987 and January of 1988.

Mr. Lindner is a member of the State Bar of Texas Administrative and Public Law Sections, the Environmental Law Section, and the Public Utility Law Section.
