attorneys.name: Samira Lineberger
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Lisa A. Vance, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Lineberger is a 1987 graduate of St. Mary’s University, School of Law in San Antonio, Texas. She has practiced in a wide range of areas of law and in many capacities. While a large part of her focus today is on Family Law matters, her vast experience in other areas of the law make her well suited to address the variety of issues that can come up in divorce suits, particularly with complex business and personal assets. Her vast litigation experience in such a wide range of the law not only gives her the depth to deal with a variety of circumstances that can find their way into a divorce action, but also provides the back drop for her well-honed, highly experienced trial and negotiation skills. Ms. Lineberger’s approach to her legal practice is to focus on service, individualism and smart sensible solutions, while still passionately fighting to protect the rights and needs of her clients. Her approach with her Family Law clients is to not only secure the best for her client, but to do so in ways that help them move towards a brighter and happier life. When there are children involved, the top priority is to look for solutions that are the best result for the children; to put them on a path that gives them the best chance of a happy, healthy and successful future. Ms. Lineberger understands that when your family is in crisis, you need support in ways beyond the law. Her family law practice is about not only getting the best results on the legal matters, but also in helping you make the best decisions for you and your family.

Ms. Lineberger’s experience beyond family law includes experience in commercial litigation, intellectual property, probate matters, bankruptcy proceedings, personal injury, employment discrimination and harassment, premises liability, products liability, construction defects, mechanics liens, fraud, defamation, FELA (Railroad employee injury cases) and DTPA (Deceptive Trade Practices Act) among other things makes her uniquely equipped to address a variety of client needs. Her trial experience ranges from damages and estates as small as four figures, to cases as high as eight figures.

Unique to Ms. Lineberger’s experience is her ownership and participation in several of her own businesses, including a multi-million dollar residential construction company, a mediation firm, and currently a consulting firm, Lineberger Consulting Group that advises law firms on business development and marketing strategies. This small business experience enhances her appreciation for what it takes to run a business, how a divorce is effective by business ownership, and how legal issues impact a small business from an ownership perspective.

Ms. Lineberger’s undergraduate work was at Texas A&M University where she received a BBA in Marketing. She is also an Adjunct Professor at St. Mary’s University, School of Law, where she teaches Business Development and Marketing for Lawyers and has taught numerous seminars on negotiation.

attorneys.name: Dan Linebaugh
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Baytown, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dan Linebaugh is certified as a specialist in Truck Accident Law and in Personal Injury Trial Law. He was admitted to the Texas Bar in 1985. Mr. Linebaugh holds a Doctor of Jurisprudence degree from South Texas College of Law and a Bachelor of Arts degree in speech communications from Youngstown State University. While attending law school, Mr. Linebaugh received recognition for excellence in scholarship and placed among the top oralists in both mock trial and moot court competitions. In 2002, Mr. Linebaugh completed advanced course work in trial advocacy sponsored by the National College of Advocacy at Harvard Law School in Cambridge, MA.

In addition to being licensed to practice law before all Texas courts, Mr. Linebaugh is licensed to practice law before the United States Supreme Court, the U.S. 5th Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of Texas.

Mr. Linebaugh is a frequent lecturer at seminars for attorneys and other legal programs. In addition to being Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Linebaugh is also Board Certified in Truck Accident Law by the National Board of Trial Advocacy.*

Mr. Linebaugh is an active member of numerous bar associations, including the American Bar Association, the American Association for Justice and the Houston Bar Association. From 1998 through 2000, Mr. Linebaugh served as president of the East Harris County Bar Association. Mr. Linebaugh is also a graduate of the highly acclaimed Trial Lawyers College in Dubois, Wyoming, where he studied under legendary trial attorney, Gerry Spence. And since 1998, Linebaugh has served the State Bar of Texas on the Pattern Jury Charge Committee for General Negligence and Personal Torts.

Mr. Linebaugh's reputation has earned him the privilege of representing clients from throughout Texas and the United States. Texas Monthly Magazine has named Mr. Linebaugh as a Texas Super Lawyer every year since 2003. Linebaugh has also been inducted into the Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum as a lifetime member.

He received his law degree from Texas Wesleyan School of Law, earning a place on the Dean’s List every semester of law school, and once again graduated cum laude.

Felipe was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2007 and the State Bar of Illinois in 2008. Before founding Link & Associates, he worked in the Dallas office of a well-known personal injury firm in Dallas, where he zealously pursued the rights of thousands who were injured by the negligence of others.

Felipe began Link & Associates with the vision of creating a well-rounded law firm that is able to handle any problems that its clients may have. An experienced trial lawyer, and Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law, Felipe has represented clients in a variety legal matters, including but not limited to personal injury, business disputes, contract disputes and collections, fraud, and insurance coverage denials.

He received his law degree from Texas Wesleyan School of Law, earning a place on the Dean’s List every semester of law school, and once again graduated cum laude.

Felipe was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 2007 and the State Bar of Illinois in 2008. Before founding Link & Associates, he worked in the Dallas office of a well-known personal injury firm in Dallas, where he zealously pursued the rights of thousands who were injured by the negligence of others.

Felipe began Link & Associates with the vision of creating a well-rounded law firm that is able to handle any problems that its clients may have. An experienced trial lawyer, and Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law, Felipe has represented clients in a variety legal matters, including but not limited to personal injury, business disputes, contract disputes and collections, fraud, and insurance coverage denials.

In May of 2000, Mr. Little graduated from the University of Texas School of Law, and obtained his license to practice law in the State of Texas in September of 2001. During his career as an attorney, Mr. Little has represented clients from throughout the United States and the world in Texas state and federal courts.

Outside of work, Linyu enjoys traveling, exploring Houston’s food scene, and spending time with family.

attorneys.name: Jodi D. Liukkonen
attorneys.practice_type: Assault Family Violence Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jodi D. Liukkonen is a seasoned criminal defense attorney with over 20 years of legal experience in criminal law, child protection, and juvenile prosecution. Prior to joining Pantheon Legal Group, PLLC Jodi handled high-profile sexual offense cases at numerous large law firms in Dallas-Fort Worth, building a reputation for her tenacity and skill in navigating complex criminal defense litigation.

Jodi’s distinguished career includes serving as an Assistant Public Defender for Minnesota's Seventh Judicial District, where she successfully represented both juvenile and adult clients in misdemeanor, felony, and child protection cases. Her ability to conduct jury and non-jury trials has resulted in dismissals, reductions, and Not Guilty verdicts for clients accused of aggravated sexual assault of a child, indecency with a child, and continuous sexual abuse of a child.

Before she practiced criminal defense, Jodi served as an Assistant Juvenile Prosecutor, where she prosecuted Termination of Parental Rights (TPR) proceedings, among others. During this time, she earned certification as a Child Forensic Interviewer . Through working closely with law enforcement, social workers, and mental health professionals, she has a depth of knowledge regarding all phases of crimes against children investigation and related proceedings that only those who have worked inside the system would know.

Jodi earned her Juris Doctor from Thomas M. Cooley Law School, where she served as Editor-in-Chief of the Thomas M. Cooley Journal of Practical and Clinical Law. She led the publication of four volumes and spearheaded a national symposium on child victims and cybercrime.

Today, at Pantheon Legal Group, PLLC, Jodi brings her extensive courtroom experience, over 20 years of experience in crimes against children cases, and practical knowledge of criminal investigation. Her proven track record in criminal law, investigation, prosecution, and defense of sex crimes, ensures clients receive guidance informed by expert knowledge and decades of experience.​

attorneys.name: Andrew M. Lloyd
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Denton, TX
attorneys.bio:
Born just south of Dallas, and true to his Texas roots, Andrew M. Lloyd fights proudly for families and justice. He exemplifies the attitude contained in the phrase - Don’t mess with Texas! He doesn’t let people mess with his clients, either. Big government and belligerent litigators threaten his clients’ lives, so he defends them. He’s a negotiator by birth and an attorney by trade, whose ultimate prowess and skill lie in the courtroom. He’s tenacious, witty, intelligent, and scrappy. With a nickname like “Texas Spanker,” what else would you expect?

A former prosecutor and continuing Texas Super Lawyer for over a decade, he's been handling family law and criminal defense cases in front of Judges and juries for over 20 years with a finesse and charisma that leaves people in awe. He can change the pace of a case quickly, understanding the underpinnings of the justice system and the inner workings of a case file. He’s real. He’s personal. And he’s a fighter.

He has held top leadership positions in his local bar associations for years, was the Master of Ceremonies for over 5 of the annual Denton County Bench Bar Conferences, where all the local Judges and lawyers spend time learning the law. He’s been a guest speaker several times over the years at these and other legal conferences.

Outside of the courtroom, Andrew’s the ultimate family man and churchgoer. He’s a father of four awesome children and husband to his beautiful Inga. He enjoys cycling, running, racquetball, horse-back riding, shooting, soccer, music, and anything else that keeps him active! He’s also a martial artist, having learned the craft of Wing Tsun Kung Fu for many years and is currently training for a black belt in American Karate again.

attorneys.name: Michele L. Locke
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Michele Locke is a former Associate Court Judge that has returned to private practice to continue pursuing her passion for family law litigation. The Court that Michele ran was a Domestic Violence Court that focused on Protective Order Applications, divorce, custody, child support, enforcement and other family law matters that arose out of those Protective Orders. Furthermore, for a period of time, she ran the Child Protective Services Court. She is knowledgeable in contested family law matters that involve issues of domestic violence, stalking, harassment, and child abuse. The Court was a forerunner in addressing issues that related to Same-Sex relationships.

Michele, prior to becoming a Judge ran a successful family law practice. She handled all ranges of cases and successfully represented clients in all types of highly contested matters.

Michele's passion since law school has been family law. As a child of divorce, step-mother of two girls, and a mother to three boys, Michele understands all too well the dynamics and complexities of divorce and the impact divorce has on the families undergoing these tumultuous times.

Michele's areas of practice include Divorce, Custody, Child Support, Family Violence, and other family law matters.

attorneys.name: Thomas J Lochry
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Thomas J. Lochry, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tom Lochry has been practicing law since 1977 representing people from all walks of life in criminal, family and personal injury cases. He is married to a career teacher that helped put him through law school. Together they have two miniature schnauzers, two married daughters and five grandchildren.

Tom Lochry grew up in Indianapolis, Indiana and graduated from Miami of Ohio in 1972 with a bachelor’s in political science. He worked at a variety of jobs in college from dishwasher to construction worker. After college, he worked for Marion County in Indianapolis as a juvenile court probation officer/caseworker for male delinquents in court ordered placements and foster homes.

He decided to go to law school at SMU in 1974. During law school, he worked at a number of jobs ranging from delivering newspapers, to drafting pension plans and law clerking. After graduating in 1977, he started his law practice handling family, criminal and personal injury cases. After trying hundreds of cases, he became board certified in criminal law in 1994. He has been recognized as a Super Lawyer and enjoys an A+ rating with the Better Business Bureau. Today, he handles criminal and juvenile cases exclusively.

Tom Lochry has been a member of the Lake Highlands Exchange Club and the Lake Highlands United Methodist Church for over 20 years. He is a past president of the Exchange Club and served on that board for ten years. He has also served in the Dallas Emmaus Community and Kairos prison ministry. Today, he serves on the board of the Dallas County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and as the legal advisor for the Feed Lake Highlands ministry.

attorneys.name: Karl P. Long
attorneys.firm_name: Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Karl Long represents people who have been injured because of another's actions. His practice includes product liability, passenger bus accidents, premises liability, construction accidents, and workplace injuries. Most of these cases involve catastrophic injuries and/or claims for wrongful death. Many of Karl's cases involve automotive and tire defects, a skillset he honed while representing tire manufacturers and retailers. His experience representing defendant manufacturers provides insight into not only what evidence is necessary to prove a case, but also into understanding how these defendants think.

Karl moved to Houston in 1995 and graduated from Bellaire High School in 1997. During high school, he captained the soccer team and led it to its first District title. Karl attended college at the University of the South in Sewanee, TN and graduated with a degree in history. During college, he was admitted to the Order of the Gown.

Following college, Karl joined the Peace Corps and served in Guatemala before attending law school at South Texas College of Law Houston. He graduated from law school cum laude and in the top 10 percent of his class. Additionally, he was admitted to the Order of Lytae, was named to Dean's List numerous times and scored the highest grade in five classes: (1) Oil & Gas; (2) Secured Transactions; (3) Agency & Partnership; (4) Damages; and (5) Marital Property.

Karl clerked at a respected defense firm during law school and joined Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner as a contract attorney after passing the Bar in 2009. Karl worked as contract attorney to firm partner, Mo Aziz, until 2012. He returned to Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner in 2019, following seven years representing tire manufacturers and retailers in lawsuits stemming from automobile accidents that resulted in catastrophic injuries and deaths.

attorneys.name: Samuel Long
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Samuel Long grew up in Newnan, Georgia with three brothers and two sisters who are all military veterans. At an early age, Sam was conditioned by a community that demanded hard work, service, and sacrifice—and insisted that failure was unacceptable.

After high school, Sam attended the U.S. Naval Academy where he played Division I baseball for four years and graduated with honors. In 2011, he was commissioned in the U.S. Marine Corps and selected as an infantry officer. For the next five years, he led two rifle platoons in combat and humanitarian assistance operations before being assigned to recruiting duty. It was these experiences that compelled his desire to go to law school.

Sam quickly figured out that battle in the civilian world was conducted in the courtroom and defending corporations was not his calling. Following an eight-year career fighting for the underserved, Sam knew he wanted to become a trial lawyer so, during law school, he spent most of his free time getting prepared. Since 2018, Sam has worked with Arnold & Itkin during the summers and while he was not in class. As a non-Texan committed to becoming a Texas lawyer, he spent his last semester as a full-time law clerk in the Harris County Civil District Courts.

During law school, Sam served as an editor of the Virginia Tax Review and President of Virginia Law Families. Based on his military achievements and career commitment to service, he was selected as a 2020 Pat Tillman Scholar. Sam is an Eagle Scout, black belt, violinist, and father of two boys.

When he is not working, Sam enjoys spending time with his wife and sons. They live in Houston and are active members of Second Baptist Church.

attorneys.name: Emilio Longoria
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Emilio Longoria is a civil litigator who focuses on eminent domain proceedings and property law disputes. A native Houstonian, Longoria graduated from Strake Jesuit High School, received a Bachelor of Arts in History from Rice University, and graduated from the University of Texas School of Law with honors.

Prior to joining the firm in 2019, Longoria taught at Cristo Rey Jesuit College Preparatory, worked in the Texas Legislature, and clerked for United States District Court Judge George C. Hanks, Jr. of the Southern District of Texas. He is admitted to practice in all Texas state courts, the Southern District of Texas, the Northern District of Texas, the Eastern District of Texas, the Western District of Texas, the Federal Court of Claims and the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Longoria is an active member of several organizations in and around Texas. For example, Longoria is a member of the Texas Bar College, and he serves on the Board of Directors for the Galveston County Bar Association. Longoria is also a member of the State Bar of Texas Court Rules Committee, and he served as an advisory member for the Texas Pattern Jury Charge Committee, which focuses on oil and gas law. In his spare time, Longoria volunteers for the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo’s Parade Committee and Poultry Auction Committee.

In 2021, Longoria accepted a tenure-track faculty position with St. Mary’s University School of Law in San Antonio, Texas. As an Assistant Professor of Law, Longoria teaches a range of property law courses at St. Mary’s, including Land Use Regulation and Property Law.

attorneys.name: E. Alejandro Lopez
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in Killeen, TX
attorneys.bio:
Alejandro Lopez is a family lawyer in Killeen, TX. His practice focuses on family law cases including divorce and custody. Alejandro enjoys using his knowledge and skills to zealously advocate for his clients, especially those from historically underrepresented communities.

Originally from Mexico, Alejandro immigrated to Alice, TX when he was five. He then attended Texas A&M University at Kingsville for his undergraduate degree before being accepted into the Texas Tech School of Law. While in Law School, Alejandro was able to work in the Family Law and Housing Clinic, where he helped families under the supervision of a licensed attorney.

Alejandro was inspired to become a lawyer by the attorney that walked his father through the immigration process. He appreciated the kindness and effort that went into helping his family come to the United States, and he now wants to help other families navigate the American court system. Alejandro is most proud of the fact that all of the hard work and sacrifices made by his parents will help not only their family, but also other families like them.

After he graduated from Law School in 2022, Alejandro moved to Belton, TX. He now lives there with his Snowshoe cat, Kong. Alejandro says he often jokes that Kong is his "purr-alegal." In addition, Alejandro loves to watch soccer, specifically the Mexican National Team, Austin FC, and Arsenal FC in London, England.

attorneys.name: Lesley Lorenz
attorneys.firm_name: Lorenz & Lorenz Accident & Injury Lawyers PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lesley Lorenz is a founding partner in the Austin based firm of Lorenz & Lorenz, L.L.P. The firm limits its practice to personal injury law, with its primary focus on auto accident cases.

Lesley received her B.A. from Purdue University and her J.D. from the University of Houston Law Center where she was a recipient of the Mark Vela Scholarship, a finalist in the Hippard Mock Trial Competition and the winner of the Hofeinz Tournament of Champions. During law school Lesley clerked for Judge Mark Davidson in the 11th District Court. She began her legal career as an Assistant District Attorney in Dallas County. After gaining valuable trial experience, she went to work for a personal injury law firm in Dallas and later joined her husband in practice, forming Lorenz and Lorenz, L.L.P.

Lesley is the chairperson of the University of Texas School of Law Department of Continuing Legal Education's Car Crash Seminar. She served as co-chair in 2004 and again in 2005-2006. Since 2007, she has served as the chairperson of the planning committee. She has authored and presented papers on topics such as Rainmaking, Claims Settlement, Negotiations with Adjusters and Medical Records Analysis. Lesley was twice honored as a Rising Star Super Lawyer as published by Texas Monthly magazine.

Lesley Lorenz is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Austin Bar Association and the American Association of Justice. She is involved with the Purdue University President's Council and has served on the Board of the Saint David's Episcopal Church Day School. She is a past member of the Travis County Democratic Party's Finance Council. Lesley has attended Experience Austin and the Leadership Academy of Public Service sponsored by the Austin Area Research Organization and Leadership Austin. She recently served as the President-Elect of the Eanes Elementary Parent Teacher Organization, as a member of the Eanes ISD District Leadership Team and as Chair of the Instructional Enrichment Committee. She is currently active in Impact Austin, Saint Gabriel's Catholic School Saber Moms and CASA of Travis County.

attorneys.name: Ted R. Lorenz
attorneys.firm_name: Lorenz & Lorenz Accident & Injury Lawyers PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ted R. Lorenz is a founding partner of Lorenz & Lorenz, LLP. The firm limits its practice to personal injury law, with its primary focus on auto accident and truck accident cases.

Ted graduated with a B.A. from the University of Texas in Austin and immediately enrolled in law school at the University of Houston. Prior to entering law school, Ted developed a strong interest in helping people who were hurt by the careless and negligent acts of others. During law school Ted took many courses designed to further his interest in using the law to help those who are injured. In an effort to help develop the trial skills that are extremely important in personal injury law, Ted competed in many mock trial competitions. Ted, along with his wife and partner Lesley, were finalists in the Hippard Mock Trial Competition and won the prestigious Hofeinz Tournament of Champions.

Most recently, Ted was award to The National Trial Lawyers Association: Top 40 under 40. Membership into The National Trial Lawyers Association: Top 40 under 40 is by invitation only and is extended exclusively to those individuals who exemplify superior qualifications, trial results, and leadership as a young lawyer under the age of 40. He has also been honored in 2006, 2007, 2008, 2009 and 2010 as a Texas Rising Star. He is particularly proud of this recognition as Rising Stars are nominated and voted on by other attorneys who have personally observed them in action. Only 2.5% of the attorneys in Texas are listed as Rising Stars.

After law school Ted began his legal career as a trial attorney for a well known plaintiff's firm in Dallas, Texas. In 2001, Ted started his own law firm and was quickly joined by his wife Lesley. Early on Ted decided to concentrate his personal injury law firm on helping car wreck and truck wreck injury victims. To this day, Ted has only represented people who were hurt by the negligent and careless acts of others.

Ted R. Lorenz is a member of the State Bar of Texas, Austin Bar Association, Capital Area Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. In addition, Ted was the 2005-2007 Secretary/Treasurer for CATLA (Capital Area Trial Lawyers Association).

attorneys.name: Josefina Louis
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Veronica Garza, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Arlington, TX
attorneys.bio:
Josefina Louis earned her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from the University of Texas in Arlington in 2010. She first became interested in immigration law in 2012, through her internship at a large nonprofit in Fort Worth, Texas. Because of her tireless work and dedication to the nonprofit's DACA program, that same year she was hired on as a part-time caseworker. During this time, Mrs. Louis was studying at the Texas Wesleyan School of Law, now known as the Texas A&M School of Law, where she received her Juris Doctorate in May 2014. In November 2014, Mrs. Louis was licensed by the Supreme Court of Texas.

Before joining the Law Offices of Veronica Garza, PLLC, Mrs. Louis worked for nonprofits and private law firms. She was the Senior Attorney at a nonprofit in Houston, Texas where she provided immigration guidance to her staff and the general public through numerous Know Your Rights presentations. Mrs. Louis's immigration experience includes family-based and humanitarian cases, such as Family Petitions, Waivers of Inadmissibility and Unlawful Presence, Special Immigrant Juvenile cases, applications for Naturalization, Asylum claims, and Nunc Pro Tunc cases.

Mrs. Louis continues to be committed to immigration law, and her main goal is to provide exceptional service, honesty, and care to every case she works on. She understands the importance of family unity and is dedicated to advocate for her immigration clients by helping them navigate a very complex area of the law. Mrs. Louis is a first-generation Mexican-American, born and raised in Texas, and she is fluent in English and Spanish. She is a member of the Arlington Bar Association. In her free time, she enjoys spending time with her husband, family, and friends.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.name: Greg Love
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
The Seventh Amendment to the United States Constitution preserves the right to trial by jury. It takes courage, commitment, and resolve to protect these rights. Greg Love has successfully protected the rights of his clients before judges and juries in both state and federal courts in Texas and throughout the US, since 1999. For over two decades, Mr. Love’s practice has focused on patent litigation, commercial litigation and personal injury. Mr. Love is a member of the invitation only American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA), former President of East Texas ABOTA and National Representative of East Texas ABOTA.

Experience

Greg Love has acted as both lead and local counsel in patent cases in the Eastern District of Texas in both plaintiff and defense cases. Mr. Love has acted as lead counsel in patent cases in other district courts including New York, California, Washington, Michigan, and Florida. In addition to district court litigation, Mr. Love has acted as lead counsel in hearings before the International Trade Commission. Mr. Love has represented inventors, non-practicing entities, patent practicing plaintiffs, as well as defendants accused of infringement. With this breadth of experience, and knowledge of local rules, practices, local Courts and jury pools, Mr. Love has acted as local counsel in patent cases in the Eastern District of Texas, and in joining the firm has expanded his practice to include representation in the Western District of Texas. In commercial litigation, Mr. Love has represented small businesses and Fortune 500 companies. Achieving results regardless of venue or forum, Mr. Love has recovered tens of millions of dollars for clients in commercial litigation. Since 1999, Mr. Love has represented individuals catastrophically injured through the negligence of others including oil field injuries, commercial trucking negligence, products liability, and work place injuries.

RECENT EXEMPLARY PATENT CASES:

GreatGigz Solutions, LLC v. Healthcare Express, LLP – Greg Love negotiated an early confidential settlement of the litigation on behalf of the defendant Healthcare Express, LLP. Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd v. Verizon Communications, Inc. et. al. – Greg Love represented Huawei as local counsel, argued in multiple discovery hearings, conducted jury selection and presented Huawei’s damages expert at trial. The case settled during trial. Nanology Alpha LLC v. WITec Wissenchaftliche Instrumente und Technologie GmbH – Greg Love represented WITec as trial counsel, conducted jury selection, examined all damages related witnesses and gave closing argument, limiting the plaintiff’s damages claim from tens of millions of dollars to roughly a quarter of a million in damages. Tinnus Enterprises, LLC v. Telebrands Corporation et al – Greg Love conducted jury selection, cross-examined the plaintiff inventor and presented the defendants’ damages expert. Allergan Sales, LLC v. Sandoz, Inc. – Greg Love represented Allergan as local counsel in a Hatch-Waxman bench trial, resulting in a finding of infringement and validity in favor of Allergan.

Recent Commercial Litigation Cases:

Weimac LLC et al v. Fireman’s Fund Insurance – Greg Love is currently representing Weimac (and affiliate restaurants) in business income loss insurance claims as co-lead counsel in the Western District of Washington and the the Court of Appeals for 9th Circuit. Butler Masonry v. Morrison Construction – Greg Love represented the defendant/counter-plaintiff as lead counsel in this construction contract dispute. The parties entered into a confidential settlement prior to trial. Zeid Women’s Health Center Ltd. v. Special Health Resources for Texas Inc. et al: Greg Love represented the plaintiff as lead counsel in this complex tortious interference with business and employment contracts. The parties entered into a confidential settlement prior to trial. Corby Hall v. York Risk Services, Group, Inc – Greg Love represented the plaintiff as lead counsel in this breach of insurance agreement and bad faith litigation. The parties entered into a confidential settlement on the eve of trial.

Recent Personal Injury Cases:

Brooklyn Mershawn v. Compass Group USA et al: Greg Love represented the plaintiff as lead counsel in this catastrophic commercial trucking case. After extensive discovery, the parties entered into a confidential settlement agreement prior to trial. Greg Love acted as co-lead counsel for families who sued Apple Inc., in Texas and California seeking to hold it accountable for distracted driving deaths. (Meador v. Apple & Modisette v. Apple). The claims against Apple revolved around a patent filed by Apple in 2008 that recognized the need for smartphones to utilize a do not disturb feature while a user was driving. Following resolution of these cases, Apple implemented the do not disturb feature for users to engage while driving. Greg Love also acted as lead counsel in a distracted driving case in Indiana involving a multiple fatality school bus crash. Mr. Love represented the only surviving child in the crash. The parties entered a confidential settlement agreement prior to the filing of litigation.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Lovelace
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Burleson, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer practices general civil trial and appellate law. She also has a special emphasis in employment matters.

Jennifer has drafted numerous winning briefs, motions, and responses to various Texas Courts of Appeals as well as Petitions for Review to the Texas Supreme Court. She has practiced before the First Court of Appeals in Houston, Second Court of Appeals in Fort Worth, Fifth Court of Appeals in Dallas, Seventh Court of Appeals in Amarillo, Eleventh Court of Appeals in Eastland, Tenth Court of Appeals in Waco, and Twelfth Court of Appeals in Tyler. In her appellate practice, Jennifer has represented clients with an array of interests, including but not limited to employment, family, and probate. She has successfully represented appellate clients: in the rare situation in which the appellate court affirmed a trial court judgment that overturned a will based on a finding of undue influence, affirm a plaintiff's trial court default judgment based on the defendant's procedural defects, and affirm the property tax valuation methods employed by a taxing authority, among others.

Jennifer maintains an active civil litigation practice. She represents both plaintiffs and defendants in complex, commercial, and consumer cases in Texas state and federal courts. She has represented clients in matters related to probate and trust litigation, family disputes, breach of contract matters, real estate matters, and employment matters. Recent experience includes representing an oilfield equipment company in an international breach of warranty dispute in federal court, filing for extraordinary remedies in a case involving fraud on the court, and representing a subcontractor defendant in a case involving suit on a sworn account.

Jennifer also maintains an employment law practice. She has drafted and reviewed employee handbooks, employment agreements, and non-competition agreements. She has also represented both employers and employees in front of administrative panels such as the Wage and Hour Division of the Department of Labor, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, and the Texas Workforce Commission.

Jennifer graduated magna cum laude from the Texas Tech School of Law where she served as the Vice Chair of Mock Trial for the Board of Barristers. Before attending law school, Jennifer had the unique experience of working for several years as a human resources generalist who specialized in employee relations for a large hospital and healthcare system in West Texas and Eastern New Mexico.

Jennifer has received numerous awards for her legal work in local and statewide publications. She is active in the community and local bar associations.

attorneys.name: W. Cade Lovelace
attorneys.practice_type: Corporations Litigation Lawyers in Burleson, TX
attorneys.bio:
W. Cade Lovelace founded this law firm based with the principle that every person should receive quality, complete and aggressive legal representation. Cade represents and advises clients in almost every aspect of law that this firm handles, from large corporations in patent litigation to small businesses as to their corporate structures to families in divorces or child custody modifications. Cade has represented clients in the Texas District Courts, the Texas Appellate Courts, the Texas Supreme Court, and the U.S. District Courts of Texas.

Cade’s legal career encompasses close to 15 years. His first experience was working in a small practice in southeast Texas. He then worked for a large bankruptcy firm in Fort Worth. Cade interned with U.S. Attorney in Lubbock and worked for a multinational firm in Dallas. After graduating Magna Cum Laude and becoming a member of the Order of the Coif at Texas Tech School of Law, Cade started his law practice with a large Fort Worth firm. Following extensive litigation training with that firm, Cade and his partners created Lovelace & Killen, PLLC.

Cade’s experience in varied areas of law helps him advise his clients of multiple legal solutions.

attorneys.name: Scott Love
attorneys.practice_type: Products Liability Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Scott Love concentrates his practice in the areas of products liability, personal injury, wrongful death, mass tort litigation and class action litigation. Over the course of his career, Scott has distinguished himself as one of the leading mass tort and trial lawyers in the country. Currently, Scott is one of only a handful of lawyers in the United States to obtain multiple verdicts in pharmaceutical and medical device cases.

In addition to his active trial practice, Scott has been selected to leadership roles in numerous consumer class actions and mass tort cases, including, insurance cases, oil & gas cases and various pharmaceutical cases such as Trasylol, Paxil, Accutane, Topamax, Zoloft, and Transvaginal Mesh.

Scott was recently appointed as national counsel on the Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for the Transvaginal Mesh federal Multi-District litigation pending in West Virginia by the Honorable Judge Goodwin. Scott currently serves on the Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for the following MDLs:

In Re: American Medical Systems, Inc., Pelvic Repair Systems Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2325

In Re: C.R. Bard, Inc., Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2187

In Re: Ethicon, Inc., Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2327

In Re: Boston Scientific Corp. Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2326

Scott was also one of the leading attorneys in the national Trasylol litigation which was transferred to the Southern District of Florida. Scott was honored with the appointment of co-lead counsel of the Plaintiff's Steering Committee by the Honorable Donald Middlebrooks in May 2008. As co-lead counsel of the PSC, Scott was responsible for coordinating the overall litigation strategy which has successfully resulted in the settlement of all of the cases pending across the country.

As a trial lawyer, Scott's accomplishments speak for themselves: Most recently, Scott obtained a verdict as lead counsel on behalf of four clients who suffered injuries as a result of the Obtryx Sling System. The Obtryx sling is a device manufactured by Boston Scientific Corp. for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence. This is the largest compensatory verdict against any mesh manufacturer for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence. (Blankenship et al v. Boston Scientific Corp., WV, MDL 2326).

As lead counsel in the first Topamax birth defect case to be tried in the country, Scott obtained a verdict (Czimmer v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). After hearing the evidence in the Czimmer case, the jury deliberated for less than 40 minutes before returning their verdict. This was followed three weeks later with a verdict in the second Topamax birth defect case. (Powell v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). One week into the third trial, Janssen settled all of his firm's Topamax birth defect cases. (Brown v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). Topamax is a medication used to treat migraines and epilepsy. It has long been recognized by Janssen that Topamax could cause a wide variety of birth defects. Even though the company knew about these side effects, they failed to warn physicians and patients until the FDA forced them to change their label in 2011.

Scott, along with two colleagues, obtained a verdict in the case of Kilker v. GSK, tried in Philadelphia, PA (October 2009) for injuries sustained by their minor client in the Paxil Birth Defect Litigation.

In addition to his active trial practice, Scott regularly speaks on topics involving litigation and trial strategies and trends, including topics such as:

Products Liability

Expert Discovery

Pharmaceutical Litigation

Catastrophic Birth Injury Cases

Cross-Examination of Expert Witnesses

Scott has been recognized as one of the top 100 trial lawyers in the country by both the National Trial Lawyers Association and Americas Top 100 Attorneys. He is a member in the American Board of Trial Advocates (Houston Chapter). Scott is rated "AV-Preeminent" by Martindale Hubble, the highest peer review rating for legal ability and ethical standards. Since 2006, Scott has been recognized every year by his peers as a Super Lawyer (A Thomson Reuters service). This honor is given to less than 5% of all attorneys in the State of Texas.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Scott Love concentrates his practice in the areas of products liability, personal injury, wrongful death, mass tort litigation and class action litigation. Over the course of his career, Scott has distinguished himself as one of the leading mass tort and trial lawyers in the country. Currently, Scott is one of only a handful of lawyers in the United States to obtain multiple verdicts in pharmaceutical and medical device cases.

In addition to his active trial practice, Scott has been selected to leadership roles in numerous consumer class actions and mass tort cases, including, insurance cases, oil & gas cases and various pharmaceutical cases such as Trasylol, Paxil, Accutane, Topamax, Zoloft, and Transvaginal Mesh.

Scott was recently appointed as national counsel on the Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for the Transvaginal Mesh federal Multi-District litigation pending in West Virginia by the Honorable Judge Goodwin. Scott currently serves on the Plaintiffs' Steering Committee for the following MDLs:

In Re: American Medical Systems, Inc., Pelvic Repair Systems Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2325

In Re: C.R. Bard, Inc., Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2187

In Re: Ethicon, Inc., Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2327

In Re: Boston Scientific Corp. Pelvic Repair System Products Liability Litigation, MDL No. 2326

Scott was also one of the leading attorneys in the national Trasylol litigation which was transferred to the Southern District of Florida. Scott was honored with the appointment of co-lead counsel of the Plaintiff's Steering Committee by the Honorable Donald Middlebrooks in May 2008. As co-lead counsel of the PSC, Scott was responsible for coordinating the overall litigation strategy which has successfully resulted in the settlement of all of the cases pending across the country.

As a trial lawyer, Scott's accomplishments speak for themselves: Most recently, Scott obtained a verdict as lead counsel on behalf of four clients who suffered injuries as a result of the Obtryx Sling System. The Obtryx sling is a device manufactured by Boston Scientific Corp. for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence. This is the largest compensatory verdict against any mesh manufacturer for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence. (Blankenship et al v. Boston Scientific Corp., WV, MDL 2326).

As lead counsel in the first Topamax birth defect case to be tried in the country, Scott obtained a verdict (Czimmer v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). After hearing the evidence in the Czimmer case, the jury deliberated for less than 40 minutes before returning their verdict. This was followed three weeks later with a verdict in the second Topamax birth defect case. (Powell v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). One week into the third trial, Janssen settled all of his firm's Topamax birth defect cases. (Brown v. Janssen, Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas). Topamax is a medication used to treat migraines and epilepsy. It has long been recognized by Janssen that Topamax could cause a wide variety of birth defects. Even though the company knew about these side effects, they failed to warn physicians and patients until the FDA forced them to change their label in 2011.

Scott, along with two colleagues, obtained a verdict in the case of Kilker v. GSK, tried in Philadelphia, PA (October 2009) for injuries sustained by their minor client in the Paxil Birth Defect Litigation.

In addition to his active trial practice, Scott regularly speaks on topics involving litigation and trial strategies and trends, including topics such as:

Products Liability

Expert Discovery

Pharmaceutical Litigation

Catastrophic Birth Injury Cases

Cross-Examination of Expert Witnesses

Scott has been recognized as one of the top 100 trial lawyers in the country by both the National Trial Lawyers Association and Americas Top 100 Attorneys. He is a member in the American Board of Trial Advocates (Houston Chapter). Scott is rated "AV-Preeminent" by Martindale Hubble, the highest peer review rating for legal ability and ethical standards. Since 2006, Scott has been recognized every year by his peers as a Super Lawyer (A Thomson Reuters service). This honor is given to less than 5% of all attorneys in the State of Texas.

attorneys.name: Melissa Eleanor Loveless
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Melissa E. Loveless PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Melissa Loveless is an experienced and motivated family law attorney assisting clients in divorce, custody, child support, visitation, prenuptial agreements, adoption, paternity cases and other family law cases. She is driven to provide her clients with the best possible options and outcomes for their family's individual needs. A true Texan, she was born, raised, and educated in Houston, Texas. She obtained her B.A. from the University of St. Thomas and her J.D. from South Texas College of Law in December of 2005. Melissa is also a Certified Family Law Mediator and believes in developing creative solutions for your specific situation. Having 20 years in the legal profession she is prepared to provide the legal advice, support, and representation you need to get the best possible outcome for you and your family in one of the most difficult times in your life.

Many times the best outcome is one which saves the emotional and financial toll of litigating a lengthy legal battle. All attempts are made to settle a matter prior to going to the judge, but if an amicable resolution is not possible, Melissa will work diligently to represent your interests to the conclusion of the case.

If you are need of estate planning, Melissa can prepare a complete package consisting of your will, powers of attorney (both statutory and medical), guardianship documents for both yourself and your minor children, if applicable, and other necessary documents.

attorneys.name: Jose Humberto Rios Lozano
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in McAllen, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jose Humberto Rios Lozano is an attorney licensed to practice throughout the Republic of Mexico and in 2009, received a Foreign Legal Consultant Certification from the State Bar of Texas. Humberto is one of only 5 Mexican lawyers to hold such a certification in Texas. He graduated from the Universidad Autonoma de Nuevo Leon Facultad de Derechos y Ciencias Juridicas in 1994. Humberto received additional certifications from the University in International Law in 1995 and in Criminal Law in 1999.

Humberto is a member of the United States - Mexico Bar Association. He has served as President of the Tamaulipas Chapter of the Colegio Juridico Nacional and as a delegate for the State of Tampaulipas to the Association of Litigation. Humberto has been a member of Consejo Nacional de Abogados as well as the Barra de Abogados de la Riberena.

Humberto has been an invited speaker at CLE seminars, including as a panelist and participant in a mock mediation titled Cross Border Products Liability - Personal Injury Case Study at the 10th Annual Conference of the Texas - Mexico Bar Association (now the United States - Mexico Bar Association) held at the University of Texas School of Law in Austin, Texas in 2003. Humberto was a speaker on cross-border litigation at the Texas Association of Defense Counsel's Annual Conference held in Cozumel, Mexico in the summer of 2005. And, Humberto authored a paper titled The Importance of the Investigation Previa to Cross Border Litigation in Death and Personal Injury Cases presented at a continuing legal education seminar hosted by the State Bar of Texas on South Padre Island, Texas in May 2006.

Humberto has rendered expert reports on Mexican law for litigation pending in the United States. He has also testified by affidavit and in open courts as an expert on Mexican Law.

attorneys.name: Shannon E. Loyd
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Recovery Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Shannon E. Loyd is board certified in Consumer and Commercial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and has extensive experience in litigating cases involving insurance recovery, bad faith, and commercial construction defects.

Shannon represents commercial businesses and property owners in disputes with their insurance companies, including property damage and business interruption, as well as defense and indemnity if a business is sued. She also represents policyholders in agent liability cases. With a substantial knowledge of coverage issues and a willingness and capability to take a case to trial, she consistently obtains very favorable results for her clients.

During law school, Shannon was a member of Phi Delta Phi, the National Mock Trial Team.

Shannon is licensed by the Supreme Court of Texas (2004) and the Northern, Eastern and Western Districts of Texas. She is also a member of the Houston Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Defense Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Frank N. Luccia was admitted to the Texas Bar in 1986. Born in Cherry Hill, New Jersey on May 10, 1961, Mr. Luccia received his B.S. in Finance, magna cum laude, from St. Louis University in 1983 and his J.D. from the University of Houston Law Center in 1996. In addition to his admission to practice in state court, Mr. Luccia is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

Mr. Luccia developed the firm's Continuing Quality Assurance Plan which helps the firm members provide the highest quality legal product, service and reports. Mr. Luccia remains responsible for its administration. He is also the firm's managing partner. Mr. Luccia is a member of the Houston Bar Association, Greater Houston Society forHealth Care Risk Managment, State Bar of Texas, American Bar Association, and Defense Research Institute.

In 1999, Mr. Luccia became an adjunct professor of law at the University of Houston Law Center in the health law section. He speaks frequently at hospital in-service programs and continuing legal education seminars. He has contributed to several risk management news letters and other health care related journals. A certified mediator since 1999, Mr. Luccia has experience in mediation of personal injury, wrongful death and healthcare liability disputes.

attorneys.name: Derrel Luce
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Derrel Luce was born and grew up in Lake Jackson, Texas. He graduated from Brazoswood High in 1971. Derrel was named a National Merit Scholar for which he earned an academic scholarship and also accepted a football scholarship to Baylor University.

He attended Baylor University and graduated in 1975 with a bachelor of arts in Geology. From 1972 through 1974, Derrel was on the varsity football team at Baylor University, and was named captain and most valuable player by his teammates for the 1974 SWC champion Bears. Derrel received recognition as a consensus all Southwest Conference and All-American linebacker following the 1974 season.

Then from 1975 through 1980, Derrel was a linebacker for the Baltimore Colts, the Minnesota Vikings ( N.F.L.P.A. Player Representative), and the Detroit Lions of the National Football League.

During the off-seasons while playing for the National Football League, he returned to Baylor University to study law and graduated from Baylor Law School in May of 1980. He has been living and practicing law in Waco for over 28 years.

Derrel and his wife Debbie have two married sons. Whitney and Brandon Luce and Beran and Barrett Luce all reside in Dallas, Texas. Derrel has devoted much of his time to coaching youth sports while Debbie has served as a volunteer for numerous local organizations. Debbie is a member of the Waco Independent School District Board of Trustees.

Derrel is an avid outdoorsman, enjoying wildlife photography, saltwater fishing, and all types of physical fitness activities. He also is a private and instrument rated pilot, a hobby he uses both recreationally and vocationally.

attorneys.bio:
Jost was born and raised in Houston, Texas, and is a sixth-generation Texan through his mother. He is also fluent in Spanish and holds German dual citizenship through his father.

Jost is a trial attorney licensed in Texas and New York. He represents plaintiffs and defendants in business and complex commercial disputes, including breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty (directors and officers), fraud, business divorces, professional negligence, deceptive trade practices, and employment disputes. He focuses a significant portion of his practice representing landowner plaintiffs in oil & gas disputes against operators as well as Latin American clients in business disputes in the U.S. He has also represented clients in catastrophic personal injury, property damage, and medical malpractice lawsuits. Outside of his legal practice, Jost is proud to serve on the board of an international electrical engineering/manufacturing company headquartered in Austria. He enjoys spending time with his wife and their dog, traveling, hiking and camping, and competing in recreational soccer.

attorneys.name: Jason Luong
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Jason Luong PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jason Luong has a general civil litigation and appellate practice. Mr. Luong’s experience involves representing and advising a variety of clients from Fortune 100 companies to individuals in commercial disputes, including securities fraud claims, class actions, and professional malpractice actions. In 2004, a leading Houston magazine named Mr. Luong one of Houston’s “Lawyers on the Fast Track” for business litigation.

Mr. Luong received his B.A., cum laude, from Rice University in 1997 and graduated with honors from the University of Texas School of Law in 2000. While in law school, he was a member of the Texas Law Review and also served as an intern to the Honorable Lynn N. Hughes, United States District Judge for the Southern District of Texas, and the Honorable Harriet O’Neill, Justice for the Supreme Court of Texas. Upon graduation from law school he served as law clerk to the Honorable Royal Furgeson, United States District Judge for the Western District of Texas. Mr. Luong’s publications include Note, Forcing Restraint: The Case for Amending the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, 78 Texas L. Rev.1181 (2000), which received the Texas Law Review’s Best Constitutional Law Note Award (1999) and Best Published Note Award (2000). Mr. Luong has authored and co-authored several articles, including Innovative Thinking in Jury Innovations, 18 Texas State Bar Litig. Sec. Rep. 15 (1999).

Mr. Luong is a member of the Asian-American Bar Association of Houston, the American Bar Association, the Houston Bar Association, and the Houston Young Lawyers Association. Mr. Luong currently serves on the Houston steering committee for Friends of Teach For America where for the past two years he has chaired Teach For America’s annual school supply drive. In 2003, Mr. Luong was selected to participate in the Houston Young Lawyers Association’s inaugural Leadership Academy.

attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Richard Lybarger Divorce & Family Law
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce & Family Law Lawyers in SugarLand, TX
attorneys.bio:
Providing Legal Services in All Areas of Family Law-

Houston and Fort Bend County divorce and family law attorney Richard Lybarger is a seasoned family lawyer.

He offers clients the benefit of his years of experience, thorough preparation, and attention to detail in all matters related to divorce and family law, including child support, child custody and visitation, alimony, contested divorce, uncontested divorce, asset division, collaborative law, and more.

Attorney Richard Lybarger serves clients throughout the Houston metro area - including Fort Bend County, Brazoria County, and Waller County - out of his offices in Katy, TX.

A Single Parent Who Became a Family Law Attorney-

Licensed in 1986, Houston divorce lawyer Richard Lybarger was a single parent when he attended law school. Having been through a divorce and other family law matters himself, he understands how frustrating and frightening it can be, and he understands the anxieties and fears people experience during the process.

Attorney Lybarger believes there is no substitute for experience and the ability to understand and appreciate what a client needs as they go through the process.

He does whatever is necessary within the bounds of values and ethics to meet client goals in a timely, honest, and practical way.

attorneys.name: Jose M. Luzarraga
attorneys.practice_type: Products, Catastrophic & Industrial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jose Luzarraga focuses his nationwide product liability litigation practice on claims involving business litigation, toxic torts such as asbestos and benzene, personal injury defense, warranty, and breach of contract. He has tried to verdict several multi-million dollar cases in a variety of trial and appellate courts as well as alternative dispute resolution forums. His clients include some of the country's most well-known automotive manufacturers, airline companies, energy corporations, real estate developers, appraisers and insurers.

Clients rely on Jose for his extensive first-chair trial experience, where has taken to verdict several high-profile commercial litigation cases and has represented clients in prosecuting and defending claims involving contract disputes, fraud cases, insurance coverage issues and intellectual property disputes. Jose has also obtained verdicts and summary judgments in multiple SUV rollover cases, seat belt and wrongful death claims, as well as catastrophic injury claims.

From 1994-1995, Jose served as briefing attorney to Justice Craig Enoch of the Supreme Court of Texas and formerly served as the Articles Editor for the Columbia Journal of Transnational Law.

attorneys.name: Jaime M. Lynn
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Round Rock, TX
attorneys.bio:
Advocating for those who have been wronged is what drove Jaime M. Lynn to become a lawyer. Jaime has been practicing law in Texas for more than two decades and has helped countless victims of personal injuries recover millions in damages. As a Round Rock personal injury lawyer, Jaime is a man who believes in justice.

Experience on your side

Jaime is an Austin native who was fortunate to be able to remain in the area. After graduating from Texas State University, Jaime went on to St. Mary's University School of Law. While in law school, Jaime spent one summer at the St. Mary's Institute on World Legal Problems in Innsbruck, Austria. After graduation, he spent several years with Austin-area law firms including a two-year stint with the Office of the Attorney General of Texas before joining The Carlson Law Firm.

Forever committed to his fight for justice, Jaime attended Trial Lawyer's College in Dubois Wyoming. As a partner for The Carlson Law Firm, Jaime is proud to be helping and fighting for clients. He is licensed to practice in the State of Texas, United States District Court-Western District of Texas and the United States District Court-Southern District of Texas.

Coupled with his experience and education, Jaime's dedication to justice and compassion for his clients is what makes him a top personal injury attorney. Clients injured in a tractor-trailer and motor-vehicle collisions, on the job, or on the premises of a business or other party can rest assured that Jaime will do all that he can to ensure proper resolution.

Among his many success stories, one of Jaime's most recent recoveries for a client was $7.4 million jury verdict in the case Claxton v. Better Logistics Trucking.

Jaime has been recognized by The Carlson Law Firm on several occasions for his dedication to his clients. He was awarded Carlson Law Firm Litigator of the Year and was also awarded the Carlson Law Firm Jared Stenbeg Award for Attorney of the Year. Additionally, he has been recognized as a Texas Super Lawyer (2016-present).

When he's not practicing law, Jaime is heavily involved in his community. He is currently on the Board of Directors of Capitol Credit Union and Meredith's Mission for Melanoma. Additionally, he donates his time to the Benevolent & Protective Order of Elks and assists in the Longhorn Corvette Club's Make A Wish Foundation fundraiser. Jaime has also held several positions with the Star of Texas Fair & Rodeo, including the former president, ambassador's committee and scholarship committee.

attorneys.name: Michael P. Lyons
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Michael Lyons is one of the founding partners of Lyons & Simmons and concentrates his practice on representing plaintiffs in catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death cases. Lyons has a national reputation for achieving outstanding results for his clients by displaying a mastery of the facts and law while utilizing creativity, tenacity, and cutting-edge technology.

Over the past 25+ years of practice, Lyons has tried cases to juries, judges, and arbitrators throughout the state of Texas and all over the country. Since 2023 alone, Lyons has obtained verdicts, awards, and settlements totaling more than a billion dollars on behalf of his clients in catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death matters.

Lyons has extensive trial experience in cases involving catastrophic personal injuries, wrongful death, product liability, business disputes, construction defects, and professional liability. Lyons’ cases are as diverse and extensive as his approach to his cases. He has handled cases involving: brain and spinal cord injuries, electrocutions, aviation disasters involving helicopters and airplanes, trucking accidents, construction site accidents, industrial accidents, motor vehicle products liability, pharmaceutical, and medical device products liability, large business disputes involving breach of contract, fraud, and breach of fiduciary duties, medical malpractice, high profile contract disputes involving college football coaches and celebrities, and fire and explosion cases.

Lyons recently secured a $109.5 million jury verdict against CPS Energy for its failure to properly maintain its gas system, leading to a natural gas explosion and fire. In 2024, Lyons served as a member of the trial team who secured a $37.5 million verdict for the estate of a man killed when an Oncor electrical service truck hit a truck disabled on the side of I-635. In 2023, Lyons was part of a trial team that secured an $860 Million jury verdict for the family of a victim killed when a tower crane collapsed and fell onto an apartment building in Dallas, Texas. The incident and the trial was a national news story. In 2022, Lyons was named to the Plaintiffs’ Executive Committee in In Re: Astroworld Festival Litigation related to the tragic events involving the deaths of 10 people at the Astroworld Festival Concert in 2021. Lyons is among a handful of attorneys selected for the Plaintiffs’ leadership of this mass casualty litigation. In December of 2022, Lyons obtained a $10.1 million verdict in an emergency room delay case that was streamed live by Courthouse View Network. It was tabbed by CVN as one of the “Top 10 Most Impressive Plaintiff Verdicts of 2022."

Lyons has obtained exceptional results for clients in just the recent past:

$860 Million – Wrongful Death, Construction Disaster

$109.5 Million – Burn Injury, Fire / Gas Explosion

$70 Million - Wrongful Death, Negligent Security/Operations

$60 Million - Wrongful Death, Worksite Explosion

$6 Million – Wrongful Death, Negligent Entrustment

$4 Million – Mild Brain Injury, Trucking Accident

$3.5 Million – Wrongful Death, Workplace Forklift Accident

$2.5 Million – Breach of Contract, College Coach Contract Buyout

$2 Million – Breach of Contract, Commercial Management Agreement

Lyons has earned the respect of his peers through the relentless pursuit of justice for his clients. In 2021, Lyons was honored by the Dallas Trial Lawyers’ Association with the John Howie Award, which is given annually for the “courageous pursuit of justice in the face of adversity”. Lyons was given the award, in part, for taking a very difficult liability case to trial in one of the most conservative venues in Texas that involved the deaths of three African American children. The verdict is believed to be the largest in history for a wrongful death personal injury case in Midland County, Texas. Lyons has been recognized by The National Law Journal as one of the top lawyers in the country as a “Trailblazer” award recipient. He has regularly appeared on Thomson Reuters Texas Super Lawyers listing (2005, 2008-2023), including being selected among the Top 100 attorneys in Dallas/Fort Worth (2018-2023) and the Top 100 attorneys in the state of Texas (2021-2022). He was recognized on the 2024 Lawdragon 500 Leading Lawyers in America listing, an honor reserved for the top 500 attorneys in the country. He also has earned Lawdragon 500 Leading Plaintiff Consumer Lawyers (2020-2023) and Best Lawyers in America (2019-2023) recognition. He was honored as a “Best Lawyer in Dallas” by D Magazine in 2005, 2011, 2013, 2015-2017, and 2019-2023 and is one of only a select few attorneys to earn recognition for both personal injury and commercial litigation. Lyons has been recognized as a member of the Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forums, was named a Lifetime Achievement member of America’s Top 100 Attorneys for Texas, and was named among America’s Top 100 High Stakes Litigators in North Texas for 2017-2024. He has attained an AV® Preeminent™ peer-review rating from Martindale-Hubbell consecutively for 15 years, signifying the highest level of professional excellence based upon peer-review evaluation from lawyers and judges who have observed his legal skill and ethical standards.

In addition to pursuing outstanding results on behalf of clients, Lyons has invested significant time in the service of his community as a leader within the Dallas Bar Association and as a leader in his community. In 2008 Lyons was recognized by Dallas CBS affiliate KTVT Channel 11 as a "Texan with Character" for his philanthropic work in the Dallas – Fort Worth Metroplex with children who were victims of abuse or neglect. In 2010, he was elected as a Fellow of the Dallas Bar Foundation, and in 2015, Lyons became a Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation.

Lyons joined the Board of Directors for the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association and the Texas Trial Lawyers Association in 2022. In 2025, Lyons became the Vice President of Finance for the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and presently serves in a leadership role on the Executive Committee of that organization.

Lyons has earned the respect of his peers through the relentless pursuit of justice for his clients. In 2021, Lyons was honored by the Dallas Trial Lawyers’ Association with the John Howie Award, which is given annually for the “courageous pursuit of justice in the face of adversity”. Lyons was given the award, in part, for taking a very difficult liability case to trial in one of the most conservative venues in Texas that involved the deaths of three African American children. The verdict is believed to be the largest in history for a wrongful death personal injury case in Midland County, Texas. Lyons has been recognized by The National Law Journal as one of the top lawyers in the country as a “Trailblazer” award recipient. He has regularly appeared on Thomson Reuters Texas Super Lawyers listing (2005, 2008-2023), including being selected among the Top 100 attorneys in Dallas/Fort Worth (2018-2023) and the Top 100 attorneys in the state of Texas (2021-2022). He was recognized on the 2024 Lawdragon 500 Leading Lawyers in America listing, an honor reserved for the top 500 attorneys in the country. He also has earned Lawdragon 500 Leading Plaintiff Consumer Lawyers (2020-2023) and Best Lawyers in America (2019-2023) recognition. He was honored as a “Best Lawyer in Dallas” by D Magazine in 2005, 2011, 2013, 2015-2017, and 2019-2023 and is one of only a select few attorneys to earn recognition for both personal injury and commercial litigation. Lyons has been recognized as a member of the Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forums, was named a Lifetime Achievement member of America’s Top 100 Attorneys for Texas, and was named among America’s Top 100 High Stakes Litigators in North Texas for 2017-2024. He has attained an AV® Preeminent™ peer-review rating from Martindale-Hubbell consecutively for 15 years, signifying the highest level of professional excellence based upon peer-review evaluation from lawyers and judges who have observed his legal skill and ethical standards.

In addition to pursuing outstanding results on behalf of clients, Lyons has invested significant time in the service of his community as a leader within the Dallas Bar Association and as a leader in his community. In 2008 Lyons was recognized by Dallas CBS affiliate KTVT Channel 11 as a "Texan with Character" for his philanthropic work in the Dallas – Fort Worth Metroplex with children who were victims of abuse or neglect. In 2010, he was elected as a Fellow of the Dallas Bar Foundation, and in 2015, Lyons became a Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation.

Lyons joined the Board of Directors for the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association and the Texas Trial Lawyers Association in 2022. In 2025, Lyons became the Vice President of Finance for the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and presently serves in a leadership role on the Executive Committee of that organization.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nathaniel Mack is the CEO and founder of The Law Offices of Nathaniel Mack III, PLLC d/b/a Mack Injury Attorneys, with offices in San Antonio, Austin, Houston, and Dallas. His firm represents clients nationwide in complex litigation matters related to catastrophic accidents, intentional torts, environmental torts, and mass torts. Mack has been a part of national trial teams that have tried cases all over the United States.

He attained his bachelor’s degree from Baylor University with a major in Political Science and his Juris Doctorate from Saint Louis University.

He is admitted to practice before each United States District Court in the State of Texas, as well as the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals located in New Orleans, Louisiana. He has been selected in 2025 to be a Super Lawyer. This distinction is only awarded to 2.5% of Texas attorneys.

Over the course of his career Mack has handled products liability, medical malpractice and personal injury cases through trial. In his own practice, he has continued to maintain a docket of products liability, medical malpractice and personal injury cases, but he has also added several mass tort campaigns to his firm’s docket. These include: 1) Representing residents of Houston, Texas in a toxic tort case against a railroad company (link); 2) Representing firefighters nationwide in the aqueous film-forming foam litigation (link); 3) Representing women nationwide in the chemical hair straightener litigation (link); 4) Representing government entities in the case involving the overpricing of insulin (link).

He has also remained engaged in the legal community. In 2023, he served on the Bexar County Judicial Selection Committee to nominate the next sitting Judge for the recently expanded Probate Division.

He has been recognized as a Top 40 Under 40 Civil Plaintiffs Lawyer by The National Trial Lawyers. He has also been featured in multiple publications including Forbes, US Weekly, LA Weekly, Life&Style, International Business Times, and Men’s Journal among others. He is an active member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association where he was a presenter at the 2023 conference in Houston, Texas.

Mack currently serves on the board of directors for Ferrari Kid. Through his nonprofit, Mack To The Future, he is able to support communities he serves through philanthropy.

He is admitted to practice before each United States District Court in the State of Texas, as well as the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals located in New Orleans, Louisiana. He has been selected in 2025 to be a Super Lawyer. This distinction is only awarded to 2.5% of Texas attorneys.

Over the course of his career Mack has handled products liability, medical malpractice and personal injury cases through trial. In his own practice, he has continued to maintain a docket of products liability, medical malpractice and personal injury cases, but he has also added several mass tort campaigns to his firm’s docket. These include: 1) Representing residents of Houston, Texas in a toxic tort case against a railroad company (link); 2) Representing firefighters nationwide in the aqueous film-forming foam litigation (link); 3) Representing women nationwide in the chemical hair straightener litigation (link); 4) Representing government entities in the case involving the overpricing of insulin (link).

He has also remained engaged in the legal community. In 2023, he served on the Bexar County Judicial Selection Committee to nominate the next sitting Judge for the recently expanded Probate Division.

He has been recognized as a Top 40 Under 40 Civil Plaintiffs Lawyer by The National Trial Lawyers. He has also been featured in multiple publications including Forbes, US Weekly, LA Weekly, Life&Style, International Business Times, and Men’s Journal among others. He is an active member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association where he was a presenter at the 2023 conference in Houston, Texas.

Mack currently serves on the board of directors for Ferrari Kid. Through his nonprofit, Mack To The Future, he is able to support communities he serves through philanthropy.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Kyle, TX
attorneys.bio:
Having worked as a top litigator in large firms, Nick gained the knowledge and experience to handle complex and large cases. He also saw firsthand the way that high-volume firms treat individuals as numbers on a spreadsheet. Knowing that there is a better way, Nick has developed the Madsen Law Office to provide the pinnacle of professional service to his clients. As a prior teacher and officer in the US Army, Nick Madsen has dedicated his life to helping others and to try and make the world around him a better place. He believes that people deserve to be treated with care and respect no matter the size or value of their case.

Madsen Law Office’s mission is to dedicate intensely to every case, fiercely negotiate for the client, leave nothing on the table, and ensure the client is kept up to date each step of the way. Unlike many larger firms, Madsen Law Office will not leave your case file sitting on a shelf until the last possible minute a phone call must be made or a court date set. You may be surprised how many firms take this approach. Nick values unwavering commitment and works to ensure things move as quickly as possible so you get paid fast. Insurance companies will stall, stall, stall, and Nick is experienced with all their tactics. Nick Madsen gets results.

Licensed in both State and Federal courts in Texas.

attorneys.name: Christopher D. Mahfouz
attorneys.firm_name: Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris Mahfouz tirelessly works on behalf of people who have been injured and had their lives turned upside down by the careless actions of others. For Chris, practicing law is not merely a job. Instead, it is a calling to stand in the gap for those who—through no fault of their own—have been wrongfully injured by the carelessness or negligence of another party and need help in piecing their lives back together.

Chris earned his B.A., magna cum laude, as a University Scholar from Baylor University. He then attended Baylor University School of Law, where he graduated cum laude with a concentration in general civil litigation. During law school, Chris was the champion of Baylor’s Matt “Mad Dog” Dawson Mock Trial Competition and a member of the Order of the Barristers. He also successfully competed across the nation on the law school’s advocacy teams.

Chris’ practice focuses primarily on cases involving catastrophic personal injury, workplace injuries, industrial accidents and explosions, maritime and offshore injuries, trucking and motor vehicle wrecks, defective products, premises liability, and wrongful death. A native of a Southeast Texas refining town, he is passionate about representing injured workers.

Chris has successfully represented numerous clients on a variety of personal injury and complex commercial litigation matters in both state and federal courts. He is also active in the legal community, previously serving as vice president and treasurer of his local young lawyers association.

As a two-time Baylor alumnus, Chris is an avid fan of the Baylor Bears and travels to as many games as he can.
