attorneys.name: Hannah D. Salinas
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Frisco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Hannah D. Salinas is an Associate Attorney at Grinke Stewart Law. Hannah always knew she wanted to practice family law and let nothing stand in her way of achieving that dream. Having been a child of divorce, Hannah brings a unique perspective that allows her to zealously advocate for her clients with an empathetic approach.

Hannah is from Prosper, Texas. She attended Texas A&M University in College Station, Texas where she graduated magna cum laude with a Bachelor of Science in Sociology in 2020. Hannah received her Doctor of Jurisprudence from St. Mary’s University School of Law in San Antonio, Texas in 2023.

While in law school, Hannah earned a spot on the prestigious dean’s list for her academic performance. Hannah also spent three semesters assisting low-income clients as a Student Attorney for the St. Mary’s Center for Legal and Social Justice Family Law Clinic. During her time in the Family Law Clinic, Hannah served as a court-appointed Amicus Attorney and advocated for her clients in various family law disputes, including divorce and suits affecting the parent-child relationship. Hannah was awarded the Francisco Leos Award and Pro Bono and Public Service Award due to her hard work and dedication to the Family Law Clinic. Hannah also received two mediation certifications from St. Mary’s for completing additional training in both Mediation and Family Law Mediation. In addition to her academic recognitions, Hannah was elected to serve the law school student body as President of the Family Law Association and Senator of the Student Bar Association. Hannah was also elected as Vice President of the Juvenile Jurisprudence Association, a peer court program that focuses on reformative justice for underprivileged teens through constructive sentencing.

Hannah furthered her professional experience during law school where she interned for the Comal County District Attorney’s Office in the Child Protective Services division and served as a judicial intern for the 296th Judicial District Court in Collin County. Hannah also interned with Grinke Stewart Law and is thrilled to be back with us as an Associate Attorney.

In her free time, you can find Hannah cheering on her favorite sports teams or binge watching her favorite reality TV shows. Hannah is also newly married and enjoys making new memories with her husband and their four-legged fur baby, Ellie.

attorneys.name: Anne Sampson
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Anne Sampson-Gbenjo, a graduate of the Western Michigan University Thomas M. Cooley Law School, has diverse litigation experience in both the state, federal trial, and appellate courts of approximately 30 years.

Proficient in complex, multi-district white-collar litigation, Anne has been consistent with litigating cases involving Employment, Age, Race, and Sex Discrimination; Sexual Harassment; and Medical Malpractice.

Licensed to practice in four states, Maryland, Washington, D.C., Georgia, and Texas, Anne, a founding member of The Gbenjo Law Group, parades an extensive litigation competence with practice covering the State, Federal, and Appellate courts.

Anne’s overzealous representation made her a familiar face in the court districts, especially federal judicial districts, where she had handled very high-profile cases. For instance, in the Bell v. Patrick R. Donahoe (Postmaster General, US Postal Service), Anne went after the Federal Government to get justice for a Caucasian female, who was subjected to a hostile work environment shortly after marrying an African American male. Also, in Henderson v. Norman Y. Mineta, Anne tackled the United States Department of Transportation to their knees to get justice for a lesbian who was denied a promotion because of her sexual orientation.

For approximately 30 years, Anne has remarkably excelled in tough courtroom battles, daring hard-to-tackle discrimination cases. In Evans v. Anthony Principi (Department of Veterans Affairs), Anne represented this plaintiff, a Caucasian male nurse subjected to a hostile work environment in an all-female environment. Her client walked away with a victory.

The governments are not the only courtroom victims of Anne’s litigation prowess. Major insurance companies are not finding it easy either. She is a familiar name to virtually most adjusters who knows that she litigates most of her PERSONAL INJURY cases. Very recently, Anne sued Walmart over employment discrimination, hostile work environment, and retaliation perpetrated against her client. She led a team of GLG lawyers in the high-profile case, battled the giant retail firm and its legal representatives to the ground, and walked away with a huge settlement.

Anne’s courtroom personality and aggressive style of representation earn her the respect of judges, clients, and jurors. Indeed, she had earned commendations from Judges and opposing colleagues complimenting her courtroom engagement prowess.

attorneys.name: Joseph E. Sampson
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Joseph "Joey" Sampson enjoys helping businesses and individuals make tough decisions, resolve difficult problems, and succeed. He prioritizes building trust with others and relishes the lawyer-counselor role, seeking to provide advice to his clients to efficiently resolve issues, achieve their goals, and avoid litigation. But sometimes litigation is necessary, and since joining McCathern in 2007 and later becoming a partner with the firm, Joey has garnered extensive experience and developed a successful practice litigating matters for plaintiffs and defendants.

Joey handles cases in all areas of business and civil litigation, including insurance coverage issues, D&O liability claims, E&O claims, contract disputes, construction claims, labor and employment claims, and catastrophic personal injury and premise liability claims. Joey also consults companies regarding risk management and insurance, employment issues, and general business and contract matters. Texas Super Lawyers recognized Joey as a Rising Star in both 2017 and 2018. Each year, no more than 2.5 percent of the lawyers in Texas are selected by the research team at Super Lawyers to receive this honor. D Magazine also included Joey on its "Best Lawyers in Dallas 2018" list.

A native of Atlanta, Georgia, Joey attended and graduated magna cum laude from the University of Georgia in 2001, where he earned his Bachelor of Business Administration degree, majoring in Risk Management and Insurance. Terry College's risk management-insurance program at the University of Georgia has long been recognized by insurance professionals and U.S. News & World Report rankings as one of the top in the country. Joey's strong risk management and insurance background allows him to bring a unique perspective to both consulting businesses and his litigation practice.

Joey earned his law degree from Baylor University School of Law in 2006. Baylor is consistently ranked as one of the top trial advocacy schools in the nation. While attending Baylor, Joey became a member of Baylor's Order of Barristers, and he also completed an externship with the McLennan County District Attorney's Office. Joey was licensed to practice in the State of Texas in November 2006. In addition to being licensed to practice in all Texas state courts, he is also licensed to practice in the United States District Courts for the Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Jose I. Sanchez
attorneys.practice_type: Immigration & Naturalization Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jose I. Sanchez is a founding member of the Jose Sanchez Law Firm, PC, in Longview, Texas. Since 2001, Jose has championed the rights of immigrants and those hurt in accidents, and has sued the government for violations of immigrants’ rights. He is a trial lawyer with numerous million-dollar personal injury verdicts including deaths and severe injury cases involving auto and workplace accidents. Being an immigrant himself, Jose had organized and led marches in East Texas in 2006 with over 4,000 in attendance, a part of the nationwide movement that was reported on by the New York Times.

Jose attended the Texas A&M University in College Station, Texas, on an academic scholarship where he was the President of the Latino students. After graduating with a Bachelor’s degree, he earned his Juris Doctorate from the Texas Tech Law School in Lubbock, Texas. Later, Jose received his Master’s in Public Administration degree from the Harvard Kennedy School of Government.

Jose was also selected to be one of twenty Texas attorneys to be chosen to participate in the prestigious 2010-2011 Texas State Bar Leadership Program, and had won the best leader award from the group. Along with numerous million dollar wins for his personal injury clients, along with his colleagues, Jose had the top verdict in Texas for a workplace accident of $2.5 million in 2019.

Jose regularly appears on television and travels throughout the United States fighting and marching for an immigration reform and meeting with important national leaders. He is sought out by local media, businesses, and groups to speak at various events and programs. For the last 17 years in East Texas, Jose has maintained a weekly radio show in Spanish in which he discusses current news and politics that affect the Latino community and legal advice.

An immigrant from Mexico City, Mexico, Jose moved with his family to the United States at age 5, and was raised in Longview, Texas. He enjoys running, working out, sports, and traveling within the United States and internationally.

attorneys.name: M. Cristina Sanchez
attorneys.practice_type: Water Contamination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Cristina Sanchez had originally planned on going to medical school, but her work at a small plaintiffs' firm after college inspired her to instead pursue a career in law. Cristina worked for the same firm while in law school and joined Baron & Budd in 2005. "I came to Baron & Budd because I enjoy doing plaintiffs' work and wanted to continue doing so. It is also such a great firm that I knew I would learn a lot by working with such experienced and respected attorneys."

Cristina is an attorney with the firm's water contamination litigation group, representing municipalities, water providers, and private well owners seeking clean-up costs for polluted drinking water supplies. She puts her strong advocacy skills as well as her undergraduate degree in biological sciences and minor in chemistry to good use in her practice. Cristina was the National Champion and won the Best Brief Award and Second Place Oralist in the 2002 Hispanic National Bar Association Moot Court Competition. She also won first place in the Southern Methodist University Client Counseling Competition in 2001 and served as Chief Counsel for SMU's Criminal Defense Legal Clinic in 2002.

Outside of her law practice, Cristina has served as the 2005 Region XII Deputy of the Hispanic National Bar Association and Co-Chair for the 2005 Hispanic National Bar Association Moot Court Competition and Midyear Conference. She also serves on the Aid to the Homeless Committee of the Dallas Young Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Gus A. Saper
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
I am Gus Saper, a fifth generation Houstonian and a third generation Texas A&M “Aggie”. I have devoted my over 50 year career as a trial lawyer dedicated to criminal defense work. However, over the years as the business world has become more regulated, I have found that my practice overlaps with that of a commercial trial lawyer. Often, civil litigation involving the SEC, CFTC and other government regulatory agencies is the precursor to criminal charges. Being able to handle these quasi-civil/criminal investigations is essential to a good outcome for the client. I pride myself in being able to do both. In addition, I represent those accused in both state and federal court with drug offenses, bank fraud, Medicare/Medicaid fraud, DWI/DUI, and various violent criminal offenses such as murder, robbery, and assault.

I am admitted to practice law in Texas, but I have and continue to take cases around the country. My practice has taken me to St. Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands, California, Washington, as far west as Alaska, as well as England, Canada and Mexico.

I encourage you to contact my office and schedule a free evaluation of your case.

attorneys.name: Paul Austin Sartin
attorneys.practice_type: Probate Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Paul A. Sartin was raised in Dallas, Texas, where he graduated from St. Mark's School of Texas. Upon graduation from high school, Paul attended The University of Texas at Austin, where he majored and graduated from the Plan II Honors Program. Upon graduating from UT, he returned to Dallas to follow in the footsteps of his father, Peter A.T. Sartin, and his mother, Linda D. Sartin, and become an attorney, and enrolled at the Southern Methodist University - Dedman School of Law.

Upon graduating from SMU in 2001, Paul was employed as an associate at a commercial litigation and commercial bankruptcy law firm in Dallas. Since that time, he has always practiced in the commercial and civil litigation areas. Paul has represented businesses of every kind and size, insurance companies, financial institutions, and individuals in a wide variety of litigation matters. Paul has primarily represented parties on the plaintiffs' side of the docket in state and federal courts across Texas. Paul's primary practice in the commercial litigation arena involves commercial creditors' rights and commercial collections. Paul represents businesses as both secured and unsecured creditors in claims involving commercial debts, commercial loans, outstanding accounts receivables, breaches of contract, and sworn accounts.

Paul also maintains a very busy practice in the probate, wills and trusts, and estate planning areas in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. In his probate practice, Paul has represented individuals and families in all manner of probate matters, from cases where a Last Will and Testament exists, to those where one does not, holographic Wills, and lost Wills. Paul has represented estates of every size and character, and has a unique perspective as an attorney in this area when advising estate executors and administrators, as Paul has served as an executor and trustee for estates and trusts involving his own loved ones.

Paul is a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Dallas Bar Association, the DBA sections on Business Litigation and Probate and Estate Planning, and a Texas Exes Life Member.

attorneys.practice_type: Military Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dan is a Senior Counsel with Tully Rinckey PLLC’s Austin, Texas office where he focuses his practice on all aspects of military law and veteran services.

Dan, a U.S. military veteran himself, has experience with appellate decisions, reviewing complex legal and medical cases, and representing clients who need assistance obtaining their VA benefits. Prior to joining Tully Rinckey, Dan worked as a Veterans Law Attorney for the Department of Veterans Affairs. Prior to that role, he also served in the U.S. Army JAG Corps, where he focused his practice on healthcare law, general administrative law, labor and ethics law. Near the end of his term, he served as the Deputy General Counsel for the U.S. Army Installation Management Command and held a responsibility for the operation of over 75 Army Installations worldwide, and managed the day-to-day operations of an office with a staff of 18 employees. He retired in 2021, after more than 24 years of service.

Dan also brings experience in litigation, mediation, and national security law.

Dan received his Juris Doctorate Degree from the University of Minnesota School of Law. He is well traveled, having lived in several different countries, and can speak Spanish at a full professional capacity.

attorneys.name: Stacy Sawyer
attorneys.firm_name: Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Stacy is a zealous advocate, dedicated to her clients and their well-being. While attending South Texas College of Law in Houston, Stacy joined Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers as a law clerk, and quickly became a valuable member of the team. Stacy worked alongside, and trained under, the partners and senior members of the firm in all areas and aspects of family law. After graduating from law school and being admitted to the State Bar of Texas, Stacy seamlessly transitioned from law clerk to associate attorney in the firm. Stacy has a passion for helping families in transition, so family law is a natural fit for her. With a combination of knowledge, dedication and compassion, Stacy works hard to guide her clients through the emotional rigors of family law proceedings, to help them achieve a desirable outcome.

Stacy takes pride in being diligent, skilled and prepared. She distinguishes herself from other family law attorneys because she is in continual contact with her clients, to discuss goals and create a game plan. This keeps matters on course and allows Stacy to prepare aggressively for hearings, arguments and negotiations.

Stacy is a native of the Houston area, having been raised in Pearland. She is a graduate of Texas A&M University – College Station with a degree in Finance, which is of benefit to her clients when navigating complex property and asset divisions. Hard work defines Stacy. While at Texas A&M, Stacy worked numerous jobs, including as a server in the food service industry and a paralegal at a family law firm. She credits her time working while she pursued her education, for her vast communication skills. She prides herself not only on being a successful advocate and solutions oriented, but also being attentive to her clients emotional needs, and a good listener. Stacy is confident, yet compassionate, relatable, and down to earth.

Stacy graduated cum laude from South Texas College of Law and ranked in the Top 15% academically in her law school class. She was editor of the Law Review. Though her formal legal education is over, Stacy considers herself a continual student of the law. She seeks every opportunity to gain further knowledge of the practice of family law and all of its nuisances. When Stacy is not advocating for her clients or working to perfect her craft, she enjoys spending time with her family, reading, and watching ALL sports, but dear to her heart are her beloved Texas A&M Aggies and our Houston Astros.

attorneys.name: Rebekah Meeks Schement Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Rebekah Meeks Schement is an attorney licensed by the Supreme Court of Texas. She is licensed to practice in all Texas Courts, the United States Federal District Court for the Western District of Texas and the United States Federal Court of Claims. Rebekah grew up in San Antonio and attended San Antonio Christian School. Rebekah received her BA in Organizational Development from The University of the Incarnate Word. She earned her law degree from South Texas College of Law in Houston and was licensed to practice law in 2005. Rebekah was happy to return to San Antonio after law school to start her legal career as she trained under the late Kenneth P. Courtright. Rebekah was a co-owner of a boutique law firm in San Antonio from 2005 through 2019 before joining The Voeller Law Firm.

Rebekah focuses her practice on Wills, Trusts, Probate, Guardianship and Estate Planning. Rebekah was named a Texas Rising Star in the area of Estate Planning and Probate for 2009 by Super Lawyers Magazine.

Rebekah is a certified mediator and regularly makes appearances on behalf of her clients in the Bexar County, Guadalupe County and Comal County courts for probate matters.

Rebekah is passionate about offering high quality legal services. One of the highlights of Rebekah’s profession is developing strong relationships with her clients by supporting and counseling them through the aspects of their estate planning and through the probate and administrative process after losing a loved one.

When Rebekah is not practicing law, she enjoys running, hiking, traveling and being active with her four energetic children.

She believes in treating people who are dealing with difficult situations as well as happy events such as adoptions and prenups with dignity, compassion, and respect while providing excellent representation and personal service.

She has chosen to focus on family law because it allows her to combine her love for law, justice, and working closely with people.

attorneys.name: Maxey M. Scherr
attorneys.practice_type: Truck Accidents Lawyers in El Paso, TX
attorneys.bio:
Since 2009, Maxey Scherr has litigated countless jury trials resulting in multi-figure verdicts and settlements across the board. In 2022, she founded Scherr Law Firm. Her areas of expertise include truck crashes, traumatic brain injuries, wrongful death claims, product liability in truck crashes and non-obvious third-party defendants. Ms. Scherr is licensed in Texas, New Mexico and Illinois and graduated from Texas Tech School of Law. After she earned her bachelor’s degree in psychology from the University of Massachusetts-Boston with magna cum laude honors, Ms. Scherr undertook postgraduate work in Neuroscience at Harvard University. Board Certified in Truck Accident Law by the National Board of Trial Advocates and Personal Injury Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Ms. Scherr has extensive experience in her specialty, undergone rigorous examinations, is supported by the reviews of peers and judges, and demonstrates an unwavering commitment to the advocacy of her clients and justice.

Ms. Scherr currently serves as the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys (ATAA) Board Secretary and is on the Board of Regents after formerly serving as Board Parliamentarian and Women’s Caucus Co-Chair. At the American Association for Justice’s Trucking Litigation Group, Ms. Scherr is on the Executive Board, is the Education Co-Chair, and manages the Broker Database. For AAJ’s Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation Group, Ms. Scherr serves as the Brain Injury Association of America Liaison and Diversity & Inclusion Committee Chair while still maintaining an active role in the Women’s Caucus. Ms. Scherr sits on the board of the Rules of Evidence Committee for the State Bar of Texas. Widely recognized as an authority in her field, Ms. Scherr frequently presents to fellow attorneys and publishes thought-provoking articles discussing key trucking and brain injury issues. Ever the passionate advocate, Ms. Scherr can be found lobbying for heightened trucking safety and finding ways and means to increase awareness concerning brain injury matters.

In her hometown of El Paso, Ms. Scherr is a Downtown Management District Board Member and Women’s Rights Commission Member. In 2023, Ms. Scherr launched the Scherr Law Firm Scholarship and Internship Program for local high school students considering a career in the legal field. Every summer, her firm also offers a clerkship to promising students pursuing a degree in the legal field.

Most recently, Ms. Scherr was honored by TopVerdict.com after successfully obtaining TWO Top Five Verdicts and TWO Top Five Settlements in the State of Texas. In the larger United States, she also received recognition for a Top 10 Truck Accident Settlement, a Top 20 Truck Accident Verdict and TWO Top 20 Occupational Injury Verdicts. She is also a co-founder of the All-Women’s Trial Lawyer Association and Of The 8, Inc. and spearheads several other noteworthy programs. Known for her integrity and work ethic, Ms. Scherr is honored to be a part of the Melvin M. Belli Society and the International Society of Barristers.

After she earned her bachelor’s degree in psychology from the University of Massachusetts-Boston with magna cum laude honors, Ms. Scherr undertook postgraduate work in Neuroscience at Harvard University. Board Certified in Truck Accident Law by the National Board of Trial Advocates and Personal Injury Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Ms. Scherr has extensive experience in her specialty, undergone rigorous examinations, is supported by the reviews of peers and judges, and demonstrates an unwavering commitment to the advocacy of her clients and justice.

Ms. Scherr currently serves as the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys (ATAA) Board Secretary and is on the Board of Regents after formerly serving as Board Parliamentarian and Women’s Caucus Co-Chair. At the American Association for Justice’s Trucking Litigation Group, Ms. Scherr is on the Executive Board, is the Education Co-Chair, and manages the Broker Database. For AAJ’s Traumatic Brain Injury Litigation Group, Ms. Scherr serves as the Brain Injury Association of America Liaison and Diversity & Inclusion Committee Chair while still maintaining an active role in the Women’s Caucus. Ms. Scherr sits on the board of the Rules of Evidence Committee for the State Bar of Texas. Widely recognized as an authority in her field, Ms. Scherr frequently presents to fellow attorneys and publishes thought-provoking articles discussing key trucking and brain injury issues. Ever the passionate advocate, Ms. Scherr can be found lobbying for heightened trucking safety and finding ways and means to increase awareness concerning brain injury matters.

In her hometown of El Paso, Ms. Scherr is a Downtown Management District Board Member and Women’s Rights Commission Member. In 2023, Ms. Scherr launched the Scherr Law Firm Scholarship and Internship Program for local high school students considering a career in the legal field. Every summer, her firm also offers a clerkship to promising students pursuing a degree in the legal field.

Most recently, Ms. Scherr was honored by TopVerdict.com after successfully obtaining TWO Top Five Verdicts and TWO Top Five Settlements in the State of Texas. In the larger United States, she also received recognition for a Top 10 Truck Accident Settlement, a Top 20 Truck Accident Verdict and TWO Top 20 Occupational Injury Verdicts. She is also a co-founder of the All-Women’s Trial Lawyer Association and Of The 8, Inc. and spearheads several other noteworthy programs. Known for her integrity and work ethic, Ms. Scherr is honored to be a part of the Melvin M. Belli Society and the International Society of Barristers.

Ultimately, this was unsuccessful for the defense and case concluded in a confidential large settlement.

attorneys.name: Claire Schindler
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
As a Louisiana native, Claire began her secondary education at Louisiana State University, where she majored in political science and was a member of Delta Delta Delta sorority. Claire’s passion for advocacy was solidified when she was hit by a drunk driver during her senior year of college. The incident sparked her interest in personal injury law, and she vowed to help others in her situation.

Upon graduation, Claire continued her education at Louisiana State University’s Paul M. Hebert Law Center where she received the Chancellor’s Scholarship and was a Dean’s List student. Claire earned the CALI Excellence Award in Legal Research and Writing, an award given to the top student in the class.

After her first year of law school, Claire studied abroad in Lyon, France, studying comparative law and gaining experience from a U.S. District Judge, Chief Judge Shelly Dick for the Middle District of Louisiana.

While at LSU Law, Claire participated in various trial competitions, including the Vinson Elkins week-long trial advocacy program where she learned from experienced trial attorneys and judges.

Prior to joining Arnold & Itkin, Claire worked for several talented trial attorneys and externed for U.S. District Magistrate Judge Richard L. Bourgeois, Jr. for the Middle District of Louisiana.

Claire graduated with a Juris Doctorate, a degree in comparative law, and a graduate certificate in energy law and policy. After moving to Houston, Claire joined Arnold & Itkin as a law clerk and was hired as an attorney upon passing the bar exam. In Claire’s short time with our firm, she has participated in hundreds of depositions and has tried 7 cases to verdict—most during a global pandemic. She has obtained nearly $60,000,000.00 in settlements for her clients over the last four years. She also was part of the trial team on a plant explosion case against Exxon Mobil in Harris County with Kurt Arnold, which resulted in a favorable settlement after nearly three weeks of trial. Claire has received several awards and is recognized amongst her peers as a formidable opponent. Claire helps our team fight for the future that clients deserve by refusing to back down, even when the other side won’t cooperate.

In her free time, she enjoys traveling, spending time with her family and friends, and new golden retriever puppy. As a two-time LSU alumnus, Claire is an avid LSU football fan and attends as many games as possible (Geaux Tigers!).

attorneys.name: Eric C. Schmalbach
attorneys.practice_type: Oil and Gas Title Examination Lawyers in Midland, TX
attorneys.bio:
Eric is a shareholder in the firms Oil, Gas and Energy Resources Section. He is Board Certified in Oil, Gas and Mineral Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization.

His practice primarily consists of advising exploration and development companies with their upstream operations in Texas. Eric provides counsel to oil and gas companies of all sizes relating primarily to transactional related matters. Prior to his experience as an attorney, Eric worked as an independent landman, where he performed due diligence, title research, and lease acquisition in Oklahoma and Texas.

AREAS OF CONCENTRATION

Oil and Gas Title Examination

Eric spends a significant portion of his time on oil and gas title examination. His title examination work involves all types of opinions, including drilling title opinions, division order title opinions, right-of-way opinions, and acquisition title opinions. Title opinions may be based on abstract examination or done by "stand-up" examination in the county clerk's office.

Oil and Gas Transactional Work

Eric also spends a portion of his time counseling oil and gas companies in negotiating and documenting oil and gas transactions. He prepares many different types of purchase and sale agreements, assignments, leases, seismic option agreements, farmout agreements, participation agreements, joint operating agreements, and other documents relating to exploration and development of oil and gas reserves. He assists clients in curative work, and drafts stipulation of interests and cross-conveyances, deeds, royalty assignments, ratifications, and other relevant documents, and conducts mineral receivership proceedings. In addition, he also counsels clients in development and operations of producing properties, including unit formation and maintenance, leasing matters, and surface use.

attorneys.name: Walter J. Schouten Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Licensed in 2014 but working in the field of family law since 2009, Walter J. Schouten has worked with, for, and against some of the best family law attorneys in the Houston area on complex family law issues at both the trial court level and appellate level. Walter’s desire to work with the best is driven by a results-oriented approach adopted as early as law school: in 2013, he graduated summa cum laude from South Texas College of Law, higher than over 90% of his graduating class, earning the highest grade in multiple courses along the way, all while working as a law clerk at a boutique family law firm in Houston.

Since then, he has continued this path by achieving victories for his clients, who benefit from his practical, level-headed, and results-driven approach. Representative experience includes:

Obtaining primary custody for a mother after a lengthy period of having no access to the child due to false allegations of abuse;

Convincing a court of appeals to reverse a termination judgment against a father;

Convincing a court of appeals to affirm a six-figure interim attorney fee award in a child custody case;

Obtaining primary custody for a father in a lengthy and highly contentious custody battle where the mother made numerous attempts to conceal evidence;

Getting a court to allow a mother to move with her child to a location beyond the standard geographical area that courts impose in the vast majority of cases—generally a very difficult feat.

Walter brings this track record, and the approach that built it, to Toombs Imel & Associates, making him a valuable asset to the firm’s clients.

Board Certified Attorney. Walter received his JD from South Texas School of Law Houston in 2013 with highest honor, summa cum laude. Walter attended the University of Houston, at which he also received a B.A. with honor, cum laude, in 2010. He is board certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization.

attorneys.name: Alan H Schreiber
attorneys.firm_name: Alan H. Schreiber, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Round Rock, TX
attorneys.bio:
In 1969, I received my Doctorate of Jurisprudence from the Indiana School of Law in Bloomington.

From 1970 to 1976, I served as the Assistant State Attorney or Prosecutor in Broward County, Florida. During this time I tried over 100 cases, both misdemeanor and felony.

From 1976 to 2005, I served eight consecutive terms in office (with three contested political campaigns) as the Elected Public Defender in Broward County, Florida. I supervised a staff of 270 employees, which included 110 attorneys. I managed a $12 million budget and personally tried 22 murder cases.

From 2005 to 2008, I worked in my part-time solo private law practice in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

In 2008, I a conducted class action document review for the Texas law firm Nix, Patterson and Roach.

In 2009, I began my private law practice in the city of Round Rock Texas, while continuing to maintain offices in Florida.

Over the course of four decades, I have been personally involved in many high-pressure, high-stakes cases, especially the 22 murder cases, an unprecedented number in the realm of a typical attorney's career, which might involve one or several at the most.

It is this level of experience that I bring to my current practice in Round Rock TX and the greater Austin area, including Georgetown, Cedar Park, and all surrounding communities.

I thank you for visiting my Web Site and encourage you to contact me if I can be of service to you.

David is proud to join the cohesive team of attorneys at FVF. His years of experience have made him a client-centered attorney, eager to help victims navigate the legal world surrounding personal injury.

In his free time, David enjoys traveling, playing video games, watching sports, and all things outdoors with his wife, Sam, and their Boston Terrier, Maisie. They love indulging in all the music and cuisine that Austin has to offer.

attorneys.name: Andrew Whiteley Schuster
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy and Collections Lawyers in Corpus Christi, TX
attorneys.bio:
Andrew was born and raised in Corpus Christi, Texas. Andrew earned a Bachelor of Arts in Economics in 2008 from the University of Texas at Austin. He worked in the oil and gas field as a landman before attending law school at the Texas Tech University School of Law, from which he graduated in 2012.

Andrew began his legal career in Corpus Christi, Texas as an oil and gas attorney. In 2015, he left private practice to work for Nueces County. Andrew began his time with the County at the District Attorney’s Office as an Assistant District Attorney. He earned court room experience prosecuting misdemeanor and felony level cases. Later, he moved to the County Attorney’s Office, where he advised the Commissioners Court and other County departments on legal and regulatory issues. In addition, he represented the County in Child Protective Services cases and represented citizens of Nueces County applying for protective orders. Since 2018, Andrew has assisted clients in defense litigation, creditors in collection matters, and other complex civil litigation.

Andrew joined ALBM Law Firm in 2021, and is excited to be working as part of the firm's trial and bankruptcy/collection teams.

Andrew and his wife, Jacquelyn, who is also a native of Corpus Christi, enjoy traveling and playing tennis.

attorneys.name: JB Schwartz
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
JB Schwartz has built a reputation as a results-driven litigator, trusted adviser, and laser-focused negotiator. He has extensive litigation experience including multiple jury trials brought to verdict. One of his federal court trials resulted in a jury award of over $31 million. JB has represented oil operating companies, municipal school districts, tech startups, mortgage lending institutions, electrical cooperatives, credit card services providers, bankruptcy services providers, restaurateurs, art galleries, and other businesses and individuals in the Dallas-Fort Worth area and across the country. And, importantly, JB has represented multiple clients with family law needs-everything from divorces to custody disputes to enforcement actions and contempt actions to complicated community property estate issues. JB's extensive business litigation experience means that you won't need to hire a team of lawyers if your divorce has complicated business issues attached to it.

JB is licensed to practice law in Texas, the Fifth Circuit, the Eighth Circuit, all Texas federal district and bankruptcy courts, and the District of Columbia. He practices the following areas of law:

Family law, divorce, and custody litigation

Business and commercial litigation

Non-competition and non-solicitation agreements (non-competes) and related litigation

Contract negotiation and formation

Results matter. For 25 years, JB has built a track record of achieving positive outcomes for his clients. Here are a few:

JB was part of a two-man team that received a unanimous jury verdict in a five-week trial in Houston federal court. They represented an oil operating company against its insurer for breach of contract and violations of the Texas Prompt Payment of Claims Act. JB conducted voir dire, examined witnesses, and drafted multiple trial and post-trial motions and briefs. The oil operating company received $25.4 million in damages and $6.25 million in attorneys' fees and costs after appeals to the Fifth Circuit were exhausted.

JB represented a private school that had been damaged by severe flooding caused by a utility company's negligence. After JB filed suit, the utility company agreed to pay the school hundreds of thousands of dollars in damages.

JB was part of a two-man team who tried a divorce case on behalf of the wife, in which the judge ordered that the husband's company be fully awarded to the wife.

JB represented a father arrested while driving for drug possession and driving with an open container of alcohol while one of his children was in the car with the father. After a trial, in which the mother was attempting to severely limit the father's access to his children, the Court found in the father's favor and ordered a framework going forward that allowed the father to regain his custody rights.

JB represented an ex-wife in a contempt and enforcement action against her ex-husband for failing to pay his portion of their child's college loans. After a trial, the Court found in the ex-wife's favor, held the ex-husband in contempt, and ordered the ex-husband to get current on his loan payments and pay the ex-wife's attorneys' fees.

JB represented a new business owner who was about to be sued by her former employer for breach of a non-compete and non-solicitation agreement. JB filed suit first on her behalf and obtained a temporary restraining order preventing her employer from enforcing the non-compete and non-solicitation agreements. After intensely litigating the case, the employer walked away and agreed that the non-compete and non-solicitation agreements were unenforceable and dismissed all claims for damages.

JB obtained a dismissal for a client who had been sued in a bankruptcy adversary proceeding for violations of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA). JB then successfully briefed and argued this case on appeal to the 8th Circuit B.A.P., which ruled in favor of his client.

JB litigated a multi-million dollar tort, bankruptcy, and adversary proceeding in the state and federal courts of New York and the Delaware bankruptcy court, saving his client tens of millions of dollars sought in a clawback action.

JB defended a restaurateur in a breach of contract lawsuit resulting in all claims against his client being dismissed at no cost.

JB obtained a dismissal with prejudice for his client under the Texas Anti-SLAPP law. His client had been wrongly sued for defamation, and this was a total vindication of his client's rights.

JB obtained a termination of a client's proposed debarment by the Defense Logistics Agency in Fort Belvoir, Virginia.

JB's client had been sued in Texas and an injunction taken against him, even though the client lived and conducted business in Tennessee. JB had the entire case against his client, including the injunction, dismissed with prejudice.

JB convinced a Texas federal judge to sanction opposing counsel approximately $9,000 for wrongfully removing a state court case to federal court.

JB obtained a six-figure settlement for a woman injured in a slip-and-fall in Dallas County, Texas.

JB represented a doctor wrongly sued by a law firm for tortious interference with a contract. JB was able to get the case against the doctor dismissed with prejudice by virtue of a motion for summary judgment.

JB secured a six-figure settlement for a client whose home was constantly and severely flooded by an adjacent apartment complex.

Throughout the course of his legal career, JB has achieved considerable success advocating on behalf of plaintiff and defendant clients alike with their serious, pressing, and complex legal issues. Along with handling numerous jury trials, he has conducted many appeals along with innumerable negotiations and mediations. No matter the issues his clients are facing, JB delivers highly personalized representation at all turns while aggressively pursuing the favorable outcomes his clients expect and deserve as efficiently and cost-effectively as possible. Through his practice, JB Schwartz PLLC, JB has served as counsel on a number of high-stakes, complex cases involving tens of millions of dollars in damages, and he has helped save his defendant clients substantial money through favorable judgments at trial and during appeal or by having their cases dismissed altogether.

A 1993 cum laude graduate of Columbia University, JB obtained his law degree from the University of Texas School of Law in 1997.

attorneys.name: David R. Scoggins
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
David Scoggins was born in Dallas, Texas and has been a lifelong Texan. He graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Government in 1976 and thereafter graduated from Texas Tech University School of Law with a Doctor of Jurisprudence degree. He immediately obtained his license to practice law from The Supreme Court of The State of Texas and shortly thereafter was licensed in the Federal Courts of the United States.

In 1981, David commenced the practice of law in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and has resolved over 6,000 cases. He has represented citizens accused in Federal Courts in Texas, Oklahoma, Arkansas, Louisiana and Tennessee, typically on drug conspiracy and fraud cases. David has also tried hundreds of jury trials in Felony and Misdemeanor courts in Texas. He has most often appeared at court in Dallas, Collin (McKinney) and Tarrant Counties (Fort Worth) with a significant docket in Denton, Rockwall, and Kaufman counties. David has also been persuaded by clients to represent them in distant counties for significant cases such as murder, intoxication manslaughter, organized crime, health care fraud and drug conspiracy prosecutions.

David is often retained by other attorneys as criminal jury trial lead or second chair counsel. He holds the highest rating that can be given to an attorney by Martindale-Hubbell which has rated attorneys nationwide for over one hundred years for their legal expertise and professional stature. He has an AV Preeminent® rating, which identifies an attorney with very high to preeminent legal ability and reflects expertise, experience, integrity, and overall professional excellence. This rating is an indication of David's highest professional and ethical standards and he is very pleased to be so regarded. He is also pleased to be rated Superb by AVVO.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Past Master of East Dallas Lodge 1200, A.F. & A.M. and former member of the Grand Lodge Jurisprudence Committee

attorneys.name: Patrick R. Scott
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Conroe, TX
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from law school, Patrick worked for a large Fort Worth defense firm representing clients in insurance litigation matters. Since 2011, he has been representing those who have been injured by the negligence of others. The types of cases Patrick has handled inlcude catastrophic injury, wrongful death, dog bites, trucking and car wrecks. Patrick has tried numberous personal injury cases to verdict.

He is licensed to practice law in all state courts in Texas, Louisiana, and Oklahoma. He is also licensed in all federal courts in Texas and in the Western District of Oklahoma. Patrick is a graduate of Baylor University School of Law where he served as Editor-in-Chief of the Baylor Law Review. While in law school, Patrick was selected to the Order of Barristers, the Texas Administrative Law Moot Court Team, and was an Octa-Finalist in Baylor's Moot Court competition. He previously served as an intern to the Honorable Calvin Botley of the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, as an intern with the Texas State Bar Rules of Evidence Committee and on the Executive Board of the National Conference of Law Reviews. Before law school, Patrick received a B.A. summa cum laude in Political Science from the University of Houston Honors College. While there, he was awarded multiple academic scholarships and awards.

Patrick was raised in Natchitoches, Louisiana. After high school, he enlisted in the United States Marine Corps as an Intelligence Analyst. In his initial Marine Corps training, Patrick was recognized as an Honor Graduate of the Navy and Marine Corps Intelligence Training Center. During his four year tour of duty in the Marines, he served overseas in various countries and capacities. For his service, he received a Naval Achievement Medal as well as several commendations.

Since 2014, Patrick has been named to the National Trial Lawyers Top 40 under 40. He is a member of the American Legion Post 198 and has served as a volunteer attorney with Texas Lawyers for Texas Veterans. Patrick and his wife reside in Conroe, Texas.

attorneys.name: Ethan Scroggins
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ethan focuses his practice on achieving practical, results-driven solutions for families, emphasizing preparation, clear communication, and a tailored strategy. He strives to reach settlements when possible, while remaining fully prepared to litigate when necessary. Clients value his steady demeanor, problem-solving ability, and commitment to guiding them through difficult transitions with professionalism and care.

Before joining Bollier Ciccone Stinson LLP, Ethan practiced at a boutique family law firm in Dallas known for aggressively pursuing cases and fighting for clients in the courtroom. In that role, he represented clients in divorces, premarital agreements, modifications, enforcements, and custody disputes, and appeared at temporary orders hearings, protective order hearings, mediations, depositions, and final trials. His courtroom experience—combined with his analytical mindset and detail-oriented approach—provides a strong foundation for thoughtful strategy development and effective client advocacy.

Ethan earned his J.D. in 2023 from Baylor University School of Law, an institution known for producing hardworking and courtroom-ready lawyers. During his time at Baylor Law, he was a member of the Baylor Barrister Society, competed on multiple mock trial teams, was a semifinalist in the Trials and Tribulations Mock Trial Competition, and was recognized on the Dean’s List. Prior to law school, Ethan graduated summa cum laude from Barrett, The Honors College at Arizona State University, with a Bachelor of Science in Business Data Analytics, earning the New American University Scholar – President’s Award.

Ethan is dedicated to serving families both inside and outside the courtroom. He has volunteered as a Crisis Counselor with the Crisis Text Line and is a member of the Tarrant County Family Law Bar Association.

Before joining Bollier Ciccone Stinson LLP, Ethan practiced family law at a boutique firm in Dallas, where he represented clients in divorces, custody matters, modifications, and other family law disputes. Prior to that role, he developed strong litigation and advocacy skills as a law clerk and through his internship with the Bexar County Criminal District Attorney’s Office. These experiences provided him with a solid foundation in courtroom preparation, strategy, and client-focused advocacy.

attorneys.name: Kala Sellers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kala has seen the inside of the courtroom more than most lawyers twice her age—and her results show it. In addition to courtroom advocacy, Kala prides herself on her ability to understand the larger picture of cases, considering all perspectives to best fight for the results her clients need. She’s methodical with her research and briefing, working diligently to achieve more than her clients might’ve thought possible.

This approach has allowed Kala to recover extraordinary settlements, including:

$46.5 million for injured plant workers

$40 million for injured Jones Act seamen

$35.5 million for a fatal motor vehicle accident

$14.5 million for an explosion survivor

$12.5 million for an electrocution

$8 million for injured motorists

$5.5 million for injured oil rig worker

$4.35 million for injured Jones Act seaman

Kala’s case experience includes a full array of personal injury catastrophes. She has represented survivors burned in explosions, injured in commercial vehicle wrecks, and permanently harmed while working offshore, as well as all types of industrial accidents. She has also worked extensively on mass pharmaceutical cases involving harmful drugs injuring innocent victims across the country.

Before becoming a trial lawyer, Kala showed her capacity for hard work and ambition. She grew up in Houston before relocating to North Carolina and enrolling at Duke University for her undergraduate studies. After excelling in political science and pre-law courses, Kala received a scholarship to Baylor Law School.

Kala graduated from Baylor Law School as a five-time Dean’s List student. During law school, she joined the ABA Labor Law Mock Trial Team, the AAJ National Mock Trial Team, and the NCTC Mock Trial Team. Her mock trial career reached its zenith when she was a semifinalist in the Baylor Top Gun Competition, an intra-scholastic mock trial tournament involving all third-year Practice Court students.

After law school, Kala sharpened her litigation skills at a small Houston firm that handled various personal injury cases in state and federal court. From there, she joined Arnold & Itkin, where her ambition and passion for advocacy found a natural home.

Her practice focuses primarily on matters involving catastrophic personal injury, offshore accidents, and large commercial vehicle accidents. She is licensed to practice in Louisiana and Texas but handles cases across the United States. She has been recognized as a Super Lawyers® Rising Star™ multiple years in a row.

Since joining the firm, Kala has married her loving and understanding husband and has expanded her family with two young boys. She enjoys spending her free time being a mother, which can sometimes be just as challenging as tackling trial, in her opinion.

attorneys.name: David Kenneth Sergi
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in San Marcos, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Sergi brings his unique back ground to the practice of law in San Marcos. He was born in Hamburg Germany where his parents where opera singers. His schooling included stints at the International Schools as well as British military schools. After he moved to Texas with his parents he attended Anderson High School in Austin and graduated from Allen Military Academy in Bryan. He thereafter graduated from Texas A and M university and South Texas College of Law.

His legal experience combines the honor of having served as a Law Clerk to a Federal Judge as well as having practiced with two of the largest and most prestigious law firms in the Country. He has also worked overseas representing major clients in Australia and served on the trial team of a defendant at the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia in The Hague as well as attending arguments for one of his clients at the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

He has established a practice in San Marcos, which combines his courtroom expertise in the areas of commercial and criminal litigation along with his passion for family law as well as his commitment to represent business interests and developers in the Hays County area.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Law Lawyers in Cedar Park, TX
attorneys.bio:
C. Matthew Shanks attended Texas A&M University and graduated Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history. Following graduation, Matt attended Texas Tech School of Law. While in law school Matt received a Jurisprudence Award in his legal writing course and was selected to work as a teaching assistant for his legal writing professor. In addition to his course work during law school, Matt also clerked for a private law firm and volunteered his time as a certified mediator at Lubbock’s Dispute Resolution Center.

After graduation, Matt began his legal career as an Assistant County Attorney with the Williamson County Attorney’s Office. As an Assistant County Attorney Matt practiced in front of each of the Williamson County Courts and handled cases involving family law, protective orders, and criminal law. In June of 2005, Matt left the Williamson County Attorney’s Office to found the Law Office of C. Matthew Shanks. Matt focuses his law practice on criminal law and juvenile law matters.

Matt also served as a member of the Board of Directors for the Williamson County Bar Association for seven years and is a Past President of the Williamson County Bar Association. Since 2014 Matt has also served as a member of the Board of Directors for the Lawyer Referral Service of Central Texas and is currently serving as its Chairman. Additionally, Matt is involved in his community and served as the President of his homeowner's association from 2007 until 2012.

Howard Shapiro has been serving the North Dallas and Collin County area for more than 40 years now. attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bedford, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Lori Shannon focuses her practice on family law, representing clients out of the Bailey & Galyen offices in Bedford, Texas. Originally from Sweetwater, Texas, Lori graduated from Texas Tech University, in Lubbock, earning her bachelor's degree in advertising. She then worked in television and radio before returning to school, completing her juris doctor at the Texas Tech School of Law.

Upon graduation and admission to the Texas State Bar, Lori honed her trial skills as a city prosecutor. An Assistant Attorney General in Texas for 23 years, she has extensive experience in matters related to both paternity establishment and exclusion, as well as the establishment, modification, and enforcement of child support and medical support. Her practice experience also includes employment law, criminal law, and general civil law. She has also served as a managing attorney for the Office of the Attorney General of Texas.

Lori handles all matters and concerns related to divorce and family law, including custody and child support matters. She is a strong and proven advocate in all types of hearings and proceedings, including mediation, discovery, and trial. Known and respected for her strong and effective communication skills, Lori is a zealous advocate for her clients.

attorneys.name: Kriti Sharma
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Frisco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kriti Sharma is a Senior Trial Attorney at Barbieri Law Firm, where she represents individuals facing serious criminal charges throughout North Texas, including Collin County, Tarrant County, and the Dallas–Fort Worth area. She focuses exclusively on criminal defense, bringing nearly five years of prosecutorial experience to her work defending clients accused of felony and misdemeanor offenses.

Before transitioning to defense, Ms. Sharma served as an Assistant District Attorney in Collin County, where she was promoted to Felony Prosecutor. She began working with the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office while still in law school and continued there after graduation. During her time as a prosecutor, she handled a wide range of criminal cases and gained firsthand insight into how charges are evaluated, filed, and prosecuted. That experience now allows her to anticipate the State’s strategy and identify opportunities to challenge the prosecution’s case.

Ms. Sharma now applies that knowledge to defending clients charged with drug offenses, assault and domestic violence, and serious sex crime allegations, including aggravated sexual assault and continuous sexual assault of a child. She understands that people often seek a defense attorney during one of the most stressful periods of their lives and works to provide clear guidance, compassion, and steady advocacy throughout the process.

Clients value Ms. Sharma’s calm, respectful approach and her commitment to open communication. She believes that trust and honesty are essential to effective representation and strives to create an environment where clients feel comfortable discussing sensitive and personal details. By fully understanding each client’s circumstances, she is able to tailor defense strategies that address both the legal and human aspects of a case.

Ms. Sharma earned her Juris Doctor from Texas A&M University School of Law, where she served as President of the Criminal Law Society and received a Texas A&M Law Fellowship. During law school, she volunteered with the Innocence Clinic and the Criminal Defense Clinic, demonstrating an early commitment to defending the accused. She also served as an extern in the Intimate Partner Violence Division of the Tarrant County Criminal District Attorney’s Office.

She earned her undergraduate degree from Texas Wesleyan University, majoring in pre-law and criminal justice with a concentration in criminal law, and was an active member of Phi Alpha Delta Pre-Law Fraternity. Ms. Sharma is licensed to practice law in Texas and is also admitted to practice federally in the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Eastern Districts of Texas.

attorneys.name: Todd Shapiro
attorneys.practice_type: DUI/DWI Lawyers in Plano, TX
attorneys.bio:
Todd Shapiro joined his father, Howard, at The Shapiro Law Firm, in 2003. A native of Plano, Todd has made North Texas his home for most of his life, except for years spent in college and law school at The University of Texas at Austin. He graduated from The University of Texas School of Law in 2000 and was licensed to practice law in the State of Texas in November of 2000.

Todd began his legal career as an Assistant District Attorney for Dallas County. As a prosecutor in Dallas, he handled a wide range of cases, from simple misdemeanors to the most complex felonies. This experience at the Dallas DA's Office has proven to be vital in his work over the past 20 years as a criminal defense attorney.

As a defender of citizens accused of various crimes, Todd has an uncommon combination of experience, knowledge and desire. A veteran of hundreds of courtroom battles, Todd has earned a reputation as an accomplished trial lawyer. He has handled many high profile and important cases around the Metroplex. He has represented students and housewives, professionals and retired persons. Athletes, doctors, lawyers and politicians often consult and use him during their most trying times. Todd is at his best when the stakes are highest and members of the community have found themselves accused of the most serious of offenses. As a result of these efforts, many of his clients often come from referrals - from former clients, from other attorneys or simply from people around town who have heard about his experience and expertise in these areas.

Todd has been recognized by various organizations as a leader in his field. He was named as the Best Criminal Lawyer in Plano by the Plano Star Courier in 2011 and 2012, Best Lawyers in Dallas (2023, 2024) by D Magazine, and also was selected by Thomson Reuters Super Lawyers for 2023 & 2024.

attorneys.name: Sheila Shea
attorneys.practice_type: Family law Lawyers in Sherman, TX
attorneys.bio:
With decades of experience, Sheila has garnered a reputation for her unparalleled dedication to her clients, expertly navigating them through the often tumultuous waters of Family Law, Divorce, and Estate Planning. Her legal journey commenced upon her graduation from Oklahoma City University School of Law in 1997, setting the stage for what would become a career marked by excellence and advocacy for families in crisis.

Specializing in family law, Sheila possesses a deep understanding of the intricate and sensitive nature of cases within this domain. She boasts over 20 years of experience in guiding clients through legal battles concerning family law, divorce, and estate planning. Recognizing the emotional and financial toll such cases can exact on individuals and families, Sheila employs a blend of legal acumen and empathetic counsel to ensure her clients’ needs are met with the highest standards of care and professionalism.

In addition to her legal practice, Sheila is a fervent advocate of mediation. For more than two decades, she has offered her services as a mediator, assisting clients and families in resolving conflicts outside the courtroom. Sheila firmly believes in the power of mediation to prevent the trauma associated with court proceedings and the public airing of family issues. Her approach not only fosters a more amicable resolution to disputes but also preserves the dignity and privacy of all parties involved.

Sheila’s exceptional service and dedication to her clients have not gone unnoticed, as evidenced by the glowing testimonials from those she has represented. Clients praise her for her organization, friendliness, and the confidence she instills in them throughout the legal process. Her ability to calm nerves, coupled with her formidable presence in the courtroom, has earned her a valiant reputation when advocating for her clients’ rights, yet a confidant to them behind closed doors.

attorneys.name: Morgan C. Shell
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
I'm the rare Austinite who was actually born in Austin, which makes me a unicorn in a city of move-ins. After graduating from nearby Marble Falls High School (Go ‘Stangs!), I attended the University of Denver, where I received a scholarship to play Division I Women's Basketball. When I wasn't polishing my three-point-shot, I was studying to earn my bachelor's degree in International Studies. I was particularly interested in how governmental and nongovernmental institutions cooperate to implement policy solutions to the diplomatic, economic and security challenges brought on by globalization. My work answering these questions always led back to the law, which is the most important tool that exists for equitable conflict resolution, and which soon became my overarching passion.

Summers found me chasing my passion for international relations to Seville, Spain, where I refined my Spanish and widened my cultural lens. After college, I was drawn back to Madrid by the dual opportunity to teach English and shadow a lawyer working in civil litigation. I left Spain with a deeper understanding of how the law can be brought to bear on local, rather than global, disputes.

Back home, I picked up where I left off, interning with the civil litigation firm Richardson & Burgess, where I would later clerk. In law school, I worked as an Articles Editor for Volume 49 of the Texas Tech Law Review. After my second year of law school, I studied at Charles University in Prague, where I competed in daily moot court competitions while studying global issues related to wrongful convictions. There, I learned about the inadequate representation that is afforded to poor defendants in the United States, which motivated me to intern and then accept a job at the Texas Indigent Defense Commission. While I am proud of the work that we did at TIDC securing the 6th Amendment rights of Texas defendants, my interest in advocacy drew me back to civil litigation and I'm proud to work with such a dynamic team of advocates at Wright & Greenhill, PC. I have been included in Texas Super Lawyers® magazine, an Internet Brands publication, as a Rising Star of 2025.

attorneys.name: Scot E. Sheldon
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Dan C. Ducote Jr
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Beaumont, TX
attorneys.bio:
Scot Sheldon has been licensed to practice in the State of Texas since 1979. Mr. Sheldon first achieved an AV Rating, the Highest Possible Peer Review Rating in Legal Ability & Ethical Standards, in 1999 and has been AV Rated each year since. Mr. Sheldon began his legal career working as an in-house attorney for a New York Stock Exchange Company practicing in the areas of securities and finance. Mr. Sheldon was also involved in the acquisition of an oil and gas company which became a wholly-owned subsidiary of the NYSE Company. Since 1982, Mr. Sheldon has been in the private practice of law in Beaumont, Texas. Mr. Sheldon is a commercial transactional attorney, who currently represents The Port of Port Arthur Navigation District of Jefferson County, Texas (more than 35 years), the South East Texas Regional Planning Commission (more than 35 years), the Port of Orange, the Calhoun Port Authority, and numerous businesses located in the Southeast Texas area. Mr. Sheldon's business clients include more than 15 car dealerships, 3 boat dealerships, and several construction companies. Mr. Sheldon's practice includes formation and start-up of business entities, mergers and acquisitions, and negotiation and preparation of contracts in connection therewith. Also, Mr. Sheldon has served as Issuer Counsel and Bond Counsel in several billion dollars of tax-exempt and taxable bond financings for commercial, health care, housing, pollution control, sewage and solid waste, and industrial/plant expansion projects. Finally, Mr. Sheldon's practice includes negotiation and preparation of pipeline and other forms of easement agreements, which Mr. Sheldon has handled for numerous landowner clients throughout the State of Texas.

When not practicing law, Mr. Sheldon enjoys sports of all types. Mr. Sheldon has been actively involved in coaching baseball at all levels throughout his legal career. Mr. Sheldon also has served on the Board of numerous charitable organizations. In addition to being a licensed attorney in the State of Texas, Mr. Sheldon is a member and former Director of the Jefferson County Bar Association and a member of the Texas Bar Foundation.

Awards and Honors

Honors

AV Rated, Martindale-Hubbell

attorneys.name: Jeff Shelton
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Shelton grew up in Lancaster, Texas and presently lives in Allen, Texas. He graduated from Baylor University with a Bachelor of Arts in History with a Minor in Environmental Studies. He then achieved the goal he set in 9th grade after reading Harper Lee’s classic To Kill and Mockingbird, by graduating from the Walter and Shelia Umphrey’s School of Law at Baylor University and becoming an attorney.

Jeff always wanted to be a trial lawyer and began his practice by defending individuals and corporations in personal injury cases. However, it did not take long until he shifted his practice to represent those injured by the negligence and recklessness of others. Over the past twenty plus years Jeff has tried more than 100 lawsuits to verdict in state and federal courts in Texas and Oklahoma. Jeff is admitted to the State Bar of Texas, the United States District Courts in the Northern, Eastern, Southern and Western Districts of Texas and the 5th Circuit Court of Appeals.

Jeff has represented clients in personal injury cases involving car wrecks (there are no accidents), truck wrecks, commercial trucking wrecks, motorcycle wrecks, auto vs. pedestrian incidents, auto vs. bicycle wrecks, medical malpractice, dental malpractice, mass tort litigation, oilfield and offshore rig incidents, premises liability, product liability, wrongful death and traumatic brain injury cases.

Outside of the office, Jeff enjoys being with his wife and two sons, listening to music, stand-up comedy, cooking and long-distance running. He founded Run4Something, Inc. a 501(C)(3) non-profit corporation that is raising money for every mile of each of the twelve marathons he is running in 2023.

attorneys.name: Trent Shelton
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
In his short career, the results Trent has obtained are staggering. You will not find many lawyers Trent’s age who have tried more cases than him. In just three years as a lawyer, Trent has obtained over $80 million in verdicts and settlements as lead counsel. In 2023, Trent obtained a $33 million verdict on a burn case where the defendants essentially offered minimal amounts to settle the case pretrial. In another case, he obtained a verdict of $1.9 million in a multi-defendant bus crash case. He also settled cases worth $9 million, $5.2 million, and 3.5 million in the same year.

In 2022, after 30 depositions, he obtained a $9.5 million settlement on behalf of an injured West Texas oil field worker. In the same year, he took on a worldwide company with cases pending nationwide due to a defective baby product put out on the market. After taking many depositions and defeating numerous motions filed by the Defendant in federal court, he was able to obtain a favorable settlement on behalf of a family who lost their 5-month-old daughter due to the product.

His results have caused him to receive many recognitions, including being named on the Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch for 2023 and 2024.

Trent grew up in the small Northeast Texas town of Hughes Springs. He attended Oral Roberts University, where he studied business and played baseball—a sport he credits with teaching him many important life lessons. His time as an athlete found him appearing in two NCAA Division I Arkansas and TCU regional tournaments.

After earning his undergraduate degree with honors from Oral Roberts University, Trent attended Baylor Law School. Here, he graduated Magna Cum Laude and at the top of his class. While studying law, Trent competed on Baylor’s national moot court team. He also served as an associate editor of the Baylor Law Review and was a member of the Order of the Barristers. His academic accomplishments include receiving top grades in numerous courses, most notably Practice Court III, one of the three courses in Baylor’s rigorous Practice Court program.

While Trent is licensed in Texas and Louisiana, his practice is not limited to those states. He appears in state and federal courts all over the country for his clients. Trent’s practice focuses primarily on catastrophic personal injury, maritime and offshore cases, premises liability, product liability, and wrongful death.

Life Fellow, Texas Bar Foundation; Member, State Bar of Texas, Colorado Bar Association, American Bar Association, Houston Bar Association, Fort Bend County Bar Association, American Association for Justice, Texas Trial Lawyers Association, and Houston Trial Lawyers Association.

For more than 29 years, Mr. Sher has been practicing in the area of environmental, personal injury and civil trial litigation representing clients in federal and state courts located in Texas and nationwide. Andrew Sher is a Martindale Hubbell AV® Preeminent™* Peer Review Rated Attorney with exceptional experience and capabilities. After graduating from the University of Texas at Austin in 1991 and obtaining his J.D. from the University of Houston Law Center in 1993, Mr. Sher spent ten years actively litigating cases with a nationally recognized civil trial law firm before founding The Sher Law Firm, PLLC, in 2003. Mr. Sher founded his law firm on the belief that he could establish "a small law firm by choice, with big-firm experience and capabilities" and he has the results to back it up. The firm has secured substantial multi-million dollar recoveries while fighting for victims injured or killed by oil field accidents, Big Rig Truck or 18-wheeler Collisions, automobile accidents and groundwater contamination. Since its inception, the firm has been actively engaged in prosecuting a wide variety of cases involving catastrophic personal injuries, dangerous drugs and products, environmental pollution claims, toxic exposure injuries, oil & gas lease and royalty disputes, real estate fraud, business, commercial and breach of contract torts, and eminent domain, right-of-way, easement and water rights disputes. The firm remains very selective about its cases, which means more personal service and better results for the firm's clients.

Mr. Sher was an invited speaker at the first annual Clear Gold Summit in September, 1999 concerning private property rights and surface and groundwater resources in the State of Texas. The Clear Gold Summit, an invitation only event, launched the debate on Water in Texas – A Commodity for the 21st Century and was attended by selected representatives with experience and expertise involving water issues from across the State. In the fall of 1999, Mr. Sher was also designated Special Assistant Attorney General by Attorney General Patricia A. Madrid for the purpose of litigating environmental enforcement actions on behalf of the State of New Mexico. In 2008, the Texas Bar Foundation Board of Trustees elected Mr. Sher to serve as a Life Fellow to the Texas Bar Foundation "in recognition of service and devotion to the highest traditions of the Bar." Mr. Sher has also regularly been selected for inclusion as a Super Lawyer by Thomson Reuters as published in Texas Monthly for "Environmental Litigation" and as one of Houston's Top Lawyers by H-Texas Magazine.

Environmental law is a practice with an interdisciplinary bent that calls for the comprehension of issues that are not new to The Sher Law Firm. "Our background makes us particularly aware of the technical and economic feasibility of complex litigation. Technical and economic feasibilities are generally not explained or defined in statutes and the understanding of such issues can only be acquired after years of experience and objective willingness to listen and learn from other disciplines. Mr. Sher and his law firm have actively engaged in prosecuting cost recovery actions, Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act ("CERCLA") and Texas Solid Waste Disposal Act ("SWDA") claims, environmental crimes, natural resource damage, pipeline leaks and releases, natural resource damage actions, and other property damage actions caused by pollution, including aquifer contamination cases, against oil and gas production and transportation companies and other corporations whose operations and/or failures have contaminated the surface, subsurface, and groundwater resources of various individual and governmental clients. In the course of this litigation experience, and during the development of these contamination cases, depositions of key company personnel and environmental experts have been taken, documenting the practices that cause surface and groundwater contamination. For example, the depositions of pipeline technicians, pipeline controllers, incident commanders, pumpers, foremen, supervisors, superintendents, regional managers, engineers, environmental engineers, and even the presidents and chief executive officers of companies and corporations document the manner in which businesses have conducted field operations throughout the United States and how those operations have actually caused surface and groundwater contamination and ultimately the destruction of other natural resources.

The Sher Law Firm frequently associates with other national firms as outside counsel, forming a seamless team to further the interest of large clients with environmental legal issues nationwide. The joining together of these diverse national trial practices has the ability to form approaches and strategies which are unique and will result in the successful conclusion of numerous and varying types of environmental litigation. There is a substantial breadth of expertise available to clients of the Firm. "We are very selective about our cases, which means more personal service and better results for our clients."
