attorneys.name: Jennifer Solak
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio: Jennifer Solak was born and raised in New Orleans, Louisiana, but has called Houston home since 2006. She graduated from Louisiana State University and Tulane Law School, and following law school, she served as a law clerk for the Honorable Mary Milloy on the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas. Jennifer has devoted much of her legal career to helping others. She worked for the Houston-based nonprofit organization Children at Risk and then represented the State of Louisiana, serving on a team that helped obtain the largest environmental settlement in United States history, including more than $5 billion for the restoration of Louisiana’s natural resources that were damaged by the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. Jennifer has also spent many years serving clients directly in estate planning and probate matters, and at Johnson Law Group, she continues to fight for those who have been injured through contamination, defective medical devices, and dangerous products. Specifically, Jennifer works with the families of clients who have passed away to ensure their estates receive the settlement funds they are due.

I represent individuals as well as major companies and have successfully helped them resolve issues involving Deceptive Trade Practices Act, consumer fraud, breach of contract, breach of fiduciary duty, employment disputes, commercial fraud, trade secret misappropriations, tortious interference, and patents.”

I graduated in the top 15% from South Texas College of Law, made the Dean’s List, earned an academic excellence scholarship and am a member of the Phi Delta Phi Legal Honor Society. Prior to law, I earned an undergraduate in computer science from the University of Texas at Austin.

With a background in computer science, I have the unique ability to help clients effectively and efficiently resolve disputes involving complicated technology, large amounts of documents, and complex multi-party disputes.

I take pride in being a member of the Rotary Club of Houston Skyline, with a commitment to bringing Rotary’s presence and preeminence back into downtown Houston.

attorneys.name: Randall O. Sorrels
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Randy Sorrels is the Immediate Past President of the State Bar of Texas, which consists of almost 105,000 lawyers. Texas lawyers voted him to serve as the President by the widest margin of victory in State Bar election history. As a Texas lawyer, Randy has also been named one of the top 100 lawyers in Texas for the last 14 years by Texas Super Lawyers magazine.

Randy holds four board certifications from the Texas Board of Legal Specialization and the National Board of Trial Advocacy. He has extensive experience handling personal injury cases, medical malpractice cases, and business disputes - including “bet the company” cases. Most recently, Randy has been named the Best Lawyers® Medical Malpractice Law - Plaintiffs "Lawyer of the Year", in Houston, and this is his third time for him to receive this honor. He has been also been awarded some of the highest legal honors in Texas. He has been awarded the State Bar of Texas' President's Award (recognizing the one Texas Lawyer who provided the most outstanding contributions through distinguished service to the lawyers of Texas), the Judge Sam Williams Award (recognizing the Texas lawyer who provides the greatest contribution to both local bars and the State Bar of Texas), and the Houston Bar Association President's Award (recognizing significant contributions to an HBA program). Early in his career, Randy was honored with the Woodrow B. Seals Outstanding Young Lawyer of Houston Award (recognizing the one young Houston lawyer who exemplified significant professional traits both inside and outside the practice of law).

Randy is the past President of the Texas Association of Civil Trial and Appellate Specialists, and past Chair of the Fellows of the Texas Bar Foundation. He has served as the President of the Houston Bar Association, President of the Houston Trial Lawyers Association, President of the Houston Trial Lawyers Foundation, Vice President of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, Trustee of the Texas Bar Foundation, Director of the State Bar of Texas (two terms), Commissioner of the Equal Access to Justice Commission, Trustee of the Texas Supreme Court Historical Society, and is currently on the Board of Directors at South Texas College of Law Houston.

Randy started his legal career at Fulbright & Jaworski, where he represented doctors, hospitals, insurance companies, and businesses in the state of Texas who were accused of civil wrongdoing. He graduated Magna Cum Laude from South Texas College of Law Houston in 1987, where he was on the Law Review and was a member of the nationally recognized Board of Advocates. South Texas College of Law Houston has honored Randy with its highest honor— the Dean's Medal, as well as its Public Service Award (the inaugural award). South Texas College of Law Houston has renamed its legal clinics The Randall O. Sorrels Legal Clinics, which represents 15,000 square feet of new, state-of-the-art facilities to bring together clients with unmet legal needs and students who are eager to work with those clients under direct supervision of their professors. In 2018, South Texas College of Law Houston honored Randy with the Distinguished Alumni Award.

Prior to law school, Randy graduated Magna Cum Laude from Houston Baptist University— where he was recognized as an NCAA Academic All-American in 1984. He attended HBU on a soccer scholarship, and the soccer field at the university now carries his name— Randall O. Sorrels Field. While at school, he was recognized as the Outstanding Student in both Political Science and Speech Communications. In the greatest honor the university gives to alumni, Randy was named as HBU's Outstanding Alumnus of the Year for 2009, and he continues to be involved in alumni events and meetings.

Randy serves as the managing partner of Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Sorrels, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner, where he has practiced since 1990. Since taking over the leadership of the firm, Abraham Watkins has become more diverse, more community involved, more academically accomplished, and more active in the courtroom.

attorneys.name: Martin A. Sosland
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy and Restructuring Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Martin Sosland has, since joining the firm when the Dallas office opened in 1987, concentrated his practice in the area of business reorganizations, debtor and creditors' rights, and refinancings and acquisitions of troubled companies.

Mr. Sosland led the firm's representation in several major chapter 11 debtor cases, including Dallas Stars, SemGroup, Crescent Resources, Texas Rangers Baseball Partners, and Blockbuster, and co-led the firm's representation of Pilgrim's Pride. He also led the firm's representation of AHMSI, a W.L. Ross portfolio company, in its acquisition of Option One Mortgage from H&R Block. He served as one of the principal partners involved in the firm's representation of Enron Corp. and its affiliates in their chapter 11 cases and led the firm's representation of Sulzer Orthopedics in its class action product liability settlement, which allowed that company to avoid seeking relief under the Bankruptcy Code. Mr. Sosland also was involved in the firm's representation of The Western Company of North America, Zale Corporation, MCorp, Edison Brothers Stores, Inc., and PennCorp Financial Group, Inc., and led the firm's representation of US ONE Communications Corp., Heartland Wireless Communications, Verado Holdings, and Hedstrom Corporation in their chapter 11 cases.

Mr. Sosland led the firm's representation of the statutory creditors' committee for Diagnostic Health Systems, Inc. and has been involved in the representation of statutory creditors' committees for First Republicbank Corporation, Texas American Bancshares, National Gypsum Company, and New Valley Corporation. He has been involved in the firm's representation of aircraft lessors in a number of restructurings including TWA and Viscount Airlines, Inc., and led the firm's representation of a major aircraft lessor in the chapter 11 case of Express One International, Inc.

Mr. Sosland was also involved in the firm's representation of PennCorp Financial Group, Inc. in its acquisition of Southwestern Life Insurance Company from ICH Corporation, and led the firm's representation of creditors which acquired Fitz & Floyd and Trenwick America through chapter 11 plans of reorganization.

In addition, Mr. Sosland has led the firm's representation of major financial institutions and other creditors in a number of cases, including First Magnus, Harbor Financial Group, FirstPlus Financial Group, Genesis Physicians Practice Association, Mirant, Senior Living Properties, Williams Communications, and Covad.

Mr. Sosland has been recognized by Chambers USA and Chambers Global as a leading bankruptcy/restructuring lawyer.

Mr. Sosland is a member of the Dallas and American Bar Associations and the American Bankruptcy Institute. He has written and spoken about bankruptcy issues for a number of CLE programs sponsored by various organizations including the State Bar of Texas and the University of Texas School of Law.

attorneys.name: Kate Soulsby
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
A divorce or custody suit may be one of the most difficult experiences of your life to go through.

Kate is not a stranger to this reality. She has built her practice with the idea that each case requires a personal approach, which she takes the time to determine and she executes accordingly. She does this by carefully listening to you, evaluating your family’s situation, and conducting an exhaustive review of the evidence. She will move forward driven by your needs and the needs of the case. High conflict cases often require an assertive approach, and Kate will litigate on your behalf to win; however, if the parties can negotiate in good faith for the best outcome, Kate is ready to help find a soft landing, with low conflict. Regardless of your situation, Kate and her team will work with you to find the right strategy to obtain the best outcome for you. This individualized approach will reduce the pain family law matters may cause while saving time and money.

Kate has been practicing in family law since 2006. She is a family law specialist as certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Kate represents a diverse range of clients with a diverse number of needs. Kate has handled hundreds of family law matters, including divorces, custody cases, terminations of parental rights, adoptions, child support matters, protective orders, spousal support, and enforcements. She has successfully tried hundreds of cases to both judges and juries.

Kate has been voted one of the “Best Attorneys in San Antonio” each year since 2014. The American Institute of Family Law voted her one of the 10 Best for Exceptional Service and Exceptional Client Service.

She attended Baylor University for her undergraduate studies, and obtained a Master’s degree from University of Denver, prior to attending the University of Denver Strum College of Law for her juris doctor.

Kate has been a member of the San Antonio Bar Association, and the San Antonio Family Law Bar Association since 2008. She was on the board of the San Antonio Family Law Bar Association from 2018 until 2020, and the San Antonio Family Law Association in 2019. Kate joined Texas Academy of Family Law Specialists in 2018 after becoming board certified. Kate has been a member of the State Bar College since 2009.

Kate has resided in San Antonio since 2005, moving here after law school. She and her husband and their two dogs enjoy traveling in their Airstream, hiking and being outside when weather permits.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Scene Magazine voted Kate one of the Best Attorneys in San Antonio, four years in a row

Voted one of San Antonio “10 Best” by the American Institute of Family Law Attorneys for “Exceptional Service and Exceptional Client Service”, 2019 - 2020

attorneys.name: Richard W. South
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Biography

Mr. South served as a police officer with the Austin Police Department from 1976 – 1982. While on the force, he was a Certified Instructor, Texas Commission on Law Enforcement Officers Training and Education. After graduating from law school, he joined the Austin office of Midland law firm Stubbeman, McRae, Sealy, Laughlin & Browder. In 1985, Mr. South and several other attorneys from that office formed Bankston, Wright & Greenhill.

Mr. South is Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. In addition, he is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA). Mr. South was first selected as a Texas FindLaw Super Lawyer in 2013 and continues to receive this honor.

Mr. South's community activities include service as an Executive Board member for the Capitol Area Council, Boy Scouts of America. He was Chairman of the City of Westlake Hills Planning and Zoning Commission between 1993 and 1995. He has also served on the Board of Crimestoppers and as a Member of the Travis County Grand Jury.

Representative Work

In his 30 years of practice, Mr. South has tried over 50 cases to a jury verdict representing both Plaintiffs and Defendants including:

successfully defending numerous insurance clients in suits alleging the breach of the duty of good faith and fair dealing

successfully defending carriers in cases involving arson and/or insurance fraud

assisted numerous carriers in the investigation of claims, including conducting examinations under oath, where the insured is believed to have violated the concealment and fraud provisions of the policy

successfully represented over 100 homeowners in product defect suits against major shingle manufacturer

successfully represented survivors, including brain injured spouse, in suit against major trailer rental company for their negligence in renting a trailer that was inappropriate for the vehicle

successfully represented Police officers and departments in suits alleging civil rights violations under 28 USC §1983

handles large subrogation losses for insurance clients

represents contractors and owners in construction disputes involving building defects, water damage and health and safety issues

assists clients in immediate post occurrence investigation of major losses including fatalities, serious injury, fire and explosions

attorneys.name: Marcus Spagnoletti
attorneys.practice_type: Maritime Personal Injury Cases Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Marcus refuses to define himself by money and he will not define his law firm by money either. Having knocked on death's door following a serious personal injury, Marcus knows that enjoyment of life is priceless. If you ask his seriously injured clients if they would trade the millions of dollars they have received, after being represented by the Spagnoletti Law Firm, to live the remainder of their lives in the condition that they were in on the day prior to their injuries, they all would say "YES"! It is for this reason that the number one priority at Spagnoletti Law Firm is getting you the best medical treatment we can possibly find.

As Marcus learned during his treatment, it is not how you fall but how you get up. He will assist you in life in every way he possibly can, beyond simply navigating the legal minefield that awaits you. We are fortunate to live in a society that provides the opportunity to hold wrongdoers accountable. Those who have committed wrongful acts must pay for past and future medical care and loss of livelihood. Marcus knows how to hold negligent parties accountable, and he does it well. He has done it in state and federal courts across the country and all over the globe.

Marcus is well experienced in not only shepherding his clients through the loss of enjoyment of life due to personal injury, but also through commercial and transactional matters. Marcus’s goal is to ensure that when problems arise, his clients are protected and have someone to fight for them until they win. He has worked on matters in five of the seven continents and sees the world through an ecumenical lens. He invites the opportunity to learn about new places and people because he enjoys working to resolve his clients’ problems.

If you would like to talk about specific matters that Marcus has handled, come by and speak with him. He does not feel the need to list them all in this forum. When you do ask him, he is likely to give you the numbers of opposing attorneys and his competitors and encourage you to call them to inquire about his ability. He knows the truth. We who labor here, in this great world, seek the truth. He invites you to seek it because he knows he will ultimately see you again.

Marcus graduated from the University of Southern California, Magna Cum Laude. Three years later, he graduated from the University of Miami School of Law. Marcus is licensed to practice law in Texas and Florida. Marcus speaks basic mandarin Chinese and is conversational in Italian. He is proud of the law firm he founded and proud of the clients he represents.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Featured In New York Times as a "2019 Power Lawyer"

Law360 Rising Star, 2023

attorneys.name: Francis “Frank” Spagnoletti
attorneys.practice_type: Torts Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Spagnoletti was born in 1954. He graduated from Emory University School of Law in 1979, and earned his Masters of Law in International and Maritime Law from the University of London in 1980. After completing his formal legal education, he began his law career at Vinson & Elkins, and became a partner in 1986, practicing primarily maritime and international litigation. In 1990, Mr. Spagnoletti started his own law firm, and continued his practice as a trial attorney, with an emphases on tort, maritime, insurance, commercial and environmental litigation. Mr. Spagnoletti has now for more than 40 years represented clients in all aspects of litigation and arbitration involving insurance, products liability, offshore construction, vessels, rigs, and platforms. Mr. Spagnoletti has also represented clients in serious white collar crime matters and Rico civil matters as well as business and commercial litigation.

In addition to his broad experience, Mr. Spagnoletti is also a Proctor in Admiralty, and a member of the Maritime Law Association. He has also lectured at Market Seminars in the London insurance market on various topics concerning maritime and insurance issues.

attorneys.name: Mary Lois Spain
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Law Lawyers in Decatur, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mary Lois Spain Sipes is a hometown girl, with deep roots in the agriculture industry,

having grown up on a dairy farm in Decatur. Mary Lois and her family call Wise County

home. She is married to Joe Sipes, who grew up in Decatur as well. Mary Lois understands the strains of our modern culture and the toll that takes on families, as she is a working mother to two young children.

Mary Lois focuses her legal practice in the areas of Wills, Trusts & Estate Planning, Probate, Guardianship, Real Estate, and Oil & Gas.

In 2016 Mary Lois established the first Wise County National Adoption Day, whereby our local courts joined the national collective effort to raise awareness of children waiting to be adopted from foster care. Mary Lois spent many years on the appointment list for Child Protection Cases in Wise, Jack, and Montague Counties where she advocated for both parents and children. She is a member of the Real Estate, Probate & Trust Law Section and Family Law Section of the Texas Bar. Mary Lois is a founding member of the Wise, Montague & Jack Counties Women’s Bar Association. Additionally, Mary Lois is a certified guardian ad litem for guardianship cases.

After graduating from Decatur High School in 2001, Mary Lois attended Texas Tech University. In December 2004 Mary Lois graduated cum laude, earning herself two undergraduate degrees: a Bachelor of Business Administration and a Bachelor of Science in Agriculture and Applied Economics.

Through Texas Tech University, Mary Lois had the opportunity to live in Washington, D.C. and work as a Presidential Congressional Intern for Congressman Lamar Smith, Texas District 21. She was then asked to be an intern for the White House Office of Media Affairs.

Prior to making the decision to attend law school, Mary Lois enjoyed researching land records as an independent landman for oil and gas companies. It was her close work with title attorneys that influenced her to make the decision to attend law school. Mary Lois attended Florida Coastal School of Law where she obtained a Juris Doctorate in 2010. Mary Lois has been licensed to practice law in the State of Texas Since 2010.

After becoming a licensed attorney, Mary Lois put her practical knowledge of real property to good use as a title attorney issuing title opinions primarily for oil and gas companies drilling in the Barnett Shale geological formation. In 2013, as Mary Lois began to see a decline in drilling, she made the decision to “hang a shingle” in her hometown of Decatur.

Mary Lois jumped into a solo law practice taking on new clients and court appointments. Shortly after starting her own practice, she joined The Reeves Law Firm as an associate and in 2014 formed the partnership of Reeves Spain-Sipes Law, LLP. In 2018, Mary Lois moved her law practice to the historic Decatur Town Square where she began to work closely with the attorneys at Woodruff & Wren, L.L.P. It was such a match that Mary Lois joined Mason L. Woodruff and Jennifer Wren as a partner attorney in January 2019, forming Woodruff, Wren & Spain-Sipes, L.L.P.

Upon the retirement of Mason L. Woodruff and the departure of Jennifer Wren from private practice in December 2019, Mary Lois began the New Year joining forces with J. Michael Carrillo and Charles R. Tibbels. In January 2020 the three attorneys formed the law firm known as Carrillo|Sipes|Tibbels, PLLC. Mary Lois is proud of the legacy entrusted to her and the opportunity to fashion a legacy of her own. She is excited for our community’s future and to share in what awaits Decatur, Wise County, and our surrounding areas.

Mary Lois Spain Sipes* Licensed to Practice In All Areas of Law By The State Bar of Texas Since 2010

*Not Certified By The Texas Board of Legal Specialization

In 2013, as Mary Lois began to see a decline in drilling, she made the decision to “hang a shingle” in her hometown of Decatur.

Mary Lois jumped into a solo law practice taking on new clients and court appointments. Shortly after starting her own practice, she joined The Reeves Law Firm as an associate and in 2014 formed the partnership of Reeves Spain-Sipes Law, LLP. In 2018, Mary Lois moved her law practice to the historic Decatur Town Square where she began to work closely with the attorneys at Woodruff & Wren, L.L.P. It was such a match that Mary Lois joined Mason L. Woodruff and Jennifer Wren as a partner attorney in January 2019, forming Woodruff, Wren & Spain-Sipes, L.L.P.

Upon the retirement of Mason L. Woodruff and the departure of Jennifer Wren from private practice in December 2019, Mary Lois began the New Year joining forces with J. Michael Carrillo and Charles R. Tibbels. In January 2020 the three attorneys formed the law firm known as Carrillo|Sipes|Tibbels, PLLC. Mary Lois is proud of the legacy entrusted to her and the opportunity to fashion a legacy of her own. She is excited for our community’s future and to share in what awaits Decatur, Wise County, and our surrounding areas.

You will want to work with Ikaha Sparrow because she is a talented and dedicated legal professional who will be committed to helping you achieve the most favorable possible outcome to your case.

attorneys.name: Arnold Spencer
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Criminal Defense Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Spencer is the founding member of Spencer & Associates, a law firm specializing in economic fraud and compliance matters. For more than twenty-five years, Mr. Spencer has both prosecuted and defended clients in investigations and litigation. He regularly defends clients accused of securities fraud, wire and mail fraud, cryptocurrency fraud, and money laundering. On the compliance side, he consults with companies regarding best practices to meet and exceed regulatory requirements. Having served as the Asset Forfeiture Chief in one of the busiest asset forfeiture programs in the country, he has handled hundreds of asset forfeiture matters.

Mr. Spencer represents companies and individuals in the federal court and before federal agencies. He has represented companies before the SEC, CFTC, FBI, Homeland Security, the U.S. Attorney’s Office, NYDFS, and state Departments of Banking and Securities, as well as federal and state grand juries. Often, Mr. Spencer is called upon to craft defense strategies in parallel with civil, criminal and administrative lawsuits. Recent representative cases include:

Defending the Chief Executive Officer of a cryptocurrency company who was a decorated Marine and who was indicted in the Southern District of New York for securities and wire fraud, and who was sued by the SEC and CFTC for fraud; Mr. Spencer obtained dismissal of the criminal case and successfully resolved the SEC and CFTC charges.

Defending the Chief Accounting Officer of a publicly traded company who was being investigated by federal law enforcement agencies, sued by the Securities and Exchange Commission, named as a defendant in a securities fraud class-action, and the subject of an administrative proceeding by the state accounting board; Mr. Spencer successfully resolved all matters for his client without any sanction in any proceeding, other than a minimal fine assessed by the SEC.

Defending a former Dallas Cowboys professional football player accused of criminal and civil fraud and false claims; Mr. Spencer’s client resolved all allegations in a civil settlement for less than one third of one percent of the alleged loss.

Representing a publicly traded company in the highway safety products industry which was the subject of federal and state criminal allegations, two civil False Claim Act trials, class-action lawsuits, state Attorney General investigations and multiple product-liability lawsuits; the company was absolved of all liability in every case.

Mr. Spencer is recognized by peers and judges as an accomplished trial lawyer. However, he believes that the best results for his clients are often achieved by avoiding litigation or by using procedural motion practice to achieve a pre-trial dismissal

From 2000 to 2010, Mr. Spencer served as an Assistant United States Attorney in the Eastern District of Texas. He specialized in securities fraud, financial fraud, and money laundering prosecutions, and prosecuted more than 100 federal cases. Mr. Spencer was selected as one of the trial lawyers that prosecuted criminal violations arising from the collapse of Enron. Among other high profile cases, he prosecuted a nationwide, securities fraud case involving real estate and automobile financing, and obtained one of the longest sentences ever imposed by a federal judge for money laundering violations. The U.S. Attorney General awarded Mr. Spencer the John Marshall Award, the highest award presented to a Justice Department attorney for contributions and excellence in legal performance.

Mr. Spencer previously was a partner at Akin Gump and Haynes & Boone in Dallas. He graduated from Amherst College and the University of Texas Law School. He has been married to Mary McClendon Spencer for 23 years, and has two boys, ages 18 and 20. He has served as the Senior Warden at St. Michael and All Angels Episcopal Church and as a Trustee of St. Philips School and Community Center.

attorneys.name: Sarah Springer
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Sarah has been practicing law since 1980 and has a wealth of experience in all aspects of family law, including divorce, child custody, possession issues, child support, modification and enforcement of prior orders, termination of parental rights, adoptions, and pre-marital agreements. Sarah has been a litigator, a mediator and a judge. She has perspective in family law from both sides of the bench. In addition to family law matters, Sarah has years of experience in estate planning and probate. Sarah’s judicial service was in Mississippi, where she was a Chancellor – a state district judge serving two counties. Chancery Court covers family law and probate as well as juvenile cases. Sarah returned to Texas in 2007 and established the Springer Law in Katy, then in 2025 decided to join the Bolton Law Firm.

In addition to her law practice, Sarah conducts family law mediations and has a great track record of successful results enabling families to avoid the stress and expense of contested trials. Sarah received the 2016 Suzanne Bartholomew Service Award in appreciation for her dedication and service to Fort Bend Lawyers Care.

Sarah has been active in the legal community throughout her career. She has served in several capacities in the Katy Bar Association and the Fort Bend County Bar Association, and served as President in both organizations. Sarah has Chaired the Texas State Bar Professionalism Committee, and is active in the Houston Bar Association as well, serving on the Senior Lawyers Committee and the Professionalism Committee. She has also served as a mentor through the Fort Bend Bar Association and the Houston Bar Association. She is currently on the Board of Directors of the Fort Bend Family Bar.

attorneys.name: Amber R. Spurlock
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Offices of Tad Nelson & Associates
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in League City, TX
attorneys.bio:
Former Air Force JAG & Special Assistant United States Attorney

Before returning to Law offices of Tad Nelson & Associates as a criminal defense attorney in April 2011, Amber Spurlock served in the rank of Captain as an Active Duty Assistant Staff Judge Advocate General (JAG) in the United States Air Force. While on Active Duty, Ms. Spurlock prosecuted military members for felony and misdemeanor level charges in military Courts-Martial. While stationed at Eglin AFB near Destin, Florida, Ms. Spurlock also served as a Special Assistant United States Attorney in the Northern District of Florida. Here, Ms. Spurlock prosecuted civilians in Federal Court for misdemeanor offenses committed on the Installation.

In 2009, Ms. Spurlock deployed to Baghdad, Iraq, where she worked with military intelligence to prosecute cases against Iraqi detainees. As a Central Criminal Court of Iraq Liaison Officer, Ms. Spurlock traveled to the Red Zone, presenting cases to Iraqi judges in their courts for offenses such as beheadings, kidnappings, executions, and IED detonations. While in Iraq, Ms. Spurlock also served on the trial team in the prosecution of an Army Captain charged with ordering the execution of two Iraqi detainees.

Upon returning from her deployment in 2010, Ms. Spurlock moved to Langley AFB in Hampton, Virginia. Again, Ms. Spurlock was sworn in as a Special Assistant United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Virginia and continued to prosecute in Federal Court. Ms. Spurlock also served as the Chief of Operations Law, ensuring that all military members were educated in the Law of Armed Conflict as well as the laws of their deployment locations. Finally, in 2011, Ms. Spurlock was honorably discharged and returned to her home in Texas.

Since returning to Houston, Ms. Spurlock has defended numerous misdemeanor and felony cases in Harris, Galveston, Brazoria, Montgomery, and Ft. Bend counties. She has found her true passion in defense work and is excited to be back at Tad Nelson & Associates where she practiced before joining the military.

attorneys.name: Kevin E. Sralla
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kevin "Buck" Sralla is a family law attorney who has been practicing in San Antonio and surrounding areas since 2006. He is a down-to-earth, hard-working lawyer with a desire and an ability to connect with his clients to achieve their litigation goals. He is the owner/managing attorney at Sralla Family Law, PLLC - an eight-member boutique firm that includes two associate lawyers working alongside Mr. Sralla. His goal has always been to achieve effective communication with his firm's clients while getting them the top-notch results they deserve in the courtroom. He identifies with client predicaments and the unique challenges they face.

As a child, he overcame a severe case of Tourette Syndrome, a condition that causes involuntary movements, tics, and vocalizations. This often made him the target of laughter and ridicule, but it never kept him from chasing and achieving his dreams. Now, his professional pedigree speaks for itself. After working as an investigative journalist for seven years, Mr. Sralla observed that he had a knack for calmly drawing the truth out of news sources and public officials he encountered, many times in the face of resistance and personal attacks. He parlayed this skill into a law degree from Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan in 1999.

While in law school, Mr. Sralla earned a coveted spot as an associate editor on the Wayne Law Review and garnered multiple honors and awards, including the Richard B. Gushee Writing Award recognizing the best writer on the law review in 1998. After graduation, his first job was a judicial clerkship for the Hon. Marilyn J. Kelly on the Michigan Supreme Court, where he drafted published opinions and had a voice in the shaping of Michigan's jurisprudence. After spending 12 years in Michigan, Mr. Sralla and his family came home to Texas in 2006, when he hung his shingle and began taking family law cases. It was also during this time that his life took a dramatic turn as he became the primary caregiver for his wife, who was struggling with a terminal illness.

As he cared for her around the clock, often sleeping by her bedside in hospitals as she clung to her life embattled by disease, he fought by her side and saw her through a double-lung transplant operation that saved her life in 2015. Through it all, he managed to maintain and grow his law practice into what it is today. He has since represented the interests of thousands of clients with their family law needs.

His practice focuses on all aspects of family law, including high-conflict and uncontested divorces, property division issues, protective orders, domestic violence situations, child custody disputes, modifications of prior orders, child support issues, same-sex marriage matters, adoptions, grandparents' rights dilemmas, and complex interstate jurisdictional cases.

Mr. Sralla is in good standing with the State Bar of Texas and maintains solid relationships with the bench and bar of Bexar County, Texas, and surrounding counties in South Central Texas. He is always eager to serve his clientele, build upon those relationships and add to his ever-growing list of accomplishments.

attorneys.name: Kimberley M. Spurlock
attorneys.firm_name: Abraham, Watkins, Nichols, Agosto, Aziz & Stogner
attorneys.practice_type: Vehicular Accidents Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kimberley M. Spurlock (“Kim”) was born in Houston, Texas and raised in Humble, Texas. She attended Humble High School and played on the varsity women’s golf team. Kim graduated from the University of Texas at Austin in 1997 with a degree in Sociology and a minor in Business. She then attended South Texas College of Law, graduating Cum Laude in 2001, ranking #13 in her class of over 240 graduates. She is a member of The College of the State Bar, The Houston Trial Lawyers Association, and The Texas Trial Lawyers Association. Kim earned her Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in 2009, and has been re-certified in this specialty area each year since 2009.

Kim opened her own law firm in 2003 and has handled thousands of cases including personal injury matters on the plaintiff and defense side, wrongful death matters, industrial accidents, and a variety of other civil litigation and personal injury matters. Kim has tried well over fifty jury trials in courtrooms throughout Texas. She has focused her practice on plaintiff personal injury work, representing individuals who have suffered injuries due to the negligence of others, using her extensive training and trial experience to obtain large settlements and verdicts on behalf of her clients. Kim joined the firm as Of Counsel in 2024, bringing over twenty years of litigation and personal injury experience.

Kim lives in Atascocita, Texas with her husband, Jimmy Spurlock. She enjoys playing golf and traveling.

Charles received his undergraduate degree, in History and Political Science, from Columbia University and his law degree at the University of Texas School of Law, where he graduated with honors (cum laude). At UT Law, Charles sat on the editorial board of The Review of Litigation, interned for the Honorable Xavier Rodriguez (United States District Judge, Western District of Texas), and worked as a research assistant.

After graduating from law school, Charles moved to Mississippi to clerk for the Honorable Debra M. Brown (United States District Judge, Northern District of Mississippi).

Charles is licensed to practice law in Texas, Louisiana, and Mississippi and was voted a Texas Rising Star by Super Lawyers, a Thompson Reuters publication, in 2022 and 2023.

attorneys.name: Bret Daniel Stanley
attorneys.practice_type: Litigating Rideshare Cases Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Over the course of his career, Mr. Stanley’s practice has focused on litigating rideshare cases, pharmaceutical device and drug cases, mass torts, complex first-party insurance claims, and catastrophic personal injury claims.

Mr. Stanley has substantial litigation and trial experience against major pharmaceutical drug & device manufacturers as well as against Uber Technologies, Inc. In 2023, Mr. Stanley was first-chair trial attorney in a three-week Texas trial against a major vaginal mesh manufacturer. Additionally, Mr. Stanley has tried many cases through final arbitration against Uber Technologies, Inc. and, in 2024, tried the first ever jury trial against Uber Technologies, Inc. concerning the question of whether Uber Drivers are employees of Uber.

Mr. Stanley has cross examined at trial many hostile corporate witnesses, taken many 30(b)(6) depositions of corporate representatives, deposed hostile expert witnesses, developed multiple general causation expert witness reports effecting thousands of cases, prepared and presented general causation plaintiff experts for depositions, developed case specific expert reports concerning hundreds of cases, prepared and presented case specific experts for depositions, drafted and served full written discovery in several MDLs, completed full motion practice (dispositive motions, Daubert motions, motions in limine, etc.), and drafted and filed appeals to the circuit court.

Mr. Stanley has been selected to leadership or assisted leadership in the following mass tort litigations:

MDL 3084 – In re: Uber Technologies, Inc., Passenger Sexual Assault Litigation– Plaintiff Steering Committee Member;

MDL 2924 – In Re: Zantac (Ranitidine) Products Liability Litigation– Deposition Committee and Discovery Committee;

SGLT2 Diabetes Drug Consolidations in Delaware and Connecticut – Executive Committee;

Option™ Vena Cava Litigation in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas of Pennsylvania – Executive Committee; and,

Transvaginal Mesh MDLs in the Southern District of West Virginia

attorneys.bio: Mrs. Stanton is a partner of Osborne, Helman, Scott, Knisely & Stanton, LLP. Mrs. Stanton specializes in probate and estate planning law and she is board certified in these practice areas. Her practice includes the representation of individuals with respect to their estate planning needs and the representation of fiduciaries and beneficiaries with regard to the administration of trusts and estates. She advises with regard to testamentary and lifetime gift and generation–skipping planning in addition to the use of family business entities, life insurance and life insurance trusts. She also provides advice concerning post-mortem tax planning, prepares federal estate tax returns and handles state probate proceedings for fiduciaries of estates and guardianships. In addition, Mrs. Stanton is a Certified Financial Planner® and has more than 14 years’ experience as a Director of Trust Services for a regional bank.

attorneys.name: William Cody Stapp
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
Cody Stapp joined Callahan & King in late 2015 after serving as an Administrative Law Judge for the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles. In that capacity he interacted with countless inmates, presided over parole revocation hearings, and helped the State of Texas discern whether a person had violated the terms of their parole.

Cody received his Bachelor of Arts degree from Austin College in Sherman, Texas. After graduation, he received practical experience as a court clerk for judges in Grayson County, Texas. Cody went on to receive his law degree from Baylor Law School where he served as an editor on the Baylor Law Review and received numerous awards for academic excellence.

While he has worn many hats, Cody’s career path has brought him full circle to serving the needs of the people of central Texas. Cody began his law practice handling family law and criminal defense cases in Waco. He is happy to return to that practice, and his keen analytical skills are greatly appreciated by his clients.

Drawing from his experience in government service and private practice, Cody helps those in his charge to navigate the complexities of the court system while constantly pushing that system to work in his clients’ favor. Cody is also passionate about criminal justice reform and trying to make the court system more efficient and fairer to everyone.

Cody lives in McLennan County with his wife, their two children and three dogs, and his Peloton bike.

attorneys.name: Thomas R. Stauch
attorneys.practice_type: Arbitration and Mediation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tom maintains a diverse civil litigation practice, representing his clients in a variety of litigation issues, including construction, real estate and commercial litigation, as well as legal malpractice claims. He is trained and qualified as a mediator, and has received an "AV" rating by Martindale-Hubbell's peer review rating system – the highest rating available. The designation recognizes Tom for high ethical standards and "very high to preeminent legal abilities."

Tom was born in Dallas, Texas in 1969. At Texas A&M University, Tom was a member of the Corps of Cadets and received the Distinguished Student Award four times. He was also a member of the Ross Volunteer Company, the official honor guard for the Governor of Texas and the oldest student organization in Texas. Tom received his B.B.A. in Management and Marketing in 1992, and entered law school at Southern Methodist University, where he became a member of the Phi Delta Phi Honor Fraternity and an Editor for The International Lawyer law review. Before receiving his Juris Doctorate in 1995, Tom authored an international business article The United States and Vietnam: Overcoming the Past and Investing in the Future, which was published in the Winter 1995 edition of The International Lawyer. Tom has been asked to speak and write for various industry groups and trade organizations, and his articles have published in Texas Homebuilder Magazine.

Tom was licensed to practice law in the State of Texas in November 1995, and is admitted to practice law in the state courts of Texas as well as the United States District Courts for the Northern, Eastern and Southern Districts of Texas, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, and the U.S. Supreme Court. Tom is currently a member of the State Bar of Texas, the Dallas Bar Association and the Texas A&M Association of Former Students. Despite his busy professional life, Tom's true passion is for his family, friends and faith. Tom and his wife, Susan, are the proud parents of three beautiful children, Lauren, Ben and Owen, and attend Chase Oaks Church in Plano.

attorneys.name: Anthony G. Stergio
attorneys.practice_type: Labor & Employment Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Board Certified in Labor and Employment Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, Anthony (Tony) G. Stergio has extensive experience in the defense of State and Federal employment discrimination claims, wage and hour compliance, noncompetition agreements and employment policy design and review.

Although Tony’s primary areas of practice are employment and commercial litigation, he has substantial experience handling commercial arbitration, computer service contract disputes and commercial litigation in State and Federal Courts. He also counsels clients regarding developments in various areas of State and Federal employment law. Tony frequently speaks at employment-related seminars.

Representative Experience:

Successfully defended national origin and race discrimination case in Federal Court.

Obtained Summary Judgment in numerous age, sex and race discrimination cases in both Federal and State Courts.

Defended an FLSA action in Federal Court regarding employee/independent contractor issues and FLSA exemptions.

Obtained Summary Judgment in a case regarding former employer’s assertion that former employee had usurped confidential information and engaged in improper competition.

Successfully established fraudulent transfer of real estate in State Court jury trial.

Analyzed numerous noncompetition agreements for enforceability issues and litigation strategy.

Drafted employment policies, handbooks and agreements for numerous large companies.

Successfully blocked a temporary injunction sought by a terminated employer/shareholder who asserted that termination was shareholder oppression.

attorneys.name: Robert Craig Stern
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Robert C. Stern is the managing partner in the New Orleans office. Mr. Stern was born in New York City in 1953. He attended Fairleigh Dickinson University (B.A. Cum Laude 1975) and obtained his law degree from Loyola University in New Orleans (J.D. 1978). While at Loyola Mr. Stern was a member of the Mock Trial Team and participated extensively in the clinical education program where he was assigned to the Orleans Parish District Attorney’s Office.

Mr. Stern is admitted to practice in all Louisiana and Texas state courts, The United States District Courts for the Eastern, Middle and Western Districts of Louisiana, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas, the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court. He has an “AV” rating with Martindale-Hubble, its highest rating.

Mr. Stern served as a special prosecutor in the St. Tammany Parish District Attorney’s Office from 1993 through 1995 where he concentrated his prosecutions on sexual offenses against children.

Mr. Stern divides his practice between civil and criminal defense. On the civil side he concentrates his practice on maritime and general casualty defense with emphasis on Risk Management as well. He has been a speaker on Risk Management at The CEO Forum West in Las Vegas, The CEO Forum East in New Orleans, the Allied Agents Association in Chicago and The Bekins Convention in Tucson. He also sits on the Advisory Board of a moving company agency.

Mr. Stern has lectured on criminal law speaking at Continuing Legal Education Seminars on Criminal Sentencing in Louisiana and the Criminal Trial in Louisiana from Start to Finish. He also lectured in The Defense of Sexual Abuse Cases and Handling Complex Auto insurance Cases. He has also been selected to speak at a seminar aimed at young lawyers preparing for their first civil trial.

Mr. Stern has handled multiple criminal cases receiving extensive media coverage including second degree murder and police corruption cases.

During his practice Mr. Stern has also had the privilege of representing both fellow lawyers and judges.

Mr. Stern has been voted New Orleans Top Lawyers by the New Orleans Magazine 2009.

attorneys.name: Carole Kustoff Stevens
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
An attorney with a strong desire to help you resolve your family law issues and move forward with your life.

Carole Stevens is an attorney who can approach your divorce or family matter from a practical, non-confrontational position. Her philosophy in working with divorce clients is to provide them with clear, concise legal advice to help them gain an understanding of the process, the legal system and the client’s options, so that each party can make the best possible decision for their family and changing family needs. She believes that each divorce or family matter is intrinsically different and personal in nature, and that you have a right to design the best possible divorce.

After receiving her Bachelor of Arts from University of Georgia, Carole was employed in Washington, DC in a series of political opportunities that included a year on the Reagan Bush ’84 campaign followed by a stint in political fundraising as Finance Director for John Kasich’s bid for the U.S. Congress in Ohio. In 1991 Carole began her legal career as an Account Representative for Lexis/Nexis legal research software, followed by the chance to work for Texas Lawyer as Managing Editor of Lexis Counsel Connect, directing editorial content and coordinating product sales. Carole began litigating in 1995, initially practicing law with Tobolowsky & Associates in Dallas in the areas of general civil litigation and family law.

Carole began her own law practice in 1996, and she chose family law as her practice area and in 1999 she joined as a partner with Nancy Amick to form Amick and Stevens. She was treasurer of the Plano Bar Association in 1997 and a member of the State Bar College , as well as a founding member of the Collin County Collaborative Divorce Alliance. Carole is also the former chair of the Family Law Section of the Collin County Bar Association.

Carole grew up in middle Tennessee, graduated from the University of Georgia with Bachelor Degrees in Political Science and English in 1984, and in 1991 received her Juris Doctorate from Cumberland Law School in Birmingham, Alabama and was admitted to the Texas State Bar.

attorneys.name: John W. Stevenson Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
John is a native Texan. He was born in Fort Worth in 1957 and later moved to Nacogdoches. He graduated Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts Degree from Trinity University in San Antonio, Texas. At Trinity, John was president of the Blue Key National Honor Fraternity and a member of Alpha Chi and Triniteers Fraternities. He earned his J.D. Degree from the University of Houston Law Center in 1982, where he won championships in Moot Court and Mock Trial competitions and was selected to the prestigious Order of the Barristers.

After graduation, John joined Ross, Griggs & Harrison, a 20-person insurance defense firm in Houston. He held the distinction of being the only first year lawyer solely responsible for his own docket. In less than a year, John had actively participated in numerous cases, many involving multiple wrongful deaths and multi-million dollar damage claims. As an associate attorney, John gained extensive trial experience, trying more cases than any other attorney at the firm while there.

In 1987, John founded his own firm to champion the rights of injured individuals. The same year he was awarded the highest rating of "AV" by the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory. Since then, John has remained focused on plaintiffs' personal injury litigation, working tirelessly to obtain the best possible outcome for his clients. In his distinguished career, John has handled many notable cases, with impressive results.

John is a member of the prestigious American Board of Trial Advocates. John is admitted to the State Bar of Texas and to practice before the U.S. District Court in the Southern and Eastern Districts of Texas. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the State Bar of Texas, the Houston Bar Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. John and his wife, Robyn, have three children.

John’s dedication to helping those in need reaches beyond his practice of law. John and his firm are generous contributors to many community organizations. His generosity and support have been acknowledged both publicly and privately.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
John is a native Texan. He was born in Fort Worth in 1957 and later moved to Nacogdoches. He graduated Magna Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts Degree from Trinity University in San Antonio, Texas. At Trinity, John was president of the Blue Key National Honor Fraternity and a member of Alpha Chi and Triniteers Fraternities. He earned his J.D. Degree from the University of Houston Law Center in 1982, where he won championships in Moot Court and Mock Trial competitions and was selected to the prestigious Order of the Barristers.

After graduation, John joined Ross, Griggs & Harrison, a 20-person insurance defense firm in Houston. He held the distinction of being the only first year lawyer solely responsible for his own docket. In less than a year, John had actively participated in numerous cases, many involving multiple wrongful deaths and multi-million dollar damage claims. As an associate attorney, John gained extensive trial experience, trying more cases than any other attorney at the firm while there.

In 1987, John founded his own firm to champion the rights of injured individuals. The same year he was awarded the highest rating of "AV" by the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory. Since then, John has remained focused on plaintiffs' personal injury litigation, working tirelessly to obtain the best possible outcome for his clients. In his distinguished career, John has handled many notable cases, with impressive results.

John is a member of the prestigious American Board of Trial Advocates. John is admitted to the State Bar of Texas and to practice before the U.S. District Court in the Southern and Eastern Districts of Texas. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the State Bar of Texas, the Houston Bar Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association and the American Association for Justice. John and his wife, Robyn, have three children.

John’s dedication to helping those in need reaches beyond his practice of law. John and his firm are generous contributors to many community organizations. His generosity and support have been acknowledged both publicly and privately.

attorneys.name: Stella A. Stevens
attorneys.firm_name: Griffin & Cain Attorneys at Law, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Conroe, TX
attorneys.bio:
With over 15 years of experience as a prosecutor and a defense attorney, Stella Stevens brings intelligence, knowledge and compassion to every case. She will also fight for you like a junk yard dog. There is nothing more stressful than a criminal charge and its implications for your future or the future of a loved one. This is when you need an attorney who will handle your case with dignity and urgency you deserve.

This 6th generation Texas graduated from the University of Texas in 1996, Attended the University of Houston Law Center and began her legal career as a prosecutor with the Montgomery Country Attorney’s Office and then the Montgomery County District Attorney’s Office where she worked as a misdemeanor and felony Prosecutor for 9 years.

The toughest job she ever had, however, came after that when she left the DA’s office to raise her two beautiful daughters for 10 years.

As rewarding as that job was, all good things must come to a close and she found a renewed calling in helping the citizen accused and returned to law practice as a criminal defense attorney. It is a calling, and it is not for the faint of heart.

In her spare time, you will find her reading, cooking for teenagers, working in her garden and identifying bird calls using her favorite bird sound app.

But despite these tranquil pursuits, make no mistake, in the courtroom, she is a junk yard dog.

attorneys.name: Scott E. Stevens
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Litigation Matters Lawyers in Longview, TX
attorneys.bio:
Scott E. Stevens was born and raised in Longview, Texas. Scott attended Texas Christian University in Fort Worth, Texas, and received his B.A. in 1991. After graduating from college, Scott attended South Texas College of Law in Houston, Texas. He received his J.D. in 1994.

After completing law school, Scott returned to Longview and went to work at Harbour, Smith, Harris & Merritt, P.C., where he primarily handled litigation matters for Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. During that time, Scott tried over 30 jury trials to verdict, both in state and federal court.

In 2004, Scott opened his own law firm in Longview, Texas. His practice consists mainly of representing large and small corporations in a variety of litigation matters, including complex litigation matters, intellectual property matters, contract disputes, insurance claims and DTPA claims. Scott continues to represent companies and individuals in personal injury actions, including product liability claims and wrongful death actions. Additionally, Scott has represented several new and used automobile dealerships before various state agencies, including the OCCC and TXDOT. Scott's practice mainly consists of cases in federal court, both in and outside of Texas.

Scott is board certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Scott was also selected for inclusion in Texas Super Lawyers in 2009 and 2010.

Scott is married to Lainey Godsey Stevens, and is the proud parent of two children, Camp and Ella Stevens.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mark was born and raised in Northeast Dallas, where he learned early on the value of hard work, community, and his love for the Dallas Cowboys. He earned his B.S. in Criminal Justice from Texas State University, and during an internship with a local law firm, he realized he had found his calling in the legal field.

After a short stint in Houston, Mark made the move to San Antonio to pursue his law degree at St. Mary’s University School of Law, where he was named the Super Brief Winner for the best overall brief in his class. As a first-generation law student, Mark balanced night classes while working full-time at Clayton, Ramirez & Null Law, sharpening his legal skills and his coffee preferences at the same time.

In 2023, Mark earned his J.D. and returned to the Dallas-Fort Worth area, where he now lives with his two energetic (and very spoiled) dogs, Kahlua and Piper. Outside the office, you can find him volunteering at pro bono clinics, coaching little league baseball teams, attending concerts, or enjoying an afternoon on the golf course.

At Clayton, Ramirez & Null Law, Mark assists clients with real estate transactions, estate planning, and business and commercial transactions.

attorneys.name: Brian C. Steward
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Brian C. Steward
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Steward is Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Mr. Steward is also a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates. These are honors reflective of over three decades of complex civil litigation in Texas, Louisiana, New Jersey and New Mexico.

Mr. Steward was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 1990 as well as the Western, Southern, Northern and Eastern Districts of the Federal Court system in 1992. Mr. Steward was admitted to the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals in 1994. Although a civil trial lawyer, he has argued numerous cases to the Fourth Court of Appeals and submitted briefing to the Fifth Circuit on civil rights cases involving the use of excessive force by law enforcement personnel.

Before starting his own law firm, Mr. Steward was a senior associate with Strasburger and Price, L.P., which was followed by Ketterman, Rowland & Westlund. In these firms, he handled products liability, medical malpractice and business litigation matters through trial. In his own practice, he has continued to maintain a docket of products liability, medical malpractice and commercial dispute litigation but he has also become a certified mediator. Prior to the mediation certification, Mr. Steward has mediated cases since the inception of the Bexar County mediation system in 1992.

He has also remained engages with the San Antonio and Texas legal communities. He has presided over the Medical Legal Liaison Committee of the San Antonio Bar Association on three separate occasions. In 2021, the San Antonio Bar Association recognized Mr. Steward with the distinguished service award due to his work with various non-profit organizations in Texas and Massachusetts. He was also elected to chair the State Bar of Texas Grievance Committee District 10. He has also been active on the San Antonio Bar Association Diversity Task force created by Lawrence Morales, II. He currently serves as a Director of the San Antonio Trial Lawyers Association and is a former Director of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association.

His dedication and hard work have been recognized by his peers as evidenced by his selection as a Texas Super Lawyer (2016 to present) and Scene in San Antonio’s Best Lawyers since 2006. In 2015, he was first recognized as one of the best 25 personal injury litigators in San Antonio.

Mr. Steward is an active supporter of the State Bar of Texas Continuing Legal Education efforts. He has been a frequent contributor and presenter to these efforts since 1999. In 2015, he was tapped to serve as the Course Director the Advanced Personal Injury Trial Seminar in 2017. He has also presented at TTLA and SATLA seminars since 2015. He is an active member of the William S. Session’s Chapter of the American Inns of Court as well as mentor programs with St. Mary’s School of Law.

Mr. Steward is a native San Antonian, who attended school at St. Mark’s Episcopal and San Antonio Academy. After graduating from The Academy in 1979, he went to Deerfield Academy. After Deerfield, he went to Duke University, where he graduated with a degree in History. He returned to San Antonio to attend St. Mary’s School of Law. Mr. Steward has been a Board Member of San Antonio Academy as well as the president of the alumni association. He is currently the regional chair for the Duke University Alumni Admissions volunteers. He also works on the Executive Committee of the Deerfield Academy Alumni Council as the Vice President.

Mr. Steward has served as a Board Member on the San Antonio Library Foundation and the Child Advocates of San Antonio. He currently serves on the Board of the San Antonio Zoological Society and the San Antonio Book Festival.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ellen's practice areas focus on estate planning, as well as uncontested and contested probate and guardianship matters. She has a depth of litigation experience gained from her work representing clients in commercial and insurance litigation. Her practice encompasses all areas of estate/trust administration, representing executors, trustees, heirs and beneficiaries, and creditors, in routine estate administrations as well as complex and contested matters. Ellen has written and presented various CLE materials on probate estate administration.

Away from the office, Ellen Stewart works pro bono with Family Eldercare and Volunteer Legal Services on projects involving estate planning, probate and guardianship. Her volunteer work also includes serving on the Texas Wellness Conference Planning Committee (2006), serving on the board of directors for the ABA Estate Planning and Probate Section. Outside of the legal community, Ellen works with college students at Southwestern University and Texas State University as an advisor. Ellen previously served as the local president of the Greater Austin Alumni Association of Southwestern University from 2007-09 and still participates in the local alumni events. During the fall, you will find Ellen and her family supporting the pride of North Austin, the Anderson High School Trojan Band at football games and competitions. Ellen and her family are members of St. Theresa Catholic Church and former members of St. Thomas More Catholic Church.

attorneys.name: Chris Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Trial and litigation Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chris Stewart has secured successful outcomes for clients for more than 30 years in federal and state trial courts, appellate courts, arbitrations, administrative proceedings, and the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board. His litigation record reflects a strong command of complex commercial disputes, high-stakes business conflicts, intellectual property enforcement, and estate and probate litigation.

Chris represents clients nationwide in trademark registration, protection, and enforcement. He has registered more than 800 U.S. trademarks and regularly represents plaintiffs and defendants in trademark infringement disputes. His work includes Trademark Trial and Appeal Board proceedings, domain-name arbitrations, and brand protection matters involving online infringement.

Chris also maintains an active copyright practice, guiding clients through copyright registration and representing them in infringement disputes. His work frequently includes DMCA enforcement and social-media takedowns to protect copyrighted content and brand assets online.

In addition, Chris advises and represents clients in trade secret and restrictive covenant litigation, including disputes involving non-compete agreements and the misuse of proprietary information. He has represented both employers and employees in these matters.

Beyond intellectual property, Chris handles complex commercial litigation and business disputes across a wide range of industries. He regularly represents clients in federal and Texas state courts and has handled hundreds of cases. Representative clients include construction companies, engineering firms, trustees and beneficiaries, nonprofit organizations and churches, trucking companies, oil and gas businesses, commercial landlords, victims of personal injury, and insurance companies.

Chris has achieved favorable outcomes in a wide range of litigation matters. Representative results include:

Representing a cattle buyer in a fraud action involving co-mingled cattle and preserving the client’s favorable judgment against multiple post-trial challenges, followed by a successful appeal affirming the judgment. Ladd v. Harmon, 2025 Tex. App. LEXIS 6508 (Tex. App.—Amarillo 2025).

Obtaining settlements in 2025 on behalf of a trucking company against two first-party insurers following a rollover accident in California, along with a separate settlement against the company’s insurance agent.

Obtaining a full appraisal-value commissioner’s verdict in a 2025 eminent domain trial on behalf of a charitable foundation.

Successfully representing a luxury watch manufacturer in a counterfeiting action resulting in a default judgment awarding $14 million in statutory damages, plus attorneys’ fees and costs.

Rolex Watch USA, Inc. v. Trujillo, 2023 U.S. Dist. LEXIS 238147 (N.D. Tex. 2023).

Representing a restaurant in a copyright infringement dispute and prevailing on a motion to dismiss. Tayama v. RIOM Corp., 2012 WL 556007 (N.D. Tex. 2012).

Representing the family of a deceased professional wrestler in claims involving the unauthorized commercial use of the wrestler’s image and likeness.

Achieving a settlement in a trade-secret dispute involving proprietary engineering drawings while successfully defeating a petition for writ of mandamus during the litigation. In re N&T Specialty Welding & Mfg., 2008 WL 5050301 (Tex. App.—Amarillo 2008).

Securing reversal and remand of an adverse jury verdict for an oil and gas company in a livestock-damage case after the appellate court found the evidence factually insufficient to support the verdict. Duke Energy Field Services, L.P. v. Meyer, 190 S.W.3d 149 (Tex. App.—Amarillo 2005).

Obtaining summary judgment for an eye-care company defending against trademark infringement and unfair competition claims under the Lanham Act. Spectrum Vision Systems, Inc. v. Spectera, Inc., 35 F. Supp. 2d 797 (D. Kan. 1998).

Chris also negotiates contracts and licensing agreements. Representative clients include software companies, equipment manufacturers, restaurants, nonprofit organizations, authors, inventors, and online retailers.

Chris has extensive experience before the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board, having represented clients in more than 100 opposition and cancellation proceedings. His clients have included advertising agencies, equipment manufacturers, medical professionals, pet food companies, restaurants, banks, dentists, healthcare companies, candy manufacturers, law firms, grocery distributors, smoke and vape retailers, pharmacies, motorcycle accessory companies, ministries, and entertainment companies.

Chris also regularly represents trademark owners in domain-name arbitrations under the Uniform Domain-Name Dispute-Resolution Policy (UDRP). Since 2008, he has prevailed in numerous arbitrations on behalf of companies including a national real estate financing company targeted by phishing schemes, an international pet food company, a knife manufacturer, a retail pharmacy network, and a smoke and vape retailer. His work frequently involves stopping competitors and bad actors from using clients’ trademarks to divert business online.

PERSONAL

Outside of his legal practice, Chris operates a small side business selling vintage cards. His favorite card is a 1954 Topps Hank Aaron rookie card, a gift from his high school government teacher. Chris and his wife are members of Polk Street Methodist Church.

attorneys.name: Mr. Stephen W. Stewart
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Stephen W. Stewart was born in Odessa, Texas on December 13, 1965. Stephen was raised in Kerrville, Texas, where his family was involved in ranching and agriculture. He was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in 1997. Mr. Stewart's preparatory education was at Texas Tech University where he obtained a B.B.A. in Finance in 1993. In 1997, Stephen graduated from law school at Texas Tech University School of Law, with honors, graduating in the prestigious Order of the Coif. Mr. Stewart is licensed in all courts in the State of Texas. Additionally, he is admitted to the United States District Courts for the Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Districts of Texas.

For the preceding years in his legal career, Mr. Stewart has worked primarily as a trial lawyer representing major national and international businesses in civil litigation matters throughout the United States, where his practice included insurance defense; product liability defense of manufacturers of automobiles, aircraft, commercial vehicles, and construction / manufacturing equipment; catastrophic personal injury and wrongful death defense; as well as commercial litigation. Mr. Stewart has handled cases in both State and Federal Courts in Texas, in addition to multiple other States. Stephen's knowledge, skill, education, training, and experience, particularly that associated with his prior defense practice, make him uniquely qualified in being able to successfully prosecute the plaintiff cases that The Stewart Law Firm handles.

Stephen Stewart is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, in which membership is limited to attorneys who have won million and multi-million dollar verdicts, awards, and settlements. He is also a member of the American Association for Justice, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the Capital Area Trial Lawyers Association, the State Bar of Texas, and the Austin Bar Association.

Stephen and his wife, Ginger, have two children, Jackson and Jordan. Stephen and his family are actively involved in various community and charitable organizations, including the Make-A-Wish Foundation and Mothers Against Drunk Driving.

attorneys.name: Ty Stimpson
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ty Stimpson is a highly-regarded trial attorney who leads Varghese Summersett Injury Law Group, where he combines his passion for the law with his compassion for helping people who have had their lives shattered through no fault of their own.

Ty is a battle-tested attorney and skilled negotiator committed to getting justice and compensation for victims who are suffering due to the negligent or wrongful acts of others. He represents victims of catastrophic car wrecks, 18-wheeler accidents, motorcycle crashes, dangerous products, workplace injuries, and other serious injury or wrongful death cases in North Texas. Ty is a fierce advocate for his clients, working tirelessly to ensure that their rights are protected and that their voices are heard.

Make no mistake, Ty – a former Division 1 football player – is not afraid to stand up to big insurance companies and will never back down from a trial. He’s a strong believer in the power of the civil (and criminal) justice system and how it can hold wrongdoers accountable and make families whole again.

A native Texan, Ty grew up in Arlington and graduated from Baylor University, where he played linebacker. He received his Juris Doctor from Thurgood Marshall School of Law at Texas Southern University and his Masters of Law Degree from St. John’s University School of Law while working with the National Football League.

After law school, Ty returned to North Texas. He began his legal career as a prosecutor – first at the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office and later at the Tarrant County District Attorney’s Office. During his years of public service, he handled hundreds of cases, ranging from capital murder to identity theft. The wealth of knowledge and experience he gained as a chief criminal prosecutor positioned him perfectly to pursue justice for those who have been wrongfully injured or killed.

As he transitioned to private practice, Ty built a reputation for being a go-to personal injury attorney due to his exceptional negotiation and trial skills. He has been named a Top Attorney for Personal Injury by Fort Worth Magazine and 360 West Magazine. He is also a National Trial Lawyer Top 40 Under 40 member. Recently, he received the 2023 Dr. Marion Brooks “Legend in the Making” Award for Law by the Beta Tau Lambda Charitable Foundation and the Beta Tau Lambda Chapter of the Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc.

When he is not in the office or courtroom, you will find Ty out in the community, giving back in any way he can.

Ty serves on numerous boards and is a member of an ever-growing list of amazing organizations, including:

Tarrant Area Food Bank, Board Chair-Elect

Boys and Girls Club of Greater Tarrant County, Board Member

LTV Rise, Board Chair (a project dedicated to serving Fort Worth’s Las Vegas Trail community)

Young Men’s Leadership Academy, Advisory Board Member

attorneys.name: Susannah A. Stinson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Susannah A. Stinson has successfully handled and favorably resolved hundreds of family law disputes for a wide array of clients.

Her decades of experience range from difficult divorces involving high net worth/complex property issues and emotionally-charged child custody matters, to paternity suits, modifications, protective orders, and pre- and post-nuptial agreements, to the many types of enforcement matters inherent in family law matters.

In addition to being Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Family Law, Susannah is recognized as a Best Lawyer in Family Law, has been listed among various Super Lawyers honors over her years of practice, including as a "Super Lawyer" and "Rising Star," and she was named to the "Top 50 for Central and West Texas" for two consecutive years. In addition, she has also been listed in "Top Women Attorneys in Texas" and Austin Monthly as a "Top Attorney for Family Law," so it is no surprise that Susannah maintains AVVO "Superb" and Martindale Hubbell "Preeminent" ratings.

In everything she does, Susannah makes the time to deliver compassionate and effective representation and results that reflect each client's personal and distinct familial objectives. Susannah knows, from many years of first-hand, honed family law practice, that each client and case is unique. She provides both the sensitivity and candid answers to the many questions her clients ask and the thorough and disciplined approach to problem-solving and advocacy required to navigate beyond the emotional mire when resolving seemingly insurmountable turmoil. Whether through discrete negotiation, mediation, before state and/or federal courts across myriad counties, at trial, or on appeal, Susannah is about getting her clients beyond what is considered one of the most stressful events of their lives.

Clients and colleagues alike appreciate that Susannah gives her all in everything she does. She is described as a top-notch professional who is skilled, thorough, detail-oriented, patient, and someone who clients trust entirely and has been referred to as the best choice (the client had) ever made. Clients also say that Susannah is "a winner in your corner" who can step into a volatile situation and methodically present the case and realize "a favorable outcome." See more reviews below or by visiting her AVVO reviews.
