attorneys.name: Felix Valenzuela
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in El Paso, TX
attorneys.bio:
Felix Valenzuela grew up in northeast El Paso and graduated from Andress High School. He then went on to pursue higher education at the University of Texas at El Paso ("UTEP"), graduating cum laude. Thereafter, he received his law degree from Yale Law School, where he was an editor for the Yale Journal of Law and the Humanities and a William S. Beinecke Scholar. Felix also received a Masters Degree in Political Science from the University of Notre Dame, where he was selected as the Joseph L. Gaia Distinguished Fellow in Latino Studies. While at Notre Dame, he also worked as an associate attorney for the Merino Law Firm. Felix then returned home to El Paso, Texas and served as a law clerk for United States Federal Judge Philip R. Martinez. In 2013, the El Paso Young Lawyers Association selected Felix as the Outstanding Young Lawyer of the year.

Since 2007, Felix has been an itinerant core faculty member of UTEP's Law School Preparation Institute, where he taught legal reasoning and provided instruction on the Law School Admissions Test. He has also taught various courses at UTEP, including Social Media and the Law, Courts in Action, and Philosophy of Law.

Felix is daddy to three daughters and spends his free time shuttling them back and forth from swim meets to piano lessons.

attorneys.name: Katie Valle
attorneys.firm_name: Bryant, Colletti, Kaplan, Kinsler, & De La Reza, LLP
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Katie Valle’s practice focuses on divorce, complex child-custody and property disputes, and cases involving family violence and substance use. She brings a steady, trauma-informed approach to high-conflict matters. Prior to private practice, Katie served as Family Legal Services Director with Volunteer Legal Services, representing families fleeing violence and substance abuse, and mentoring attorneys new to family law. She currently sits on the Board of Directors for the Austin Bar Association Family Law Section.

Katie is candid and practical, empowering clients with clear advice so they can make informed decisions for their families. Katie experienced multiple parental divorces as a child and adolescent and is intimately familiar with the trauma divorce can create for a child as well as the stress associated with the introduction of new people and new family units. She empathizes with clients in a unique way and deeply respects the need to make any transition as easy for children as possible. While she works to resolve conflicts in the most collaborative way possible, Katie is an advocate in her soul and ready to fight for her clients in the courtroom.

Outside the office, Katie volunteers with local legal-services organizations and her children’s school community. A proud Longhorn, she is married to an Aggie and enjoys the friendly rivalry at home.

attorneys.name: Martin Valko
attorneys.practice_type: U.S. Immigration and Nationality Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Martin Valko is a founding partner of Chavez & Valko, LLP, managing its principal office in Dallas. He has navigated the complexities of the U.S. immigration process for decades-both as an immigration attorney and as an immigrant himself. His diverse practice embraces family, humanitarian, and employment-based immigration, along with the pursuit of temporary nonimmigrant visas.

Martin focuses primarily on representing both individual and corporate clients ranging from small businesses and startups to Fortune companies and transnational corporations. A former collegiate athlete himself, Martin has advised and represented other collegiate and amateur athletes and Olympians as well as professional teams and players from the NFL, NHL, and the USA Cricket Association.

Due to this deep and wide experience and a desire to give back, Martin is a frequent speaker at educational and business seminars on various immigration law topics. He is a former committee member of the AILA National USCIS Field Operations Liaison Committee as well the AILA National USCIS Service Centers Liaison Committee (SCOPS/Texas Service Center). He is also a legal advisor to the Mexican Consulate General in Dallas (2011 - 2027) as well as to the Slovak Embassy on U.S. immigration laws and represents the Slovak Republic as its Honorary Consul to Texas (since 2010).

A testament to his varied skillset and interests, Martin's career has included forays outside of traditional immigration law, into entertainment law and tech. Through his representation of legendary Slovak pop/rock singer Pavol Habera and his band TEAM, Martin obtained an out-of-court settlement with Sony Pictures regarding the use of the band's song in the 2005 horror film Hostel, including a written apology from the film's director, Eli Roth. Martin is also a co-founder of Lawpilot, an immigration case management platform that includes the Lawpilot Guardian, a one-of-a-kind mobile app that alerts attorneys of a client's encounter with ICE or the police, providing instant GPS location information and an audio recording.

Outside of the office, Martin is husband to a 5-time Olympian (2-time Olympic silver medalist) and a World Champion swimmer, Martina Moravcova Valko, and father to their children, Karolina and Michal with whom he resides in Dallas, Texas. He is an avid cyclist and spends his free time with an interesting book.

attorneys.name: David Andrew Van Buskirk
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate and Commercial Transactions Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
David Andrew "Andy" Van Buskirk's practice is devoted to commercial real estate, corporate and commercial transactions.

His real estate practice covers all aspects of commercial real estate, including leasing, acquisition, disposition, development and financing of all types of commercial real estate. He has experience representing buyers, sellers, developers, lenders, landlords and tenants of all types of commercial real estate including raw land, office buildings, retail centers, industrial projects and residential developments.

His corporate and commercial practice covers most aspects of business law from the formation to disposition of business entities and everything in between including acquisitions, mergers, restructuring, management buy outs, review and preparation of various agreements and the representation and counseling of clients in their ongoing business activities.

Representative Experience:

Represent several real estate investors and developers in connection with the acquisition and sale of all types of commercial real estate including retail centers, office buildings, mixed-use projects, apartments, industrial projects and raw land.

Represent several real estate developers in connection with the acquisition and development of raw land for retail use, residential developments and industrial projects.

Represent both landlords and tenants in commercial leasing including representing tenants in Class A retail centers such as the Galleria and landlords leasing their retail centers.

Represented real estate developer and contractor in the acquisition and financing of raw land, negotiation and drafting of build to suite lease and construction of 70,000 square foot single tenant building.

Represented several out-of-state investors in the purchase of properties within Texas.

Represented owner in the refinance of multi-property mixed-use development.

Represent several local entrepreneurs in the acquisition and sale of various businesses including service firms, construction, restaurants, bars and various other businesses and the continued representation of such businesses.

Form and represent numerous entities including limited liability companies, partnerships and corporations in multiple states including obtaining various business licenses in numerous states.

Represent numerous entrepreneurs in all aspects of their various investments including real estate, franchises, lending and other business ventures.

Represented industrial container company in the sale of its business for $34 million to publically traded corporation.

Represented construction business in the sale of its business for several million in cash, stock and earn out to a publically traded construction company.

Represented family-owned oil and gas services company in connection with the sale of its business for $7.5 million to a publicly traded oil and gas services company.

attorneys.name: Kay L. Van Wey
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kay Van Wey is a Board Certified Personal Injury Trial Lawyer with over 25 years of experience. She was selected by her peers as a Texas Super Lawyer for eleven consecutive years (2003–2012).

Kay has also attained membership in the Million Dollar Advocates Forum and the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum in recognition of the results she has achieved for her clients.

Kay Van Wey began her legal career in 1984 in her hometown of Lawton, Oklahoma as a Comanche County Assistant District Attorney. As a young prosecutor, Kay gained valuable courtroom experience. She later built upon the fundamentals she learned as a prosecutor as she tried numerous civil and criminal cases throughout Texas and Oklahoma.

Over the years, Kay Van Wey has focused her practice on representing plaintiffs in personal injury litigation. She has represented many people who have become the unwitting victims of catastrophic personal injury or wrongful death. She has received national media attention for her work and achievements on her clients' behalf.

Kay Van Wey is licensed to practice law in Texas, Oklahoma, and Illinois and is admitted to practice before the US District Court for Northern District of Texas, the US District Court for Eastern District of Texas, the US District Court for the Western District of Oklahoma and the US District Court for the Northern District of Oklahoma.

attorneys.name: Lisa A. Vance
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Lisa A. Vance, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lisa has over 40 years of wide-ranging experience as a trial lawyer in state and federal courts, winning significant verdicts for companies with challenging disputes, including dangerous vicarious liability claims of sexual assault and murder as well as document-intensive national litigation. She founded her own law firm in San Antonio, in 2001, now focused on all aspects of family law.

Lisa advocates for a gentler approach to marital termination, convinced that a family's energies should be spent on the healthy development of children rather than end-of-marriage angst. Her practice has expanded from litigation to collaborative law, and in addition to practicing collaboratively when possible, she also advocates for working in tandem with mental health professionals to help married couples and their children work toward healing.

When situations call for litigation, however, particularly in protecting families, she successfully promotes the best interests of her clients and their children in the courtroom. Abuse and violence is prevalent in many forms, and these call for aggressive trial strategies-to protect the victims.

Lisa's clients know her as someone who really cares about them and their family. She works hard to find solutions that work for all the members of the client's family, regardless of what that family looks like. Lisa's firm is based on the realization that for all of us, our families matter most. Choosing a lawyer to protect a family's future, and work toward peace of mind, is a critically important decision. And for this firm, we are acutely aware of the obligation that imposes on us.

Lisa has accumulated numerous awards throughout her career. She has been named one of the city's Best Family Lawyers by SA Scene magazine every year since their survey began, a Texas Super Lawyer, and an AV lawyer, meaning that her clients and peers have found her to have the highest skills and ethics. Lisa is most proud of creating a firm registered in the Martindale-Hubble Bar Register of Pre-Eminent Lawyers, made up of talented, knowledgeable lawyers who allow her to serve the wide-ranging family law needs of a diverse clientele.

What clients may not know about Lisa is how deeply she loves her non-human friends and family-and the value of their participation as peace-promoters. She learned the value of having animals present in the firm decades ago, when she worked with distraught law students. Lisa was in charge of the recruiting efforts for the local office of an international law firm. It was up to her to be sure that the students who came to the firm understood their responsibilities. That experience could be frightening for young law students, and sometimes, they would need support. As scared students would shyly come to Lisa and close her door, it would not take long to ferret out their fears. So, Lisa developed the habit of placing one of her fat white rabbits into the student's laps. As the student stroked the rabbit, all the anxiety would float away, and the students could talk and plan.

There are now three cats and four bunnies who live in the office. A few of the office staff bring their dogs with them daily. The bunnies are brought out when clients, who have no other choice, bring their children along. The children can sit next to the bunny cage and just watch bunny antics. The animals are never seen by clients, unless the situation needs them. If a client is fearful or is just not a critter-lover, they work with the lawyers and paralegals in a conference room and never know the animals are there.

At home, Lisa and her husband have rescued horses, donkeys, goats, dogs-and no telling how many cats have shown up for cuddles and kibbles. At the end of a long day of working through the pain of her clients, Lisa will bury her face in the neck of one of the rescued horses, and her own stress bubbles away.

At the end of a long day of working through the pain of her clients, Lisa will bury her face in the neck of one of the rescued horses, and her own stress bubbles away.

attorneys.name: Edward DiMare Vassallo Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Eminent Domain Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Founder of the firm, Edward DiMare Vassallo, Jr. focuses his practice in the areas of commercial litigation, real estate, eminent domain, inverse condemnation, condemnation, zoning, planning, and land use.

Mr. Vassallo is a native of Dallas and has served clients in Texas throughout his career. He received his B.A. in 1967 and Juris Doctor degree in 1969 from Southern Methodist University. While in law school, he was a member of the legal fraternity Phi Delta Phi and a member of the Order of the Barristers and served as Chief Justice of the Moot Court Board. From 1968 to 1969 he served as a member of the Southwestern Law Journal.

Mr. Vassallo was admitted to the Texas Bar and the U.S. District Court, Northern District of Texas in 1969. In 1975, he was admitted to the U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Texas and the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Texas. He was admitted to the U.S. Court of Appeals, Fifth Circuit and the U.S. Claims Court in 1988.

Mr. Vassallo is a member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association, the American Bar Association and the State Bar of Texas, where he served as a member of the State Bar Grievance Committee.

Mr. Vassallo has hosted and lectured on State and Federal Eminent Domain, Federal Inverse Condemnation and Environmental Liability for State Bar of Texas and American Bar Association as well as a Continuing Legal Education International Lecturer from 1980 - present. He has delivered over 125 papers and lectures in real estate law and litigation in Texas and several other states. The firm has been and is currently involved in eminent domain cases in Texas, Arizona, California, Colorado, Nevada, North Carolina, Washington, and other jurisdictions.

Mr. Vassallo has extensive experience as an author and lecturer on topics such as eminent domain, inverse condemnation, environmental liability, and eminent domain trials. He is the author of articles such as "Law of Eminent Domain," "Anatomy of an Eminent Domain Trial," "Problems in Real Estate," "Real Estate Litigation Guide," "Use of Expert Witnesses," and numerous other articles on State and Federal Eminent Domain, Trial Strategy and Environmental Law. He has also authored statutory changes in the Texas Property Code which is currently practiced in 35 different counties in Texas.

attorneys.name: Vincent P. Vasquez
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Vincent P. Vasquez was born and raised in San Antonio, Texas. Following graduation from St. Anthony's Catholic High School, Vincent attended St. Mary's University, where he worked full-time while taking a full-time class load in order to put himself through college. After graduation, Vincent continued his education at St. Mary's School of Law. After graduating from law school in 2008 and becoming licensed, Vincent has worked in litigation his entire career as a lawyer throughout state and federal courts in Texas.

Prior to joining the Gámez Law Firm, Vincent worked for seven years for an insurance defense firm in San Antonio primarily defending commercial trucking companies and their drivers when sued as a result of motor vehicle crashes. This experience exposed Vincent to the inner workings of insurance companies and how commercial vehicle claims are evaluated.

This experience also allowed Vincent thoroughly understand how the trucking industry operates and the numerous federal and state regulations that govern their operations from hiring to driving. Vincent also has experience in defending insurance companies directly when sued by their policy holders following the denial of benefits under the insurance policy.

"Based on my experience as an insurance defense attorney, I'm very familiar with the tactics insurance companies will use to devalue and minimize your claim while trying to save every penny to benefit their bottom line," Vincent said. "Now that I'm working in personal injury law, I want to help injured Texans fight to get what they are rightfully owed."

Shortly after joining the Gámez Law firm, Vincent successfully settled two significant commercial cases.

attorneys.name: Daniel Vazquez
attorneys.practice_type: General Counsel Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
“As the son of an immigrant business owner, I saw my father struggle to navigate his small business through situations with adverse results that could have been mitigated or avoided with the advice of counsel. Now, I strive to be a resource and an advisor to other Hispanic business owners.”

Solutions for Unique Concerns of Cross-Border Businesses

Daniel’s role as an outside general counsel has given him experience in a wide array of transactions, from the acquisition of a sizable oil field services companies to entity creation for small startups, Daniel has proven that he can accomplish his clients’ goals. His clients benefit from the diversity of his experiences in niche or cross-industry problems. Companies’ legal needs are complex, and Daniel excels in this complexity due to his breadth of experiences.

Many of Daniel’s clients are Latin American businesses or families looking for investment opportunities or to transition their business to the US. Daniel’s highly coveted experience in the corporate office of PEMEX in Mexico and with federal judges in largely Hispanic border regions of Texas, combined with his own bicultural background, allows him to connect with clients from Mexico or Latin America and relate to their particular cross-border needs and concerns as they seek business, investment, or real-estate opportunities in the US.

Legal Structures for Long-term Success

Transitioning from an emerging company to a high-growth company entails logistical and legal challenges. This transition’s quick pace sometimes becomes an obstacle to a long-term strategic approach to business success. As a Collaborative Business Counsel, Daniel provides strategies and solutions to manage the legal needs of this transition efficiently. He handles contracts, acquisitions, and investments and coordinates cohesively with a network of professionals to meet these needs. With Daniel behind the details, business owners can reclaim their time for what matters most-their business’s continued success.

Relational and Efficient Communication

Daniel strives for clear, efficient communication, actively listening to the clients’ goals, and working diligently to accomplish those goals. He also appreciates the ongoing advisory relationships with clients that the firm cultivates. He devotes his full attention to the tasks at hand, with an objective, balanced attitude that allows him to calmly adapt to the diverse set of challenges that come with inter-industry and international work.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Victor Vazquez is an associate attorney at Naimeh Salem and Associates PLLC. He was born and raised in El Paso, Texas. His ethnic background inspired his legal studies and career as an immigration attorney. Attorney Vazquez has experience representing clients in removal defense proceedings in Immigration Court and in matters before the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

Attorney Vazquez earned his Bachelor’s Degree in Political Science from Texas Lutheran University in 2019. He also served as a legislative intern in the U.S. House of Representatives for the current Congressional representative Veronica Escobar of the 16th Congressional District of El Paso in 2019. While serving as a congressional intern, Attorney Vazquez was enrolled as an undergraduate student at American University in Washington D.C. He pursued his legal education and graduated from Thurgood Marshall School of Law in 2023, where he served as Chief of Staff of the Student Bar Association.

Attorney Vazquez is admitted to practice law in New Mexico and in the Immigration Courts throughout the United States.

attorneys.name: Amber Vazquez
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Amber Vazquez has had years of misdemeanor, felony and federal trial experience and has a full service staff to attend to her clients' needs. After graduating from the University of Texas, she attended law school at the University of Denver College of Law, where she served as vice-president of the student body, served as president of the DU Political forum and wrote several articles on international human rights, criminal law and politics.

Amber is a passionate and zealous advocate who always puts her clients interests first. She has built her firm around the idea that every client deserves the best representation possible, and is always willing to take cases to trial if necessary.

Amber cares about how criminal justice affects our community, and currently serves on the Board of Directors for Truth Be Told, a non-profit organization that assists women in prison get the counseling, education and support to transition out of prison. In addition, she is actively involved in the Hispanic Bar Association of Austin, the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and the National Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

She is also well connected in the legal community and currently serves as Chairperson for the Criminal Justice Section of the Austin Bar Association as well as serving as Vice-President of the American Bar Association's Criminal Justice Section YLD.

In her spare time, Amber loves being with her kids, two French Bulldogs, gardening, cooking, traveling, yoga, and making floral arrangements.

attorneys.name: Daniel Vela
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Daniel Vela was born and raised in San Antonio, Texas. He graduated from Burbank High School and attended St. Mary's University in San Antonio, Texas. While at St. Mary's, he played the trumpet in the University band. Mr. Vela was on the Dean's List and received a Bachelor of Business Administration degree in Finance. In addition, while going to undergraduate school, he worked at United Services Automobile Association (USAA), as an insurance adjuster. Mr. Vela worked in the evenings while attending college during the day.

In 1995, Mr. Vela continued his education at St. Mary's University School of Law. During law school, Mr. Vela interned at the Bexar County District Attorney's Office, participating in felony trials.

After graduating from law school in 1998, Mr. Vela was hired by the District Attorney's Office, where he gained valuable trial experience in cases ranging from Driving While Intoxicated to Murders. His last position at the District Attorney's Office was as a Felony Prosecutor in the White Collar Trial Division.

In 2003, Mr. Vela left the District Attorney's Office and opened his private practice where he focused primarily on Criminal Defense, Family Law, and Personal Injury Law. In 2005, Daniel Vela and Gladys Del Fierro formed the law firm, Vela & Del Fierro, PLLC, where he has been a managing partner to date. The firm focuses primarily on Family Law, State Criminal Defense (including Bail Bond assistance for clients), Federal Criminal Defense and Personal Injury.

Mr. Vela was featured on Fox 29 News to provide his expert opinion on Federal Mandatory Minimum Sentences.

Mr. Vela is currently licensed to practice law by the State Bar of Texas, the United States Western District, the United States Southern District and the United States Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals. He is also a member of the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association and the San Antonio Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Morgan Velasquez
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
As a Supervisory Attorney at the Devadoss Law Firm PLLC, Morgan primarily focuses on litigating discrimination and adverse employment actions before the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and the Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB). She also handles internal employment investigations, Office of Special Counsel (OSC) complaints, and assists clients with responding to proposed discipline. Additionally, Morgan has experience negotiating settlement agreements on behalf of federal employees. Throughout her legal career, Morgan has handled countless cases involving federal government agencies such as USPS, Veterans Affairs, U.S. Attorney's Office, National Security Agency, and many more. In addition to her own practice, Morgan supervises and provides guidance to our associate and senior associate attorneys.

Morgan's philosophy is that great attorneys do not just know the law but also know their clients. No two situations are the same, and a victory can look different for different clients. As such, Morgan prides herself in working with clients not only as their attorney but as their advocate.

Originally from Kalamazoo, Michigan, Morgan is a graduate of Calvin University, where she obtained her bachelor's degree in Spanish and psychology. Morgan moved to Dallas, Texas where she obtained her juris doctor from Southern Methodist University Dedman School of Law. While in law school, Morgan was an active member of the Hispanic Law Student Association and Criminal Clinic representing indigent defendants. In her spare time, Morgan enjoys traveling, cooking, cheering for Tottenham Hotspur, and spending time with her family and friends.

attorneys.name: Kent G. Vestal Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Disputes Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
With his background as a CPA and real estate developer, and with more than 30 years’ experience practicing law, Kent Greer Vestal, Jr., is exceptionally suited to handle a variety of issues facing Blazier, Christensen, Browder & Virr, P.C.’s business and tax clients. Over the years he has successfully helped companies of various sizes navigate legal issues related to taxes, employment, real estate, business disputes, business formation and estate planning, among others.

Early in his career, Mr. Vestal spent time working in both large and small companies serving as a former Vice President of one of the largest firms on Wall Street, and later in the capacities of general counsel and chief financial officers for several small to medium-sized businesses. It was the latter that helped him find his passion for helping small business clients manage the unique legal and financial issues inherent in their day-to-day operation.

His practicing philosophy is that while obstacles to business success are inevitable, no problem is too large to overcome. He prides himself on consistently meeting the challenges that small businesses face.

Mr. Vestal attended Hendrix College and The University of Arkansas, receiving a B.S.B.A in Accounting in 1981. He received his law degree from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock’s Bowen School of Law in 1987 and is licensed to practice in three states: Arkansas, New York and Texas. He has worked as remote counsel to the Firm for several years and now resides in Austin to take on a more central role.

A 25-year member of the Arkansas Bar Association, Mr. Vestal is also a member of the New York State Bar Association, AICPA and the Texas Bar Association.

During his spare time, Mr. Vestal enjoys spending time with family, including his three sons, who are active in the youth sports of baseball and basketball, and also enjoy fishing and sharing hobbies with their dad. He serves as a community volunteer on the White Oak Bayou Wetlands Management Steering Committee.

attorneys.name: Kevin W. Vice
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Royse City, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kevin Vice's journey in the legal profession is a testament to his unwavering commitment to excellence. Born in Abilene, Texas, and raised in Dallas, he embarked on a path of academic distinction early in life. His pursuit of knowledge and dedication to his craft have culminated in a distinguished career.

Kevin's educational foundation is marked by high achievements. He graduated with high honors from Hillcrest High School in Dallas, setting the stage for his future accomplishments. He continued to excel academically, earning a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) degree from the University of North Texas, graduating cum laude.

Recognizing the importance of a well-rounded education, Kevin ventured into the world of business, gaining valuable experience before he decided to further his legal aspirations. He earned his Juris Doctorate degree from Texas Tech University School of Law, an institution known for its rigorous academic standards. Kevin's academic prowess was affirmed when he was admitted into the prestigious Order of the Coif, an honor reserved for those who graduate in the top 10% of their class.

In 1992, Kevin was admitted to the State Bar of Texas, marking the beginning of his legal career. Over the years, he expanded his reach, gaining admission to practice in all Texas State Courts, as well as the Federal United States District Courts for the Northern, Eastern, and Southern Districts of Texas, as well as the United States District Court for the Northern District of California and the U.S. Court of Appeals 5th Circuit.

Today, Kevin stands as a managing partner of Vice Henley and Dilbeck, PLLC. His legal practice is dedicated to advocating for individuals who have suffered injuries due to the negligence of others.

Kevin's professional mission revolves around delivering a world-class service experience to each client and fostering an equally remarkable work environment for his team members. He upholds core values of integrity, dedication, optimism, and compassion, recognizing the potential in every individual. He supports and challenges his team members to reach the highest standards because he believes in their ability to achieve greatness when striving for the truest purpose: providing exceptional service to clients and society as a whole.

Committed to making Vice Henley & Dilbeck the premier personal injury law firm in Texas, Kevin's vision and dedication have fueled the firm's growth without compromising its commitment to outstanding client service. His leadership has made a lasting impact on the legal landscape, setting a standard of excellence that inspires both his colleagues and clients alike.

attorneys.name: Karen M. Villanueva
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning (wills, trusts & powers of attorney) Lawyers in Temple, TX
attorneys.bio:
A native Central Texan, Karen graduated magna cum laude from St. Edward’s University in 2013 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science. In 2016, she received her Doctor of Jurisprudence with a concentration in Estate Planning from Baylor Law School. While in law school, she was also a member of Baylor Law’s Pro Bono Transactional Team that helped draft estate planning documents for members of the community.

Following law school, Karen volunteered with client legal services at Fort Sill, Oklahoma, preparing estate planning documents for soldiers and their families. After PCS’ing with her husband to Fort Bliss, Texas, she practiced with a prominent El Paso law firm, Firth Bunn Kerr Neill. During her time in El Paso, Karen’s experiences ranged from simple, uncontested probate and guardianship cases to contentious, litigated trust disputes and complex will and guardianship contests.

Karen joined the firm in February 2021, where her practice areas include probate, guardianship, and estate planning. Karen is a member of the State Bar of Texas, REPTL (the Real Estate, Probate, and Trust Law section of the bar), and the Bell County Bar Association. She is also certified to represent both applicants and proposed wards in guardianship proceedings.

When Karen isn’t working, she enjoys gardening, reading, quilting and crafts, and spending time with her husband and three sons.

attorneys.name: Thomas F. Virr
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
As a director at Blazier, Christensen, Bigelow & Virr, P.C., Tom Virr advises both individuals and small businesses on tax planning, tax controversy, estate planning and probate matters. Mr. Virr’s previous experience as an Estate Tax Attorney, District Conferee and Appeals Officer for the Internal Revenue Service, as well as his years in private practice, lend a particular depth and insight to his work with the Firm’s clients. He has also assisted in the formation and operation of numerous charitable entities.

Mr. Virr was born in Topeka, Kansas. He received his B.A. degree from the University of Texas 1967. Following graduation, he entered in the U.S. Navy, was commissioned as an officer, and served aboard the U.S.S. Washburn, LKA108 for three years, including two deployments to Vietnam. He was awarded the Navy Achievement Medal with combat distinguishing device for his service.

Mr. Virr returned to the University of Texas at Austin to obtain his J. D. in 1972, and was admitted to the Texas state bar in 1973. He is Board Certified in Tax Law, by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He is an active member of the Austin Bar Association, and is licensed to appear before the U.S. Tax Court, and the U.S. District Court, Western District of Texas.

Mr. Virr is a charter member of Triumphant Love Lutheran Church, founded in Austin in 1977. He has served that congregation in a number of capacities over the years, including assisting in the creation of an Endowment Fund for the congregation.

Pursuing a life-long interest in agriculture, Mr. Virr currently operates a cattle ranch in Lampasas County. He enjoys sharing the rural lifestyle with both grandchildren and with friends.

David is sorely missed by all who knew him.

Throughout his career, Jim has helped families structure their affairs in order to eliminate the threat of government intervention into their private lives and protect their assets from lawsuits. In the process, he has helped families save millions of dollars in estate taxes and probate costs.

Jim primarily represents individuals and business owners in both business and estate planning matters.

attorneys.name: Aaron Von Flatern
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Aaron von Flatern is a founding partner of FVF Law and one of the most trusted Austin personal injury attorneys for individuals and families facing serious injuries or wrongful death. As a former insurance adjuster turned Austin injury lawyer, Aaron brings rare insider knowledge of how insurers evaluate claims, giving his clients a strategic edge in cases involving car accidents, truck accidents, catastrophic injuries, and wrongful death.

Aaron is known for breaking down complex legal and insurance issues into clear, actionable guidance – helping clients understand their rights, the value of their case, and what to expect at every step. His balanced approach of practical advice and trial-ready advocacy has made him a go-to personal injury lawyer in Austin for people who want an attorney who actually explains the process, not just promises results.

Aaron’s results have earned him membership in the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum® and Million Dollar Advocates Forum, distinctions reserved for attorneys who have secured significant recoveries for their clients. He has been recognized as a Texas Super Lawyers® honoree since 2022, following four consecutive years as a Super Lawyers® Rising Star.

A proud Longhorn, Aaron earned his economics degree from the University of Texas before receiving his J.D. from Baylor Law School. Outside the courtroom, he’s all Austin – supporting Austin FC, catching live music, seeking out good barbecue, and attempting exactly one marathon, which he’s happy to leave in the past. His greatest joy is coaching his son Fielder’s baseball team, where he brings the same heart, patience, and leadership he’s known for in his practice.

attorneys.name: BILL VOSS
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial and Business Litigation Lawyers in The Woodlands, TX
attorneys.bio:
Bill Voss and the attorneys at The Voss Law Firm, P.C. have expertise in areas of commercial and business litigation, business law, insurance litigation, wrongful death litigation, offshore injuries, catastrophic personal injury litigation, employment litigation, oil and gas law, rare coin fraud and first party insurance claims. If you need legal assistance and want results, contact The Voss Law Firm, P.C. toll free at 866-276-6179.

Attorney Bill Voss is a ninth-generation Texan who had the opportunity to grow up overseas. His father, James David Voss, started out as a roughneck on derricks in West Texas and after 15 years in the oil patch was promoted to operator for OTIS Engineering. The opportunity - his family was transferred to Saudi Arabia. Bill Voss now looks at the move as something he wouldn't trade for a buffalo nickel. "The travel was a tremendous opportunity to get to know so many types of great people and learn the ways of many cultures. It truly helped me understand viewpoints from so many different angles."

But Mr. Voss' story goes much further back than the move to a foreign land. His grandmother, on his mother's side, Billie Prue "Crockett" Parnell, is a direct descendant of Davy Crockett - yes, "the Davy Crockett". Records indicate the Wilburn (Billie Prue's other side) and the Crockett families were one of the first 12 families granted permission by Mexico to farm Texas. The Wilburn and Crockett families settled in what is now known as Fort Worth. You can read more on their interesting journey and eventual move to New Mexico to raise sheep in a book titled Ghosts Of The Guadalupes.

Attorney Bill Voss serves individuals and business owners helping them resolve their disputes with the passion his clients deserve. He has been recognized in local and national publications such as The Legal News, Forbes, Newsweek, Inc. 500, Texas Monthly, H Texas Magazine, Texas Lawyer and The Houston Press. He has been named a Super Lawyer - Rising Star by his peers, as well as a Top Attorney in the Country by Newsweek Magazine. He was recently named one of Houston's Top Attorneys for the People.

Attorney Bill Voss is passionate about the law and helping the proverbial "little guy." "I truly enjoy what I do, bringing wrong doers to justice and helping clients, especially in those ‘Gorilla-type' cases." Hard work and tenacity are attributes that helped Mr. Voss achieve success not only in trial, but also in life and these qualities are ones he impresses on the attorneys and staff of The Voss Law Firm. "We have an outstanding track record of success here. We have the resources and experience to handle the largest, most complex cases. Clients and referring attorneys can be assured that we do not back down in the face of adversity. The tougher and bigger the opposition, the better for our law firm; we get completely fired up for a good legal battle. Those are the type of employees that I have assembled here, ones that are going to fight hard for our clients. We wouldn't have it any other way."

attorneys.name: Nicole Voyles
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Nicole Voyles enjoys helping clients navigate their way through family law matters, always remembering that it is important to listen to their particular needs and finding a way to assist them in having these needs met in the most amicable way possible. Nicole has experience in complex property disputes, custody matters, paternity matters, and premarital and marital property.

Nicole graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a degree in Marketing prior to attending law school at Southern Methodist University in Dallas. Once she graduated from law school, Nicole practiced insurance defense and general litigation before turning her focus to family law which provides her a broad background in the law. Nicole immediately fell in love with family law in that it allows her to help people manage a very difficult time in their lives, while also making certain that person and their children are protected in the future. Nicole’s end goal is to make sure the client and their family make it through the experience as unharmed emotionally and financially as possible. Nicole thinks outside of the box to create a final settlement that suits the client’s specific desires and needs.

Nicole has been board certified since 2010 and is a fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers since 2015. She is often asked to write for and speak at at continuing legal education seminars throughout the state. Nicole is extremely active in the Houston Bar Association. She has been a co-chair on several different committees. She also is a board member of Houston Young Lawyers Foundation and the Houston Volunteer Lawyers.

Outside of practicing law, Nicole enjoys working out and competes in various running races and triathlons. She is also a volunteer with Victory which supports the efforts of the American Cancer Society.

attorneys.name: Leslie Vásquez Rodriguez
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Leslie Vásquez Rodriguez was born and raised in Weslaco, Texas. She received a Bachelor of Arts in English and Communication Studies from St. Mary’s University in 2007, graduating summa cum laude. She graduated from St. Mary’s University School of Law in May 2014. While attending St. Mary’s University School of Law, Leslie was a member of the External Advocacy Program’s national mock trial team and was admitted into the Order of the Barristers. After law school, Leslie was sworn in as an Assistant District Attorney, at the Bexar County District Attorney’s Office, where she was promoted into a felony prosecutor supervisory role and then later to the Major Crimes Division. As an Assistant District Attorney, Leslie tried and supervised over 30 jury trials to verdict. Before returning to the Plaintiff’s bar, Leslie practiced insurance defense litigation, handling auto and commercial vehicle accident litigation, in both state and federal court. Leslie serves on the Board of Directors of the St. Mary's University School of Law Alumni Association, on the Board of Directors of San Antonio Trial Lawyers Association, on the Board of Directors and as a Past-President of the Hispanic Law Alumni Association, on the Board of Directors of the Bexar County Women’s Bar Association, and is Adjunct Faculty at St. Mary's University School of Law, in the Advocacy Program—mentoring and coaching the incoming generation of trial lawyers and community advocates is one of Leslie’s favorite ways of giving back to her legal community. Her greatest treasures—and the reason behind everything she does—are her two children, Luke David and Ryan Grace, and her partner and co-counsel in life, her husband—a civil litigator in his own right—David Rodriguez.

attorneys.name: M. Brandon Waddell
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Waddell concentrates his practice on the representation of design professionals and resolving construction and business disputes. Mr. Waddell is consistently retained by many of the nation’s largest design firms and insurance carriers to defend design professionals in claims arising from allegations of professional negligence. Through his approach to the defense, Mr. Waddell has assisted his clients in avoiding litigation in some of the most significant design claims asserted in Texas.

Additionally, Mr. Waddell has negotiated hundreds of contracts for his clients related to the design and/or construction of significant projects—some of which involve professional fees in excess of $60,000,000. He is also retained to offer strategic planning advice to the design and construction industries, and based on his significant experience, Mr. Waddell is also a frequent speaker at seminars and conventions regarding issues related to professional liability, trial practice and issues affecting the design construction industries.

Mr. Waddell represents a wide variety of businesses, design firms, insurance carriers and individuals including architects, engineers, registered land surveyors, and contractors, including ENR Top 5 Design and Design-Build Firms.

Representative Matters

Design and Construction

Mr. Waddell has represented various contractors, architects and engineers in drafting and negotiating construction contracts, preparing liens and defending construction disputes including professional liability claims in excess of $100,000,000.00. Below is a sampling of significant construction litigation matters handled by Mr. Waddell:

Lead counsel for the design firm of Allen Eagle Stadium—the nation’s largest high school stadium which was temporarily closed for repairs and modifications stemming from allegations of construction and design defects. Mr. Waddell and his client were able to develop and implement a resolution strategy which avoided litigation and implemented all repairs within approximately one year of notice of the claim.

Represented an engineering firm in negotiating and drafting a 5-year engineering services contract related to Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant.

Represented a structural engineer in the defense of a design defect claim in excess of $25,000,000.00 related to the failure of an 800' wharf in Texas. After managing a team of five experts in an investigation which supported a theory that the wharf failed due to construction defects, Mr. Waddell obtained a substantially favorable settlement for his client.

Represented an architect in the defense of design defect and contract administration claims arising from the design and construction of a 165,000 square foot public school in which the alleged damages exceed $14,600,000.00. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

Represented a structural engineer in the defense of a design defect claim arising from the collapse of a temporary lighting tower for use during a motocross event broadcast on ESPN. Obtained a highly favorable settlement for the client after establishing that the staging company failed to erect the tower in accordance with engineer's plans and specifications.

Represented two geotechnical engineers in the defense of design defect claims arising from excessive vertical foundation movement in sixty-seven (67) homes located in six phases of a residential subdivision. Obtained complete dismissal of all claims against both engineers by way of summary judgment.

Represented an architect in the defense of a design defect claim related to the design and installation of a bentonite pond liner installed at a public university. Obtained settlement of all claims within sixty days of receipt of the Notice of Claim.

Represented an engineer in the defense of a contract administration claim in excess of $2,500,000 arising from the failure of various welds in a parking structure located at a 1,130,000 square foot mall. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

Represented a geotechnical engineer in the defense of a design defect claim in excess of $8,000,000 related to the design of an earthen dam that failed. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

Represented a geotechnical engineer in the defense of a design defect claim in excess of $6,000,000 arising from recommendations for the foundation design of a 60,000 square foot public building which experienced over 4" of differential movement. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

Represented a geotechnical engineer in the defense of a contract administration claim arising from the alleged failure to terminate over 100 piers in the proper bearing strata at a multi-million dollar residence. Obtained favorable settlement of all claims.

Represented a geotechnical engineer in the defense of a design defect claim arising from the premature failure of a roadway. Obtained favorable settlement for the client

Other Matters

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Mr. Waddell concentrates his practice on the representation of design professionals and resolving construction and business disputes. Mr. Waddell is consistently retained by many of the nation’s largest design firms and insurance carriers to defend design professionals in claims arising from allegations of professional negligence. Through his approach to the defense, Mr. Waddell has assisted his clients in avoiding litigation in some of the most significant design claims asserted in Texas.

Additionally, Mr. Waddell has negotiated hundreds of contracts for his clients related to the design and/or construction of significant projects—some of which involve professional fees in excess of $60,000,000. He is also retained to offer strategic planning advice to the design and construction industries, and based on his significant experience, Mr. Waddell is also a frequent speaker at seminars and conventions regarding issues related to professional liability, trial practice and issues affecting the design construction industries.

Mr. Waddell represents a wide variety of businesses, design firms, insurance carriers and individuals including architects, engineers, registered land surveyors, and contractors, including ENR Top 5 Design and Design-Build Firms.

Representative Matters

Design and Construction

Mr. Waddell has represented various contractors, architects and engineers in drafting and negotiating construction contracts, preparing liens and defending construction disputes including professional liability claims in excess of $100,000,000.00. Below is a sampling of significant construction litigation matters handled by Mr. Waddell:

Lead counsel for the design firm of Allen Eagle Stadium—the nation’s largest high school stadium which was temporarily closed for repairs and modifications stemming from allegations of construction and design defects. Mr. Waddell and his client were able to develop and implement a resolution strategy which avoided litigation and implemented all repairs within approximately one year of notice of the claim.

Represented an engineering firm in negotiating and drafting a 5-year engineering services contract related to Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant.

Represented a structural engineer in the defense of a design defect claim in excess of $25,000,000.00 related to the failure of an 800' wharf in Texas. After managing a team of five experts in an investigation which supported a theory that the wharf failed due to construction defects, Mr. Waddell obtained a substantially favorable settlement for his client.

Represented an architect in the defense of design defect and contract administration claims arising from the design and construction of a 165,000 square foot public school in which the alleged damages exceed $14,600,000.00. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

Represented a structural engineer in the defense of a design defect claim arising from the collapse of a temporary lighting tower for use during a motocross event broadcast on ESPN. Obtained a highly favorable settlement for the client after establishing that the staging company failed to erect the tower in accordance with engineer's plans and specifications.

Represented two geotechnical engineers in the defense of design defect claims arising from excessive vertical foundation movement in sixty-seven (67) homes located in six phases of a residential subdivision. Obtained complete dismissal of all claims against both engineers by way of summary judgment.

Represented an architect in the defense of a design defect claim related to the design and installation of a bentonite pond liner installed at a public university. Obtained settlement of all claims within sixty days of receipt of the Notice of Claim.

Represented an engineer in the defense of a contract administration claim in excess of $2,500,000 arising from the failure of various welds in a parking structure located at a 1,130,000 square foot mall. Obtained a favorable settlement for the client.

attorneys.name: Len E. Walker
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Len Walker transactional experience in business transactions, corporate structure, stakeholder matters, and facilitating capital raises and financing compliments his work in litigation. During his career, Len has served as the General Counsel for both public and private companies and has been involved in virtually all corporate related business matters. Len’s experience working with start-up and established companies has given him a keen understanding and perspective of business matters and challenges.

Len thrives at helping companies in all industries navigate complex issues by creating business structures and ownership metrics that best match the business needs of his clients. For example, Len helped a start-up tech company through its initial capital raise to develop an ultra-secure cell phone. He advised a cryptocurrency company during a security token offering. He routinely handles contract negotiations and expansion restructuring for technology companies. Len also assists construction and engineering companies with master service agreements, purchase orders, subcontracts, and government proposals.

Len is adept at structuring entities for optimizing performance, growth, and stakeholder value as well as ease of merger, acquisition, or sale, while limiting liability and risk. His experience allows him to counsel his clients on the most effective, efficient legal courses of action to achieve their goals.

Len served as a Marine Corps officer and helicopter pilot in both Iraq and Afghanistan. His experience leading Marines and flying combat missions honed his leadership skills and encouraged him to embrace the necessity and importance of organizational structures and hierarchy, detailed planning and preparation, and flexibility. These skills translate perfectly to his practice, in which he is trusted for diligence and attention to detail, tackling compliance and regulatory concerns. For Len, the overarching business objectives of his clients are paramount, and he is steadfast in his focus on maintaining client trust.

EXPERIENCE

Companies seek out Len because he is a trusted advisor. Len’s experiences as a General Counsel, both within organizations and as an outside advisor, include:

Led negotiations for a multi-year, cyber and physical security contract with Fortune 500 energy company that required proprietary equipment, software, systems, and the engagement of highly specialized personnel.

Successfully negotiated a temporary pilot contract and a multi-year Software as a Service (SaaS) contract with a global news giant for representative services, subscription services, routine and specialty training, and engineering upgrades.

Engineered a ‘reverse merger’ with a private company and a publicly traded shell-corporation to facilitate a substantial capital raise as an alternative to traditional IPOs.

Restructured corporate holdings for leading engineering company to form a wholly-owned subsidiary for database, security, and specialty construction projects.

Advised multiple start-ups in their development and execution of fundraising plans utilizing convertible promissory notes, Private Placement Memorandums (PPM), Simple Agreements for Future Equity (SAFE), equity lines of credit, equity-based options and warrants, and security token offerings.

Counseled national technology staffing firm in negotiating master service agreements, employment agreements, and membership purchase agreements.

Works closely with software and technology inventors and patent agents to create impressive patent portfolios, producing, filing, and prosecuting 29 domestic and international patent applications and ten trademarks.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Air Medal with 10 Strike Flights

Meritorious Service Medal

attorneys.name: W. Jason Walker
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Trials Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jason Walker is a litigator and trial lawyer whose practice focuses on the trial and arbitration of construction law disputes including breach of contract, mechanic's liens, bonds, collections, fraud, construction defects, contract termination, differing site conditions, bid protests, schedule compression, acceleration and jobsite personal injuries. He has represented owners, general contractors, subcontractors and suppliers, on commercial, residential and industrial construction projects of all sizes. Jason's litigation experience includes jury and bench trials in state and federal courts, injunctive proceedings and adversary proceedings. He also assists clients with drafting and negotiating contracts and claims. Jason was recognized as a "Rising Star" in Texas construction law by Texas Monthly in 2006 and 2007.

Representative Experience:

Represented owner in a suit by contractors in claims related to Hurricane Ike resulting from the insurance carrier's failure to pay the claim.

Represented general contractor in a suit against an owner wherein the owner arbitrarily withheld final payment to the contractor and attempted to assess over $300,000 in liquidated damages.

Represented general contractor in a suit against a subcontractor who alleged prior material breach by the general contractor and who abandoned a school job in Port Neches, Texas.

Defended general contractor against a temporary injunction requested by homeowner to halt all construction activities at a school renovation.

Prosecuted claim by general contractor against a subcontractor who failed to honor its bid to the general contractor after the general contractor used the subcontractors' bid in its bid to owner.

Represented pipeline contractor in the negotiated settlement of a dispute regarding the scope of work and damages along a fifty-mile long right-of-way through wetlands.

Represented general contractor in an arbitration with a concrete subcontractor who simultaneously walked off three school projects claiming that the general contractor delayed the subcontractor's performance, failed to issue change orders and failed to make timely payment.

Represented a concrete subcontractor in an arbitration with a general contractor after the subcontractor refused to complete work when the general contractor failed to make timely payment.

Negotiated settlement for electrical and instrumentation subcontractor against an industrial plant owner relating to delay and schedule compression claims.

Negotiated dismissal and settlement terms for underground utility and clearing contractor in a suit for injunctive relief and damages resulting from allegations of violations of the Texas Clean Air Act.

Obtained numerous summary judgments on behalf of construction suppliers against subcontractors who failed to pay for materials purchased on credit.

Represented owner in a dispute with a concrete supplier who attempted to assert and foreclose a $600,000 lien claim on a multi-family development.

Negotiated settlement for specialty contractor in a dispute with a freight carrier for damages to electrical and computer equipment.

Brought suit and foreclosed on mechanics and materialmen's lien claim by HVAC subcontractor against new medical office building. Claim settled after court entered order to foreclose lien.

Drafted and revised numerous business credit applications, purchase orders and personal guaranty agreements for construction suppliers.

attorneys.name: Jenna Wallace
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Midland, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jenna is a Shareholder practicing in the Estate Planning, Probate and Trust Section of Cotton Bledsoe Tighe & Dawson, PC in Midland, Texas. Jenna is licensed to practice in Texas, New Mexico, and Oklahoma.

AREAS OF CONCENTRATION

Estate Planning

A significant portion of Jenna's practice is devoted to the preparation of wills and the creation and modification of trusts. Jenna assists her clients in creating, implementing, and modifying estate plans that accomplish clients' key objectives and goals regarding the disposition of estates and assets or to address changes in family or financial situations. She prepares specialized estate plans designed to reduce or avoid estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer taxes.

Probate, Estate, and Trust Administration

Jenna also dedicates a significant part of her practice to advising fiduciaries and estate beneficiaries in matters relating to the probate of estates of decedents. She advises surviving spouses of decedents regarding their statutory rights and advises fiduciaries, such as executors, administrators, and trustees, regarding the disposition of decedents' estates in both contested and uncontested matters. In addition to original probate proceedings in Texas, New Mexico, and Oklahoma, Jenna also handles ancillary probates of non-resident decedents who owned property in Texas, New Mexico, and Oklahoma.

Incapacity Planning

Jenna spends a significant amount of time advising clients with making decisions related to their care and the management of their property in preparation for any period of incapacity. She advises clients about Directives to Physicians (Living Wills), Medical Powers of Attorney, Statutory Durable Powers of Attorney, and Revocable (Living) Trusts. In addition, she advises clients about the option of pre-need guardian designations, including care for minor children.

Asset Protection

Jenna's practice also involves advising clients concerning lawful asset protection techniques, including the establishment of family limited partnerships and limited liability companies, separate property trusts, gun trusts, and the preparation of pre-marital and post-marital property agreements, and transmutation agreements.

Family Wealth Transfers

Part of Jenna's practice involves helping families plan for the orderly transfer of family assets. She advises business owners develop and implement succession plans to help family businesses thrive after the founding generation retires or passes away. Including representation of family offices, she counsels clients on the equitable division of estates. Jenna also commonly advises owners of oil and gas interests regarding transfer techniques designed to avoid further fractionalization of interests over time.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Grimes Family Service Award

Legal Practice Top Appellate Brief Award

M. Penn L. Award

attorneys.name: Jerry R. Wallace
attorneys.practice_type: School Law Lawyers in El Paso, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jerry Wallace was born in Corinth, Mississippi and grew up in Mississippi and Alabama where he attended public schools. He earned degrees in Urban Planning and Economics, with emphasis in Municipal Administration and Finance, from UNA. Mr. Wallace entered law school where he was an officer in the Phi Alpha Delta Legal Fraternity, receiving the Distinguished Service Award and representing the law school in the American Bar Association Regional Trial Practice Competition Finals. After earning the degree of Doctor of Jurisprudence at Mississippi College School of Law in 1981, Mr. Wallace worked in the oil and gas industry before joining a civil litigation, school law and municipal litigation practice.

Mr. Wallace is admitted to practice before all state courts in Texas and Mississippi, including the Texas and Mississippi Supreme Courts, the Federal District Courts, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit and the United States Supreme Court.

Since 1983, Mr. Wallace has represented numerous school districts as general counsel and as special counsel with respect to all aspects of school law, including school administration (open meetings, open records, public purchasing, student and employment hearings, and preparation of minutes and official records); student suspension and discipline; student search and seizure; employment issues with respect to teachers and other school staff, including employment discrimination and defending sexual harassment claims; teacher termination and non-renewal; acquisition, leasing and disposal of real property; administration of trust properties; and public finance, including general obligation bonds, state aid special revenue bonds, tax anticipation notes, limited tax obligations, and lease purchase certificates of participation. Mr. Wallace has handled the preparation and submission of materials for rating of credits by Standard & Poors and Moody's Investor Services, rating reviews, and submissions necessary to obtain municipal bond insurance to reduce the tax revenues required to service debt.

Mr. Wallace has represented school districts in cases involving the Federal Voting Rights Act, school desegregation and public finance. Mr. Wallace developed the first program for private funding of public school athletic facilities in Mississippi and for joint venture private/public development of trust properties in Mississippi, funding construction of stadium improvements and generating hundreds of thousands of dollars in additional revenues from school trust property management.

Mr. Wallace is an active member of the Texas and Mississippi Association of School Boards' Council of School Attorneys and the National School Boards Association Council of School Attorneys. He is a recognized speaker at continuing legal education seminars on all aspects of school law and school finance.

Mr. Wallace represents municipalities, municipal utility commissions, and utility districts in numerous matters involving: municipal enlargement; expansion and extension of municipal and utility infrastructure (annexation and long-range fiscal effort plans for services and infrastructure); employment matters; and land use regulation, including the regulation of property uses as well as the preparation and administration of development impact fee regulations ordinances. He has worked with numerous cities to develop long-range plans for growth management, public facilities improvements, and expansion of infrastructure.

Mr. Wallace has recently represented municipal authorities in matters involving requests for approval of commercial development plans, and with respect to disputes regarding the application of land use regulations ordinances. Mr. Wallace is a member of the Texas City Attorneys Association, Mississippi Municipal Attorneys Association and the State and Local Government Section of the American Bar Association. He is a frequent speaker at continuing legal education seminars and serves as a consultant on municipal annexation, extension of municipal infrastructure and development and administration of land use regulations. Mr. Wallace has served as underwriter's counsel, issuer's counsel and bond counsel on all types of tax-exempt municipal bonds, including utility revenue bonds, lease purchase certificates of participation, special revenue jail bonds, tax increment financing obligations and special assessment bonds. Recently Mr. Wallace has served as Underwriter's Counsel on the following school bonds: Socorro ISD Unlimited Tax Refunding Bonds, Series 2010, $16,215,000.00; Clint ISD Unlimited Tax Refunding Bonds, Series 2010, $231,377.35; Socorro ISD School Rebuilding Tax Revenue Bonds, Series 2011, $50,345,000.00; Clint ISD Tax Revenue Bonds, Series 2011, $8,979,998.10; Socorro ISD Unlimited Tax Refunding Bonds, Series 2012, $17,794,990.45; Socorro ISD Unlimited Tax School Building Bonds, Series 2012, $129,370,000.00; Socorro ISD Unlimited Tax School Building Bonds, Series 2013, $95,290,000.00; Socorro ISD Unlimited Tax Refunding Bonds, Series 2013A, $55,670,000.00. Mr. Wallace is listed as approved bond counsel in the Bond Buyer's Municipal Marketplace Directory (the Red Book) and is a member of the National Association of Bond Lawyers.

An avid conservationist, Mr. Wallace is a life member of the National Wildlife Federation, the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation and a member of Safari Club International.

attorneys.name: Colin Walsh
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Walsh has represented clients in state court, federal court, administrative actions, and internal grievance hearings. He has appeared before state and federal judges, state and federal agencies, administrative law judges, and hearing officers across Texas and in Washington, D.C. Mr. Walsh also has extensive appellate experience. He has drafted numerous appellate briefs for state and federal courts, petitions for review and briefs on the merits for the Texas Supreme Court, and has presented oral argument before the Fifth Circuit, the Federal Circuit, and the Dallas, Austin, San Antonio, and Eastland state courts of appeal.

Mr. Walsh’s practice focuses on representing employees against employers in cases involving discrimination, retaliation, unpaid wages, unpaid overtime, contract disputes, and whistleblowing actions. He has represented private sector employees, as well as state and federal workers.

Mr. Walsh graduated from The University of Texas School of Law with honors. During law school, Mr. Walsh was awarded a three-year endowed presidential scholarship, the Tom Hathaway Memorial Scholarship for Trial Advocacy, and the Dean’s Achievement Award for the highest grade in his Federal Courts class. He participated in the National Security Clinic, was on the Interscholastic Arbitration Team, and studied international and comparative law at University College London. During law school, Mr. Walsh completed internships at the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office and the 14th Court of Appeals in Houston. Before attending law school, Mr. Walsh graduated from The University of Texas at Austin with a bachelor’s degree in theatre.

From 2015 until the present, Super Lawyers Magazine, a Thomson Reuters publication, has selected Mr. Walsh as a Texas Rising Star in employment litigation, an honor given to only the top 2.5% of attorneys in Texas. He is a member of the Texas Employment Lawyers Association, National Employment Lawyers Association, the Austin Bar Association, the Austin Bar Foundation, Austin Young Lawyers Association, Texas Young Lawyers Association, and a lifetime member of the Texas Exes. Hook ’em Horns!

Mr. Walsh is licensed to practice law in Texas and the District of Columbia. He is admitted to practice in the Northern, Eastern, and Western Federal District Courts in Texas, the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Federal Circuit Court of Appeals, and Texas state courts.

attorneys.name: Jackie R. Waneck
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Bastrop, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jackie R. Waneck joined Tuck McClimon, PLLC in January 2026. She was admitted to practice law by the State Bar of Texas in October 2025 after earning her Juris Doctor from The University of Texas School of Law in May 2025.

Prior to attending law school, Jackie spent 16 years in public education, most of which she served as the Special Education Director for Bastrop Independent School District. During her career in public schools, she developed a strong commitment to advocating for children, families, and public educators, an interest that continues to inform her legal practice.

While in law school, Jackie focused her studies on environmental law, elder law, and child advocacy. She gained hands-on experience in family law as a Student Attorney ad Litem representing children under CPS supervision through Children’s Rights Clinic at Texas Law.

Jackie’s legal experience also includes federal judicial internships in the Western District of Texas and legal clerkships with Walsh Gallegos Trevino & Kyle, Lloyd Gosselink Rochelle & Townsend, Allensworth & Porter, and the Lower Colorado River Authority. Before joining Tuck McClimon, she practiced as an Associate Attorney with Allensworth & Porter in Austin, Texas.

Since joining Tuck McClimon, Jackie has focused her practice on family law, civil litigation, and estate planning. She is committed to providing thoughtful, practical, and client-centered representation, recognizing that each legal matter presents unique challenges and requires tailored solutions.

Jackie resides in Rosanky, Texas, with her husband, a wildlife biologist and cattle rancher. In her free time, she enjoys traveling, spending time with family and friends, and being outdoors with their three dogs. She is proud to serve the people of Bastrop and the surrounding communities.

He is a trained mediator, and past president of the Corpus Christi Bankruptcy Association. His first novel, Fatal Practice, was published in 2001.

attorneys.name: Justin C. Warner
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Justin is a trial lawyer who understands how to maximize recoveries for clients who were seriously injured in maritime and offshore accidents, oilfield accidents, trucking accidents, and catastrophic workplace accidents and explosions.

Prior to joining Zehl & Associates, Justin spent six years working as an attorney in the maritime group at one of Louisiana’s oldest and most prominent defense firms, where he represented maritime employers, vessel owners, and insurers in complex maritime and personal injury cases under the Jones Act. Justin has significant experience handling limitation actions, platform fires/explosions, and vessel allisions/collisions.

Justin is from Natchitoches, Louisiana and received his bachelor’s degree from Northwestern State University. While at NSU, he was a member of the school’s football team. Justin later obtained his law degree from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law. During law school, Justin was a member of Loyola’s Maritime Law Journal, where he served as managing editor.

In 2022 and 2023, Justin was selected as a Super Lawyers Rising Star—a distinction awarded to less than 2.5 percent of practicing lawyers—in the areas of Maritime Law and Transportation.

When not at work, Justin enjoys hunting, playing golf, and spending time with his wife Alexa and their dog Pita.

attorneys.name: Gary R. Warren
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Richardson, TX
attorneys.bio:
Gary is a native Texan with a passion for American history, politics and the law. He was educated in the great state of Texas, graduating from Garland High School – one of the oldest campuses in the state. Following high school, he attended Texas Tech University, receiving a B.A. in History. With his strong interest in law, he proceeded to Thomas M. Cooley Law School, graduating in 1991.

Initiating his law career in 1992 with Consolidated Financial Resources, Inc., Gary served as in-house corporate counsel. During his tenure, he was in charge of litigation coordination, reviewed bond indentures for tax consequences, and administered jail standards for private jail facilities. In 1994, while still maintaining his position with the Consolidated Financial Resources, Inc., Gary entered into private law practice with a focus in complex criminal and civil litigation.

After eleven years in private practice, Gary formed Warren & Associates, L.L.P. with partner Christopher Migliaccio. In 2008, the law firm was renamed Warren & Migliaccio L.L.P. Over the years the firm has expanded to offer more services including family law, credit card lawsuits, bankruptcy, and personal injury. Gary is passionate about serving the needs of families in Dallas, Rockwall, Collin and Hunt counties.

attorneys.name: Jessica Warren
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jessica M. Warren is a licensed attorney with over twenty-six years of experience. Jessica obtained her undergraduate degree in 1992 from the University of Texas at Austin, where she majored in an honors program called Plan II. She went to Baylor Law School and graduated in 1995. While at Baylor, Jessica was named the “Thomas R. Phillips Scholar.” After graduating, Jessica began her legal career in Houston, Texas litigating products liability claims. Jessica moved back to Austin, Texas in 1998 and began to transition to the practice of estate planning and probate in 2004. Jessica has been named as a Five Star Wealth Advisor and a Five Star Estate Planning Attorney. The selection is based upon numerous criteria including peer reviews. Jessica was an adjunct professor at Texas State University and taught Introduction to Fiduciary Law in the McCoy School of Business. Jessica has given several speeches on the topic of estate planning and probate issues, including the following:

Fiduciary Duties of a Trustee presented to the Travis County Women Lawyers and Solo and Small Firm Section of the Austin Bar Association (2008)

Speaker to the Economics Business Growth Incubator (EBGI) of the Greater Austin Hispanic Chamber of Commerce on the topic of Organizing Your Business (2012, 2013, and 2014)

Preparing Your Estate Plan presented to the Texas Minority Program, State Bar of Texas (2013)

When There Is Not A Will – Intermediate Estate Planning and Probate Course sponsored by the State Bar of Texas (2014)

Jessica strongly believes in the commitment to give back to the community. Over the years, she has served on several non-profit boards, including the Travis County Women Lawyers Foundation, Legal Services to the Poor in Civil Matters subcommittee of the State Bar of Texas, and served as the President of the Estate Planning and Probate Section of the Austin Bar Association.
