attorneys.name: Jonathan Watkins
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Jonathan Watkins
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Our firm provides boutique services for an array of criminal accusations. Our focus is customer-based and we treat every one of our clients with respect and dignity. I was fortunate to start my career at the District Attorney's Office. I was able to try to verdict several misdemeanor and felony allegations. My experience as an advocate ranges from a simple Class C misdemeanor case all the way up to aggravated felony allegations, like Sexual Assault and Murder.

I learned the value in "doing the right thing" while a prosecutor; and this same principle has followed my path as a criminal defense attorney. When the government files a case against you this is serious business, whether is a Driving While Intoxicated case or an Aggravated Assault case. Our goal is to have every case dismissed; or to get a result that benefits our clients. We specialize in jury trial work; and have been able to prevail on several contested pretrial hearings. Coming from a humble background has allowed me to develop a unique bond and sense of trust with my clients. Our justice system would be a failure without defense attorneys willing to work toward holding the prosecution to its burden.

In addition to specializing in criminal defense, our firm also handles select Personal Injury matters. Our focus with these cases is to get our clients the help they need, while pursuing justice on their behalf. Our law firm has been able to obtain several positive settlements for those with injury cases.

attorneys.bio:
Trevon Watson is a founding partner at the Law Office of Trevon Watson, PLLC, and focuses primarily on advising clients on business, commercial real estate transactions and commercial and residential construction defects in Texas. Mr. Watson’s practice is centered around effectively drafting, researching and negotiating for investors, property owners and contractors in Texas. Mr. Watson drafts deeds, purchase and sale agreements, commercial real estate leases, company agreements and advises clients of his findings.

Mr. Watson’s goal is to provide his clients with the representation, knowledge, and advice necessary to keep their businesses moving forward. To achieve this, Mr. Watson’s approach is thorough and practical. Mr. Watson carefully considers the facts and all relevant information, while tailoring his services to the unique needs of his clients. Mr. Watson takes great pride in delivering comprehensive, polished, and efficient work products to his clients.

Mr. Watson’s approach is calm and pragmatic – first, through an understanding of his client’s business, goals, and the demands of the client’s investors and, secondly, through his knowledge of real estate and construction.

Originally from Louisiana, Mr. Watson attended the University of Louisiana at Lafayette in Lafayette, Louisiana where he graduated with a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice with a minor in Law. Mr. Watson went straight from undergraduate studies into law school at Texas Southern University, Thurgood Marshall School of Law where he graduated ConCum Laude and received his Juris Doctorate.

Outside of the office, Mr. Watson enjoys playing Tennis and creating memories with his family.

Mr. Watson drafts deeds, purchase and sale agreements, commercial real estate leases, company agreements and advises clients of his findings.

Mr. Watson’s goal is to provide his clients with the representation, knowledge, and advice necessary to keep their businesses moving forward. Mr. Watson carefully considers the facts and all relevant information, while tailoring his services to the unique needs of his clients. Mr. Watson takes great pride in delivering comprehensive, polished, and efficient work products to his clients.

Mr. Watson’s approach is calm and pragmatic – first, through an understanding of his client’s business, goals, and the demands of the client’s investors and, secondly, through his knowledge of real estate and construction.

attorneys.name: Joe M. Wearmouth
attorneys.practice_type: Trucking Accidents Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Joe Wearmouth has practiced law in the private or public sector for almost 20 years. After graduating as the valedictorian from Mitchell Hamline School of Law in 2009, he practiced complex civil litigation at an AmLaw 100 firm in Minneapolis and then at a satellite office of a major southeastern law firm in Houston. His clients have ranged from international corporations to owners of small shrimping vessels. Joe relocated to El Paso in 2015 and worked as an in-house litigation attorney for federal law enforcement agencies, including as lead counsel for a multi-agency intelligence center and as a special assistant United States attorney prosecuting felony drug and firearm offenses on the U.S./Mexico border. He also spent two years as a staff attorney for the Texas Eighth Court of Appeals.

Joe grew up in small-town Iowa where he gained a deep understanding and respect for the famous Midwest work ethic. He studied history and wrestled at Central College in Pella, Iowa before he moved to Minnesota for law school. He currently lives in El Paso with his wife, two daughters, and their English bulldog.

attorneys.name: Brittany Ann Weaver
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law and Appeals Lawyers in Denton, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brittany Ann Weaver is a partner at Yale, Weaver & Phillips, in Denton, Texas, where she brings extensive experience in family law, probate, civil litigation, and appellate advocacy. Known for her exceptional skills as an appellate lawyer, Brittany has a keen eye for legal strategy and a deep understanding of complex legal issues, making her a formidable advocate both in trial and on appeal. Her expertise also extends to real estate and business law, providing clients with well-rounded legal guidance.

A proud Texan through and through, Brittany earned her Bachelor of Business Administration from Texas Lutheran University in 2011 before obtaining her Juris Doctor from Texas Tech University School of Law in 2014. She also earned a Master of Business Administration from Texas Tech’s Rawls College of Business, equipping her with valuable insight into the intersection of law and business. Her dedication to legal excellence has been recognized by her selection to the Texas Super Lawyers "Rising Stars" list from 2021 to 2024.

Beyond her legal career, Brittany is an active member of the Argyle community, where she and her family are deeply involved. Whether participating in local events, supporting small businesses, or engaging in community service, she takes pride in giving back to the place she calls home.

When she’s not advocating for her clients, Brittany enjoys spending time with her two children. She’s also a devoted dog mom to Elvis, their beloved French Bulldog, who often keeps the family entertained with his larger-than-life personality. In her free time, she loves traveling, trying out new restaurants, and cheering on her sweet babies in their various activities.

With her sharp legal acumen, strong community ties, and unwavering dedication to her clients, Brittany continues to make a lasting impact in both the courtroom and the Argyle-Denton area.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Richard Weaver, the Principal Attorney at The Weaver Law Firm, is double Board Certified in residential real estate law and commercial real estate law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Mr. Weaver enjoys helping clients in a wide range of real estate matters. Individuals and businesses trust Mr. Weaver to help in matters pertaining to real estate disputes and transactions. Mr. Weaver was honored to serve the State of Texas after the Office of the Attorney General of Texas and the Texas Department of Transportation engaged Mr. Weaver as a testifying expert. Mr. Weaver has also been called on by other attorneys to service as a testifying expert on real estate law.

News outlets including but not limited to the Washington Post, KHOU 11, ABC 13 Houston, Univision, Fox 26 Houston and the Houston Chronicle interview Mr. Richard Weaver as a legal expert for his opinions on legal matters due to his experience. The Annual List of Top Attorneys published by Thomson Reuters has continuously recognized Mr. Weaver on their list. Thomson Reuters and Texas Monthly have continuously named Mr. Weaver as a “Super Lawyer” in their Top Attorneys publication, a distinction that is afforded to no more than 2.5 percent of the lawyers in the state of Texas.

The State Bar of Texas recognized Mr. Richard Weaver for exceeding the State Bar’s aspirational goal for serving the public good in their efforts to address the vast unmet legal needs of the public. The Texas Bar College of the State Bar of Texas granted upon Mr. Weaver, membership to its Society of Legal Scholars for leadership in the Texas legal community and legal education. Houstonia Magazine has recognized Mr. Weaver of one of Houston’s Top Lawyers. Avvo has provided Mr. Weaver with a 10.0 out of 10.0 rating based on his professional background, experience, and qualifications.

Martindale-Hubbell has awarded Mr. Richard Weaver with the AV Preeminent rating, which signifies the highest level of professional excellence for a lawyer, as determined by his peers. According to Martindale-Hubbell , the AV Preeminent rating reflects a lawyer's strong legal knowledge, ethical standards and communication skills. According to Martindale-Hubbell, this rating is a significant achievement, placing the lawyer among the top in his field.

Mr. Richard Weaver was also awarded the Judicial Edition of the AV Preeminent Attorney award. The Judicial Distinction award is based on evaluations specifically from judges who have recognized that Mr. Weaver achieved the highest possible rating for legal ability and ethical standards. He is used to handling high-stakes deals and high-stakes litigation. When it comes to dealing with complex deals and complex litigation, clients call Mr. Weaver because he is known for matching big firm quality at reasonable costs.

Additionally, Richard Weaver was selected by Expertise.com after a comprehensive evaluation of reputation, experience, and professional excellence among Texas attorneys.

Mr. Richard Weaver has experience leading attorneys recognized by Best Lawyers as Ones to Watch and Super Lawyers. Mr. Weaver’s clients regularly provide 5 Star reviews on Yelp and 5 Star reviews on Google business reviews.

Mr. Richard Weaver has tried numerous jury and non-jury cases, providing him with a litigation background that translates to protecting clients in court and prior to litigation. He and the attorneys at The Weaver Law Firm represent clients in both state and federal courts, and before the Texas Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Kristin Weaver
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
With years of experience in family law, Kristin is a seasoned attorney skilled in litigating and resolving issues on behalf of individuals, parents, and families. She provides efficient and effective representation, tailoring her practice to meet each client's unique needs. Kristin understands the unpredictability of family law cases and strives to comprehend her client's individual goals, approaching every case with honesty, integrity, and zealous advocacy. Her practice is exclusively focused on Family Law, and she has successfully handled a wide variety of family law matters, drawing from her years of practice at Colorado's largest domestic relations firm and one of Austin's prominent family law firms.

From complex property division and military issues to pre and post-marital agreements and cases involving domestic violence, Kristin's extensive experience covers the full spectrum of family law.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Kristin gained valuable experience as an extern for Colorado Legal Services Family Violence Unit, assisting victims of domestic violence. She also worked as a student attorney in the Sturm College of Law Civil Litigation Clinic, representing victims of domestic violence in various legal proceedings. Additionally, Kristin served as a Guardian Ad Litem in civil protection order cases through the Rocky Mountain Children's Law Center, showcasing her expertise as an expert in the field. Her substantial experience extends to representing parents, grandparents, stepparents, and members of traditional and non-traditional families in cases involving divorces, child custody, enforcement, modification, and emergencies.

When you work with Kristin

“You can count on her preparedness, attention to detail, and unwavering support throughout your legal journey. She takes great pride in truly understanding her clients' concerns, ensuring that you receive practical advice and steadfast representation. Backed by her extensive experience in litigation and certification as a mediator, Kristin brings a distinct perspective and skill set to effectively navigate complex issues. Whether through strategic litigation her commitment remains unwavering—to secure the best possible outcome for you.” – Kristin Weaver

attorneys.name: Chase Weber
attorneys.firm_name: Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Chase is a dedicated family law attorney at Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers, where he combines legislative experience, legal expertise, and client-focused representation to guide families through complex legal challenges. He understands that every family law matter is deeply personal and works tirelessly to protect his clients’ rights, interests, and peace of mind.

Chase earned his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from Baylor University before beginning his career in the Texas Legislature as a Legislative Director and Policy Analyst. There, he developed a strong understanding of how laws are created and applied - experience that now informs his analytical and strategic approach to family law cases.

He obtained his Juris Doctorate from South Texas College of Law Houston and was admitted to the State Bar of Texas in November 2016. While in law school, Chase clerked for the Honorable Judge David Farr and Associate Judge Eileen Gaffney in the 312th District Court, where he gained valuable insight into the intricacies of family law litigation.

Chase began his legal career with Jenkins & Kamin, LLP in 2015 as a law clerk and became an associate attorney in 2016. In 2021, he joined the Law Office of Phillip G. Ghutzman, representing clients in matters involving paternity, child custody, property division, and marital agreements. In 2024, Chase joined Walters Gilbreath, PLLC, where he handled high-conflict custody disputes and complex asset division cases, managing each case from intake to resolution.

In October 2025, Chase joined Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers as an Associate Attorney, continuing his commitment to providing compassionate and results-driven advocacy in all areas of family law. His practice includes divorce, custody, mediation, property division, and prenuptial and post-nuptial agreements. Chase’s clients value his approachable demeanor, strategic mindset, and dedication to achieving positive outcomes both in and out of the courtroom.

attorneys.name: Frank D Weedon
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio:
CERTIFICATIONS & LICENSES

Frank Weedon is an attorney Board Certified in Workers' Compensation Law, a certification held by less than one hundred attorneys in Texas. Frank is licensed to practice law in all Texas courts, as well as the Eastern and Southern Districts of the United States District Court. Frank is also a multi-lines insurance adjuster, licensed in Mississippi, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Arizona and Texas.

PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION

Frank attended Kilgore Junior College before receiving a Bachelor of Business Administration in Economics from the University of Texas at Arlington in 1993. Frank obtained his law degree from South Texas College of Law in 1998, while working full time as an insurance adjuster attending classes at night.

PROFESSIONAL BACKGROUND

Frank began working in the insurance claims industry in January 1991. He worked his way up from a file room clerk to a catastrophic workers' compensation adjuster, who investigated complex industrial injury claims. After graduating from law school, Frank worked as a civil defense lawyer. He represented large corporations and most of the major Texas insurers. In 2002, Frank began representing wrongful death and personal injury victims in East Texas and proudly continues to do so today. Frank has special competence in industrial and work-related injuries and has handled thousands of such claims as an adjuster and attorney. He is OSHA certified and SafeLand Drilling Certified by the Petroleum Education Council. Frank taught insurance adjusters how to handle claims as an approved provider through the Texas Department of Insurance. Frank is widely recognized as an expert in insurance claims handling tactics and has testified as an expert witness approximately ninety times in federal and state courts in Texas, Oklahoma and Arizona. Frank frequently lectures and speaks to bar associations, and has twice testified before the Texas Legislature on behalf of injured workers. Frank is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, and the American Association for Justice.

PERSONAL BACKGROUND AND INTERESTS

Frank was born in Austin, Texas in 1967. He is a proud Longview Lobo, having attended elementary, middle and high school in Longview, Texas. Frank is active in his church, serving on various boards and committees. He and his wife are the parents of three daughters and one granddaughter.

attorneys.name: Patrick S. Weir
attorneys.firm_name: McCarn, Weir, & Sherwood Attorneys at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Oil, Gas & Mineral Law Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
As an Amarillo native, Patrick Weir enjoys practicing law in the Texas Panhandle. Patrick focuses his practice in the areas of Oil, Gas & Mineral Law, along with real estate transactions and general business or corporate transactions. In 2012, Patrick earned the qualification of Board Certification in Oil, Gas & Mineral Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, becoming the youngest with that qualification in Amarillo at the time. As a Board Certified Oil, Gas & Mineral Law attorney, he is committed to the continued development of energy production in the Texas Panhandle.

Patrick’s Oil, Gas & Mineral Law practice includes the representation of clients involved in acquisition, development and exploration of oil and gas properties, the drafting of oil and gas contracts and leases, the preparation of drilling and division order title opinions, and the resolution of disputes involving title or lease issues, surface damages, sub-surface easements and royalty issues. His transactional practice involves advising new businesses on entity selection, resolving disputes between business owners, and assisting clients with the purchase or sale of a business, including drafting buy-sell and merger agreements. In addition, Patrick assists in drafting residential, commercial, and governmental leases, and resolving real property disputes.

Patrick serves as General Counsel for an industrial gas company that is currently expanding and acquiring assets in order to vertically integrate into all phases of that gas development process including exploration and production, midstream, processing and distribution. As General Counsel, he assists and advises the company in various matters including intellectual property, corporate governance, financing and securities, and negotiations of gas purchase contracts.

Patrick actively participates as a Director of the Amarillo Area Bar Association and is also actively involved in various other industry organizations including Panhandle Producers and Royalty Owners Association, Panhandle Association of Petroleum Landmen, Tulsa Association of Petroleum Landmen, and Oklahoma City Association of Petroleum Landmen.

Patrick and his wife, Mackenzie, are proud graduates of Texas A&M University. They have been blessed with two wonderful children. In addition to spending quality time with his children, Patrick enjoys golfing, skiing, coaching little league baseball and following his favorite sports teams. He is an avid Aggie, Dallas Cowboys, and Cubs fan.

attorneys.name: Les Weisbrod
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
According to Michael Rustad, a Professor of Law at Suffolk University Law School in Boston, who has done extensive research on punitive damage awards:

Les Weisbrod has obtained more medical malpractice punitive damage jury verdicts for his clients than any other attorney in the United States. - Michael Rustad: Professor of Law; Suffolk University, Boston

His $31 million verdict against Baylor University Medical Center in Dallas was one of the top 100 verdicts in the United States in 2003, according to the National Law Journal.

Case: John Edward Millichamp, III v. Baylor University Medical Center

Injury: Quadriplegia (Failure to diagnose and treat fractured neck)

*A contingent (%) fee charged on the successful recovery resulted in a fee of $15,589,631.50 and $791,310.23 in litigation expenses which were reimbursed by the client out of the gross settlement amount.

Les Weisbrod has been dubbed the “pitbull” of the Texas medical malpractice bar. His tenacity and relentless pursuit of discovery is demonstrated by his appellate cases including: Barnes v. Whittington, 751 S.W.2d 494 (Tex. 1988) (orig. proceeding); Walker v. Packer, 827 S.W.2d 833 (Tex. 1992) (orig. proceeding); and S.A.B. v. Schattman, 838 S.W.2d 290 (Tex. App.--Fort Worth 1992) (orig. proceeding).

Since May 1986, Mr. Weisbrod has tried or settled over 204 medical malpractice and medical product cases that have resulted in large recoveries for his clients.

Mr. Weisbrod received his B.A. magna cum laude in 1975 from Claremont Men’s College and his J.D. in 1978 from Southern Methodist University Law School, and he is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Personal Injury Trial Law and Civil Trial Law.

He is a past president of the Dallas Trial Lawyers Association in 1993 and has been a member of the Texas Trial Lawyers Association Board of Directors since 1990. Mr. Weisbrod has served as President, President-Elect, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer and Parliamentarian of the American Association for Justice (AAJ) (formerly ATLA).

Mr. Weisbrod has also served on the AAJ Board of Governors since 1998 and has served on the 17-member Executive Committee of AAJ since 2001. Mr. Weisbrod was the founding Co-Chair of AAJ’s Birth Trauma Litigation Group in 1991, founding Co-Chair of AAJ’s Medical Negligence Litigation Group in 1999, and Chair of AAJ’s Professional Negligence Section in 1996.

In 1990, he was chosen as a Rising Star of the ATLA and presented a paper entitled, "Dirt and Greed: A New Look at Medical Malpractice Cases." He is a contributing author to the 1996 text Operative Obstetrics published by Williams & Wilkins, and co-author of the Drugs & Medical Devices chapter in AAJ’s Litigating Tort Cases.

He has lectured to lawyer groups across the U.S., Canada, England and Australia, and has written extensively on medical malpractice and medical product topics. He is recognized nationally and internationally as one of the top plaintiff’s medical malpractice trial lawyers in the United States.

attorneys.name: Charlie Weisinger
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Charlie is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in the Specialty Area of Estate Planning and Probate. Charlie grew up in San Antonio and graduated from Business Careers High School. After high school, he went straight to work installing two-way radios, sirens, and lightbars in public safety vehicles. After several years of working and attending school part-time, Charlie returned to school full time at The University of Texas At San Antonio where he Graduated Cum Laude with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in History and Political Science. Charlie remains an avid Roadrunners fan. Look for him at Roadrunner Football games. Charlie received his law degree from St. Mary's University School of Law. Charlie is licensed to practice by the Supreme Court of the State of Texas and the Federal District Court for the Western District of Texas.

Charlie met his wife Olivia while in college and attending the same church here in San Antonio, Texas. They married in August 2002 and then continued their studies. Charlie and Olivia are blessed with two young boys, Jack and Lincoln. Olivia graduated with her Masters in Physical Therapy from The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio. Olivia worked as a physical therapist at University Hospital for several years, before leaving to work with Weisinger Law Firm. She now handles all of the marketing for the firm.

When not working, Olivia and Charlie like to travel, attend plays, find new and unique restaurants, and play games with friends.

attorneys.name: Becca Weitz
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
The most meaningful moments in Becca Weitz’s family law career have been when she helps a client obtain justice, whether that is a parent reuniting with their child that was in CPS custody, fighting parental alienation, or establishing a father’s parental rights. Becca’s experience includes high conflict custody disputes, divorces, modifications, enforcements, paternity, adoptions, and CPS issues. In addition to her desire to fervently advocate for her client’s goals, Becca understands that these matters have long-term impacts on her clients and their families. She strives to provide her clients with thorough and useful information about their case to feel empowered, not only to make decisions about their case outcomes, but also to have a long-term impact on their family’s future long after the case has been resolved.

In addition to family law litigation, Becca also practices estate planning law, including premarital and marital agreements, and probate law, including guardianships.

Becca grew up in Dallas and enjoys traveling and trying new restaurants with her husband, Brett. She loves to dote on her two dogs, Chilly and Rime.

attorneys.name: Dennis Weitzel
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mesquite, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dallas personal injury lawyer, Dennis Weitzel has spent the last 35 years handling toxic tort, product liability, mesothelioma, and wrongful death cases in Texas and across the country. Dennis has tried, as lead attorney, over 75 cases to verdict on issues involving personal injury, wrongful death, and mesothelioma.

Dennis is Board Certified in Personal Injury Trial Law and Civil Trial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. He has been elected a Life Fellow of the Texas Bar Foundation and elected to the Dallas Chapter of the prestigious American Board of Trial Advocates (ABOTA). Dennis has been named Super Lawyer in the area of plaintiff's product liability by Texas Monthly magazine and has received the highest AV rating for competency and ethics by Martindale-Hubbell, a nationwide directory of attorneys.

Dennis specializes in difficult and complex cases he takes on a very selective basis. Only after an arduous and objective review and gathering the necessary proof does Dennis take on a case. "This way I can righteously fight for those unable to fight for themselves" Dennis believes.

Dennis has been active in Dallas on the Boards of Parkland Hospital Foundation and the Union Gospel Mission. He is a third generation Texas attorney; and he and his wife Lori have five children.

attorneys.name: Judi C. Wells
attorneys.firm_name: Skelton Slusher Barnhill Watkins Wells PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Oil and Gas Law, Title Examination Lawyers in Lufkin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Wells is a founding member of Skelton Slusher Barnhill Watkins Wells. She was an associate and later partner with Zeleskey Law Firm, and an associate at Fulbright & Jaworski.

Ms. Wells' practice focuses on oil and gas law and she represents several large oil and gas exploration companies performing title examination, preparing title opinions, acquiring receivership leases, assisting with due diligence and contracts, and litigation. She is experienced in negotiating oil and gas leases, pipeline agreements, seismic agreements, filing mineral liens, etc. She also represents individuals in estate planning, probate, guardianship and in forming and maintaining business organizations.

Ms. Wells serves as an adjunct professor at the Nelson Rusche College of Business at Stephen F. Austin State University, where she teaches undergraduate oil and gas law, negotiations, and business law. She received the college's Outstanding Adjunct Faculty award in 2013.

attorneys.bio:
Since 1980, Brent has been actively engaged in a commercial litigation practice which has emphasized creditor's rights, collections, defense of consumer claims, and resolution of business disputes. Brent is nationally certified as a Creditors' Rights Specialist by the American Board of Certification and is also Board Certified in Consumer and Commercial Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Brent was also selected for inclusion in Texas Super Lawyers in 2008-2012 and 2014-2017.

Brent is an advocate for institutional parties in various industries, such as manufacturing, retailing, energy, advertising, and finance. In addition to representing his clients in the state and federal trial and appellate courts, Brent is also available as a neutral mediator and arbitrator of commercial, debtor/creditor, and consumer issues which are submitted to him by parties who choose out-of-court alternatives to litigation.

Brent is frequently called upon as a seminar trainer and speaker by groups such as the National Association of Credit Management, the Texas Society of CPAs, the Texas Manufactured Housing Association, the National Petroleum Energy Credit Association, and the International Energy Credit Association. He has authored materials and presented hundreds of educational programs on topics such as Creditors' Rights in Bankruptcy, Successful Judgment Collection, Defending Against the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices-Consumer Protection Act (DTPA), and the Pros and Cons of Consumer Arbitration.

attorneys.firm_name: Skillern Firm Divorce & Child Custody Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Sugar Land, TX
attorneys.bio:
Robert “Robby” Wendell is a dedicated advocate for those traversing life’s impactful moments. Robby has worked exclusively at family law firms since his first law clerk position during his studies at South Texas College of Law. Robby has seen the emotional, mental, and financial strain that accompanies family law matters, and has thus devoted his career to navigating these issues for his clients to achieve their short and long-term success.

Robby understands that every family is different, and no case is the same. He thus maintains continuous attention to his clients while utilizing the intricacies of family law and litigation strategies.

Robby is a Houston area native, having grown up in Pearland. Robby attended The Ohio State University, where he obtained his Bachelor of Arts in History and was a regular Dean’s List member. He then returned home and continued his Dean’s List membership at South Texas College of Law. While at South Texas, Robby developed his true passion for the law and helping people, having received Cali awards for Legal Research and Writing and First Amendment Law, and obtaining his mediator certificate.

Robby has been advocating for his clients ever since, providing his personable and knowledgeable approach to hundreds of people from all backgrounds across Harris, Fort Bend, Brazoria, and Montgomery Counties.

When he is not working hard to improve the lives of others, Robby spends his time with his wife, two adorable toddlers, and his yorkie, Brutus. Robby is also an avid history buff and fan of his Buckeyes, Astros, and Texans.

attorneys.name: Jeff Wendt
attorneys.practice_type: Patents & Trademarks Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
I consider myself an intellectual property law generalist. My law practice has focused since 1989 on preparation and prosecution of patent and trademark applications, legal opinions concerning patent and trademark infringement, validity, and enforceability, transactional work involving intellectual property, such as software licensing, and occasional advice on copyright matters.

On the patents & technology side of my practice, my experience varies over a wide variety of technologies, including carbon capture and sequestration, geothermal energy, oil & gas exploration and production (with emphasis on offshore technology such as managed pressure operations, horizontal well development, and fracturing), combustion technology, glass and glass fiber production, medical devices such as anti-snoring and bruxism reducing oral appliances, wireless communications, cogeneration, syn-gas, drilling fluids, drilling platforms, BOPs, coiled tubing and associated downhole tools, marine geophysical data acquisition, acoustic ranging, water treatment equipment and processes, adhesives, elastomers, ionomers, thermosetting and thermoplastic polymeric materials, plastics (polyethylene, PVC, polypropylene, and the like), polymerization catalysts and processes, consumer items such as bicycle repair racks, commercial cleaning products, abrasives, reflective materials, semiconductors, fiber-optics, cryogenic materials, pulp & paper chemistry, electronic specialty gas purification techniques for semiconductor production, carbon nanotube technology, molecular sieves, heat transfer fluids, fluorinated chemicals, and many others.

Regarding trademarks, I have a considerable trademark docket, and enjoy helping clients choose protectable marks, and avoid problems with third party marks.

I have maintained a private practice since 2003, and previously served as in house counsel to 3M in St. Paul, and Air Liquide in Houston, as an associate with Townsend & Townsend (now Kilpatrick Townsend) in San Francisco, and of counsel with Winstead PC in The Woodlands/Houston. I formerly consulted on chemical patents for the JL Salazar Law Firm.

Prior to my law career, I worked as a process engineer, operations engineer, and inspection engineer for Unocal Corp. (now part of Chevron).

Ms. Werkema recently joined the firm’s pharmaceutical litigation group, where she represents clients and their families adversely affected by Granuflo, a product used in dialysis that has caused countless deaths due to misleading and inadequate use instructions provided to health care professionals by its manufacturer.

Prior to joining Baron & Budd, Ms. Werkema served the State of Florida Department of Financial Services as an attorney in the Prosecution and Enforcement Litigation Group. Here she developed her litigation skills representing the Department in enforcement proceedings, rule challenge proceedings, property claim denial proceedings and garnishment proceedings.

She started as a summer associate and continued working as a law clerk during her last year of law school before joining the firm full time. Melina practices in regulatory investigations, white collar criminal defense, and complex commercial and civil securities litigation.

While at Ford O’Brien Landy LLP, Melina has assisted with the following representations:

An individual indicted on federal healthcare fraud and Anti-Kickback Statute charges in the United States District Court, District of New Jersey

A state-affiliated college bringing a $15 million insurance claim for damage resulting from a winter storm

An individual accused of orchestrating a multi-million-dollar pump and dump scheme in parallel SEC and DOJ proceedings.

A company subject to an SEC investigation and a private suit for failure to disclose criminal history

Prior to joining the firm, Melina gained experience working at the Harris County District Attorney’s Office as a legal intern, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality as a legal assistant, and the Arizona Supreme Court as a legislative intern.

Melina holds a J.D. from The University of Texas School of Law in Austin, Texas. Throughout her time in law school, Melina participated in interscholastic mock trial, served on the editorial board for the Texas Environmental Law Journal, and studied at Stockholm University as part of The University of Texas School of Law’s study abroad program.

attorneys.bio:
Pete has been practicing law for over 35 years. He is Board-Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in Consumer Bankruptcy and Business Bankruptcy and has been since 1994. He graduated from Texas Tech University with a business degree. He then went on to obtain his law degree from South Texas College of Law where he made the Dean’s list and the Spurgeon Mock Trial Team. Prior to practicing law, Pete served as an assistant Professor at Sam Houston State University. Pete also holds an active real estate broker’s license.

Pete is an AV Rated attorney by Martindale-Hubell where he has a 5 rating out of a possible 5 by his attorney peers. He is a member of the National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys and Houston Associate of Debtor Attorneys. He is licensed in Texas State and Federal Courts. Pete is also a routine speaker and attendant of the International Bankruptcy Law Conference.

Pete has been married to his wife Kathy for over 30 years. His oldest son is a former police officer and currently works for the Department of Justice. His youngest son Mike followed in his footsteps to become an attorney helping consumers with debt.

When not in the office helping clients, Pete enjoys spending time with his wife, two sons, and three grandsons. Being an Eagle Scout, Pete is an avid outdoorsman.

Pete is exclusively licensed to practice law in the state of Texas.

attorneys.name: Shelby Wetsel
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Flower Mound, TX
attorneys.bio:
Shelby Wetsel is a compassionate, highly-skilled Texas family law attorney. She joined our firm in September 2024 after graduating from the prestigious Texas Tech University School of Law. In October 2024, she successfully passed the bar exam and is eager to use her newfound role alongside our growing team of lawyers to provide value and selfless advocacy for our clients and their families. Shelby has a put-me-in-coach mentality and prides herself on sensitivity, communication, a strong sense of purpose, and being solutions-minded no matter the situation.

Hailing from Sweetwater, Texas, Shelby’s road to finding her true calling as a lawyer was far from a straight line. She earned a Master’s Degree and Bachelor of Science in Environmental Engineering from Texas Tech in 2018 and spent the early part of her career working as an environmental facilities engineer for ExxonMobil. The opportunity arose to continue her work in Mozambique, Africa, but she declined. Around this time, she developed a strong interest in the law and ultimately chose to pursue her Juris Doctor. During her studies, she interned with the Hearings Division of the Railroad Commission of Texas. She also spent time as a summer intern for the Texas Tech University System Office of General Counsel and as a legal intern for the Honorable United States District Judge Matthew J. Kacsmaryk in Amarillo. Before joining our firm, she was a qualified student representative for the Texas Tech University School of Law Family Law Clinic.

Shelby fits in perfectly with the ideals of this practice. She believes the best lawyers have vast legal knowledge and are willing to walk clients step-by-step through whatever they are going through, whether it be a contested divorce or a complicated child custody battle.

In her free time, Shelby is always up for eating at a local restaurant, dancing, traveling, and taking in a good stand-up comedy show. She also loves attending concerts, watching sports, and spending time with friends and family. She and her husband, Quentin, were married in 2023 but have been close friends since elementary school. Quentin is in energy law and was in the final year of law school when Shelby made her career shift to family law.

attorneys.name: Roderick E. Wetsel
attorneys.practice_type: Wind Law Lawyers in Sweetwater, TX
attorneys.bio:
Roderick E. Wetsel is a founding partner at the firm of Wetsel & Lederle, LLP in Sweetwater, Texas where he has practiced law for 36 years. He is Board Certified in Oil, Gas, and Mineral Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Mr. Wetsel received a B.A. with high honors and special honors in History from the University of Texas at Austin in 1975. In 1974, while earning his undergraduate degree, he was elected to Phi Beta Kappa. He later received his J.D. from the University of Texas School of Law in 1977.

Mr. Wetsel is an Assistant Editor of the Texas Title Standards Joint Editorial Board, where he has served as a member since 1991. Mr. Wetsel was also a member of the Texas, Oil, Gas, and Energy Resources Law Council from 2003 to 2006 and currently is a charter member of the Kay Bailey Hutchison Center for Energy, Law, & Business.

Mr. Wetsel currently teaches Wind Law and Mineral Titles at the Texas Tech School of Law.

In 2011, Mr. Wetsel co-authored the first treatise on Texas Wind Law with Professor Ernest E. Smith, Steven K. DeWolf, and Becky H. Diffen, which is published by LexisNexis and revised annually. In the 2015 edition, the title was changed to Wind Law to make the book more national in scope and is now co-authored by Wetsel along with Professor Ernest E. Smith, Becky Diffen, and Professor Melissa Powers. Additionally, Mr. Wetsel has written numerous other articles on wind energy as well as oil and gas law. He is a frequent speaker on wind energy issues throughout the United States.

attorneys.name: Quentin Wetsel
attorneys.practice_type: Real Property Law Lawyers in Sweetwater, TX
attorneys.bio:
Quentin Wetsel is a partner with Wetsel & Lederle, LLP with offices in Sweetwater and Lubbock, Texas. Licensed to practice in Texas, New Mexico, and Oklahoma, Quentin specializes in real property law, primarily energy law, including, but not limited to, the drafting and examination of mineral and surface titles, real estate contracts, oil and gas leases, and renewable energy leases.

Quentin received a B.B.A. in Energy Commerce from Texas Tech University in 2018, and he received his J.D. with honors from Texas Tech University School of Law in 2022. While in law school he co-founded the Journal of the Energy Law Practitioner ("JELP") where he served as Lead Articles Editor and proceeded to publish: "Texas Wind Severance: The Missing Private Property Right," and “Lyle v. Midway Solar and The Accommodation Doctrine,” both of which were published in JELP’s first edition in July 2022.

As a born and raised native of Sweetwater, Texas, Quentin understands the importance of private property ownership and the growing concern to preserve such ownership for the generations to come.

attorneys.name: Noah Wexler
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Noah has spent his entire career providing help to those who need it the most. When negligent parties turn lives upside down, Noah is always ready to hold them accountable. No matter what. For Noah, being a trial lawyer means making a difference in people’s lives when they have nowhere else to turn.

Noah’s unyielding commitment translates to consistent and impressive results. He’s led Arnold & Itkin’s efforts against the manufacturers of transvaginal mesh products and dangerous pharmaceutical drugs, representing tens of thousands of individuals harmed by these harmful products. He’s also fought for hundreds of individuals and business owners suffering from the Deepwater Horizon explosion.

The key to Noah’s success is his aggressive approach. He preps for every case as if it will go to trial. This way, when the other side isn’t being fair, he’s ready to hold them accountable in a courtroom. His mission is to help clients level the playing field against massive companies and the powerful law firms they pay for defense. Noah calculates every step, never backs down, and refuses to let intimidation be used as a weapon by the other side.

Noah’s fierce advocacy for clients has earned respect from peers and opponents. He has been recognized since the 2018 edition of The Best Lawyers in America® for his work in admiralty and maritime law and named on the prestigious list of Lawdragon 500 Leading Plaintiff Consumer Lawyers. Since 2012, he has been selected in the Texas Super Lawyers® Rising Star list. Texas Monthly Magazine has named him one of Texas’ Top Attorneys and Outstanding Young Lawyers from 2014-2017 and recognized him as one of Texas’ Up-And-Coming 100 attorneys. The National Trial Lawyers Associations named him as a Top 40 Under 40 and in the Top 100 Trial Lawyers. The National Academy of Personal Injury Attorneys selected him as one of the Top 10 Under 40 in the field of personal injury law. He’s earned membership in both the Million and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. In addition, he received a Lifetime Achievement award among America’s Top 100 Attorneys. He is an active member of the Texas Trial Lawyer’s Association, American Association for Justice, and the American Bar Association.

Noah is proud to be a native Houstonian. He received his bachelor’s degree in Economics from the University of Texas and earned his law degree from South Texas College of Law, graduating cum laude. At South Texas College of Law, he received numerous accolades and served as an assistant editor for the South Texas Law Review. In addition to academic accomplishments, he had the privilege of serving as the judicial clerk in the 11th Judicial District Court of Harris County.

Not only has Noah negotiated thousands of successful settlements for clients, but he has also taken more than 20 cases to verdict. When the other side knows they’re facing him, it knows they’re facing a lawyer who’ll hold them accountable, no matter how tough the fight. Noah is proud of his trial experience because it proves that he’s never willing to accept anything less than clients’ best results.

Noah is licensed to practice law in Texas, Louisiana, Pennsylvania, and New Mexico. He has handled matters pending before the U.S. Supreme Court; U.S. District Courts for the Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Districts of Texas; U.S. District Courts for the Middle and Eastern Districts of Louisiana; and numerous state courts across Texas, Louisiana, Pennsylvania, and New Mexico. In addition, Noah has argued matters before the U.S. Third and Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals, as well as Texas’ First and Fourteenth Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Kalandra Wheeler
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law (Plaintiffs) Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Kalandra N. Wheeler is a trial lawyer with the Houston office of Wiley Wheeler, P.C. Ms. Wheeler is Board Certified in the area of labor and employment law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization, a certification obtained by less than 10% of attorneys in the state Texas.

Ms. Wheeler has nearly 20 years of experience representing clients in difficult situations. Ms. Wheeler understands that it is challenging and stressful for individuals to deal with legal issues. Accordingly, Ms. Wheeler has dedicated her career to the pursuit of justice and works diligently to protect the rights and interests of her clients.

In 2014, Ms. Wheeler joined the Dallas office of Rob Wiley, P.C. before moving to Houston in 2016 to its office there, now Wiley Wheeler, P.C.

Since joining the firm, Ms. Wheeler has represented employees in various disputes and negotiations with employers. She has negotiated terms and conditions of employment to resolve internal disputes between her clients and their employers. She has negotiated severance agreements for employees departing their jobs. Ms. Wheeler has represented employees in all manner of legal claims, including but not limited to those falling under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (e.g., race, national origin, gender, and religious discrimination claims), the Americans with Disabilities Act Amendments Act, and the Age Discrimination in Employment Act. Ms. Wheeler's representation of employees also includes wage and hour disputes until the Fair Labor Standards Act – when employers fail to pay proper wages or overtime – and disputes arising from medical leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act. Ms. Wheeler's representation includes attempting to negotiate resolutions of these claims, as well as representation of employees in pursuing their claims through administrative agencies or courts in litigation.

Prior to entering her practice as a plaintiffs' employment lawyer, Ms. Wheeler worked as a criminal defense lawyer. Through hard work and aggressive defense strategies, Ms. Wheeler was successful in helping many clients avoid criminal convictions, obtain reduced charges, and avoid jail time and/or prison sentences. Additionally, Ms. Wheeler represented clients in administrative proceedings where her attention to details resulted in countless favorable rulings. As a result of her experiences practicing before the administrative law judges of the State Office of Administrative Hearings, Ms. Wheeler had the opportunity to educate other attorneys on winning strategies by presenting to the Tarrant County Criminal Defense Lawyer’s Association. This dedication to protecting the rights of individuals is what she brought with her to her practice in employment law.

Ms. Wheeler believes that successful representation of clients comes with continuing her legal education, but understands that her responsibilities require more than legal knowledge. Over the years, Ms. Wheeler has had the opportunity to counsel many clients. Ms. Wheeler knows that a listening ear and an honest assessment of each client’s case in terms relative to their needs is necessary for clients to understand their options and make informed decision with their best interests in mind. Even in instances where the law may fail to protect an employee, she hopes that people walk away from any meeting with her armed with more knowledge than they had coming in.

Over the years, Ms. Wheeler has been recognized by her peers and the legal community. She was voted by her peers to Fort Worth Magazine’s 2013 Top Attorney list. Then, each year from 2017 through 2019, she was named a Rising Star on Thomson Reuters' Super Lawyers list in the area of labor and employment law. Now, each year since 2020, she has been named on its Super Lawyers list.

Ms. Wheeler received her law degree from the University of Arkansas at Fayetteville, Arkansas. While attending law school, Ms. Wheeler maintained a place on the Dean’s List. Ms. Wheeler was a member of Arkansas’ 2005 Thurgood Marshall Mock Trial Team, which won the mid-west regional championship and finished as semi-finalist in the national competition. Ms. Wheeler was also a member of W. B. Putman American Inns of Court and was nominated for the Jessup Moot Court Team. Prior to attending law school, Ms. Wheeler obtained her Bachelor of Science degree in Political Science from the University of Houston. She also obtained an Associate of Arts degree from Tyler Junior College, where she was also a member of the Apache Belles.

attorneys.name: Morgan Whisenhunt
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Morgan Whisenhunt is known for her calm confidence, steady presence, and thoughtful advocacy. With deep empathy and a sharp analytical mind, she helps families navigate emotionally complex situations with clarity and care. Morgan’s experience working with victims of domestic violence and sexual assault continues to shape her approach, particularly in high-conflict and sensitive family law matters.

A Dallas-area native, Morgan graduated fourth in her class from Sachse High School before heading to the University of Texas at Austin. There, she double-majored in English and Government, graduating with honors in both, and minored in Philosophy of Law. While at UT, Morgan volunteered with the SAFE Alliance, a nonprofit dedicated to supporting survivors of child abuse, domestic violence, and sexual assault.

Her desire to serve her hometown community brought Morgan back to Dallas to attend Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law. During law school, she gained hands-on experience with the Sexual Assault and Crimes Against Children divisions of the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office and interned at a local women’s shelter. She also represented clients through the Judge Elmo B. Hunter Legal Center for Victims of Crimes Against Women. At graduation, Morgan’s commitment to service earned her a place on the Pro Bono Honor Roll.

Morgan approaches family law with a practical, solution-oriented mindset. She believes in the power of negotiation and values clear communication and collaborative problem-solving. When possible, Morgan aims to help families reach peaceful resolutions and create lasting agreements that work for everyone involved. When court becomes necessary, Morgan is a focused and determined advocate who works tirelessly to protect her clients and their families.

Away from the office, Morgan enjoys spending her free time with her friends and family—especially her pug, Kiwi—reading, playing video games, and cheering for Longhorn sports.

attorneys.bio:
Brian White is a long time resident of Houston, Texas and surrounding areas. Brian was born in Texas City, Texas. Both of Brian’s grandfathers spent their entire careers working in industrial plants in the Texas City and La Marque area. Brian graduated high school from Ball High in Galveston, Texas and later attended Texas A&M University, where he earned a B.B.A. degree in Business Analysis. Brian attended South Texas College of Law in Houston, where he was given the honors of selection to serve on Law Review and he received the Dean’s Merit Scholarship. During law school, Brian interned in the United States District Court for The Southern District of Texas. Before forming his own law firm, Brian worked for a large international law firm where he gained a great deal of experience on a variety of legal matters. He regularly volunteers for public service and children's charities.

Brian has achieved large settlements and trial verdicts on behalf of injured persons. “I treat every case as if it were my own. I will uncover every rock and fight for every penny that my clients are entitled to. I keep in close communication with my clients and promptly return phone calls. I understand that reputation is one of the most valuable assets that a lawyer has. My practice is based upon excellence in representation by treating every client with ultimate respect and aggressively handling each client’s case until conclusion”.

Many of Brian’s cases come from referrals from other attorneys. This is because those attorneys know that Brian will provide excellent representation of the client and will work tirelessly to properly prove up each case and obtain a maximum recovery.

Brian has been the lead trial lawyer on both sides of the docket for clients involved in many cases. Brian is licensed to practice law in the State of Texas and before the United States District Courts for the Southern and Eastern Districts of Texas. He is a member of the Christian Trial Lawyers Association (CTLA), The College Of The State Bar Of Texas, American Association of Justice (AAJ), Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA), American Bar Association (ABA), and was selected to attend the National Institute for Trial Advocacy's Trial Skills Seminar. In addition, Brian frequently attends seminars across the country regarding 18-Wheeler Trucking cases, Car Accidents, Jones Act/ Maritime Cases and trial seminars.

attorneys.name: Brantley White
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in Corpus Christi, TX
attorneys.bio:
Brantley White is an "AV" rated lawyer in the Martindale-Hubbell legal directory. He focuses his practice on defective tire litigation, automotive product liability, commercial truck wrecks, and general negligence cases including workplace accidents and premises liability cases. Brantley's trial experience spans two decades and includes numerous seven and eight figure verdicts in both general negligence cases and product liability cases.

Experience on your side

Brantley has successfully resolved many cases against Ford Motor Company, General Motors and Chrysler by meticulously gathering evidence to prove the availability of safer alternative designs including the following: stronger roofs (reinforced roof pillars), improving vehicle stability (by managing vehicle height to width ratios to prevent rollovers), preventing post-collision fuel fed fires (fuel line cut-off valves and safer fuel tank placement) and the inclusion of safer vehicle restraint systems (improved seat belt design and air bag sensors). Brantley's success in multiple areas of automotive and tire product liability cases has resulted in his "AV" rating and national reputation and many lawyers associate him on their cases to maximize case value. Brantley has successfully recovered in excess of $250,000,000 in settlements and verdicts for his clients from lawsuits alleging defects in automobiles, tires, and vehicle child restraints.

His representative experience includes one of the largest personal injury verdicts in Waco Federal Court history on behalf of a motorcyclist who was severely injured after being struck by a tractor-trailer; a substantial verdict for the family of a Laredo man killed by a Burlington Motor Carriers tractor-trailer as well as the largest single injury tire product liability verdict in Texas for an individual injured by a defective BF Goodrich tire.

Mr. White's knowledge in litigating and trying cases involving dangerous premises defects and activities has resulted in settlements exceeding $50,000,000 and the following 7-figure premises liability jury trial verdicts: Samaniego v. Garrett Paving, Nueces County TX (negligent supervision of work site; Weiss v. Rough Creek Lodge, Dallas County TX (dangerous condition on property); Hines v. Railserve Inc., Fulton County GA (negligent supervision of employees).

attorneys.name: Joshua J. White
attorneys.practice_type: • Banking and Financial Services Lawyers in Waco, TX
attorneys.bio:
After working at the Waco-based law firm of Haley & Olson, P.C. for nearly twenty years, Josh joined Cherry Johnson Siegmund James PLLC in an “Of Counsel” or “Special Counsel” role. Josh presently practices from his home in the Rocky Mountains. However, Josh regularly returns to Texas to advocate and counsel with his Texas clients. As a Baylor Law graduate, with a concentration in Business Litigation, Josh has a passion for trial advocacy. He has tried numerous cases to verdict and judgment throughout the State of Texas. Josh has also mediated and arbitrated many claims through his career. Josh often mentors young lawyers in the areas of trial advocacy, business litigation, and construction law.

Josh focuses his practice in the area of business litigation, including the investigation and litigation of business tort claims; common law contract claims; and, generally, claims involving the Uniform Commercial Code: Articles 2 (contracts), 3 (negotiable instruments) & 4 (bank deposits and collections), 4A (funds transfer) and 9 (secured transactions). Josh is proficient in defending and pursuing, on behalf of financial institutions, wire-transfer cases in which a cybercrime is alleged to have been committed. Josh also pursues trade secret cases in state or federal court. Josh further represents creditors in adversary proceedings in bankruptcy court, including the pursuit of fraudulent transfer claims, violations of the Texas Construction Trust Fund Act, and so forth. Josh offers mediation and dispute-resolution services for business disputes.

Josh is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in the area of Construction Law. Approximately 40% – 50% of Josh’s law practice is dedicated to Construction Law matters, including drafting, reviewing, and negotiating construction contracts, with access to and proficiency in AIA®, ConsensusDOCS™, and DBIA contract forms. Josh also investigates and litigates all types of construction claims, such as defect claims; warranty claims; time and liquidated damages claims; project delivery-system claims; and other construction-related claims. Josh purses mechanic’s lien and payment bond claims on behalf of general contractors and subcontractors throughout the State of Texas. Josh offers mediation and dispute-resolution services for construction disputes.

From 2021 to 2022, Josh served as Chief Operating Officer for a Top-20 Utah law firm, Pearson Butler. Josh resigned that role in October 2022 in an effort to recover from long-COVID condition at the AVIV Clinic, where he participated in a three-month intensive-care outpatient program. Due to the success he encountered through the AVIV Medical Program, Josh often shares his story with and offers hope to those suffering from long-COVID condition.

attorneys.name: Paul O. Wickes
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Plano, TX
attorneys.bio:
Paul has a trial and mediation practice. He has earned experience in all facets of trial from preliminary hearings through trial and appeal. He has tried to verdict cases in Dallas, Fort Worth, and Marshall federal courts and the state courts of Dallas, Collin, Tarrant, Denton, Harrison, Rusk, Lubbock, and Harris counties. He has argued cases before the Dallas Court of Appeals, Texas Supreme Court, and federal Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Paul started his legal career with the law firm of Worsham, Forsythe, Sampels & Wooldridge, L.L.P., a venerable Dallas firm started in the 1930's that focused on representation of railroads, utilities, and industrial clients. When Worsham Forsythe merged with the Hunton & Williams, L.L.P. in 2002, a 100-year-old Virginia-based firm, Paul joined as a litigation partner. Over the next seven years, Hunton & Williams grew to a firm with 1000 lawyers, 150 of which practiced in Dallas.

In 2009, Paul started his own firm, originally known as Wickes Mediation and now operating as Wickes Law, PLLC. While he continues to represent large corporate clients, his practice now also includes the representation of individuals and small businesses. He has represented parties on both sides of the docket with generally an equal representation of plaintiffs and defendants over the last decade. He has handled all types of civil litigation from minor slip-and-fall claims for the plaintiff to commercial disputes with more than $50M at stake. The types of cases have included rail transportation and FELA litigation, car wrecks, medical malpractice, premises liability, large commercial and contract disputes, trucking accidents, take or pay disputes, and other significant personal injury claims.

Paul started his legal career with the law firm of Worsham, Forsythe, Sampels & Wooldridge, L.L.P., a venerable Dallas firm started in the 1930's that focused on representation of railroads, utilities, and industrial clients. When Worsham Forsythe merged with the Hunton & Williams, L.L.P. in 2002, a 100-year-old Virginia-based firm, Paul joined as a litigation partner. Over the next seven years, Hunton & Williams grew to a firm with 1000 lawyers, 150 of which practiced in Dallas.

In 2009, Paul started his own firm, originally known as Wickes Mediation and now operating as Wickes Law, PLLC. While he continues to represent large corporate clients, his practice now also includes the representation of individuals and small businesses. He has represented parties on both sides of the docket with generally an equal representation of plaintiffs and defendants over the last decade. He has handled all types of civil litigation from minor slip-and-fall claims for the plaintiff to commercial disputes with more than $50M at stake. The types of cases have included rail transportation and FELA litigation, car wrecks, medical malpractice, premises liability, large commercial and contract disputes, trucking accidents, take or pay disputes, and other significant personal injury claims.

attorneys.name: Jared Wiggins
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jared Wiggins is a proud Texas native and a dedicated trial lawyer focused on personal injury, criminal defense, and civil litigation. As an Associate at the firm, Jared handles a wide range of criminal matters on a daily basis and works directly on personal injury cases.

Jared earned his undergraduate degree in Political Science from Southwestern University in December 2019, where he was a four-year member of the football team, a brother of Phi Delta Theta, and an active participant in several student organizations. He went on to earn his Juris Doctor from Texas Southern University’s Thurgood Marshall School of Law in May 2024. During law school, Jared clerked for the Hon. Lonnie Cox of the 56th District Court of Texas as well as multiple respected Houston-area law firms. These formative experiences strengthened his commitment to the courtroom and passion for advocacy.

In his criminal defense practice, Jared works daily on cases ranging from misdemeanors to serious felony charges. He is a fierce protector of constitutional rights and stands up to government overreach by challenging unlawful prosecutions and fighting for dismissals, charge reductions, and favorable outcomes for his clients. In personal injury practice, Jared works to hold negligent parties accountable and pursue full and fair compensation for his clients. He understands the emotional, physical, and financial toll injuries can take on a person's life and he approaches every case with both empathy and determination.

Jared brings energy, preparation, and a strong work ethic to every case he handles. Whether it be criminal defense or personal injury, Jared is a fierce advocate in the courtroom that seeks to deliver justice and a winning result for his clients.

Outside the courtroom, Jared enjoys watching sports, the outdoors, and traveling.

attorneys.name: Mark D. Wigder
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mark D. Wigder is Of Counsel at Kaplan Law Group, PLLC, where he focuses on corporate, securities, and mergers and acquisitions law. With over five decades of legal experience, Mark represents private companies, investors, and financial institutions in a broad range of matters, including entity formation, private financings, corporate governance, exit planning, and complex M&A transactions.

Mark earned his B.A. in Government and Economics from the University of Texas at Austin, graduating with High Honors and Phi Beta Kappa. He received his J.D. from the University of Texas School of Law, where he graduated in the top 1% of his class with High Honors, and was named to the Chancellors and Order of the Coif. He began his legal career in the U.S. Navy Judge Advocate General Corps.

Before joining Kaplan Law Group, PLLC, Mark served as a partner or senior counsel at several prominent law firms, where he advised clients in the corporate/securities space for over five decades. He has also written and lectured extensively on capital formation, acquisition strategy, and securities regulation for organizations including the University of Texas School of Law, PLI, and the Exit Planning Institute.

Mark has been recognized by Super Lawyers as a Texas Super Lawyer and is listed in Who’s Who in American Law. He is a member of the Dallas Bar Association and the State Bar of Texas, including its Securities Law and Mergers & Acquisitions Sections.

attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Law Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Paul F. Wieneskie has effectively represented clients throughout the Lone Star State for more than 40 years, concentrating his practice on

Civil appeals—Petitioners or respondents in appeals related to divorce, contract disputes, real estate and other non-criminal matters

Municipal law—The representation of private citizens in disputes with cities, towns, counties and other governmental bodies or agencies

Land use and planning disputes—Representation of private citizens in proceedings related to variances, rezoning, specific use permits, and special exceptions

Economic development issues—Representation of private citizens in matters related to planning, rezoning, eminent domain and other issues arising as a part of proposed economic development

Paul has long been an active member of various professional organizations, serving as a director of the Arlington Bar Association, as well as its president (1993-94). He is also a member of the Appellate Law sections of the Tarrant County Bar Association, and the State Bar of Texas.

Paul has extensive experience handling all matters related to civil appeals and has successfully represented clients in appellate cases involving real estate law, family law and divorce, and personal injury claims, as well as business or fiduciary (estate and probate) cases. Though he is admitted to the federal bar, he focuses his appellate practice in the state courts.

Ashley Wilder represents and defends property owners in Texas whose property rights are being taken by condemning entities. Ashley has been recognized for her eminent domain litigation work by “Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch” for 2022 and 2023.

Ashley is passionate about defending landowners’ constitutional rights and has represented hundreds of landowners across the state of Texas. She has advocated for her clients at dozens of Special Commissioners’ Hearings, at court hearings, and at trial, handling oral argument and witness examinations. Ashley graduated with honors from the University of Texas School of Law, where she was the Chief Articles Editor for the Texas Law Review, Volume 94. She is admitted to practice in Texas and the Southern and Western Districts of Texas. Ashley is a member of the Austin Bar Association and the Austin Young Lawyers Association. Ashley has lived in many places in Texas and now calls Austin home. She was a longtime board member of Servant Church in Austin, and is married to her husband Zach, who she met while teaching first grade in Teach for America before attending law school.

attorneys.name: Robert J. Wiley
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dallas employment lawyer Rob Wiley is the owner of Rob Wiley, P.C., a law firm representing workers in employment law cases. With over sixteen years of experience, Mr. Wiley has represented numerous clients in wrongful termination, discrimination, retaliation, unemployment, and unpaid wages cases. Mr. Wiley represents employees in state and federal court, as well as before agencies like the EEOC, the Department of Labor, OSHA, the MSPB, and other agencies.

Mr. Wiley was the lead counsel on Nelson v. UT Dallas, which established the right of state employees to sue in the Fifth Circuit if they are denied Family & Medical Leave for their own medical conditions.

Mr. Wiley is a past president of the Dallas-Fort Worth Employment Lawyers Association, a Council Member of the Dallas Bar Association’s Employment Law Section, and an active member of the National Employment Lawyers Association and the Texas Employment Lawyers Association.

Mr. Wiley is Board Certified in Labor and Employment Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. Mr. Wiley is named by Thompson Reuters as a Texas Superlawyer in Labor and Employment Law (2014-16) and by D Magazine as one of the Best Employment Lawyers in Dallas (2016).

Mr. Wiley is a graduate of Vanderbilt University and an honors graduate of Tulane Law School.

attorneys.name: Cara Wilkins
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law and Immigration Law Lawyers in Bellaire, TX
attorneys.bio:
Cara Wilkins is a former Assistant Chief Counsel & Legal Advisor for U.S. Department of Homeland Security Immigration & Customs Enforcement (DHS ICE). She represented the U.S. government in employment law and immigration law matters for 10 years before opening her private law office. While at DHS ICE, Attorney Wilkins developed an expertise with federal government employment law issues. She was the agency attorney who counseled, advised, and represented DHS ICE management officials and department chiefs in employment law issues and personnel actions involving suspensions, terminations, discrimination complaints and lawsuits, and investigations. She represented the agency before the U.S Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), U.S. Merit Systems Protection Board (MSPB), and Federal Courts.

During her tenure at DHS ICE, Attorney Cara Wilkins provided legal advice and counsel to all DHS ICE departments including deportation, naturalization and citizenship, investigations, asylum, and adjustment of status. She represented the U.S. before immigration courts for deportation and removal hearings, bond hearings, and before the Board of Immigration Appeals. She also served as agency counsel on numerous worksite enforcement I-9 cases enforcing employer compliance. Attorney Wilkins served as an instructor at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC) training immigration agents and officers and DHS ICE management officials.

Attorney Cara Wilkins brings her vast knowledge of employment law and immigration law to her private practice representing individuals and businesses. She has successfully represented federal employees from numerous federal agencies such as:

U.S. Department of Homeland Security Immigration and Customs Enforcement (DHS ICE), U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), Executive Office for Immigration Review ( EOIR), U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA), Transportation Security Administration (TSA), and NASA, as well as several other agencies.

Attorney Wilkins has also zealously and successfully represented individuals in the private sector in various industries including healthcare, oil and gas, manufacturing, food and beverage, and education. She has also assisted small businesses with employment law consulting. Passionate about her work, she has served as an adjunct Employment Law professor at Texas Southern University Thurgood Marshall School of Law sharing her expertise and experiences with law students.

Attorney Cara Wilkins received her law degree from Tulane University Law School in New Orleans, Louisiana. She received her B.A. from the University of Notre Dame in South Bend, Indiana.

From her office in Houston, Texas, Attorney Wilkins represents clients throughout Harris County and surrounding areas. She also represents clients nationwide in federal employee employment law matters and immigration matters.

Her extensive knowledge and understanding of both federal government and private sector employment laws, and immigration law, enable us to offer exceptional representation to a diverse clientele, including individuals from various federal agencies and backgrounds.

attorneys.name: Clark B. Will
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
I joined Kilgore & Kilgore PLLC in 2017, as Senior Counsel, after 19 years with another Dallas law firm as Stockholder and Senior Litigation Partner by the name of Quilling, Selander, Lownds, Winslett & Moser. Between 1986 and 1993, I was a Partner, Shareholder, or Associate with several law firms in Dallas. Prior to that, I served as a Captain with the Judge Advocate General’s Corp, U. S. Army. I am AV Preeminent-rated by Martindale-Hubbell. Over my 30-year legal career, I have received numerous other awards and recognitions. After leaving the military, and during the above tenures, I was involved in the following types of matters:

Oil and gas cases over 30 years from three perspectives: operator, working interest (costs), and royalty interest (land owner). This work involved approximately 250 cases throughout all of Texas.

Environmental cases over ten years involving a 120-acre site in Texas with underground leaking storage tanks, a CERCLA Superfund, a RECRA solid waste matter, many Clean Air Act cases, quarry owners, and state and federal regulatory compliance.

Receivership cases over 19 years in Texas involving millions of dollars including distressed businesses and assets, company rehabilitations, insolvencies, Federal SEC, collateral preservation, post-judgment collections, monitoring, and disbursements.

Real estate cases involving distressed properties, SBA loans, servicing collateral, DOA loans, and environmental pollution.

Intellectual property cases involving the theft of trade secrets with regard to the location, harvesting, and development of frack sand for a horizontal drilling operation in Texas. Other cases included non-compete and non-disclosure agreements and employee poaching. Other cases included equipment and processing trade secrets for an aftermarket parts manufacturer.
