attorneys.name: Burgess Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Wrongful Death Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Burgess Williams is a dedicated and experienced personal injury attorney with over 15 years in the field. His legal career has been focused on helping individuals during some of the most challenging times of their lives. Burgess has secured settlements and won jury trials in commercial motor vehicle crashes and workplace injuries, representing clients with orthopedic and brain injuries requiring lifetime care.

Burgess brings a vibrant array of experiences to his legal practice. A graduate of Wake Forest University in 2000 where he majored in history and played on the varsity soccer team, his journey did not stop there. Burgess immersed himself in the cultures of Costa Rica and Argentina, becoming fluent in Spanish while working as a hunting and fishing outfitter. His entrepreneurial spirit also led him to found Cacciani, an e-commerce business specializing in leather apparel and accessories.

Burgess returned to the U.S. to attend law school at Florida State University, graduating in 2008 with a certificate in international law.. He started his legal career at the Florida Department of Transportation General Counsel’s office before moving to Austin, Texas, in 2010 to join a plaintiff personal injury firm. Burgess has not looked back and has dedicated his career to helping victims of negligence. His unwavering commitment to holding insurance companies accountable and making the world a safer place has always been his driving force.

Burgess’ steadfast dedication to his clients exemplifies his deep passion for justice. Fluent in Spanish, he can effectively communicate with clients who may feel disadvantaged in our legal system, ensuring they receive the support they need. He is committed to guiding individuals through some of the most difficult periods in their lives, working tirelessly to ensure justice is served and responsible parties are held accountable.

He is recognized in the Top 100 Verdicts in Texas (2018) and is a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum. He has been listed as a Texas Rising Star by Super Lawyers and a Super Lawyer in 2024. Additionally, Burgess has published research, having written “The Fate of Third-party Ownership of Professional Footballers’ Rights: Is a Complete Prohibition Necessary?” in the Texas Review of Entertainment & Sports Law.

Burgess is a member of multiple state bars, including Florida, Texas, D.C., Minnesota, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico, and is admitted to practice in numerous U.S. District Courts across these states. He is also actively involved in several professional organizations, such as the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, the Capital Area Trial Lawyers Association, the American Association for Justice, the Colorado Trial Lawyers Association, the New Mexico Trial Lawyers Association, and the Academy of Truck Accident Attorneys.

Burgess is married to Amanda Williams, whom he met in law school, and they have two daughters, Teagan and Vivian. He is an avid soccer fan, supporting Austin FC, FC Barcelona, and Boca Juniors.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Experienced

Mr. Williams is a founding partner in the law firm of Howard Lotspeich Alexander & Williams, PLLC. Prior to starting the law firm, he served as an Assistant District Attorney with the Lubbock County Criminal District Attorney’s Office as well as an Assistant City Attorney with the City of Plano, Texas. As an Assistant District Attorney, Mr. Williams prosecuted a wide variety of criminal cases, ranging from a simple traffic ticket to Capital Murder and everything in between. In addition to his experience in the courtroom, he has handled various issues involving civil and transactional matters. As an Assistant City Attorney, Mr. Williams served as in-house counsel and municipal prosecutor with the City of Plano. Mr. Williams helped the city in resolving civil litigation, reviewing contracts, drafting ordinances, and preparing legal opinions across a broad spectrum of complicated legal issues involving the City of Plano.

Mr. Williams has taught in-house classes on Arson Prosecution and Investigation, Expunctions and Non-Disclosures, Voir Dire Techniques, and conflict strategies dealing with disgruntled citizens.

Accomplished

Since stepping foot out of law school, Mr. Williams has firmly established himself as a capable and effective trial lawyer. In 2013, he was recognized as a Top Attorney by Fort Worth Magazine and was selected by the National Trial Lawyers Association as one of the Top 100 Trial Lawyers. Whether representing the State of Texas or an individual client, he has always practiced zealous advocacy. While attending Texas Tech University School of Law, he served on the Board of Barristers. Mr. Williams is a trial attorney that will fight hard and fight smart to see that justice is done in every case.

Hard-working

Mr. Williams was born and raised in Post, TX. The son of a cotton farmer and an elementary school teacher, he was raised knowing that there is only one constant for success in life: hard work. He has brought his West Texas work ethic to the Metroplex and looks forward to dedicating his time and energy to effectively representing his clients. His hobbies include playing cards with friends, hunting, fishing, golf and reading. He is an active member of Elevate Life Church in Frisco, TX.

attorneys.name: Q. Tate Williams
attorneys.practice_type: White Collar Crimes Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
For more than two decades, Tate Williams has helped people and organizations seek justice in and out of the courtroom in a broad range of complex civil and criminal cases.

He has handled criminal investigations, trials and appeals in state and federal courts across Texas and elsewhere. His career has included white-collar crimes such as Health Care Fraud, Water Pollution, Securities Fraud, Mail Fraud, Wire Fraud, Conspiracy, and Prescription Drug Diversion, to trials defending people accused of Murder, Assault, Bank Robbery, Drug Trafficking, DWI, various sex and other crimes.

The courtroom skills Tate has honed across dozens of criminal trials have also helped him in his civil litigation practice where he has handled many civil matters through settlement, trial, or appeal including DTPA, TMFPA, False Claims Act, Breach of Contract, Breach of Fiduciary Duty, Defamation, False Imprisonment, Malicious Prosecution, Divorce, Child Custody, and Partition actions. Likewise, Tate has represented ordinary Texans and licensed professionals in administrative matters before the State Office of Administrative Hearings and the State Commission on Judicial Conduct.

For several years he was the co-host of a local cable television talk show featuring interviews and commentary from community leaders and the criminal justice community. Tate has been a speaker at conferences and courses on Ethics, Jury Selection, Mental Health, and DWI.

Mr. Williams received his B.A. with majors in Archaeological Studies and Anthropology from the University of Texas at Austin in 1996. He received his J.D., from the University of Houston Law Center in 1999.

He is a member of the State Bar of Texas Criminal Justice and Family sections, the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and other local bar organizations. A sixth generation native Houstonian, Tate resides in the area with his family.

For several years he was the co-host of a local cable television talk show featuring interviews and commentary from community leaders and the criminal justice community. Tate has been a speaker at conferences and courses on Ethics, Jury Selection, Mental Health, and DWI.

Mr. Williams received his B.A. with majors in Archaeological Studies and Anthropology from the University of Texas at Austin in 1996. He received his J.D., from the University of Houston Law Center in 1999.

He is a member of the State Bar of Texas Criminal Justice and Family sections, the Texas Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and other local bar organizations. A sixth generation native Houstonian, Tate resides in the area with his family.

attorneys.name: Tesha Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tesha L. Williams became an attorney to help change people’s lives who have been wronged by the negligence of others. She is a loving wife, doting mother, and practicing attorney in Dallas, Texas. Her perseverance coupled with her passion for service and aid is what drives her to fiercely advocate for her clients.

Ms. Williams grew up in a small country town with a population of fewer than 2,500 people. This close-knit upbringing curated her deep desire to help people, especially those who cannot help themselves. Prior to joining KTC Law Firm she worked as a medical malpractice paralegal and ultimately decided to go to law school at the University of North Texas at Dallas College of Law (“UNT Dallas COL”). While at law school, Ms. Williams interned for the Honorable Chief Justice Barbara M. G. Lynn in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas and the City of Irving Attorney’s Office. Ms. Williams also practiced at the Community Lawyering Clinic, helping low-income clients with various legal issues. She truly has a “plaintiff’s heart,” always seeking an opportunity to correct injustice.

Ms. Williams is an avid volunteer at Solar Preparatory School for Girls (“Solar”) where she is on the board for Site Based Decision Making, a robotics coach, a Fierce Female speaker, and a debate team speaker. In her spare time, Ms. Williams enjoys spending time with her hilarious, analytical daughter and traveling with her architect husband to new destinations.

attorneys.practice_type: Wills and Trusts Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Paul is a native of Amarillo, Texas. Paul confesses Jesus Christ as Lord and seeks, as best he is able, to be a Christ-follower. Paul graduated from Amarillo High School in 1978. While at Baylor University, Paul met and married his college sweetheart, Sarah Heinze. Paul acknowledges that Sarah’s commitment to life and her unwavering care for unborn children and pregnant mothers-to-be, is inspiring. Paul has admiration for Sarah’s meaningful use of her training as a registered nurse to serve as a sonographer at Hope Choice Centers, in Amarillo. Sarah is, has been, and continues to remain, his best friend. Paul counts himself fortunate to enjoy greatly his role as father to Brad, Aaron, and Alyssa; and his role as grandfather to Braeden, Kynzleigh, Benjamin, Ellie, and Raeleigh. Family trips, family meals, and family times together, are truly treasured.

At the office, Paul considers it a humble calling to serve his clients in planning their estates through effective uses of wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and other planning tools and techniques. Paul appreciates opportunities to guide families through the probate process and trust administration process, following the death of a loved one. Paul considers it a unique privilege to counsel business owners in the formation and operations of their partnerships, corporations, and limited liability companies. Paul diligently applies his experience and knowledge to negotiating and navigating business transactions from both seller and buyer perspectives. Paul is pleased to provide assistance to boards of elders and boards of trustees of churches, as well as to boards of directors and governing persons of all types of charitable and 501(c)(3) organizations. In all of his work, Paul prioritizes clear and caring client communication, efficiency, high quality work product, and results.

attorneys.name: Mary Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mary Wilson was previously a partner in the law firm of Lyons & Rhodes, P.C. Mrs. Wilson graduated from the University of Texas at San Antonio in 1979 and received her J.D. from St. Mary's University School of Law in 1985.

Mrs. Wilson has served as lead litigator in numerous complex litigation matters, since admitted to practice in 1985. She possesses special expertise in litigation involving scientific, technical, medical, and pharma-ceutical issues, and, over the past 23 years, has successfully tried more than 80 cases to a jury verdict.

Mrs. Wilson has handled civil cases throughout the State of Texas. She has also tried cases in the United States District Court for the Western District of Texas, San Antonio Division. Mrs. Wilson is also admitted to practice before the Courts of New Mexico.

Recent examples of Mrs. Wilson's skills in multi-party complex litigation include Bowman v. United States, a case involving medical treatment at an army medical facility, which was tried to a jury verdict in Federal Court in favor of Mrs. Wilson's clients; Garcia v. HCA, Inc., and a jury verdict in State District Court. Further, Mrs. Wilson was a trial team member in Cervantes v. Columbia/St. David's Healthcare System, L.P., Correia v. Humana, Inc., and Fey v. Honeywell, which were promptly resolved in favor of her clients because of extensive preparation of witnesses and experts, identification of complex, disputed issues and persuasive presentation of the merits of the cases.

Mrs. Wilson has been honored by her peers for her trial expertise, and has been inducted into the American Board of Trial Advocates and Best Lawyers in America. She is an active member of numerous professional organizations including the American Association of Justice, New Mexico Trial Lawyers, and Texas Trial Lawyers Association.

Mrs. Wilson is admitted to practice in the following courts: Texas Courts, the United States District Court, Western District of Texas, the United States District Court, Eastern District of Texas, and the New Mexico Courts.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Sallye Wilton is the Firm’s founding partner. What began as a boutique criminal defense firm has since evolved into a full-service law practice. Sallye represents clients throughout the State of Texas on a variety of matters, ranging from representing defendants through all stages of criminal proceedings to assisting clients in negotiating contracts.

Sallye is a dynamic advocate who represents clients charged with misdemeanors and felonies at both the state and federal level. She has dedicated her career to protecting the rights of individuals who are facing difficult legal circumstances. Sallye has obtained successful results for her clients through grand jury presentations, suppression hearings, plea agreements, and verdicts in hundreds of cases. Sallye has also assisted clients in a number of civil matters, ranging from lease agreements to oil and gas agreements.

Sallye is licensed to practice law in the State of Texas and is admitted to practice law in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas. She primarily handles cases in Dallas and Collin Counties. But Sallye’s practice is not limited to the Dallas Fort Worth area; she has been retained to handle cases throughout the State of Texas.

attorneys.name: Jay Winckler
attorneys.practice_type: Birth Injuries Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
“A lawsuit is a battle. When I take on a case, I become the aggressor. I battle with the defendant, the defense attorneys and their insurance company. Preparedness and execution - that's how to bring litigation to a successful conclusion.”

Brilliant and probing are two words used to describe Jay Winckler. He examines each aspect of a case until he has found the winning piece that others have failed to see. Always head and shoulders above the crowd, Jay received a full academic scholarship as a Presidential Alumni Scholar at the University of South Dakota, where he graduated Phi Beta Kappa and then proceeded to another academic scholarship from the University of Texas Law School, where he got his law degree "with honors". He is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Certification as a trial specialist in Personal Injury Trial Law.

Jay brings intelligence and persistence to the practice of law and that has made for a successful combination. Jay’s success has allowed him to represent people from all over Texas - McAllen to Amarillo, Texarkana to El Paso.

With an emphasis on medical malpractice, Jay Winckler takes his outstanding legal skills and translates it into his clients' success.

attorneys.name: Mary Blake Windham
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Corporate Law Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Mary Blake grew up in Georgetown, Texas. She attended Texas Tech University, where she earned her bachelor’s degree in political science with minors in English and general business. Mary Blake was an active member of Delta Gamma Fraternity, served as the vice president of the Texas Tech Club Tennis Team, and worked as a student assistant at the Texas Tech University Writing Center. During her summers, Mary Blake worked as a Senate messenger for the Texas State Senate, where she was able to sit in on committee hearings and be present on the Senate floor during legislation.

After graduating from Texas Tech in 2020, Mary Blake moved east to attend law school at LSU Paul M. Hebert Law Center. There, she was a member of the Women’s Law Student Association and the Public Interest Law Society. She also had the pleasure of serving as a judicial clerk for the Texas State Office of Administrative Hearings the summer of 2022, where she gained valuable insight to the inner workings of the Texas judicial system.

After graduating from law school in 2023, Mary Blake returned to Austin and joined Wright & Greenhill, P.C. shortly after taking the bar exam.

attorneys.name: Majorie Winters
attorneys.practice_type: Transactions Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Majorie’s practice specializes in corporate law and venture finance. She has deep experience in company structures, financings, executive advisement, due diligence, contract drafting and negotiations. She has counseled start-ups and entrepreneurs, as well as large private and public companies, serving as in-house counsel and outside general counsel. She has over fifteen years of expertise in supporting corporate growth, international expansion, and acquisitions while protecting against legal risks. As a business and legal strategist, she blends her background in corporate law and entrepreneurial business to evaluate and advise on opportunities for clients to build a competitive position in a variety of markets.

Prior to joining Potts Blacklock Senterfitt, PLLC, Majorie was senior legal editor at Thomson Reuters, senior counsel at Foley & Lardner and of counsel at DLA Piper. She served as in-house counsel for Trade Technologies, JUUL Labs and Altisource Services. She began her legal career at Gunderson Dettmer as an associate. Majorie received her law degree with Honors from The University of Texas School of Law and her M.B.A. with Honors from The University of Texas McCombs School of Business. She earned her B.A. from The University of Virginia and was a member of Phi Beta Kappa. She is admitted to the Texas and Virginia State Bar.

attorneys.name: Alison Wise
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Lisa A. Vance, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Alison Wise is an Associate Attorney at The Law Office of Lisa A. Vance, P.C., where she practices exclusively in the area of family law. A passionate advocate for children and families, Alison is committed to helping clients navigate some of the most personal and challenging moments of their lives with compassion, clarity, and care.

Alison earned her J.D. from St. Mary’s University School of Law in 2025. During law school, she gained extensive hands-on experience through the Family Law Clinic, first as a Student Attorney and later as a Teaching Assistant. In that role, she handled real cases under a Student Bar Card for two years, developing a strong foundation in client advocacy and courtroom practice. She was also a Staff Writer for the St. Mary’s Law Journal and a member of the Phi Delta Phi Legal Honor Society.

Before law school, Alison graduated summa cum laude from Arizona State University with a Bachelor’s degree in Mass Communications and Media Studies. She also holds an Associate’s degree in Journalism and is a member of the Phi Theta Kappa Honor Society. Prior to becoming an attorney, Alison worked as a paralegal at a family law firm, where she deepened her commitment to this area of law.

Alison chose to pursue family law because she believes that healthy and supportive family relationships are essential to a strong and thriving society. She is particularly passionate about cases involving children and is honored to advocate for their well-being.

She is licensed to practice law in the state of Texas.

attorneys.name: Kathleen Witkovski
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
“With my educational background in psychology, I became a lawyer to help people. I appreciate that my clients are going through very stressful situations, and my goal is that you always know what is going on in your case.”

Compassionate Family Law Attorney and Amicus

Kathleen Witkovski’s role as Senior Associate and head of the Family Law department at Murrah & Killough centers around helping clients through significant moments in their lives-contested and uncontested divorces, custody suits, adoptions, premarital and post marital agreements, other areas of family law, and probate and estate planning. Kathleen has represented clients in highly contested custody battles and high net-worth property divisions, including divorces involving the valuation and division of businesses. Her experience in a wide variety of cases provides in-house services for clients whose legal needs transcend simple transactional or litigation matters.

By Court appointment, Kathleen serves as an Amicus Attorney in highly contested custody disputes as an advocate for a child’s best interests by providing legal services necessary to assist the Court in protecting those interests.

Empathy in Crisis Situations

Family law is a broad branch of law that encompasses much more than matrimonial and divorce matters; custody, child support, and other areas must be also addressed by a family law professional. These crises usually generate high levels of stress in people that can often impair decisions.

For this reason, Kathleen sees empathy as one of her main tools as a family law professional, especially useful in keeping in mind the best interests of children involved in cases. She develops an actively communicative, compassionate strategy for her clients, walking with them through the process and helping them continue into a new stage of life.

Consistent, Responsive Communication

Kathleen deeply empathizes with her clients, knowing that they are going through some of the most stressful moments of their lives. She seeks to provide quick responses and consistent communication to her clients about the status of their cases, to build a bridge to the next stage of their life as smoothly as possible.

attorneys.name: Craig Stephen Wolcott
attorneys.firm_name: Craig Wolcott, PLLC Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Probate Lawyers in Kerrville, TX
attorneys.bio:
Craig Wolcott has been practicing law for almost 40 years, during which time he has represented clients in a wide variety of civil matters throughout Texas. Over a decade ago, he founded his own law practice in the Texas Hill Country, and ever since then, he has been doing his best to help the people of his neighborhood and surrounding areas find effective solutions to their legal problems.

Mr. Wolcott’s office has always been a safe space for clients to share their concerns openly and honestly, with the goal of finding a mutually beneficial resolution. He is a board-certified attorney in both civil trial law and personal injury trial law. He is well-versed in civil litigation and possesses the skills, work ethic and tenacity to tackle even the most challenging cases.

In order to assist his clients prepare for the future or cope with the present, Mr. Wolcott offers them individualized services in the areas of estate planning and probate. No one wants to think about dying, but if you take the time to prepare for it, you may help your loved ones avoid unnecessary hardship and expense as they honor your life and legacy. He can assist you at the probate court if you find yourself in a scenario where there is a disagreement over the estate of a loved one.

Mr. Wolcott has devoted a great deal of his time to representing victims of personal injury and wrongful death in court, helping them to obtain the justice and recompense they deserve. Clients who have been in unusual or very difficult accidents can rely on his experience as a board-certified personal injury trial law attorney.

Over the course of his 30-plus years at a Houston law practice, Mr. Wolcott handled cases ranging in scope from those involving people or small businesses to those involving multinational corporations. In his current firm, he continues to assist businesses of all sizes in developing and addressing their legal issues.

Whether you're having trouble at work, have been hurt in an accident, or are in need of an estate plan, Mr. Wolcott can help you figure out what's wrong and give you advice on how to fix it.

attorneys.name: Marquette W. Wolf
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Lawyers in Mesquite, TX
attorneys.bio:
Marquette Wolf began working for the firm while attending the Southern Methodist University School of Law. Since then, he has handled dozens jury trials to verdict and cases in arbitration, gaining critical expertise representing clients in major cases. When searching for a lawyer, Marquette encourages clients to only consider hiring a lawyer that has tried a similar case, to verdict, and won. "This is the only way to be sure the attorney has the resources and knowledge to bring to a jury the expertise necessary to prove your case" Wolf believes.

Marquette has successfully tried to verdict traumatic brain injury, pipeline explosion, refinery explosion, wrongful death, business dispute, environmental contamination, elder care, medical malpractice, consumer rights, catastrophic personal injury, product liability, premise liability, fire/death and child abuse/neglect jury trials, and won.

Marquette also served as District Attorney Pro Tem for Dallas County, prosecuting public integrity cases against current and former law enforcement personnel in Dallas County.

attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Business Litigation and Bankruptcy Practice:

Business Litigation: State and federal court litigation: securities fraud, partners’ and shareholders’ disputes, construction projects, deceptive trade practices, lender liability, judicial foreclosures, negotiable instruments, contracts, age and sex discrimination, wrongful termination and fraud and other business and property torts; appeals to U.S. District Courts for Southern District of Texas and Eastern District of Virginia, and Courts of Appeals for the Fourth and Fifth Circuits. Mediations and formal arbitrations of disputes.

Secured Creditor and Debtor Representation: Loan restructures, comprehensive pre-bankruptcy analyses and strategy, debtor-in-possession financing, cramdown plans, creditor plans, tax-advantaged mergers, acquisitions and divestitures, sales of assets, structured acquisition and development financing, use of cash collateral, assumption and rejection of executory contracts and unexpired leases. Secured lenders represented in bankruptcy, workout and business reorganization matters: Bank One, Chevy Chase Savings Bank, F.S.B., Crossland Savings F.S.B., First Union National Bank, The Manhattan Savings Bank, The Prudential Insurance Company of North America, and The Riggs National Bank of Washington, D.C.

Noteworthy Cases:

Sale of assets and restructuring of debts of oil services company, Petroleum Industry Inspectors, Inc., restructuring of guarantors’ obligations, Houston, Texas, 2002-2003.

Counsel to plaintiff in employment litigation in the United States and the Netherlands, Richard A. Johnson, et al. v. Jomed N.V., Netherlands, et al., No. H-02-4876, United States District Court, Southern District of Texas; and Rechtbank Amsterdam, Sector Kanton, Locatie Amsterdam, 2002-2003.

Counsel to Plaintiff in large securities fraud litigation, Philip Gamble v. Hamilton Lewis Capital Management, Inc., No. 2001-64060, 80th District Court, Harris County, Texas, 2001-2003.

Counsel to the general partner of the debtor in In re Plaza 1-A Associates Limited Partnership, 1995-1996, a Virginia bankruptcy case in which the general partner was instrumental in confirming a cramdown plan of reorganization with a 27 year term.

Counsel to both the debtor in In re J.H. Acquisition Corporation, District of Vermont, 1994-1995, and its subsidiary, Capital City Press Company, a $25 million per year printing company; successfully confirmed a plan of reorganization merging the two corporations and restructuring the debt of the two entities.

Chapter 7 Trustee representation in large oil and gas bankruptcy, In re Topco, Southern District of Texas, 1987-1992: sale of producing properties; suit by sole shareholder for fraud and unjust enrichment; suit to rescind sale of producing properties, River Production Co., Inc. v. Jack Webb, Trustee, 894 F.2d 727 (5th Cir. 1990).

Counsel to title insurer in largest title insurance fraud claim in U.S. history, In re J.R. McConnell, Southern District of Texas, 1987-1992; extensive fraud and RICO litigation in federal court concerning attempts to defraud title company.

attorneys.name: Daniel C. Wood
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Fort Worth, TX
attorneys.bio:
Daniel Wood was born and raised in Fort Worth Texas. He graduated from Western Hills High School in west Fort Worth. Daniel stayed in DFW to attend the University of Texas at Arlington where he graduated with honors all while interning at the Securities and Exchange Commission in downtown Fort Worth.

Daniel then moved to Waco to attend Baylor Law School. His accomplishments there included becoming a member of the Order of the Barristers for excellence in moot court and making the Dean's List. Since graduating Daniel has worked as an attorney for 10 years primarily in Tarrant County and has extensive Family Law experience. Daniel's time spent participating in Baylor Law School's rigorous Practice Court program and his time as an attorney in Tarrant County has made him comfortable fighting for his clients in front of judges and juries alike.

Daniel now works at Bailey and Galyen's Summit office handling Family Law cases ranging from divorces and child custody cases to adoptions and child support.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning and Probate Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
James C. Woo is a shareholder of the Firm and a member of the Practice Management Committee. He is head of the Firm's Estate Planning and Probate and Business Sections. Mr. Woo is a native San Antonian and received his undergraduate degree from the University of Texas San Antonio and his Juris Doctor from St. Mary's University School of Law.

Mr. Woo is Board Certified in Estate Planning and Probate Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. In the area of Estate Planning and Probate, his practice is primarily focused in the areas of Wills, Trusts, Estate Administration, Probate Litigation, and Guardianship. Mr. Woo's practice also includes business succession planning, asset protection, corporations, and real estate transactions.

Mr. Woo is a frequent speaker at professional seminars, including the State Bar of Texas Advanced Estate Planning and Probate Seminar - Problems Related to Guardianship Proceedings [2001] and Planning for the Physical Reality of Death and Disposition of Remains Mental Health Commitments [1994]; State Bar College - Summer School (Mental Health Commitments - Patient's Rights vs. Benefits of Treatment [2004] and The Top Five Things Babyboomers Have to Know About Estate Planning and Probate [2003] and the State Bar of Texas Fiduciary Litigation Seminar - Issues In Elder Law [2008].

Mr. Woo is also active in leadership positions in many bar related organizations including:

Texas Board of Legal Specialization Chairman Advisory Commission

San Antonio Estate Planners Council Board of Governors

San Antonio Bar Association Board of Directors

Supreme Court of Texas District 10 Unauthorized Practice of Law Committee

State Bar of Texas District 10 Grievance Committee

Fellow Texas Bar Foundation

Fellow American College of Trust and Estate Counsel

Mr. Woo was admitted to practice law in the State of Texas in 1983 and is also licensed to practice in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas, U.S. Court of Appeals Fifth Circuit, and the U.S. Tax Court.

attorneys.name: Channy F. Wood
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Amarillo, TX
attorneys.bio:
Channy is a 6th Generation Texan, born and raised on his family's Texas Panhandle farm. Channy lives by values learned early: honesty, fairness, responsibility, and hard work. "Defending those values attracted me to the law. I specialize in representing families and individuals in personal injury cases because insurance companies and big corporations have plenty of lawyers and plenty of money on their side. When tragedy strikes the average working family, they deserve a lawyer on their side that understands their loss and will go fight to get them a fair shake. I strive to be that lawyer." Channy spent several years working in the West Texas oil fields as a derrick hand, roustabout, welder, and machinist before completing his education at Texas Tech. "Growing up on a farm, raising livestock, and working in the oil field gave me an education and experiences that cannot be taught in a classroom or at a university. I understand what it's like to work from sunrise to sunset in the heat of July and the cold of January. I understand the lives and labor of working people because I have done it myself." Channy and his family continue their agrarian roots and traditions by operating an active Angus cow/calf operation, and overseeing peanut and cotton farming operations on land continuously operated by his family for four generations.

"Most companies and people are fair, honest and care about safety, quality and their employees, which is all the more reason to require them to take responsibility for carelessly or recklessly causing injuries, harm and tragedies to innocent hard working families."

Channy and his wife Edwina have three children: Chanel, Caitlin, and Chancellor. In their free time Channy and his family enjoy upland bird hunting with their Hungarian Vizsla, "A-Jax", trips on "Big Red", their Harley Road Glide, and looking after their cattle.

Taylor Wood began working with Ramos & Del Cueto in 2018. Ms. Wood's personal dedication to clients and focus on mitigation of punishment makes her an integral member of the Firm.

Ms. Wood was born in Iowa and raised in Alabama and Texas. She attended Texas Lutheran University where she earned a bachelor's degree in English with a specialization in Writing. Ms. Wood also studied for a time in the Netherlands, where she completed a Law and Criminology program at Vrije Universiteit - Amsterdam. After receiving her undergraduate degree, she attended the University of St. Mary's School of Law, where she earned her Juris Doctorate in 2019.

While attending law school, Ms. Wood started her criminal defense career working as a law clerk for Ramos & Del Cueto. Upon earning her law license, Ms. Wood was hired by the Firm as an associate attorney. With her tireless work ethic, meticulous attention to detail, and personal touch with clients, Ms. Wood is an embodiment of the qualities that set Ramos & Del Cueto apart.

attorneys.name: Christina Woods Duffy
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lubbock, TX
attorneys.bio:
Something I Love About Lubbock...

The people, trite as it sounds, the people make living in Lubbock special. Whether we are talking about the other attorneys, the courts, or the clients, this area in Lubbock is the best place to practice law and to raise a family.

What I love about being a Lawyer...

Providing a voice for marginalized clients that might not have had their day in Court. I am ultimately most proud of growing a law firm that employs and empowers other women in the field of law to reach beyond what they thought was possible for themselves and in their careers.

Favorite Quote...

"It matters not how strait the gate, how charged with punishments the scroll, I am the master of my fate: I am the captain of my soul." From "Invictus" by William Ernest Henley

If I Weren't a Lawyer, I would be...

Playing with my grandbabies

Christina Woods Duffy graduated from Texas Tech University in May 2012 with her Doctor of Jurisprudence (School of Law) and Master of Public Administration. While in law school, Christina was a member/ Articles Editor of the Texas Tech Law Review (2011-2012). Christina was licensed to practice law in the State of Texas in November 2012.

Christina initially opened her solo practice under Christina L. Woods, Attorney at Law in 2013 with offices in Lubbock and Levelland (2014-2017). The Duffy Law Firm, P.C. offers legal services in several areas including family law, probate, estate planning, and some criminal matters.

Christina and her family have lived in the Lubbock area continuously since about 1994. Christina first moved to Reese AFB as a child dependent of a service member and her family decided to stay in the area. Christina and all three of her biological children graduated from Smyer High School in Smyer, Texas.

Christina and Bryan Duffy love hosting their large family and friends, often at Texas Tech Red Raider football and basketball games as active alumni members. All three lawyers at the firm are Texas Tech Alums and proudly display our Red Raider pride!

Christina has been a member of the following organizations: Hockley/Cochran County Bar Association, Lubbock Area Bar Association, Lubbock County Defense Lawyers Association, The College of the State Bar (2014-16), Texas Tech School of Law American Inns of Court (2013-2015), Legal Aid Society of Lubbock, Inc. (Board member 2015-2018).

attorneys.name: Luke Woodward
attorneys.practice_type: Corporate governance Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
With a background in corporate governance, mergers, contracting, and competition/consumer protection laws, Luke Woodward brings a wealth of knowledge and experience to the team at Blazier, Christensen, Browder & Virr, P.C.

During this time with the Antitrust Division of the Texas Office of the Attorney General, Mr. Woodward worked directly on the landmark case Texas v. Google, which challenges the search giant’s data collection practices and dominance in digital advertising. His extensive knowledge of business operations, data privacy, and competition in the rapidly evolving tech landscape allows him to carefully advise business clients navigating the complexities of today’s digital economy.

Mr. Woodward holds an undergraduate degree in Finance with Honors from Texas Tech University and graduated Summa Cum Laude from Texas Tech School of Law. Additionally, he earned a Master of Business Administration from the Rawls College of Business at Texas Tech University, combining a strong legal foundation with a deep understanding of business dynamics.

In his free time, Mr. Woodward enjoys golfing and spending quality time with his wife, son, and two dogs while immersing himself in Austin's vibrant culture.

attorneys.name: Crystal Monique Wright
attorneys.practice_type: Automobile Collisions Lawyers in San Antonio, TX
attorneys.bio:
Crystal Wright knew by the time she was nine years old that she wanted to be a lawyer, because even at that young age, she wanted to help others. It troubled her to see people being taken advantage of because they didn't have the education or understanding of how processes work.

After graduating from high school in San Antonio, Crystal attended Southern Methodist University, where she majored in philosophy. After that, she attended the Thurgood Marshall Law School at Texas Southern University, graduating with her juris doctor degree in 2009.

She started her legal career in the areas of criminal and family law, followed by probate law. She moved into practicing personal injury law full time in 2016. She worked at several San Antonio law firms before joining the Gámez Law Firm.

As a single mother and a full-time attorney, Crystal understands the importance of family and being able to provide for the ones you love. She understands that being involved in a personal injury case, doesn't just affect you, but also those around you. Crystal is passionate about always representing the best interests of her clients. She works closely with them to ensure they understand the full extent of their rights and options under the law.

"I want to make the legal process easier for my clients to understand," Crystal said. "I strive to always do what's best for my clients, and it's very important to me to maximize their recoveries as much as possible."

attorneys.name: Keron A. Wright
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Keron is a trial attorney adept at obtaining results for his clients. His practice focuses on construction disputes, business disputes, product liability, personal injury, ANTI-SLAPP, defamation, employment, real estate, and civil rights matters. Keron is comfortable on either side of the "v", handling litigation for individuals and Fortune 500 companies alike.

Keron's knowledge of the litigation process and the procedural rules puts his clients at an advantage and allows them to make informed decisions early in litigation. When trial is necessary, however, Keron is not afraid to prosecute or defend a case to completion. He has tried cases in both state and federal courts and has an innate ability to connect with witnesses and jurors.

Over his career, Keron has been recognized by his peers and clients for his extraordinary work and his commitment to excellence.

Keron is from Jamaica and lived in Toronto, Canada before moving to Texas. After graduating from the University of Houston, Keron attended Washburn University School of Law, where he was not only a published author in the school's Law Journal, but also served as an editor on its Board of Editors.

After graduating from law school, Keron served as a Law Clerk for Senior Judge Julie A. Robinson of the United States District Court for the District of Kansas. He then worked at an international law firm in Kansas City, before moving to Dallas, Texas. Since moving to Dallas, Keron has worked at an international law firm, a nationally recognized law firm, and a small local firm, before he opened and operated his own law firm for several years.

attorneys.name: Mr. Trenton E. Wright
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lewisville, TX
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Trenton E. Wright is a highly experienced legal professional who has served clients in Texas for decades. Attorney Wright went to Trinity University in San Antonio, where he played soccer. He graduated from the University of Tulsa’s College of Law in 1999. He gained admittance to the Texas Bar in 2000 and has since been admitted to various courts including Texas’s Eastern and Northern District, as well as the Northern Bankruptcy Court. He has experience in real estate, finance, construction, insurance, employee rights, elder, and family law.

Before joining North Texas Family Lawyers, Attorney Wright was the head of Wright Law & Title, a firm that focused on facilitating residential and commercial property transactions. The office was an industry leader that provided numerous people with personalized services that helped them successfully close on properties.

Attorney Wright is an asset to North Texas Family Lawyers because of his acumen, skill, and dedication to providing clients with the time and attention they deserve. A family man himself, he understands how impactful the outcomes of family law cases are. This is why he works tirelessly to advocate for the best interests of his clients and treats them with compassion and respect. Time and again, Attorney Wright has been a lifeline for the people he has represented. Not only that, but he has long shown his commitment to bettering the lives of families in and around Denton by contributing to charitable organizations such as Serve Denton and Denton County Friends of the Family.

When he is not guiding clients through complex legal processes and fighting for their rights, he enjoys spending time with his own family and traveling.

attorneys.name: Jonathan W. Wu
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Jonathan W. Wu is a partner at The Weaver Law Firm and a business litigation attorney who focuses on resolving disputes involving ownership, fiduciary obligations, and contractual rights within closely held businesses. He represents business owners and companies in complex litigation matters, including shareholder disputes, fiduciary duty disputes, and buy sell business disputes that arise when internal relationships break down.

Jonathan Wu is frequently retained when disagreements among owners, partners, or shareholders escalate into formal legal conflict. These disputes often involve claims of misconduct, alleged breaches of fiduciary duties, disputes over management authority, or conflicts arising from contractual rights and obligations during ownership transitions, forced sales, or business separations.

He regularly represents clients in shareholder disputes involving closely held companies. These matters often develop when owners disagree on governance, strategic direction, or financial decision making, or when trust between stakeholders erodes. Jonathan Wu assists clients with disputes involving minority shareholder protections, voting control, and allegations of improper corporate conduct, while remaining mindful of the financial and operational impact of these conflicts.

Fiduciary duty disputes are a core component of Jonathan Wu’s litigation practice. These cases commonly arise when directors, officers, or managing owners are accused of acting contrary to the interests of the business or its stakeholders. Mr. Wu helps clients pursue and defend claims involving loyalty, disclosure, and accountability, recognizing that fiduciary litigation often influences the future control and viability of the business.

Jonathan Wu also handles buy sell business disputes when contractual exit mechanisms are challenged under real world conditions. These disputes frequently involve valuation disagreements, contested triggering events, or disputes over enforcement of buy sell provisions. His business litigation experience allows him to evaluate these matters with an understanding of both legal rights and practical business considerations.

Jonathan Wu approaches business litigation with an appreciation for how companies operate beyond the courtroom. He understands that disputes often affect cash flow, operational continuity, and long term strategy. His approach balances strong advocacy with practical judgment tailored to the realities facing business owners.

Working closely with Richard Weaver and the firm’s business litigation team, Jonathan Wu represents clients throughout Texas, with a strong presence in Houston. Clients confronting ownership disputes and fiduciary conflicts rely on Mr. Wu for clarity, experience, and disciplined representation in complex business litigation matters.

attorneys.name: Hon. Dan Wyde
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Dan Wyde graduated from the University of Texas at Austin with a Bachelors of Business Administration in Finance in 1985. Judge Wyde graduated from the University of Houston Law Center with a Doctor of Jurisprudence in 1990, where he placed first in the school's mock trial competition and was named Best Oralist.

Since 2000, Judge Dan Wyde has been a Board Certified Criminal Law Specialist by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. From 1990 to 1997 Mr. Wyde served as an Assistant District Attorney in Dallas County, Texas. During his time as a trial court prosecutor he was lead counsel in 75 jury trials and 75 bench trials. He developed expertise in drug and controlled substance law, child abuse and sex crimes, white collar crimes and intoxication offenses.

In 1997 Dan was appointed by the Dallas County Commissioners Court to complete the unfinished term of another judge. Judge Wyde was elected to the bench in 1998 and re-elected in 2002. He presided over County Criminal Court No. 3 until December 2005, when he resigned to run for District Attorney. During this time Judge Wyde presided over 500 jury trials and 500 non-jury trials. He was appealed approximately 100 times and was affirmed in 99 cases.

Former Judge Wyde is a member of the Texas Bar Association - Judicial and Criminal Law Sections and a former Advisory Member to the Committee on Rules of Professional Conduct. A member of the Dallas Bar Association's Judicial Committee, Criminal Justice Section and Bench/Bar Committee.

attorneys.name: Penny Wymyczak
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Penny Wymyczak White handles all types of criminal defense matters including felonies, misdemeanors and violations. I am qualified and experienced in handling these matters in a competent and aggressive manner. I will fight for your rights and make sure that justice prevails.

If you are accused of a crime or violation, it is in your best interest to retain an attorney. You need an experienced attorney willing to devote the time and effort necessary to resolve your case. I can promise that your case will get the full attention at every stage of the proceeding. What this means is that we will prepare a strategy for your defense using all the facts and circumstances available to us. If necessary, we will work with a private investigator, and witnesses to uncover additional facts in your defense. We will also look at the law and the procedure to make sure that that we have exhausted all available avenues to help in your defense.

There are two different ways a criminal case gets resolved. The most common way is to resolve the case in through plea bargaining. This means communicating with the prosecutor regularly in order to negotiate a reduction or elimination of some of the charges against you. These discussions typically revolve around the case itself, the amount of evidence available for or against the charges brought, and also the defendant’s overall status and criminal history. In the process, we also look for any technicalities that will result in getting the case dismissed.

If a resolution cannot be achieved through plea bargaining, the case usually proceeds to trial where the issue of guilt or innocence is left to a jury or a judge. While the decision to go to trial on a case should never be taken lightly, there are times when it is absolutely necessary to go to trial. This decision is ultimately left to the client. We will counsel and guide our client so that he or she knows all the consequences involved in the decision. Once a client decides it is in his best interest to go to trial, we will use all of our resources to defend our client at every stage of the trial.

Throughout this whole process we stress to our clients that we work for them. If there is anything at all that is unclear or requires our attention, our clients are always free to call us and discuss the case. Our clients are encouraged to use us as a resource as much as possible: call us with your questions and we will strive to give you complete answers. We believe that the client is the first priority and that he or she should never be left in the dark.

Criminal defendants are "innocent until proven guilty," but we all know that the presumption of innocence is all but forgotten most of the time. In our media-saturated society, where people regularly read or watch TV news reports about criminal investigations and arrests, ordinary citizens form opinions about a person's guilt or innocence long before criminal charges are filed or a trial begins. I'll work diligently to ensure that you receive fair treatment from law enforcement, a fair trial, and the benefits of all other rights, including the right to be presumed innocent until proven guilty, to which you are entitled.

attorneys.bio:
Roger was born in White River, Arizona and raised in upstate New York. Roger obtained a Bachelor of Science in accounting and business administration at Washington and Lee University in Lexington Virginia in 1979.

After a multifaceted business career including a hotel, real estate and gasoline businesses Roger attended Texas Wesleyan University Law School where he earned his law degree in 1994.

Roger has been in private practice for 18 years in Denton and Dallas, Texas. Roger's practice emphasis is on Family Law, Civil Litigation, and Wills/Probate. Roger is also active in the Denton real estate market as the owner of multiple office buildings in and around the Denton County courthouse.

Roger and his wife Ann have four children, three daughters and a son.

attorneys.bio:
Terry W. Yates is a lifelong Texan, graduate of The University of Texas, and a board-certified criminal defense attorney. During his 20 years of experience as both a prosecutor and a criminal defense attorney, Terry ranks among the top criminal defense lawyers in America. Texas Monthly recognizes Terry as a Texas Super Lawyer, a designation given only to the top attorneys in Texas. Terry and his cases have received national and international media coverage. Terry has appeared on ESPN, 48 Hours and Fox news networks concerning his cases and as a commentator on other legal issues.

The Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory lists Terry W. Yates since 2005 Bar Registry of Preeminent Lawyers, an honor "limited to only the most distinguished law practices; those that have achieved the AV rating. The 'A' signifies the highest level of legal ability, while the 'V' denotes 'very high' adherence to professional standards of conduct, ethics, reliability, and diligence."

Some Highlighted Cases:

Acquittal of Captain Mark Aguirre in the infamous "K-Mart Raid" prosecution.

Acquittal for client of Capital Murder charge (at the time only the second acquittal in 22 years of capital murder prosecution in Houston).

Defense of Dynegy, Inc. executive in a multi-jurisdictional securities, wire fraud and mail fraud prosecution.

Defense of Enron attorneys (Result: No charges filed).

Defense of "Oil for Food" Investigation by the Southern District of New York (Result: No charges filed).

attorneys.name: Tommy L. Yeates
attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Dan C. Ducote Jr
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Beaumont, TX
attorneys.bio:
Tommy L. Yeates graduated with highest honors from Southwest Texas State University in 1981. Upon graduation, he attended Texas Tech University School of Law where he graduated in 1984.

Following his graduation from law school, Tommy joined Moore Landrey, L.L.P. He has been with the same law firm ever since.

Tommy is Board Certified by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization in the areas of Personal Injury Trial Law and Civil Trial Law. He has been named as a Texas Super Lawyer in personal injury law and is AV+ rated by Martindale-Hubbell. In the 2021 Judicial Edition of Martindale-Hubbell, Tommy received the highest possible rating in both legal ability and ethical standards, reflecting the confidential opinions of the bar and judiciary.

"For over 36 years, it has been my honor and privilege to represent working people and their families. I do not represent insurance companies. I have the experience, financial resources, and most importantly, the passion, to fight for you. Please call me for a free consultation."

Sample Million Dollar or More Trial Verdicts

Cause No. A-187,120; Maria Granja, et al v. Best Transportation Services, et al; In the 58th District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Yeates served as co-counsel in an 18-wheeler death action and multiple injury action which resulted in of the largest verdicts in 2011 as reported by Verdict Search.

Cause No. 11,842; Fredricka Ann Mason, As Next Friend of Jalyn Nicole Coxen, A Minor vs. Dawn McKillip Odom, et al; In the 273rd Judicial District Court of Sabine County, Texas. Mr. Yeates was lead counsel on a case involving a small child who was severely injured in an accident involving a logging truck. The jury verdict was reported to be the largest personal injury verdict ever reported in Sabine County, Texas.

Civil Action No.: 1:11-CV-300-RC; Phillip A. Davis vs. Signal International Texas GP, LLC, et al; In the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas. Mr. Yeates was named as co-counsel in an employment case that was certified as a class action in federal court, Eastern District of Texas. Plaintiffs brought an action against Signal for Signal's failure to provide proper notification of a mass layoff pursuant to the provisions of WARN Act. A judgment was entered in favor of all laid off employees. This case was affirmed by the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals in Case No. 12-41262; Phillip A. Davis, et al v. Signal International Texas GP, LLC, et al.

Cause No. B-126,144; Texas Metal Works v. O. L. Gear Company; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Yeates served as co-counsel in a case whereby the Defendant sold and serviced a faulty industrial steam hammer. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff, including an award of punitive damages.

Cause No. H-85-4884; Jim Arnold Corporation v. Al Monsoori; In the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas. Mr. Yeates served as co-counsel on a case involving breach of contract and fraud. The Plaintiff leased oil field equipment to the Defendant. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff, including an award of punitive damages.

Cause No. A-163,080; Belinda Horn, et al v. Allco, Inc.; In the 58th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Yeates was lead counsel on a case where a deceased worker's family sued an employer for punitive damages. This case involved the death of a worker in which the employer possessed workers' compensation coverage. Accordingly, the Plaintiffs could sue for punitive damages only. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff, including punitive damages.

Cause No. B- 149,309; Steven McKnight, et al v. Park Central Nursing Home, et al; In the 60th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. Mr. Yeates was local counsel on a wrongful death of a nursing home resident. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff, including an award of punitive damages.

Cause No. D-157,637, Roy Solomon v. Mission Petroleum; In the 136th Judicial District Court of Jefferson County, Texas. The Plaintiff was fired for allegedly failing a drug screen. The Plaintiff was employed as a commercial truck driver. Jury verdict for the Plaintiff, including an award of punitive damages.

Committed to your rights

Tommy is dedicated to workers' rights and getting you the compensation you may be entitled if you've been injured in an accident.

attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Lawyers in Tyler, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ginger Young has practiced in the Immigration Law Section of Flowers Davis since 2009. Tyler Immigration Law is a full-service practice ranging from family-based cases, employment based cases, permanent residency cases, naturalization cases, among other matters. She is a member of AILA (American Immigration Lawyers Association), a select group of highly trained immigration lawyers who are on the cutting edge and daily monitoring of changes in the immigration field. She and her entire in-office staff are fluent in Spanish.

Ginger has long been an advocate for the vulnerable. During law school, she interned for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and later with the firm of Fanning, Harper & Martinson. After graduating from law school, she continued with the firm of Fanning, Harper & Martinson primarily representing governmental entities and school districts in employment and civil rights litigation. Ms. Young continued her labor and employment defense practice at Thompson & Knight prior to joining Flowers Davis in 2000. Her first nine years at Flowers Davis were focused on employment law and civil rights litigation, primarily defending law enforcement and governmental agencies.

For more information about Ginger's immigration law practice, please visit flowersdavisimmigrationlaw.com or download Flowers Davis Immigration Law Info here.

When Ginger is not working, she enjoys spending time with her husband, Bob, and her daughter, Olivia.

She is the President of the Texas A&M University School of Law Alumni Organization and serves on the Board of Directors of the Tarrant County Probate Bar Association and on the Board of Directors of Guardianship Services, Inc. Dana is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys.

Dana was recently honored as the 2021 recipient of the Texas Aggie Bar Association's Rising Aggie Lawyer award. For 2019 through 2021, Dana has been named a Texas Super Lawyers Rising Star, a designation awarded to no more than 2.5% of eligible attorneys, and she has been named a Top Attorney by Fort Worth, Texas magazine and 360 West magazine. She was selected as a member of the State Bar of Texas Real Estate, Probate, and Trust Law (REPTL) Leadership Academy Class of 2018-2019. While in law school, Dana was on the Executive Board of the Texas Wesleyan Law Review and was named a 2008 Law Fellow. She is a frequent speaker for the Alzheimer's Association, Lockheed Martin's elder care network, Brookdale assisted living communities, as well as UT Arlington and TCU. Dana and her husband, Andrew, live in Fort Worth with their sons, Declan and Jackson.

attorneys.name: Joe I. Zaid
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Pasadena, TX
attorneys.bio:
Joe I. Zaid & Associates is a Houston personal injury law firm focused on car accident cases, representing injured victims and families throughout Houston and Harris County and working to help them pursue full financial compensation after serious crashes. The firm is led by founder Joe Zaid, a seasoned personal injury attorney known for a client-centered approach that emphasizes both results and responsive service tailored to each person’s situation. Since 2013, Joe has represented thousands of clients in personal injury and wrongful death matters and has recovered millions of dollars in settlements, including numerous seven-figure settlements on behalf of individual clients. His practice covers a wide range of cases, from minor impact collisions to accidents that cause life-altering injuries, and he understands that a crash that appears “small” can still lead to significant pain, medical treatment, time away from work, and lasting limitations.

Joe’s experience handling an extensive caseload has sharpened his ability to identify critical details that are often overlooked in injury claims—facts that can influence how liability is evaluated, how injuries are understood, and how the full impact of the accident is presented. He takes time to understand the physical and emotional challenges accident victims and their families face, and he works tirelessly to pursue maximum results, whether through negotiation or in the courtroom. Before starting his firm, Joe spent almost 10 years working for one of the world’s largest insurance companies, giving him valuable insight into how insurers assess and challenge claims. He uses that knowledge to advocate effectively for clients while continuing to provide personal guidance throughout the litigation process, including making himself available to clients 24/7.

Joe has been nominated by H-Texas Magazine as one of Houston’s Top Lawyers, Super Lawyers 2026 and was also nominated as a Top 40 Under 40 Trial Lawyer. He is an active member of the Houston Trial Lawyers Association, the Texas Trial Lawyers Association, and other professional organizations. Joe graduated from South Texas College of Law Houston and is licensed to practice in Texas. At every stage, Joe I. Zaid & Associates prioritizes clear communication and individualized attention, aiming to deliver strong advocacy while keeping the focus on what matters most: each client’s unique needs and recovery.

attorneys.name: Lama Zakzok
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Lama represents clients in the financial services industry. Lama’s primary focus for her fintech clients is consumer arbitrations and EFTA compliance. Currently, Lama works on a national consumer dispute docket for one of the largest digital banks on the country. Her passion is client service. With every dispute she handles, Lama works to resolve the dispute on the most favorable terms for clients while at the same time guiding her clients towards dispute-proofing their practices. The firm often calls upon Lama to research cutting edge legal issues for the firm’s fintech clients. In addition, Lama works closely with the firm’s legal assistants to make sure every detail of every dispute is tracked and organized, so that our clients can make evidence-based decisions and can easily see both the forest and the trees.

A rare Austin native, Lama was born and raised in Austin, Texas. She received her Bachelor of Arts degree from Baylor University and specialized in the study of cultural and archaeological anthropology. Her research resulted in the receipt of a second-place award at the annual Society for Applied Anthropology conference among hundreds of undergraduate, graduate, and post-graduate applicants.

Lama earned her law degree from the University of Houston Law Center. She was a member of the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) team where she participated in two national competitions and placed as a quarterfinalist in one. Lama is fluent in Arabic. During her free time, Lama loves to travel, be outdoors, and attend music festivals and concerts. Lama is also an avid fan of the Dallas Cowboys, otherwise known to her as the greatest football team of all time.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Stephen J. Zayler
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Lufkin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Stephen J. Zayler graduated from the University of Tyler in 1979 where he was on the President's Honor Roll from 1978-79 as well as Who's Who in American Colleges and Universities in 1978. After Graduating from the University of Tyler, he attended the Texas Tech University School of Law and graduated in 1982. He has been practicing law ever since.

Steve has over 30 years experience as a practicing attorney and over 20 years experience as a Chapter 7 Trustee for the Eastern District of Texas. He has handled over 20,000 cases as a Chapter 7 Trustee with some of the cases being consumer bankruptcies and other being very complex business bankruptcies.

In addition to his busy practice, Steve has served on the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Eastern District of Texas Local Rules Committee from 1993 to 1995 and then from 2010 to present.

Steve has earned gratitude and respect from his colleagues, clients, bankruptcy court officials by hard work, integrity and being committed to providing high quality legal services. He has his practice limited mainly to Chapter 7 and Chapter 13 bankruptcies for individuals and businesses.

attorneys.name: Charles E. Zech
attorneys.firm_name: Denton Navarro Rodriguez Bernal Santee & Zech, P.C.
attorneys.practice_type: Local Government Entities Lawyers in Austin, TX
attorneys.bio:
Charles E. Zech is a Partner/Shareholder in the Firm and has over 20 years of experience in the representation of various local government entities, including cities, counties, economic development corporations, tax increment reinvestment zones and others. Mr. Zech is Past President of the Board of Directors of the Texas City Attorneys Association (TCAA) and former board member of the Texas Municipal League Board of Directors. He is an International Municipal Lawyers Association (IMLA) Local Government Fellow and previously served as Chair of its Ethics Section. He is a member of the Texas City Managers Association, The Texas City Attorney's Association, has served as Faculty speaker to the Suing and Defending Governmental Entities State Bar Program and as faculty on the University of Texas Land Use Seminar planning committee since 2005. He is the 2011 recipient of State Bar of Texas Governmental Section Outstanding Government Lawyer Award. Mr. Zech is a past Adjunct Professor at Texas State University where he taught Problems in Public Law. In connection with his work on his Masters in Public Administration, Mr. Zech completed an update of Terrell Blodgett's 1994 monograph on Texas Home Rule Charters. That research resulted in a comprehensive review of the content and policies of Home Rule Charters in Texas.

Mr. Zech is a proud veteran and of the U.S. Navy and the Gulf War. During his time of service Mr. Zech earned a Meritorious Unit Accommodation and a National Defense Service Medal among other accolades.

Awards and Honors

Honors

2011 Outstanding Government Lawyer Award, State Bar of Texas

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
Ryan is a Trial Lawyer who's recovered the largest verdicts and settlements in history for clients who were involved in a car accident, catastrophically injured, seriously burned, and tragically killed across Texas, Louisiana, New Mexico and the United States.

His record-setting verdicts and settlements have received national media attention, distinguished Ryan as one of the top personal injury lawyers in the country, and qualified him for lifetime membership in both the "Million Dollar Advocates Forum" and the “Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum,” organizations limited to less than 1% of the top trial lawyers in the country.

In recognition of these and his firm's many other accomplishments, Zehl & Associates was one of only two law firms in the United States to be consecutively selected as the 2020, 2021, and 2022 “Personal Injury Law Firm of the Year" by Law.com and The National Law Journal.

Since founding the firm, Ryan and his team have repeatedly recovered the largest verdicts and settlements in history for their clients, including the:

Largest Oilfield Accident Settlement in US History

Largest Oilfield Burn Injury Settlement in US History

Largest Truck Accident Settlement in Texas

#1 Largest Accident Verdict in Texas

#1 Largest Accident Settlement in Texas

#1 Largest Verdict in Offshore Liftboat's Corporate History

#1 Largest Verdict in R&L Trucking Company's Corporate History

#1 Largest Settlement in Oakley Trucking's Corporate History, and

#1 Largest Accident Verdict in Greyhound Bus Lines' Corporate History

Ryan has been featured on the cover of Texas Super Lawyers magazine, a Thompson Reuters publication, voted as one of the top 100 personal injury lawyers in Texas by the National Trial Lawyers Association, and selected as a "Texas Super Lawyer" and "Rising Star" every year since 2009.

After graduating in the top 5 percent of his law school class, Ryan worked as a briefing attorney for Justice Scott Brister of the Texas Supreme Court. When his term with the Supreme Court expired, Ryan joined Gardere’s litigation and appellate group, where he quickly distinguished himself as an aggressive trial lawyer in complex commercial and personal injury cases.

Ryan has been interviewed on CNN, Fox & Friends, Good Morning America and news outlets throughout Texas and appeared in almost every major newspaper across the world, including the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, the Washington Post, the International Herald Tribune, Bloomberg, the Houston Chronicle, and the Dallas Morning News.

attorneys.name: Harjeen Zibari
attorneys.practice_type: Discrimination Lawyers in Dallas, TX
attorneys.bio:
Harjeen Zibari is a trial attorney in the Dallas office of Rob Wiley, P.C.

Harjeen has considerable litigation experience, including in state court, federal court, and arbitration. She also has experience in front of administrative and governmental agencies such as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) and the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC). Regardless of what stage a case is in, her ultimate goal is achieving the best outcome possible for her clients. Her practice specializes in variety of claims, which include Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), and the Texas Labor Code. Harjeen appreciates that with every client comes a unique story and experience worthy of compassion and zealous advocacy.

Harjeen has always been dedicated to the fight for justice and has represented clients in courts across Texas. Prior to joining the firm, Harjeen worked at a nonprofit organization as a criminal justice reform attorney, where she represented low-income Texans who faced incarceration solely due to their inability to afford court costs and fines. Outside of the courtroom, Harjeen advocated at the state and local level for criminal reform bills and measures, including testifying at the state legislature. She also worked on large-scale civil litigation matters dedicated to bail reform, immigration, and homelessness.

Harjeen is a proud Dallas native. She attended the University of Texas at Dallas for her undergraduate degree as a Dean’s Scholar, where she graduated summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and Child Learning and Development with a minor in Political Science. Harjeen was also a member of Phi Beta Kappa honors society and competed in undergraduate moot court.

For law school, Harjeen attended the University of Texas at Austin School of Law, where she graduated with pro bono honors for completing over 100 hours of extracurricular pro bono service. She provided pro bono assistance such as wills and estate planning, expunctions, special education advocacy, Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewals, and name and gender marker changes. While in law school, Harjeen was a student attorney in the Civil Rights Clinic and the Criminal Defense Clinic. Harjeen continued to compete in moot court at the law school level and was selected to participate in UT’s annual Hutchinson Moot Court competition, further developing her advocacy skills.

Harjeen also served as the Peer Mentorship Coordinator for Texas Law’s Women’s Law Caucus, focusing on expanding the school’s mentorship opportunities for first-generation women of color like herself. Additionally, Harjeen served as Managing Editor of Publication for the Texas International Law Journal, which honed her legal writing skills and her attention to detail. In recognition for her successes in law school, Harjeen received distinctions as a Farris-Cisneros Scholar from the Travis County Women Lawyers Association (TCWLA) and as an Access to Justice Scholar from the National Association of Women Judges (NAWJ).

Harjeen is currently licensed to practice law in Texas, and is admitted to the Western, Northern, Eastern, and Southern Federal District Courts of Texas. She is fluent in English and Kurdish.

attorneys.name: Bryan E. Zubay
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Houston, TX
attorneys.bio:
With experience as a law clerk to federal judges and as a trial lawyer for large companies, Bryan’s expertise is crafting compelling, case-winning arguments for Zehl & Associates’ clients, through briefing to the trial and appellate courts on the most important legal issues in their cases.

Bryan grew up in Sugar Land, Texas, and graduated from New York University with a Bachelor of Arts in Economics, and from the University of Texas at Austin School of Law before returning home to Houston.

He clerked for both the Honorable Magistrate Judge Peter J. Bray and the Honorable Judge George C. Hanks, Jr., where he assisted the court in making decisions and writing opinions about complicated personal injury, wage and labor, civil rights, and commercial disputes. This rare and prestigious experience has taught Bryan what arguments persuade courts, and how to identify and exploit the weaknesses in our opponents’ cases to our clients’ advantage.

Prior to joining Zehl & Associates, Bryan practiced at one of the largest law firms in the world, then moved to a trial boutique, where he primarily defended Fortune 100 and 500 companies. He quickly realized that his most personally rewarding cases were those where he represented and sought justice on behalf of people who were seriously injured or tragically killed, prompting his move to Zehl & Associates.

Outside of the office, Bryan enjoys running and cycling, spending time with his family and friends, and reading and writing fiction novels. He is also active in a number of charitable organizations that mentor underprivileged children and adolescents in the greater Houston area.
